case_source: (From the judgment and order dated 21.07.2008 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 3850 of 1998)
full_judgment:
Syed Mahmud Hossain J. This appeal, by leave, is directed against the judgment and order dated 21.07.2008 passed by the learned Single Judge of the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 3850 of 1998 making the Rule absolute and setting aside the judgment and decree dated 09.11.1997 passed the then learned Subordinate Judge, Second Court, Moulvi Bazar in Title Appeal No.175 of 1986 allowing the appeal and reversing the judgment and decree dated 31.08.1986 passed by the then Upazila Munsif Kulaura, Moulvi Bazar in Title Suit No. 354 of 1983 decreeing the suit.

2. The facts, leading to the filing of this appeal, in brief, are:

The respondents as the plaintiffs filed Title Suit No.354 of 1983 for declaration of title and recovery of khas possession in the Court of the then Munsif, Kulaura, Moulvi Bazar. The plaintiffs case, in short, is that the suit land belonged to their predecessor. The plaintiffs have been possessing the suit land as khas khamar and graveyard. On Chaitra, 1378. B.S. the plaintiffs went to the local Tahsil Office for payment of rent and came to know that the suit land appertaining to plot No.1/2 was recorded in the names of the defendants. Having learnt the above wrong record, the plaintiffs filed Title Suit No.112 of 1974 but the plaint of the suit was returned to the plaintiffs. After that, on Baishak,1388 B.S., the defendants in collusion with each other dispossessed the plaintiffs illegally from plot Nos.1, 2 and 4 of the suit land. After that, the plaintiff's went to the local Tahsil Office and came to know that disputed plot Nos.2 and 3 were wrongly recorded in the names of defendant Nos. 1 and 2 and plot No. 4 was recorded in the name of defendant No. 3. The plaintiffs approached the defendants for correction of record of right and recovery of khas possession of the land in plot Nos. 1, 2 and 4 but the defendants denied the claim made by the plaintiffs. Hence the plaintiffs have filed this suit for declaration of title and recovery of khas possession of the suit plot Nos. 1, 2 and 4.

3. The defendants contested the suit by filing written statement denying the material statements made in the plaint. Their case, in short, is that the plaintiffs were landlord (Mirasdar),who used  to settle land in favour of different persons. The suit plot No. 4 was settled in favour of Md. Maznu by a registered kabuliyat by plaintiff No.1 on 1st Baishak,1350 13.S. After that, Md. Maznu sold the said property in favour of defendant Nos.1 and 2 by a registered deed of sale dated 04.03.1949. Suit plot Nos.2 and 3 were owned and possessed by the plaintiff and his 2 sisters, Sundani Bibi and Dudu Bibi, who sold the same to Md. Salim in Baishak,1353 13.S. After that, Md. Salim also sold 24 decimals of land in favour of defendant Nos.1 and 2 by a registered deed of sale dated 13.04.1946 and the plaintiff had the full knowledge about that transfer. Thus the defendants became the owners and possessors of the suit land. However, the plaintiffs out of ill motive filed Title Suit No. 63 of 1954, which was dismissed on contest. After that, Title Appeal No. 64 of 1957 filed by the plaintiffs before the learned District Judge, Sylhet, was also dismissed. As such, the defendants-petitioners prayed for dismissal of the suit.

4. The trial Court after hearing the parties by its judgment and order dated 31.08.1986 decreed the suit. Against the judgment and decree passed by the trial Court, the defendants preferred Title Appeal No.175 of 1986 before the learned District Judge, Moulvibazar. On transfer, the appeal was heard and disposed of by the then teamed Subordinate Judge, Second Court, Moulvibazar, who by his judgment and order dated 30.10.1997 allowed the appeal setting aside the judgment and decree of the trial Court.

5. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with judgment and decree of the appellate Court, the plaintiffs tiled a revisional application before the High Court Division and obtained Rule in Civil Revision No. 3850 of 1998. After hearing the parties, the learned Single Judge of the High Court Division, by the judgment and order dated 21.07.2008 made the Rule absolute.

6. Feeling aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the judgment and order passed by the High Court Division, the leave-petitioners moved this Division by filing Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal Nos. 2337 of 2010, in which, leave was granted on 24.11.2013, resulting in Civil Appeal No. 15 of 2014.

7. Mr. Abdul Quiyum, learned Senior Advocate, appearing on behalf of the appellants, submits that if an under raiyat has been allowed to continue occupation after expiry of his term of lease, his tenancy can only be terminated in accordance with Bengal Tenancy Act and that in the case in hand, the defendants continued as lawful tenants by holding over and that after acquisition of rent receiving interest under the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, the defendants became tenants directly under the Government and that the High Court Division failed to consider this aspect of the case and as such, the impugned judgment should be set aside. He further submits that the defendants have been in possession of the suit land for more than 40 years and that the plaintiffs had failed to prove the story of the possession followed by the dispossession by adducing evidence and that the suit has been filed within the statutory period of limitation and as such, the impugned judgment should be set aside.

8. Mr. A. J. Mohammad Ali, learned Senior Advocate, appearing on behalf of the plaintiffs, on the other hand, supports the impugned judgment delivered by the High Court Division.

9. We have considered the submissions of the learned Senior Advocates of both the sides, perused the impugned judgment and the materials on record.

<u>10. Before entering into the merit of this appeal, it is necessary to go through the grounds, for which, leave was granted. The grounds arc quoted below:</u>

<u>"The appellate Court being the last Court of fact, the High Court Division committed 'tied in interfering with the findings of the appellate Court in the absence of any infirmity in those findings.</u>

<u>Even if an under-raiyat has been allowed to continue occupation after expiry of his term of lease, his tenancy can only be terminated in accordance with the Bengal Tenancy Act (1954) [8 DLR 366, 6 DLR (1952) 652] and that in the case in hand, the defendants continued as lawful tenant by holding over and after acquisition of rent receiving interest under the State Acquisition and tenancy Act, the defendants petitioners became tenants directly under the Government and that the High Court Division failed to consider this aspect of the case.</u>

<u>The High Court Division failed to consider that the rent receipts and record of rights have got evidentiary value and that the defendants-petitioners had been possessing the suit land for more than 40 years within the knowledge of the plaintiffs respondents and as such, the impugned judgment should be set aside.</u>

<u>The defendants-petitioners have been possessing the suit land for more than 40 years and the plaintiffs-respondents had failed to prove the story of possession followed by dispossession by adducing evidence and that the suit has been filed within the statutory period of limitation and as such, the impugned judgment should be set aside. The High Court Division committed error in failing to reverse the finding of the appellate Court that the plaintiffs earlier filed Title Suit No. 63 of 1954 for declaration of title in respect of 4 plots of the suit land and that the said suit was dismissed after hearing both the sides and that the present suit being Title Suit No. 63 of 1954 in respect of the suit land is barred by res judicata as well as limitation and as such, the impugned judgment should be set aside.</u>

11. The plaintiffs-respondents claimed that they are the owners of the suit land by way of inheritance. The plaintiffs further claimed that they went to the Tahsil Office for payment of rent and came to know that the suit land appertaining to plot No. 1/2 was recorded in the names of the defendants. On Baishak, 1388 B.S. The defendants in collusion with each other dispossessed the plaintiffs illegally from the suit plot Nos. 1, 2 and 4 of the suit land. The defendants contended that that the plaintiffs were the landlords (Mirasdars), who used to settle land in favour of different persons. Plaintiff No. 1 settled suit plot No. 4 to Md. Maznu by a registered kabuliyat dated 01.01.1340 B.S. After that, Md. Maznu sold the said property in favour of defendant Nos. 1 and 2 by a registered deed of sale dated 04.03.1949. Suit plot Nos. 2 and 3 were owned and possessed by the plaintiff and his 2 sisters, Sundari Bibi and Dudu Bibi, who sold the same to Md. Salim in Baishak,1353 B.S. After that, Md. Salim also sold 24 decimals of land in favour of defendant Nos. 1 and 2 by a registered deed of sale dated 13.04.1946. The plaintiff filed Title Suit No. 63 of 1954 which was dismissed on contest and Title Appeal No. 64 of 1957 filed by the plaintiffs before the learned District Judge, Sylhet, was also dismissed.

12. Plaintiff No.1 settled suit plot No. 4 to Md. Maznu by a registered kabuliyat dated 1st Baishak,1340 B.S. (exhibit-B) for a period of 8 years. Before expiry of 8 years, Md. Maznu sold the suit land to defendant Nos. 1 and 2 by a registered deed of sale dated 04.04.1949 (Exhibit-C). The trial Court came to a finding that before expiry of the tenure of lease Md. Maznu sold the suit land to defendant Nos. 1 and 2 and that Md. Maznu did not have the right to sell the land of suit plot No. 4 to defendant Nos. 1 and 2 violating the terms of the kabuliyat. The appellate Court, however, came to the finding that defendant Nos. 1 and 2 acquired title to the land of suit plot No. 4 by way of holding over.

13. The plaintiffs did not state anything in the plaint about the registered kabuliyat dated 1st Baishak, 1350 B.S. which was for a period of 8 years. Admittedly, before expiry of the tenure mentioned in the kabuliyat Md. Maznu sold the land of suit plot No. 4 to defendant Nos. 1 and 2. This purchase is of course subject to right of plaintiff No.1 to get the property back. Since the kabuliyat was for a period of 8 years, the plaintiffs could take step to get back the land of plot No. 4 from defendant Nos. 1 and 2 soon after expiry of the tenure of the kabuliyat. There is even no statement in the plaint that defendant Nos. 1 and 2 surrendered possession of suit plot No. 4 to the plaintiffs after expiry of the period of lease. By the purchase dated 04.03.1949, defendant Nos. 1 and 2 became tenants under the plaintiffs. After expiry of the tenure of lease defendant Nos. 1 and 2 remained as lawful tenants under the plaintiff's by holding over.

14. In this connection reliance may be placed on the case of Jagabandu Basak and others Vs. Karim Mondal and others, (1956) 8 DLR 366, in which, it has been held that if an under-raiyat has been allowed to continue occupation after expiry of his term of lease, his tenancy can only be terminated in accordance with the provisions of the Bengal Tenancy Act.

15. We have already found that the plaintiffs did not take any step to get back the land of plot No. 4 after expiry of the period of lease mentioned in the kabuliyat. Defendant Nos. 1 and 2, the under-raiyat, continued their possession in suit plot No. 4 as lawful tenants under the plaintiffs by holding over and after acquisition of rent receiving interest, they became tenants directly under the Government.

<u>16. Reliance may also be placed on the case of Awswini Kumar Poddar and others Vs. Taraq Chandra Rajbangish and others, (1954) 6 DLR 652, in which, it has been held that the provisions of section 116 of the Transfer of Property Act are applicable where the tenant remains in possession of the lease-hold property after determination of the lease granted to the tenant and his continuing possession is assented to by the landlord. A tenant, who surrendered possession, does not come within the meaning of the words "remains in possession" of this section.</u>

17. in the case in hand, the plaintiff could not make out any case that after expiry of the tenure of lease defendant Nos. 1 and 2 surrendered the land of suit plot No. 4 to the plaintiffs. Therefore, defendant Nos. 1 and 2 continued their possession in the land of suit plot No. 4 and became tenant under the Government after wholesale acquisition of superior interest by the Government.

18. Suit plot Nos. 2 and 3 were sold by plaintiff No. 1 and his two sisters to Md. Salim, who sold 24 decimals of land in favour of defendant Nos. 1 and 2 by a registered deed of sale dated 13.04.1946 A.D.

<u>19. From the discussion made above, it is crystal clear that the plaintiffs miserably failed to prove their title to the suit land. Admittedly, the plaintiffs filed Title Suit No. 63 of 1954 for declaration of title in respect of the suit land which was dismissed. Subsequently, the plaintiffs filed Title Appeal No. 64 of 1957 before the learned District Judge, Sylhet, which was also dismissed. Therefore, it appears that instant Title Suit No. 112 of 1972 filed by the plaintiffs is hopelessly barred by limitation.</u>

<u>20. The defendants have produced the records of right standing in their names in respect of the suit land and also the rent receipt showing payment of rent to the Government. Having gone through the evidence of the witnesses, we find that the defendants had been in possession of the suit land for more than 40 years within the knowledge of the plaintiffs. The plaintiffs-respondents failed to prove the story of their alleged possession followed by dispossession by adducing convincing evidence and they also failed to prove that the suit has been filed within the statutory period of limitation and as such, the suit was barred by limitation on this score also.</u>

21. In the light of the findings made before, we find substance in this appeal.

22. Accordingly, this appeal is allowed without any order as to costs and the impugned judgment delivered by the High Court Division is set aside and the judgment and decree passed by the appellate Court is restored.

End.

full_judgment:
2018 BLD (HCD) 38

A. K M Zahirul Hoque, J.

A. K. M. Zahirul Hoque,J.: Since the common questions and facts and law are involved in both the Rules as such both the Rules heard together and delivered the judgment by this single judgment.

2. In Civil Revision No. 3479 of 2004, Rule was issued calling upon the opposite parties No. 1-12 to show cause as to why the judgment and decree dated 30.05.2004 passed by the learned Additional District Judge, 3rd Court, Comilla in Title Appeal No. 79 of 1999 (analogously heard with Title Appeal No. 83 of 1999 allowing the appeal) reversing the judgment and decree dated 21.03.1999 passed by the learned Senior Assistant Judge, Burchang in Title Suit No. 34 of 1996 should not be set aside and or such other or further order or orders passed as to this Court may seem fit and proper.

3. In Civil Revision No. 3480 of 2004, Rule was issued calling upon the opposite parties No. 1-12 to show cause as to why the judgment and decree dated 30.05.2004 passed by the learned Additional District Judge, 3rd Court, Comilla in Title Appeal No. 83 of 1999 (analogously heard with Title Appeal No. 79 of 1999) allowing the appeal upon reversing the judgment and decree dated 21.03.1999 passed by the learned Senior Assistant Judge, Burichang in Title Suit No. 34 of 1996 should not be set aside and or such other or further order or orders passed as to this Court may seem fit and proper.

4. Facts, relevant for the purpose of disposal of both the Rules in short, are as under;

5. That the petitioner as plaintiff instituted Title Suit No. 119 of 1989 for partition on 30.07.1989 in the 1st Court of Subordinate Judge, Comilla which on being transferred at the court of Senior Assistant Judge, Burichang re-numbered as Title Suit No. 34 of 1996 praying a decree for partition of ejmali property mentioned in the plaint schedule claiming his share for 1.74-7/10 acre in total divisible land described in 1st (Ka)-1st (Cha), and 2nd (Chha) and 3rd schedule not shown as divisible in the plaint 2nd (Uma)-2nd (Chha) have been shown to be plaintiffs self acquired property and 3rd schedule property is ejmali indivisible pond. The 2nd (Uma)-2nd (Chha) schedule have been brought on Hotchpotch to meet the objection raised by the defence.

7. The case of the petitioner in short is that in schedule 1st (Ka)-1st (Chha) property Charu Gazi, Budha Gazi and Chan Gazi were the owners in equal share. The defendant Nos. 35-52 are heirs of Budha Gazi and defendant Nos. 53-117 are heirs of Chand Gazi, Charu Gazi died leaving one son Ramja, two daughters Raiman Bibi and Kulchum Bibi. On trial the trial Court decreed the suit in part in respect of 1.37 acres of land out of 1.74 7/10 acres of land by the judgment passed on 21.03.1999 and he did not commit decreed in respect of schedule 1st (Ka) which is admittedly a joint pond of both the parties and on appeal the lower appellate Court maintained the judgment and decree and finding of the trial Court but modifying the decree reduced the share of the plaintiff petitioner and decreed in respect of 95 acres of land. In this Rule the learned Advocate for the plaintiff-petitioner mainly argued that the land has mentioned in schedule 1st (Ka) -1(Cha) admittedly obtained by their predecessor of the plaintiff' and defendant namely Charu Gazi, Buda Gazi and Chand Gazi during their life time while they were living jointly in a same mess. 22. In this regard, the Court of trial after considering the Exhiibit-2ka, Exhibit-2, Uma (Ka) along with other materials-on-records got the findings to the effect that:

“স্বীকৃত মতেই নালিশী ১ম(ক) ১ম(ঙ) এবং ১ম(ছ) তপছিলের ভূমিতে চারু গাজী, চান গাজী এবং বুধা গাজী ভ্রাতা ক্রয় তুল্যাংশে মালিক দখলকার ছিলেন।

২নং বিবাদীপক্ষ তাহাদের বর্ণনা এবং জবান বন্দীতে বলেন যে নালিশী ১ম(গ) তপছিলের ভূমি চান্দ গাজীর এবং ১ম(ঘ) ও ১ম(চ) তপছিলের ভূমি বুধা গাজীর নিজ অর্থে স্বার্থে খরিদা ভূমি হয়। কিন্তু কোন তারিখের কবলা মূলে তাহারা তাহ খরিদ করেন কাহার নিকট হইতে খরিদ করেন তাহার কোন উল্লেখ করেন নাই। কিংবা তদ্রুপ কোন দলিল ও দাখিল করা হয় নাই।২ নং বিবাদী ও জেরায় স্বীকার করে যে, উক্ত তিন তপছিলের ভূমি কবে তাহার নিকট হইতে খরিদ করা হয় তাহা বলিতে পারিবে না। তৎমর্মে কোন দলিল নাই। বিবাদীপক্ষ দাবী করেন যে সি আর জরিপের পূর্বেহ ভ্রাতাগনের মধ্যে আপোষে বন্টন হয় এবং এ বন্টন মূলেই ১ম (গ) তপছিলের ভূমি চান গাজী এবং ১ম (ঘ) ও (চ) তপছিলের ভূমি বুধা গাজী প্রাপ্ত হয়। কিন্তু কোন মনে ভ্রাতাগন পৃথক হয় তাহা জানে না এবং বন্টনমূলে দখলে থাকার কোন প্রমান বা সাক্ষী নাই বলিয়া স্বীকার করেন। দেখা যায় তাহাদের নামে সিধার ৩২/৩৫/২/১৫/১৯ নং খতিয়ানে যৌথভাবেই রেকর্ড হয়। ফলে ধারনা করা যায় যে তখন তাহারা এজমালীতে ছিল। ইহা ছাড়া ২নং বিবাদী পক্ষ ১৫/১/৯১ ইং তারিখে বর্ণনা দাবি ক্রমে উল্লেখিত ৩ ভ্রাতা তুল্যাংশে উল্লেখিত তপছিলে ক্রয়ের মালিক দখলদার ছিলেন বলিয়া স্বীকার করেন। ২/৯/৯৮ ইং তারিখের পূর্ব পর্যন্ত বিবাদী পক্ষের তদ্রুপ দাবী ছিল এবং উক্ত তারিখে ২ নং বিবাদী বর্ণন সংশোধন করিয়া বলেন যে, ১ম (গ) তপছিলের চান গাজী এবং ১ম (ঘ) ও ১ম (চ) তপছিলে বুধা গাজী এককভাবে মালিক ছিলেন। এতদব্যতীত স্বীকৃত মতেই ইতিপূর্বে ও পক্ষগনের মধো উল্লেখিত তপছিতাদি সম্পর্কে বন্টনের মামলা হয় এবং তাহাতে ২ নং বিবাদী বাদীর সাথে সোলনামা দিয়া স্বীকার করেন যে, উল্লেখিত তপছিল ক্রয়ে ও তিন ভ্রাতা তুল্যাংশে মালিক দখলদার ছিলেন। ফলে ২ নং বিবাদী এক্ষনে ভিন্নবুপ দাবী করিতে পারেন না। অধিকন্তু বিবাদীপক্ষ আপোষ বন্টনমূলে তদ্রুপ দাবী করেন কিন্তু আপোষ বন্টন আইনের চোখে গ্রহনযোগ্য নহে। কাজেই ১ম (গ), ১ম(ঘ) এবং ১ম (চ) তপছিলের ভূমি ও চারু গাজী চান গাজী এবং বুধা গাজীর তুল্যাংশে মালিকীয় এবং দখলীয় ভুমি ছিল বলিয়া সিদ্ধান্ত গ্রহন করা হইল।”

So, the trial Court after considering the plaintiff and defendant witnesses got the finding that the predecessor of the plaintiff and defendant namely Charu Gazi, Buda Gazi and Chand Gazi were living jointly in a same mess and they got equal share in respect of the land of the schedule 1' (Ka), Uma and Cha. Subsequently the claim by the defendant No. 2 that the land in question of schedule I St Ga and Gha and Cha obtained by Chand Gazi and Buda Gazi by their own interest with their own fund for the said land. In support of such claim there is no piece of documentary nor any oral evidence to prove the said fact of his statement. Even the said fact was not disclosed in the earliest point of time of suit as well as in the solenama rather it was admitted that said three brothers Chand Gazi, Buda Gazi Charu Gazi were living together in same mess jointly. It appears that the trial Court on consideration of the materials on record including the records in the khatian itself got the finding to the effect that:</u>

<u>“আর্জির ১ম (গ) তপছিলে বর্নিত ভূমিতে শাসনগাছা মৌজার ১১ নং খতিয়ানতুক্ত। উক্ত খতিয়ানের সত্যায়িত নকল প্রদর্শনী-২৫ক) পর্যালোচনায় দেখা যায় এতে বাদীর পূর্ববর্তীর রমজান আলী বা চারু গাজীর কোন নাম নেই। বাদী উক্ত ১১ নং" খতিয়ানাধীন ভূমি তার পূর্ববর্তী চারু গাজী গং ৩ ভাইয়ের এজমালি বলে দাবী করলেও এর স্বপক্ষে কোন কাগজপত্র না থাকায় এবং বাদীর দাখিলকৃত প্রদর্শনী ২(ক) তে বাদীর পূর্ববর্তী রমজান আলী বা চারু গাজীর নাম না থাকায় আমি মনে করি নালিশী ১ম (গ) তপছিলের বর্ণিত ১১ নং খতিয়ানাধীন ভূমিতে বাদী চারু গাজী বা রমজান আলীকে স্থলবর্তী হিসেবে কোন অংশ পেতে পারে না।</u>

<u>আর্জির ১ম (ঘ) তপছিলে বর্ণিত ভূমি একই মৌজার ৫ নং খতিয়ান ভুক্ত মর্মে দেখা যায়। উক্ত ৫ নং খতিয়ানের সত্যায়িত নকল প্রদর্শনী-২ পর্যালেচনায় দেখা যায় এতেও বাদীর পূর্ববর্তী রমজান আলী বা তার পিতা চারু গাজীর নাম নেই। এই ৫ নং খতিয়ানাধীন ভূমি বাদী তার পূর্ববর্তী চারু গাজী গং ৩ ভাইয়ের তুল্যাংশে মালিকীয় ভূমি হিসেবে বাদী করলেও এর স্বপক্ষে বাদী জন্য কোন কাগজপত্র দাখিল করেননি। তাই আমি মনে করি বাদীর দাখিলকৃত ৫ নং খতিয়ানের সত্যায়িত নকল প্রদর্শনী-২ মূলে উক্ত খতিয়ানাধীন ভূমিতে ���াদীর পূর্ববর্তী রমজান আলী বা চারু গাজী অংশীদার ছিলনা।</u>

<u>আর্জির ২য় (চ) তপছিলের বর্ণিত ভূমি একই মৌজার ১৮ নং খতিয়ানের অন্তর্ভুক্ত। উক্ত খতিয়ানের সত্যায়িত নকল প্রদর্শনী-২ (ঙ) পর্যালোচনায় দেখা যায় এটি বুদা গাজীর নামীয় সত্যায়িত নকল প্রদর্শনী-২(ঙ) পর্যালোচনায় দেখা যায় যে এটি বুদা গাভীর নামীয় খতিয়ান। বাদীর দাখিলকৃত এই খতিয়ানে ও বাদীর পূর্ববর্তীদের কোন নাম নেই। এই ক্ষেত্রে ও বাদীর পূর্ববর্তী চারু গাজী গং ও ভ্রাতা বা তাদের পিতা গদা গাজীর মালিকামার স্বপক্ষে অন্য কোন দলিলপত্র বাদী দাখিল করে নাই। তাই আমি মনে করি ১ম (চ) তপছিলের বর্ণিত ১৮ নং খতিয়ানের গাজী গং তিন ভাই তুল্যাংশে মালিক থাকার দাবীটি বাদী প্রমান করতে পারেনি।”</u>

24. To justify the said finding about the joint ownership of the said 03 brothers .by the trial Court as well as the lower appellate Court, I have carefully perused the evidences-on-record along with the said finding of both the courts below, the trial court found that the defendant witness No. 2 corroborated and admitted the plaintiff's case that Charu Gazi, Buda Gazi and Chand Gazi were living on the same mess and during their joint family the names of the predecessor of the plaintiffs and defendants were recorded in the khatians as mentioned in first schedule No. 1 Ka, l Uma and 1 Cha in equal share. On perusal the said khatian along with deposition of PWs and D. W. 2 it appears that the said finding of the trial Court is correct and based on material-on-record. But there is no basis to incorporate the name of the predecessor of the defendant in the subsequent khatian. It further appears that the trial Court gave explanation and reasons in his finding. Even the defendant No. 2 did not disclose the said fact in the earlier suit of partition as well as in course of execution of the solenama between the parties as evident from Exhibit-10. Non discloser the said fact of the defence plea in the earliest point of time and subsequent discloser such fact without any valid reasons are not free from principle of subsequent embellishment by the defendants for their interest. On perusal it appears that the finding of the Court of trial based on materials-on-record with cogent reasons as mentioned above. Whereas, the finding of the Court of appeal below in respect of first schedule No. 1 Ga, 1 Gha and 1 Cha are without any basis as such the same has no legal in the eye of law. As such only incorporated the name of the predecessors of the defendant in the subsequent khatian does not create any title neither in favour of their predecessors nor in favour of the defendants in any way and while the predecessor of the defendant namely Charu Gazi and Buda Gazi admittedly were the members of joint family with Chand Gazi. Thereby the incorporate of the name of the Chand Gazi and Buda Gazi in Khatian No. 5, 11 and 18 have no legal basis and as such no title has been passed by such wrong records of right in favour of the defendants. Therefore the finding of the lower appellate Court to that effect is baseless as well as misreading and non-consideration of the materials-on- record as mentioned above thereby it has committed an error in his decision and thereby occasioning failure of justice.

25. Considering the above facts and circumstances and discussion made above, I find substance and merit in both the Rules.

26. In the result, both the Rules are made absolute without any order as to costs.

27. The judgment and decree dated 30.05.2004 passed by the learned Additional District Judge, 3rd Court, Comilla in Title Appeal No. 79 of 1999 and Title Appeal No. 83 of 1999 (analogously heard) allowing the appeals reversing the judgment and decree dated 21.03.1999 passed by the learned Senior Assistant Judge, Burchang in Title Suit No. 34 of 1996 is hereby set aside. Consequently the judgment and decree of the trial Court is restored.

28. The order of stay of both the Civil Revisions are stands vacated.

29. Send down the lower Court records together with a copy of the judgment and order to the Court below at once.

End.

full_judgment:
This Rule at the instance of the defendant opposite parties No. 1-16 is directed against the judgment and decree dated 9-9-2010 passed by the learned Additional District Judge, First Court, Chittagong dismissing the Other Appeal No. 16 of 2009 and affirming the judgment and decree dated 25-11-2008 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, Second Court, Chittagong in decreeing the Other Suit No. 137 of 2001.

2. The opposite-parties herein as plaintiffs instituted Other Suit No. 92 of 1991 in the Sub-ordinate Judge, First Court, Chittagong, on 28-9-.1991 impleading the petitioners Nos. 1-16 and opposite party Nos. 17-43 as defendants for declaration of title and partition of their shares in the land more fully described in the schedule to the plaint. Subsequently, same was transferred to the Joint District Judge, Second Court, Chittagong and renumbered as Other Suit No. 137 of 2001. Thereafter, the plaintiffs amended the plaint seeking relief for setting aside the final decree in previous partition suit and also for cancellation of auction purchase in the Decree Execution Case No. 18 of 1953.

3. The case of the plaintiffs, in short are that the suit plot of RS Khatian No. 2926/15 measuring an area of 0.04 acre of land was transferred by Abul Bashar and Khairul Bashar to Moulavi Aminullah by way of settlement and was correctly recorded in the RS Khatian No. 2629/16, RS plot No. 13105 measuring an area of 0.04 acre out of total area of 0.33 acre. RS Khatian No. 2926/15 was recorded in the name of. Abdul Samad and Aminullah to the extent of two annas share measuring an area of 0.035/8 acre each. Abdul Samad died leaving son Hafizur Rahman and daughter Kulsuma Khatun as his legal heirs. Hafizur Rahman died leaving no children excepting one sister Kulsuma Khatun, who inherited his property. That Kuluma Khatun got married with Aminullah and on her death, husband Aminullah, three sons Tazul Huda, Serajul Huq and Hedayetullah inherited her property. Thereafter, Aminulla died leaving three sons and after their death plaintiff Nos. 1-16 inherited their properties as legal heirs. RS plot Nos. 13104 and 13108 measuring an area of 0.51 acre of land belonged to Abdul Samad and Moulavi Aminulla 1/3 share each and recorded in their names in RS Khatian No. 2926/17 and the remaining 1/3 share was jointly belonged to Abul Bashar and Khairul Bashar in equal share, who transferred their share to Moulavi Aminulla and same was correctly recorded in his name in RS Khatian No. 2926/18. Accordingly, Aminulla became owner of 2/3 share of these plots measuring an area of 0.34 acre of land.

4. That RS Khatian No. 2629/21 appertaining to RS plot No. 13119 and 13109 comprising an area of 0.10 + 0.06 = 0.16 acre were recorded in the names of Ahammad Khalil and Ahammad Kabir to the extent of 4 annas and 16 gandas each and the remaining 6 annas 8 gandas were recorded in the name of Hafizur Rahman, who by amicable settlement with other co-sharers lived in 0.6 acre homestead portion and same was recorded in his name. In this way plaintiff Nos. 1-16 inherited through their predecessor Aminulla 0.07 1/4 acre from RS Khatian No. 2926/15, .04 from RS Khatian No. 2926/16, 0.34 acre from RS Khatian No. 2926/17, 0.17 acre from RS Khatian No. 2926/18 and 0.6 acre from RS Khatian No, 2926/21 totaling an area of 0.68 1/4 acre of land. The plaintiff Nos.1-16 have got their right, title interest and possession in the schedule properties. The defendant Nos. 3-16 are co-sharers of the disputed khatians for which they have been impleaded as defendants to avoid defect of parties. Since the names of other defendants are wrongly recorded in the BS khatian, they have also been impleaded in the suit. It was further stated in the plaint that the predecessor of the defendant Nos. 1 and 2, Md Abdul Monayem filed Other Suit No. 53 of 1968 in the Court of Fifth Munsif, Chittagong for Khas possession of 0.07 acre of homestead land of RS plot No. 13108 against three sons of Aminulla, Tazul Huda, Serajul Huq and Hedayetullah. They appeared in the said suit and filed joint written statement stating that they have no knowledge about Other Suit No. 39 of 1950. In that suit no notice was served upon the defendant and the decree was collusive, no auction sale was held in Decree Execution Case on 27-1-1954 and there was no commission report by the Advocate Commissioner and delivery of possession of the Property on 11-4-1957 through court. Ultimately the above suit was dismissed on compromise. In fact Partition Suit No. 39 of 1950, Execution Case No. 18 of 1953 and Other Suit No. 53 of 1968 are illegal, void, inoperative and without jurisdiction. The plaintiff tried to compromise the matter with the defendants through the arbitration of local Commissioner, but the defendants did not appear. Subsequently, the defendants with a view to harass the plaintiffs filed Non-GR No. 468 of 1986 under section 107 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, Criminal Case No. 254 of 1990, and Panchlaish GR Case No. 33(8) of 1990 in local Police Station against the plaintiffs. The cause of action arose on 19-9-1991 when the defendants threatened the plaintiffs to dispossess them. Subsequently, by amending the plaint the plaintiff prayed for a declaration that the decree dated 31-7-1952 passed by the Fifth Munsif Court, Chittagong in Partition Suit No. 39 of 1950 and auction sale held on 27-9-1954 in Title Execution Case No. 18 of 1953 are null and void, ineffective, fraudulent, collusive and not binding upon the plaintiffs and for partition.

5. Defendant Nos. 1 and 2 contested the said suit by filing joint written statement denying all the materials allegation made in the plaint and contending, inter alia, that the suit is not maintainable in the present form, there is no cause of action and the suit is barred by section 42 of the Specific Relief Act and the same is not maintainable without prayer for declaration of title and khas possession and further the suit is barred by waiver, Estoppel and acquiescence, the principle of res-judicata, defect of parties and also barred by limitation. The positive case of the defendant Nos. 1 and 2 are that the predecessor of the defendants are that, Abdul Monayem obtained the preliminary decree in Partition Suit No. 39 of 1950 on 31-7-1952 passed by the Munsif Fifth Court, Chittagong against Moulvi Aminulla, the predecessor of the plaintiffs in respect of the land described in the suit schedule alongwith other property. Accordingly, final decree was prepared on 5-3-1953 in which the decree-holder got saham of 0.342/7 acre in his share from RS plot No. 13104 and 13108. Thereafter in respect of cost of the suit he filed Title Execution Case No. 18 of 1953 in which he purchased 0.06 acre of land in auction sale from RS plot No. 13109 and took delivery of possession through court on 11-4-1957. Aminulla, the predecessor of the plaintiffs was permitted to live in RS plot No. 13108 temporarily, but after his death his three sons Tazul Huda, Serajul Huq and Hedayetullah refused to surrendered possession to the predecessor of the defendants and for which he filed Other Suit No. 53 of 1968 in the Court of Fifth Munsif, Chittagong for eviction. Ultimately the suit was dismissed in terms of solenama on 16-8-1969.

6. The predecessor of the defendants, Abdul Monayem had recorded his name in appeal Case No. 2147 under section 19(2) of the EBSA and Tenancy Act vide order dated 11-6-1961 passed by the Appellate Officer after hearing the parties, wherein the predecessors of the present plaintiffs were parties and the appellate officer also observed that the present plaintiffs predecessors were found to be in possession of only 0.04 acre of homestead land in RS plot No. 13108. Schedule described RS plot No. 13105 comprises in all 0.33 acre of land from which defendant Nos. 1 and 2 purchased 0.04 acre of land by kabala No. 3129 registered on 5-6-1951 from Aminulla. After the death of CS recorded owner Abdul Bayesh his heirs and subsequent heirs of Halimunnessa, Khairul Islam, Safia Khatun, Nazu Mia, Mariam Khatun transferred by registered Kabala No. 3526 dated 20-10-1933 in favour of the predecessor of these defendants, Abdul Monayem, along with the land of some other khatians, in all 0.36 acre land described in the schedule of the plaint. The remaining lands of the schedule described RS plot No. 13105 have been purchased by three defendants by way of several deeds from other sharers on different dates. Under such circumstance the land of RS plot No. 13104 recorded exclusively in the name of Aminulla in Korfa title is not possible, so the record of RS khatian No. 2926 is wrong. The PS khatian have been recorded in the names of these defendants or in the name of their predecessors. BS record are also recorded in same manner in the names of these defendants and other sharers save and except RS plot No. 13109, which, in collusion with the survey employees, are recorded in their names, which is wrong and baseless. Practically, except the above mentioned 0.07 acre they were not in possession.

7. The plaintiffs have field the instant suit without paying required court fee on proper valuation of the suit land. These defendant along with other co-sharers are in possession of the suit land for more than 12 years by paying rents regularly, receiving rent-receipts. Hence they have got the absolute right, title, interest and possession over the suit land which the Plaintiffs have got no right to deny. The defendants have filed criminal case No. 523 of 1990 against the plaintiffs for theft of their fish from the pond of RS plot 13105 perhaps in turn of which they might have filed the present test suit which deserves to be dismissed. In fact the plaintiffs are well aware of the Final decree of Partition Suit No. 39 of 1950 and Title Execution Case No. 18 of 1953 and the auction sale which have been purchased by the predecessor of the defendants and all other deeds also. It is utter surprise to mentioned that where the plaintiffs have already admitted in their plaint about the sole decree dated 16-8-1969 passed in Other Suit No. 53 of 1968 how they can file the instant suit. Their predecessor-in-interest have specifically admitted the conditions save and except the possession of 0.07 acre of homestead land of RS plot No. 13108 they would never claim their previously sold out properties of all other khatians to the predecessor of the defendants. As per sole decree the predecessor of the defendants, Abdul Monayem had recorded his name correctly in BS khatian Nos. 693 and 695 which have finally been published in his name. After death, his heirs and subsequent heirs transferred 0.39 acre of land from BS plot Nos. 13252 and 13253 to Ashekane Awlia Abdul Monayem High School by registered Deed of Gift No. 7542 dated 1.6-12-1987 and delivered possession, which is within the schedule described in the plaint. Having been well aware of all these facts and circumstances, the plaintiffs intentionally did not make these defendants as parties to the suit. Now the defendants along with their transfers are, in fact, is in possession of their respective lands about which the plaintiffs are not at all entitled to claim any decree and the suit is liable to be dismissed.

8. The case of the defendant Nos. 17-23 as per their written statement, are that, they are subsequent heirs of aforesaid decree-holder Abdul Monayem and their statements are similar to the written statement filed by the defendant Nos. 1 and 2 and they also want dismissal of the suit.

9. Defendant no. 24 contested the suit by filing a separate written statement wherein he also stated all the facts of final decree of Partition Suit No. 39 of 1950 and Decree Execution Case No. 18 of 1953 and reiterated the same facts as stated in the written statement filed on behalf of the defendant Nos. 1-2. It was further stated that Abdul Monayem executed registered Wasiatnama No. 34 dated 31-12-1974 in favour of sons and daughters relinquishing all his properties including the land of the schedule khatians of the suit. After his death, his daughter Mst Numahar Begum having been in possession of her properties died leaving 2 sons 5 daughters and husband as her legal heirs. Her husband Md Ismail Hossain Seraji executed another registered Wasiatnama No. 25 dated 19-7-1995 in favour of his two sons Md Aminul Islam and Azizul Islam. Thereafter Aminul Islam and Azizul Islam having acquired the property by way of Wasiatnama from father, by way of inheritance from their mother and 2 daughter of Abdul Monayem Tahera Parvin and Farida Yasmin having from mother by way of inheritance jointly transferred by kabala No. 4340 dated 5-8-1996 to this defendant from RS plot No. 13104 an area of 8 gandas 2 karas 2 kranti and 1 1/2 danta Ithiti land and handed over possession to this defendant. This defendant having delivery of possession of his purchased land constructed boundary walls around the land and pucca gate where he engraved his name and has been possessing peacefully since purchase. He was not aware of the suit and he was not made party to the suit. Having been informed from reliable source he appeared with a prayer to be added as party in the suit and was made party on his prayer. All the claims of the plaintiffs are false. They cannot deny the decree and decree execution case. This defendant is in possession of his purchased property by paying rent, cesses and receiving rent receipts. The suit is hopelessly barred by the principles of waiver, estoppel Acquiescence and also barred by limitation and res-judicata and is liable to be dismissed.

10. The learned Joint District Judge upon consideration of materials evidence on record by his judgment dated 25-11-2008 decreed the suit. Against the said decree, the defendants preferred Title Appeal No. 16 of 2009 in the Court District Judge, Chittagong and in due course appeal was transferred to the Additional District Judge, First Court, Chittagong. In Title Appeal No. 16 of 2009 plaintiff filed an application on 13-6-2010 calling for the record of Partition Suit No. 39 of 1950 of Fifth Munsif Court, Chittagong and Other Suit No. 53 of 1968 of the same court describing the papers and documents in the said application and same was rejected by the appellate court by order No. 17 dated 14-7-2010. Ultimately, the learned Additional District Judge after hearing the parties, dismissed the appeal by judgment and decree dated 9-9-2010 and affirmed the judgment and decree passed by the trial court.

11. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the judgment and decree dated 9-9-2010 passed by the appellate court the defendants moved this revisional application and obtained the present Rule.

12. During pendency of the revisional application before this court, the petitioner filed an application under Order XLI, rule 27 of the Code of Civil Procedure on 10-3-2013 for additional evidence stating the facts that the record of the Partition Suit No. 39 of 1950 and Title Suit No. 53 of 1968 were called for in the present Other Class Suit No. 137 of 2001 and the record of Partition Suit No. 39 of 1950 was transmitted to the trial court but record of Title Suit No. 53 of 1968 could not be transmitted as it was found missing at the relevant time. But due to bonafide Mistake of the learned Advocate for the defendants as well as the trial court the relevant order of Partition Suit No. 39 of 1950 was not exhibited. On the basis of such bonafide mistake, both the courts below erroneously found that the defendants did not take steps to prove the service of summons of Other Class Suit No. 39 of 1950 which was duly served upon the defendants. But on scrutinizing the order sheet of Partition Suit No. 39 of 1950, it appears that the defendant No. 1 Aminulla, the predecessor of the present plaintiffs was appeared in that suit and filed written statement on 22-2-1951 (order No.8) It also transpired from the order sheet of Title Suit No. 53 of 1968 that the defendant (present plaintiff) appeared in that title suit and filed written statement and ultimately the suit was decreed on compromise and accordingly compromise decree was drawn upon. It is pertinent to mentioned here that those documents were submitted by the plaintiffs in the appellate court but the appellate court below did not consider those documents as additional evidence. It was further stated that the record of Partition Suit No. 39 of 1950 are now before this hon'ble court and the petitioners on the advice of their learned Advocate collected certified copy of entire order sheet of Title Suit 53 of 1968 and written statement filed by defendants dated 10-3-1969. From those documents it will be crystal clear that summons were duly served upon the defendants in Title Suit No. 53 of 1968 and they have contested the said suit by filing written statements in Partition Suit No. 39 of 1950 and Title Suit No. 53 of 1968 respectively. It is also stated that in paragraph No. 2 of the plaint of the present suit the plaintiffs admitted that they appeared and filed written statements in Title Suit No. 53 of 1968. Since the plaintiffs are admitting the facts of their appearance in the Title Suit No. 53 of 1968, which can be easily taken as additional evidence, as admitted facts need not be proved.

13. Against this application of additional evidence, a counter affidavit was filed on behalf of the opposite party stating the facts that no summons was served upon the defendant No.1, 1vId Aminulla, predecessor of the plaintiffs in Other Suit No. 137 of 2001 and that he did not appear or file written statement on 22-2-1951 or on any other date. It is also stated that ex-parte preliminary decree was passed in the said suit without serving summons on defendant No. 1, Aminullah and the final decree was also passed without his knowledge. It was further denied that Abdul Munayem, the predecessor of the defendant Nos. 1-16 purchased 0.25 acre of land in auction held in Execution Case No. 18 of 1953 for realization of cost of the suit including the land of Aminulla.

14. It is also denied that the decree holder Abdul Munayem gave 0.7 acre land to Aminullah for residing there temporary as licensee. It was further denied that Tajul Huda and his two brothers appeared and filed written statement on 10-3-1969 or on any other date in Title Suit No. 53 of 1968 filed by Abdul Munayem. It is also denied that they filed a compromise petition on 7-8-1969 or any on other date and on the basis of said compromise petition suit was decreed. It was further stated that defendants had ample opportunities to exhibit the order sheet of Other Suit No. 39 of 1950 and both the courts below have given their findings on the decree passed in Other Suit No. 39 of 1950, the Execution Case arising there from and on Other Suit No. 53 of 1968 and hence the petitioners are not entitled to adduce additional evidence before the revisional court to patch up the weak part of their case which is not permissible under Order XII, rule 27 of the Code of Civil Procedure.

15. Mr Khalilur Rahman with Mr Khalilur Rahman(Helal) and Mr Mohammad Zafar Ali Khan, the learned Advocates appeared on behalf of the Defendant-petitioners. Mr Khalilur Rahman, the learned Advocate for the petitioners firstly, submits that the present suit was filed on 28-9-1991 challenging the decree passed in Title Suit No. 53 of 1968, and the plaintiffs had knowledge about filing of earlier Title Suit No. 53 of 1968 which they have admitted in paragraph no. 2 of the plaint of the present suit. Since the present suit is filed long after 23 years from their knowledge, same is hopelessly barred by limitation. Secondly, Mr Khalil, submits that in respect of suit property, Abdul Munayem, father of the defendant nos. 1-2 filed Partition Suit No. 39 of 1950 against the predecessors of the plaintiffs Aminullah who contested the said partition suit by filing written statement and ultimately preliminary and final decree was passed in Partition Suit No. 39 of 1950. Thereafter, the predecessors of the defendant again filed Other Suit No. 53 of 1968 against the predecessor of the plaintiffs, Aminullah who appeared and contested the Other Suit No. 53 of 1968 by filing written statement on 10-3-1969 and the said suit was decreed on compromise on 7-8-1969. Thirdly, learned Advocate submits that the plaintiffs claimed title in the suit on the basis of korfa lease of their predecessors Aminullah and RS khatian was published in the name of their predecessor but they, failed to file any lease deed as such korfa lease and record of right does not create any title in the suit land. So, after passing of the final decree in a Partition Suit No. 39 of 1950 and compromise decree dated 7-8-1969 between the parties, and for the same self suit land, the present second suit is barred under the principles of res-judicata and not maintainable. Since the trail court failed to frame any issue in the present suit, whether the suit is barred by res-judicata and thus committed gross error of law in not dismissing the suit. Fourthly, the learned Advocate submits that the plaintiffs has miserably failed to prove that fraud was committed in the earlier suits being Partition Suit No. 39 of 1950 and Other Suit No. 53 of 1968 and also failed to prove that the summons were not duly served upon them in earlier suits. Fifthly, both the courts below failed to consider that most of the title deeds of the present defendants are 30 years old documents, but without considering this legal aspect of the suit, the courts below erroneously passed the decree declaring that those documents are forged documents. Sixthly, he submits that the plaintiff failed to established their title in the suit land, so they cannot challenge the title deeds of the defendants, who acquired title through the process of law. He lastly submits that both the courts below totally failed to consider the evidence, both oral and documentary and misread and non-considered the materials evidence on record and thus committed gross error of law in not dismissing the suit. Accordingly, the learned Advocate prayed that the rule should be made absolute.

16. In support of his submissions learned Advocate placed reliance on the following decisions: 42 DLR 459, 6 MLR (AD) 64, 25 DLR 91, 250, 26 DLR 34 and 32 DLR 252,16 BLD (AD) 251, 9 MLR (AD) 294.

17. On the other hand, Mr Abdul Wadud Bhuiyan, learned Senior Advocate appearing with Mr Syed Mokaddas Ali, the learned Advocate submits that the suit is not barred by limitation because of the fact that the previous suit being Partition Suit No. 39 of 1950 filed by Abdul Munayam, predecessor of defendant Nos. 1 and 2 of the present suit and the defendants Aminullah, predecessors of the present plaintiffs are not aware about the final decree passed in that suit. Since both the courts below concurrently found that no summons were served upon the defendants in Partition Suit No. 39 of 1950 and the said decree was obtained by practicing fraud, then auction sale held in other Execution Case No. 18 of 1953 were not effective and thus the suit is not barred by limitation and same are not binding upon the plaintiffs. In support of his submission he referred two decisions reported in 32 DLR (AD) 167 and 19 DLR (SC) 433, He further submits that the lower appellate court concurred with the findings of the trial court that the plaintiffs are in possession of the suit land, thus the plaintiffs suit for declaration of title and partition is not barred by limitation.

He next submits that the defendants have failed to prove that the predecessor of the plaintiffs signed the solenama filed in Other Suit No. 53 of 1968 which was affirmed by the appellate court. Therefore, the present suit is not barred by the principles of res-judicata and waiver. He also submits that the trial court found that the RS record prepared in the name of the predecessor of the plaintiffs during the period from 1924 to 1930 in Chittagong region same has presumptive value and the defendants did not challenge the same in any court of law. The predecessors of the plaintiffs-Aminuddin being korfa lessee and his successors continued in possession for more than 12 years and on the basis of the RS khatian they acquired title in the suit land. In this respect he placed reliance two decisions reported in 16 DLR (SC) 287 and 54 DLR (AD) 173. He then submits that both the courts below concurrently found that the decree in the Other Suit No. 39 of 1950 was void and defendants did not try to prove by sufficient evidence that the solenama filed in Other Suit No. 53 of 1968 was actually executed by the three sons of Aminullah and therefore the defendants did not acquire any title by the said deeds, further the defendants did not appear in Other Suit No. 53 of 1968 by filing written statement and compromise petition have been filed fraudulently by the plaintiffs of that suit. Since both the courts below concurrently found that the judgment and decree in the earlier partition suit are void, in-operative and not binding upon the plaintiffs. Therefore, the present partition suit filed by the plaintiffs is quite maintainable and it is not necessary to have a separate decree for cancellation of the registered two deeds of the defendants. He further submits that both the courts below in consideration of the evidence, found that the deeds through which the defendants claimed title did not confer any title or possession on the defendants and gave cogent reasons in support of their findings and the courts had jurisdiction to consider whether the deeds conferred title or possession on the defendants even though some of those were 30 years old documents and the genuineness of such documents may be challenged and there is no misreading or nonconsideration of the material evidence by the courts below and the defendants are not entitled to challenge those findings. In this connection he refers the decision reported in 17 BLD (AD) 199. He also submits that the trial court found that the defendants claimed that Abdus Sabur is the owner of land described in the first schedule to the plaint, and in that case the onus is upon the defendant to prove the claim of ownership of Abdus Sabur but they did not file any documents in support of the ownership of Abdus Sabur. DW 1 in his cross-examination admitted that he did not know about any deed showing title of Abdus Sabur. Moreover the document dated 19-6-1895 shows that in that deed ten gandas of land stating Moghi dags were mentioned. But in the written statement the corresponding CS and RS dags had not been mentioned. The defendants did not adduce any documentary or oral evidence to show that the land mentioned in the above deed dated 19-6-1895 and the lands described in the schedule to the plaint are the same land. He also submits that the RS khatian have got presumptive value relating to title in the Chittagong region and the RS record was prepared in Chittagong region from the years 1924 to 1930. After settlement with Aminulla, Abul Bashar and Ithairul Bashar have no title in the land settled with Aminulla. Since the korfa settlement was coupled with possession, the defendants are not entitled to challenge the settlement of Aminulla after 12 years from the time of preparation of RS khatian. He further submits that the defendants fails to prove that Aminulla the predecessor of the plaintiff are in permissive possession of some land was not prove either in the earlier suit or in the present suit. So, the auction was not effective and hence the defendants did not acquire any,title in the land allegedly sold in auction. He finally submits that the application regarding the additional evidence as provided under Order XLI, rule 27 of the Code of Civil Procedure prescribed that the need for additional evidence must be felt by the court itself. This provision of law is clearly not intended to allow a litigant who has been unsuccessful in the lower court to fill up the omission. In this respect he referred to a decision reported in 36 DLR (AD) 220 and accordingly prayed for discharged of the Rule.

18. The points for determination is that whether the court of appeal below committed any error of law in decreeing the suit which caused any failure of justice.

19. Before considering the respective contentions of the learned Advocates, I like to take up to issue whether the concurrent findings of both the courts below are based on materials and evidence on record.

20. It appears that the trial court dismissed the suit on the findings that—

“বাদীপক্ষ ৫ম মুন্সেফী আদালতের অপর ৩৯/৫০ নং মামলা এবং ৩৯/৫০ নং মামলা হইতে উদ্ভুত অপর জারি মামলা ১৮/৫৩ নং মামলায় বাদীগনের পূর্ববর্তীর নামীয় সমন নোটিশ জারি হয় নাই মর্মে দাবী করিয়াছে। পক্ষান্তরে বিবাদীপক্ষের দাবী হচ্ছে বাদীগন, উপযুক্ত সমন নোটিশ প্রাপ্ত হইয়াছে। বাদীপক্ষ দাবীর সমর্থনে সাক্ষ্য প্রদান করিয়াছে। কিন্তু বিবাদীপক্ষ উপযুক্ত অপর ৩৯/৫০ নং মামলার মুলনথি তলব করিয়া সমন জারির বিষয় প্রমান করে না।”

But the trial court miserably failed to appreciate and consider the order No.6 dated 22-1951 passed in Other Suit No. 39 of 1958 which, clearly proved that summons were duly served upon the defendants and defendant Nos. 1 and 2 prayed for one month time to file written statement and thereafter the defendants filed written statement and contested the suit. Thus it is evident that such finding of the trial court is apparently erroneous and not based on the material and evidence on record.

21. It further appears that earlier the suit land was partitioned in Partition Suit No. 39 of 1950, which was filed by the predecessor of the present defendants against the predecessor of the present plaintiffs, Aminulla and others and got a decree. In support of their claim defendants exhibited the preliminary decree (Exhibit-Ka), final decree with Advocate Commissioner report (Exhibit-kha), certified copy of the order sheet of original Execution Case No. 18 of 1953, Sale Certificate dated 8-4-1954 (Exhibit-Gha), certificate of delivery of possession dated 11-4-1957 (Exhibit-Ga) and kabala No. 3139 dated 5-6-1951 in favour of defendant No. 1.  But both the courts below failed to consider those documents of the defendants and erroneously found that by the said documents the defendants, present petitioners did not get any decree in the said suit.

22. It also appears that the predecessor of the present defendant filed Title Suit No. 53 of 1968 against the present plaintiffs and in that title suit defendant appeared and filed written statement and said suit was decreed on compromise and accordingly compromise decree was drawn. To prove such facts the present defendants filed the application for compromise (Exhibit-Ja) and the sole decree (Exhibit-Ja(1) respectively, wherefrom it is evident that three sons of Aminulla executed the said solenama, but both the courts below failed to consider such vital aspect of the case and erroneously found that the defendants could not prove the said facts. It further transpires that the defendants filed an applications before the appellate court on 13-6-2010 for calling for the records of Title Suit No. 53 of 1968, Title Suit No. 39 of 1950 and Execution Case No. 18 of 1953. The appellate court heard this application and rejected the same by order No. 17 dated 14-7-2010 on the ground that— “আপীলকারী বিবাদীপক্ষে আনীত দরখাস্তটি অনাবশ্যক বিধায় আপাতত না মঞ্জুর করা হইল, তবে অত্র মোকদ্দমার আপীল শুনানীঅন্তে উক্ত দরখাস্তের বিষয়বস্তু বিবেচনাযোগ্য।

23. But it transpires that at time of hearing of the appeal although the preliminary and final decree with Advocate Commissioner report (Exhibit- Ka and Kha) was considered but the compromise petition and decree passed in Title Suit No. 53 of 1968 Exhibit Nos. Ja and Ja(1) were not considered but erroneously found that the appellants could not prove the those documents by sufficient evidence. Although the positive case of the defendants was that the predecessor of the plaintiffs was in permissive possession of the defendants and further that the compromise decree passed in Other Suit No. 53 of 1968 has been upheld. Since the appellate court failed to consider all those documents filed before the appellate court at the time of hearing of the appeal and when the appellate court rejected the application of the defendant observing that all those documents will be considered and dealt with at the time of hearing of the appeal.

24. It also appears that the defendants of the present suit claimed that the predecessors of the plaintiffs compromised the Title Suit No. 53 of 1968 by filing Solenama by which the plaintiffs admitted the right of the defendants-petitioners in the suit lands. Hence the plaintiffs had no cause of action in the present suit, which was denied by the plaintiffs. Normally, the onus of proof lies on the person who assert that the sole-decree had obtained by fraud. The onus of proving fraud was thus clearly on the plaintiffs and it was not the duty of the defendants to disprove the existence of fraud or collusion in anticipation of any case made out by the plaintiffs themselves. In this view of the matter, the courts below were totally wrong in taking view that the defendants failed to proved by calling of the records of earlier suit and erroneously found that summons were not duly served upon the predecessors of the plaintiffs in earlier two suits.

25. In this revision the defendant-petitioners have filed an application under Order XLI, rule 27 of the Code of Civil Procedure for additional evidence annexing certified copy of entire order sheets of Title Suit No. 53 of 1968 and also written statement dated 10-3-1969 filed in the said suit by the defendants Tajul Huda and other, predecessors of the present plaintiffs, for declaration of title and recovery of khas possession filed by the predecessors of the present defendants, Abdul Munayam.

26. The learned Advocate for the defendants petitioners strenuously argued that the High Court Division conferred wide power in order to do justice in a case and it shows that in the instant case the appellate court failed to exhibits the aforesaid vital documents although the same was also filed before the appellate court but those documents were not considered at the time of hearing of the appeal. After consideration and appreciation of the materials and evidence on record it appears that the documents and papers filed by the defendants-petitioners are very much necessary for proper adjudication of the suit. It is, however, felt that ends of justice will be meet if both the parties should be given opportunity to prove their case by filing those documents in appellate court. In this connection reference is made to the case of Sunil Krishna Banki vs Kailash Chandra Saha reported in 36 DLR (AD) 220. Since the court below totally misread and non-considered the Exhibits namely, Exhibit Nos. Ka to Umo, Exhibit Nos. Ja and J(1) and also did not call for the record of the Title Suit No. 53 of 1968 which is very much material to consider that whether the present defendants, the plaintiffs of Title Suit No. 53 of 1968 obtain any decree fraudulently against the predecessors of the present plaintiffs. The opposite parties has filed the present Other Suit No. 92 of 1991 137 of 2001 seeking, firstly prayed for declaration that both preliminary and the final decree passed in Partition Suit No. 39 of 1950 and also the decree passed in Title Suit No. 53 of 1968 are illegal collusive and fraudulent, Secondly, the BS khatian No. 693 and 695 are wrong and baseless and also for partition of total 0.90 acres land claiming entire 0.64 1/4 acres which was partitioned in Partition Suit No. 39 of 1950. In that suit the predecessors of the defendant Nos. 1-2, Md Abdul Monayem was the plaintiff and predecessors of the present plaintiffs Aminullah was the defendant.

27. On going through the materials on record it is apparent that the heirs of the defendant of the earlier suit were all out to deprive the plaintiff of the said suit of the fruit of the decree and as last resort has filed the present Other Suit No. 92 of 1991 on 28-9-1991 after 41 years of the first suit and 23 years of the second suit seeking the relief primarily by way ul setting aside the decrees that were passed in those two suits under the shadow of the relief seeking separate saham in respect of the schedule land. It is seen from the materials on record and admitted by the plaintiffs of the present suit that the land which was the subject matter of Partition Suit No. 39 of 1950 and Title Suit No. 53 of 1968 has also been made subject matter of present Other Suit No, 92 of 1991.

28. It is not disputed from the side of the plaintiffs that relief sought for in Other Suit No. 92 of 1991 relates to seeking set aside the decree passed in Partition Suit No. 39 of 1950 and Title Suit No. 53 of 1968 but the courts below failed to frame any issue whether the decisions made in the former suits operates as res-judicata in the present suit.

<u>29. In the background of the facts stated herein before and the discussions made above, I am of view that for proper and effective adjudication of the suit a issue should be framed by the appellate court to determine this point whether the suit is barred under the principles of res-judicata.</u>

30. It appears that in respect of the suit land preliminary and final decree was passed on 11-8-1953 in Partition Suit No. 39 of 1950 and the defendants took possession of 34 2/7 acres of their saham on 20-6-1956 though court in Execution Case No. 18 of 1953. Thus after passing of the final decree in the said partition suit between the same parties, the second suit filed by the plaintiffs after 41 years is not maintainable and is barred by limitation. So, the decisions referred by the learned Advocate for the opposite parties reported in 32 DLR (AD) 167 is not applicable in the present case. In the present suit, the plaintiffs have miserably failed to prove that the decree obtained fraudulently in the earlier suits being Partition Suit No. 39 of 1950 and Other Suit No. 53 of 1968 against the predecessors of the present plaintiffs and that the plaintiffs also failed to prove that the summons were not duly served upon them in earlier suits. Further, both the courts below failed to consider that most of the title deeds of the present defendants are 30 years old documents, but without considering this legal aspect of the suit, the courts below erroneously passed the decree declaring that those documents are forged documents.

31. I find that the lower appellate court has passed the impugned judgment without giving any specific finding in respect of those Exhibits. Since both the courts below failed to found that the defendants derived right, title and interest in the suit land on the basis of the decree passed in the earlier suits which seriously prejudiced the defendants. I have meticulously examined the oral and documentary evidence and relevant provisions of law and find that the court of appeal below failed to consider those materials evidence on record and committed error in law, in decreeing the suit.

32. In the present case it must be noted that the evidence offered by the defendants to prove that the plaintiffs were no longer a co-sharer was already produced before the trial court, but the evidence was not considered by the trial court. On the other hand, the documents referred to in their application for additional evidence could if considered according to the defendants, have shown that the plaintiffs had ceased to be co-shares, particularly when the necessary issue to determine this point has to be framed by the trial court.

33. Learned Advocate for the opposite party vehemently submits that since the predecessors of the plaintiff being a korfa lessee and continued in possession of the suit land and RS khatian was prepared in his name, so he acquired title in the suit land. This submission is absolutely fallacious in as much as the RS khatian are not document of title and that the khatians, if at all, record the possession and not title to the land.

34. In the present suit RS khatian was wrongly prepared in the name of the predecessors in the defendants although BS khatian was rightly recorded in the name of the predecessors of the plaintiffs.

35. In the event of conflict between the old record of right and the recent record of right, the recent record of right would prevail in as much as presumption of the record of right loses its weight with the passage of time and entries in the subsequent khatian would be mere acceptable to a court than the entries in the earlier khatian. In the case of assessment of relative value of two khatians, the latest khatian should prevail over the earlier khatian. Support of this proposition of law is sought to be drawn from in the case of Abdul Hamid vs Abul Hossain Mir being dead his heirs, Abdus Sobhan Mir reported in 35 DLR 295.

<u>36. In the suit plaintiffs based their claim as korfa lessee and RS record but they did not file any lessee deed to prove their claim and on the other hand defendant claimed their title on the basis of several deeds, starting from the year 1895, 1940, 1942. This is a well established principle of law that a registered kabala is an evidence of title which will prevail over the other records of rights as such until and unless such kabala is cancelled on specific allegation of fraud by any civil court in an appropriate civil suit. Reliance may be placed in case of Mr Sultanuddin. Chowdhury vs Government of People's Republic of Bangladesh reported in 32 DLR 252.</u>

I have gone through the decisions reported in 32 DLR 163 and 19 DLR (SC) 433 as cited by the learned Advocate for the opposite party, those decisions have no manner of application so far the points involved in this case.

37. The learned Advocate for both the parties has referred good number of decisions, since I proposed to send back the case on remand to the appellate court for re-trial. I do not like to discuss about each and every decisions referred by the learned Advocate of the parties.

38. In view of the above, the impugned judgment and decree. dated 9-9-2010 passed by the learned Additional District Judge, First Court, Chittagong dismissed the Other Appeal No. 16 of 2009 is set aside and the case is sent back to the appellate court for fresh trial and for disposal of the same in accordance with law in the light of observation as made above after giving the parties opportunity to take necessary steps to examine necessary witnesses and then to dispose of the suit at an early date in accordance with law.

39. In the result, the rule is made absolute without any order as to costs.

40. The learned Additional District Judge, First Court, Chittagong is directed to dispose of the appeal within a period of three months from the date of receipt of the records from this court. The appellate court is further directed not to grant any adjournment to either of the parties except on very urgent reason since the matter is an old one.

41. The order of stay granted at the time of issuance of the Rule is hereby vacated.

Send down the lower court records at once.

End.
