full_judgment:
On an application under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure, this Rule was issued calling upon the opposite party Nos. 1-7 to show cause as to why the impugned judgment and decree dated 14-1-2016 passed by the learned District Judge, Munshigonj in Title Appeal No. 126 of 2012 affirming the judgment and decree dated 25-9-2012 passed by the learned Senior Assistant Judge (In charge), Munshigonj in Title Suit No. 48 of 2008 dismissing the suit should not be set aside and/or pass such other or further order or orders as to this Court may seem fit and proper.

2. Facts relevant for disposal of this Rule, in short, are that the petitioners, as plaintiff, instituted Title Suit No. 48 of 2008 in the court of Senior Assistant Judge (In-charge), Munshigonj against the opposite party Nos. 1-9, as defendant for declaration of Title and SA Khatian No. 120, RS khatian No. 141 to be declared wrong and without any legal basis stating inter alia, that the property measuring 52 decimals covered by CS and SA plot No. 601 corresponding to RS plot No. 696 of Mouza-Atigaon, originally belonged to one Rojonikanto Bhattracharya who transferred the property to one Monindra Lal Talukder by a patta. While said Monindra Lal Talukder was in possession and enjoyment of the same he transferred the schedule land to one Yunus Mollick and Jalal Uddin Mollick by a registered deed of sale No. 961 dated 16-3-1948. Said Yunus Mollick was in possession and enjoyment in the half share of the property measuring 26 decimals who subsequently, transferred his share by way of settlement to one Abdul Latif Bepari on 2nd Chaitra, 1355 BS Said Abdul Latif Bepari while in possession and enjoyment of the property by way of settlement from Yunus Mollick, by a registered deed No. 1775 dated 30-3-1956 transferred the suit property along with other non-suited property to Most. Ashura Khatun, Harun Or Rashid Mollick and Joynal Abedin. The said Ashura Khatun died issueless and her brother Brigadier (Rtd.) Moniruzzaman Khan succeeded her. Said Harun Or Rashid died leaving behind the plaintiff Nos. 8-13 and Joynal Abedin died leaving behind the plaintiff Nos. 1-7. While the plaintiffs went to the Tahsil office on 17-3-2008 for payment of rent for the suit property came to know that SA and RS Khatian stand recorded in the name of the predecessor of the defendants wrongly and for such wrong entry in the khatian title of the plaintiffs have become clouded, hence, the present suit for declaration.

3. The defendant-opposite parties contested the suit by filing written statement contending inter alia, that the property in question originally belonged to Rojonikanto Bhatracharya who transferred the same to one Monindra Lal Talukder and the said Monindra Lal Talukder by a registered sale deed No. 961 dated 16-3-1948 transferred the suit property to Yunus Mollick and Jalal Uddin Mollick in equal share. The said Jalal Uddin Mollick transferred his share in the property in favour his wife Arjumonnessa before SA operation. Accordingly, SA and RS khatian correctly recorded in the name of Yunus Mollick and Arjumonnessa. Arjumonnessa died leaving defendant Nos. 2-7 and Yunus Mollick died leaving defendant No. 1, they have been possessing the suit land amicably and the defendant No. 1 mutated her name in RS Khatian and has been possessing the suit land on payment of rent to the government. The plaintiffs have no right, title, interest and possession in the suit property, hence, the suit is liable to be dismissed.

4. The trial court framed as many as five issues for determination of the dispute between the parties. In course of hearing the plaintiffs examined four witnesses as PWs and the defendant examined two witnesses as DWs. Both the parties filed documents in support of their claim in suit which were duly marked as exhibits. The trial court upon hearing the parties dismissed the suit on contest finding that the plaintiffs could not prove their title as well as possession in the suit property by its judgment and decree dated 25-9-2012.

5. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the judgment and decree of the trial court, the plaintiffs preferred Title Appeal No. 126 of 2012 before the learned District Judge, Munshigonj who upon hearing disallowed the appeal on contest by the impugned judgment and decree dated 14-1-2016. At this juncture, the plaintiff-appellant-petitioners moved this Court by filing this revisional application under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure and obtained the present Rule and order of stay.

6. Mr AJ Mohammad Ali, Senior Advocate with Mr Shahjada Al Amin Kabir, learned Advocates appearing for the petitioners at the very outset submit that admittedly, the suit property originally belonged to Rojonikanto Bhattacharya. CS khatian stands recorded in his name. The said Rojonikanto Bhattacharya permanently settled the suit property along with other non-suited property to one Monindra Lal Talukder by a Patta and the said Monindra Lal Talukder by a registered sale deed No. 961 dated 16-3-1948 transferred the suit property to one Yunus Mollick and another Jalal Uddin Mollick in equal share. There is no dispute between the parties regarding title of Yunus Mollick and Jalal Uddin Mollick. But both the courts below by making a 3rd case most unfortunately held that the parties to the suit could not satisfy the court how Monindra Lal Talukder acquired the property from CS recorded owner. As such, both the courts below travelled beyond their jurisdiction in deciding title of Monindra Lal Talukder which was not a matter to be determined by the court below.

7. Mr Ali further submits that title deed of Yunus Mollick and Jalal Uddin Mollick is of the year 1948 more than 30 years old document which was filed in original by the defendant in suit (exhibit-Ga). As per section 90 of the Evidence Act the said deed has a strong presumptive value as the same is not required to be formally proved, but both the courts below without assigning any reason what-soever unfortunately found that Yunus Mollick and Jalal Uddin Mollick did not acquire any title in the suit property in the absence of any explanation how Monindra Lal Talukder acquired the property from CS recorded owner. He further submits that Yunus Mollick settled his share in the property in favour of one Abdul Latif Bepari on 2nd Chaitra, 1355 BS. In support of which the plaintiffs submitted counterfoil of the rent receipt showing payment of rent to Yunus Mollick by Abdul Latif Bepari (exhibits-3 and 3ka). But the court below instead of finding genuineness of the exhibites-3 and 3ka unfortunately held that the said document generally should be remained with the owner of the property Yunus Mollick how the said document could be produced by the tenant under Yunus Mollick. He further goes to argue that the question before the court whether Abdul Latif Bepari got the property by way of settlement from Yunus Mollick and the document exhibits-3 and 3ka prove that Yunus Mollick accepted rent from Abdul Latif Bepari by issuing rent receipt to him. Mr Ali further goes to submit that Abdul Latif Bepari while in possession and enjoyment of the property by way of settlement from Yunus Mollick transferred the same to Most. Ashura Khatun, Harun-or-Rashid Mollick and Joynal Abedin the predecessor of the plaintiffs by a registered sale deed No. 1775 dated 30-3-1956 (exhibit-5).

8. The trial court observed that the said deed of sale has not been proved by the plaintiffs by calling the concern volume form the registry office and as such, the plaintiffs could not prove their title in the property by the aforesaid sale deed. In this regard he submits that in the absence of any contrary thing a registered document cannot be disbelieved by the court that it was not duly executed and registered and by the said deed the property was not transferred. Moreover, the deed in question of the year 1956 and an old document acquired a presumptive value under the law since nothing could produce from defence side contrary to the document of the plaintiffs. However, before the appellate court the plaintiff-appellants filed an application for calling the concern volume of the deed in question from the registry office. The appellate court upon hearing rejected the application on 17-9-2015 holding that since the learned Advocate for the respondent admitted the existence of the sale deed dated 30-3-1956 there is no need to call the volume of the deed from the registry office. Therefore, the appellate court ought to have found that the deed of the year 1956 exhibit-5 is a valid deed and by the said deed the plaintiffs acquired title through their predecessor. He further submits that mere record of right in the name of some person does not ipso facto create title in their favour. But the court below relying on the record of right in the name of defendant and also observing that the plaintiffs could not prove their possession in the property, dismissed the suit as well as disallowed the appeal.

9. Mr Mohammad Ahasan, with Mr SM Ariful Islam, learned Advocates appearing for the opposite parties submit that there is no dispute that the properties belonged to Yunus Mollick and Jalal Uddin Mollick by purchase in the year 1948. But the fact is that Yunus Mollick never transferred his share in the property to Abdul Latif Bepari or anybody by way of settlement as alleged by the plaintiffs. He further submits that in the absence of any valid deed or documents showing settlement in favour of Abdul Latif Bepari, said Abdul Latif Bepari cannot transfer the property to Most. Ashura Khatun and two others. As such, by the deed dated 30-3-1956 the predecessor of the plaintiffs did not acquire any title in the property in question and both the courts below rightly held that the plaintiffs could not prove their title by producing any valid document. He further argued that the plaintiffs filed two counterfoils of rent receipt to prove settlement in favour of Abdul Latif Bepari showing that Yunus Mollick on receipt of rent issued rent receipt in favour of Abdul Latif Bepari. But the plaintiffs could not produce any rent receipt issued to Abdul Latif Bepari and as such, both the courts below rightly observed that it is not at all conceivable by any means that a tenant can hold a counterfoil of rent receipt issued by his landlord Yunus Mollick.

10. Mr Ahasan further submits that the sale deed dated 30-3-1956 exhibit-5 is a certified copy obtained by the plaintiffs from the concern registry office on 19-3-2008 and the plaintiffs did not prove the said document by calling respective volume from the concern registry office. Moreover, the plaintiffs failed to prove that the suit property was settled by Yunus Mollick in favour of Abdul Latif Bepari. As such, by the said deed executed by Addul Latif Bepari the predecessor of the plaintiffs did not acquire any title in the property. He further submits that in the absence of any valid document of transfer of the property in favour of Abdul Latif Bepari, the plaintiffs cannot say that said Abdul Latif Bepari acquired title in the property to be sold to the predecessor of the plaintiffs. He further submits that the defendant No. 1 as daughter of Yunus Mollick inherited the property and accordingly, SA and RS khatians stand recorded in the name of Yunus Mollick with the wife of another owner Jalal Uddin Mollick. He further goes to submit that the relevant khatian of the property, payment of rent by the defendant proved that the defendants acquired title in the property by inheritance and have been possessing the suit property more than statutory period of limitation on payment of rents to the government. As such, both the courts below rightly found that the plaintiffs by any evidence both oral and documentary could not prove their title and possession in the suit property. Finally, he submits that this is a suit for simple declaration and both the courts below concurrently found that the plaintiffs could not prove their possession in the property, as such, the suit is not maintainable in its present form without prayer for recovery of possession. 11. Heard the learned Advocates for both the parties, have gone through the revisional application, plaint, written statement, evidences both oral and documentary adduced and marked as exhibits before the trial court and impugned judgment and decree of both the courts below.

12. From perusal of plaint and written statement, it appears that both the parties unequivocally admitted and declared that the property in question, originally belonged to Yunus Mollick and Jalal Uddin Mollick by purchase vide sale deed No. 961 dated 16-3-1948. Both the courts below in finding title of Yunus Mollick and Jalal Uddin Mollick observed that the said two persons purchased the property from one Monindra Lal Talukder, but both the parties to the suit in their plaint and written statement failed to give any explanation or fact how Monindra Lal Talukder acquired the property from CS recorded owner. I have gone through the registered deed No. 961 dated 16-3-1948 filed in original by the defendant No. 1 (exhibit-Ga) and a certified copy of the same by the plaintiff (exhibit-4) and from perusal of both the exhibits it appears that in the recital of the said deed it has been clearly mentioned that Monindra Lal Talukder acquired the property by way of permanent settlement by a registered patta dated 25 Magh 1344 corresponding to 8-2-1938. But this pertinent facts missed the notices of the trial court as well as appellate court below.

13. Moreover, where there is no dispute between the parties regarding acquisition of title by Yunus Mollick and Jalal Uddin Mollick why the trial court as well as the appellate court shall decide a question not raised before it by any party whatsoever. Therefore, this Court finds that the findings and observation of the courts below in respect of acquisition of title by Monindra, thereafter, by Yunus Mollick and Jalal Uddin Mollick is totally contrary to the actual state of affairs. The trial court as well as the appellate court in deciding title of Abdul Latif Bepari in the suit property held that the plaintiffs could not produce any document showing settlement of the property in favour of Abdul Latif Bepari by Yunus Mollick, but they could file two counterfoils of rent receipt exhibit-3 and 3ka which ought to have remained in the possession of Yunus Mollick as Zaminder and this cannot come before the court from the custody of the plaintiffs as their vendor Abdul Latif Bepari was a tenant under Yunus Mollick and also held that Abdul Latif Bepari did not acquire any title in the absence of any patta and he could not transfer the property to Most. Ashura Khatun and two others by a registered deed dated 30-3-1956 (exhibit-5). I have gone through the (exhibit-3 and 3ka), it appears that the suit property was settled by Yunus Mollick in favour of Abdul Latif Bepari on 2nd Chaitra, 1355 BS.

14. From perusal of registered deed No. 1775 dated 30-3-1956 it appears that the recipient No. 1 of the deed Most. Ashura Khatun is the wife of Yunus Mollick, recipient Nos. 2 and 3 Harun Or Rashid Mollick and Joynal Abedin are nephews of Yunus Mollick and in the said deed Yunus Mollick and Jalal Uddin Mollick who are admittedly owners of the property by purchase from Monindra Lal Talukder are attesting witnessess. Though an attesting witness is not bound by the contents of the deed, but in the present case Yunus Mollick knowing fully well that Abdul Latif Bepari is the owner of the property by settlement transferred the same to his wife Ashura Khatun and nephews Harun Or Rashid Mollick and Joynal Abedin. Therefore, daughter of Yunus Mollick as well as heirs of Arjumonnessa wife of Jalal Uddin Mollick cannot deny existence of settlement made by Yunus Mollick in favour of Abdul Latif Bepari and the transfer made by Abdul Latif Bepari in favour of Ashura Khatun and two others.

15. Both the courts below while dismissing the suit as well as disallowing the appeal failed to consider those documentary evidences produced by the parties to the suit in its true perspective and without going through the contents of the exhibits most unfortunately disbelieved the exhibits 4 and 5 both are registered document of the year 1948 and 1956, more than 30 years old. Apart from this, this Court finds that the observations and finding of both the courts below are totally contrary to the actual state of affair and based on serious misconstruction of the evidence and misconception of law. The trial court as well as the appellate court concurrently held that Yunus Mollick and Jalal Uddin Mollick did not acquire title in the property by the deed from Monindra Lal Talukder in the absence of any explanation how Monindra Lal Talukder acquired the property, which also goes against the defendants in suit. But they did not prefer any appeal against the judgment of the trial court as well as any revision against the judgment and decree of the appellate court. In this situation, question may arise how the defendant-opposite parties can defend themself before the appellate court as well as this Court where their title also negated by the judgment and decree of both the courts below.

16. In this precarious situation, this Court is to observe that this suit is of the plaintiffs not the defendants and according to law the plaintiffs are to prove their case and no benefit can be taken from the weakness of the defence. Where the plaintiffs by submitting documentary evidences namely, registered kabala dated 16-3-1948 and registered kabala dated 30-3-1956 could establish that the property owned by Yunus Mollick thereafter, Abdul Latif Bepari and lastly, by Ashura Khatun, Harun Or Rashid and Joynal Abedin the suit property ought to have recorded in the names of Ashura Khatun and two others but the property stands recorded in the name of Yunus Mollick who happens to be the husband of Ashura Khatun and vendor of Abdul Latif Bepari. Recording of name of Yunus Mollick in SA and RS khatian, in my opinion, is not so fatal because Yunus Mollick was the vendor of Abdul Latif from whom Ahsura Khatun and two others purchased the same. And, for such recording, it cannot be said that Yunus Mollick never transferred the property to anybody or the defendant No. 1 acquired any title in the property on the basis of record of right. Both the courts below failed to notice the fact that mere recording of khatian in the name of vendor does not ipso facto create title in favour of the defendant No. 1 or any other defendants. It is also found that the defendant No. 1 got her name mutated in the khatian as her father's name was appearing in the record of right. Mere mutation in the khatian also cannot create any title in favour of any person without any basis.

<u>17. In the present case the plaintiffs could able to prove their title, right from Monindra Lal Talukder to Ashura Khatun and two others by successive transfers vide exhibites-3, 3ka, 4 and 5. Therefore, the trial court ought to have decreed the suit and the appellate court also misdirected himself in not considering the evidences both oral and documentary. I have gone through the evidences adduced by the parties as PWs and DWs. Though the PWs could not specifically tell the boundary of the property as well as the quantum of land in the plot it does not mean that the plaintiffs are not in possession as well as the DWs also could not substantiate their claim by oral evidence that they have been possessing the same specifically, exclusively ousting the plaintiffs in suit. Where the plaintiffs could prove their title in the suit property and in the absence of clear evidence and exclusive possession of the defendants in the suit property the plaintiffs need not pray for any consequential relief by way of recovery of possession.</u>

18. In view of the above, this Court finds that both the courts below committed an error of law in dismissing the suit as well as disallowing the appeal calling interference by this Court.

19. Taking into consideration the above, I find merit in the Rule as well as in the sub-missions of the learned Advocate for the petitioners.

20. In the result, the Rule is made absolute, however, without any order as to costs.

21. The impugned judgment and decreed dated 14-1-2016 passed by the learned District Judge, Munshigonj in Title Appeal No. 126 of 2012 affirming the judgment and decree dated 25-9-2012 passed by the Senior Assistant Judge (In-charge), Munshigonj, in Title Suit No. 48 of 2008 are hereby set aside. Title Suit No. 48 of 2008 is hereby decreed in favour of the plaintiffs.

22. The Order of stay granted at the time of issuance of the Rule stands vacated.

Communicate a copy of this judgment to the court concerned and send down the lower court records at once.

End.

parties:

VS
Asis Bewa and others -------- Plaintiff-Appellant-Opposite Parties
full_judgment:
This Rule has been issued calling upon the opposite parties, to show cause as to why the impugned judgment and decree dated 12-2-2014 (decree signed on 17-2-2014), passed by the learned Additional District Judge, Gaibanda, in Other Appeal No.41 of 2013, allowing the appeal and reversing the judgment and decree dated 28-4-2013 (decree signed on 5-5-2013), passed by the learned Joint District Judge, 1st Court, Gaibanda, in Other Suit No.8 of 2003, should not be set-aside and/or pass such other order or orders passed as to this Court may seem fit and proper.

2. Facts, relevant for disposal of the Rule, in brief, are that one Most Asia Khatun and others, as plaintiffs, filed Other Suit No. 20 of 2002, subsequently re-numbered as 8 of 2003, against Md Azadul Islam and others, impleaded as defendants, with a prayer for declaration of title and permanent injunction, in respect of the schedule property. However, the plaintiffs have subsequently dropped the prayer as regards declaration of title in the suit property. Hence, the suit remains to be one for permanent injunction, and, evidently, the defendant did not challenge this amendment of the plaint.

3. Be that as it may, the defendants Nos. 6-8/11/13/20/24-26 have filed written statements and contested in the suit.

4. I have gone through the pleadings of the parties which need not be reproduced here.

5. The Trial Court, after hearing the parties and assessing the evidence on record, dismissed the suit by his judgment and decree dated 28-4-2013 (decree signed on 5-5-2013).

6. Against the said judgment and decree of the Trial Court, the plaintiff-appellant-opposite parties, preferred Other Appeal No.41 of 2013 (as appellants) before the District Judge, Gaibanda, which was heard by the learned Additional District Judge, Gaibanda, who being the Appellate Court, has passed the impugned judgment and decree, allowing the appeal by setting aside the judgment and decree of the trial court, vide judgment and decree dated 12-2-2014 (decree signed on 17-2-2014).

7. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the judgment and decree of the Appellate Court, the Defendant-Respondent-Petitioners filed this application under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure and obtained the present Rule.

8. Learned Senior Counsel Mr Mohammad Jamiruddin Sircar with learned Advocate Mr AHM Abdul Wahab appeared for the petitioners. Mr Sircar has placed the petition. He first of all submits that, the trial court having properly assessed the evidence on record, had come to the correct findings as regards the facts and circumstances of this case, which ought not to have been set-aside by the appellate court. He also submits that, the trial court has rightly found that, the genology placed by the heirs of late Azizur Rahman (predecessor of the defendant) was not correct and that, the CS khatain No. 122 Ext. 1 does not support the plaintiff's case of taking grant (patton) from Kosir Uddin, who had the superior rent receiving interest in the suit property. He next submits that, the findings of the trial court has been wrongly set-aside by the appellate court without applying the judicial mind or assessing the evidence on record. He, making reference to the judgment of the appellate court as well as to the CS khatain No. 1, also submits that the plaintiff could not prove their prima-facie title in the suit land in as much as Vomor Ali Sarker is entitled to get 59 decimals of land as per CS khatain, but the plaintiffs have made out a case of obtaining kabuliat for 90 decimals of land in the suit property, which is in excess of the land owned by Kosir Uddin, who was son of Vomor Ali Sarker. In support of his contention, he has referred a decision reported in 8 MLR (AD) 41 = 55 DLR (AD) 9: between Sushil Kumar Paik vs Harendra Nath Samadder. He further submits that, the plaintiffs have submitted certain documents purported to be the kabuliat dakhila in support of the alleged kabuliat to prove their title in the suit property, but the court cannot take the same into consideration, vide the decision reported in 51 DLR (AD) 150: between Chandan Mondal Kushal Nath Mondal vs Abdus Samad Talukder. But, the appellate court has totally ignored the law declared in the said decision and thereby passed the impugned judgment and decree and has committed serious error of law in passing the impugned decision occasioning failure of justice and, therefore, the impugned judgment and decree passed by the appellate court are liable to be set-aside and the judgment and decree passed by the trial court may be upheld, he prayed for.

9. Mr Bivash Chandra Biswas along with Mr Mrinal Kanti Biswas, learned Advocates appeared for the opposite parties. Mr Bivash Chandra Biswas, on the contrary, submits that, this is a case for permanent injunction in which the question of proof of title does not at all arise. The learned Advocate submits that, the question of title may be looked into incidentally in a suit for permanent injunction. He submits that, the plaintiffs have filed RS khatian No. 147 showing 16 annas lands in the suit plot No. 796 and 830/1685, comprising 98 decimals of land, and the said khatian is in the name of predecessor of the plaintiffs, but the other side (defendants) did not challenge the said khatians and the presumption of the validity of the said khatians remains un-rebutted and this proves the prima-facie basis of the plaintiff's acquiring and remaining possession of the suit land. He next submits that, the schedule "Ka" to the plaint correctly described the land shown in the SA khatian No. 147 of Mouza Sathalia, PS Saghata, under District- Gaibanda. He further submits that, the plaintiffs have proved their case by adducing PW 1, who has deposed in support of the plaintiff's case and proved the documentary evidence including aforesaid khatian, to support their prima-facie case regarding the plaintiff's lawful possession in the suit land. PW 1 was then corroborated by PWs 2 and 3. He next submits, the defendants did not cross examine these PW Nos. 2 and 3, nor did the defendants adduce any witness to prove their positive case. He also submits that, the appellate court has pointed out all these aspects of this case and has rightly passed the impugned judgment and decree, which calls for no interference by this revisional Court. In support of his contention, he has referred to the decisions reported in 1986 BLD 155: between Pasharuddin Mir vs Ismail Mir, 4 BLD (AD) 285: between Manindar Nath Sen Sarma vs Bangladesh, 9 BLD 368 = 42 DLR 408: between Sheikh Ahmed vs Abdul Alim and also the decision reported in 56 DLR (AD) 53: between Government of Bangladesh, represented by the Additional Deputy Commissioner, Gazipur vs AKM Abdul Hye. In these decisions, referred to above, the superior Court has confirmed the presumption of the validity attached to RS khatain as per section 144A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950, and also held that, failure to prove the title in a case for permanent injunction will not disentitle the plaintiff to get permanent injunction, if they prove their exclusive possession in the suit property. He proceeds on that, the impugned judgment and decree passed by the appellate court suffers from no illegality or from any other lacuna, whatsoever, and this Rule has no merit and the same may be discharged.

10. I have heard the learned Advocates for both sides, perused the application for revision, lower Court's record as well as the judgment of both the Courts below and other materials in the record.

11. This is a case for permanent injunction, in which the question of declaration of title does not at all arise, though the question of title should be looked into incidentally, to satisfy the court about the basis of the lawful possession of the plaintiff (as opposed to the possession of a trespasser or land grabber).

12. I find that, RS khatian No. 147, shows 16 annas lands of the suit plot No. 796 and 830/1685, comprises 98 decimals of land, and that the said khatian is in the name of predecessors of the plaintiffs, but the other side (defendants) did not challenge the legality or correctness of the same and the presumption of the validity of these khatian remains un-rebutted. The schedule "Ka" to the plaint has correctly described the land shown in the SA khatian No. 147 of Mouza Sathalia, PS Saghata under District-Gaibanda.

13. I also find that, the plaintiffs have proved their case by adducing PW 1, who has deposed in support of the plaintiff's case and proved the documentary evidence including aforesaid khatians to support their prima-facie case regarding their lawful possession in the suit land and he was corroborated by PWs 2 and 3, but the defendants did not cross examine these PW Nos. 2 and 3, nor did they adduce witness to prove their positive case.

14. I also find that, the appellate court has pointed out and discussed all these aspects of this case and has rightly passed the impugned judgment and decree, which call for no interference by this revisional Court.

<u>15. I am also of opinion that, in a suit for permanent injunction, this Court should satisfy itself as regards the lawful nature of the plaintiffs' possession. In a suit for permanent injunction, the issue regarding title need not be and should not be conclusively decided, because the purpose of granting the relief of permanent injunction is to prevent forceful ouster of an apparently lawful occupant of the suit property, thereby disapproving the act of taking law into the defendants own hands. Nonetheless, the court should incidentally look into the title or other lawful basis of the plaintiffs acquiring and continuing in possession, to satisfy itself that the plaintiff is not an usurper or trespasser or a land grabber and that he has come in clean hands. Therefore, decree in a suit for permanent injunction will not operate as res-judicata, in a subsequent suit, so far as the issue of title is concerned.</u>

16. With these findings and observations, I find that, the impugned judgment and decree passed by the appellate court suffers from no illegality, nor from any other lacuna whatsoever, and this Rule has no merit and the same should be discharged.

Order

In the result, the Rule is discharged. The impugned judgment and decree dated 12-2-2014 (decree signed on 17-2-2014), passed by the learned Additional District Judge, Gaibanda, in Other Appeal No.41 of 2013 is hereby upheld. The order of stay granted earlier by this Court is hereby vacated.

No costs.

Let a copy of this judgment along with the Lower Court's Record be sent down to the concerned Courts at once.

End.

full_judgment:
Khizir Ahmed Choudhury J : This first appeal has been preferred against the judgment and decree dated 4-11-2012 passed by learned Joint District Judge, 5th Court, Dhaka in Title Suit No. 484 of 2012 decreeing the suit in favour of the plaintiff.

2. Gopal Chandra Majumder, the predecessor-in-interest of respondent Nos. 1-7 and respondent Nos. 8-12 as plaintiffs instituted the aforesaid title suit impleading the present appellants and respondent Nos. 15-26 as defendants praying for declaration of title in the "ka" schedule property and further declaration that registered deed of sale No. 4132 dated 7-9-1996, deed of sale No. 4134 dated 7-9-1996, deed No. 4130 dated 7-9-1996, deed No. 4139 dated 7-9-1996. deed No. 3510 dated 31-8-1998, as described in the "kha" schedule to the plaint are inoperative, valueless, ineffectual and plaintiffs are not bound by those deeds and also to pass decree for evicting the defendant Nos. 1-11 from schedule Ga(1)-Ga(5).

3. The case of the plaintiff, in brief, is that suit properties belonged to Shatish Mohon Roy who has two sons namely Sushil Mohon Roy and Narayon Chandra Roy, 4 daughters namely Purno Shashi, Chara Bala, Swadesh Bala and Bina Bala. Purno Shashi was married with Subol Chandra Das, son of Subodh Chandra Das. Except Purno Shashi Das, sons and others daughters left for India where they started residing as their permanent abode and in spite of earnest request by Shatish Mohon Roy, they did not return to Bangladesh. Purno Shashi Das and her Husband Subol Chandra Das came to the homestead of Shatish Mohon Roy and started to reside there taking care of Shatish Mohon Roy. Subsequently Shatish Mohon Roy executed a will in favour of Purno Shashi Das on 3-1-1963 appointing Subol Chandra Das as executor of the will. Puma Shashi Das and her husband Subol Chandra Das continued to reside with Shatish Mohon Roy by looking after him. Thereafter Shatish Mohon Roy passed away and subsequently Subol Chandra Das, executor of the will initiated a Probate Case being Probate Case No. 19 of 1963 and learned District Judge granted Probate on 1-7-1963 in favour of Purno Shashi Das. Subsequently, Subol Chandra Das, transferred the suit land to plaintiff Nos. 1-3, Jatendra Chandra Majumder, father of plaintiff Nos. 4-6 and grand father and father-in-law respectively of plaintiff Nos. 7-8 vide five (5) sale deeds and delivered possession thereof. The plaintiffs mutated their names in the record of rights, paid rent and continued to hold and possess the same by themselves and through Bharatias. The defendants were monthly ejectable tenants but they were habitual defaulter in payment of rent and in spite of repeated demand they didn't pay rents. Subsequently, on being approached, Marshal Law authority issued notice to defendants to quit suit properties.

4. Challenging the notices, the defendants instituted Civil Suit being Civil Suit No. 98 of 1984 in the 1st Court of Subordinate Judge Dhaka which was renumbered as Civil Suit No. 93 of 1991, wherein they made an application for amendment of plaint claiming to have purchased the suit land from Narayon Chandra Roy through registered deed of sale but their application for amendment of plaint was rejected against which they preferred Civil Revision No. 1810 of 2000 before the High Court Division.

5.  In the plaint they admitted to be a Bharatia but subsequently they claimed ownership to the suit land by filing amendment application and, as such, their claim has rightly been rejected. The plaintiffs have been holding and possessing the suit land but due to creation of collusive deeds, title of the plaintiffs being clouded, they issued notice under section 106 of Transfer of Property Act but in spite of getting Notice, the defendants did not pay heed thereto which constrained the plaintiffs to file the instant suit.

6. Defendant Nos. 1 and 2, 10-12 contested the suit by filing written statement contending, inter-alia that Shatish Mohon Roy being owner of the suit properties died leaving behind two sons namely Sushil Mohon Roy and Narayan Chandra Roy, wife Naresh Bala Roy and four daughters namely Tanu Bala Roy, Shadeshi Bala Roy, Bina Bala Roy and Purno Sashi Das. The defendants were tenants under the original owner and subsequently under Narayan Chandra Roy son of Sushil Chandra Roy. Thereafter, they used to pay rent to Narayan Chandra Roy through plaintiff No. 1, Narayan Chandra Roy transferred 0.017 acres of land on 7-9-1996 in favour of Ramesh Chandra Das vide deed of Sale No. 4131, 0.0175 acres of land in favour of Nur Mohammad Gazi vide deed of sale No. 4132, 0,0175 acres of land in favour of Shanti Ranjon Sarker vide deed of sale No. 4133 and 0.0175 acres of land in favour of Khorshed Alam vide deed sale No. 4134 and thereafter transferred 0.1697 acres of land in favour of Shanti Ranjon Sarker and aforementioned other purchasers vide deed of sale No. 3510 dated 31-8-1998. Defendant Nos. 1-2 in the meantime filed Civil Suit No. 94 of 1984 before the sub-judge, 1st Court Dhaka praying declaration of title and challenging Notice dated 6-3-1984 issued from the office of Deputy Commissioner, Dhaka for evicting defendant Nos. 1-2. Shatish Mahon Roy without executing any will died leaving behind his aforesaid heirs and hence, the will as mentioned in the plaint is fraudulent and the plaintiff probated the will through deceitful means without serving any Notice to the next of kin of Shatish Mohon Roy. With a view to grab the suit property plaintiffs created the deed of sale showing Subol Chandra Das as vendor who had no saleable interest in the suit land and, as such, the suit be dismissed.

7. Both the parties examined 3 witnesses from each side and also submitted documentary evidences. The trial Court, after hearing the parties and upon perusal of the evidences held that the plaintiffs submitted the certified copy of the Probated will dated 1-7-1963 whereby it is proved that Shatish Chandra executed will in favour of daughter Purno Shashi which has been duly probated and record of right has been prepared in the name of Purno Shashi. The trial Court further found the defendants contention that the sons and daughters of Shatish Chandra did not go to India has not been substantiated. The trial Court further found that Purno Shashi through the executor transferred the suit properties to the plaintiffs and they mutated their name in the record of right and paid all utility bills to the authority and the defendants being tenants under the plaintiffs subsequently claimed title by creating registered documents denying plaintiffs title and accordingly decreed the suit.

8. Mr Md Oziullah, the learned Advocate appearing for the appellant submits that the Subol Chandra Das, the executor of the will has no right to transfer the suit property. He further submits that the suit is barred by Limitation. The suit as framed by the plaintiff for declaration of title and other claims are not maintainable and the defendants being purchaser of the suit land have been possessing the same. He further submitted that notice under section 106 of the Transfer of Property Act is not a proper notice and without filing a suit for partition instant suit is not maintain-able. In support of his contention learned Advocate has referred the case of Kamruzzaman Khan vs Shahidul Alam Khan, reported in 51 DLR 393 and case of the Sahida Alam vs Md Hasmat Ali, reported in 61 DLR (AD) 8.

9. On the other hand Mr AM Aminuddin, learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the respondents submits that the plaintiff purchased the suit property from the lawful owner namely Purno Shashi who has got the suit properties from her father Shatish Chandra Roy by virtue of will which was duly probated and also record of right was prepared in her name. Purno Shashi transferred the suit property through her husband Subol Chandra Das by registered sale deeds and after purchase, the plaintiffs have mutated their names in the record of right, paid utility bills and while owning and possessing through tenants i.e. the defendants, they denied title of the plaintiffs for which the plaintiffs have been constrained to file the instant suit and, as such, the suit is maintainable. He further submits all the reliefs are required to be sought in a suit for proper adjudication. He further submits that as the defendants by creating documents regarding the suit properties denied title of the plaintiffs, their varatia right has been forfeited and the trial Court rightly and reasonably decreed the suit. Mr Aminuddin in support of his contention referred a decision reported in 1 BLC (AD) 156 wherein it has been reiterated that the tenant cannot set up title to a property in which he is monthly tenant, without surrendering possession to his landlord.

10. It is found that the original owner Shatish Chandra made a will in favour of his daughter Pumo Shashi Roy on 3-1-1962 which has duly been probated and by virtue of the said will Purno Shashi as owner and possessor, transferred the same to plaintiffs through his executor Subol Chandra Das. The said will has not been challenged till date by any other heirs of Shatish Chandra Roy for which it is assumed that the will is genuine one. By filing title suit being Title Suit No. 93 of 1991, defendants challenged the eviction notices and also they prayed for declaring the plaintiffs deeds being collusive and void and also for decree of permanent injunction in respect of the suit land wherein the present plaintiff are defendants. Although the defendants intended to assert that they tendered rent to the plaintiffs, on behalf of the Narayan Chandra Roy son of Shatish Chandra Roy, but said contention is not sustainable as because they failed to submit papers showing payment of rents to Narayan Chanda Roy. In that suit they have challenged the notices issued by Martial Law Authority and also they have claimed tenancy right for the suit properties. But subsequently they sought to amend the plaint claiming purchase of the suit property from Narayan Chandra Roy son of Shatish Chandra Roy by registered instrument. Such prayer for amendment has not been allowed by the Court of original jurisdiction which has been upheld up to revisional stage. From the above conduct of the defendants, it can be assumed that the defendants shifted from their earlier position and subsequently they raised claim for ownership and thereby forfeited bharatia right in the suit property.

11. The plaintiffs, after purchase mutated their name in the record of right, paid rents and other utility services which also proved that plaintiffs documents have been acted upon. It is curious that no heirs of Shatish Chandra Roy challenged the probate proceeding at any point of time and also they did not challenge the documents executed and registered in favour of the plaintiffs which also prove that plaintiffs are owner of the suit properties.

12. Now we shall deal with the contention of the learned advocate for the Appellant that due to insertion of so many prayers in the plaint, the suit is not maintainable. Order 2 rule 2(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure runs as follows:

2. "(1) Every suit shall include the whole of the claim which the plaintiff is entitled to make in respect of the cause of action; but a plaintiff may relinquish any portion of his claim in order to bring the suit within the jurisdiction of any Court".

(2) Where a plaintiff omits to sue in respect of, or intentionally relinquishes, any portion of his claim, he shall not afterwards sue in respect of the portion so omitted or relinquished

(3)  .............

13. So, as per provisions of law all the prayers are to be inserted in a suit which the plaintiffs have rightly done.

<u>14. So far the defects of notice under section 106 of the Transfer of Property Act as submitted by the learned advocate for the appellant it can be said that the defendant forfeited their right to stay in the suit properties by denying the title of the plaintiffs and, as such, the contents of the notice or any purported facts are insignificant here. Because if someone denies title of the land lord, notice under section 106 of the Transfer of Property Act may be dispensed with. Consequently the decision referred in 51 DLR 393 is not applicable here. On the other hand the case reported in 1 BLC (AD) 156 as reported by Mr AM Amin Uddin has got semblance with the present case. Submission of the learned Advocate for the appellant that instead of filing a SCC suit the present suit filed by the plaintiff for declaration of title along with other prayers being not maintainable is also cannot stand. In the instant case the defendants have created some registered instruments regarding the suit properties denying the title of the plaintiffs and, as such, plaintiffs have legitimate right to file the instant suit for declaration of title and other reliefs and the present suit is quite maintainable.</u>

<u>15. Upon consideration of the evidences, documents and other circumstances we found that the defendants as tenant denied title of the plaintiffs and so they forfeited right to stay in the suit properties and, as such, the trial Court justifiably decreed the suit in favour of the plaintiffs.</u>

16. We find no merit in the appeal.

17. In the result, the appeal is dismissed without any order as to costs.

Let a copy of this judgment be sent to the concerned Court. Send down the Lower Court Record.

End.

full_judgment:
On an application under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure, this Rule was issued at the instance of the petitioners calling upon the opposite parties to show cause as to why the impugned judgment dated 184-1996 and decree dated 23-4-1996 passed by the learned Subordinate Judge, (now Joint District Judge), 2nd Court, Moulvibazar, in Title Appeal No. 121 of 1993 reversing the judgment and decree dated 31-10-1993 passed by the Assistant Judge, Kamalgonj in Title Suit No. 46 of 1991 dismissing the suit should not be set aside and/ or pass such other or further order or orders as to this Court may seem fit and proper.

2. Facts relevant for disposal of this Rule, in short, are that the predecessor of the opposite party Nos. 1-8, Moniruddin Majumder as plaintiff filed Title Suit No. 46 of 1991 in the court of Assistant Judge, Kamalgonj, Moulvibazar, against the petitioners as defendant for recovery of possession stating, inter alia, that the schedule-1 land was sold to the plaintiff by defendant No. 1 by a registered sale deed dated 17-5-1983. After purchase the plaintiff constructed a tin shed house on the property and have been residing there with his family. Thereafter, Amena Khatun wife of the plaintiff purchased 8 sataks of land from plot No. 1362 adjacent south to the schedule-1 land by sale deed dated 25-11-1987. The plaintiff constructed a four storied building on the property purchased by him and his wife and now living therein. Again by a sale deed Amena Khatun purchased 15 sataks of land from south portion of plot No. 1362. In the aforesaid way the plaintiff and his wife purchased in total 49 sataks of land from plot Nos. 1362 and 1363. The said land is situated in a compact block wherein the plaintiff planted various trees and installed tube well. While the plaintiff in possession and enjoyment of the property since purchase, the defendant No.1 requested the plaintiff in the last part of Falgoon 1396 BS to allow him to stay in the suit house for the time being to enable him to construct his house on the adjacent land to the plaintiff's land. The plaintiff on candid allowed the defendant No: 1 considering his distress condition to stay in the suit house on the assurance that he will vacate and surrender possession of the suit house when asked by the plaintiff. But the defendant No. 1 on various pretext and pleas continued to live in the house for several months. Finding no way out the plaintiff in the midst of Baishakh 1397 BS finally asked the defendant No. 1 to vacate the house and handover vacant possession of the same to the plaintiff.

3. The defendant No. 1 assured the plaintiff that he will vacate the house very soon and handover vacant possession to the plaintiff. The defendant also disclosed that he sold the property in plot No. 1363 to the defendant No. 2. Meanwhile, taking advantage of defendant No. l's possession in the schedule-2 land the defendant No. 2 with the help of other threatened the plaintiff with dispossession form the north part of the suit land on 23rd Jaistha 1398. For the reason, the plaintiff filed Title Suit No. 33 of 1991 for a decree of permanent injunction against the defendant Nos. 1 and 2 along with others and in that suit got the suit land inspected through court by an Advocate Commissioner. Learned Advocate Commissioner found that the defendant No. 2 constructed a tin shed house measuring 8 x 7 hands just adjacent to south-east corner of the plaintiff's suit house. In the meantime, taking advantage of possessing the suit house by the defendant No. 1 as permissive possessor the defendant No. 2 dispossessed the plaintiff from the suit land.

4. In the situation the plaintiff has withdrawn Title Suit No. 33 of 1991 with permission to sue a fresh and filed the instant suit for recovery of possession. It is also stated that the defendant No. 1 filed a criminal case against the plaintiffs and his son being No. 221 of 1991 under sections 107/114/117(c) of the Code of Criminal Procedure which was ultimately rejected. The defendant Nos. 1 and 2 most illegally dispossessed the plaintiff from the suit land claiming that they have title in the suit property by purchase and dispossessed the plaintiff by constructing a tin shed house on the south-east corner of the suit land.

5. The defendant Nos. 1 and 2 contested the suit by filing written statement denying all the allegations made in the plaint contending inter alia, that the suit is not maintainable without a suit for partition and also denied that they dispossessed the plaintiff from the suit land on the date stated in the plaint or any other date. The case of the defendants are that plot No. 1362 measuring 44 sataks and plot No. 1363 measuring 35 sataks under khatian No. 99 are the suit land. The defendant No. 1 purchased in total 50 sataks of land from plot Nos. 1362 and 1363 from different persons and has been in possession of the same by constructing house and living therein with their family. While Ekhlas Mia the defendant No. 1 in possession he transferred 26 sataks of land to the plaintiff from plot No. 1362 by sale deed dated 17-5-1983 out of 57 sataks. After sale he remains in possession of 31 sataks land wherein his homestead and other establishment exists. The defendant No. 1 by sale deeds dated 1-6-1991 and 3-6-1991 transferred the said 31 sataks land to the defendant No. 2 and delivered possession of the same.

6. It is also stated that the defendant No. 1 never possessed the suit land as permissive possessor under the plaintiff and the plaintiff in the earlier Title Suit No. 33 of 1991 filed against the defendant did not claim that the suit property has been possessing by the defendant No. 1 as permissive possessor. But for the purpose of filing of the present suit against the defendants the plaintiff very cunningly made out a case that the defendant No.1 has been possessing the suit land as permissive possessor with the permission of the plaintiff. As such, the suit is a false one and liable to be dismissed.

7. The trial court framed four issues for determination of the dispute. In course of trial the plaintiff examined four witnesses including himself and submitted some documents which was marked as exhibits 1 and 2. On the other hand the defendants examined five witnesses including an Advocate Commissioner and submitted documents in support of their case which was marked as exhibits 'Ka' to exhibit-'Chha' series. The trial court after contested hearing dismissed the suit by its judgment and decree dated 31-10-1993.

8. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the judgment and decree the plaintiff preferred Title Appeal No. 121 of 1993 before the District Judge, Moulvibazar. Eventually the said appeal was heard by the Sub-ordinate Judge (now Joint District Judge) 2nd court, Moulvibazar on transfer who upon contested hearing allowed the appeal and reversed the judgment and decreed of the trial court by the impugned judgment and decree dated 18-4-1996. At this juncture the defendant-Respondent-Petitioners moved this Court by filing this revisional application under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure and obtained the present Rule and order of stay.

9. Mr Mahbub Ali, learned Advocate appearing for the petitioners submits that admittedly there is no dispute regarding title of the defendant No. 1 Ekhlas Mia. Both the parties to the suit unequivocally admitted that Ekhlas Mia was rightful owner in possession of 57 sataks of land in plot Nos. 1362 and 1363. Admitting indefeasible title in the property the plaintiff by sale deed No. 3481 dated 17-5-1983 purchased 26 sataks of land from Ekhlas Mia, the defendant No. 1 in suit and possession was delivered to him. Accordingly, he has been possessing the same since his purchase in the year 1993. Mr Mahbub Ali further submits that it is also not disputed that after selling 26 sataks of land to the plaintiff the defendant No. 1 Ekhlas Mia was in possession and enjoyment on the remaining 31 sataks of land which was his homestead in a compact block. Said Ekhlas Mia while in possession and enjoyment of 31 sataks land by sale deed No. 2609 dated 1-6-1991 sold out .24 sataks of land covered by plot Nos. 1362 and 1363 to defendant No. 2, Md Ali. Again by a sale deed No. 2610 dated 3-6-1991 Ekhlas Mia transferred 7 sataks of land in plot Nos. 1362 and 1363 to the defendant No. 2. Thus Ekhlas Mia sold entire land in the said two plots. The defendant No. 2 after purchase got delivery of possession of the property with definite boundary as given in the sale deed and accordingly, he has been possessing the same with the knowledge of all. He further submits that the story of dispossession of the plaintiff is false and concocted as the plaintiff in the earlier Title Suit No. 33 of 1991 filed against the defendant for permanent injunction did not even utter a single word that the defendant No. 1 has been possessing the suit land as permissive possessor under the plaintiff or the defendant No. 2.

10. He also argued that the plaintiff when could understand that he being out of possession the suit for injunction must fail then he has withdrawn the said suit with permission to sue a fresh and subsequently filed the instant suit making a story of premissive possessor seeking recovery of possession of the suit property. In fact the plaintiff never possessed the suit land. The property so far sold to him by deed of the year 1983 is totally separate and different from the land possessed and transferred to defendant No. 2. Mr Ali further submits that admittedly plaintiff and the defendants are co-sharers in two plots and there is no partition by metes and bounds among them. As such, the proper and appropriate relief for the plaintiff is to file a suit for partition praying saham of his share in the suit land. But the plaintiff filed the instant suit for recovery of possession against a co-sharer of the property which is not maintainable at all. Referring schedule to the sale deed dated 17-5-1983 exhibit-1, Mr Mahbub Ali submits that the property sold to the plaintiff is not specific and the schedule as described shows that the plaintiff purchased the property from defendant No. 1 only from plot No. 1362 and the possession of the property purchased by the plaintiff as not being described by giving definite boundary with specific possession the plaintiff cannot say that he has been dispossessed by the defendant.

11. It is also argued that the trial court while dismissing the suit rightly observed that schedule to the deed of the plaintiff is unspecific and the witnesses examined on behalf of the plaintiff could not prove exclusive possession and dispossession by the defendants. But the appellate court while allowing the appeal and decreeing the suit wrongly found that Ekhlas Mia is the owner of only 49 sataks of land covered by plot Nos. 1362 and 1363. The appellate court also wrongly found that Ekhlas Mia by sale deed dated 7-6-1983 acquired 7 sataks of land from plot No. 1359 not from plot Nos. 1362 and 1363 and as such, Ekhlas Mia cannot transfer 31 sataks of land claiming to be owner of the same to defendant No. 2. By filing an application under Order XLI, rule 27 of the Code of Civil Procedure the petitioner prayed for accepting the sale deed dated 7-6-1983 and deed No. 2601 dated 1-6-1991 as additional evidence and to mark the same as exhibits. It is also submitted that since the deed dated 7-6-1983 has already been taken into consideration by the appellate court and observed that the said deed is in respect of plot No. 1359 only, the deed of rectification dated 1-6-1991 filed by a supplementary affidavit as annexure-'A', may be considered and marked as exhibits which left due consideration of the appellate court for better appreciation of the case and to ensure justice.

12. Finally, Mr Mahbub Ali argued that should the appellate court below consider the aforesaid two documents in conjunction with other sale deeds the appellate court below ought not to have allowed the appeal and decreed the suit because by the aforesaid two deeds it is clear that Ekhlas Mia acquired 57 sataks of land in plot Nos. 1362 and 1363. The appellate court considered title of Ekhlas Mia in respect of only 49 sataks which lead the appellate court below into an erroneous finding and on that finding allowed the appeal finding that defendant No. 1 had no title in 31 sataks of land transferred to the defendant No. 2.

13. Heard the learned Advocate for the opposite parties, have gone through the revisional application, impugned judgment and decree of both the courts below, evidences available in lower court records both oral and documentary and the document filed by a supplementary affidavit as annexure-'A'.

14. From perusal of plaint and written statement it appears that both the parties admitted that Ekhlas Mia is the owner of 57 sataks of land covered by plot Nos. 1362 and 1363. Admitting his title the plaintiff purchased 26 sataks of land from him from the said plots in question. In the plaint the plaintiff clearly stated that after his purchase defendant No. 1 Ekhlas Mia had 31 sataks of land and he was in possession of the same. It is not the case of the plaintiff that he did not get possession of the property purchased and Ekhlas Mia had no possession in the remaining 31 sataks of land covered by said two plots. The case of the plaintiff is that the defendant No. 1 requested him to permit him to live in the suit house for the time being to enable him to construct his house on the property adjacent to the plaintiff's property. The defendant No. 1 Ekhlas Mia while in possession of the schedule-2 suit house the plaintiff filed Title Suit No. 33 of 1991 against the defendant No. 2 and others for a decree of permanent injunction. Now here in the said plaint in Title Suit No. 33 of 1991 the plaintiff claimed that the suit property is in possession of defendant No. 1 as permissive possessor. But the plaintiff clearly stated that he is in possession and the defendant No. 2 in the present suit along with his gangmen threatened the plaintiff with dispossession on 23rd Jaistha 1398 BS and in the said suit the plaintiff claimed that the defendant No. 2 of this suit purchased the land just adjacent to his land and trying to dispossess the plaintiff declaring that he will construct pucca building on the suit land.

15. Subsequently, the said suit was withdrawn on the ground of formal defect with permission to sue a fresh and then filed the instant suit for recovery of possession. From the pleadings of the party and the evidences adduced, it appears that the property in question is an undivided one. Both the parties are co-sharer in the suit land. There was no partition by metes and bound. In such a situation if a co-sharer of the property thinks that he has been deprived of his share by other co-sharer may ventilate his grievance by filing a partition suit seeking saham of his share and get the property partitioned through court and delivery of possession of the same but a suit for mere recovery of possession is not maintainable without determination of their share in the property. From evidences both oral and documentary it is not clear in which portion of the two plots the possession was delivered to the plaintiff.

16. Moreover, from the schedule to the sale deed, exhibit-1 it is difficult to find that possession in which portion of the suit plot was delivered to the plaintiff. In such a situation without a suit for partition a suit for recovery of possession is not at all maintainable. The trial court upon consideration of the evidences on record rightly found that Ekhlas Mia is the owner of 57 sataks land. He transferred 26 sataks to the plaintiff and the remaining 31 sataks of land to the defendant No. 2. The trial court also observed that there is no evidence to be believed that the plaintiff was dispossessed from the suit land but it is the clear admission of the plaintiff that the defendant No. 1 is in possession of the suit land though he claims that he has given permission to the Defendant No. 1 to live therein.

<u>17. The plaintiff as PW 1 deposed in respect of possession and dispossession, no other witnesses supported his claim that he was in possession and he has been dispossessed by the defendants. In a suit for recovery of possession the plaintiff is to prove his possession at first and then his dispossession by the defendant by evidence. But in the present suit nobody came forward to depose that the plaintiff was dispossessed on such and such date or the plaintiff had been in possession of the suit land since his purchase and he permitted the defendant No. 1 to live in the suit house for the time being. In the absence of such assertion or evidences possession and dispossession of the plaintiff in the suit land is not established.</u>

18. Moreover, in the earlier suit the plaintiff did not make such story that he has been possessing the suit land through defendant No. 1 as permissive possessor. No evidence adduced on behalf of the plaintiff to establish his case in whose presence the defendant No. 1 was allowed to reside in the suit house. Mere testimony and claim of the plaintiff alone cannot ipso facto prove that he allowed the defendant No. 1 to reside in the suit house as permissive possessor or before that he had been possessing the same and dispossessed by the defendant Nos. 1 and 2.

19. It is also not the case of the plaintiff that defendant No. 1 refrained himself from surrendering possession of the suit house to the plaintiff denying title of the plaintiff or claiming title in the property. But a case has been made out to the effect that taking advantage of possession of the defendant No.1 in the suit house the defendant No. 2 with his gangmen dispossessed the plaintiff. The trial court while dismissing the suit found that the plaintiff could not prove exclusive possession of the suit property before alleged date of dispossession and also could not prove in what manner and on what time the defendant No. 2 dispossessed the plaintiff.

20. I have gone through the judgment of the appellate court. From perusal of the same this Court finds that the appellate court while allowing the appeal mainly considered the fact that Ekhlas Mia did not acquire 57 sataks of land in two suit plots by considering a deed dated 7-6-1983 by which he purchased 7 sataks of land. The said deed shows that Ekhlas Mia purchased 7 sataks of land from plot No. 1359, but subsequently, by a deed of the year 1991 annexure-'A' to the supplementary affidavit the deed dated 7-6-1983 has been rectified by the vendor wherein plot No. 1362 has been inserted by the rectification deed dated 1-6-1991. It is established that Ekhlas Mia purchased 7 sataks of land from plot No. 1362 not from plot No. 1359. The deed dated 7-6-1983 has not been marked as exhibit before the trial court, but the appellate court has taken the same into consideration and considering the said deed came to a finding that in the absence of title of the Ekhlas Mia in 31 sataks of land he cannot transfer the same to defendant No. 2 and the Defendant 2 cannot claim 31 sataks in the two suit plots. Had the rectification deed dated 1-6-1991 been placed before the appellate court and considered it in conjunction with the deed dated 7-6-1983, the lower appellate court would not have allowed the appeal and decreed the suit. Since the appellate court considered the deed dated 7-6-1983 in its judgment this court thinks that it would be just and expedient to consider the deed of rectification dated 1-6-1991 submitted before this Court by supplementary affidavit as annexure-'A' in conjunction with the deed dated 7-6-1983 for ends of justice. Accordingly, for proper adjudication of the dispute before this Court I am inclined to allow the application and mark those documents as 'X' and 'Y' respectively. Apart from this where both the parties admitted that Ekhlas Mia is the owner of 57 sataks of land in two plots the appellate court should not have made out a 3rd case beyond pleadings and evidences on record. In such a situation both the documents of the year 1983 and 1991 have been considered to come into a definite finding that there cannot be any question at all that Ekhlas Mia is not the owner of 57 sataks of land.

21. In the instant suit since the plaintiff failed to prove his possession and dispossession by evidence the trial court rightly dismissed the suit. But the appellate court instead of considering evidences on record piecemeally considering a deed of the year, 1983 (Mark-"X") and allowed the appeal and as such, has committed an error of law occasioning failure of justice.

22. Taking into consideration of the above, this Court finds merit in the Rule as well as in the submissions of the petitioners counsel calling interference by this Court.

23. In the result, the Rule is made absolute.

24. The judgment and decree dated 18-4-1996 passed by the learned Sub-ordinate Judge, (now Joint District Judge), 2nd Court, Moulvibazar, in Title Appeal No. 121 of 1993 is hereby set side and the judgment and decree dated 31-10-1993 passed by the trial court in Title Suit No. 46 of 1991 is restored.

25. The order of stay granted at the time of issuance of the Rule stands vacate.

26. There will be no order as to costs.

Communicate a copy of this judgment and send down the lower court records to the court concerned at once.

End.
