full_judgment:
This Rule was issued at the instance of the defendant-respondent-petitioners calling upon the plaintiff-appellant-opposite party Nos. 1-5 to show cause as to why the judgment and decree dated 12-7-2010 (decree signed on 19-7-2017) passed by the Additional District Judge, Second Court, Gazipur in Title Appeal No. 133 of 2009 allowing the appeal and setting aside the judgment and decree dated 4-6-2009 (decree signed on 10-6-2009) passed by the Assistant Judge, Second Court, Gazipur in Title Suit No. 3256 of 2008 dismissing the suit should not be set aside.

2. Facts giving rise to the emergence of the present Rule are that on 30-11-2006 the opposite party Nos. 1-5 as plaintiff instituted Title Suit No. 275 of 2006 (subsequently renumbered as Title Suit No. 3256 of 2008) before the Senior Assistant Judge, Second Court, Gazipur against the petitioners and proforma opposite parties praying for a declaration to the effect that the plaintiffs have title in the suit land to the extent of 39 decimals of land as specified in schedule 'Ka' to the plaint and for a further declaration that 9 (nine) registered sale deeds and hiba-bil-ewaj deeds as specified in schedule 'Kha' to the plaint are collusive, illegal and not binding upon the plaintiffs on the contention that the suit land originally belonged to one Sheikh Salam Uddin whose name was recorded in CS Khatian No. 114 in respect of 16.86 acres of land; that Sheikh Salam Uddin died leaving behind two sons, namely Usman Ali and Rusmat Ali; that each son got 270 decimals of land by inheritance from Plot No. 187, and 843 decimals from C. S. Khatian No. 114 from their father by inheritance; that on 19-5-1937 Rusmat Ali transferred 843 decimals of land to his wife Alimon Nessa through registered sale deed No. 3419; that thereafter on 5-4-1943 Alimon Nessa transferred 21 decimals of land to five persons including one Hasen Ali; that thereafter on 14-6-1946 Alimon Nessa transferred 813 decimals of land to her husband Rusmat Ali by registered sale deed No. 6225; that on 6-2-2005 Rusmat Ali transferred land to Nur Mohammad, lnsan Ali i.e. the father of plaintiff Nos. 3 and 4 and Ahamad Ali i.e. the father of plaintiff Nos. 1 and 2 through sale deed No. 1995 and in this way each transferee got 17 decimals of land and accordingly, the SA Khatian Nos. 290 and 291 were rightly recorded in their names; that on 5-5-1951 Rusmat Ali transferred 35 decimals of land to his sister-in-law Olimon Nessa through deed No. 1878 and the said 35 decimals of land was acquired through LA Case No. 23/67-68 and through acquisition the right and title of Olimon Nessa was extinguished over the land; that even after the above acquisition, on 21-11-1982 Olimon Nessa transferred 12 decimals of land to one Shahid Ullah through deed No. 8868, on 27-6-1983 transferred 8 decimals of land to Abdul Khaleque through deed No. 6976 and on the same date transferred 17 decimals of land to defendant Nos. 1 and 2 through deed No. 6987 though there was no legal sanction of those deeds which also had no legal effect i.e. deed No. 4066 dated 27-6-1993, deed No. 6802 dated 14-9-1997, deed No. 8792 dated 8-12-97, deed No. 4282 dated 5-6-1998, deed No. 8392 dated 7-9-2002 and deed No. 9444 dated 30-10-2004; that Rusmat Ali, Usman Ali and Moslem Ali became extinguished in her title through transfer; that the plaintiffs became owner of 39 decimals of land on the strength of sale and inheritance; that the plaintiffs have been enjoying and possessing the suit land peacefully by planting trees and cultivating vegetables therein; that the defendants have no right, title, interest and possession in the suit land; that on 1-10-2005 the plaintiffs came to know about the wrong RS record in the name of Olimon Nessa when they went to the local Tahshil office to pay the rent; that on 6-10-2005 the plaintiffs became fully aware of the wrong R.S. Khatian after collecting the certified copy of the same from the concerned office; that the wrong RS record of the suit land in the name of Olimon Nessa clouded the title of the plaint and in order to dispel that cloud, the plaintiffs earlier filed Title Suit No. 217 of 2005 but later on they withdrew the suit with a permission to sue afresh for material defects in the plaint, and that afterwards they filed this suit praying for a decree for declaration of title over the suit land with a further prayer for cancellation of the deeds as mentioned in schedule 'Kha' to the plaint.

3. That the defendant Nos. 1, 6 and 10 contested the suit by filing a joint written statement denying all the material facts of the plaint and contending, inter alia, that the suit is not maintainable in its present form and manner; that the suit is barred by waiver, estoppel and acquiescence; that the suit land originally belonged to CS recorded tenant Sheikh Saham Uddin in whose name CS khatian No. 114 in respect of 16.86 acres of land was prepared and published; that Saham Uddin died leaving behind two sons named Usman Ali and Rusmat Ali and each of them got 270 decimals of land by inheritance from plot No. 187; that SA Khatian No. 291 was recorded in the name of Usman Ali, and SA Khatian No. 290 was recorded in the name Rusmat Ali who transferred 35 decimals of land to his wife Olimon Nessa by a registered sale deed being No. 1878 dated 5-2-1951; that on 21-11-1982 Olimon Nessa transferred 12 decimals of land to Shahid Ullah through deed No. 8868, on 27-6-83 transferred 8 decimals of land to Abdul Khaleque through deed No. 6976 and on the same date transferred 7 decimals of land to defendants Nos. 1 and 2 through deed No. 7987; that the defendants got title over the suit land through some deeds i.e. deed No. 4066 dated 27-6-1993, deed No. 292 dated 5-6-1998, deed No. 7042 dated 4-9-1997 and deed No. 6802 dated 14-9-1997; that only 3 decimals of land out of 35 decimals were acquired from the property of Olimon Nessa and she remained in possession of the rest 32 decimals of land and accordingly, the land was rightly recorded in RS Khatian No. 354 in Plot No. 111 in her name; that on 23-12-1961 Shamsul Huq transferred 70 decimals of land through deed No. 5000 to Moslem Ali, the father of plaintiff Nos. 1-4; at the defendants No. 1 become the owner of land recorded in RS Plot No. 1112; that the suit land was correctly recorded in RS Khatian in the name of the defendants who have right, title, interest, possession and control over the suit land and the plaintiffs do not have any title and possession in the suit land; that the plaintiffs brought suits one after another in respect of the suit land to harass the defendants and hence, the suit is liable to be dismissed with cost.

4. The suit was tried by the Assistant Judge, Second Court (Sreepur), Gazipur on 6 (six) issues.

5. During trial the plaintiffs examined 3 witnesses including the plaintiff No. 4 Md Azizur Rahman as PW 1, and the contesting defendants also examined 3 witnesses including the defendant No. 7 Abdul Khaleque as DW 1 and both the parties adduced documentary evidences in support of their respective claims.

6. The trial Court by its judgment and decree dated 4-6-2009 dismissed the suit holding, inter alia, that the suit is barred by limitation, not maintainable in its present form and manner, and that the plaintiffs failed to prove their case by documentary and oral evidence.

7. Feeling aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the aforesaid judgment and decree of the trial Court, the plaintiffs preferred Title Appeal No. 133 of 2009 before the District Judge, Gazipur and the appeal was eventually heard by the Additional District Judge, Second Court, Gazipur who by the judgment and decree dated 12-7-2010 (decree signed on 19-7-2010) allowed the appeal decreeing the suit and declaring plaintiffs' title to 34 decimals of land as against their claim of 39 decimals by setting aside the judgment and decree of the trial court holding, inter alia, that the plaintiffs successfully managed to prove their right, title, interest and possession in the suit land and that the defendants acquired no title to the suit land since their transferor Alimon Nesa became completely extinguished therefrom following the acquisition of her entire share to the extent of 35 decimals vide LA Case No. 23/67-68.

8. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the aforesaid judgment and decree dated 12-7-2010 (decree signed on 19-12-2010) passed by the Additional District Judge, Second Court, Gazipur in Title Appeal No. 133 of 2009, the petitioners moved an application under Section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure and obtained the present Rule.

9. Mr Md Ashraful Alam, the learned Advocate for the defendant-petitioners, instead of pressing any of the grounds taken in the revisional application, took me to schedule 'Kha' of the plaint in the form of a table containing the particulars of the impugned deeds of hiba and sale deeds (Exhibits-5-14) and submits that the schedules of the said deeds are not given in the plaint and, as such, the suit being manifestly barred by Order VII, rule 3 of the Code of Civil Procedure due to lack of specification, the lower appellate court ought to have dismissed the suit as the trial court did albeit on different reasonings.

10. Mr Ashraful Alam next submits that the cause of action of the suit is not clear and discernible even upon a close scrutiny and perusal of the plaint, and, as such, the suit lacks a clear and meaningful cause of action for which the same is liable to dismissed.

11. Mr Alam lastly submits that the plaintiffs prayed for a decree for declaration of title vis-a-vis of 39 decimals of land whereas the lower appellate court decreed the suit in part by declaring their title to 34 decimals of land, and the instant suit being a suit for declaration simpliciter as opposed to a suit for partition, there is no scope to decree the suit in part and therefore, the impugned judgment and decree of the court of appeal below being illegal, perverse and beyond the standard norms of a declaratory decree, is liable to be set aside.

12. Per contra, Mr Zakir Hossain Bhuiyan, learned Advocate appearing for the plaintiff-opposite party Nos. 1, 3-5 submits that the plaintiffs successfully managed to prove their right, title, interest and possession in the suit land by adducing sufficient oral and documentary evidence of convincing nature and, as such, the suit has been rightly decreed by the court of appeal below reversing the erroneous, illegal and perverse findings and decision of the trial court. In this regard Mr Bhuiyan added that the defendants neither through their written statement nor evidence denied the accuracy and genuineness of the title deeds of the plaintiffs, which were duly produced, examined and used as evidences by putting exhibit marks thereon as Exhibits 26 and 34-43.

13. Mr Bhuiyan next submits that the plaintiffs successfully managed to prove that entire 35 decimals of land as specified in the registered sale deed being No. 1878 dated 5-2-1951 (Exhibit- 20) was lawfully acquired from its admitted owner Alimon Nesa Bibi vide LA Case No. 23/67-1968 for the purpose of constructing Dhaka-Mymensingh Highway, and the said Alimon Nesa Bibi drew/received the compensation money/award against the said acquisition of her total quantum of land. Drawing my attention to Exhibits-15 and 50.

14. Mr Bhuiyan submits that the defendant-petitioners miserably failed to prove by any minimum iota of evidence, oral or documentary, that only 3 decimals as opposed to 35 decimals of land was acquired from the said Alimon Nesa Bibi. Placing his reliance on Exhibit-15 and 50, Mr Bhuiyan submits that those exhibits were duly proved by the plaintiffs before the trial Court and the defendants did not raise any objection against those documents either before the trial court or the lower appellate Court although they got copy thereof or access thereto in the course of trial. In support of this submission Mr Bhuiyan refers to the cases Jinnat Ali Muktear vs Abdul Majid 27 DLR 385 and Pubali Bank vs Md Selim 7 BLT 21.

15. Mr Bhuiyan further submits that entire 35 decimals of land belonging to Alimon Nesa Bibi having been acquired from her vide LA Case No. 23/67-68 and the compensation money against that acquisition having been drawn on 15-2-1971, she had no subsisting interest in the suit land and, as such, the impugned sale deeds and hiba-bil-ewaj deeds (Exhibits 5-14) having been executed and registered during the period ranging from 21-11-1982 to 30-10-2004, are illegal, forged, fraudulent, collusive and without any legal effect in view of the fact that no title passed either from Alimon Nesa Bibi or her transferees or successive transferees on the strength of the said impugned deeds and, as such, the transactions effected by the impugned deeds are mere paper transactions and ineffective for not being followed up by any consideration and delivery of actual/physical possession, rather the defendants in connivance with each other created the said documents with a sinister design to grab the suit land. In support of his submission Mr Bhuiyan refers to the cases Sohiruddin Mondal being dead his heirs Mansur Ali vs Banu Bibi 2 ALR 385; Ibrahim vs Sardar Ahmad 7 DLR 62.

16. Mr Bhuiyan also submits that out of 37 defendants, only the defendant Nos. 1 and 6-10 contested the suit by filing a joint written statement substantially admitting the case of the plaintiffs, and although the defendant Nos. 2-5 and 11-37 are the recipient/beneficiary of the impugned deeds as contained in Exhibits 5-14, they did not contest the suit by filing any written statement or adducing any evidence, oral or documentary, and, as such, the plaintiffs' claim against the said non-contesting defendants stands unopposed, unassailed, uncontroverted and admitted within the meaning of law. On this point Mr Bhuiyan continues to argue that the contesting defendants i.e. defendant Nos. 1 and 6-10 directly or indirectly admitted the claim of the plaintiffs as made in paragraph 1-9 of the plaint vide paragraph 8-16 of their written statement and, as such, the plaintiffs' case stands proven on the admission of the defendants. Taking me to paragraph 19(Ga) of their written statement, Mr Bhuiyan submits that the contesting defendants

categorically admitted that Alimon Nesa Bibi did not have title to the entire suit land.

17. Mr Bhuiyan goes on to add that the defendants signally failed to explain in paragraph 19(Ga) of their written statement as to how Alimon Nesa Bibi lost her title to 17 decimals of land which was allegedly transferred in favour of the defendant Nos. 1 and 2 vide a registered deed of hiba-bil-ewaj being No. 6987 dated 27-6-1983 (although wrongly written as deed No. 7987 and the defendants' lack of such explanation otherwise lends support to the plaintiffs' contention that Alimon Nesa's entire 35 decimals of land was acquired for the purpose of constructing Dhaka-Mymensingh Highway vide LA Case No. 23/67-68, and in spite of having specific knowledge about Alimon Nesa's lack of title to the lands transferred to them vide the said deed of hiba-bil-ewaj being No. 6987 dated 27-6-1983 (Ext. 14), the defendant Nos. 1 and 2 collusively effected the execution and registration of the said deed in their favour with a sinister design to grab the suit land or a portion thereof in the garb of the said deed of hiba.

18. On the point of plaintiffs' acquisition of right, title, interest and possession in the suit land, Mr Bhuiyan takes to paragraph 9 of the plaint and submits that the contention made in that paragraph having not been specifically denied and no counter version having been offered by the defendants vide paragraph 16 of their written statement, the plaintiffs' right, title, interest and possession in the suit land stands admitted within the meaning of Order VIII, rules 3-5 of the Code of Civil Procedure. In this connection Mr Bhuiyan placed reliance on Nurul Islam vs Jamila Khatun 53 DLR (AD) 45; and Zafela Begum vs Atikulla 16 BLC (AD) 46.

19. On the defendants' failure to prove their title to the suit land by producing all of their title deeds, Mr Bhuiyan submits that only 2 (two) out of 10 (ten) deeds i.e. registered sale deed No. 6976 dated 27-6-1983 (Exhibit-13) and registered sale deed No. 6802 dated 14-9-1997 (Exhibit- 6) were produced before the trial court in support of their contention and they offered no explanation as to the non-production of 8 (eight) other documents for reasons best known to them. More so, Exhibit-6 bears noticeable interpolations, which invite serious suspicions as to its accuracy and genuineness.

20. Mr Bhuiyan lastly submits that while decreeing the suit, the trial court unduly and illegally laid over emphasis on RS Khatian No. 354 erroneously prepared and published in the name of Alimon Nesa Bibi since she had no subsisting interest in the suit land at the time of preparation and publication of the same, and that the trial court recorded a gratuitous and unreasonably lengthy findings on the said RS Khatian without taking any issue thereon and thereby made out a third case in favour of the defendants, falling into an oblivion of the settled/entrenched principle of law that RS Khatian has got no presumptive value of correctness. In support of his submission Mr Bhuiyan refers to the cases Guru Charan Mondal vs Sree Bhaba Sindhu Sarkar 13 MLR (AD) 6; Abdul Mannan Bhuiyan vs Md Nasir Hossain 6XP (AD) 54; Md Kalam Molla vs Sheikh Samsu 23 BLT 320; Abdus Samad Khan vs Md Wazed Ali Fakir 14 BLD 375 = 44 DLR 495; Md Shamsul Huda being dead his heirs; Hafez Mohammad Ismail vs Bangladesh 20 BLD (AD) 48 = 5 BLC (AD) 108.

21. I have meticulously gone through the revisional application, the impugned judgment and decree, the pleadings of the respective parties, evidence led by them and other materials-on-record and also heard the learned Advocates for the contending parties at length for days together and perused the decisions relied upon by them with utmost circumspection and the relevant provisions of law wherefrom it transpires that Exhibit 15 and 50 are the sheet anchor of the instant suit and the ultimate outcome of the same hinges on the consideration thereof in their proper and true perspective. I will also endeavour to address all other connected issues involved in the Rule in proportion to their respective weight and importance.

<u>22. It transpires from Exhibit 15 and 50 that Alimon Nesa's entire share to the extent of 15 decimals of land was acquired by the then East Pakistan Government for constructing Dhaka-Mymensingh Highway vide LA Case No. 23/67-68 and on 15-2-1971 she received compensation against that acquisition for which she lost her subsisting interest in the suit land and therefore, subsequent transfers of the same from 21-11-1982 to 30-10-2004 by the so-called transferees and successive transferees of Alimon Nesa by the impugned sale deeds and hiba-bil-ewaj deeds as contained in Exhibit 5-14 happen to be sham and mere paper transactions given the fact that the suit land having earlier been acquired for a public purpose, subsequent sale and delivery of possession thereof was impossible. Although the defendants contended that only 3 decimals of land was acquired from Alimon Nesa, they did neither produce any evidence to substantiate that contention nor did they raise any objection against Exhibit 15 and 50 before the either of the lower courts in spite of having ample opportunity to do so and, as such, their main contention falls through. In this regard, I think it would be profitable to quote the ratio decidendi of the cases relied upon by the plaintiff-opposite parties.</u>

23. In Jinnat Ali Muktear vs Abdul Majid 27 DLR 385 it was held that "If objection to the formal proof of a document has not been taken at the earliest point of time, it cannot be taken subsequently and also not in appeal".

24. The view of the High Court Division in Pubali Bank vs Md Selim 7 BLT 21 runs as "Unless objection as to admissibility of a document was taken at the earliest opportunity, that is, at the time of admitting the documents into evidence and marking it as an exhibit, the question of its admissibility cannot be raised at a subsequent stage."

25. Although the defendant Nos. 1 and 6-10 out of a total number of 37 defendants contested the suit by filing a joint written statement, the rest i.e. defendant Nos. 2-5 and 11-37 didn't feel any necessity to contest the suit by filing written statement or adducing evidence despite the fact that they are the recipient/beneficiary of the impugned deeds. Upon perusal of paragraphs 8-16 of written statement filed by the contesting defendant Nos. 1 and 6-10, it appears that they substantially admitted the claim of the plaintiffs as raised vide paragraphs 1-9 of the plaint. Again, the contesting defendants vide paragraph 19(Ga) of their joint written statement categorically admitted that their predecessor-in-title had no title to the entire suit land and the manner/mode of loss of title to the half of her share by Alimon Nesa as well as the purchase by the defendant Nos. 1 -2 from the said Alimon Nesa in spite of her lack of title having althrough been unexplained, the case of the plaintiffs otherwise stands proven/ supported by such lack of explanation on the part of the defendants. Paragraph 19(Ga) of the said written statement reads as follows:

“গ) উপরোক্ত আলিমন নেছা সি এস ১৮৭ দাগে ৩৫ শতাংশ সম্পত্তিতে খরিদমূলে মালিক দখলকার নিয়ত হইয়া ------ বিগত ২৭-৬-৮৩ তারিখের ৭৯৮৭ নং দলিলমূলে ১৭ শতাংশ সম্পত্তির ১ ও ২নং বিবাদীর বরাবরে হস্তান্তর করেন। উক্ত দলিল ১ ও ২ নং বিবাদী ১৭ শতাংশ সম্পত্তির ১৭ শতাংশ দাবী করে না। উক্ত কারণ উক্ত আলিমন নেছার সম্পত্তি হস্তান্তর করার মালিকানা ছিল না?

<u>26. Admissions (arising out of non-denial and offering counter version) made by the contesting defendants in paragraphs 8-19 of their written statement against the claim/contentions raised by the plaintiffs in paragraphs 1-9 of the plaint ultimately support the plaintiffs' acquisition of right, title, interest and possession in the suit land within the meaning of Order VIII, rules 3-5 of the Code of Civil Procedure. Although the admissions made by the defendants in their written statement are not discussed in a muscle for the sake of brevity, the wording of Order VIII, rules 3-5 of the Code of Civil Procedure are reproduced below in verbatim:</u>

<u>R. 3 Denial to be specific. It shall not be sufficient for a defendant in his written statement to deny generally the grounds alleged by the plaintiff but the defendant must deal specifically with each allegation of fact of which he does not admit the truth, except damages.</u>

<u>R. 4 Evasive denial, Where a defendant denies an allegation of fact in the plaint, he must not do so evasively, but answer the point of substance</u>

<u>R. 5 Specific denial. Every allegation of fact in the plaint, if not denied specifically or by necessary implication, or stated to be not admitted in the pleading of the defendant, shall be taken to be admitted except as against a person under disability; Provided that the Court may in its discretion require any fact so admitted to be proved otherwise that by such admission.</u>

27. The above findings find support from a good number of judicial pronouncements by both the Divisions of this Court. Our apex court in the case of Zafela Begum vs Atikulla 16 BLC (AD) 46 unanimously held that " ------------- The written statement must not only deal with specifically, the defendant must also answer the point of substance. If his denial of fact is not specific but evasive, the said fact shall be taken to be admitted. In such event, the admission itself being proof no further proof is necessary."

28. The trial court appears to have committed a patent illegality in laying over emphasis on RS Khatian No. 354 prepared and published in the name of Alimon Nesa who had no subsisting interest in the suit land at the time of RS operation. The trial court's illegality is fortified by its uncalled for, unsolicited, gratuitous and unduly lengthy discussion and finding on the said RS Khatian in the absence of any plea taken or evidence adduced by the defendants or issue taken thereon and, as such, the same is in direct conflict with the entrenched legal principle that RS Khatian is without any presumptive value of correctness as our Appellate Division held in Guru Charan Mondal vs Sree Bhaba Sindhu Sarkar 13 MLR (AD) 6 in the following terms:

"State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950—

Section 144- Record of rights in SA and RS Khatian do not confer any title- Kabala deed prevails over record of rights. "

29. On the question of possession it is found that all the 3 (three) PWs in unison deposed that the plaintiffs have been enjoying and possessing the suit land by erecting dwelling houses and shops thereon and inducting tenants therein, and the defendants could not extract anything to the contrary by cross-examining them.

30. Reverting to the submissions advanced from the defendant-petitioners as to the lack of schedule of the impugned deeds, lack of cause of action and partial decree passed in the instant suit for declaration simpliciter, I am constrained to hold that schedule 'Kha' to the plaint contains all the necessary particulars of the impugned deeds i.e. the name of the parties, the date, number and nature of the deeds, and the volume number and the pages thereof in which those deeds are copied. It appears from paragraphs 10 and 12 of the plaint and the testimony of the PW 1 Md Azizur Rahman that the plaintiffs mentioned specific dates of cause of action of the suit. Moreover, the trial court itself found that "The cause of action narrated in the plaint is substantiated by PW 1 and by other witnesses of the plaintiff", but the defendants did not file any cross appeal against the said observation of the trial court. With regard to the partial decree passed by the lower appellate court, it is found that the appellate court took much pain in ascertaining the actual quantum of land the plaintiffs are entitled to, upon calculation of the shares of their predecessors subsequent to their transfer/s and thus, I am of the considered view that the submissions advanced by the petitioners, Advocates are devoid of merit being directly contrary to the pleadings of the parties, evidence and other materials-on-record and the provisions of law holding the field and therefore, the said submissions being altogether new, fresh and unique in nature for having not been raised before the courts below earlier, do not deserve any consideration by or interference from this Court.

31. In the course of hearing, on 28-3-2017 the defendant-petitioners filed a supplementary affidavit alleging that the signature of the trial judge in Exhibit-15 does not match with his other signatures as appearing in Exhibits 1-24 and 16-49, and that Exhibit 50 is not signed by the said judge and, as such, the same is prepared as a second thought. Again, on 29-3-2017 the petitioners filed an application seeking a direction upon the Registrar of the Supreme Court of Bangladesh, High Court Division to send Exhibit-15 to a handwriting expert for his opinion on the genuineness of the signature of the trial judge.

32. 1 have compared the signature of the trial judge in Exhibit-15 with his other admitted signatures available on record and upon such comparison, I found a very slight variation in the signature of the trial judge in the said exhibit and such trivial variation in varied situations being quite natural for any human being, does not affect the merit of the case or jurisdiction of the court. Coming to the question of lack of signature of the trial judge on Exhibit-50, I hold that such an omission is a bona fide mistake of the court itself as opposed to any fault or laches on the part of the plaintiffs themselves and, as such, that mistake of the trial court is curable under sections 99 and 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure. Section 99 of the Code reads as follows:

Section 99. No decree to be reversed or modified for error or irregularity not affecting merits or jurisdiction---

No decree shall be reversed or substantially varied, nor shall any case be remanded, in appeal on account of any misjoinder of parties or causes of action or any error, defect or irregularity in any proceedings in the suit, not affecting the merits of the case or the jurisdiction of the Court.

33. In the case of Arshed Ali Sikder (Md) vs Gourango Chanra Shil 57 DLR 635 it has been held that "Mere omission to sign and seal exhibits or deposition sheet does not affect the merit of the case nor the jurisdiction of the court and such omissions are mere defects or irregularities in the procedure and not an illegality when section 99 of the Code of Civil Procedure aims to prevent such procedural technicalities. Non-compliance of the procedure for marking the exhibits and to prepare the exhibits list does not destroy the validity of the Court proceeding."

34. The Appellate Division in the case of Keramat Ali Bhuiyan being dead his heirs, Shahida Khanam vs Ramizuddin Ahmed Bhuiyan 43 DLR (AD) 58 held that "When an injury is caused to a party due to any mistake or default committed by a court or its officers, it is not only the right but also the duty of the court to correct its own mistake."

35. In the case of Abdul Mannan Sikder vs Matilal Dhupi 18 BLD 318 = 50 DLR 403 it has been held that "The Court has inherent power to rectify its own mistake or any mistake committed by any Court official causing prejudice to any particular party for no fault of its own, by resorting to the provision of section 151 CPC. A party cannot be made to suffer for the mistake done by the Court and the aggrieved party cannot be pushed to take recourse to any ardourous, costly and time-consuming exercise for rectifying such a mistake. In such circumstances, exercise of power under section 151 of the Code is not only permissible but also imperative for preventing an injustice."

<u>36. In the wake of the above legal provision, principle and precedents, I cannot remain silent about the sufferings of the plaintiffs for no fault of their own, rather in exercise of revisional jurisdiction under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure this Court is not only empowered and competent to undo the wrong done to them, but also it is imperative and obligatory on me to rectify the mistake in the interest of justice, and, as such, Exhibit-50 as submitted by the plaintiffs before the trial court is treated as being duly signed by trial judge. This exercise of power also finds support from the decisions reported in 51 DLR 493, 53 DLR 217, 49 DLR 414, and 19 BLC 649. In this connection 1 cannot resist myself from the temptation to quote the ratio given in the case of Abdus Sailor on being dead his heirs: Sayera Khatun vs Abdun Noor 49 DLR 414:</u>

<u>"This Court in revisional jurisdiction is not powerless and can for the ends of justice rectify any illegality committed by the inferior court even if such defect is not pointed out by either party.</u>

37. Moreover, the objection raised before me to Exhibits 15 and 50 was never raised before the courts below although the defendants had ample opportunity to do so and they have not offered any explanation for their failure to raise such objection earlier and, as such, the supplementary affidavit dated 28-3-2017 is discarded from consideration and the application for expert opinion on Exhibit 15 is hereby rejected for the reasons stated above.

38. Upon perusal of the judgment of the trial court it appears that it recorded certain wrong, illegal and perverse findings on the question of possession, limitation, maintainability of the suit and burden of proof in total disregard of the pleadings and evidence of the contending parties, other materials available in record and the provisions of law. Again, while dismissing the suit it failed to appreciate that the weight of evidence and preponderance of documents is in favour of the plaintiffs and against the defendants and, as such, it ought to have decreed the suit.

39. For the discussions made and reasons stated above, it appears to me that the lower appellate, court as the final court of fact correctly allowed the appeal on some cogent, legal and well-founded findings and reasonings upon discussion of all the issues revolving round the suit and, as such, the impugned judgment and decree being a proper judgment of reversal, does not call for any interference.

40. Accordingly, I find no merit in the Rule for which it fails. In the result, the Rule is discharged without any order as to cost and the impugned judgment and decree dated 12-7-2010 (decree signed on 19-7-2017) passed by the Additional District Judge, Second Court, Gazipur in Title Appeal No. 133 of 2009 allowing the appeal and setting aside the judgment and decree dated 4-6-2009 (decree signed on 10-6-2009) passed by the Assistant Judge, Second Court, Gazipur in Title Suit No. 3256 of 2008 dismissing the suit is hereby affirmed.

Send down the lower Court record along with a copy of this judgment to the Court concerned at once.

End.

lawyer:
Md Khalilur Rahman with Junaed Hossen Khan with Md Rashidul Karim Advocates—For the Petitioners. 

Manzill Murshed, Advocate—For the Respondent No. 1. 

AKM Farhan, Advocate—For the Respondent.

full_judgment:
Gobinda Chandra Tagore J : On an application under Article 102 of the Constitution of the People's Republic of Bangladesh, the Rule Nisi was issued calling upon the respondents to show cause as to why constituting a 7 (seven) member committee comprising of respondent Nos.2 to 8 under Memo No. 31.036.033.00. 00.221.2010-409(7) dated 27-7-2011 (Annexure-D) issued under the signature of respondent No.9 for investigating the finally published Dhaka City Survey Record-of-Rights in respect of 191 mouzas to ascertain the genuinity of such publication and to uphold/cancel the same and the report of the said committee dated 22-5-2012 (Annexure-E) and also the office order under Memo No. মপ/08/2011/83 dated 26-1-2012 issued by respondent No.10 (Annexure-F) forming two committees to investigate the alleged irregularities of the officials engaged in preparing and finally publishing the said Record-of-Rights, and thereby taking departmental actions against the petitioner and/or to initiate criminal cases under the Anti Corruption Law shall not be declared to have been done/issued without lawful authority and is of no legal effect and as to why the respondents shall not be directed to interfere with the quasi-judicial functions of the field level officers engaged in preparing and finally publishing the Record-of-Rights under the provisions of State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 and Tenancy Rules, 1955 in any manner, whatsoever other than under the provisions of the aforesaid Act and Rules and/or why such other or further order or orders as to this Court may seem fit and proper, shall not be passed.

2. Pending hearing of the Rule, the operation of the office order dated 26-1-2012 (Annexure-F) was stayed for a period of 4 (four) months.

3. The respondents were also restrained from giving effect to the recommendations made vide report dated 22-5-2012 (Annexure-E) and the said respondents are also restrained from interfering with the quasi-judicial functions of the field level non cadre officers/employees engaged in preparing and publishing the record-of-rights under the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 and Tenancy Rules, 1955 for a period of 4 (four) months. Subsequently, the order of stay and that of the order of restraint were extended from time to time.

4. Shortly stated the relevant facts necessary for disposal of the Rule are as follows:

The petitioner No.1 is the President of Assistant Settlement Officer Welfare Association and the petitioner Nos.2 and 3 are Secretary and Vice-President of the same Association of Dhaka unit. All of them are serving under the office of the Directorate of Land Records and Surveys as Non-Cadre Servants of the Government and were engaged in the preparation and publication of the recent Dhaka City Survey Khatians following the Dhaka City Survey, which were finally prepared and published in the Gazette Notification on different dates. The Directorate of Land Records and Surveys is empowered to prepare and publish the record-of-rights as per order issued by the Government from time to time by issuing Gazette Notification under section 144 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950. The employees and officers engaged in preparation and publication of the record-of-rights of that office are divided into two categories- Non-Cadre Service Holders starting from Chainman to Assistant Settlement Officer i.e. Chainman, Badar Amin, Sarder Amin, Halka Officer/Sub-Assistant Settlement Officer and Assistant Settlement Officer/Circle Officer and the other group belongs to the Cadre Service, who are deputed to the Directorate. The preparation and publication of the record-of-rights are quasi-judicial functions under the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950, the Tenancy Rules, 1955, Survey and Settlement Manual, 1935, the Survey Act, 1875 and Technical Rules, 1957. The Rules 26-31 of the Tenancy Rules, 1955 are the main rules for preparing record-of-rights. Like judicial protection Act, 1850, section 77(1) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 and the rule 39 of the Tenancy Rule, 1955 and also the circular No. ভূঃমঃ/শাঃ-২(অডিট আপত্তি)-৭/২০০৬-৩৯০/১(৯০)dated 2-6-2008 issued by the Ministry of Land have given a safeguard to the persons involved in preparing and publishing the record-of-rights. The record-of-rights of Dhaka City Survey of 191 mouzas prepared under the Dhaka City Survey have already been completed and published in the Bangladesh Gazette as per rule 34 of the Tenancy Rules, 1955 as well as, as per section 144(7) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950, except some of the khatians of each mouzas against which Writ Petitions or Civil proceedings are pending. When the dispute on finally publishing the record-of-rights were being adjudicated by the Land Survey Tribunals, the Ministry of Land suddenly issued the impugned office order bearing No. 31.036.033.00.00.221. 2010-409 dated 27-7-2011 forming an enquiry committee consisting of the respondent Nos.2-8 for giving an opinion either for affirming or cancelling the finally prepared and published City Survey Khatians of 191 Mouzas under the Dhaka City Survey after 5 years of publication of the same in the Gazette Notification. The said enquiry committee submitted the impugned report dated 22-5-2012 as contained in Annexure-E. In the said report, it was, amongst other, opined that approximately 2815.00 acres of the land of the Government were not recorded in the name of the Government while, most of those properties earlier belonged to the Court of Wards and subsequently, in the name of the private persons by operation of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950. On receiving the said report dated 22-5-2012, the respondent No. 10, DGDLRS issued the impugned Memo No. মপ/০৮/২০১১/৮৩ dated 26-1-2012 forming two committees-one consisting of respondent Nos.11-15 and the other consisting of respondent Nos.16-19 to enquire into the matter in order to find out the irregularities in not recording the Government land and also to take action against the persons involved in such preparation and publication of the record-of-rights by starting departmental proceeding as well as by filing anti-corruption case against them. The petitioners being aggrieved by the said impugned orders and enquiry report contained in Annexures D, E and F filed the instant Writ Petition and obtained the Rule and the orders of stay and restraint.

5. The respondent No.1, the Ministry of Land contested the Rule by filing an affidavit-in-opposition by denying the material allegations made in the Writ Petition and contending, inter alia, that the respondents, including the respondent Nos.11, 16 and 17 are not only responsible for management and administration of the Directorate or they are not only the supervising officer but they are also engaged in preparing and publishing record-of-rights. Therefore, the allegation made by the petitioners that the respondents are interfering with the so-called quasi-judicial function is not true. The superior officers starting from the post of Charge Officer of the DGLRS are legally authorized to supervise the official activities of the sub-ordinates of the Directorate. They also exercise their revenue powers for preparing and publishing of the record-of-rights in accordance with law as well as the instructions of the Government passed from time to time. Section 149(4) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 authorizes the Board of Land Administration to pass any order for correction of any entry in a record-of-rights maintained under Part-V of the Act or in a settlement-roll prepared and finally published under Part-V thereof. If there is any bonafide mistake, the superior officer of the Directorate may interfere with the functions and activities of the petitioners and others as per the provision of section 149(4) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950; rules 27, 28, 31, 36, 38, 39, 40, 41, 42, 42A 42B, and 44 of the Tenancy Rules, 1955, the Technical Rules, and Chapter (iv) Rule 16, 19, 32 and Chapter (viii) rule-20 of Instructions of the Settlement Department, 1957. The position of a DGLRS is clearly manifested in rule 12 of Survey and Settlement Manual, 1935. The Government can issue circulars, memorandums and other instructions as per rules of Business and Allocation of Business and make rules under section 152 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950. Therefore, issuing circulars etc. by the Government or the Directorate for making it responsible and accountable is within the legal authority of the Government and the Directorate. Section 77(1) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 provides safeguard to the petitioners and others only if the acts are done in good faith. The circular dated 2-6-2008 was issued as a directive for the audit team to follow the same during auditing the field level offices. Rule 39 of the Tenancy Rules, 1955 authorizes the Revenue Officer with the additional designation, Settlement Officer or Assistant Settlement Officer to exercise power like a Civil Court. The Rules do not give any immunity to the officials from accountability for their activities. The Revenue Officers and others engaged in preparing and publishing the record-of-rights cannot escape the responsibility and liability in securing the public interest in preparing the records-of-the public property. The respondents have every authority to look into whether the petitioners and others had any negligence or committed any deviation from the assigned tasks in preparing the records-of-land properly. Every judicial or quasi-judicial officer has a right to pass an order but it must be guided by the existing laws. The respondent Nos.11, 16 and 17 are empowered to exercise revenue powers and accordingly, they can look into the activities of their subordinate officers. The authority can hold any enquiry or form any committee to look into the allegations of any mischief or gross irregularities and negligence or intentionally done wrong activities committed by any of subordinate revenue officers at any stage of the survey. There are allegations published in different dailies that some revenue officers have recorded the land belonged to different public agencies in the name of some unscrupulous private persons although the previous record i.e. RS Record was in the name of public agencies and thus, helped misappropriation of the public lands by the land grabbers. The respondents are constitutionally bound to look into the serious allegations in public interest in order to take appropriate measures for recovery of the public property and also to take punitive measures against the persons found responsible for the misdeeds and causing losses to the state and public in general. There being serious allegation of irregularities against the finally published record-of-rights of 191 mouzas of City Survey, the respondents formed committee to scrutinize/investigate into the legal aspects as to whether there was any scope for cancellation of the records to redress the public sufferings and accordingly, the enquiry committee was formed by the Memo dated 27-7-2011. Moreover, no penal decision was taken against the petitioners. Accordingly, they cannot be aggrieved thereby and come before this Court under Article 102 of the Constitution for that purpose. No law or any rule gives any immunity to any officials involved in doing irregularities in the name of quasi-judicial functions or any public-office-functions. The petitioners having done gross irregularities in publishing the record-of-rights cannot claim the safeguards under the law and circular as has been claimed by them. The impugned orders were very much within the purview of law. The impugned report contains the facts based on the case studies. The petitioners could have sought relief through normal official procedure and there was nothing to worry about the said impugned order and reports unless he or she is found to have done anything wrong in malafide intention. Hence, the Writ Petition is not maintainable.

6. Having placed the Writ Petition, Mr Md Khalilur Rahman along with Mr Junaed Hossen Khan and Mr Md Rashidul Karim, learned Advocate for the petitioners submits that since the record-of-rights prepared finally has already been published in the official Gazette, the Government including the respondents have no legal authority under section 144 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act to cancel the same and the aggrieved persons including any Government agencies can take recourse to law before the Land Survey Tribunal for correcting the errors, if any, in preparing the said record-of-rights and, as such, the impugned orders as contained in Annexures D and E and the report prepared in pursuance thereof as contained in Annexure-E are liable to be declared to have been passed or prepared without lawful authority and are of no legal effect.

7. Then, the learned Advocate for the petitioners submits that the petitioners and others engaged in preparing and publishing, the record-of-rights being protected by section 77(1) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 as well as by rule 39 of the Tenancy Rules, 1955 issuance of the impugned orders as contained in Annexure D and F and the enquiry report prepared in pursuance thereof as contained in Annexure-E are liable to be declared to have been done without lawful authority and are of no legal effect.

8. The learned Advocate for the petitioners further submits that the petitioners haying performed quasi judicial functions according to law, they are not answerable to their superior in this regard and, as such, the impugned orders were issued and the impugned enquiry report submitted in pursuance thereof are liable to be declared to have been done without lawful authority and are of no legal effect.

9. On the other hand, Mr Manzill Murshed, learned Advocate for the respondent No.1 submits that the petitioners and others involved in preparing and publishing the record-of-rights are not immune in law and they are legally bound to discharge their official duties in accordance with law and, as such, there is no legal bar to initiate any proceeding in order to look into whether they have performed their duties in accordance with law or in malafide intention and if anybody is found responsible, they should be taken to book while, in the present Writ Petition, no departmental proceeding has yet been started against the petitioners, not any punitive measure has yet been taken and, as such, there being no cause of action in the Writ Petition, the Rule is liable to be discharged.

10. The learned Advocate for the respondent No.1 further submits that in order to enquire into the allegation brought against the preparation and publication of the Dhaka City Survey Records, the respondents upon issuing Annexure D and E only formed committee to enquire into the allegation and the committee submitted its report as contained in Annexure-E with the clear findings that no wholesale proceeding or punitive measure should be taken but such measures would be taken against the persons, who are found liable and there are only allegation against the petitioners and others and nobody has yet been found even liable and, as such, the Writ Petition being a premature one, the Rule is liable to be discharged.

11. Then, the learned Advocate for the respondent No.1 submits that as per the preliminary enquiry about 2815.056 acres of land of the Government or the Government agencies appertaining to 191 mouzas have been illegally recorded in the name of the private persons through the petitioners and others and, as such, it is the constitutional as well as the legal duty of the respondents to get those record corrected in the name of the Government or the Government agencies whatever may be the case and for that purpose, the impugned orders were issued for ascertaining the liability of the persons involved therein, but the liabilities of the persons including the petitioners have yet not been asserted let alone any proceeding has been drawn against them and therefore, there being no cause of action, the Rule is liable to be discharged.

12. We have perused the Writ Petition, the affidavit-in-opposition and the documents annexed thereto and heard the learned Advocate for the petitioners.

13. The petitioners and others were involved in preparing and publishing the Dhaka City record-of-rights following the Dhaka City Survey. The record-of-rights have already been finalized and published in the official Gazette. As per the case of the respondents, there were serious allegations of irregularities and illegalities in conducting survey and preparing and publishing the record-of-rights. Even 2815.0569 acres of land appertaining to 191 mouza of Dhaka have been wrongly and illegally recorded in the name of private persons through the petitioners and others, who were involved in conducting the survey and preparing and publishing the record-of-rights. In order to ascertain the liability of the persons involved in such illegalities or irregularities, the respondent No.1, Ministry of Land issued the impugned office order dated 27-7-2011 as contained in Annexure-D forming an Enquiry Committee for a recommendation whether the record-of-rights of the said 191 mouzas should be maintained or cancelled. The Enquiry Committee upon enquiry submitted a report dated 22-5-2012 and the said report was forwarded to the Secretary, Ministry of Land by the impugned Memo dated 22-5-2012. But it appears from the said report dated 22-5-2012 that it was an incomplete report and thereby the liability of the persons involved in preparing such illegal and erroneous record-of-rights was not ascertained. Accordingly, the Directorate of Land Record and Survey by the impugned office order dated 26-1-2012 formed two committees underlining the terms of reference of the committee as under:

“কমিটি নিম্নবর্ণিত কাজ করবে।

(ক) ঢাকা মহানগর ১৯১ টি মৌজার মধ্যে যে সকল মৌজায় খাল রয়েছে তা শনাক্ত করে এ সকল মৌজাগুলোকে সমান ২টি ভাগে ভাগ করে প্রতিটি কমিটি ১ টি ভাগের উপর কাজ করবে। ১ম কমিটি অগ্রাধিকার ভিত্তিতে কল্যাণপুর খাল ও কল্যাণপুর ক, খ, গ, ঘ, ঙ খাল এবং

২য় কমিটি অগ্রাধিকার ভিত্তিতে হাজারীবাগ খাল, ডুমনি খাল, সেগুনবাগিচা খাল, গুলশান- বনানী খাল এর কাজ সম্পন্ন করবে।

(খ) প্রতিটি কমিটি গুরুত্পূর্ণ সরকারি স্থাপনা, খাল, খাস জমি ইত্যাদি আর, এস রেকর্ড ও প্রয়োজনে সি,এস রেকর্ড, রেজিষ্ট্রার-২ পর্যালোচনা করে মহানগর জরিপে কোন মৌজার কোন দাগে কতটুকু বিভিন্ন দপ্তরের মালিকানাধীন সরকারী জমি ব্যক্তি মালিকানায় রেকর্ড হয়েছে, তা নির্ধারণ করবে।

(গ) মহানগর জরিপের ওয়ার্কিং কমিটির যাচাই করে এ সকল জমি কোন স্তরে কোন কর্মচারী ও কর্মকর্তার দুর্নীতি, গাফিলতি ও দায়িত্হীনতার কারণে তা ব্যক্তি মালিকানায় রেকর্ড হয়েছে তাদেরকে চিহ্নিত করে সুস্পষ্ট অভিযোগ আনয়ন করবে।

বিষয়টি গুরুত্বপূর্ণ ও জরুরী ।”

14. It was also observed therein that upon ascertaining the liability of the persons involved apart from taking departmental action, cases may be filed with the Anti-Corruption Commission upon obtaining approval thereof from the Ministry of Land.

<u>15. It appears from the Writ Petition that the petitioners filed the Writ Petition with an apprehension only that upon such enquiry, departmental and punitive measures may be taken against them. But it appears from the said office order dated 26-1-2012, Annexure-F that it was intended not to take punitive measures against all the persons, who were involved in preparing and publishing the record-of-rights but only against the persons who are liable for committing any irregularity and illegality. Thus, it appears from the said impugned orders as contained in Annexures D, E and F that the Ministry of Land or the Directorate of Land Record and Survey has yet not completed the enquiry fixing the liability of the persons responsible for any illegality. However, once the record-of-rights, whether it was prepared wrongly or rightly has already been published in the official Gazette, the respondents have no legal authority under section 144 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 to cancel the same by any administrative order. The same can only be cancelled or altered or corrected by the competent Court of civil jurisdiction.</u>

16. However, the Government has every legal authority to conduct a new survey in respect of the said 191 mouzas of Dhaka City in order to record the land appertaining to those mouzas correctly.

17. In such facts and circumstances, it appears that the Writ Petition is pre-mature while, the respondents have no legal authority to cancel the record-of-rights published finally.

18. However, the respondents shall not file any criminal case against any employee before ascertaining his/her liability in accordance with law.

19. In such facts and circumstances, the Rule is disposed of.

However, there would be no order as to costs.

End.

full_judgment:
This rule has been issued calling upon the opposite parties Nos.1-10 to show cause as to why the judgment dated 18th August, 1997 of the learned Additional District Judge, Hobiganj in Title Appeal No. 86 of 1985 should not be set aside.

2. Girindra Chandra Bonik, the predecessor of the present petitioners as plaintiffs instituted Title Suit No. 55 of 1981 before the Subordinate Judge, Hobiganj impleading the predecessor of the present opposite parties Nos. 1-9 and other opposite parties as defendants under Order XXI, rule 103 of the Code of Civil Procedure for establishment of right and possession in the suit premises.

3. The case of the predecessor of the petitioner is that late Girindra Chandra Bonik entered into an agreement with late Nandalal Roy for purchase of the suit property for a consideration of Taka 6000. Pursuant thereto the said Nandalal Roy on receipt of a part consideration executed a kabala in favour of the opposite party No. 11 for and on behalf of the said Girindra Chandra Bonik with an assurance that he would register the kabala on receipt of the income tax clearance certificate and the balance of the purchase price from the said Girindra Chandra Bonik. The said Nandalal Roy did not take steps for obtaining income tax clearance certificate on receipt of the balance of the consideration of sale price. As such the said Girindra Chandra Banik instituted Title Suit No. 13 of 1963 for Specific performance of contract against the said Nandalal Roy, who filed a written statement in the said suit and upon an application being filed by said Girindra Chandra Banik a temporary injunction was issued against the said Nandalal Roy restraining him from transferring the suit property. Nandalal Roy was examined on commission on 12th June, 1966 and in cross-examination he admitted the execution of the kabala as aforesaid. Thereafter, the said Nandalal Roy did not contest the suit. Girindra Chandra Banik obtained permission under the disturbed persons rehabilitation Ordinance and deposited in Court the said permission and the balance consideration money. Thereafter the suit was taken up for hearing but as none appeared on behalf of the said Nandalal Roy, the Court passed an ex parte decree on 20 July, 1966 in favour of the said Girindra Chandra Banik. Thereafter, the said Nandalal Roy filed an application under Order IX, rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure for restoration of the suit in Miscellaneous Case No. 16 of 1966; during the pendency of the said Miscellaneous Case Nandalal Roy died on 12th November, 1966. The said Miscellaneous Case was dismissed for non prosecution. The further case of the petitioners is that in execution of the said decree, the said Girindra Chandra Banik obtained a kabala executed by the only son and heir of the said Nandalal Roy, and obtained delivery of possession through Court on 30th April, 1969 evicting the men of late Mobashwar Ali who were in possession of the suit property. On the same day the evicted persons came in a body and trespassed into the suit property assaulting the said Girindra Chandra Banik and his wife opposite party No.11 and on receipt of information, the police appeared in the scene and drove out the trespassers and restored the possession to the said Girindra Chandra Banik who remained in possession and after his death, the petitioners and opposite party No. 11 and 12 are still in possession of the suit property. The further case of the petitioners is that the said Mobashwar Ali instituted Miscellaneous Case No.71 of 1969 under Order XXI, rule 101 of the Code of Civil Procedure which though contested by the said Girindra Chandra Banik, was allowed on 9th July, 1980 directing restoration of possession to him. Against the said order Girindra Chandra Banik commenced a proceeding against the said Mobashwar Ali and the opposite party No. 10 claiming a right to the suit property on the basis of the aforesaid decree, consequent kabala and delivery of possession through Court which was registered as Title Suit No. 55 of 1981 in the Court of the Subordinate Judge, Habiganj.

4. Mobashwar AU, the predecessor of opposite party Nos. 1-9 contested the suit by filing written statement contending inter alia that the aforesaid Nandalal Roy and his younger brother Jogendra Lal Roy, father of the opposite party No. 10 were members of a Joint Hindu family and Nandalal Roy purchased the suit land with the joint family fund, and, as such, he owned it in equal shares. There was an amicable partition between the brothers by an unregistered deed of partition dated 1st October, 1960 wherein the said Jogendra Lal Roy got the suit property in his share. The said Jogendra Lal Roy thereafter instituted partition suit No.28 of 1968 which was decreed on the basis of the said deed of partition dated 1st October, 1960. The said Jogendra Lai Roy thereafter executed a kabala in favour of the said Mobashwar Ali whose man came in possession of the suit property and were evicted in course of delivery of possession through Court of the suit property on 30th April, 1969 in execution of the alleged decree in Title Suit No. 13 of 1963. In the foregoing situation the said Girindra Chandra Bonik did not acquire any right, title and interest in the suit property.

5. By his judgment dated 3st March, 1985, the learned Subordinate Judge on consideration of documentary and oral evidence adduced by the parties, decreed the suit in favour of the said Girindra Chandra Bonik on the finding that the said Mobashwar Ali failed to prove his case.

6. The appellate Court reversed the decision and finding of the trial Court by judgment and decree dated 18.08.1997 against which the instant rule.

7. Mr. Momtaz Uddin Fakir learned advocate, appearing for the petitioners submits that Order 21 Rule 103 of the Code of Civil Procedure is not appealable and this vital point has been raised before the appellate Court but the appellate Court without adverting and considering that vital point allowed the appeal which caused serious miscarriage of justice. He next submits that learned Additional District Judge committed error in reversing the decision of the Court of 1st instance without reversing the findings recorded by it who arrived at a decision on true and proper consideration of the oral and documentary evidence. He next submits that the appellate Court failed to consider that Nandalal Roy being purchaser of the suit land by sale deed dated 8th Jaistho 1360 BS by his own money and benefit entered into agreement with the plaintiff for sale on 4-7-1962 but subsequently Nandalal resiled from his agreement and refused to execute and register deed of sale for which the plaintiff by filing Title Suit No. 13 of 1963 got decree in his favour which has been duly executed through execution case. The plea of suit property being jointly owned by Nandalal Roy and Jogendra Lal Roy have not been proved by evidence but the appellate Court failed to advert that vital aspect of the case and erroneously allowed the appeal which caused failure of justice.

8. Having gone through the pleadings, exhibits and other documents it appears that Girindra Chandra Bonik, the predecessor of the present petitioners instituted Title Suit No. 13 of 1963 before the first Court of Subordinate Judge, Sylhet for specific performance of contract wherein Nanda Lal Roy made appearance, contested the suit by filing written statement and subsequently deposed on commission on 16-6-1966 admitting transfer of suit land in favor of the plaintiff of the suit. As he failed to appear subsequently, the suit was decreed exparte and for setting aside the said exparte decree Nandalal Roy filed Miscellaneous Case No. 16 of 1966. On the death of Nandalal Roy his daughter Sushama Bala Roy claiming herself as heir of late Nanda Lal made prayer of substituting herself in the said miscellaneous case but subsequently it is detected that Nanda Lal Roy has a son namely Nagendra

Lal Roy and, as such, application for substitution of Sushama Bala Roy was rejected and consequent civil revision being Civil Revision No. 103 of 1968 filed before the High Court Division was also rejected. Thereafter Girindra Chandra Bonik filed Execution Case No. 10 of 1967 and got a deed of sale executed and registered and by filing title Execution Case No.8 of 1969 got delivery of possession on 30-4-1969.

9. It further appears that Jogendra Lal Roy, the brother of Nanda Lal Roy filed Partition Suit No. 28 of 1968 claiming joint family property with Nanda Lal Roy and the said partition suit was decreed exparte on 26-4-1968. Thereafter defendant No.1 by filing Miscellaneous Case No. 71 of 1969 under Order XXI, rules 101 of the Code of Civil Procedure prayed for restoration of possession purportedly claiming the suit land by virtue of baina patra having executed by Jogendra Lal Roy dated 7-12-1963 and after hearing the said case was allowed ordering restoration of possession. Challenging the said judgment and order, the petitioners filed Title Suit No.51 of 1981 before the Subordinate Judge, Habiganj under Order XXI, rules 103 of the Code of Civil Procedure.

10. The trial Court in his judgment held that there is no convincing evidence that Nanda Lal Roy and Jogendra Lal jointly held and possessed the suit land. The trial court with reference to DW 4 Abul Hossain, DW 5 Chunu Mia and DW 10 Shaheb Mia held that Nanda Lal resided in the suit premises till his death and defendant No.1failed to prove that on the basis of baina patra he went to the possession of the suit land on 7-12-1963. The trial court with reference to DW 1 Azizul Haque found that he himself and other persons resided in the suit land time to time. The Court also discussed the evidence of DWs 5, 6, 8, 9, 10 and 11 and held that there are anomalies in their deposition regarding possession of the suit land and that defendant No. 1 did not enter into the suit land by virtue of the baina patra dated 7-12-1963, rather the men of defendant No.1 came to the suit land after the death of Nanda Lal Roy. The trial Court also disbelieved the baina patra as claimed by defendant No. 1 and also found that Jogendra Lal Roy never claimed the suit land during the lifetime of Nanda Lal Roy. The trial Court also held that the plaintiff after getting decree in a suit for specific performance of contract got kabala through court and also obtained possession by filing execution case. The Court found that Jogendra Lal Roy filed Title Suit No. 28 of 1968 in the third Court of Munsif, Habigonj and obtained preliminary decree on 26-4-1968 impleading Nanda Lal's son Nagendra Lal Roy as defendant No.1 and Nanda Lal's daughter as defendant No. 2 although the address of defendant No.1 was shown at Habigonj town but it is claimed that his whereabouts was not known and Sushama Bala was no legal heir of Nanda Lal Roy and, as such, the decree has been obtained by practising fraud and for unknown reason Sushama Bala did not contest the suit. The trial Court by elaborate discussion also held that there is no trace that Jogendra Lal Roy and Nanda Lal Roy jointly held and possessed the suit land as member of joint family and, as such, alleged purported unregistered Batwaranama and other documents shown by defendant No.1 are nothing but collusive and created papers and accordingly the trial Court decreed the suit in favour of the plaintiff upholding plaintiff's possession.

11. Before the Appellate Court contention was raised on behalf of the petitioner-respondent that an order passed in the proceeding under rule 103 of Order XXI of the Code of Civil Procedure is conclusive and no appeal is maintainable against such order but the appellate Court disregarding the legal provision and established principle held that since it is a regular suit and decree is drawn thereon as such appeal is maintainable. Such view is patently illegal and not sustainable. For proper appreciation, rule 103 of Order XXI is reproduced below:

"Any party not being a judgment-debtor against whom an order is made under rule 98. rule 99 or rule 101 may institute a suit to establish the right which he claims to the present possession of the property; but, subject to the result of such suit (if any), the order shall be conclusive."

12. In the case of Nirmal Chandra Choudhury vs Nikunja Behari Biswas 6 DLR 333 it is held that:

"Under what authority, with due respect to the learned Judges in those cases, they came to this conclusion it is difficult for me to ascertain. Section 115 does not prevent any revision on the ground that there is another remedy. Rule 103 contains the words "subject to the result of such suit, (if any)" the order passed under Rules 98, 99 and 101 will be conclusive. The word 'conclusive' means no appeal lies but it does not mean that High Court cannot revise the order of the Court passed under Rules 98, 99 and 101 of the Code of Civil Procedure."

<u>13. Apart from this, right to prefer appeal is statutory right but in the instant matter rule 103 of Order XXI of the Code of Civil Procedure mandates that order passed under the said section will be final meaning hereby that there is no scope of appeal which is clearly reiterated in 6 DLR 333. Besides jurisdiction cuts the root of the matter and if the Court got no jurisdiction everything shall fall through. In the case of Managing Director, Rupali Bank limited vs Tafazal Hossain 44 DLR (AD) 260 it is held that:</u>

"Jurisdiction of a Court goes to the very root of a matter brought before it, and if the Court got no jurisdiction, everything shall fall through. We are surprised to find that the learned Single Judge in this case held that the Court's jurisdiction is a mere technicality and that it is the merit of a case that matters. The Court which got no jurisdiction over a matter shall not go into the merit of the matter. The view expressed by the learned Single Judge regarding jurisdiction is grievously erroneous. Similarly, the other view of the learned Single Judge is that in the present position of section 115 CPC, the question of `jurisdiction' is replaced by 'error of law' is equally faulty. The assistant Judge having no jurisdiction over the matter the decree passed in the suit is void."

14. So it is crystal clear that the opposite party committed error in preferring appeal against the impugned judgment and decree passed by the Trial Court and, as such, judgment passed in such appeal is not sustainable in the eye of law. Consequently, the judgment and decree passed by the trial Court remained unassailed.

15. The appellate Court also failed to consider that Girindra Chandra Bonik by filing Title Suit No. 13 of 1963 before the Subordinate Judge, Sylhet got a decree for specific performance of contract by virtue of baina patra dated 7-12-1963 which has not been denied by Nanda Lal Roy and by virtue of the said decree he got kabala and delivery of possession in the suit land by evicting the daughter of Nanda Lal and the other occupants of the suit land and since then the heirs of said Girindra Chandra Bonik i.e. the present petitioners are still in possession therein.

16. The appellate Court relied on the judgment and decree obtained by Jogendra Lal Roy in Title suit No.28 of 1968 whereby Jogendra Lal Roy got an exparte decree on 26-4-1968 for partition regarding the suit land and held that by said deed of partition Jogendra Lal Roy got a preliminary decree but appellate Court failed to consider that by virtue of a judgment and decree passed in a suit for specific performance of contract as mentioned above the suit land has been devolved upon the predecessor of the present petitioners who is succeeded by the present petitioners and admittedly they are in possession. The trial Court clearly held that the judgment and decree dated 26-4-1968 passed in Title Suit No. 28 of 1968 is outcome of fraud and forgery as it has been obtained in collusion with the daughter of Nanda Lai Roy without service of summons upon the son of Nanda Lal Roy namely Nogendra Lal Roy who is the actual successor-in-interest of Nanda Lal Roy and, as such, the opposite parties got no title or interest over the suit land but those vital facts also has not been controverted by the appellate Court who erroneously reversed the findings of the trial Court.

17. In the above factual scenarios it is clear that the judgment and decree passed by the appellate Court is not sustainable as per law. In fact the judgment and decree of the appellate Court is non-est in the eye of law and consequently the judgment and decree passed by the Court of first instance stands as an unassailed one.

18. In the above context, I find merit in the Rule and accordingly the Rule is made absolute without any order as to cost.

19. The order of status-quo granted at the time of issuance of the rule is hereby re-called and vacated.

Let a copy of the judgment along with the Lower Court record be sent to the concerned Court.

End.

lawyer:

parties:
Jannatul Maowa Runa and others ------------ Petitioners 
Vs.
AHM Roushan Ali Miah and others ----------- Opposite Parties
full_judgment:
At the instance of pre-emptees in Pre-emption Miscellaneous Case No. 9 of 2002, this Rule was issued calling upon the opposite party No. 1 to show cause as to why the judgement and order dated 15-11-2012 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, 1st Court, Bogra in Miscellaneous Appeal No. 82 of 2011 dismissing the appeal and thereby affirming the judgement and order dated 4-4-2011 passed by the learned Senior Assistant Judge, 1st Court, Bogra in Pre-emption Case No. 9 of 2002 allowing the pre-emption case should not be set-aside and/or pass such other or further order or orders as to this court may seem fit and proper.

2. At the time of issuance of the Rule, this court also stayed the operation of the impugned judgement and order dated 15-11-2012 passed in Miscellaneous Appeal No. 82 of 2011.

3. The salient facts leading to issuance of the Rule are:

4. The predecessor of the present-opposite party Nos. 1(a)-1(e) named AHM Roushan Ali Miah as pre-emptor filed the aforesaid pre-emption case for pre-empting the case land measuring an area of 17 decimals of land so described to the schedule of the petition for pre-emption.

5. The case of the pre-emptor as has been set out in this revisional application in precise is that, the case land originally belonged to one, Mofiz Pramanik and Mosirunesa. After the demise of Mosirunessa her husband, Mofiz inherited the property. While Mofiz had been enjoying title and possession over that land he transferred 10 decimals of land to one, Korban Ali on 4-9-1984. The pre-emptor then purchased 5 decimals of lands from Korban Ali on 26-11-1997 and thereby he became the co-sharer by purchase in the case holding. In further development, one Akbar Ali, the opposite party No. 4 to the pre-emption case, transferred 17 decimals of land to the opposite party No. 3 by disputed kabala that registered on 11-9-2001 though without serving any notice upon the pre-emptor-opposite party though the purchaser pre-emptees is the stranger-purchaser to the case holding. Pre-emptor came to learn about the disputed transfer on 3-10-2001 and after obtaining the certified copy of the said deed on 4-10-2011 filed the instant pre-emption case on 29-1-2002. It has further been stated in the petition for pre-emption that, if the pre-emptor had the knowledge about the said transaction. he would have purchased the same. Since the pre-emption case has been filed within the very statutory period of limitation so the pre-emptor is entitled to have the lands through pre-emption and hence the instant case.

6. Per contra, the present-petitioner as pre-emptee-purchaser contested the said Miscellaneous Case by filing a joint written statement denying all the material allegations so made in the petition for pre-emption contending, inter alia, that, one Akbar Ali had been in possession over 30 decimals of land on mutating his name in the khatian and while he had been enjoying title and possession over that 30 decimals of land he at first proposed the pre-emptor to sell the case land even the father of the pre-emptees named, Nazrul Islam also proposed the pre-emptor and his son to purchase the land but as they refused to purchase the same, the pre-emptees then purchased the case land by registered kabala dated 11-9-2001. Soon after purchasing the case land, the pre-emptees then started enjoying title and possession over the suit properties by planting various trees that cost Taka 65,000. It has further been stated that, there has been a Madrasha located in the case land though it was not made party in the case. It has then stated that, the vendor, Korban Ali who transferred 5 decimals of land upon purchasing 10 decimals of land had separated his jama before selling 5 decimals of land to the pre-emptor. It has stated in the written objection that, inspite of having no preferential right the pre-emptor filed the case having absolute knowledge about the disputed transfer. It has further been stated that, if the pre-emption case is allowed in that event, the pre-emptee Nos. 1-3 will suffer irreparable loss and injury and therefore the pre-emption case is liable to be dismissed.

7. In order to dispose of the said case, the learned Assistant Judge, framed as many as 4 different issues. The pre-emptors examined 3 witnesses while the pre-emptees-petitioners examined 2 witnesses in support of their respective case.

8. Apart from that, the pre-emptor produced several documents which were marked as exhibits and on the contrary, the pre-emptees-petitioners did not produce any document in support of their cases.

9. After conclusion of the trial, the learned Senior Assistant Judge, by it judgement and order dated 4-4-2011 allowed the pre-emption case on contest against the pre-emptees-purchaser Nos. 1-3 and exparte against the rest.

10. Challenging the said judgement and order passed by the trial court, the pre-emptees-petitioners then preferred an appeal being Miscellaneous Appeal No. 82 of 2011 before the learned District Judge, Bogra. The said appeal was however on being transferred heard by the learned Joint District Judge, 1st Court, Bogra.

11. The learned Joint District Judge, after hearing the parties to the appeal and on considering the materials and evidence on record ultimately dismissed the appeal and thereby affirmed the Judgement and order passed by the trial court resulting in allowing the pre-emption case.

12. Feeling aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the concurrent judgement and order passed by the learned Judges of the courts below, the pre-emptees-purchasers as petitioners then came before this court and obtained the instant Rule and order of stay as has been stated hereinabove.

13. Mr Morshed Ahmed Khan, the learned Counsel appearing for the pre-emptees-petitioners submits that, both the courts below have committed a grave error of law in not considering that, the pre-emption proceedings itself was not sustainable in law, in view of the fact that the vendor had mutated his name before transferring 5 decimals of land to the present-petitioners for which the pre-emptor ceased to be any co-sharer by purchase in the case holding but that very legal point has been overlooked by the learned Judges of the courts below which has occasioned failure of justice.

14. The learned Counsel goes on to submit that, though the case was barred by the principle of waiver of acquiescence but learned Judges of the courts below did not consider the said aspect of the case when it is the clear case of the pre-emptees-petitioners that, the vendor and the father of the present-pre-emptees-purchasers at first proposed the pre-emptor to purchase the case land but as they refused to purchase the same the vendor then compelled to transfer the case land to the pre-emptees-purchasers-petitioners.

15. By filing two supplementary-affidavits, the petitioners also produced the registered kabala dated 26-11-1997 and registered kabala dated 11- 9-2001, a filed porcha bearing khatian No. 721 appertaining to plot No. 629 standing in the name of the pre-emptees-petitioners in respect of 17 decimals of land. By filing another supplementary-affidavit dated 22-11-2017, the petitioners also annexed some documents which were marked as exhibits `E1 -E2.' In another supplementary-affidavit the pre-emptees-petitioners also produced a registered kabala dated 15-7-2001 through which 20 decimals of land was transferred by the son of the pre-emptor in favour of the opposite party No. 1 Akbar Ali.

16. In support of submission, the learned Counsel has then placed his reliance in a slew of decisions reported in 19 DLR 510, 33 DLR (HC) 18, 50 DLR (AD) 97, 17 BLD 513, 12 BLC (HC) 787, 42 DLR (AD) 189, 32 DLR (AD) 55. With such submission, and relying on those decisions, the learned Counsel finally prays for making the Rule absolute on setting aside the concurrent judgement and order passed by the learned Judges of the courts below.

17.
