Vs.
Ayesha Khatun Bibi and others ------------- Opposite-Parties
full_judgment:
This Rule was issued calling upon the opposite party No.1 to show cause as to why the impugned judgment and decree dated 29-7-2004 and 5-8-2004 respectively passed by the learned Joint District Judge, 1st Court, Mymensingh in Other Appeal No. 27 of 2001affirming the judgment decree dated 27-11-2000 and decree dated 30-11-2000 respectively passed by the learned Senior Assistant Judge Sadar, Mymensingh in Other Case No. 261 of 1991 should not be set-aside and/or such other or further order or orders passed as to this Court may seem fit and proper.

2. The short facts for disposal of the Rule are that the instant revisional application has arisen against the judgment dated 29-7-2004 and decree dated 5-8-2004 passed by Joint District Judge, 1st Court, Mymensingh, in Other Class Appeal No. 27 of 2001 affirming the judgment dated 27-11-2000 and decree dated 30-11-2000 passed by Senior Assistant Judge, Sadar, Mymensingh in Other Case No. 261 of 1991.

3. The opposite party No.1 instituted the Other suit being No. 261 of 1991 seeking the following reliefs:

সে মতে প্রার্থনা যে,

(ক) নালিশী তপশিলস্থ ভূমিতে ক্রয়সূত্রে বাদিনীর স্বত্ত্ব ও স্বার্থ থাকা মর্মে বাদিনীর অনুকুলে এবং বিবাদীগনের প্রতিকূলে এক স্বত্ব ঘোষনার ডিক্রী দিতে,

(খ)বিবাদীগণ স্বেচ্ছায় দখল না ছাড়িলে নালিশী তপশিলস্থ ভূমিতে বিবাদীগণের উত্তোলিত গৃহাদি সমূহ অপসারন পূর্বক বিবাদীগণকে উচ্ছেদক্রমে তৎস্থলে বাদিনীকে আদালত যোগে দখল দিবার জন্য বাদিনীর অনুকুলে এবং বিবাদীগনের প্রতিকূলে ডিক্রী দিতে,

4.  The suit of the opposite party No.1 plaintiff in short is that the suit land is situated at Mouja Kustia under Sadar Upazilla, District Mymensingh the CS Plot No. 684 was originally belonged to one late Naimuddin, the father of petitioner No. 1 and 2 and one Zinnat Ali who became the owner and possessor of the suit land by inheritance from their ancestral, and by purchase Zinnat Ali transferred 3 decimals of land to the plaintiff and on 22-7-1975 vide registered deed No. 22683 Naimuddin transferred 6.50 decimals of land vide registered deed No. 15620 to plaintiff dated 22-10-1975. Since purchase plaintiff planted 60 betel nut trees, their age is 7 years and before 3/4 years planted 4 mango trees, four jackfruit trees, two Jamrul trees, one Amra tree, all these are available there, defendants are trying to enter into the suit premises and to destroy those. Due to car accident the husband of the plaintiff was sentenced and was in jail hajat and the plaintiff was in bed ridden. On 1st Shraban 1397 BS Mojibur Rahman and Mofazzal erected a tin shed house and others defendants erected four katcha house (Chaner Ghar). The defendants erected those houses forcefully. So the plaintiff instituted suit for declaration and to evict the defendants and to deliver the possession of the suit land to plaintiff. 5. The defendant No. 1, 2 and 3 filed a written statement and defendant No.4 now the petitioner No.3 also filed a separate written statement denying the contention made in the plaint and defendant No.4 now the petitioner No.3 stated in his written statement that on 25-2-1976 vide registered deed serial No. 3636 and deed No. 3643, his brother Mujibur Rahman purchased 4 decimals of land from CS Plot No. 684 corresponding to DP Khatian No. 1278 DP Plot No. 2891. The brother of the defendant No. 4 now the petitioner No. 3 erected a tin shed house and a katcha house (Chaner ghar) and by growing different kinds of trees have been enjoying its peaceful possession since purchase without interruption from any quarter, the plaintiff opposite party No. 1 never possessed the suit land just to grab the land of the defendant No.4 now petitioner No.3 has filed the false fabricated, cooked up and vexatious suit against the petitioner the plaintiff has no and had no right, title, interest and possession over the 4 decimals of land of the defendant. The suit of the plaintiff is liable to be dismissed. The suit property 4 decimals of land is a homestead and the brother of the defendant No. 4 i.e. petitioner No.3 has been living with family members by erecting tin shed and katcha ghar (Chaner Ghar) therein.

6. The defendant No.1 and 2 now the petitioner No.1 and 2 filed a written statement denying the contention of the plaint and stating that the suit property was originally belonged to their father Naimuddin and Naimuddin died, leaving behind his heirs this defendant and others. During the life time of Naimuddin they had been living in the suit land with family members as homestead. Naimuddin did not transfer 6.50 decimals of land from the suit plot to the plaintiff and no question arise regarding delivery of possession of the suit land to the plaintiff. After the death of Naimuddin after 13 or 15 years the plaintiff instituted the false and fabricated suit showing a false deed which was not executed and registered by Naimuddin in favour of the plaintiff. The so-called deed is fully denied by the defendant-petitioners. During DP Khatian operation the names of the defendants-petitioners were correctly recorded in DP Khatian.

7. Ms Beheshti Marjan, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioners while Mr Md Golam Mostafa, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the opposite parties.

8. Ms Beheshti Marjan, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioners submits that the learned Senior Assistant Judge, did not apply his judicial mind both law and facts, by considering the materials on record, evidences on record and exhibits No. 2 and 3, came to an erroneous findings and decision which is slipshod, surmises, arbitrary, fanciful, hypothesis, it is liable to be set-aside.

9. She further submits that both the learned trial judge and appellate judge did not consider in their findings and decisions of the impugned judgment and orders that the contention of the plaint and the evidence of the plaintiff is contradictory, falsehood, cooked up. They came to an erroneous findings and decisions, their judgments are slipshod, fanciful, and arbitrary, it is liable to be set-aside.

10. She further submits that the deed writers of suit deeds exhibits 2 and 3 were not examined. If they died, their death certificates were not produced before the trial court or appellate Courts. The attesting witness of suit deeds exhibit 2 and 3, Yusuf Ali, Abul Kalam, Motiur Rahman were not examined, the fathers name and address of PW 8 Md Abul Mansur is not written in the deed (Exhibit-2) non examination of attesting witness and vital witness it creates doubt regarding execution and registration of suit deeds exhibit 2 and 3. No witness deposed before the learned trial judge that they saw Md Naimuddin and Zinnat Ali Munshi appeared before the concerning Sub registry office to submit the deeds for registration before the Sub register and put their left thumb impression (LTI) in the volume of concern registry office on the date of so called registration dated 22-7-1975 and 22-10-1975. The impugned judgments are slipshod, surmise, occasioning failure of justice, liable to be set-aside.

11. She further submits that in the impugned judgment the learned trial judge and appellate judges committed an error in their findings and decisions regarding possession of the plaintiff. The plaintiff stated in the plaint at paragraph No. 3 that after purchase on 22-7-1975 and 22-10-1975 to 1-8-1991 there is about 16 years, the age of 7 years of nut trees are quite doubtful, plaintiff admitted in her examination in cross that she planted trees in the early year of 1975 is quite doubtful. No witness deposed regarding the measurement of suit land after so called registration of deeds and nobody also deposed that Naimuddin and Zinnat Ali delivered the possession of suit land after the so called execution and registration, infavour of the plaintiff, the impugned judgments and decrees are slipshod and liable to be set-aside.

12. She further submitted that the plaintiff stated that she dispossessed on 1st Shraban 1397 BS i.e. 17-9-1990 of Christian Era, she instituted the suit on 1-8-1991 near about 1 year, she did not disclose anything regarding the late of filing suit after so called dispossession from the suit land, no GD entry is made or no criminal case is instituted, no local salish was held and the plaintiff did not seek relief under section 9 of Specific Relief Act for restoration of possession, no Medical certificate for illness of plaintiff or no documents regarding the sentence of plaintiffs husband was exhibited before the learned trial judge or appellate judge, plaintiff stated she was dispossessed at the noon of 1397 BS but PW 4 stated house was built in the morning, PW 7 stated plaintiff was dispossessed at 10.30 am on the date of so called dispossession PW 7 stated plaintiff register the dispossession, plaintiff admitted she was in bed ridden, the statements are contradictory PW 7 admitted that in the suit land there is dwelling house and a kitchen house of Naimuddin and PW 4 admitted that there is no house in the suit land now, the learned courts below committed an error in their findings and decisions in the impugned judgments and decrees resulting in an error occasioning failure of justice, it is contradictory and liable to be set-aside.

13. She has also added that the depositions of DW 1, DW 2, DW 3, DW 4, DW 5 and DW 6 were not denied by plaintiff, DW 1 clearly stated they did not dispossess the plaintiff, they lived their father's house since livelihood of their father and their father died in the suit land. Their father did not execute the so called deed on 19-10-1975, there is a graveyard in the suit land, plaintiff never possessed the suit land. The statements of PWs are contradictory. There is corroborating evidence of DWs. The learned trial judge and appellate judges committed an error in discussing the deposition of DWs resulting in an error occasioning failure of justice, it is liable to be set-aside.

14. The learned Advocate lastly submits that PW 6 clearly stated that there is different in left thumb impression of suit deeds with the left thumb impression of record of Sub registry office, he is the so called identifier of executor, Naimuddin. P.W. 3 is hearsay witness PW 4, 5, 6, 7 and 8 are interested witness, the statements are contradictory. The impugned judgment and orders suffers error of law, it is needless to prove the limitation by the defendants as per provision under section 56 of the Evidence Act. The learned trial judge and appellate judges committed an error in their findings and decision, occasioning failure of justice.

15. The learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioners in support of her contentions has referred the following case, such as the case of Abul Hossain vs Amjad Hossain, reported in 62 DLR (AD) 437, the case of Gopinath Das vs Government of Bangladesh reported in 64 DLR 167, the case of Md Mozaffer Rahman vs Government of Bangladesh, reported in 15 MLR (AD) 170, the case of Md Amzad Hossain Parag vs. Md Saiful Islam, reported in 9 ADC 224. She lastly referred the case of Md Hossain Mia vs Shujayatullah, reported in 36 DLR 191.

16. Mr Golam Mostafa, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the opposite parties submits that both the parties admit that Naimudin and Jinnat Ali were owners and possessors of the suit land. The said Naimuddin on 22-7-1975 through Saf-kabala deed No. 22683 sold 3 decimals of suit land to the plaintiff and delivered the possession of the same and late Jinnat Ali on 22-10-1975 through Saf-kabala deed 15620 sold 6.50 decimal of the suit land to the plaintiff and delivered possession to the plaintiff and in this way the plaintiff was owner and possessor of 9.50 decimals of suit land.

17. The learned Advocate further submits that it is submitted that PW 8 Abdul Mansur identified the Vendor (Jinnat Ali) of the deed by exhibiting the deed No. 22683 dated 22-7-1975 as Exhibit 2 (Ka) and PW 6 Md Kalu identified the vendor (Naimuddin) of deed No. 15620 dated 22-10-1975 and exhibited the deed being exhibit No. 3 and this witness also deposes that the vendor is his "Talai" and the deed was written in front of him and the same was read out to the vendor and the said Naimuddin called this witness to be witness in the deed and also deposes that the plaintiff paid consideration money to Naimuddin who after receipt of the same executed and registered the deed. The PW 2 has clearly deposed the plaintiff purchased the suit land from Nazimuddin and Jinnat Ali in 1975 and got possession of the same and she planted so many trees in the suit land but the defendants dispossessed her from the suit and built houses thereon.

18. He further submits that PW 2 Hurmat Ali, PW 4 Jalaluddin and PW 7 Noor Hossain deposed in the court and supported the case of plaintiff and denied the contents of the defendants. The plaintiff by oral and documentary evidences could well proved her case i.e. purchases of the suit land and got the possession of the same and was in physical possession and enjoying the same by planting several trees on the suit land and lastly she dispossessed by the defendants from the suit land.

19. He further submits that the defendants No. 1 and 2 sons of late Naimuddin contested the suit and DW 1 Hashem Ali son of Naimuddin deposed in the Court but did not claim that his father did not execute the Deed or put thumb impression in the said deed as in exhibit No. 3 and more over in cross-examination stated also that he does not know anything about this sale. DW 2 and DW 3 does not depose anything regarding the execution of the sale deed.

20. He lastly submits that the defendant Nos. 4 and 5 contested the suit by filing written statement stating that on 25-7-1976 they purchased 4 decimals of suit land from Taleb Ali who got the properties from Jinnat Ali (The father of defendant Nos. 4 and 6) by Ewaz Badal on the same day. But none of his witnesses deposed nothing regarding delivery of possession of the said land and, as such, the Ewaz Badal was not acted upon have no legal effect DW 4 witnesses for defendant No. 4 in cross-examination stated that he does not know whether Jinnat Ali sold the said land to the plaintiff earlier than their purchase and in this way the purchase of the suit land by the plaintiff through two deeds exhibited Nos. 2 and 3 were well proved.

21. The learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the opposite parties in support of his contentions has referred the following case, such as the case of Joynal Abedin vs Hafizur Rahman reported in 13 BLD (AD) 150 = 44 DLR (AD) 162, in the case of Chairman, Mongla Port Authority vs Kazi Brothers, reported in 59 DLR (AD) 9, in the case of Mahmud Ali vs Bangladesh reported in 1986 BLD (AD) 56, in the case of Abdus Samad Khan vs Wazedali Fakir, reported in 44 DLR 495, in the case of Md Shah Alam vs Musammat Farida Begum, reported in 2 MLR (AD) 153 = 2 BLC (AD) 92, in the case of Mohammad Yeasin Khan vs Deputy Commissioner; Brahmanbaria, reported in 2 MLR (AD) 211, in the case of Sadaruddin Miah vs Abdul Mannaf Mia, reported in 3 MLR (AD) 22, in the case of Government of Bangladesh represented by the Additional Deputy Commissioner vs Abdul Hoque Khan, reported in 3 MLR (AD) 255. He lastly referred the case of Haiderunnessa vs Monowara Begum reported in 16 BLD (AD) 280.

22. I have perused the impugned judgment dated 29-7-2004 and decree dated 5-8-2004 passed by Joint District Judge, 1st Court, Mymensingh, in Other Appeal No. 27 of 2001 affirming the judgment dated 27-11-2000 and decree dated 30-11-2000 passed by the learned senior Assistant Judge, Sadar Mymensingh in Other case No. 261 of 1991.

23. Heard the learned Advocates of both the sides and perused the revisional application filed under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure.

24. Before arriving at a proper finding it is utmost important to go through the citations as referred by the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioners first of all I would like to go through the case of Abul Hossain vs Amjad Hossain reported in 62 DLR (AD) 436 where our Apex Court held that—

"Section 110 of the Evidence Act provides for a presumption of ownership in favour of the person who is in possession of the property. A person in possession of land however imperfect his title may be, has a good title against whole world except the true owner and until the true owner comes in Court to assert a claim to the property. Possession is evidence of title, and gives a good title as against wrong doer."

"The High Court Division in the premises fell in an error in reversing the judgment of the learned Subordinate Judge without adverting to the findings arrived at as regards acquisition title and possession of the suit lands by the appellants. On consideration of the fact and circumstances of the matter, we are of the view that the High Court Division erred in law in disbelieving the appellants title in the suit lands."

25. In the case of Gopinath Das, vs Government of Bangladesh, reported in 64 DLR 167 where it is held that—

"Initiation of suit is not seen by the superior Courts as an unrestricted right to be exercised at pleasure. It must disclose a cause of action' within the meaning of 'right as to any property' or 'legal character' so far as section 42 of the Specific Relief Act is concerned."

26. In the case of Md Mozaffer Rahman vs Government of Bangladesh, reported in 15 MLR (AD) 170, where our Apex Court held that—

"Suit for declaration of title in the absence of satisfactory proof thereof is not maintainable—

In the instant case the plaintiffs could not prove their title to the suit land by producing documentary evidence as well as oral evidence. The trial court dismissed the suit on specific finding which the court of Appeal, High Court Division and the Appellate Division held perfectly justified."

27. It appears that the trial Court as well as the Court of Appeal below on consideration of the evidence, both oral and documentary found that the plaintiffs could not prove their right and title in the suit land, it appears that in the instant case, the plaintiffs claimed their predecessor-in-interest became tenant of the suit land by way of pattan as well as oral gift but at the trial the plaintiff could not prove neither the story of pattan nor the oral gift by adducing any reliable or documentary evidence. It also appears that the plaintiffs had no title to the suit land and the story of pattan as well as oral gift is false. Accordingly, both the Courts below rightly and correctly arrived at a finding that the plaintiffs failed to establish their right and title in the suit land.

28. In the case of Md Amzad Hossain Parag vs Md Saiful Islam, reported in 9 ADC 224 where it is held that—

The Specific Relief Act, 1877, section 42 Declaration of Kabla deed collusive and forged Onus of proof lies upon.

"The trial court, on consideration of evidence adduced by the contesting parties and other facts and circumstances, dismissed the suit by the judgment and order dated 17-4-2004 holding mainly that the plaintiffs could not prove the case that the impugned kabala deed was forged, collusive etc. The trial Court also found that the contesting defendants have been possessing the suit land in recording the same in their names and on payment of rent since their purchase."

29. In the case of Md Hossain Mia vs Shujayatullah, reported in 36 DLR 191 where it is held that—

Presumption- possession goes with title.

30. It the evidence of possession on behalf of the plaintiffs and on behalf of the defendants as to the farmer's possession within 12 years before suit is evenly balanced the presumption that possession goes with title shall prevail; where the evidence adduced by both the parties, although unsatisfactory is not altogether valueless, the court is entitled to take into consideration the presumption arises from title.

<u>31. The presumptive possession of the plaintiffs in the land on proof of their title in the facts of the case would be sufficient to discharge the onus of proving possession because presumption is an inference as to existence of a fact from the existence of some other founded fact.</u>

32. In view of the attending facts and circumstances and the submissions as advanced by the learned Advocates of both the sides and citations as referred in support of their respective contentions I find merit in the submissions of the learned advocate for the petitioners and the citations as referred by the learned Advocate for the petitioners in support of her contention are fully applicable in the facts and circumstances of the present case.

33. On the other hand, the submissions as advanced by the learned Advocate for the opposite parties is devoid of any substance and the citations as referred by him have no manner of application in the facts and circumstances of the present case,

34. Thus, the Rule having merit, it succeeds.

35. In the result, the rule is made absolute without any order as to cost.

36. The impugned judgment dated 29-7-2004 and decree dated 5-8-2004 passed by Joint District Judge, 1st Court, Mymensingh, in Other Appeal No. 27 of 2001 affirming the impugned judgment dated 27-11-2000 and decree dated 30-11-2000 passed by the learned Senior Assistant Judge, Sadar Mymensingh in Other case No. 261 of 1991 is hereby set-aside.

37. The order of stay granted earlier at the time issuance of the Rule is hereby recalled and vacated.

The office is directed to communicate the judgment to the concerned Court below and send down the lower Court's records at once.

End.

case_source: Against the judgment and decree dated 9-11-2006 passed by learned Joint District Judge, 1st Court, Brahmanbaria in Title Suit No. 26 of 2005.
full_judgment:
Md Emdadul Huq J : This first Appeal is directed against the judgment and order dated 9-11-2006 by which the learned Joint District Judge, 1st Court, Brahmanbaria dismissed Title Suit No. 26 of 2005.

2. In that suit, the plaintiffs and two sets of defendants raised claim to the suit land as follows:

Plaintiff-appellants' case: The appellants, as plaintiffs, filed the above noted suit for declaration of their title to the suit land measuring a total of 1.79 acres comprising 35 decimals of the entire 1st suit plot being CS plot No. 338 and 1.44 acres of the 2nd suit plot being CS plot No. 340. The suit land has been fully described with further description in the schedule to the plaint.

3. Plaintiffs have stated that their grandmother's father Khorrom Hajee was the owner and CS recorded tenant of the suit land. The 1st suit Plot (CS 338) was solely owned and possessed by Khorrom Hajee. In the second suit plot (CS 340) Khorrom Hajee had eight annas share amounting to 1.255 acres. However, by virtue of an amicable partition, Khorrom Hajee used to possess a little larger part, namely 1.45 acres out of the 2nd suit plot.

4. Khorrom Hajee had no son and, on his death, his property including the suit land devolved upon his only brother Abdul Majid and 6 (six) daughters, Mohor Chan and 5 others. There was an amicable partition among the said heirs of Khorrorn Hajee, and his daughter Mohor Chan was allocated the suit land.

5. On the death of Mohor Chan, the suit land devolved upon her son Mohammad All (now deceased) and two other sons and one daughter, being proforma-defendant Nos. 29-31. However, there was an amicable partition among the said children of Mohor Chan and the suit land was allocated to her son Mohammad Ali.

6. On the death of Mohammad Ali, his three sons i.e. the present three plaintiffs and six daughters, being proforma-defendant Nos. 32-37, inherited the entire suit land. There was an amicable partition among the said children of Mohammad Ali and the three plaintiffs, as the Sons, got the suit land.

7. Proforma-defendant Nos. 22-28 are the heirs of Abdul Majid, brother of Khorrom Hajee. Proforma-defendant Nos. 38- 48 are the heirs of the 5 (five) other daughters of Khorrom Hajee i.e., the five sisters of Mohor Chan. These defendants have no claim over the suit land.

8. But the principal defendant Nos. 1- 21 have raised claims to the suit land as the successors-in-interest of some persons in whose names SA Khatian No. 51 has been wrongly prepared. Hence the suit.

Case of defendant No.13 (respondent):

9. He contends that the suit is not maintainable in its present form, that it is bad for defect of parties and also barred by limitation. He claims title to, and possession over, the entire 1st suit plot being CS Plot No. 33% measuring 35 decimals.

10. He admits that, the suit land originally belonged to CS recorded tenant Khorrom Hajee, who died leaving six daughters including Mohor Chan and brother Abdul Majid, as stated in the plaint.

11. He claims that Khorrom Hajee had another brother named Abdul Karim and that there was an amicable partition among the said heirs of Khorrom Hajee. In that amicable partition, the 1st suit plot (CS Plot No. 338) measuring 35 decimals was allocated to the said brother Abdul Karim and 1.44 acres of the 2nd suit plot (CS Plot No.340) was allocated to the said daughter Mohor Chan, the paternal grandmother of the plaintiffs. However Mohor Chan, during her life time, sold out her entire share of 1.44 acres to the predecessors of defendant Nos. 1-10.

12. He further claims that Abdul Karim, brother of Khorrom Hajee, died leaving two sons named Abdul Aziz, being the husband of Mohor Chan and paternal grandfather of the plaintiffs, and another son named Abdul Alim and one daughter named Multi Begum. By virtue of an amicable partition with the said brother and sister, Abdul Alim got the suit plot being CS plot No.338 measuring 35 decimals.

13. On the death of Abdul Alim, his 4 sons, being defendant Nos. 11-14, and another son Renu Bhuyian and two daughters inherited the 1st Suit plot. Upon amicable partition among the said heirs of Abdul Alim (son of Abdul Karim), defendant No. 13 got the entire 1st suit plot and he is in possession thereof. The latest BS Khatian No. 280 has been accordingly prepared in the name of defendant No. 13.

Case of defendant Nos. 1 and 4-7 and 10 (respondents):

14. They contend that the suit is not maintainable in its present form, that it is bad for defect of parties and also barred by limitation.

15. Like defendant No.I3, these defendants have stated the same genealogy of inheritance, namely that Khorrom Hajee, the original owner, died leaving the 6 (six) daughters including Mohor Chan and two brothers named Abdul Majid and Abdul Karim and that Mohor Chan acquired 1.44 acres of the 211 suit plot as a result of an amicable partition among the said heirs of Khorrom Hajee.

16. They claim title to and possession over the entire 2nd plot (CS plot No. 340) by virtue of a registered deed of permanent lease (ralcu:ir aqio) executed by Mohor Chan on 24-5-1957 and registered on 12-9-1957 in favour of Abdul Majid Molla, being the paternal grandfather of these defendants.

17. They claim that, before the said transfer document of 1957, their predecessor Idrish, Shahidul and Abdul Alim, being the three sons of Abdul Majid, (brother of Khorrom Hajee), had purchased 51.5 decimals out of the 2nd suit plot No. 340 from Mohammad Ali, the father of the plaintiffs. The said three sons of Abdul Majid was under an impression that Mohammad All had acquired the same by virtue of an oral gift from Khorrom Hajee. But, being suspicious of the oral gift, their father Abdul Majid obtained the transfer document of 1957 from Mohor Chan herself for the entire share of Mohor Chan amounting to 1.44 acres of the 2nd suit plot in favour of Abdul Majid and his three sons.

18. These defendants have further stated that their grandfather Abdul Majid, after acquiring the said 1.44 acres from Mohor Chan, equally distributed the same among his four sons, namely defendant No. 1 (Abdul Gafur), Idrish Mia (father of defendant Nos. 2 and 3) Shahidul Islam (father of defendant Nos. 4-7) and Abdul Alim (father of defendant No. 8-10).

19. Their grandfather Abdul Majid Molla died leaving the said four sons and one daughter Shah Chan. There was an amicable partition among the children of Abdul Majid Molla and the four sons were allocated equal shares in the 1.44 acres of the 2nd suit plot. The sister Shah Chan was given some land in a non-disputed plot.

20. The said equal shares of the four sons of Abdul Majid have been correctly recorded in the four separate BS Khatians being Nos. 98, 50, 270 and 42 in the names of the defendants and they are in possession thereof.

Proceeding and decision of trial court:

21. The trial court took up five issues for determination, namely (1) maintainability of the suit, (2) limitation, (3) defect of party, (4) the relief prayed Tor by the plaintiffs; and (5) any other relief.

22. At the trial, both sides adduced oral and documentary evidence. The trial Court, upon discussion of the evidence so adduced, decided that the plaintiffs have failed to prove their title and possession and dismissed the suit.

Deliberation in Appeal:

23. Mr Tabarak Hossain, the learned Advocate for the plaintiff-appellants, submits that the plaintiffs are the grandsons of the admitted owner of the suit land i.e., Mohor Chan being one of the six daughters of the admitted original owner Khorrom Hajee.

24. Mr Hossain next submits that since the defendants claim that Mohor Chan had exhausted her interest in the suit land, particularly in the 2nd suit plot, by virtue of a transfer document registered in 1957, the burden of proof of that claim is on the defendants.

25. Mr Hossain next draws our attention to the said transfer document of 1957 (Exhibit-3) and refers to the various writings contained on the reverse of the 2nd and 3rd pages in the form of the report of the sub-Registrar, Brahmanbaria and the decision of the District Registrar, Dacca as recorded in 1957.

26. Mr Hossain next submits that these writings clearly show that, under direction of the then District Registrar, Dacca, the Sub-Registrar of Brahmanbaria conducted an inquiry on two occasions and reported that the executants of the deed Mohor Chan did not appear to admit the alleged execution of the deed by her and then the District Registrar recorded his decision under section 75 of the Registration Act, 1908 to the effect that the document had been duly executed and accordingly registered the same.

27. Mr Hossain next submits that since the admitted owner Mohor Chan never presented herself before the registering authority and thus denied the execution of that deed, no title passed to Abdul Majid, the transferee of that deed, being the predecessors of the defendant Nos. 1 and 4- 7 and 10.

28. Mr Hossain lastly submits that the oral evidence also support plaintiffs' possession over the suit land and therefore the Appeal should be allowed and the suit should be decreed.

29. In reply Mr Khair Ezaz Masud, the learned Advocate for the respondent-defendant Nos. 1 and 4-7 and 10, submits that the 1st set of contesting defendants, namely defendant No. 13, claims the 1st suit plot CS plot No. 338 measuring 35 decimals as the heirs of Abdul Karim, being one of the two surviving brothers of the admitted original owner Khorrom Hajee.

30. Mr Masud next submits that the plaintiffs, in their plaint are silent about the existence of Abdul Karim, but plaintiff No. 3, deposing as PW I, admitted such existence and further admitted that defendant No. 13 is one of the grandsons of the said Abdul Karim.

31. Mr Masud next submits that this very admission of PW 1 shows that the plaintiffs are not entitled to the entire suit land and that they would be entitled to a lesser quantum of share, because on the death of Khorrom Hajee his 6 (six) daughters including plaintiffs predecessor Mohor Chan were entitled to 2/3 share as Koranic heirs and the two brothers of Khorrom Hajee were entitled to the remaining 1/3 share as residuary and therefore the instant suit for simple declaration of title to the entire suit land is not maintainable.

32. Mr Masud next submits that the trial Court correctly and lawfully held that plaintiffs', predecessor Mohor Chan had exhausted her entire interest by virtue of the transfer deed (Exhibit-Kha) executed by Mohor Chan on 24-5-1957 and registered under order of the District Registrar on 12-9-1957.

33. Mr Masud next submits that, according to section 75 of the Registration Act, 1908 a District Registrar has the lawful authority to cause an inquiry in case of refusal by the executant of a deed to present the deed for registration.

34. Mr Masud next submits that, in the instant case, the District Registrar, Dacca had jurisdiction to cause the inquiry over the genuineness of the execution of the deed and he recorded his decision to register the said transfer document, because he was satisfied about the fact that the Mohor Chan, the executant, was found to be avoiding the presentation of the deed.

35. Mr Masud next submits that the other documents namely the RS Katian and the latest BS Khatians show that the predecessor of the contesting defendants, after acquisition of the suit land by virtue of the said transfer deed, were in possession and accordingly these records of right were prepared in their names and they have been paying rent.

36. Mr Masud lastly submits that the trial Court lawfully and correctly dismissed the suit and this appeal is liable to be dismissed. Discussion, findings and decision in Appeal:

37. The trial court framed five issues and discussed the merit of the claim of the parties and generally recorded its decision on all the issues together against the plaintiffs. This manner of recording general decision on the issues is not proper. So, in this judgment, we have recorded our decision on the individual issues as mandated by law.

38. With regard to the issue No. 2 on defect of party, the defendants have neither stated in their writer statement nor have they adduced any evidence in support of their claim. The materials on record do not show any defect of party. Moreover, this issue was not agitated at the hearing of this Appeal. So this issue is decided in favour of the plaintiffs.

39. The other issues being Nos.1 and 3, 4 and 5 on maintainability of the suit, limitation, plaintiffs' title and possession and the relief prayed for interlinked. So, these are taken up together and discussed in the following part of this judgment.

40. The pleadings of the parties show that the contesting defendants admit that the suit land originally belonged to Khorrom Hajee. This is further proved by the two CS Khatians, Exhibit-1 and Exhibit-1 (ka). The CS khatians show that the entire 1st suit plot and the eight anas of share in the suit holding including 2nd suit plot (340) were recorded in the name of Khorrom Hajee. Exhibit-1 (ka) further shows that the entire 2nd suit plot measuring 1.44 acres was possessed by Khorrom Hajee.

41. Plaintiffs have, in their plaint, stated that Kharrom Hajee left only one brother named Abdul Majid. But the defendants claim that Khorrom Hajee had, apart from Abdul Majid, another brother named Abdul Karim. In this respect plaintiff No.3, deposing as PW I on behalf of all the plaintiffs, in cross-examination, stated that

“খোররম আলী ভূঁইয়ার এক ভাইয়ের নাম আব্দুল মজিদ ভূঁইয়া; অপর ভাইয়ের লাম আব্দুল করিম ভূঁইয়া। আব্দুল আজীজ ভূঁইয়ার আরেক ভাই ছিলেন তাহার মাম ছিল আব্দুল আলীম ভূঁইয়া । আব্দুল আলীম ভূঁইয়ার পুক্রগণ হইতেছে ১১.১৪ নং বিবাদী ।.........আমার দাদী মোহর চানকে বিবাহ দেওয়া হয় আব্দুল করিম ভূঁইয়ার পুত্র আবদুল আজিজ ভূঁইয়ার নিকট”

42. The above statement of PW 1 clearly prove the existence of Abdul Karim as one of two surviving brothers of Khorrom Hajee. It follows that the six daughters of Khorrom Hajee, as Koranic heirs, inherited 2/3 (two-thirds) share, and the two brothers, as residuary heirs, inherited 1/3 (one third) share of the property left by Khorrom Hajee.

43. With regard to the time of death of Khorrorn Hajee and the events thereafter, not much evidence is available on record. However, SA Khatian No. 51, Exhibit- 2(kha), shows that the various plots of the earlier CS Khatian No.46, including the 2nd suit plot (CS 340) measuring 1.44 acres were recorded in the names of a number of persons. The name of Khorrom Hajee is not there in the said SA Khatian. Four of those SA recorded tenants are Mohor Chan, daughter of Khorrom Hajee and Abdul Alim, Sahidul Islam, and Idrish Ali, being the three sons of Abdul Majid i.e. the brother of Khorrom Hajee. So the SA Khatian indicates that CS tenant Khorrom died before preparation of the SA Khatian and that there was an amicable partition among the heirs of Khorrom Hajee and the 2nd suit plot, which was in possession of Khorrom Hajee as per CS record, fell in the share of the Mohor Chan.

44. The said SA Khatian further proves the truth of the purchase and possession of some land by the three sons of Abdul Majid. It is noted that the 2nd set of defendants claim that the said three sons of Abdul Majid were misled to purchase 51.5 decimals by kabala dated 9-4-1956 (Exhibit-ka) executed by the self declared owner Mohammad Ali, the son of Mohor Chan and father of the plaintiffs.

45. The defendants further claim that Abdul Majid, the father of the said three purchasers and the predecessor of the 2nd set of defendants, did not rely on that kabala and got a subsequent transfer deed of 1957 (Exhibit-Kha) executed by the Mohor Chan herself.

46. This subsequent transfer document (Exhibit-Kha) shows that it was executed by Mohor Chan by putting thumb impression and that the transfer has been described as চিরস্থায়ী রায়তী পত্তন in respect of the entire 2nd suit plot No. 340 in favour of Abdul Majid Mollah, the predecessor of the 2nd set of defendants.

47. However, on the reverse of the 2nd page of that document (Exhibit-Kha), the District Registrar, Dacca recorded his decision on 12-9-1957 and thereby appointed the Sub-Registrar, Brahmanbaria as the Commissioner under section 38 of the Registration Act, 1908 to ascertain as to whether the deed was executed by Mohor Chan. Accordingly, the Sub-Registrar, Brahmanbaria recorded the report as follows:

"Having visited the residence of one "Abdul Aziz Bhuiyan Shahib" of Suhilpur, Thana Brahmanbaria, District-Tripura, I have this day could not examine the said Mohar Chan Bibi W/O of Abdul Aziz Bhuiyan, as no such executant named as Mohar Chan Bibi was found at the residence as mentioned with petition."

48. After the said report, the District Registrar again directed the Sub-Registrar, Brahmanbaria to report on the matter. This time the Sub-Registrar reported as follows:

"Having visited the residence of Mohor Chan Bibi wife of Abdul Aziz Bhuiyan of Suhilpur, Thana Brahmanbaria, District-Tripura, religion Muslim, by profession-House wife, I have this day could not examine the said Mohor Chan Bibi, as she was found unwilling keeping out of the way in spite of due intimation which was proved to my satisfaction."

49. After the second report, as quoted above, the District Registrar, Dacca recorded his decision on the reverse of the 3rd page as quoted below:

"Admitted to registration u/s 75 of Act XVI of 1908 by order of the District-Registrar Dacca on 16-6-1958 in case No. 3, u/s 74 of 1908."

50. For considering the legality of the above decision of District Registrar, Dacca, section 38 of the Registration Act, 1908 is quoted below

"38. Persons exempt from appearance at registration office:

(1)(a) A person who by reason of bodily infirmity is unable without risk or serious inconvenience to appear at the registration-office, or

(b) a person in jail under civil or criminal process, or

(c) persons exempt by law from personal appearance in Court and who would but for the provision next hereinafter contained be required to appear in person at the registration-office.

shall not be required so to appear.

(2) In the case of every such person the registering officer shall either himself go to the house of such person, or to the jail in which he is confined, and examine him or issue a commission for his examination"

51. It is evident that section 38 empowers a Sub-Registrar to go to the residence of certain type of executants or to a convenient place for examining such executant.

<u>52. Sections 73 to 75 of the Registration Act, 1908 provide for a situation where an executant denies the execution or refuses to an executed deed for registration. Section 73 requires that, in such case, an application is to be filed to the Registrar, superior in rank and then the Registrar shall follow the procedure as laid down in sections 74 and 75, which are quoted below:</u>

<u>"74. Procedure of Registrar on such application.— In such case, and also where such denial as aforesaid is made before a Registrar in respect of a document presented for registration to him, the Registrar shall, as soon as conveniently may be, enquire."</u>

<u>(a) whether the document has been  executed:,</u>

<u>(b) whether the requirement of the law for the time being in force have been complied with on the part of the applicant or person presenting the document for registration, as the case may be, so as to entitle the document to registration."</u>

<u>75. Order by Registrar to register and procedure thereon:</u>

<u>(1) If the Registrar finds that the document bad been executed and that the said requirements have been complied with he shall order the document to be registered.</u>

<u>(2) If the document is duly presented for registration within thirty days after the making of such order, the registering officer shall obey the same and thereupon shall, so far as may be, practicable, follow the procedure prescribed in sections 58, 59 and 60.</u>

<u>(3) Such registration shall take effect as of the document had been registered when it was first duly presented for registration."</u>

<u>53. It is evident that section 75 empowers a Registrar (superior in rank) to cause an inquiry in a case where the executant denies the execution of a deed and refuses to present himself or herself before the registering authority (Sub-Registrar).</u>

54. In the instant case, the District Registrar, Dacca after causing an inquiry recorded his decision in favour of the transferee and the deed was accordingly registered. Section 75(3) provides that the deed so registered has all the legal effect of a regular deed, as if presented for registration.

55. In consideration of the 2nd inquiry report under section 38 as quoted earlier and the provisions of 73-75 of the Registration Act, 1908, we find no illegality or infirmity in the decision recorded by the District Registrar, Dacca. Accordingly we hold that the District Registrar lawfully exercised his authority in registering the deed in 1957 in the ordinary course of his official job. His action and decision were legal.

56. We further hold that the result of registration of the deed executed by Mohor Chan (Exhibit-Kha) is that her title to 1.44 acres of the 2nd suit plot CS 340 passed on to the transferee Abdul Majid, the predecessor of the defendant Nos. 1 and 4-7 and 10.

57. In the body of this transfer document the nature thereof is stated as "চিরস্থায়ী বন্দোবস্ত/পাট্টা দলিল” along with a statement about receipt of consideration and delivery of possession. So, it is essentially a sale deed and the said bangla expression indicating settlement বন্দোবস্ত/পাট্টা does not affect the passing of title.

58. The fact of passing of the title to Abdul Majid by virtue of the transfer document of 1957 is further evidenced by the collateral documents, namely the 4 (four) (Halkhatian) (Exhibit-Ga series) prepared in the names of the defendants and also by the rent receipts (Exhibit-Gha series) showing payment of rent by them for the years 1392 to 1412 BS.

59. On the possession aspect, the oral evidence adduced by the plaintiffs and the 2nd set of contesting defendants through PWs 1-3 and DWs 1-4 respectively appear to be evenly balanced. But considered with the title documents, Exhibit-Ka and Kha, read with the SA khatian (Exhibit-2), the BS khatians Exhibit- (Ga-series) and the rent receipts, (Exhibits Gha-series), we hold that the testimony of the DWs are credible and that the said defendants are in possession of the 2nd suit plot.

60. The trial court's decision on disbelieving the title and possession of the plaintiffs is correct and lawful. We agree with that decision.

61. It is noted that the trial Court recorded a finding that the 1st suit plot being CS plot No. 338 has been recorded in the names of the defendant Nos. 11-14.

62. In respect of the said 1st suit plot, defendant No. 13 or the plaintiffs did not produce the SA Khatian or the certified copy of the BS Khatian or any rent receipt.

63. However, defendant No. 13 himself deposed as DW 2 and supported his claim. He also produced a copy of BS Khatian No.280 (Exhibit-A) comprising the single BS plot No. 569 measuring 35 decimals. This document contains the remark of the Union Revenue Assistant “রাজস্ব আদায়ের স্বার্থে বি এস খতিয়ানের অবিকল নকল কপি দেওয়া গেল।” This document is not the certified copy. But it contains the names of defendant No. 13 and his three brothers.

64. This document (Exhibit-A) read with our findings on the fact of inheritance of 1/3 share from Khorrom Hajee by his two brothers named Abdul Majid, the predecessor of 2nd set of defendants, Abdul Karim, grandfather of defendant Nos. 11-14, and the fact of inheritance of 2/3 share by the six daughters of Khorrom Hajee, and the admitted amicable partition among those heirs, and the corroborating fact of inclusion of the name of only Mohor Chan as the SA recorded tenant for the only 2nd suit plot and the failure of the plaintiffs to produce any SA Khatian in respect of the 1st suit plot and failure of the plaintiff to prove their possession over the 2nd suit plot, we hold that plaintiffs have failed to prove their exclusive title to, and possession over the 1st suit plot.

65. Accordingly we hold that the present suit for simple declaration of title is not maintainable. We further hold that since defendant Nos. 1 and 4-7 and 10 have been in possession of the 2nd suit plot since 1957, that is, since a time when plaintiffs predecessor Mohor Chan and her son Mohammad Ali were alive and were aware of the possession of the said defendants, the cause of action, if any, arose in 1957, when the defendants got into possession not as cosharers by inheritance from Khorrom Hajee but as the purchasers from the said Mohor Chan. The instant suit having been filed in 2006 is barred by limitation.

66. In view of the above findings, issue Nos. 1 3, 4 and 5 are decided against the plaintiffs.

67. We conclude that the trial court lawfully and correctly dismissed the suit. This appeal has no merit and hence liable to be dismissed.

68. Court fee paid is correct.

69. The appeal is dismissed on contest.

Send down the lower Court records at once.

End.

full_judgment:
Shah Abu Nayeem Mominur Rahman J. These two appeals by leave arose out of a common judgment and order dated 26.08.1999 passed in Civil Revision Nos. 761 and 762 of 1989 by the High Court Division making the Rules absolute.

2. The relevant facts are that the plaintiffs filed the suits being Title Suit No. 166 of 1976 for permanent injunction and Title Suit No. 97 of 1977 for declaration that the decree passed in Title Suit No. 92 of 1969, 4th Court of Munsif, Narayangonj, is illegal, void and not binding upon the plaintiffs.

3. The plaintiffs in Title Suit No. 166 of 1976 claimed to have purchased the lands described in the schedule from the admit-ted owners on the basis of a decree passed in Title Suit No. 98 of 1967 by the Court of 2nd Munsif, Narayangonj, followed by execution of the required sale deed as well as delivery of possession through Title Execution Case No. 37 of 1967 and that thereafter one Nur Box sold his share to the plaintiff No. 6 by registered kabala dated 12.01.1970. Thus while the plaintiffs being owners as aforesaid were possessing the suit land detailed in schedule 'A' peacefully, the defendant Nos. 1-7 tried to dispossess the plaintiffs from the suit land claiming their title thereon on the basis of a decree dated 04.09.1974 passed in Title Suit No. 92 of 1969 and the sale deed obtained through Court on execution; of the said decree vide Execution Case No. 7 of 1975, which fact has been disclosed in the written objection and written statement filed by the defendants in Title Suit No. 166 of 1976 and faced with such situation the plaintiffs filed the Title Suit No. 97 of 1977 with prayer for declaring that the decree passed in Title Suit No. 92 of 1969 as illegal, void and not binding upon the plaintiffs. In the plaint, of Title Suit No. 97 of 1977 the plaintiffs included schedules 'A' and 'B', of which schedule 'A' land corresponds to the schedule of P land detailed in the plaint of Title Suit No. 166 of 1976 and the lands detailed in schedule-B of Title Suit No. 97 of 1977 corresponds to the lands claimed by the defendants, got through execution of the decree passed in Title Suit No. 92 of 1969 vide Title Execution Case No. 7 of 1975. The respondents hereof as defendants contested both the suits by filing written statements. Both the parties adduced witnesses and produced documents, marked exhibits.

4. The contesting defendants of both the suits i.e. Title Suit No. 166 of 1976 and Title Suit No. 97 of 1977, as plaintiffs, filed Title Suit No. 92 of 1969 in the Court of 4th Munsif, Narayangonj, for Specific Performance of Contract, based on a sale-agreement dated 07.12.1963, wherein the plaintiffs of the instant suits were made defendants and they were contesting the suit (Title Suit No. 92 of 1969) and that the said suit was initially dismissed on 21.09.1971 for default. However after liberation of this Country they said suit was restored and ultimately heard and disposed of exparte on 04.09.1974 and the required kabala was obtained through Court by filing Execution Case No. 7 of 1975 covering the lands detailed in the schedule-land of the plaint of Title Suit No.166 of 1976, which is schedule-B land of Title Suit No.97 of 1977.

5. The learned Munsif framed the following issues to arrive at his decision for disposing of both the cases:- (1) Whether the suits as framed and filed are maintainable; (2) Whether the plaintiffs are entitled to get decree as prayed for; (3) Whether the plaintiffs are entitled to get a decree for permanent injunction as prayed for; and (4) To what other relief(s) the plaintiffs are entitled to.

6. The learned Munsif heard both the cases together and recorded one set of depositions of witnesses for both the cases. On consideration of the materials and evidence available on record and the submissions of the learned Advocates of the respective parties learned Munsif decreed both the suits to the effect that the decree dated 04.09.1974 passed in Title Suit No.92 of 1969 by the 4th Court of made by the learned Advocates of the Munsif, Narayangonj, be declared as illegal, void, fraudulent and not binding upon the plaintiffs and that the plaintiffs have acquired right, title and interest in schedule A land and that the defendant Nos.1-6 are permanently restrained, from entering into the schedule-A land.

7. Being aggrieved, the defendants preferred Title Appeal No. 223 of 1983 against the judgment and decree passed in Title Suit No. 166 of 1976 and Title Appeal No. 224 of 1984 against the judgment and decree passed in Title Suit No. 97 of 1977. The appeals were heard one after another and disposed of by a common judgment dated 19.03.1983 dismissing both the appeals holding, amongst others, that the plaintiffs were aware about the Title Suit No. 92 of 1969 and that the plaintiffs were found to be in possession of the suit land.

8. Being aggrieved there against the Civil Revision Cases were filed by the defendants in the High Court Division. The Civil Revision No. 761 of 1989 arose out of the judgment and decree passed in Title Appeal No. 224 of 1983 and Civil Revision No. 762 of 1989 arose out of Title Appeal No. 223 of 1983, which were heard one after another and disposed of by the common judgment and order dated 26.08.1999 making both the rules absolute, against which the present appeals were preferred upon obtaining leave.

9. We have perused the impugned judgments passed by the Courts below as well as the impugned judgment and order passed by the High Court Division.

10. We have considered the submissions respective parties. On careful examination of the submissions of the learner Advocates as well as the schedules 'A' 'B', as detailed and or referred to in IV plaints of the Title Suit No. 166 of 1976 Title Suit No. 97 of 1977 and Title Suit No. 92 of 1969, it appeared that out of the plots of land mentioned in the schedule of the plaints, except one plot; other plot are not same. But on the incorrect statement made in the written objection as well as in the written statement filed by the defendants in Title Suit No.166 of 1976 the plaintiffs had to file Title Suit No. 97 1977 for declaring that the judgment as decree dated 04.09.1974 passed in Tit Suit No.92 of 1969 by the Munsif, 4th Court, Narayangonj, as illegal, void fraudulent and not binding upon the plaintiffs.

11. On consideration of the evidence are materials on record of the cases, appeared that the plaintiffs could not prove their claim that they were not away about the exparte decree passed in Title Suit No. 92 of 1969 in the year 1974, rather it is found from the copy of the order sheet of Title Suit No. 92 of 1969, annexed to the Additional Paper Boo filed on 12.04.2009 by the Appellants, the after liberation of the Country on restoration of the suit (Title Suit No. 92 of 1969 to its original file and number, since d missed for default earlier, the defender, appeared in the suit on 19.04.1972, 18.07.1972 and 18.12.1973 but did not appear at the hearing and the suit w decreed exparte on 04.09.1974.

12. It appears on comparison of the land described in the schedule of the plaintiff Title Suit No. 92 of 1969 and the lands described in the schedules of plaint of 'We Suit No. 97 and 1977 that the scheduled lands of Title Suit No. 92 of 1969 do of correspond to the lands detailed in Schedule-B of the plaint of Title Suit No. 97 of 1977 and those are not same or Common, except one plot being plot N0.158 under Khatian No. 51 measuring 15 decimals as to the lands detailed in Schedule of Title Suit No. 166 of 1976 and Schedule-A of Title Suit No. 97 of 1977.

13. The plaintiffs of Title Suit No. 97 of 1977 and Title Suit No. 166 of 1976 aimed, to have purchased land measuring 1.58 acres in four plots detailed in schedule-A of the plaint of Title Suit No. 97 of 1977 and in the schedule of Title Suit No. 166 of 1976, which are as under:-

15. Thus on comparison of Schedules-A and B detailed above it appears that except the land measuring 0.15 acres in Plot No.168 under Khatian No.51 (underlined), which is a tank, other plots of the schedule 'A' and 'B' are not same.

16. Thus there could not be any cause of action for challenging the decree passed in Title Suit No. 92 of 1969 by the plaintiffs and that the defendants having no claim for any right, title and interest in respect of other three plots of Schedule-A land i.e. plot Nos. 121, 159 and 119 the plaintiffs may get a decree for permanent injunction as prayed for in Title Suit No.166 of 1976 against the defendants in respect of the lands detailed in Schedule-A, except said plot No. 168 under Khatian No. 51 admeasuring 15 decimals, which is described as a pond/ditch, which plot appears to be included in the schedules of both Title Suit No. 92 of 1969 and Title Suit No. 166 of 1976 and that the dispute relating to Plot No. 168 under Khatian No. 51 may be resolved separately, if the parties so desire, in a proper forum and in accordance with law.

17. Thus, we are of the view that the plain-tiff-appellants may get a decree for permanent injunction in Title Suit No.166 of 1976 in respect of the Schedule-A lands except said 15 decimals of land being a pond in plot No. 168 under Khatian No. 51 restraining the defendants from interfering illegally or forcibly with the peaceful possession of the plaintiffs thereon. The Title Suit No. 97 of 1977 is liable to be dismissed being barred by limitation, since the record of the Title Suit No. 92 of 1969 shows that the plaintiffs hereof, being defendants in Title Suit No. 92 of 1969, took steps in the suit after its restoration after liberation of the Country in 1972 and thus aware about the decree passed in Title Suit No. 92 of 1969 in the year 1974 and also for want of cause of action having no proof of any right, title or interest on the lands in reference.

18. Accordingly the Civil Appeal No. 229 of 2002 is dismissed with cost and the Civil Appeal No. 230 of 2002 is allowed in part but without any order as to costs. Thus Title Suit No. 97 of 1977 is dismissed and the Title Suit No. 166 of 1976 is decreed in part. The defendant Nos.1-6 are accordingly restrained permanently from entering into and or interfering with peaceful possession of the plaintiffs in the land detailed in the schedule of the plaint of Title Suit No. 166 of 1976, except Plot No.168 under Khatian No.15 measuring 15 decimals of land. The lands on which injunction in granted, are situated within the District-Dhaka, P.S. Fatullah, Mouja No.152 Pikuni, consisting of 39 decimals (Nal) in Plot No. 121 on the North of which is Audhar Mondal and 56 decimals (Nal) in Plot No. 159 on the North which is Halat and both plots are and Khatian No. 161; and 48 decimals (Nal) Plot No. 119 on the North of which Makhan Mondal under Khatil Nos. 173/189/20 and the total area land which is 1.43 acres.

19. Let the records of the Court below, any received, be sent down immediately.

End.

case_source: (From the judgment and order dated 7-9-2016 passed by the High Court Division in Writ Petition No.7166 of 2015 and judgment and order dated 21-8-2017 passed by the Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 1790 of 2017.)
full_judgment:
Hasan Foez Siddique J: Civil Appeal No.1460 of 2017 has arisen out of the judgment and order dated 7-9-2016 passed by the High Court Division in Writ Petition No.7166 of 2015. Civil Review Petition No.181 of 2018 has arisen out of the order dated 21-8-2017 passed by this Division in Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal (CPLA) No.11790 of 2017. The civil appeal as well as the review petition originate from the impugned judgment and order passed by the High Court Division in Writ Petition No.7166 of 2015 and so, both the matters have been heard together and are being disposed of by this common judgment.

2. The respondents of Civil Appeal No.460 of 2017 and Civil Review Petition No. 181 of 2018, as writ petitioners, filed Writ Petition No.7166 of 2015 in the High Court Division stating, inter alia, that the writ petitioners were appointed in the "Small Scale Dairy and Poultry Farmers Support Services in 22 Selected Districts Project" (herein after referred to as the Project) in 5 different categories of posts and on different dates under the Ministry of Fisheries and Livestock (shortly, the Ministry) through written and viva-voce examinations. Writ Petitioner Nos. 1-13 have been working as Veterinary Surgeons, Writ Petitioner Nos. 14-21 have been working as Scientific Officers, Writ Petitioner Nos.22-26 have been working as Animal Production Officers, Writ Petitioner Nos.27-40 have been working as Veterinary Compounders and Writ Petitioner Nos.41-146 have been working as Laboratory Technicians.

3. The first phase of the Project had started on 1-1-2010 and ended on 30-6-2013. Thereafter, it was extended for 1 year up to 30-6-2014 and then it was extended for further 1 year till 30-6-2015. Even after completion of the Project, the writ petitioners are still serving in their respective posts. According to the project proposal (shortly, the PP), the writ-petitioners were supposed to be transferred to the revenue budget inasmuch as the PP contained that after completion of the Project, the assets and manpower would be transferred to the revenue budget. Clause 4.3 (খ) of the decision of the Executive Committee of National Economic Council (ECNEC) dated 81-12-2007, was amended and it was circulated by the Planning Division vide Memo No. পবি/এনইসি-একনেক/সমন্বয়-২/২৬/২০০৭ dated 10-1-2008, where in it has been stated that " সমাপ্ত প্রকল্পের জনবল বিদ্যমান বিধির বিধান অনুসরণ পূর্বক দ্রুত রাজস্ব বাজেট স্থানান্তরের ব্যবস্থা করতে হবে" The Prime Minister also gave her consent to transfer the manpower to the revenue budget from completed projects started after July, 1997.

4. The Director General, Department of Livestock, wrote a letter being Memo No. এলএস/পিইসি-৬৫(১ম খন্ড)/২০১৪/৫৩৬ dated 30-11-2014 (Memo dated 30-11-2014) to the Project Director of the Project informing that a resolution was taken on 9-11-2014 with a view to transferring the manpower for the completed project to the revenue set up. The Project Director was also asked to submit a proposal in the Form as prescribed. In response of the letter dated 13-11- 2014, the Project Director, submitted a proposal vide Memo No. SDPFSP/রাজস্ব খাত/২০১৮/৭০৮ dated 11-12-2014 (shortly, Memo dated 11-12-2014). After, getting the said proposal, the Director General, Department of Livestock sent a letter vide Memo No. শাখা-১/৬এ ৭৬৮/২০১৪/২৩৭২ dated 28-12-2014 to the Secretary of the Ministry with recommendation to transfer the manpower of the Project to the revenue set up. The Ministry thereafter sent a complete proposal vide Memo No.৩৩.০১.০০০০.১২০.১৫.০৪.১৫-১৭ dated 4-2-2015 (shortly, Memo dated 4-2-015) to the Secretary, Ministry of Establishment in order to create 77 posts of 5 categories in revenue budget on a temporary basis. The Ministry of Establishment then wrote a letter under Memo No. ০৫.০২.০০০২.১৫.১৫৭.০০৮.১৫-৭৭ dated 22-3-2015 to the Secretary of the Ministry of Fisheries and Livestock requesting him not to apply separately for the Project rather to apply in combination with the organogram of the Ministry. The Director General, Department of Livestock sent another proposal vide Memo No. ৩৩.০১.০০০০০.০০১.১৫.৭৮৬.১৫-১১১১ dated 24-5-2015 to the Secretary of the Ministry in accordance with the check list as provided by the Ministry of Establishment. Thereafter, in the meeting of steering Committee held on 1-1-2015 it was decided that in order to continue the Project and also to extend activity of the Project in other areas a new project proposal would be launched. An inter-ministerial meeting was held on 29-1-2015 and it was decided that after completion of the Project, the same would be expanded to more areas. After completion of the various development projects under the Ministry, the assets as well as the manpower have been transferred absorbed in the revenue budget on 24-5-2004, 27-3-2007, 10-4-2011 and 8-10-2013 but the petitioners were not absorbed in the revenue budget.

5. In the above circumstances, the writ-petitioners filed the above mentioned Writ Petition for a direction upon the writ respondents for transferring/regularising/absorbing their service in the revenue budget and obtained a Rule.

6. Respondent No. 1, the Secretary, Ministry of Fisheries and Livestock contested the Rule by filing an affidavit-in-opposition, contending, inter alia, that the petitioners were appointed in the Project under the Ministry with consolidated pay temporarily for the Project period only on contractual basis. The Project started in 2010 and ended in 2015. Therefore, the writ petitioners are not entitled to be absorbed in the revenue budget. The Ministry and the Department of Livestock have taken a decision for starting a new project and duration of the said project would be up to 30th June, 2020 and the writ petitioners would be given preference for recruitment in the said new project and the age limit would be relaxed, if necessary and, as such, the Rule should be discharged.

7. Respondent No.2, also contested the Rule by filing an affidavit-in-opposition contending, inter alia, that the Government had never made any promise to absorb the writ petitioners in the revenue budget. The appointment letters of the petitioners clearly contained that their services would be terminated after completion of the Project. The Project had started in 2010 and ended in 2015. Therefore, the writ petitioners cannot claim to be absorbed in the revenue budget and, as such, the writ petitioners have no cause of action to file the Writ Petition. The writ petitioners were appointed in different posts of the Project temporarily with consolidated pay for the Project period only. In order to absorb the employees and officers of development Project, the Government has promulgated Rules namely উন্নয়ন প্রকল্প হইতে রাজস্ব বাজেটে স্থানান্তরিত পদের পদধারীদের নিয়মিতকরণ ও জ্যৈষ্ঠতা নির্ধারণ বিধিমালা, ২০০৫. In rule 2(n) of the said Rules, the projects mean the projects started between 9 April, 1972 and 30th June 1997. The Project, where the writ petitioners were working does not fall within the ambit of rule 2(n) of the Rules. The Rules prescribed the guidelines for the transfer of employees and officers of the development projects to revenue set up. The writ petitioners do not fall within the scope of the guidelines given by the Appellate Division in the case reported in 17 BLC (AD) 91. Therefore, the writ petitioners are not at all entitled to be transferred/absorbed/regularized in the revenue set up and, as such, the Rule is liable to be discharged.

8. The High Court Division, upon hearing the learned Advocates for the contending parties, disposed of the Rule with the following directions:

"Respondents are directed to regularize/ absorb the petitioners under the revenue budget with continuity of service and other benefits subject to availability of the same/equivalent posts provided that they have requisite qualifications."

9. In the aforesaid facts and circumstances, the writ-respondents being aggrieved filed CPLA No. 1790 of 2017 and leave was granted to consider as to whether the post of Scientific Officers, Veterinary Surgeons and Animal Production Officers could be absorbed in the revenue set up without recommendation of the Public Service Commission as directed by the High Court Division.

16. Learned Attorney-General drew our attention to the Gazetted Officers (Department of Livestock Service) Recruitment Rules, 1984. (b) by promotion; or

17. Rule 4 provides that no appointment to specified post by directs recruitment shall be made except upon the recommendation of the Commission. Schedule of the said Rules provides the method of direct recruitment that the recruitment should be made as prescribed in the BGS (Agriculture Livestock) Recruitment Rules, 1984.

18. The non-gazetted employees (Department of Livestock Services) Recruitment Rules. 1985 provides the provisions for recruitment of the Non-gazetted Employees.

19. Rule 3 of the said Rules provides that subject to the provisions of the Schedule and instructions relating to reservation and quota, appointment to a specified post shall be made-

(a) by direct recruitment, or

(b) by promotion.

20. Sub-rule (2) of Rule 3 provides that no person shall be appointed to a specified post unless he has the requisite qualifications, and in the case of direct recruitment, he is within the age limit, if any, prescribed in the Schedule for that post. Rule 4 provides that no appointment to a specified post by direct recruitment shall be made except upon the recommendation of the Commission. 

21. In Bangladesh Civil Service Recruitment Rules, 1981, the provisions and procedure for appointment of officers in the, posts for which some of the writ petitioners sought for absorption have specifically been mentioned.

22. Those are the regular and usual statutory provisions for appointment through the Public Service Commission in the posts, for which, the writ petitioners have prayed for absorption.

23. It appears that sometimes the Courts have not kept the legal aspect in mind and have occasionally even stayed the regular process of employment being set in motion and in some cases, even directed irregular or improper entrants to be absorbed into service. The Court has also on occasions issued direction which cannot, said to be consistent with the laws of public employment. Our constitutional scheme envisages employment by the Government and its instrumentalities on the basis of legally approved procedure established by the relevant laws. However, article 133 of the Constitution does not abridge the power of the executive to act without a law. But, if there is, statutory Rule on the matter, the executive must abide by that Rule and it cannot in exercise of executive power ignore or, work contrary to that Rule. Sometimes it is found that the process is not adhered to and the constitutional scheme of public employment is bypassed.

24. It is the case of the writ petitioners that since in the PP it has been mentioned that after completion of the project, the assets and manpower of the Project should be transferred in the revenue budget the writ petitioners legitimately expected that their service would be absorbed in the revenue set-up.

“গণপ্রজাতন্ত্রী বাংলাদেশ সরকার

পরিপত্র

সম/আর-১/এস-৬/৯১-৩০৮ (২৫০),  তারিখঃ ৫-১১-১৯৯১ইং/২০-৭-১৩৯৮বাং।

বিষয়ঃ উন্নয়ন প্রকল্পের পদধারীকে রাজস্ব খাতভুক্ত পদে এবং রাজস্ব খাতভুক্ত পদধারীকে উন্নয়ন প্রকল্পের পদে নিয়োগ/ পোষ্টিং/পদোন্নতি প্রদান সম্পর্কিত ।

উপরোক্ত বিষয়ে গত ২৯-৫-৯১ইং তারিখে জারীকৃত সম/আর-১/এস-৬/৯১১৬৪ (২০০) নং পরিপত্রটি সেংযুক্ত) বাতিলপূর্বক আলোচ্য পরিপত্রটি জারী করা হইল। ইদানিং লক্ষ্য করা যাইতেছে যে, উন্নয়ন প্রকল্পের পদধারীকে রাজত্ব খাতযুক্ত পদে এবং রাজত্ব খাতভূক্ত পদধারীকে উন্নয়ন প্রকল্পের পদে নিয়োগ/পোষ্টিং/পদোন্নতি প্রদান করিবার প্রবণতা দেখা দিয়াছে। এই প্রবণতা দূর করিবার লক্ষ্যে সরকার নিম্নরুপ সিদ্ধান্ত গ্রহণ করিয়াছেনঃ

(ক) উন্নয়ন প্রকল্পের পদ এবং রাজন্থ খাতডুক্ত পদ সম্পূর্ণ ভিন্ন। উভয়ের নিয়োগ ক্ষেত্রে নিয়োগ বিধিও ভিন্ন । কাজেই উভয়ের পারস্পরিক নিয়োগ/পোষ্টিং। বদলী/পদোন্নতি সম্পূর্ণ বিধি বহির্ভূত । উন্নয়ন প্রকল্পের চাকুরীর কোন নিশ্চয়তা নাই। উনুয়ন প্রকল্প শেষ হইয়া গেলে প্রকল্পে চাকুরীরতদের চাকুরী হইতে অব্যাহতি দেওয়া হয়। তবে উন্নয়ন প্রকল্প মেয়াদ শেষে রাজস্ব খাতভুক্ত হইলে সেইক্ষেত্রে প্রকল্পে চাকুরীরতগণ ৯-৩-৮৬ইং তারিখের সম/আর-১/এস-৮/৮৬-৫৫ (১০০) নং স্মারক বা সময়ে সময়ে সরকার কর্তৃক সংশোধিত স্মারক মোতাবেক রাজস্ব খাতভুক্ত পদে নিয়োগের জন্য কতিপয় শর্ত সাপেক্ষে বিবেচিত হইতে পারেন। প্রধান শর্ত এই যে, তাহাদের রাজস্ব খাতভুক্ত পদের নিয়োগ-বিধির শর্ত পুরণ করিয়া অন্যান্য সকল প্রার্থীর সহিত প্রতিযোগিতার মাধ্যমে নির্বাচন লাভ করিতে হইবে। কাজেই উন্নয়ন প্রকল্পের পদধিকারী কোন অবস্থাতেই রাজস্ব খাততুক্ত পদে বদলী বা পদোন্নুতির মাধ্যমে নিয়োগ/পোষ্টিং লাভ করিতে পারেন না।

খে) রাজন্ব খাতভুক্ত কোন কর্মকর্তা/কর্মচারীকে প্রকল্পের নিয়োগ-বিধির অধীনে উন্নয়ন প্রকল্পের পদের বিপরীতে বদলী, পদোন্নতি প্রদান বা পদোন্নতি প্রদানপূর্বক নিয়োগ/ পোষ্টিং দেওয়া যাইবে না।

(গ) রাজস্ব খাতভুক্ত কোন কর্মকর্তা/কর্মচারীকে শুধুমাত্র স্বীয় পদমর্যাদা ও বেতন স্কেলেরসহ উন্নয়ন প্রকল্পের কোন পদে প্রেষণে নিয়োগ/পোষ্টিং প্রদান করা যাইবে । এইক্ষেত্রে প্রেষণে নিয়োগলাভকারী তাহার গেড পে অর্থৎ রাজস্ব বাজেটাধীন পদে তিনি যে বেতন-ভাতাদি পাইতেন তাহাই পাইবেন।

(ঘ) রাজস্ব খাতভুক্ত কোন কর্মকর্তা/কর্মচারী স্বেচ্ছায় সরাসরি নিয়োগের সকল আনুষ্ঠানিকতা পালনপূর্বক উন্নয়ন প্রকল্পের সরাসরি নিয়োগলাভ করিতে পারিবেন । তবে সেইক্ষেত্রে উন্নয়ন প্রকল্পে যোগদানের তারিখ হইতে তিনি পূর্ব পদে (রোজস্ব খাতভুক্ত পদে) প্রত্যাবর্তনের যোগ্যতা হারাইবেন। অর্থাৎ উন্নয়ন প্রকল্পে যোগদানের তারিখ হইতে তিনি উন্নয়ন প্রকল্পের কর্মকর্তা/কর্মচারী হিসাবে গণ্য হইবেন।

২। সকল প্রশাসনিক মন্ত্রণালয়/বিভাগকে তাহার নিয়ন্ত্রণাধীন সকল অফিস/প্রশিক্ষণ প্রতিষ্ঠানে বিষয়টি অবহতি করিয়া কার্যকারী পদক্ষেপ গ্রহণ নিশ্চিত করিবার জন্য অনুরোধ করা হইল ।

৩। ইহাতে অর্থ মন্ত্রণালয়ের সম্মতি রহিয়াছে ।

“গণপ্রজাতন্ত্রী বাংলাদেশ সরকার

বিষয়ঃ সমাপ্ত উন্নয়ন প্রকল্পের পর রাজস্ব বাজেটে স্থানাত্তরের প্রস্তাব সংগঠন ও ব্যবস্থাপনা অনুবিভাগে প্রেরণ ।

মন্ত্রণালয়/বিভাগ ও তদধীনস্থ সংস্থা সমূহের সমাগ উন্নয়ন প্রকল্পের পদ, যানবাহন, অফিস সরঞ্জামাদি রাজস্ব বাজেটে স্থানান্তরের প্রস্তাবে প্রাথমিকভাবে সংস্থাপন মন্ত্রণালয়ের সংগঠন ও ব্যবস্থাপনা অনুবিভাগে এবং অর্থ মন্ত্রণালয়ের অর্থ বিভাগের সম্মতির প্রয়োজন হয়। প্রকল্প সমান্তির পর প্রস্তাব প্রেরণ করা হলে এ ধরনের জনবলের বেতন ভাতাদি প্রদানসহ অন্যান্য নানাবিধ জটিলতা দেখা দেয় বলে প্রকল্প সমাপ্তির অন্তত ছয় মাস পূর্বে । অনুরূপ প্রস্তাব সংস্থাপন মন্ত্রণালয়ে প্রেরণ করার নির্দেশ ইতিপূর্বে অর্থ বিভাগ থেকে জারি হয়েছে। তা আরো সংশোধন করে সরকার এ মর্মে সিদ্ধান্ত গ্রহণ করেছে যে, রাজস্ব বাজেটে স্থানাস্তরযোগ্য পদের প্রস্তাব প্রকল্প সমাপ্তির অন্তত ছয় মাস পূর্বে যুগপত্ভাবে সংস্থাপন মন্ত্রণালয়ের সওব্য অনুবিভাগ এবং অর্থ বিভাগের উন্নয়ন অনুবিভাগের প্রেরণ করতে হবে। শিক্ষা ও স্বাস্থ্য প্রতিষ্ঠান সম্পর্কিত প্রকল্পের ক্ষেত্রে প্রকল্প সমাপ্তির অনধিক এক বৎসর এক বৎসর কিংবা অন্তত ছয় মাস পূর্বে প্রস্তাব পাঠাতে হবে । প্রস্তাবে রাজন্ব বাজেটে স্থানাস্তরযোগ্য জনবলের যৌক্তিকতা, ন্যুনতম জনবলের সংখ্যা এবং প্রস্তাবিত সাংগঠনিক সম্পর্কে একটি বিশ্লেষণধর্মী স্বয়ংসম্পূর্ণ সার-সংক্ষেপ থাকতে হবে।

২। উল্লেখ্য যে, বর্তমানে উল্লিখিত প্রস্তাব সংস্থাপন মন্ত্রণালযের প্রেরণের সময় এ মন্ত্রালয়ের ১-২-১৯৮৭ তারিখের সম/সওব্য (সমন্বয়)-১১/৮৭-৫৮ (২৩৩) সংখ্যক স্মারক মারফত প্রণীত ছকটি অনুসরণ করতে হবে । এ ছকটি আংশিক সংশোধনের প্রয়োজন অনুভূত হওয়ায় একটি সংশোধিত ছক প্রণয়ন করা হয়েছে। সংশোধিত ছক সংলগ্নী “ক' রূপে সংযোজন করা হল ।

৩। এখন থেকে প্রথম অনুচ্ছেদে বর্ণিত সার-সংক্ষেপসহ সংলগ্ন ছক (ছকের পরিশিষ্টে বর্ণিত সকল তালিকাসহ) পুরণপূর্বক উল্লিখিত প্রস্তাব সংস্থাপন মন্ত্রণালয়ের প্রেরণের জন্য অনুরোধ করা হলো। যথাযথভাবে প্রেরিত প্রস্তাবের উপর সংস্থাপন মন্ত্রণালয়ের মতামত প্রস্তাব প্রাপ্তির এক মাসের মধ্যে প্রদান করা হবে।

(মুহাম্মদ হুমায়ুন কবির)

উপ-সচিব ।”

28. On 24th December 2008, the Minister of Establishment issued another circular with the subject heading, “উন্নয়ন প্রকল্প সমান্তির পর অত্যাবশ্যকীয় পদ রাজস্ব বাজেটে স্থানাস্তর” The contents of the circular dated 24-12-2008 run as follows:

“গণপ্রজাতন্ত্রী বাংলাদেশ সরকার

সংস্থাপন মন্ত্রণালয়

সওব্য-১৫৪) অধিশাখা ।

পরিপত্র

নং-সম (সওব্য-৪)-১প-১/২০০৮-২৫৫

তারিখঃ ১০ পৌষ, ১৪১৫/২৪ ডিসেম্বর, ২০০৮।

বিষয়ঃ উন্নয়ন প্রকল্প সমাপ্তির অত্যাবশ্যকীয় পদ রাজস্ব বাজেটে স্থানান্তর ।

সরকার সিদ্ধান্ত গ্রহণ করেছে যে, উন্নয়ন প্রকল্পের মাধ্যমে গৃহীত কর্মসূচী সমাপ্তির পর পরিচালনার জন্য রাজস্ব বাজেটে পদ সৃজন ও স্থানান্তরের বিষয়ে নিম্নরূপ বিধান অনুসৃত হবেঃ

১। এখন থেকে যে সকল উন্নয়ন প্রকল্প অনুমোদিত হবে তাতে প্রকল্প চলাকালীন পদের চাহিদার পাশাপাশি প্রকল্প সমাপ্তির পর সংশ্লিষ্ট প্রতিষ্ঠানের বিদ্যমান পদের অতিরিক্ত যেসব পদ অপরিহার্য বলে গণ হবে, সে সকল পদের চাহিদাও একই পদ্ধতিতে পর্যালোচনা করে উন্নয়ন প্রকল্প ছক (DPP)-এ অন্তর্ভুক্ত করতে হবে অতঃপর (DPP)-তে অন্তর্ভুক্ত রাজস্বখাতে স্থানাত্তরযোগ্য অপরিহার্য পদের ক্ষেত্রে বিধি মোতাবেক সংস্থাপন মন্ত্রণালয়ে সম্মতি গ্রহণ করতে হবে। মন্ত্রিপরিষদ বিভাগের ২২-১-২০০৩ খ্রিঃ তারিখের মপবি/কঃবিঃশাঃ/মক-০১/২০০৩/২৮ নং প্রজ্ঞাপন মূলে গঠিত উন্নয়ন প্রকল্পের পদ/জনবল নির্ধারণ সংক্রান্ত কমিটি পুঙ্খানুপুজ্খ পরীক্ষা-নিরীক্ষা করার মাধ্যমে প্রকল্প চলাকালীন ও সমাপ্তির পর রাজস্ব খাতের অপরিহার্য উভয় প্রকার পদের শ্রেণী ও সংখ্যা নির্ধারণের সুপারিশ প্রদান করে।

২। প্রকল্প সমাপ্তির সাথে সাথে রাজস্বখাতে স্থানাস্তযোগ্য অপরিহার্য পদ স্বয়ংক্রিয়ভাবে অস্থায়ীভিত্তিতে রাজস্ব বাজেটে স্থানান্তরিত হবে। সংশ্লিষ্ট প্রশাসনিক মন্ত্রণালয় সংস্থাপন মন্ত্রণালয় ও অর্থ বিভাগকে অবহিত রেখে রাজস্ব বাজেটে পদ স্থানাস্তরের আদেশ/ধজ্ঞাপন জারী করবে। এক্ষেত্রে সংস্থাপন ও অর্থ মন্ত্রণালয়ের পুনরায় সম্মতি গ্রহণের প্রয়োজন হবে না।

৩। প্রকল্পের মাধ্যমে গৃহীত কোনো কর্মসূচী দ্বারা উপজেলা, জেলা ও বিভাগীয় পর্যায়ে কোন দপ্তর, থানা ও তদন্ত কেন্দ্র স্থাপন এবং পদ সৃজন করা হলে সে ক্ষেত্রে প্রশাসনিক উন্নয়ন সংক্রান্ত সচিব কমিটির সুপারিশ ও নিকার এর পূর্ব অনুমোদন গ্রহণ করতে হবে।

81 উন্নয়ন প্রকল্প সমাপ্তির পর রাজন্বখাতে স্থানাত্তরিত পদে নিয়োগ বিধি ও বিদ্যমান বিধি-বিধান অনুসরণ করে জনবল নিয়োগ করতে হবে। তবে প্রকল্প সমাপ্তির পূর্বে নিয়োগ প্রক্রিয়া শুরু করা যেতে পারে। এছাড়াও প্রচলিত বিধি-বিধান ও পদ্ধতি অনুসরণ করে রাজস্বখাতে স্থানাত্তরিত পদগুলো সংরক্ষণ ও স্থায়ীাকরণের ব্যবস্থা গ্রহণ করতে হবে। স্থায়ীকরণ প্রক্রিয়া সম্পন্ন হওয়ার পর সরকারি আদেশসমূহের কপিসহ টিও এন্ডই সংশোধননের প্রস্তাব সংস্থাপন মন্ত্রণালয়ে প্রেরণ করতে হবে।

৫। উন্নয়ন প্রকল্প বাস্তবায়নের জন্য জনবল নিয়োগের ক্ষেত্রে অর্থ বিভাগ কর্তৃক ২২-৫-২০০৮ খিঃ তারিখের অম/অবি/বা-১২/বিবিধ-৬৫/০৭ (অংশ)/১০৪০ নং স্মারকে জারীকৃত পরিপত্র অনুসরণ করতে হবে।

৬। এপরিপত্র জনস্বার্থে জারী করা হলো এবং তা ১ জানুয়ারী, ২০০৯ ধিঃ হতে কার্যালয় হবে।

সংস্থাপন মন্ত্রণালয়ের ২৪-১২-২০০৮ তারিখের স্মারক নং সম (সওব্য-৪)-১প-১/২০০৮-২৫৫ মূলে জারীকৃত পরিপত্রের উল্লেখ করা হয়েছির যে, ১ জানুয়ারী ২০০৯ হতে যে সকল উন্নয়ন প্রকল্প সংশ্লিষ্ট কর্তৃপক্ষ কর্তৃক অনুমোদিত হবে। তাতে প্রকল্প চলাকালীন প্রয়োজনীয় পদের পাশাপাশি প্রকল্প সমাপ্তির পর সংশ্লিষ্ট প্রতিষ্ঠানের বিদ্যমান পদের অতিরিক্ত যে সব পদ অপরিহার্য বলে গণ্য হবে, সে সকল পদের চাহিদাও একই পদ্ধতিতে পর্যালোচনা করে উন্নয়ন প্রকল্প ছক (DPP)-এ অন্তর্ভুক্ত করতে হবে। অতঃপর DPP তে উক্তরূপে অন্তর্ভূক্ত অত্যাবশ্যকীয়/অপরিহার্য পদসমূহ রাজস্বখাতে স্থানান্তরের ক্ষেত্রে বিধি মোতাবেক সংস্থাপন মন্ত্রণালয়ের সম্মতি গ্রহণ করতে হবে।

২। কিন্তু উক্ত পরিপত্রটি জারীর পর উন্নয়ন প্রকল্প প্রণয়নও অনুমোদনের ক্ষেত্রে পরিপত্রটির বিধি-বিধান যথাযথভাবে অনুসৃত না হওয়ায় উক্ত পরিপত্রের নির্দেশনামতে রাজস্বখাতে স্থানাস্তরযোগ্য অপরিহার্য পদের চাহিদা DPP-তে অন্তর্ভুক্ত করে রাজস্বখাতে স্থানাত্তরযোগ্য অপরিহার্য পদসমূহ রাজস্বখাতে স্থানান্তরের নিমিত্ত কোন প্রস্তাব অদ্যাবধি সংস্থাপন মন্ত্রণালয়ে পাওয়া যায়নি । উন্নয়ন প্রকল্পের মেয়াদ শেষে অত্যাবশ্যকীয়/অপরিহার্য পদসমূহ যথাসময়ে এবং যথাযথ উপায়ে DPP-তে অন্তর্ভূক্ত না করা হলে অপরিহার্য পদসমূহ রাজস্বখাতে স্থানান্তরের ক্ষেত্রে ভবিষ্যতে জটিলতা সৃষ্টি হতে পারে।

Except the aforesaid Government memorandum, circulars or orders, we do not find any specific statutory provision to transfer/absorb the officers or employees of the development: project to revenue set up. However, in the circular dated 24-8-2008 it has been specifically mentioned that after completions of the development project, appointment should be given in the transferred revenue set up following the related service Rules. As the Government has got a right to issue executive instructions in the spheres which are not covered by the Rules, any administrative instructions issued are, supposed to be followed. It is to be remembered that the executive power could be exercised only to fill up the gaps but the instructions cannot and should not supplant the law, but only supplement the law. No express power was conferred and in fact cannot be conferred to relax the rules of recruitment. Broadly speaking, those administrative orders, circulars on instructions do not have any statutory force and those do not give rise to any legal right in favour of the party aggrieved and cannot be enforced in a court of law against the Government.
