full_judgment:
SM Maniruzzaman J : Common questions of law and facts are involved in both the writ petitions and have been taken up for hearing together and are being disposed of by this single judgment.

2. These Rules Nisi, issued under Article 102 of the Constitution of the People's Republic of Bangladesh, the respondents have been called upon to show cause as to why the impugned order dated 5-1-2006 and 17-4-2006 respectively passed by the respondent No. 1 vide Letter No. ৫ম/২০(১৮)এলসি(এডমিন)/২০০২ (পার্ট-১)/১৯৭২-৯৫ ordering the respondent No. 2 for imposing minimum value at US$ 580 per MT of imported frozen "Hilsha Fish" (Annxure-G & G-1) and assessment order dated 13-7-2006 passed by the respondent No. 4 in Bill of Entry Nos. C-1500-06 and 1499-06 both dated 13-7-2006 imposing minimum value at US$ 580 Per MT of imported frozen "Hilsha Fish" in place of Invoice Value US$ 300 per MT (Annexure-F) should not be declared to have been made without lawful authority and is of no legal effect and/or such other or further order or orders passed as to this Court may seem fit and proper.

3. At the time of issuance of the Rules, the respondents were directed to release the petitioners' imported consignment under Bill of Entry Nos. C-1500-06 and C-1499-06 both dated 13-7-2006 on payment of customs duties and other taxes on the basis of invoice value and for the difference between the invoice value and the value demanded by the Customs Authority 20% should be paid in cash and on furnishing bank guarantee for the rest within 5 (five) days from the date of receipt of this order. 4. Facts, necessary for disposal of the Rules, in short, are that the petitioners of both the writ petitions are businessman engaged in the business of importation of various home consumption items from abroad and after importation, they sell the same in the local market. Both the petitioners have been continuing their business by obtaining necessary permission from the government concerned.

5. The petitioners in course of their business decided to import 33.333 Metric Ton of frozen "Hilsha Fish" bearing HS Code No. 0303.29.29 from Myanmar. As per the business practice prevalent in Teknaf, the petitioners made Foreign Demand Draft being No. BTA/ FD0005978 dated 117.2006 for an amount of US$ 10,000 and BTA/FD0005998 dated 13-7-2006 for an amount of US$ 10,000 in Sonali Bank, Teknaf Branch, Cox's Bazar in favour of Mayanmar Economic Bank, Maungdaw Branch, Maungdaw, Mayanmar under Border Trade Agreement executed between Myanmar and Bangladesh on 18-5-1994.

6. After receiving the aforesaid payment orders, the supplier made shipment of the goods and issued necessary shipping documents namely Commercial Invoice and Packing List in support of shipment. After arrival of the goods at Land Customs Station, Teknaf, the petitioners of the respective writ petitions submitted Bill of Entry Nos. C-1500-06 and C-1499-06 both dated 13-7-2006 through their C & F agent along with necessary shipping documents for assessment and releasing the consignment on the basis of invoice value. The Customs authority rejected the invoice value at the rate of US$ 300 Per Metric Ton and assessed the goods at the rate of US$ 580 Per Metric Ton being minimum assessable value, which was fixed as per recommendation of the Value Fixation Committee, Customs House, Chattogram. The respondent No.1, the Commissioner, Customs, Excise and VAT Commissionerate, Chattogram had fixed the minimum assessable value of the frozen "Hilsha Fish" at the rate of US$ 580 Per Metric Ton vide letter No. ৫ম/২০(১৮)এলসি(এডমিন)/২০০২ (পার্ট-১)/১২৭-২৯  dated 5-1-2006. Said order came in force on 31-12-2005 and would remain in force till further order (Annexure-G). Subsequent, thereto the said respondent issued another order vide Nothi No. ৫ম/২০(১৮)এলসি(এডমিন)/২০০২ (পার্ট-১)/১৯৭২-৯৫ dated 17-4-2006 fixing the minimum value of some imported goods including the frozen "Hilsha Fish" at the rate of US$ 580 Per Metric Ton giving effect from 16-4-2006 to 30-6-2006 (Annexure-G1).

7. In the supplementary affidavit to the writ petition, it has been further stated that the respondent No.1 by his office order dated 19-7-2006 further fixed minimum value of some imported goods including the frozen "Hilsha Fish" at the rate of US$ 580 per Metric Ton giving effect from 1-7-2006 to 30-9-2006 (Annexure-I). The aforesaid 3 (three) orders were issued by the respondent No.1, fixing the minimum assessable value of frozen "Hilsha Fish" at the rate of US$ 580 per Metric Ton. On the basis of the said minimum value, the respondents Customs authorities have assessed the petitioners' consignment fixing the value of Taka 13,90,207 instead of invoice value of Taka 6,98,000.

8. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the aforesaid office circulars and subsequent assessment orders the petitioners have filed the instant application under Article 102 of the Constitution of the People's Republic of Bangladesh and obtained the present Rules and interim order of stay.

9. Mr MA Hannan, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner in both the writ petitions submits that under the provision of section 25(3) of the Customs Act, 1969 the government has authority to fix minimum value by publishing notification in the official gazette but, no gazette notification was made fixing the minimum value of the frozen "Hilsha Fish" in question under section 25(3) of the said Act. Hence, the fixation of minimum value by the impugned orders are liable to be declared to have been passed without lawful authority. He further goes to submit that there is no existence of the Value Determination Committee either under the Customs Act, 1969 or the Customs Valuation Rules, 2000 and as such, fixation of the value by the Value Determination Committee for the imported frozen "Hilsha Fish" at the rate of US$ 580 Per Metric Ton and on the basis of the said value making assessment of the petitioners' goods in question is fully without jurisdiction. Lastly, he goes to submit that the transaction value of the consignment at the rate of US$ 300 Per Metric Ton has been rejected by the Customs authority and has imposed the value of US$ 580 Per Metric Ton in violation of the provision of rule 3 read with rules 4,5,6,7,8 and 9 of the Valuation Rules, 2000. In support of his contention the learned Advocate for the petitioner has placed reliance on an unreported decision passed by this Court in writ petition No. 2025 of 2006 along with two other writ petitions.

10. Countering the said submissions, Mr Samarendra Nath Biswas, the learned Deputy Attorney-General appearing on behalf of the respondent-government without filing any affidavit-in-opposition, submits that the present Rules must fail as being not maintainable, for the petitioner had alternative forum under the Customs Act, 1969 as well as Customs Valuation Rules, 2000 against the impugned assessment order before the Appellant authority concern, so have been challenged in this writ petition. Hence, the present Rules are liable to be discharged as being not maintainable.

11. We have heard the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner, the learned Deputy Attorney-General appearing for the respondent government, have perused the writ petitions along with annexures so have been appended thereto and relevant provision of the law.

12. Admittedly, the petitioners of the respective writ petitions imported 33.333 Metric Ton frozen "Hilsha Fish" from Myanmar at the rate of US$ 300 Per Metric Ton and total value of the consignment was US$ 10,000. After arrival of the goods at Land Customs Station, Teknaf, Cox's Bazar, the petitioners of respective writ petitions through their C & F agent submitted Bill of Entry Nos. C-1500.06 and C-1499-06 both dated 13-7-2006 for assessment and releasing the goods. On perusal of Bills of Entry (Annexure-F to the writ petitions) it appears that the goods were duly inspected by the Customs authority and found that—

“১০% দৈবচরনের ভিত্তিতে কায়িক করে প্রতি বস্তার গড় নীট ওজন ১৮.৩৯৫৬ কেজি করে পাওয়া যায়। Invoice ও packing list এর ঘোষণা অনুযায়ী মিল রয়েছে।”

13. It also appears that the invoice value of the consignment is US$ 300 Per Metric Ton total invoice value is US$ 10,000 equivalent to Taka 6,98,000 but, the Customs authority without accepting the transaction value has fixed the assessable value of Taka 13,90,207 upon giving adjustment US$ 1.9917% on the invoice value. In this regard, the categorical assertion of the petitioners are that the Customs authority has fixed the assessable value as per direction so given by the respondent No. 1 by his office orders dated 5-1-2006, 17-4-2006 and 19-7-2006 respectively.

14. The cardinal issue requires determination in the instant Rules is that whether the respondent No. 1, the Commissioner, Customs, Excise and VAT is empowered to fix the minimum assessable value of any imported goods as well as frozen "Hilsha Fish" in question by his office order or by recommendation of any committee under the Customs Act, 1969 or Rules framed thereunder. In this regard the learned Advocate for the petitioners has argued that the government is only the authority to frame Rules for determination of assessable value of imported goods and to fix tariff or minimum value of any imported goods by publishing the Gazette notification as per provision under section 25 of the Customs Act. Section 25 of the Customs Act is quoted below:—

"Secion-25: Value of goods for assessment purpose 1. whenever customs duty is leviable on any goods by reference to their value, the actual price, that is, the price actually paid or payable, or the nearest ascertainable equivalent of such price, at which such or like goods are ordinarily sold, or offered for sale, for delivery at the time and place of importation or exportation, as the case may be, in course of international trade under fully competitive conditions, where the seller and the buyer have no interest in the business of each other and the price is the sole consideration for sale or offer for sale, shall be the value.]"

[Explanation—For the purposes of this sub-section, the expression—

[(a) "the time of importation" means the date on which a bill of entry is delivered under section 79.]

(b) "the time of exportation" means the time when the bill of export is delivered under section 131, or, when export of the goods is allowed [under that section] without a bill of export or in anticipation of the presentation of a bill of export, the time when the goods is [?] taken to the customs port or customs airport or customs station for the purpose of export;

(C) (i) "the place of importation" means the customs port or customs airport[?] or the customs station at which the bill of entry is first submitted; and

(ii) "place of exportation"[?] means the customs port or the station[?] at which the bill of export is submitted.]

(2) Subject to the provisions of sub-section (1), the price referred to in that sub-section in respect of imported goods shall be determined in accordance with the rules made in this behalf.

(3) Notwithstanding anything contained in this section, the Government may, by notification in the official Gazette, fix, for the purpose of levying customs duties, tariff values [or minimum values] for any goods imported or exported as chargeable with customs duty ad valorem:

Provided that any imported or exported goods, the declared value of which is higher than its tariff value fixed under this sub-section, shall be chargeable with customs duties on the basis of its declared value.

15. On perusal of the aforesaid section 25, it appears that the government is only the authority to frame Rules for determination of assessable value of imported goods as per sub-section 2 and to fix tariff or minimum value of any imported goods by publishing the notification in the official Gazette as per sub section 3 of section 25 of the Customs Act for the purpose of assessment of the imported goods.

16. In the impugned office orders dated 5-1-2006 (Annexure-G) dated 17-4-2006 (Annexure-G 1) and subsequent order dated 19-7-2006 (Annexure-I) respectively, it appears that the respondent No. 1, the Commissioner, Customs, Excise and VAT had fixed the minimum value of the imported frozen "Hilsha Fish" by those office orders. But, section 25 of the Customs Act has not empowered the Customs authority as well as the respondent No.1 the Commissioner, Custom, Excise and VAT to issue such kind of circulars fixing minimum value of any imported goods. Rather, sub-section (3) of section 25 authorizes only the Government to fix the tariff/minimum value of any imported goods to be determined and fixed by the Gazette notification.

17. In the present case, the respondent No. 1, the Commissioner, Customs, Excise and VAT Commissionerate had fixed the minimum value of some imported goods including the frozen "Hilsha Fish" in question bearing HS Code No. 0303.10.10 at the rate of US$ 580 Per Metric Ton by the impugned office order/ circulars dated 5-1-2006 (Annexure-G) giving effect from 31-12-2005 until further order, Orders dated 17-4-2006 (Annexure-G1) and dated 19-7-2006 (Annexure-I) respectively were circulated by the said respondent giving effect from 16-4-2006 to 30-6-2006 and 1-7-2006 to 30-9-2006 respectively. The petitioner of the respective writ petitions submitted Bill of Entry on 13-7-2006 (Annexure-F to the respective writ petitions) and that the Customs authority had assessed the imported frozen "Hilsha Fish" at the rate of US$ 580 Per Metric Ton on the basis of impugned circulars, not by following the Customs Valuation Rules, 2000.

18. Under the statutory obligation, a government is bound to declare tariff value or minimum value in the official gazette for the purpose of import and export. In the present case, no such gazette notification has been published in respect of importation of frozen "Hilsha Fish" The value as fixed at the rate of US$ 580 Per Metric Ton by the Commissioner, customs, Excise and VAT Commissionerate does not have any sanction of law; rather the same having been issued in violation of section 25(3) of the Customs Act, 1969, it is liable to be knocked down.

19. In this regard, in the unreported case of SM Abdul Alim vs Commissioner of Customs, Customs House, Chittagong and other passed by one of the Benches of this Division in writ petition No. 2025 of 2006, it has been observed, inter-alia that;

"It appears that the respondents get the consignment assessed on the recommendation of the assessment committee which is also illegal and without lawful authority because law does not provide for such mechanism for making the assessment."

20. Also, in the case of Collector of Customs vs TK Oil Refinery Ltd, and 22 others reported in 62 DLR (AD) 217, it has been held that;—

"As it appears, that High Court Division made the Rules absolute holding that a reading Of the provisions of section 25(1)(2)(3) and section 30(1) of the Customs Act show that the Customs Authority is authorised to assess customs duties of imported goods at the value prevalent on the date when the bill of entry is presented for assessment of customs duties but, in the present case, the Customs authority fixed the indicative value for the purpose of assessment of customs duties of the imported CDSO and CPO imported by the respondents long before the presentation of the bill of entry and accordingly, "indicative value, that has been Ned by the circular dated 3-7-94, cannot be considered to have been fixed in the light of the provisions of section 25(1)(2) and (3) of the Customs Act and that in terms of the above section the Customs Authority, in appropriate cases, no doubt, is competent to fix normal value of imported goods upon rejection of the invoice value or the declared value but in such case the Customs authority would be required to notify importers informing them that the Customs authority is not accepting the invoice value or declared value as the basis for the purpose of assessment of customs duty and is going to fix the normal price of the imported goods for the assessment of customs duties and the customs authority would also be required to afford an opportunity to the importers to place their cases, if any, in support of their claim that the invoice value, in fact, is the normal price of the imported merchandise for the purpose of assessment of customs duties or that as against the invoice/declared value of the imported goods the customs authority is going to tax the normal price of the goods for the purpose of assessment of customs duties but, in the instant case, that has not been done by the customs authority and the Customs  authority fixed through internal circular, certain prices of CDSO and CPO for the purpose of assessment of customs duties  terming the same as "indicative value" but  under the Customs Act. the revenue realizing Authority or the Customs Authority is authorised to fix tariff value under 'section 25(7) of the Act at a prior date through Gazette notification for the purpose of assessment of customs duties and the  indicative value that has been fixed later On and circulated through Circular dated 3-7-94  was admittedly not notified in the official Gazette,"

21. Further, it has been held that;—

"As it appears, at the conclusion, that High Court Division directed that the customs authority is to assess the customs duties of the goods in respect of which the letters of credit were opened prior to the deletion of the tariff value by the SRO dated 9-6-1994 on the basis of tariff value prevalent at the time of opening of letters of credit and in other cases taking the invoice value but the above order of the High Court Division to the extent that "in other cases taking the invoice value" is modified to the extent, that if the invoice  value as shown by the respondents are not acceptable to them the Customs Authority  will be at liberty to fix normal price in terms  of the provisions of section 25(1) of the  Customs Act is accordance with law and then assess customs duty and other duties on the  basis of normal price so fixed."

22. In view of the above, fixing the value of frozen "Hilsha Fish" by the Commissioner, Customs, Excise and VAT, Commissionerate, Chattogram in the impugned official circulars has no legal basis and without sanction of law.

<u>23. The assertion of the learned Deputy Attorney-General in respect of availability of the alternative remedy, in the present context is a misconceived one, it is the settled principle of law that when an illegality is apparent on the face of record and the respondents performing the function of the Republic have acted totally without jurisdiction, invoking forum as provided under Article 102 of the Constitution of the People's Republic of Bangladesh is not a bar. The fiAtion of minimum value by the respondent No. 1, the Commissioner of Customs, Excise and VAT, Chattogram without publishing in the Gazette notification ,and assessment thereafter pursuant to the said ,value is without jurisdiction.</u>

24. In view of the above, the forum as provided under the Customs Act, 1969 is not a bar invoking Special Original Jurisdiction as provided under Article 102 of the Constitution of the People's Republic of Bangladesh.

25. Considering the facts and circumstances of the cases as stated hereinabove, we find substance to the contention so have been raised by the petitioners and accordingly we are inclined to make the Rules absolute.

26. In the result, both the Rules are made absolute without any order as to cost. The fixation of the minimum value of Frozen "Hilsha Fish" under HS Code No. 0303.39.10 at rate of US$ 580 Per Metric Ton by the official circulars dated 5-1-2006, 17-4-2006 and 19-7-2006 (Annexure-G, G1, I respectively), pursuant thereto the assessment order as appeared in Bill of Entry Nos. C-1500-06 and 1499-06 both dated 13-7-2006 (Annexure-F to the writ petitions) are hereby declared to have been passed without jurisdiction and hence, of no legal effect.

27. Since, the goods in question have already been released by the Customs authority on the basis of interim order of direction so passed by this Court at the time of issuance of the Rules, in this situation, the concerned respondent is hereby directed to assess finally the imported goods of the petitioners, covered under Bill of Entry Nos. C-1500-06 and 1499-06 both dated 13-7-2006 fixing the normal value under the provision of the Customs Valuation Rules, 2000 and shall return back the bank guarantee if the amount (if any) that becomes due after such final assessment is paid in cash within 120 (one hundred twenty) day from the date of receipt of the copy of this judgment and order, positively.

Communicate the copy of the judgment and order to the concerned respondents forthwith.

End.

full_judgment:
In this revision Rule was issued calling upon the opposite party Nos. 1 and 2 to show cause as to why the impugned judgment and decree dated 27-11-2000 passed by the learned District Judge, Shariatpur, in Title Appeal No. 06 of 1998 allowing the appeal and thereby reversing the judgment and decree dated 17-11-1997 passed by the learned Subordinate Judge, 2nd Court, Shariatpur, in Title Suit No. 02 of 1996 decreeing the suit in part should not be set aside and/or pass such other or further order or orders as to this Court may seem fit and proper.

2. Facts relevant for disposal of this Rule, in short, are that the petitioner, as plaintiff, instituted Title Suit No. 2 of 1996 in the Court of learned Subordinate Judge (now Joint District Judge), 2nd Court, Shariatpur, against the opposite parties, as defendant, for declaration of title and partition praying separate saham stating inter alia, that CS khatian No. 61 measuring 3.7 acres of land stand recorded in the name of Sabdar Sarder, Aminnesa, Emannesa and Khatunnesa out of which, they settled 0.51 acres of land from plot No. 144 to one Mubiullah as mentioned in the remark Column of relevant khatian. Sabder Sarder got 1.20 acres of land in the said CS khatian against his six annas share who died leaving wife Asha Bibi, son, the plaintiff and a daughter, Moyna. Subsequently, Moyna died leaving daughter Fatema and her husband Nayan Sikder along with the plaintiff and his mother Asha Bibi. Aminnesa died leaving Emannesa and Sabder Sarder, a sister's son by Mominnesa. In this way, Emannesa got 1.20 acres of land and Sabder Sarder inherited 1.13 acres of land. RS khatian No. 202 and 3 SA khatians for the land under Mouza Nagerpara stand recorded in their names wrongly giving share partially. CS khatian No. 9 containing 3.30 acres of land under mouza Pashimerchar belonged to Sabder Sarder and Emannesa. CS khatian stand recorded in their names and they settled 0.74 acres of land in plot No. 68 with Muhibullah as appearing from remark column in the said CS khatian. Sabder Sarder possessed 1.29 acres of land under plot Nos. 150, 17 and Emannesa possessed 1.29 acres of land under plot No. 150, 17 and Emannesa possessed 1.25 acres of land of Plot No. 16 and 18. Sabder Sarder inherited 0.78 acres of land in 2nd schedule from his father and sister Moyna Bibi, but Emannesa gifted 1.20 acres of land under schedule-1, 0.621/2 acres of land under schedule-2 and 0.74 acres of land under schedule-3 in favour of Surjaban Bibi a daughter of Aytunnesa.

3. The plaintiff got 0.621/2 acres of land from Emannesa through his father and in this way he got 1.401/2 acres of land in 2nd schedule. 3.39 acres of land under mouza Vadra Chap belonged to Sabder Sarder in 6 annas share, Aminnesa in 6 annas share and Emannesa in 4 annas share as recorded in CS khatian. They settled 0.94 acres of land from plot No. 159 with one Jabber Ali Sikder, Sabder. Sarder possessed 1.40 acres of land of plot No. 149 and 0.5½ acres of land of plot No. 201 and he inherited 0.88 acres of land from his father and sister. Emennesa gifted 0.27 acres of land out of 0.54 acres under plot No. 150 and 0.47 acres of land under plot No. 169 in favour of Surjaban. Aminnesa died leaving behind a sister Emannesa and Sabder Sarder, son of Mominnesa. RS and SA record partially recorded in the name of Asha Bibi wrongly, who transferred .58 acres of land to one Abdul Haq and Abdul Jalil by a registered deed dated 5-8-1964. Subsequently, said Abdul Haq and Abdul Jalil executed a deed of relinquishment in favour of plaintiff on 24-2-1965.

4. In the manner aforesaid the plaintiff in total got 4.74 acres of land in the suit Joma by way of inheritance, and inter-transfer and has been possessing the suit land with the defendants in ejmali. The suit property never partitioned among the co-sharers by metes and bound for which the plaintiff demanded partition of the same for convenience of their possession as well as development of the property. But the defendants refused the proposal on the plea that the property was partitioned between Sabder Sarder and Emannesa by a registered deed of partition of the year 1926 which, in fact, has not been acted upon at any point of time, hence the present suit.

5. The defendant Nos. 1 and 2 contested the suit by filing written statement denying all the material allegations made in the plaint contending inter alia, that the plaintiff has no cause of action; the suit is barred by defect of parties stating that 3.19 acres of land under CS khatian No. 9 and 3.39 acres of land under CS khatian No. 76 originally belonged to Sabder Sarder, Emannesa and Aminnesa and after death of Aminnesa, Sabder Sarder and Emannesa became the owner of the property. The said owners by a registered partition deed of the year 1926 got the property partitioned between them and by the said partition deed Sabder Sarder got in total 6.32 acres under 6 khatians and Emannesa got 5.53 acres of land under 5 khatians. Emannesa by a deed of gift No. 2079 dated 29-11-1933 gifted her entire property to her granddaughter (daughter's daughter) namely Surjaban and handed over the possession of the property as per deed of partition. RS and SA record stand recorded in the names of Surjaban, her legal heirs and in the name of other transferee.

6. Thereafter, Surjaban gifted 5.84½ acres of land to her sons, the defendant Nos. 1 and 2 and thereafter died leaving aforesaid two sons, defendant Nos. 1 and 2, husband, Akkel Ali and daughter, Wasera Bibi who have been enjoying the property by way of gift and inheritance by raising dwelling houses and cultivating nal land. The plaintiff earlier filed a Title Suit No. 23 of 1969 for declaration of his title over 0.34 acres of land under mouza Paschimer Char which was dismissed on contest. Against the said decree the plaintiff preferred Title Appeal No. 134 of 1970 which was also disallowed on contest. Resultantly, the plaintiff lost his right, title and interest in the said quantum of land. The defendants have been possessing the land got from Emannesa by gift and inheritance. One of the CS owner Aminnesa died leaving behind one son Sabdar Sarder who died leaving the plaintiff and the plaintiff and defendants have been possessing the suit jama by metes and bounds after CS operation. The suit is misconceived one and not maintainable in law.

7. The defendant Nos. 4-7, 11, 13, 16-20, 22-24, 26, 28, 31, 37-39, 41-46, 48-50 contested the suit by filing separate written statement stating that the predecessor of the defendants purchased 0.65 acres of land from Nayan Sikder by registered kabala and also got 0.14 acres of land of CS plot No. 15 from the plaintiff by way of exchange and these defendants have been enjoying and possessing the same raising dwelling houses and cultivating the nal land. Said Nayan Sikder inherited the said land from his wife Moyna Baru who died leaving behind him as husband, son Kashem and daughter Fatema. Kashem died leaving his father Nayan Sikder and sister Fatima. RS and SA khatian stand recorded in their names. Accordingly, 0.79 acres of land separately recorded in SA khatian No. 181. RS khatian No. 202 in the name of these defendants. Therefore, the property in question by a deed of partition of the year 1926 and subsequently, by separate record of right stood partitioned among the co-sharers. As such, the present suit for declaration of title as well as partition is not maintainable in law.

8. The trial court framed as many as 7 issues for determination of the dispute. In course of hearing the plaintiff examined four witnesses as PWs and the defendant examined five witnesses as DWs. Both the parties submitted certain documents in support of their claim which were duly marked as exhibits. The trial court upon hearing and considering evidences on record decreed the suit in part declaring title of the plaintiff over 3.35 acres of land under CS khatian No. 61, 9 and 76, but refused to give a decree for partition by its judgment and decree dated 17-11-1997.

9. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the judgment and decree of the trial court, the defendants in suit preferred Title Appeal No.6 of 1998 and the defendant No. 5 filed cross appeal before the District Judge, Shariatpur. The appellate court upon hearing allowed the appeal and dismissed the suit by reversing the judgment and decree of the trial court. At this juncture, the plaintiff-respondent-petitioners moved this Court by filing this revisional application under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure and obtained the present Rule.

10. Mr. Golam Ahmed, learned Advocate appearing for the petitioners submits that the trial court upon consideration of the evidences both oral and documentary found title of the plaintiff in respect of 3.35 acres of land in three schedule to the plaint, and observed that, the plaintiff may institute a suit for partition bringing all the properties owned by the plaintiff into hotchpotch. But the appellate court while allowing the appeal and reversing the judgment and decree of the trial court wrongly found that the plaintiff is entitled to get only 2.90 acres of land instead of 3.35 acres and dismissed the suit on the ground that, the property in question was earlier partitioned between the parties by a registered deed of partition of the year 1926 and the plaintiff may institute a suit for partition of the property got by his predecessor Sabdar Sarder by way of partition vide partition deed of the year 1926. He cannot claim any saham against the present defendants who got the property from 2nd party to the deed of partition.

11. He further submits that the appellate court wrongly observed and found that by the partition deed of the year 1926, the predecessor of the plaintiff Sabdar Sarder, got only 5.53 acres of land instead of 6.32 acres and Emannesa got 6.32 acres of land instead of 5.53 acres and also observed beyond record that the property was partitioned between the parties considering value of the same. It is also argued that there has been a registered deed of partition of the year 1926 showing partition of the property between Sabdar Sarder and Aminnnesa, but the said partition never been acted upon and on the basis of said deed, parties to the proceeding did not possess the property till filing of the suit, rather all the co-sharers have been possessing the suit property in ejmali. Therefore, in the absence of actual and physical partition of the property merely on the basis of a deed of the year 1926, it cannot be said that the property was partitioned by metes and bound and have been possessing separately pursuant to partition held in the year 1926. He further submits that the trial court though refused to give partition, but decreed the suit in part declaring title of the plaintiff in 3.35 acres of land holding that he has been possessing the same in ejmali and his possession and ownership are joint with other co-sharers. As such, without partition a suit for mere declaration declaring share of a co-sharer in ejmali can be passed in law. In support of his such contention he has referred to the case of Shankar Chandra Das vs Kalachand Das, reported in 46 DLR 419. It is also argued that without bringing all the properties into hotchpotch the plaintiff can file a suit seeking partition for some specific property, and it is not incumbent upon the plaintiff to bring all the property into hotchpotch. In support of his such contention he has referred to the cases of Muhammad Latif vs Muhammad Hafiz, reported in 6 DLR (PC) 111 and Rabija Khatun vs Badsha Meah, reported in 15 BLD 325.

12. He finally submits that the trial court rightly decreed the suit in part declaring title of the plaintiff in the property in ejmali, but the appellate court upon misconception of law, as well as misreading of the evidences on record in one hand reduced the share of the plaintiff, and on the other hand set aside the judgment of the trial court. Referring to the relevant khatian for the property, he submits that the record of right establishes that the said deed of partition of the year 1926 has not been acted upon and the khatian also not prepared in line with the said deed of partition. As such, the trial court righty held that the partition deed of the year 1926 never saw the daylight and acted upon at any point of time. Therefore, the suit for declaration of title and the partition is well maintainable in its present form.

13. Mr. Sikder Mahmudur Razi with Mr. Mohammad Saiful Islam, learned Advocates appearing for the opposite party Nos. 1 and 2 submit that the present suit in respect of declaration of title is not maintainable for the reason that all the common land has not been brought in hotchpotch, and the property in question already partitioned among the co-sharers in the year 1926 by a registered deed of partition. He further submits that the trial court wrongly decreed the suit in part declaring title of the plaintiff in 3.35 acres of land without specification. He further argued that the court cannot declare title of the plaintiff in the suit property independent of subsequent relief of partition. As such, the suit is barred by section 42 of the Specific Relief Act. He further submits that to give a declaration of title over any property the suit land must be specified, but in the present suit, the suit land is not specified by any boundary. In support of his such submissions he has referred to the case of Noor Mohammad Khan vs Government of the People's Republic of Bangladesh, reported in 42 DLR 434.

14. It is also argued that the suit property covered by CS khatian Nos. 61, 9 and 76 along with other property were partitioned between the predecessor of the plaintiff and defendants i.e. Sabdar Sarder and Emannesa Bibi by a registered partition deed dated 22-11-1926 (exhibit-C). By the said deed entire property belonged to Sabdar Sarder and Emannesa were partitioned by metes and bounds and subsequently, SA khatian also stand recorded separately in the names of the plaintiff and the defendants predecessor in respect of land of Nagerpara and Paschimar char mouza, although the SA khatian in respect of Vadra-chap mouza was published jointly. But in the said khatian, share of the parties has been clearly written mentioning specific possession of the parties in the remark column against the plot. As such, not only by deed of partition, but also from record of right it is amply established that the property was partitioned among the owners of the property and for such partition co-sharership of the parties has put an end for all practical purpose irrespective of separation of joma. In support of his such contention he has referred to the case of Aktaruzzaman Shaheen vs Abdur Rashid Khan, reported in 62 DLR (AD) 250.

15. He further submits that the suit is bad for defect of parties as the plaintiff did not implead the heirs of Khatunnesa Bibi who was RS and S.A. recordee and also did not implead Abdul Haque Howlader and Abdul Jalil Howlader who are also owners of some property alleged to have been relinquished the same of in favour of plaintiff by a "nadabi patra". In the absence of aforesaid owners of the property the suit itself suffers from defect of parties. In support of his such contention he has referred to the cases of Jahangir Alam (Md) vs Shabdir Ahmed, reported in 22 BLC (AD) 75 and Mobinnessa vs Khalilur Rahman, reported in 37 DLR (AD) 216.

16. It is also argued that the plaintiff claimed title in the property, claiming to be a heirs of Aminnesa as son of Sabder Sarder brother of the deceased. But according to Muslim Law of Inheritance brother's son does not inherit any property in the presence of full sister. As such, on the death of Aminnesa, Emannesa as full sister got her share as reflected in the partition deed of the year 1926, as such, the appellate court rightly observed and held that the plaintiff is entitled to get 2.90 acres of land under three khatians and he may file a properly constituted partition suit against the persons who inherited the property from Sabdar Sarder or acquired the property by purchase from the heirs of Sabdar Sarder, but they cannot claim the property got by Emannesa by the partition deed and seek any relief against the subsequent owners of the property through Emannesa.

17. Heard the learned Advocates for the parties, have gone through the revisional application, plaint, written statement, evidences both oral and documentary available in the lower court records and judgment and decree of both the courts below.

18. Admittedly the property in question along with other non-suited property originally belonged to Momennesa, Aminnesa, Emannesa and Khatunnesa, Momennesa died leaving Sabdar Sarder. Thereafter, Aminnesa died leaving Emannesa to inherit her property. The plaintiffs in suit claimed that on the death of Aminnesa his father Sabdar Sarder being sister's son (nephew) got eight annas share from Aminnesa. But as per Muslim Law of Inheritance a sister's son is excluded from inheriting any property in the presence of full sister. As such, predecessor of the plaintiff, Sabdar Sarder was not entitled to get any property from his aunt Aminnesa and the property as per law of inheritance devolved upon Emannesa a full sister of Aminnesa.

19. As stated by both the parties that there has been a deed of partition dated 22-11-1926 (exhibit-C). Recital of the partition deed clearly described that on the death of Aminnesa, Emannesa, 2nd part of the deed got entire property left by her sister and admitting the position as stated in the deed of partition both Sabdar Sarder and Emannesa executed and registered the same partitioning all their properties with specification and following the said deed Emannesa subsequently, by a registered deed of gift No. 2079 dated 29-11-1933 gifted her entire property to her granddaughter Surjabannesa. Subsequent to the said transfer, relevant khatians also stand recorded separately in the name of Surjaban except the property under mouza Vadrachap. The plaintiff though claimed that the said partition deed has not been acted upon, but failed to substantiate such claim by any evidence either oral or documentary and, as such, on the basis of a statement made in the plaint and made on oath, a registered deed of the year 1926 cannot be construed as not acted upon in the absence of any contrary evidence from plaintiff side. If we consider the existence and validity of the partition deed executed and registered in between Sabdar Sarder and Emannesa, in that case, it can be easily construed that the suit property was amicably partitioned between the co-sharers and by the partition deed co-sharership between the parties has come to an end, therefore, a suit for partition of the property making the persons as principal defendants who are claiming title through Emannesa is not at all maintainable in law.

20. From perusal of partition deed (exhibit-C), this Court finds that the property was partitioned giving specification of each plot and as per said partition Sabdar Sarder possessed and enjoyed the property until his death and thereafter, the plaintiff along with other co-sharer of the suit property and they also made inter transfer of the property left by Sabdar Sarder, not left by Emannesa. As such, had there been any cause of action for partition of the property, the plaintiff may institute a properly constituted partition suit against the persons who claims title through Sabdar Sarder bringing all the property left by him into hotchpotch and also making all the co-sharers through Sabdar Sarder as principal defendants and the persons whose names appearing in the khatian jointly as proforma defendants in the suit. But in the instance suit the plaintiff though claimed that the partition deed of the year 1926 has not been acted upon, but no relief has been sought for, against the said deed either by way of declaration or by any prayer for cancellation of the same. In the presence of a partition deed of the year 1926 executed and registered in between the predecessor of the plaintiff and the defendants the property fell in the share of Emannnessa, and thereafter, owned by the defendants cannot be subject matter for partition which were already partitioned in between the co-sharers in the year 1926.

<u>21. I have gone through the plaint in suit. It appears that the property claimed by the plaintiff as described in the schedule to the plaint are unspecified. Where the trial court refused the prayer for partition of the property it cannot decree the suit in part declaring title of the plaintiff in respect of unspecified property and also declare title in excess to the entitlement of the plaintiff, though the trial court rightly observed that the decree of partition cannot be given to the plaintiff as all the property has not been brought into hotchpotch, and the concern parties have not been made parties in suit.</u>

22. From perusal of the judgment and decree of the appellate court, this Court finds that the appellate court though wrongly described the quantum of land owned by the parties to the partition deed of the year 1926. But rightly observed that where the property in question earlier partitioned in between the predecessors of the plaintiff and defendants, there is no earthly reason for the plaintiff to bring subsequent suit for partition seeking relief against the heirs of Emannesa who was 2nd party to the deed, but the plaintiff can institute as suit for partition against the persons who claim title through Sabdar Sarder, first part of the partition deed dated 22-11-1926.

23. I have gone through the decisions referred by both the parties and found that the facts of those cases referred by the learned counsel for the petitioners are different from the present case.

24. In the circumstances, this Court finds that the appellate court rightly observed that the present suit for partition filed by the plaintiff petitioner without bringing all the properties got by Sabder Sarder into hotch-potch and making all the parties as defendant, the present suit is not maintainable in law. The plaintiff may file a partition suit in the light of the observations made hereinabove, if so advised.

25. In view of the above, this Court finds no error in the judgment passed by the appellate court except a description made regarding quantum of land partitioned between the parties to the deed of the year 1926, calling any interference by this Court.

26. Taking into consideration the above, this Court finds no error in the judgment of the appellate court and no substance in the Rule issued.

27. In the result, the Rule is discharged, however, without any order as to costs.

Communicate a copy of this judgment to the court concerned and send down the lower court records at once.

End.

case_source: (From the common Judgment and Order dated 24th August, 2015 passed by the High Court Division in FA No.167 of 2010 and TA Nos.7-11 of 2014.)
full_judgment:
Zinat Ara J : Civil Appeal Nos.30-32 of 2017 and Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 4232 of 2018 have arisen out of the common judgment and decree/Order dated 24th August, 2015 passed by the High Court Division in First Appeal No.167 of 2010, heard analogously with Transfer Appeal Nos.7, 8, 9, 10 & 11 of 2014 disallowing First Appeal No. 167 of 2010, Transfer Appeal Nos.7 of 2014, 09 of 2014, 10 of 2014 and 11 of 2014 and thereby, affirming the judgment and decree dated 18-8-2009 of the 1st Court of Subordinate Judge, Dhaka (shortly, the trial court) in Title Suit Nos. 483 of 1974, 112 of 1984, 113 of 1984 and 66 of 1990 dismissing the aforesaid suits but allowing Transfer Appeal No.08 of 2014 and decreeing Title Suit No.224 of 1997, thereby reversing the judgment and decree dated 18-8-2009 of the 1st Court of Joint District Judge, Dhaka in Title Suit No.224 of 1997. 2. The aforesaid Civil Appeals and Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal have arisen out of the common judgment and decree of the High Court Division in First Appeal (FA) No.167 of 2010 with Transfer Appeal (TA) Nos.7, 8, 9, 10 and 11 of 2014 and the aforesaid first and transfer appeals arose out of the common judgment and decree dated 18-8-2009 of the trial court in the above mentioned suits and the parties are all claiming the same property in the aforesaid appeals/suits and the present civil appeals and the civil petition. Therefore, the Civil Appeal Nos.30- 32 of 2017 and Civil Petition No.4232 of 2018 have been heard together and are being disposed of by this common judgment. Jamila Khatun's case in Title Suit (TS) Nos.483 of 1974 as Plaintiff and as defendants of other suits 3. Plaintiff-appellant-Jamila Khatun (briefly, Jamila) on 27-9-1974 filed Title Suit No.483 of 1974 in the 1st Court of Subordinate Judge, Dhaka (the trial court) against Raisa Aziz Begum (shortly, Raisa) and others for specific performance of contract and also for some other reliefs stating, inter alia, that Raisa, defendant No.1 of the suit had entered into an agreement with plaintiff-Jamila on 20-1-1972 to transfer 29.36 decimals of land with buildings, structures and shop rooms standing thereon of Holding No.10, Purana Paltan, Dhaka, present Plot No.1184, Khatian No.217 of Mouza-Ramna being old Dag Nos.26, 27 and 28, Ward No.3, Sheet No.22 of Mouza-Sahar Dhaka, (hereinafter referred to as the suit property). The price of the suit property was fixed at Rs.1,10,000 and Raisa received a sum of Rs 3,000 as earnest money on the terms and conditions that Raisa would obtain necessary clearance certificates and complete all other formalities within six months and intimate the same to Jamila and Jamila, within three months of such intimation would pay the balance consideration amount of Rs.1,07,000 to Raisa and then Raisa would execute and register a sale deed in favour of Jamila. Subsequently, Raisa received Taka 92,000 from Jamila on different occasions between 15-3-1972 to 19-8-1974 and Raisa admitted/acknowledged about receiving of the said amount through some money receipts. Thus, Taka 15,000 remained outstanding out of the total consideration money. Raisa did not execute the sale deed on receiving the balance amount. Therefore, Jamila filed TS No.483 of 1974. Initial result of the Suit & subsequent events, etc. 4. The suit was decreed ex-parte on 18-7-1978 against Raisa. So, plaintiff Jamila deposited the balance consideration of Taka 15,000 through Chalan No.561 dated 13-7-1978. Subsequently, Raisa filed Miscellaneous Case No.34 of 1979 to set-aside the ex-parte judgment and decree. Whereupon, the learned judge of the trial court by order dated 24-3-1980 allowed the said miscellaneous case, set aside the ex-parte judgment and decree and restored the suit to its original file and number. 5. Jamila thereafter amended the plaint of the suit alleging that after filing of the suit by Jamila, defendant Nos.3-7 knowing fully well about the agreement between Raisa and Jamila created some forged and fraudulent documents including sale deed and they were engaged in a conspiracy to deprive Jamila from the suit property. Jamila Khatun's Case in TS No.66 of 1990 as plaintiff and as defendants of other suits 6. Plaintiff-Jamila of TS No.483 of 1974 filed another suit being TS No.66 of 1990 for cancellation of sale deed as well as lease deed in favour of Khadiza Islam (briefly stated as Khadiza), contending, inter alia, that Raisa did not sale/transfer the suit property to Syed Badiur Rahman (briefly, Badiur) as claimed by him inasmuch as Badiur negotiated the Baina agreement dated 20-1-1972 between Jamila and Raisa and so, the alleged sale deed in favour of Badiur is forged. Khadiza purchased the suit property from Badiur knowing about her agreement for purchase the suit property from Raisa dated 20-1-1972 and also about the fact that the sale deed in favour of Badiur was/is forged. Khadiza created the sale deed in her favour knowing the aforesaid facts. Therefore, the deed of purchase as well as the deed of lease extension in her favour is liable to be cancelled. It was specifically alleged that there was no agreement of sale between Raisa and Badiur dated 11-9-1969 and that the alleged agreement of sale and registered deed dated 15-1-1982 are all forged and fraudulent documents without consideration. Badiur did not get any possession of the suit property through his forged deed of purchase at any time. Similarly, Khadiza did not get possession of the suit property at any time through her alleged deed of purchase. After knowing about the alleged forged deeds of Badiur and Khadiza, Jamila filed this subsequent suit for cancellation of the aforesaid deeds. Noor Mohammad Khan's(being dead his heirs) Case as plaintiff in Title Suit No.113 of 1984 (original Title Suit No.364 of 1982) and as defendants of other suits 7. Noor Mohammad Khan (Khan), defendant No.5 of Title Suit No.483 of 1974, as sole plaintiff, filed Title Suit No.364 of 1982 in the 3rd Court of Subordinate Judge, Dhaka against Raisa, Badiur, Jamila and some others for specific performance of contract against Raisa on the basis of an agreement for sale dated 23-7-1969 as well as an agreement dated 10-7-1977 renewing the previous agreement for sale and also for khas possession of the suit property contending, inter alia, that Raisa for raising cash money wanted to sell the suit property. Whereupon, Khan offered to purchase the same at Taka 45,000. Raisa accepted the said offer. Thereafter, on receipt of Taka 15,000 as earnest money she entered into an agreement for sale of the suit property with Khan on 23-7-1969. Raisa's cousin Badiur was a witness to the agreement for sale. It was decided that after procuring clearance certificate Raisa would execute and register the sale deed in favour of Khan but Raisa could not procure all necessary documents for registration of the deed and on her request Khan paid her Taka 5,000 on 23-10-1970 but due to political disturbance at the relevant period Khan could not obtain the deed of sale from Raisa. After liberation of Bangladesh, Khan traced out Raisa and Badiur in September, 1973 and came to know from Raisa that some miscreants took over possession of the suit property and that the suit property was enlisted as an abandoned property. Raisa disclosed that after release of the suit property, she would execute and register necessary deed of sale in favour of Khan. At her request, Khan paid further amount of Taka 3,000 in the 1st part of January, 1977. Raisa and Badiur demanded a further amount of Taka 50,000 to meet the expenses for release of the suit property from the list of abandoned property and to evict the unauthorized occupants therefrom. Considering all those aspects another instrument was executed between them on 21-1-1977 in the form of an agreement. This agreement provided that Mr Yakub Ali, the learned Advocate for Raisa would take steps to release the suit property and Khan would pay Taka 50,000 for this purpose. Accordingly, Khan paid Taka 20,000 and a cheque of Taka 30,000 to Raisa and the said instrument was kept in the custody of Mr Yakub Ali. Subsequently, Raisa and Badiur told Khan that Mr Yakub Ali, trapped them and if the transaction of cash as well as the encashment of cheque was made with the knowledge of Advocate Mr Yakub Ali, he would keep a major portion thereof. They requested Khan to stop payment of the cheque. Subsequently, on mutual understanding Raisa issued a notice rescinding the agreement dated 21-1-1977 through Mr Yakub Ali and then Raisa and Khan entered into a new agreement dated 1-5-1977 fixing the price of suit property at Taka 4,50,000 out of which Taka 1,35,500 was paid earlier according to the previous agreement and Taka 92,500 was paid on 1-5-1977. It was also decided that Khan would pay Taka 60,000 for release of the suit property. Then, Raisa disclosed that she would go to Pakistan to attend the marriage ceremony of her daughter and she appointed her brother as her attorney by an instrument dated 17-5-1977 to complete the transaction. Badiur showed a photocopy of the said power of attorney to Khan. On 11-7-1977 Khan departed for London after paying Taka 10,000 to Badiur on 10-7-1977 for release of the property. He returned to Bangladesh in the middle of 1979 and Badiur told him that they were processing the matter. Badiur also asked him to pay further amount as Raisa was badly in need of some money. So, he again paid Taka 1,80,000 in cash out of the balance consideration money as well as Taka 10,000 to Badiur for the purpose of release of the suit property and then left for London. He returned in November, 1980 and requested Badiur to complete the transaction and paid Taka 40,000 in cash and further amounts on different dates against written money receipt issued by Badiur on behalf of Raisa. The suit property was accordingly released from the list of abandoned property on 12-1-1982. Accordingly, Memo No.Sec. XVI/AP-28/77/20 dated 21-1-1982 was issued by the abandoned property authority releasing the suit property from the list of abandoned property. So, Khan came back to Dhaka on 18-1-1982 for getting the sale deed registered from Raisa. He paid Taka 40,000 on 25-1-1982 to Raisa but again Raisa informed him that she would go to Syedpur for seven days and asked him to get ready with necessary papers for obtaining income tax certificate. Accordingly, Khan procured necessary papers but Raisa did not return in time. Thereafter, she refused to execute and register the sale deed in his favour. Subse-quently, Badiur also disclosed that he purchased the suit property from Raisa and he would not transfer it to him, unless he pays an amount of Taka 25,00,000. Then, on search he found out that Badiur has created a forged sale deed on 15-1-1982 and has been claiming the suit property through it illegally. 8. Title Suit No.364 of 1982 was subse-quently, transferred to the trial court and renumbered as Title Suit No.113 of 1984. Khadiza Islam's case as plaintiff in Title Suit No.224 of 1997 (original Title Suit No.75 of 1996) and defendants of other suits 9. Khadiza, defendant No.7 of Title Suit No.483 of 1974, as sole plaintiff, filed Title Suit No.75 of 1996 in the 5th Court of Subordinate Judge, Dhaka on 27-4-1996 impleading Md Waziuddin, Jamila, Salauddin, Mobarak Hossain, Noor Mohammad Khan and Bangladesh as defendant Nos.1, 2, 3, 4, 5 and 6 respectively for cancellation of sale deed No.4722 dated 30-11-1982 obtained through Court by Md Waziuddin as well as for declaration of her right, title to and interest in the suit property and also for recovery of khan possession thereof by evicting Md Waziuddin therefrom and permanent injunction upon Md Waziuddin not to transfer the suit property to anyone stating that Raisa left the suit property under lock and key in the wake of liberation war of Bangladesh and in her absence, some miscreants took over possession thereof. The Government erroneously included the suit property in the list of abandoned property. However, on Raisa's application, the Government released the suit property on 12-1-1982 and handed over possession thereof to her. Then Raisa transferred the suit property to Badiur by a registered deed of sale dated 15-1-1982 in pursuance of an agreement dated 11-9-1969 and delivered possession to him. He got his name mutated and then with the permission of the Government sold it to Khadiza for a sum of Taka 10,00,000 by a registered deed of sale dated 4-9-1984. Badiur also delivered vacant possession of the suit property to her after execution of sale deed. She, after renewal of the lease deed from Government, had been in possession thereof till 5-5-1993, by using it as storage of construction materials of her construction company namely, Nirman Construction Company Limited (shortly, Nirman). Md Waziuddin (Waziuddin) disposses-sed her therefrom through Court on 5-5-1993 in Title Execution Case No.6 of 1992 arising out of the judgment and decree in First Appeal No.23 of 1984 arising out of Title Suit No.541 of 1982. Khadiza Islam was neither a party to Title Suit No.541 of 1982 nor in First Appeal No.23 of 1984 and she had no knowledge about the suit or appeal. Khadiza and the Managing Director of Nirman filed Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal (CPLA) No.195 of 1993 before the Appellate Division against the judgment and decree of First Appeal, but it was rejected as not being pressed. Thereafter, Khadiza filed the suit. In the plaint, it was further stated that according to the decree of First Appeal No.23 of 1984, Waziuddin was to deposit the balance consideration money within ninety days from the date of judgment and decree failing which the suit would stand dismissed. Waziuddin deposited the balance consideration money on 12-2-1992 by Challan No.24047, which was beyond the period of ninety days and, as such, the said suit stood dismissed but the execution case was filed on the basis of an inoperative decree and Khadiza was dispossessed from the suit property illegally. This suit on transferred to the trial court and was renumbered as Title Suit No.224 of 1997. Title Suit No.112 of 1984 Plaintiffs-Salau-ddin and Mobarak's case 10. Plaintiffs Salauddin and Mobarak also filed Title Suit No.436 of 1982 before the 3rd Court of Subordinate Judge, Dhaka for specific performance of contract against Raisa, relating to the suit property. The suit was transferred to the 1st Court of Subordinate Judge, Dhaka i.e. the trial court and renumbered as Title Suit No.112 of 1984. They claimed specific performance of contract relating the suit property on the basis of an agreement of sale dated 4-5-1979 with Raisa. Written statement case of defendant No.1 Md Waziuddin in Title Suit No.224 of 1997 11. It needs be mentioned that previously in the year 1997, one Waziuddin filed Title Suit No.541 of 1982 before the Subordinate Judge, Dhaka for specific performance of contract against Raisa on the basis of an oral agreement for sale of the suit property. The said suit was dismissed. Then Waziuddin filed First Appeal No.23 of 1984 before the High Court Division and the said appeal was allowed and the suit was decreed. 'Thereafter, Waziuddin got the sale deed registered through Court on 30-11-1992 and in execution of the said decree got possession of the suit property. Whereupon, Khadiza filed CPLA No.195 of 1993 before this Division against the said judgment and decree but it was dismissed as not pressed by Khadiza. Subsequently, Khadiza, as plaintiff, filed TS No. 224 of 1997 challenging the said judgment and decree of Waziuddin as discussed hereinbefore. Written statement case of Raisa (defendant No.1 in TS No. 483 of 1974) 12. Raisa filed written statement on 10-8-1976 denying all the allegations made in the plaint of Title Suit No.483 of 1974 and stating that she was not acquainted with Jamila and she did not enter into any agreement for sale with Jamila and that Jamila filed the suit with forged and created Bainapatra/agreement for sale and so, the suit is liable to be dismissed. However, Raisa eventually did not contest the suit. Written statement case of Syed Badiur Rahman (defendant No.6 in TS No.483 of 1974) 13. Defendant No.6 Badiur also filed a written statement and an additional written statement denying the plaint case and stating that Raisa left the suit property under lock and key in the wake of liberation war of Bangladesh and in her absence some miscreants took over possession thereof. The Government erroneously included the suit property in the list of abandoned property. However, on Raisa's application, the Government released the suit property on 12-1-1982 and handed over possession thereof to her. Then Raisa transferred the suit property to Badiur by a registered deed of sale dated 15-1-1982 in pursuance of an agreement dated 11-9-1969 and made over possession to him. He got his name mutated and then sold it to Khadiza for a sum of Taka 10,00,000 by a registered deed of sale dated 4-9-1984 and delivered possession to Khadiza. Written statement case of Defendant Government in the suits 14. The Government as defendant of Title Suit Nos. 483 of 1974, 112 of 1984, 113 of 1984, and 66 of 1990 contested the suits by filing separate written statements denying all material allegations made in the plaints of the aforesaid suits. However, the Government admitted part of plaint case of Title Suit No.224 of 1997 filed by Khadiza. In the written statements the Govern-ment stated, inter alia, that original owner and possessor of the suit property was Norendra Mohan Sen by virtue of a long term lease granted by the then Secretary of the State for India Council through registered deed dated 24-4-1924. While Remendra Sen was in physical possession of the suit property, he transferred his lease-hold interest to Aswimi Kumar Bhowmik, who subsequently transferred the same to Raisa by Deed No.8497 dated 11-12-1957. Raisa being a non-bengali Urdu speaking person abandoned the suit property during liberation war. She was not traceable after liberation. So, the suit property was legally declared as abandoned property and some persons including the plaintiffs of the suits were trying to grab the suit property by creating forged bainapatra, deeds, etc. 15. However, mysteriously the Government subsequently changed its stand, released the suit property from the list of abandoned property allegedly on an application filed by Raisa. There-after, Raisa allegedly transferred her lease-hold interest to Badiur by registered deed No. 1204 dated 15-1-1982. While Badiur had been exercising his right to and possession in the suit property as lessee under the Deputy Commissioner, Dhaka, he transferred his lease-hold interest of the suit property to Khadiza through deed No. 368 dated 4-9-1984. Khadiza got the lease renewed from the Government on 3-7-1985 in continuity for a further period of 30 years as provided under section 170 of the Government Estate Manual, 1958. The suit property is the Khas Mohal Property of the Government. The transferees acquire only lease hold interest in the suit property subject to the terms of the renewal deeds, both Badiur and Khadiza mutated their names in the record of right maintained by the Revenue Department and she has been possessing the suit property as a lessee under the Government. Khadiza became a recognized lessee under the Government through Misc. Case No. 48 of 1984. The suit property is being administered by the Dhaka Collectorate. The documents like bainapatra or otherwise must be false, fabricated and inoperative and are not binding upon the Government in anyway. The decree, if any, must have been obtained by practicing fraud. Issues, trial and decisions in Title Suit Nos. 483 of 1974, 112 of 1984, 113 of 1984, 66 of 1990 and 224 of 1997. Issues 16. এবং আবেদনকারিনী পাকিস্তানে যাওয়ার ইচ্ছা প্রকাশ করিয়াছেন কিনা এই মর্মে প্রতিবেদন দেওয়ার জন্য স্বরাষ্ট্র মন্ত্রণালয়কে অনুরোধ করা হয় । অত্র মন্ত্রণালয়ের বক্তব্যেও অনুসরণে জনাবা রাইসা আজিজ তাহার দাবীর স্বপক্ষে যেসব দলিলপত্র ও কাগজাদি পেশ করেন তাহা ৬৩-৮৭ পাতায় দেখা যাইতে পারে স্বরাষ্ট্র মন্ত্রণালয় কর্তৃক প্রদত্ত সনদ হইতে দেখা যায় যে তিনি পাকিস্তানে যাওয়ার ইচ্ছা প্রকাশ করেন নাই। জনাবা রাইসা আজিজ যে বরাবরই বাংলাদেশী নাগরিক সে মর্মেও স্বরাষ্ট্র মন্ত্রণালয় সনদপত্র জারী করিয়াছেন। অবস্থা দৃষ্টে প্রতীয়মান হয় যে রাইসা আজিজ বেগমই উক্ত বাড়ীর প্রকৃত মালিক । বর্তমানে যাহারা উক্ত বাড়ীতে বসবাস করিতেছেন তাহাদের বক্তব্যেও রাইসা আজিজকে মালিক বলিয়া উল্লেখ করিয়াছে। তবে ইতিপূর্বে বিষয়টি সম্পর্কে কোন সিদ্ধান্ত নেওয়া হয় নাই। নথি খানা লিগেল সেলে ছিল। ২৬। অনুচ্ছেদ ৭ হইতে প্রতীয়মান হয় উক্ত বাড়ী সংক্রান্ত আরো একটি ফাইল ছিল এবং টি এস কেস নং-৪৯৩/৭৪ এর প্রেক্ষিতে ১৯৭৬ সালে সরকারি উকিলের নিকট প্রেরণ করা হয়। এ বিষয়ে আমি ব্যক্তিগতভাবে সরকারি উকিলের সহিত যোগাযোগ করিয়াছি কিন্তু ফাইল উক্ত মামলা সম্পর্কে কোন পাত্তাই পাওয়া যায় নাই । ফাইলটি পাওয়া যাওয়ার পর কোন সন্তাবনা আছে বলিয়াও মনে হয় না। এ প্রসঙ্গে নোটের ১২ এবং ১৩ অনুচ্ছেদের প্রতি সদয় দৃষ্টি আকর্ষণ করা হইল। উক্ত মামলাটি কি সংক্রান্ত তাহা বুঝা যাইতেছে না। মামলার প্রকৃতি সম্পর্কে অবহিত হওয়ার পূর্বে মালিকানা দাবী সম্পর্কে কোন সিদ্ধান্ত নেওয়া সমীচীন হইবে বালয়া মনে হইতেছে না। বাড়ীর উপর মালিকানা দাবীদারকে মামলা সংক্রান্ত কোন কাগজপত্র থাকিলে তাহা পেশ করার জন্য বলা যাইতে পারে। Yes স্বাক্ষরঃ আজিজের অনুকূলে খারিজ করা হইয়াছে। বাড়ী বসবাস কারীগণের মধ্যে শুধুমাত্র শান্তিনগর ক্লাব ব্যতীত বাকী ৬জন বসবাসকারী মালিককে দখল বুঝাইয়া দিয়াছে বলিয়া জনাবা রাইসা আজিজ আবেদনে জানাইয়াছেন। (পত্রাংশ ১২৪ হইতে ১৫৬) শান্তিনগর ক্লাবের দখলীয় অংশ বুঝাইয়া দেওয়ার জন্য ২২-৫-৮২ তাং জনাবা রাইসা আজিজ আবেদন করিলে উপদেষ্টা মহোদয়“Can’t we help if she is stating the facts?" বলিয়া মন্তব্য করিয়াছেন। ৪৮। শান্তিনগর ক্লাব, উপদেষ্টা মহোদয়ের নিকট অস্থায়ীভাবে থাকার অনুমতি প্রার্থনা করিলে সমস্ত বিষয়টি লিখিতভাবে উপদেষ্টা মহোদয়ের দৃষ্টিগোচর করা হয় (পত্রাংশ ১৬০) শান্তিনগর ক্লাবকে ২৭-২-৭৬ তারিখে ইষ্টেট অফিস হইতে তাহাদের দখলীয় অংশ বরাদ্দ করা হয়। কিন্তু ভাড়া ধার্য্য কিংবা পরিশোধের কোন প্রমাণ নথিতে নাই। সরকারি বাসস্থান পরিদপ্তর হইতে কোন সময়ই তাহাদের নিকট হইতে ভাড়া আদায়ের কোন ব্যবস্থা গ্রহণ করে নাই । এক্ষনে শান্তিনগর ক্লাবের দখলীয় অংশের ভাড়া নির্ধারণ করিয়া উহা আদায়পূর্বক বাড়ীর মালিককে দখল বুঝাইয়া দেওয়ার জন্য ব্যবস্থা গ্রহণ করা যাইতে পারে। S/d. illegible 10-6-82 ৪৯। ৪৭-৪৮ অনুচ্ছেদ অফিস টৌকা দ্রষ্টব্য । শান্তিনগর ক্লাবকে ০৭ দিনের ভিতর দখল ছাড়িয়া দেওয়ার জন্য নোটিশ দেওয়া যাইতে পারে৷ এর ভিতর দখল না বুঝিয়ে দিলে উচ্ছেদ করা যাইতে পারে। অন্য কোথাও খালি জায়গা/বাড়ী থাকিলে শান্তিনগর ক্লাবের অনুকূলে বরাদ্দ বিবেচনা করা যাইতে পাবে। স্বাঃ দুষ্পাঠ্য ২-১১-১৯৮২ ৫৬। আলোচ্য পত্রাংশ দয়া করিয়া পত্র পাতা ১৬২ দেখা যাইতে পারে। ক্রীড়া ও সংস্কৃতি বিভাগ শান্তিনগর ক্লাবের আবেদনে শান্তিনগর ক্লাবের অনুকুলে বর্তমান ঘরটি পুনঃ বরাদ্দ অথবা অন্য একটি ঘর বরাদ্দের জন্য আন্তঃ মন্ত্রণালয়কে অনুরোধ করিয়াছেন। এই প্রসংগে উল্লেখ্য যে ১০নং পুরানা পল্টন বাড়ীটি বর্তমানে পরিত্যক্ত বাড়ী ঘর এর তালিকা হইতে ইহার মূল মালিক জনাবা রাইসা আজিজ বেগমকে দখল বুঝাইয়া দেওয়া হইয়াছে, শুধুমাত্র এঁতিহ্যবাহী শান্তিনগর ক্লাব তাহাদের দখল জনাবা রাইসা আজিজকে ছাড়িয়া দেন নাই। এমতাবস্থায় যখন ক্লাব বাড়ী ছাড়িতে প্রস্তুত, অতএব ক্লাবের জন্য ক্লাবকে তাহাদের নিজস্ব এলাকায় একটি পরিত্যক্ত বাড়ী খুঁজিয়া অত্র মন্ত্রণালয়কে জানাইতে বলা যাইতে পারে কেননা ক্লাব কি ধরণের বাড়ী চায় তাহাও তাহাদের জানান প্রয়োজন। স্বাঃ দুষ্পাঠ্য ২২-১১-১৯৮২ ৬০। পরবর্তীতে দেখা যাইতেছে যে উক্ত সম্পত্তি জনৈক সৈয়দ বদিউর রহমান দলিল নং ৩৬৮৬ তাং-৪-৯-৮৪ তারিখে জনাবা খাদিজা ইসলামের অনুকূলে বিক্রয় করেন (পৃঃ ১৬৬-১৭৭) এবং তদানুসারে উক্ত খাদিজা ইসলামের নামে নামজারী পরচা ও খাজনা প্রদান করা হইতেছে (পঃ পৃঃ ১৬৪-১৬৫)। কিন্তু ইহা অত্যন্ত সন্দেহ প্রবণ যে উক্ত সম্পত্তি রাইসা আজিজ বেগমের নিকট হইতে কিভাবে সৈয়দ বদিউর রহমানের নামে হস্তান্তরিত হয়েছে তাহার কোন প্রমাণ নাই। এছাড়া ক তালিকাভুক্ত বাড়ীর ব্যাপারে সঠিক সিদ্ধান্তের জন্য Court or Settlement এর নিকট প্রেরণ করা যাইতে পারে। স্বাঃ দুষ্পাঠ্য ২৪-৮-৮৬ 40.
