উন্নত পরিবেশগত ব্যবস্থাপনার লক্ষে এই এলাকার বিধিনিষেধ পরিবর্তন/পরিবধন করার ক্ষমতা পরিবেশ অধিদপ্তরের মহাপরিচালক সংরক্ষন করেন।

রাষ্টপতির আদেশক্রমে

সৈয়দ মার্গুব মোরশেদ

সচিব।

Subsequently, the notification dated 19.4.1999 was amended by another notification dated 3.5.1999 excluding certain areas from the earlier notification which is reproduced below:

পরিবেশ ও বন মন্ত্রনালয়

শাখা-৪

প্রজ্ঞাপনসমূহ

তারিখ, ২০শে বৈশাখ ১৪০৬/৩রা মে ১৯৯৯ ইং

পবম-৪৭/৮৭/৯৯/২৬৯- পরিবেশগত সংকটাপন্ন এলাকা সংকান্ত পরিবেশ ও বন মন্ত্রনালয়ের ১৯-৪-১৯৯৯ ইং তারিখের পবম-৪/৭/৮৭/৯৯/২৪৫ সংখক প্রজ্ঞাপনের আংশিক সংশোধনক্রমে বাগেরহাট খুলনা সাতক্ষীরা জেলার সুন্দরবন রির্জাভ ফরেষ্ট এলাকা এবং কক্সবাজার জেলার কক্সবাজার-টেকনাফ সমুদ্র সৈকত ও সোনাদিয়া দ্বীপ এর সংশ্লিষ্ট রির্জাভ ফরেষ্ট এলাকাসমূহ বর্লিত উল্লিথিত বিধি নিষেধের আওতা বর্হিভূত করা হলো। উক্ত প্রজ্ঞাপন উল্লেথিত অন্যান্য এলাকা সমুহ জারীকৃত প্রজ্ঘাপনের বিধি নিষেধ যথারীতি বহাল থাকবে।

রির্জাভ ফরেষ্ট এলাকা বন অধিদপ্তরের নিয়ন্তনাধীন হওয়ায় এবং বন ব্যবস্থাপনার জন্য সুনিদষ্টি আইন বিধি কও ব্যবস্থাপনা পরিকল্পনা থাকায় উল্লেখিত রির্জাভ ফরেষ্ট এর আওতাধীন এলাকায় যাবতীয় কার্যাবলি বন আইন বন্যপ্রানি সংরক্ষন আিইন এবং সরকার অনুমোদিত কাযকরী পরিকল্পনা অনুযায়ী সকল সম্পদ সংরক্ষণ ও ব্যবস্থাপনা করা হবে।

446. Mr. Mahbubey Alam, the learned Attorney General next submits that in order to protect the environment which is the crying need of the society, by the aforesaid legislation the government came up to solve the problem of environmental Pollution in as much as the problem of pollution is an out come of urbanization and Industrialization and submits that in the mean time the people of our country have witnessed with bitter experience that rivers of Dhaka such as Buriganga, Shitalakha, Bali and Turag etc have become severely polluted and to combat the pollution, the High Court Division of the Supreme Court in the meantime had issued rule which was made absolute with certain directions and held the Rule be treated as a continuing mandamus in order to save rivers.

<u>447. He next submits that before giving lease the government at the relevant time during 2001-2006 without taking into notice of the existence of Notification dated 19.4.1999 declaring the Cox's Bazar Sea Beach as Ecologically Critical Area under Section 5 of the Act, 1995 had leased out the land of the Beach having total disregard to the need of the people though the state is the Trustee of all natural resources which are by nature meant for public use and enjoyment. He further contends that public at large are the beneficiary of the sea, seashore, beach, running waters, airs, forests and ecologically fragile lands and that the state as a trustee is under a legal duty to protect the natural resources but the government had favored some fortunate gray hair persons in giving lease of the Beach which is in the heart of Cox's Bazar Beach disregarding the rights of the 14 crore people. He submits further that the rights of 14 crores people should prevail upon the alleged rights of the 59 lessees who have allegedly acquired right by lease.</u>

448. The learned Attorney General has urged fervently urged that the environment and the running waters do not have any Border and when Bangladesh faces catastrophe like Cyclone, and Flood and other natural disaster suffers along with other neighboring countries specially Myanmer, Chaina, Nepal, Bhutan and India so the ecology and ecological hazard touches the interest of Bangladesh along with the other neighboring countries and consequently, the world as a whole expresses concern. He submits any disturbance of the basic environment elements namely air , water and soil which are necessary for "life" would be hazardous to "life" within the meaning of Article 32 of the Constitution.

<u>449. He further submits that the government being the Executive wing of the State is also under an obligation to obey law, protect law and act in accordance with law made by the legislature and in no way the Government can violate the law and referring to the decision reported in Supreme Court Cases 2001, in the case of M.C. Mehata Vs. Kamal Nath. he submits that Indian Supreme Court taking into consideration of the case of different states of United States of America and also of their own cases, on the subject has adopted a legal theory known as "Doctrine of the Public Trust" that is the state is Trustee of all natural resources and being a Trustee is under a legal duty to protect the natural resources and draw our attention to paragraph No. 23, 24, 25, 33 and 34 and submits that the time has come that we should adopt the same Doctrine as a part of our jurisprudence, the crucial passage of the above mentioned paragraphs are reproduced below:-</u>

<u>"23. The notion that the public has a right to expect certain lands and natural areas to retain their natural characteristic is finding its way into the law of the land. The need to protect the environment and ecology has been summed up by David B. Hunter (university of Michigan) in an article titled An ecological perspective on property : A call for judicial protection of the public's interest in environmentally critical resources published in Harvard Environmental Law Review, Vol. 12 1988, p. 311 is in the following words:</u>

<u>"Another major ecological tenet is that the world is finite. The earth can support only so many people and only so much human activity before limits are reached . This lesson was driven home by the oil crisis of the 1970s as well as by the pesticide scare of the 1960s. The current deterioration of the ozone layer is another vivid example of the complex, unpredictable and potentially catastrophic effects posed by our disregard of the environmental limits to economic growth. the absolute finiteness of the environment, when coupled with human dependency on environment, leads to the unquestionable result that human activities will at some point be constrained. Human activity finds in the natural world its external limits. In short, the environment imposes constraints on our freedom these constraints are not the product of value choices but of the scientific impetrative of the environment's limitations. Reliance on improving technology can delay temporarily, but not forever, the inevitable constraints. Professor Barbara Ward has written of this ecological imperative in particularly vivid language. We can forget moral imperatives. But today the morals of respect and care and modesty come to us in a form we cannot evade. We cannot cheat on DNA. We cannot get round photosynthesis. We cannot say I am not going to give a damn about phytoplankton. All these tiny mechanisms provide the preconditions of our planetary life. To say we do not care is to say in the most literal sense that "we choose death." There is a commonly recognized link between laws and social values, but to ecologists a balance between laws and values is not alone sufficient to ensure a stable relationship between humans and their environment. Laws and values must also contend with the constraints imposed by the outside environment. Unfortunately, current legal doctrine rarely accounts for such constraints, and thus environmental stability is threatened. Historically, we have changed the environment to fit our conceptions of property. We have fenced, plowed and paved. The environment has proven malleable and to a large extent still is. But there is a limit to this malleability, and certain types of ecologically important resources for example, wetlands and riparian forests can no longer be destroyed without enormous long term effects on environmental and therefore social stability. To ecologists, the need for preserving sensitive resources social stability. To ecologists, the need for preserving sensitive resources does not reflect value choices but rather is the necessary result of objective observations of the laws of nature. In sum, ecologists view the environmental sciences as providing us with certain laws of nature. These laws, just like our own laws, restrict our freedom of conduct and choice. Unlike our laws, the laws of nature cannot be changed by legislative fiat; they are imposed on us by the natural world. An understanding of the laws of nature must therefore inform all of our social institutions."</u>

<u>24. The ancient Roman Empire developed a legal theory known as the "Doctrine of the Public Trust." It was founded on the ideas that certain common properties such as rivers, seashore, forests and the air were held by Government in trusteeship for the free and unimpeded use of the general public. Our contemporary concern about " the environment" bear a very close conceptual relationship to this legal doctrine. Under the Roman law these resources were either owned by no one (resnullious) or by every one in common (res communions). Under the English common law, however, the Sovereign could own these resources but the ownership was limited in nature, the Crown could not grant these properties to private owners if the effect was to interfere with the public interests in navigation or fishing. Resources that were suitable for these uses were deemed to b e held in trust by the Crown for the benefit of the public. Joseph L. Sax, Professor of Law, University of Michigan — proponent of the Modern Public Trust Doctrine —in an erudite article "</u>

<u>Public Trust Doctrine in Natural Resource Law: Effective Judicial Intervention", Michigan Law Review, Vol. 68, Part 1 p. 473, has given the historical background of the Public Trust Doctrine as under:</u>

<u>"The source of modern public trust law is found in a concept that received much attention in roman and English law- the nature of property rights in rivers, the sea, and the seashore. That history has been given considerable attention in the legal literature, need not be repeated in detail here. But two points should be emphasized. First, certain interests, such as navigation and fishing, were sought to be preserved for the benefit of the public; accordingly, property used for those purposes was distinguished from general public property which the sovereign could routinely grant to private owners. Second, while it was understood that in certain common properties- such as the seashore, highways, and running water- `perpetual use was dedicated to the public', it has never been clear whether the public had an enforceable right to prevent</u>

<u>infringement of those interests. Although the State apparently did protect public uses, no evidence is available that public rights could be legally asserted against a recalcitrant government."</u>

<u>25. The Public Trust Doctrine primarily rests on the principle that certain resources like air sea, waters and the forests have such a great importance to the people as a whole that it would be wholly unjustified to made them a subject of private ownership. The said resources being a gift of nature, they should be made freely available to everyone irrespective of the status in life, The doctrine enjoins upon the Government to protect the resources for the enjoyment of the general public rather than to permit their use for private ownership or commercial purposes. According to professor Sax the public Trust Doctrine imposes the following restrictions on governmental authority.</u>

<u>"Three types of restrictions on governmental authority are often thought to be imposed by the public trust: first , the property subject to the trust must not only be used for a public purpose, but it must be held available for use by the general public; second , the property may not be sold, even for a fair cash equivalent; and third the property must be maintained for particular types of uses.</u>

<u>33. It is no doubt correct that the public trust doctrine under the English common law extended only to certain traditional uses such as navigation, commerce and fishing. But the American Courts in recent cases have expanded the concept of the public trust doctrine. The observations of the Supreme Court of California in Mono Lake case clearly show the judicial concern in protecting all ecologically important lands, for example fresh water, wetlands or riparian forests. The observations of the Court in Mono Lake case to the effect that the protection of ecological values is among the purposes of public trust, may give rise to an argument that the ecology and the environment protection is a relevant factor to determine which lands, waters or airs are protected by the public trust doctrine. The Courts in United States are finally beginning to adopt this reasoning and are expanding the public trust to encompass new types of lands and waters. In Philips Petroleum Co. v. Mississippi the United States Supreme Court upheld Mississippi's extension of public trust doctrine to lands underlying non-navigable tidal areas. The majority judgment adopted ecological concepts to determine which lands can be considered tide lands. Philips Petroleum case assumes importance because the Supreme Court expanded the public trust doctrine to identify the tide lands not on commercial considerations but on ecological concepts. We see no reason why the public trust doctrine should not be expanded to include all ecosystems operating in our natural resource.</u>

<u>34. Our legal system-based on English common law- includes the public trust doctrine as part of its jurisprudence. The State is the trustee of all natural resources which are by nature meant for public use and enjoyment. Public at large is the beneficiary of the sea-shore, running waters, airs, forests and ecologically fragile lands. The state as a trustee is under a legal duty to protect the natural resources. These resources meant for public use cannot be converted into private ownership.</u>

450. The learned Attorney General finally, submits that the government admittedly granted lease of land to the petitioners and others on acceptance of some consideration and the government can not over look such aspect of the case and if the government in future give lease of land for Hotel and Motel and in that case the priority could be given to those persons and the petitioners also can reinvest to develop the tourism. He lastly, submits that Government is also not unmindful to the interest of the petitioners as they are citizens of the country.

451. He contends that if Bangladesh is desirous to invite the attention of the tourists to the soil of Cox's Bazar in that case the Cox's Bazar Beach should be kept free from any disturbance of the basic environment elements namely air, water and soil which are necessities for enjoyment of life and as such, the area cannot be degraded from present condition with some Bricks and sands which will definitely obstruct the free movement, free life and free air.

452. Mr. Rafique-ul Huq, in reply to the submission of the learned Attorney General contends that the assertion as to declaration of ecologically critical area of Cox's Bazar Sea Beach of the learned Attorney General is not correct in as much as the area "Wqc" of Cox's Bazar Sea Beach has already been excluded by Environment and Forest Ministry vide notification dated 3.5.1999 and drawn our attention to page No. 12 of Annexure-1 annexed to the affidavit-in-opposition filed by the respondent No. I (government) and further contends that it would be evident from the notification: কক্সবাজার জেলার কক্সবাজার in টেকনাফ সমুদ্র সৈকত” has been excluded from the Ecologically critical area and hence, the Cox's Bazar Beach was free from encumbrances and the government had legally allotted land to the petitioners.

453. Mr. Huq then contends that if this Court find that the Sea Beach of Cox's Bazar had not been excluded from the ecologically critical area to have been made by notification dated 19.4.1999 in that case also the lease cannot be cancelled in as much no one can take advantage of his own wrong.

454. He cites 2 decisions 1981 BLD(AD) 91 para 9 and 10 and 10 MLR(AD) 23 para 6, in support of his contention.

"9. The High Court Division accordingly allowed the aforesaid Miscellaneous Appeal on April 15, 1976. Being aggrieved, the appellants moved this court and obtained leave to appeal to consider only the last two among the three questions raised before the High Court. As the decisions by the the several benches of the High Court on the second question were found conflicting the issues involved therein required to be finally resolved by this Court. So far as the third question is concerned, the contention of the learned Counsel of the appellants was that the learned Judges were wrong in dismissing the application for pre-emption since they ignored the doctrine of his pendens."

"10. The first question mentioned above required no further consideration as the point involved therein was already settled by the aforesaid Full Bench decision."

"6. The main thrust of the submission of the learned Advocate-on-Record is that action in allowing extension by the Government of the period for payment of the installment by the writ petitioner was wrong. We are not oblivious of the legal maxim "Commondum Ex Injuria Sua Nemo Habera Debet" i.e. no person ought to have advantage from his own wrong. We are, therefore, of the view that even any wrong is committed no one can take advantage of his own wrong to the prejudice of other. In the instant case however we do not find that there was any wrong in allowing the prayer of the writ respondent extending the time of payment of salami in the facts and circumstances. We further find that the writ petitioner complying with the direction for making payment within six months from the date of service of the letter dated 23.03.1992 discharged the duties and as such she cannot be punished for the alleged wrong. if any, committed by the Government. We like to add in this connection that the actions of the State should generally be in favour of protecting the rights of the citizens and should not, in the state of affairs as in the instant case, be aimed at causing prejudice taking away such right. We are thus of the view that the High Court Division did not commit any error in making the rule absolute.

455. Mr. Huq further contends that the authority cited by the learned Attorney General is not applicable in the facts and circumstances of the present case in as much as in the said case the family of Kamal Nath (a former Minister for Environment and Forests, India) had direct link and had built a club at the bank of River Beas by encroaching land including substantial forests land. On the basis of the said case the Indian Supreme Court has developed a legal theory known as the "Doctrine of Public Trust" but in the instant case the petitioners have not encroached the Government land rather they have admittedly got lease of the land from the Government.

456. Mr. Mahbubey Alam contradicting the submissions of Mr. Huq the learned Senior Advocate for the petitioners submits that contents of the subsequent notification dated 3.5.1999 has to be read in its entirety in as much as he submits “কক্চবাজার জেলার ককবাজার টেকনাফ সমুদ্র সৈকত ও সোনাদিয়া দ্বীপ এর সংষ্লিষ্ট রিজার্ভ ফরেষ্ট এলাকাসমূহ বর্ণিত প্রজ্ঞাপন উল্লেথিত বিধি নিষেধের আওতা বহিভূত করা হলো। উক্ত প্রজ্ঞাপন উল্লিথিত অন্যান্য এলাকাসমুহ জারীকৃত প্রজ্ঞাপনের বিধি-নিষেধ যথারীতি বহাল থাকবে। and thereby it is clear that Cox's Bazar Sea Beach has not been excluded from the Ecologically critical area and also urged, the court to read the notification entirely in as much as he submits from paragraph 2 of the notification, it would be evident that the intention of the notification has clearly been expressed and if the entire notification is taken into consideration, it would be further evident that Cox's Bazar Sea Beach has not been excluded rather the reserve forest attached with Cox's Bazar Sea Beach has been excluded but not the Cox's Bazar Sea Beach and as such, the Sea Beach of Cox's Bazar has remained within the scope of Ecological critical area and thus, the government having violated the law at the relevant time had allotted the land to the lessees. He adds further that no body including the government can violate the law and again referring to the decision submits that the Indian Supreme Court having found that the Ilimachal Government had violated the law, Supreme Court of India itself quashed the lease agreement. He again submits that when anything is done violating the law in personal capacity or by the Government and in such case violation cannot be approved and again submits that the Rangs Building having been found constructed violating the law, the Appellate Division of the Supreme Court directed to demolish the same and under the direction of the Appellate Division of Supreme Court the said Rangs Buildings was demolished.

457. In order to appreciate issues before us, we have to look into the Bangladesh Environment Conservation Act, 1995 (Act No. 1 of 1995) and it is pertinent to mention the definition and the relevant section on the basis of which the Government declared the area Ecologically Critical Area. The definitions are quoted below for ready reference:

Definitions. –

"Conservation of environment" means improvement of the qualitative and quantitative characteristics of different components of environment as well as prevention of degradation of those components; [ Ref Clause (f).]

"Ecosystem" means the inter-dependent and balanced complex association of all components of the environment which can support and influence the conservation and growth of all living organisms; [ Ref: Clause (g).]

"Environment" means the inter-relationship existing between water, air, soil and physical property and their relationship with human beings, other animals , plants and micro-organisms; [ Ref: Clause (d).]

"Environment pollutant" means any solid, liquid or gaseous substance which causes harmful effect to the environment and also includes heat, sound and radiation; [ Ref: Clause (e).]

"Pollution" means the contamination or alteration of the physical, chemical or biological properties of air, water or soil, including change in their temperature, taste, odor, density, or any other characteristics, or such other activity which, by way of discharging any liquid, gaseous, solid, radioactive or other substances into air, water or soil or any component of the environment, destroys or causes injury or harm to public health or to domestic, commercial, industrial, agricultural, recreational or other useful activity, or which by such discharge destroys or causes injury or harm to air, water, soil, livestock, wild animal, bird, fish, plant or other forms of life; [ Ref: Clause (b).]

"5.Declaration of ecologically critical area.- ( I ) If the Government is satisfied that an area is in an environmentally critical situation or is threatened to be in such situation, the Government may , by notification in the official Gazette, declare such area as an ecologically

critical area.

(2) The Government shall, in the notification published under suhn-section (1 ) A vehicle emitting smoke or gas injurious to health or environment shall not be operated nor shall such vehicles be switched on except for the purpose of test-operation for stopping the emission of such smoke or gas."

458. We have examined the above notifications regarding the declaration of Ecologically Critical Area along with submissions of the learned Advocates for the petitioners and the learned Attorney General for respondent No.1 (Government).

<u>459. There is no dispute as to the declaration made by the lst notification dated 19.04.1999 . Mr. Rafiq-ul-Huq, the learned Advocate for the petitioner submitted that the Cox's Bazar Sea Beach had been excluded by the subsequent notification dated 03.05.1999 and the lease was granted free from all encumbrances and having taken into consideration such submission we have very meticulously examined the notification dated 03.05.1999 by which certain areas were excluded from the declaration and found that</u>

<u>“ককচবাজার জেলার ককচবাজার-টেকনাফ সমুদ্র সৈকত ও সোনাদিয়া দ্বীপ এর সংশ্লিষট বিজার্ভ ফরেষ্ট এলাকাসমীহ বণির্ত প্রজ্ঞাপন উল্লেথিত বিধি নিষেধর আওতা বহিরভূত করা হলো।” Thus this clearly means that রিজার্ভ ফরেষ্ট এলাকাসমূহ বর্লিত প্রজ্ঞাপন উল্লেথিত বিধি নিষেধের আওতা বহির্ভূত করা হলো।</u>

<u>This means "Reserved Forest Area" of the Cox's Bazar Sea Beach has been excluded from the Ecologically Critical Area but not the Cox's Bazar Sea Beach from the declaration of Ecologically Critical Area. We have no hesitation to accept the interpretation advanced by the learned Attorney General and in such circumstances, we hold that the lease was granted to the petitioners violating the declaration made by notification dated 19.4.1999. Therefore, we find no merit in the Rules.</u>

460. However, we direct as under:-

A. The Director General of Environment, Bangladesh is directed to appoint a Director having its office at Cox's Bazar to protect the area which have been declared Ecologically Critical Area relating to Cox's Bazar Sea Beach by notification dated 19.4.1999 and is further directed to demarcate the Ecologically Critical Area putting pillar within 6 months from date of receipt of the order.

B. The Director General is further directed to display Sign Boards depicting the area which have been declared by the aforementioned notification dated 19.4.1999 Ecologically Critical Area of the Cox's Bazar Sea Beach for public information and is tUrther directed to take appropriate step to maintain basic environment of the said declared area.

C. The Deputy Commissioner Cox's Bazar is directed to appoint a Commission consisting of not less than two Civil Engineers to ascertain the land to have been alloted to the petitioners along with the Construction cost to have been allegedly made in the land which have been leased out to the petitioners after receipt of the order.

D. The petitioners are directed to cooperate with the Commission in the process without creating hindrance and obstacle.

E. The respondent No. 1 is directed to return the consideration money to the lessee if they approach, the Secretary, Ministry of Land.

F. The respondent No. 1 is further directed to consider the application from the present lessees, if any allotment is given in future for construction of the Motel and Hotel in Cox's Bazar.

461. With the above directions and observations made hereinabove, the Rules are discharged without any order as to costs.

462. The orders of stay granted in all the writ petitions are thus vacated.

463. A copy of the judgment and order communicate to the Secretary Ministry of Land, Secretariat, Dhaka and Deputy Commissioner, Cox's Bazar at once.

Ms. Naima Haider, J:- I agree.

End.

Abdul Quiyum, Senior Advocate, instructed by Md. Sajjadul Haq, Advocate-on-Record. ------ For the Appellants 
A.J. Mohammad Ali, Senior Advocate instructed by Mvi. Md. Wahidullah, Advocate-on-Record. ------ For the Respondents

case_source: (From the judgment and order dated 11.04.1985 passed by the High Court Division in Second Appeal No. 375 of 1979.)
full_judgment:
Amirul Kabir Chowdhury J: This appeal by leave at the instance of the plaintiff is against the judgment and order dated 11.04.1985 passed by the High Court Division, Comilla Bench in Second Appeal No. 375 of 1979.

<u>2. Predecessor of the plaintiffs, late Moulvi Joynal Abedin purchased the suit land in revenue sale held on 11 July 1942. The judgment debtor namely, Haralal challenged the sale by filing Title Suit No. 48 of 1942 but lost it at all stages and finally in second appeal which was dismissed on 3 August 1948. Joynal Abedin mutated his name and paid rent all through till his death in 1960 and his name was recorded in the preliminary Record-of-rights. But after his death the heirs of his brother Dr. Abdul Halim in collusion with Revenue Officers got their names recorded in the finally published khatian in respect of 8 annas share of the suit land, putting up the claim that the revenue sale was benami transaction in that Dr. Abdul Halim younger brother of Joynal Abedin, had purchased 8 annas share in the land and that there was threat of dispossession of the plaintiffs from half of the land. Hence the plaintiffs filed Title Suit No. 502 of 1975.</u>

3. Defendant respondents contested the suit denying the allegations and claiming that Joynal Abedin admitted the joint purchase and relinquished his claim to the extent of 8 annas share by a registered Nadabipatra dated 21 June, 1945 in the basis of which the finally published khatian recorded their 8 annas inter-est. The suit was decreed by the trial court. Both the trial court and the lower appellate court concurrently found that the Nadabipatra was forged document, copy of which was produced for the first time after the death of Joynal Abedin, that the finally published khatian in favour of joint purchase got no basis and on those findings decreed the suit. In second appeal S.A. No. 375 of 1979 a learned Single Ridge of the High Court Division observed that the concurrent findings were not sustainable in law as the courts below wrongly shifted the onus of proof of the benami purchase and the Nadabipatra upon the defendants.

4. The learned Single Judge by the impugned judgment and order allowed the appeal setting aside the judgment and decree of the courts below and sent back the suit on remand to the trial court to adjudicate the matter afresh in the light of the observation made in the body of the judgment.

5. Hence is this appeal

6. Leave was granted to consider the submissions made on behalf of the appellants that the order of remand is improper in that concurrent findings of the trial court and the lower appellate court are based on evidence and that the onus to prove the benami purchase to the extent of 8 annas share of the suit land is upon the defendant and that presumption in favour of nadabipatra Ext.C has been rebutted by the plaintiffs and therefore there was no room of the High Court Division to send the suit on remand.

7. Mr. Abdul Quiyum, learned Counsel appearing on behalf of the appellants reiterated the aforesaid submissions made earlier.

8. He thereafter submits that on the basis of evidence both the courts below came to con-current conclusion that the nadabipatra produced on behalf of the defendant respondents was not a genuine document and without adverting to the materials on record the High Court Division passed the impugned judgment on remand. There being cogent evidence indicating that the nadabipatra was not a genuine document and there being concurrent conclusive finding to the effect by both the courts below the High Court Division committed error in sending the suit again on remand.

9. Mr. A. J. Mohammad Ali, learned Counsel opposes the appeal.

10. We have considered the submissions and perused the materials on record.

11. It appears that the High Court Division in consideration of the materials on record observed, inter-alia,

"Oral evidence with regard to possession, as have been claimed by both the parties in respect of the disputed land, seems to be very much balanced. The courts below could not find any direct contradiction among the witnesses of the defendants side, who were examined to prove their possession. But upon making certain aspersion on the character of the D.Ws. The courts below have believed the evidence of P.Ws. in arriving at a finding of possession. I have already mentioned that payment of rent for long time is also a piece of evidence regarding possession but the courts below without considering such evidence, specially exhibit-A series, have found possession in favour of the plaintiffs upon taking into consideration only the oral evidence of Borgaders notwithstanding the fact that P.W.2 Daiya Gazi appears to be a partisan witness as one of his son has purchased some land out of the disputed property from the plaintiffs.

12. As a matter of fact, the courts below have abruptly held that exhibit-C is a gorged document. Thus, in my opinion, non-consideration of exhibit-A series by the courts below has caused a serious error in the decision of the case merit and that the courts below have also committed an error in procedure by shifting the onus upon the defendants to prove that exhibit-C is a genuine document. I have already observed that the plaintiffs did not take any stop to prove their case that during his life time Joynal Abedin got his name mutated in the relevant register in pursuance of exhibit-1 and did not also produce any rent receipt in support thereto. In the interest of justice a chance should be given to the plaintiffs to prove their case by producing any evidence in support thereto if there be any."

<u>13. In view of above mentioned observation we are of the view that the High Court Division did not commit any error in sending the case on remand to adjudicate the matter afresh in accordance with law giving the parties opportunity to adduce further evidence in support of their respective claims in addition to the evidence already on record. The order does not put any bar upon the plaintiffs to adduce evidence to prove their claim.</u>

<u>14. We are at a loss to understand as to what prompted the plaintiffs to prefer this appeal.</u>

15. In view of the discussion made above we do not find any substance in this appeal.

16. The appeal is, therefore, dismissed.

17. Parties do bear their respective costs.

End.

parties:
Abdul Moin  ------ Petitioner
Vs.
Bangladesh represented by the Secretary, Ministry of Land, Secretariat Building & ors  ------ Respondents.
full_judgment:
Md Joynul Abedin J: This Rule was issued under Article 102 of the Constitution of the People's Republic of Bangladesh calling upon the respondents to show cause why the impugned order dated 3-6-1998 (Annexure-I) passed by the respondent No.3. Additional Deputy-Commissioner (Revenue), Sylhet and the proceeding of mutation Appeal No. 22 of 1994 should not be declared to have been made without lawful authority and to be of no legal effect:

2. It is stated in the writ petition that the petitioner's father acquired the property in question measuring 3.33 acres of land in Khatian No. 2 under Sylhet Municipality by purchase on 12th Chaitra, 1354 BS by a registered Kabala. But since the respondent No.4. Lacca Tura Tea Estate illegally took over possession and managed to record the same in its name in the record of rights, father of the petitioner filed Title Suit No. 371 of 1963 in the First Court of Sadar Munsif, Sylhet against the Ministry of Land and Lacca Tura Tea Estate and others for declaration of title and recovery of khas possession in respect of the said land along with other lands. The said suit was decreed in part declaring title only in favour of the father of the petitioner in respect of the second schedule land by judgment and decree dated 27-2-1973 against which the respondent Nos.l and 4, namely, the Ministry of Land and Lacca Tura Tea Estate, preferred Title Appeal No. 100 of 1973 in the Court of District Judge, Sylhet. Similarly, the father of the petitioner preferred cross appeal, Title Appeal No. 76 of 1973, as the trial Court failed to pass a decree for recovery of khas possession regarding the second schedule land and also for not making the commission Report, Map, etc part of the decree. Title Appeal No. 100 of 1973 filed by the respondent Nos. 1 and 4 was dismissed and Title Appeal No. 76 of 1973 was allowed by judgment and decree dated 8-9-1983. During pendency of the aforesaid appeal petitioner's father died and accordingly, his three brothers and mother impleaded themselves as appellants. Thereafter, the petitioner and his co-owners filed Title Execution Case No.5 of 1984 and ultimately, obtained possession of the land on 8-3-1984 through Court by executing the decree. After conclusion of the said execution case the mother of the petitioner died leaving behind the petitioner and his three brothers and of them, two died unmarried and the third died leaving behind one daughter and the said daughter transferred-her share in favour of the petitioner and delivered possession thereof. The petitioner thus became the sole owner in possession of the suit land. The heirs of the respondent No.4 in Title Appeal No. 76 of 1973 however, preferred two revisional applications being Civil Revision Nos.161 and 162 of 1984 before the High Court Division. Ultimately, the Rules in the aforesaid two revisional applications were discharged by the judgment and order dated 3-9-1987. The said heirs then filed two Civil Petitions for Leave to Appeal Nos. 245 and 246 of 1988 before the Appellate Division which were also dismissed by judgment and order dated 27-1-1991.

3. Accordingly, the petitioner filed Mutation Case No. 107/83-84 before the Revenue Deputy Collector Sylhet under section 54 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 for correction of record of rights in his favour in pursuance of the aforesaid judgment and decrees passed by the highest Court of the country. But the Revenue Deputy Collector stayed the matter. Hence the petitioner preferred Mutation Appeal No. 95 of 1990 before the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue), Sylhet, who heard and allowed the said appeal with direction to record the name of the petitioner. The petitioner thereafter filed Miscellaneous Case No. 26 of 1991 before the Assistant Commissioner (Land) Sadar, Sylhet for correction of the record of rights. The Assistant Commissioner (Land) thereafter by order dated 23-1-1994 approved mutation in favour of the petitioner and consequently, a separate khatian was opened in the name of the petitioner.

4. The respondent No. 4 Lacca Tura Tea Estate, thereupon, preferred Mutation Appeal No. 22 of 1994 before the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue), Sylhet against the order passed by the Assistant Commissioner (Land) asserting that the land in question was a vested property and, as such, it took settlement of the same from the Government and it was therefore rightly recorded in its name in the record of right. The petitioner having received notices of the said mutation appeal, contested the same submitting all papers, namely, the judgments and decrees passed by the Civil Courts including the Appellate Division of the Supreme Court declaring title of the petitioner thereto and giving possession. But the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue) by the impugned order dated 3-6-1998. Annexure-I, forwarded the case record to the Ministry of Land without giving any decision either allowing or rejecting the mutation. Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue) while forwarding the record to the Ministry observed the Lacca Tura Tea Estate was the owner and possessor of the land in question on the basis of settlement by the Government and there was no scope of mutation in favour of the petitioner. He also mentioned in the aforesaid order that there were two title suits pending in respect of the land in question by two other private individuals and without disposal of the said suits and without the results of the said suits being submitted to the Ministry there was no scope to pass any mutation order.

5. No affidavit-in-opposition has been filed on behalf of the respondent Nos.1, 2 and 3 i.e. the Government. An affidavit-in-opposition is, however, filed on behalf of respondent No.4, Lacca Tura Tea Estate, during the hearing stating, inter alia, that the land in question was leased out in its favour by the Government and the mutation in favour of the petitioner was rightly withheld.

6. We have heard Mr IN Deb, the learned Advocate for the petitioner in support of the Rule and Mr ABM Mustafa Kamal, the learned Advocate for the respondent No.4 and also heard Mr Abul Hossain Azadi, the learned Assistant Attorney-General opposing the Rule.

7. It is noted from the record that the petitioner in order to establish his right, title and interest in the land in question and for recovery of khas possession thereof filed a civil suit being Title Suit No. 371 of 1963 and obtained the decree in his favour which was finally affirmed by the Appellate Division of the Supreme Court. The dispute with regard to the title and possession of the land in question between the parties, namely, the Government of Bangladesh, Lacca Tura Tea Estate and the petitioner should therefore be taken to have been finally resolved. The petitioner therefore started a Mutation case under section 54 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 for mutation of his name by removing the name of the Government and/or Lacca Tura Tea Estate in the record of right on the basis of the aforesaid decrees. The petitioner eventually obtained necessary Mutation order on 23-1-199.4 in his favour by the Assistant Commissioner (Land) in Miscellaneous Case No. 26 of 1991 and in pursuance thereto a separate khatian was opened in his name. The respondent No.4 Lacca Tura Tea Estate thereupon filed a Mutation Appeal No. 22 of 1984 before the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue) whereupon the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue) dragged on with the matter for 4 years and then without deciding the matter himself forwarded the case record regarding the mutation to the Ministry of Land by the impugned order dated 3-6-1998 with the observation as stated above.

8. Since the petitioner sought correction of the record of right by mutating his name in respect of the land in question on the strength of the final judgment and decree of the highest Civil Courts of the country he rightly approached the Revenue Deputy Collector by filing an application under section 54 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. Section 54 reads as under:

"The Revenue-officer shall make such alteration in the records-of-rights or the Compensation Assessment Roll as may be necessary to give effect to any directions issued by the Commissioner or other officer under section 49 or an order made by a Special Judge under section 51 or section 53 or under sub-section" (4) of section 52 or to any final order or decree of a Civil Court of the High Court Division passed in any suit, appeal or proceeding declaring tide to and, or possession of any land."

<u>9. When the matter was subsequently brought before the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue) he was required in law to decide the matter either giving a decision instead of forwarding the same to the Ministry of Land by giving unwarranted and illegal observations. Since the question of title and possession have been settled by the highest Court of the country the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue) had, in fact, no option in law but to mutate the name of the petitioner by correcting the record of right: The Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue) not only acted without jurisdiction in sending the matter to the Ministry of Land without deciding the matter himself with untenable observations but also did so in colourable exercise of his official power. The impugned order dated 3-6-1998 passed by the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue) Sylhet is therefore declared to have been passed without any lawful authority.</u>

10. Since the impugned order dated 3-6-1998 by the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue) was without jurisdiction and an outcome of the colourable exercise of his official power the petitioner was competent to invoke writ jurisdiction under Article 102 of the Constitution instead of taking the matter to the Board of Land Administration in terms of section 146 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. Accordingly, the contention of the learned Advocate for the respondent No.4 that the petitioner was required to take the matter before the Board of Land Administration by filling a revision and the writ petition was not maintainable has no substance.

In the result, the Rule is made absolute without any order as to costs.

End.

parties:
Government of Bangladesh------Petitioner 
Vs
Md Saiful Islam------Respondents
case_source: (From the judgement and order dated 25th of April, 2012 passed by the High Court Division in Writ Petition No. 3562 of 2011)
full_judgment:
Md Imman Ali J: This civil appeal, by leave, is directed against the judgement and order dated 25-4-2012 passed by the High Court Division in Writ Petition No. 3562 of 2011 disposing of the rule Nisi.

2. The facts of the case, in short, are that a project namely "Development of Selected Colleges (Government and Non-Government) Project (2nd Revised)" (hereinafter "the Project") under the Ministry of Education was started in 1997 which was primarily targeted to be, completed in June, 2005. In the said project a total of 115 hostels were established, and to run the hostels, total 460 posts were created of which 115 posts for Head Cook, 115 for Assistant Cook, 115 for Night Guards and 115 posts for Sweeper. For appointment in those posts an employment notification was published in different newspapers. The present petitioners (who are 129 in number) and others filed applications. Accordingly examination was held for selection of suitable candidates. The writ-petitioners participated in the said examination and were selected. Their names were published in the daily newspapers. Getting appointment letters they joined in their respective posts in different districts. Writ-petitioner Nos. 1-36 joined as Head Cook, Writ-petitioner Nos. 37-68 joined as Assistant Cook, writ-petitioner Nos. 69-97 joined as Sweeper and writ-petitioner Nos. 98-129 joined as Night Guard. After expiry of the project period in June, 2005, the same was extended from time to time till June, 2008. The writ-petitioners and others got salary up to June, 2007. Though it was mentioned that the period of the project would expire in June, 2005, but there was a stipulation in the project proforma that after completion of the project those posts would be transferred to the revenue budget as per Government rules. Several letters were exchanged between the Ministries for taking step to transfer or absorb the service of the writ-petitioners in the revenue budget, but finally the same has not been done, although the writ-petitioners legitimately expected that their service might be transferred/ absorbed in the revenue budget. But the writ-respondents did not take any positive step to transfer/absorb the services of the writ-petitioners in the revenue budget. In such a situation the writ-petitioners issued notice demanding justice, but to no effect. Thereafter, the writ-petitioners moved the High Court Division and obtained the rule Nisi.

3. Writ-respondent Nos. 2 and 3 entered their appearance and contested the Rule by filing two sets of affidavits-in-opposition contending, inter alia, that the provisions made in the project proforma did not give any guarantee to transfer any post and manpower from development project to revenue setup. Transfers of posts from development budget to revenue setup are guided by specific rules and regulations. The Ministry of Establishment did not recommend 460 posts for transfer to the revenue setup. The decision of ECNEC was to transfer the post from project to revenue budget, but the incumbents were not recommended by the Ministry of Establishment because they did not satisfy the necessary rules and regulations. While recruiting the writ-petitioners it was made clear that their appointments would stand terminated at the end of the project. The appointees could not have any legitimate expectation that they would be included in the revenue budget. In such view of the matter the rule Nisi should be discharged.

4. By the impugned judgment and order, the High Court Division disposed of the Rule directing the respondents to consider the case of the writ-petitioners in the light of the decision of ECNEC dated 30-12-2007 and the provisions of SRO No. 182-Ain/2005/Shomo/Bidhi-1/S-9/2000 dated 20-6-2005. Hence, the writ respondents as petitioners filed Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 464 of 2013 and leave was grafted to consider the following submissions of the learned Deputy Attorney-General for the petitioners.

"I. That the project in which the writ petitioners were working was started after 30th June, 1987, and, therefore, the SRO No. 182 dated 20th June, 2005 has no manner of application for the regularisation of the petitioners in the revenue set up and thus, the High Court Division erred in law in directing the petitioners to consider their cases in the light of the said Rules.

II. That since the writ petitioners' project was started after 30th June, 1987, their case is covered by SRO No. 183- Ain/ 2005/Shomo/Bidhi-1/S-9/2000 dated 20th June, 2005, under which SRO, the writ petitioners cannot claim any right of absorption in the revenue setup. III. That in the absence of proper pleadings laying foundation in support of the claim of legitimate expectation, the High Court Division erred in law in holding that in view of the letter mentioned above, the writ petitioners can claim for regularisation on the doctrine of legitimate expectation."

5. Mr Ekramul Haque, learned Deputy Attorney General appearing on behalf of the appellants made submissions in line with the grounds upon which leave was granted. He further submitted that the High Court Division failed to appreciate that the SRO No. 182-Ain/2005/ Shomo/Bidhi-1/S-9/2000 dated 29-6-2005 is not applicable for the writ-petitioners, SRO No. 183 Am/2005/Shomo/Bidhi-1/S-9/2000 is applicable for them, but nowhere in SRO No. 183 or in the project proforma or in the appointment letters of the writ-petitioners, is there any express clear promise made that after completion of the project their service would be transferred to the revenue budget, as such, no legitimate expectation arises in respect of the petitioners for absorbing them in the revenue budget, hence, the High Court Division erred in law in making the direction and, as such, the appeal may kindly be allowed. He further submitted that the writ petitioners having not been assured or promised by any authority of the Government that their services would be regularised in the revenue budget after the expiry of the period of the project, the High Court Division erred in law in making the direction as such the impugned judgment is liable to be set aside and the appeal may kindly be allowed. He further submitted that the writ-petitioners being amenable to the jurisdiction of Administrative Tribunal, writ petition at their behest is not maintainable, hence, the High Court Division erred in law in entertaining the writ petition and making the direction sitting in special statutory jurisdiction under Article 102 of the Constitution of People's Republic of Bangladesh, as such the impugned judgment is liable to be set aside and the appeal may kindly be allowed.

6. Mr Masud Hossain Dolan, learned Advocate appearing for the respondent submitted that the Appellate Division has given eleven guidelines for absorption in the Revenue-setup in several other cases and the High Court Division in Writ Petition No. 4013 of 2012 directed the authority concerned to absorb 76 (seventy six) writ petitioners from the "Development of Selected College (Government and Non-Government) Project (2nd Revised) to revenue setup in accordance with the Appellate Division's guidelines and after scrutiny of the documents absorbed 66 (sixty-six) employees out of 76 (seventy-six) and still 394 (three hundred ninety four) employees posts are vacant and the writ-petitioners-respondents are still in service and have requisite qualifications, experience and satisfactory service record; and in the similar position the writ-petitioners are expecting to be transferred in the revenue set up and, as such, the appeal is liable to be dismissed. He submitted that the High Court Division correctly held that from the employment notice, Project Proforma and the letters of the Ministry of Education and the Director General of Secondary and Education Directorate, it appears that the respondents while making employment notification assured the writ-petitioners that their services might be transferred /absorbed in the revenue budget. From the letters of the Education Directorate, it appears that even the Government did not depart from the intention to transfer/absorb the services of the petitioners in the revenue budget, rather they failed to take any decision for want of time to make necessary amendment in the organogram of the Secondary and Higher Secondary Education Directorate; and the petitioners have also been assured through the Principals of the respective colleges wherein the Petitioners had been serving that they would be informed if any positive step is taken to transfer/absorb their services in the revenue budget, and, as such, the appeal is liable to be dismissed. He submitted that the High Court Division correctly held that it is found from the several letters that decision was taken in several meetings that the writ-petitioners-respondents would be absorbed in the revenue set up and the Government is duty bound to absorb the writ-petitioners-respondents by giving assurance, and such an assurance has created a legitimate expectation in the mind of the writ-petitioners-respondent. At this stage, the writ-respondents -appellants now cannot back out from such an assurance and, as such, the appeal is liable to be dismissed. He submitted that after completion of the project work the writ-petitioners-respondents were permitted to continue to work and they were under expectation that they will be absorbed in the revenue set up and the posts of the respondents are required by the Government thus the Ministry of Education recommended to transfer the service of the respondents to the revenue set up and, as such, the appeal is liable to be dismissed. He also submitted that the petitioners are working in the "Development of Selected Colleges (Government and Non-Government) Project (2nd Revised)" under the Ministry of Education and have not yet been absorbed/regularised in the service of the Republic as such the Administrative Tribunal Act is not attracted/applicable in the present case and the writ-petitioners-respondents have no other equal efficacious remedy and, as such, the Writ Petition No. 3562 of 2011 is maintainable. He submitted that the services of the respondents were legally utilised by appellant Nos. I and 2 for such a long time without any break, but their absorption in the revenue set up was kept hanging without any reason and most illegally and arbitrarily by misusing the position and such the same is without any lawful authority and is of no legal effect and, as such, the appeal is liable to be dismissed. He submitted that 394 (three hundred ninety four) vacant posts existing in the Ministry of Education have been declared to be filled by direct appointment, which is unfair and discriminatory. The Ministry of Education has on a previous occasion approved the absorption of 66 (sixty six) persons in the vacant posts and if the writ petitioners apply for the direct appointment they would be at a disadvantage due to the fact that they would be over the age limit and the writ-petitioners-respondents have necessary experience and qualification to be transferred in the revenue set up and the same is conventional and, as such, the appeal is liable to be dismissed. He lastly submitted that the Government is duty bound in accordance with the SRO No. 182/ LAW/ 2005/SHOM/BIBIDN/5-9 dated 20-6-2005 and, as such, the appeal is liable to be dismissed.

7. We have considered the submissions of the learned Deputy Attorney General and learned Advocate for the respondents, perused the impugned judgment and order of the High Court Division and other connected papers on record.

8. The High Court Division considered the employment notice, project proforma and the letter dated 30-1-2006 issued by the Ministry of Establishment addressing the Secretary, Ministry of Education and the letter dated 15-2-2006 issued by the Ministry of Education to the Project Director and the Director-General, Secondary and Higher Secondary Education and the letter dated 30.12.2007 issued by the Director-General of the Secondary and Higher Secondary Education Directorate to the Principals of Colleges where the petitioners had been serving and noted that the petitioners' expectation to get their services transferred/absorbed in the revenue setup has got basis. It was also noted that a direction was given by the High Court Division to absorb/regularise the writ-petitioners in Writ Petition No. 5667 of 2008 in almost identical circumstances. The civil petition for leave to appeal filed by the respondents earlier having been dismissed by this Division, the direction of the High Court Division was implemented. Hence, the High Court Division directed the respondents to consider the ease of the petitioners in the light of the decision of ECNEC dated 30-12-2007 and the provisions of SRO No. 182-A in/2005/Shomo/Bidhi-I/S-9/2000 dated 20-6-2005.

<u>9. It appears from the facts and circumstances of the instant case that the petitioners had been given assurances that their services might be transferred/absorbed in the revenue budget. Furthermore, since in similar circumstances the government has implemented the directions of the Supreme Court and absorbed the writ-petitioners in Writ Petition No. 5667 of 2008, it would be discriminatory not to treat the present respondents equally.</u>

10. In the light of the facts and circumstances discussed above, we do not find any illegality or infirmity in the impugned judgment, which calls for any interference. Accordingly, the appeal is dismissed, without however, any order as to costs.

End.

caseno: Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 4057 of 2018.
lawyer:
Mahbubey Alam, Attorney-General, instructed by Haridas Paul, Advocate-on-Record-----For the Petitioner. 
AJ Mohammad Ali, Senior Advocate, instructed by Md Tawfique Hossain, Advocate-on-Record-----For the Respondents.
parties:
Government of People's Republic of Bangladesh and others-------Petitioners 
Vs 
Md Mushfaqur Rahman and another-------Respondents
case_source: (From the judgment and order dated 16-7-2017 passed by the High Court Division in Writ Petition No. 631 of 2010).
full_judgment:
Syed Mahmud Hossain CJ: This civil petition for leave to appeal is direction against the judgment and order dated 16-7-2017 passed by the High Court Division in Writ Petition No. 631 of 2010 making the Rule Nisi absolute.

2. The facts, leading to the filing of this civil petition for leave to appeal, in brief, are:

The writ-petitioners are law abiding citizens and come from respectable Muslim families. One Mr Ahsan Habib applied to the Government for allotment of Khas land within Cox's Bazar's Hotel/Motel Zone for construction of a hotel. The Government allotted 1.00 acre of land initially but the land was submerged in water. Subsequently, the Government allotted Plot No. 13 (Kolatoli Road) on 26-1-2003 by a lease deed for a period of 99 years. Thereafter, the lessee Mr Habib filed an application before the Deputy Commissioner of Cox's Bazar seeking permission to transfer the allotted land in favour of the writ-petitioners. The application was allowed and the writ-petitioners deposited transfer fees on 13-7-2006. Thereafter, on 27-6-2006 transfer deed had been executed and registered. The writ-petitioners thereafter mutated the land in their names. After that, the writ-petitioners obtained possession of the land and constructed boundary walls and proceeded with the construction work. The writ-petitioners, in one part of the land constructed a Motel which was rented out to the tourists. Soon thereafter, the Care-taker Government took over charge. As a result, due to unavoidable circumstances, the construction work had to be suspended temporarily.

3. In 2009, the writ-petitioners obtained No Objection Certificate' from the Civil Aviation Authority for the construction of the hotel. The writ-petitioners also prepared plan and submitted the same to the Paurashova and the plan was approved on 19-6-2009. On 01-7-2009, they submitted a copy of the approved plan to the Deputy Commissioner of Cox's Bazar. The writ-petitioners also filed applications to the Deputy Commissioner, Cox's Bazar and the Ministry of Land seeking three years extension for completion of the project. However, no decision on the applications had been communicated to the writ-petitioners. Thereafter, writ-respondent No. 2 abruptly issued the order dated 12-1-2010 (impugned before the High Court Division) informing the writ-petitioners that the lease agreement had been cancelled and directed the writ-petitioners to hand-over the land to the Government. Prior to the cancellation of lease no show cause notice had been issued.

4. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with order dated 12-1-2010 issued under the signature of writ-respondent No. 2, the writ-petitioners moved the High Court Division by filing a writ petition and obtained Rule Nisi in Writ Petition No. 631 of 2010.

5. Writ-respondent No.1 filed an affidavit-in-opposition controverting the material statements made in the writ petition. It was stated that the order dated 12-1-2020 was issued in the light of a detailed inspection report and therefore, there was no illegality in issuing the impugned order. It was also pointed out that prior to issuance of the cancellation order, an inter-ministerial meeting was held on 28-5-2009. A committee was formed in the said meeting and the representatives of the Committee visited Cox's Bazar and found that the writ-petitioners and others violated the terms of lease agreement. This led to the issuance of the lever of cancellation. Writ-respondent No. 1 also relied on certain judgments passed by the High Court Division in Writ Petition Nos. 639, 511 and 894 of 2010 in support of their contention and, as such, the Rule should be discharged.

6. A supplementary affidavit-in-opposition had also been filed. It was stated therein that the lease agreement was cancelled on 12-1-2010 and subsequently, the writ-respondents obtained possession of the land in question.

7. The writ-petitioners filed a supplementary-affidavit from which it appears that a list of 59 plots was prepared showing breach of terms of the lease deed and it was recommended that lease in respect of those plots should be cancelled. It was pointed out, amongst others, that in preparing the list no show cause notice was issued. By another supplementary-affidavit, the writ-petitioners have annexed a letter dated 26-8-2015 which shows that the writ-petitioners' plot is not within the ecologically critical area.

8. The learned Judges of the High Court Division upon hearing the parties by the judgment and order dated 16-7-2017 made the Rule absolute.

9. Feeling aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the judgment and order passed by the High Court Division, the writ-respondents as the leave-petitioners filed this civil petition for leave to appeal before this Division.

10. Mr Mahbubey Alam, learned Attorney-General, appearing on behalf of the leave-petitioners, submits that the original lessee Md Ahsan Habib seriously violated the mandatory conditions of lease-agreement (Annexure-B to the writ petition) and that because of violation of mandatory condition of lease agreement, the cancellation order dated 12-1-2010 passed by the Government is quite legal and, as such, the impugned judgment and order is liable to be set aside. He further submits that both the plots in question are situated within Jhilanja Mouza which is within the Ecologically Critical Area (ECA) and is protected by the prohibitions mentioned in the Gazette Notification dated 19-4-1999 and, as such, leasing out those plots were illegal and without jurisdiction. He then submits that by the subsequent Notification dated 3-5-1999 only the reserve forest areas are excluded from the ECA, and not the sea beach area. He then submits that the subsequent letter dated 2-11-2015 issued by the Department of Environment was somehow procured after the judgment was delivered by the High Court Division arising out of similar writ petitions. He also submits that the aforesaid letter dated 2-11-2015 was issued at the instance of one of the parties and it cannot override the Notification dated 19-4-1999 published in the official Gazette.

11. Mr AJ Mohammad Ali, the learned Senior Advocate, appearing on behalf of respondent Nos. 1 and 2, the subsequent purchasers from the original lessee, submits that the impugned order of cancellation was issued in violation of principle of natural justice as no prior notice was served upon them before cancellation of the lease agreement. He also submits that respondent Nos. 1 and 2, the subsequent purchasers from the original lessee relied upon the letter issued by the appropriate authority approving the transfer and that the writ-petitioners paid the transfer fees which. were accepted by the proper authority and the names of respondent Nos. 1 and 2 herein were mutated and, as such, the impugned order of cancellation is illegal and without lawful authority. He then submits that the disputed plots were not within ECA as evident from Annexure-M dated 26-8-2015 signed by Assistant Director, Paribesh Directorate, Cox's Bazar and, as such, the impugned cancellation of lease was illegal and without jurisdiction. He lastly submits that the present case is distinguishable from writ petitions disposed of by the High Court Division vide judgment and order dated 22-7-2010 and, as such, the impugned judgment and order calls for no interference.

12. One Mohammad Ahsan Habib applied to the Government for allotment of khas land within Cox's Bazar Hotel/Motel Zone for construction of a Hotel. The Government allotted 1 (one) acre of land initially but the land was submerged in water. Later the Government allotted plot No.13 (Kolatoli Road) on 26-1-2003. The lessee filed an application before the Deputy Commissioner, Cox's Bazar, seeking permission to transfer the allotted land in favour of the writ-petitioners. The application was allowed and the writ-petitioners deposited transfer fees on 13-7-2006. After that, the transfer deed was executed and registered on 27-6-2006. In 2009, the writ petitioners obtained No objection Certificate from Civil Aviation Authority for construction of the hotel. The writ-petitioners also prepared plan and submitted the same with the Paurashova which approved it on 19-6-2006. They filed applications to the Deputy Commissioner, Cox's Bazar and the Ministry of Land seeking 3 years extension for completion of the project. But no decision on those applications had been communicated to the petitioners. After that, writ-respondent No. 2 abruptly issued the order dated 12-1-2010 (impugned before the High Court Division) informing the writ-petitioners that the lease agreement has been cancelled and directed the writ-petitioners to hand over the land to the Government.

13. The High Court Division made the Rule absolute holding that the impugned order was issued arbitrarily, not taking into account the relevant facts and that the High Court Division was convinced that the impugned order was issued in violation of the principle of natural justice. The High Court Division found that a lease agreement was not automatically nullified and that it had to be nullified. The High Court Division noticed that since the lease agreement was not cancelled prior to the transfer approval in favour of the writ-petitioners, a right under a valid lease was transferred in favour of the writ-petitioners. The High Court Division noted that admittedly the writ-petitioners could not complete the work within the period of 3 years but that on its own could not justify the order of cancellation of lease dated 12-1-2010. The High Court Division found that the impugned decision to cancel lease was taken on the recommendation of a committee which recommended that 59 plots should be cancelled including the plots belonging to the writ-petitioners. The High Court Division then held there was nothing on record that the committee heard the lessees including the writ petitioners prior to the recommendation for cancellation and that the order of cancellation based on committee's recommendation was illegal.

14. With regard to the claim of illegal cancellation of the lease, we find from the papers submitted by the writ-respondents that the lease was cancelled as both the plots were found empty, that is, there was no construction. Therefore, the writ-petitioners were in breach of the terms and conditions specified in the lease deed.

15. The learned Attorney-General mainly concentrated his argument on the preservation of ecological balance of the environment and protection of natural resources. The learned Attorney-General submits that the Government granted the lease without taking notice of the Gazette Notification dated 19-4-1999 declaring Cox's Bazar Sea Beach as Ecologically Critical Area (ECA) under section 5 of the Bangladesh Environment Conservation Act, 1995.

16. The learned Counsel for the writ-petitioner-respondents draws attention to the second Gazette Notification dated 3-5-1999 by which the disputed two plots were excluded from ECA. With regard to the submission that both the plots have been excluded in the later Gazette Notification dated 3-5-1999, the High Court Division by the judgment and order dated 22-7-2010 delivered in Writ Petition No.639 of 2010 and others held as follows:

"We have meticulously examined the notification dated 3-5-1999 by which certain areas were excluded from the declaration and found that “কক্সবাজার জেলার কক্সবাজার-টেকনাফ সমুদ্র সৈকত ও সোনাদিয়া দ্বীপ এর সংশ্লিষ্ট রিজার্ভ ফরেস্ট এলাকাসমূহ, বর্ণিত প্রজ্ঞাপন উল্লিখিত বিধি নিষেধের আওতা বহির্ভূত করা হলো।” Thus this clearly means that রিজার্ভ ফরেস্ট এলাকাসমূহ, বর্ণিত প্রজ্ঞাপনে উল্লিখিত বিধি নিষেধের আওতা বহির্ভূত করা হলো।This means "Reserved Forest Area" of the Cox's Bazar Sea Beach has been excluded from the Ecologically Critical Area but not the Cox' s Bazar Sea Beach from the declaration of Ecologically Critical Area."

20. The writ petitioners claimed that the Sea Beach from Cox's Bazar to Teknaf is excluded from the ECA. In this connection, we are of the view that the Notification dated 3-5-1999 must be construed in its entirety. It is clear that the sentence read as a whole refers to the "Reserve Forest areas of the Sundarbans in Bagerhat, Khulna and Satkhira District," and the "Reserve Forest areas of the Sea Beach within Cox's Bazar District from Cox's Bazar to Teknaf and Sonddia Island."

21. From clause 2 of the said Notification, it appears that the Reserve Forest areas are being excluded from the ECA due to the fact that they are under the control of the Forest Department and are governed by other specific laws, rules and management plans.

22.
