full_judgment:
Moyeenul Islam Chowdhury J : Let the Supplementary-Affidavit do form part of the main application.

2. Today is fixed for passing necessary order.

3. This is an application under Article 102 of the Constitution of the People's Republic of Bangladesh.

<u>4. It has submitted before us that the petitioners have not come up with this Writ Petition for quashing the criminal proceedings pending against them in the Courts below; rather they have come up with the instant Writ Petition for protection of their fundamental rights as guaranteed under Part III of the Constitution and form arbitrary and malafide actions of the police personnel by way of filing fictions criminal cases namely, Paltan Model Police Station Case No. 38 dated 16-9-2018 under sections 143/147/148/ 149/186/353/307/332/333/109/114/34 of the Penal Code read with sections 316 of the Explosive Substances Act, 1908 Paltan Model Police Station Case No. 23 dated 11-9-2018 under sections 1451147/149/186/353/307/332/333/109/ 114/34 of the Penal Code read with sections 3/6 of the Explosive Substances Act, 1908, Paltan Model Police Station Case No. 25 dated 12-9-2018 under sections 143/147/148/149/186/353/307/332/333/ 109/114/34 of the Penal Code read with sections 3/6 of the Explosive Substances Act, 1908, Paltan Model Police Station Case No. 26 dated 12-9-2018 under sections 143/147/148/149/186/353/ 307/332/333/109/114/34 of the Penal Code read with sections 3/6 of the Explosive Substances Act, 1908, Paltan Model Police Station Case No. 31 dated 14-9-2018 under sections 143/147/148/ 149/186/353/307/332/333/109/114/34 of the Penal Code read with sections 3/6 of the Explosive Substances Act, 1908, Mirpur Model Police Station Case No. 56 dated 15-9-2018 under section 15(3) of the Special, Powers Act, 1974 read with sections 4/5/6 of the Explosive Substances Act, 1908 against the petitioners and others. As the petitioners have not come up with the instant Writ Petition for quashing the proceedings of the cases pending against them in the Courts below and as a reference to Annexure-D' to the Supplementary-Affidavit, that is to say, paper-clipping of 'The Daily Jugantor' dated 24-9-2018 positively indicates that the Inspector-General of Police had already alerted the Police Headquarters for safeguarding the image of the police in filing cases against various persons who are allegedly dead, sick and away from the Juntry, 1 think, a Rule Nisi may be issued in the following terms:</u>

5. Let a Rule Nisi be issued calling upon the respondents 'to show cause as to why the allegedly arbitrary and malafide actions of the police officers currently being executed under the control and supervision of the respondents upon filing of the aforesaid purported fictitious criminal cases against the petitioners and other indefinite number of people belonging to various different political parties/groups as evidenced by Annexure-'A' series to the Writ Petition should not be declared to be without lawful authority and of no legal effect and why the respondents should not be directed to take appropriate legal actions against the police officers who were involved in the lodging of those alleged malafide and fictitious criminal cases against the petitioners and others and/or such other or further order or orders passed as to this Court may seem fit and proper.

6. However, the Investigating Officer; are at liberty to carry out the investigation of the criminal cases filed against the petitioners and others in accordance with law.

7. The Inspector-General of Police Head-quarters, Police Station Shahbagh, Dhaka (respondent No. 2) is hereby directed to take steps to monitor and enquire into the alleged aforesaid fictitious and malafide criminal cases filed against the petitioners and others with different Police Stations of Dhaka Metropolitan City and submit a report to this Court by filing an Affidavit-in-Compliance within 60(sixty) days from the date of receipt of a copy of this order. 8. The Rule is returnable within 4(four) weeks from date.

9. The petitioners are directed to put in requisites for service of notices upon the respondents by registered post as well as through usual process within 3(three) working days, failing which, the Rule shall stand discharged.

10. Put up the record on 17-12-2018 for passing necessary order.

Ashraful Kamal J: আমি মাননীয় জ্যেষ্ঠ বিচারপতি জনাব মইনুল ইসলাম চৌধুরী মহোদয়ের রুল ইস্যুর আদেশটি শুনলাম। আমি তাঁর প্রতি শ্রদ্ধা রেখে দরখাস্তকারীগণের অত্র দরখাস্ত দায়ের করার ন্যূনতম কোন কারণ না থাকায় তথা প্রাথমিকভাবে বিচারের কোন বিষয় না পাওয়ায় তাঁর রুল ইস্যুর আদেশের সহিত একমত হতে না পেরে তথা ভিন্নমত পোষণ করে দরখাস্তটি প্রাথমিক শুনানীতে সরাসরি প্রত্যাখান করছি।

১২. দরখাস্তকারীগণের দরখাস্ত পর্যালোচনা করলাম। দরখাস্তকারীগণের এবং বিজ্ঞ অ্যাডভোকেটগণের যুক্তিতর্ক বিস্তারিতভাবে শ্রবণ করলাম এবং তা যথাযথভাবে মূ্ল্যায়নসহ বিবেচনা করলাম।

১৩. অত্র রীট পিটিশন নিষ্পত্তিতে গুরুত্বপূর্ন বিধায় দরখাস্তকারীগণ রীট পিটিশনে যে বক্তব্য উপস্থাপন করেছেন তা নিয়ে অবিকল অনুলিখন হলোঃ

"1. The petitioners are law abiding citizen of Bangladesh. All the petitioners are legal practitioners and are practicing law regularly before both the Divisions of the Hon'ble Supreme Court of Bangladesh. They are members of Bangladesh. Supreme Court Bar Association. The petitioner No. 1 is a Senior Advocate and former president of Supreme Court Bar Association for 4 consecutive terms and was also elected as vice-chairman of Bangladesh Bar Council for 2 consecutive terms. He is the vice-chairman of Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP). The petitioner No. 2 is an Advocate and is the vice-chairman of BNP. He was Cabinet Minister for Youth and Sports and he was also served as the State Minister for Ministry of Education and Ministry of Law Justice and Parliamentary Affairs. The petitioner No. 3 is also an Advocate and served as an Additional Attorney-General for Bangladesh. He is also a vice-chairman of BNP. The petitioner No. 4  is an Advocate and a former president of Dhaka Bar Association. He is the law  secretary of BNP All the petitioners have been falsely entangled in various criminal cases, which are currently pending. 2. The petitioners are conscious of their duty as politicians and citizens in consonance with Article 21 of the Constitution to ensure the observance of the Constitution and the law of Bangladesh and to ensure the prevention of illegal and unconstitutional encroachments upon the civil rights of the indefinite number of people and citizens of Bangladesh. The petitioners are interested in the welfare of the Republic and also aware of the fundamental rights enshrined in the Part 111 of the Constitution in general and in Articles 27, 33, 35, 36, 37, 38 and 39 of the Constitution in particular whereby all citizens are entitled to equal protection of law and which prohibit taking any action detrimental to the life, liberty, body, reputation or property of any person except in accordance with law. As democratic politicians and practicing lawyers of the Supreme. Court of Bangladesh, the petitioners, having sufficient interest and being aggrieved by the impugned actions, is filing this Writ Petition under Article 102 of the Constitution.

3. The writ petition is filed by the petitioners in their capacity as concerned, affected and aggrieved persons to protect the  national interest of Bangladesh being its democratic character having the best ride of law and independence of judiciary and to ensure the interest of indefinite number of people of Bangladesh and to uphold the Rule of Law by way of public interest litigation. The petitioners being committed to the welfare of the Republic and to ensure that the Rule of Law is upheld and to protect the public interest and as a public good spirited and concerned person brings this action pro bono publico in respect of matters set out herein. The petitioners are aware that all powers in the Republic belong to the People, and their exercise on behalf of the people shall be effected under, and by the authority of this Constitution and that the Constitution is as the solemn expression of the will of the people, the Supreme Law of the Republic, and if any law and/or actions are 'inconsistent with this Constitution that other law and/or actions, to the extent of the, inconsistency, shall be void.

4. This writ petition is also maintainable in view of the latest guidelines given in the case of National Board of Revenue vs Abu Saeed Khan reported in 18 BLC (AD) 116 inasmuch as it has been brought before, this Hon'ble Court as a public interest litigation challenging the blatant abuse and misuse of power violating the directions of law in general and direction of the Hon'ble Appellate Division of the Supreme Court of Bangladesh in particular given in the case of Bangladesh vs BLAST reported in 69 DLR (AD) 63.

5. The Respondent No. 1 is Bangladesh represented by the Secretary, Ministry of Home Affairs; Respondent No. 2 is Inspector-General of Police; Respondent No. 3 is Commissioner, Dhaka Metropolitan Police; Respondent No. 4 is Deputy Commissioner of Police, Ramna Zone, Dhaka Metropolitan Police; Respondent No. 5 is Deputy Commissioner of Police, Detective Branch, North Zone, Office of Detective Branch; Respondent No. 6 is Additional Deputy Police Commissioner, Ramna Zone, Dhaka Metropolitan Police; Respondent No. 7 is the Officer-in-Charge, Ramna Police Station, Dhaka; Respondent No. 8 is Officer-in-Charge, Paltan Police Station, Dhaka; and Respondent No. 9 is the Officer-in-Charge, Shahbagh Police Station.

6. The addresses of the parties mentioned in the cause title are their correct addresses and all notices may be served upon them in the said addresses.

7. The petitioner impugns herein this Writ Petition the arbitrary and malafide  actions of the Respondents executing through police officers under their control and  supervision upon filing of fictitious criminal  cases against the petitioners and other indefinite number of people who belong to different political groups than the government, which is evident from different newspaper reporting including the Daily Star, Prothom Alo, Nayadiganta and Manab Zamin published on several dates In September 2018. The petitioner further prays for an order of direction upon the respondents to take appropriate legal actions against the officers who are involved in the lodging of arbitrary, malafide and fictitious lodging of cases.

8. It transpires from the record maintained by BNP that in last 20 days (between 1-9-2018 and 20-9-2018) as many  as 3,736 cases have been filed against 3,13,130 known and unknown number of persons who belong to BNP and its alliance all over Bangladesh. Such cases are no doubt based on fictitious and concocted stories which have been filed by the Respondents under their supervision having malicious intention to harass, detain and control the opposition activists ahead of the ensuing parliamentary election scheduled to be held on any date between October 2018 and 9th January 2019. The reports supporting the aforesaid statements of the petitioners, published in different newspapers, amongst others the Daily Prothom Alo dated 5-9-2018 and 12-9-2018 and the Daily Nayadiganta dated 19-9-2018 and a report dated 20-9-2018 obtained from the office of BNP are annexed hereto and marked as Annexure-A series.

9. That it is stated that several newspaper reports also suggests that the police have filed some cases out of their blue design against dead persons, persons having severe health conditions, persons admitted into intensive care unit of various hospitals and clinics, persons who had gone for performing Hajj and so on. For instance (i) in the Daily Prothom Alo, a news report has been published with a caption “পুলিশের মামলায় আসামী মৃত ব্যক্তি ও প্রবাসীরা”; (ii) in jagonews 24.com, a news report has been published with a caption “মামলার প্রধান আসামী মৃত ব্যক্তি;

22. দত্তরাজ নাথুজি থাওয়ার বনাম মহারাষ্ট্র, (২০০৫) ১এসসিসি-৫৯০, ৫৯২-৫৯৩ (প্যারা ৪) (Dattaraj Nathuji Thaware vs State of Maharashtra, (2005) 1 SCC 590, 592-93 (para 4) মোকদ্দমায় ভারতীয় সুপ্রীম কোর্ট অভিমত প্রদান করেন যে,

"A person acting bonafide and having sufficient interest in the proceeding of public interest litigation will alone have a locus standi and can approach the Court to wipe out violation of fundamental rights and genuine infraction of statutory provisions, but not for personal gain or private profit or political motive or any oblique consideration."

23. উপরিল্লিখিত মোকদ্দমায় ভারতীয় সুপ্রীম কোর্ট আরও অভিমত প্রদান করেন যে,

"A writ-petitioner who comes to the Court for relief in public interest must come not only with clean hands like any other writ petitioner but also with a clear heart, clean mind and clean objective."

24. অত্র মোকদ্দমার দরখাস্তকারীত্রয় একটি রাজনৈতিক দল তথা বাংলাদেশ ন্যাশনাল পার্টি (বিএনপি) এর শীর্ষস্থানীয় নেতৃবৃন্দ। আযাডভোকেট ড. কামাল হোসেন তিনিও একটি রাজনৈতিক দলের প্রধান এবং বর্তমানে বাংলাদেশ ন্যাশনালিষ্ট পার্টি (বিএনপি) এর সাথে এক মঞ্চে জোটবদ্ধ হয়ে রাজনীতি করছেন। ফলে অব্র মোকদ্দমাটি কোনভাবেই জনন্বার্থে তথা জনগণের স্বার্থে দায়ের করা মোকদ্দমা নয় । বরং বলা যায় এটি একটি শুদ্ধ রাজনৈতিক স্বার্থে দায়ের করা মামলা । দরখান্তকারী- গণের দরখান্তে যে বর্ণনা দেওয়া হয়েছে এবং আাডভোকেট ড. কামাল হোসেনের যুক্তিতর্ক পর্যালোচনায় এটা দিবালোকের মত স্পষ্ট যে, এটি একটি রাজনৈতিক উদ্দেশ্য হাসিল তথা রাজনৈতিক ফায়দা হাসিলের মোকদ্দমা ।

25. আযাডভোকেট ড. কামাল হোসেন বিভিন্ন পত্রিকায় রিপোর্ট উপস্থাপন পূর্বক নিবেদন করেন যে, সারাদেশে বিএনপির নেতা, কর্মী ও সমর্থকদের বিরদ্ধে মিথ্যা ও গায়েবী মামলা হচ্ছে। এ প্রসংগে ওসেনা বেগম এবং অন্যান্য বনাম রাষ্ট্র ৫৫ ডিএলআর ২০০৩ পাতা ২৯৯) মামলার সিদ্ধান্ত হলোঃ

“Evidence Act (1 of 1872)

Section 65 Newspaper report cannot be admitted into evidence unless the correspondent of such a report comes to the witness box to vouchsafe in support of the report on oath.”

26. আাডভোকেট ড. কামাল হোসেন যুক্তিতর্ক উপস্থাপনকালে নিবেদন করেন যে, একই ঘটনা এবং অভিযোগের ভিত্তিতে প্রতিপক্ষগণ দরখাস্তকারীগণের বিরুদ্ধে দরখান্তে বর্ণিত ৭টি মামলা করেছে। এতদ্বিষয়ে, তেহাং প্যাকেজিং বিডি লিঃ বনাম বাংলাদেশ (১৮ বিএলসি (এডি) (২০১৩) পাতা ১৪৫) প্যারা ১৬৬ এবং ১১৮ মোকদ্দমায় আপিল বিভাগ (বিচারপতি মোঃ আবদুল ওয়াহহাব মিঞা) সংখ্যাগরিষ্ঠের ভিত্তিতে অভিমত প্রদান করেন যে,

"Before issuance of the Rule the learned Judge had a responsibility to see as to whether the cause title and prayer of the writ petition confirmed with language of Article 102 of the Constitution and High Court Division Rules and whether the facts and circumstances at all warranted any interference by way of judicial review."

27. উপরিল্লিখিত মোকদ্দমায় আপিল বিভাগ আরও সিদ্ধান্ত প্রদান করেন যে, "If the accused felt that they are being harassed in malafide manner through the filing of the series of cases over the self same incident or allegation they have other forum to redress such harassment but not been Special jurisdiction of the High Court Division."

28. বেগম খালেদা জিয়া বনাম এসিসি (৭০ ডিএলআর (এডি) (২০১৮) পাতা ৫০) মোকদ্দমায় আপিল বিভাগ সিদ্ধান্ত প্রদান করেন যে,

"In proceedings under Article 102 of the Constitution it is not open to the High Court Division to hold an elaborate enquiry into disputed and complicated questions of fact. The High Court Division would only interfere with the proceeding of a criminal court if it s found that such proceeding is without jurisdiction and if there is no other efficacious relief provided in law against such proceeding or the vires of the law basing on which the proceeding initiated is challenged.

Constitution of Bangladesh, 1972

Article 102(2)

Where a person has an equally efficacious remedy, the High Court Division would not interfere with criminal proceeding in exercising extra-ordinary jurisdiction. Such powers are to be exercised in rare and exceptional cases.

29. আপিল বিভাগের উপরিলিখিত সিদ্ধান্ত হাইকোর্ট বিভাগ মানতে বাধ্য ৷ আপিল বিভাগের উপরিল্লিখিত সিদ্ধান্ত সমূহ পর্যালোচনায় এটা স্পষ্ট যে, সংবিধানের অনুচ্ছেদ ১০২ মোতাবেক অত্র দরখাস্ত দাখিল করার দরখাস্তকারীগণের কোন অধিকার নাই ।

<u>30. এটা স্বীকৃত যে, দরখাস্তকারীগণের বিরুদ্ধে দরখাস্তে বর্ণিত মামলাসমূহের প্রত্যেকটি মামলা তদস্তাধীন। তদস্তাধীন মামলা সংশ্লিষ্টতায় কোন আদেশ নির্দেশ দেওয়া ঘায় না। এটা আইনের সুপ্রতিষ্ঠিত নীতি । কিন্তু দরখাস্তকারীর সর্বশেষ প্রার্থণাটি হল “Pending hearing of the Rule retrain the Respondents from proceeding with the investigations of the cases filed against 016 19601019065 যা আইন অনুমোদন করে না।”</u>

<u>31. সংবিধানের বিধান মোতাবেক হাইকোর্ট যে কোন আইন সংবিধানের বিধি বিধানের সহিত সাংঘর্ষিক হলে বাতিল করতে পারে, কিন্তু আইন বানাতে পারে। সুতরাং সাংবিধানিক ধারাবাহিকতা সমুন্নত রাখতে আদালত সকল সময় 'নিজেকে নিয়ন্ত্রণ নীতি অনুসরন পূর্বক বিচারিক প্রজ্ঞার পরিচয় দিয়ে থাকে।</u>

32. সংবিধানের অনুচ্ছেদ ১১১ গুরুত্পূর্ণ বিধায় এখানে উল্লেখ করা প্রয়োজনঃ__

“সুপ্রিম কোর্টের রায়ের বাধ্যতামূলক (১১১) আগিল বিভাগ কর্তৃক ঘোষিত আইন হাইকোর্ট বিভাগের জন্য

কার্যকরতা এবং সুপ্বিম কোর্টের যে কোন বিভাগ ঘোষিত আইন অধস্তন সকল আদালতের জন্য অবশ্যপালনীয় হইবে ।

<u>33. আপিল বিভাগ কর্তৃক ঘোষিত আইন হাইকোর্ট বিভাগের জন্য এবং সুপ্রিম কোর্টের যে কোন বিভাগ কর্তৃক ঘোষিত আইন অধস্তন সকল আদালতের জন্য অবশ্য পালনীয় হবে । অর্থাৎ আপিল বিভাগ যে মতামত যে সিদ্ধান্ত প্রদান করবেন হাইকোর্ট বিভাগ সেটা মানতে বাধ্য । সংবিধানের অনুচ্ছেদ ১১১ এর বিধান মোতাবেক এবং আপিল বিভাগের উপরিল্লিখিত সিদ্ধান্তের আলোকে অত্র দরখাস্তটি আইন, আপিল বিভাগের সিদ্ধান্ত এবং সংবিধান পরিপন্থী বিধায় সরাসরি প্রত্যাখ্যাত হওয়া উচিত।</u>

34. অতএব, আদেশ হয় যে, অত্র দরখাস্তটি সরাসরি প্রত্যাখ্যাত হল।

Judgment

Md Nazrul Islam Talukder J : This is an Application under Article 102(2)(a)(i) and (ii) of the Constitution of the People's Republic of Bangladesh. 1972 filed by the Petitioners challenging arbitrary and mala fide actions of the respondents executing through police officers under their control and supervision upon filling fictitious criminal cases against the petitioners and others indefinite number of people who belong to different political groups other than the government, which is evident from the different newspapers reporting including the Daily Star, Prothom Alo, Nayadiganta, Manab Zamin published on several dates in September 2018 as evident from Annexure-A Series to the application as well as for direction upon the respondents to take appropriate legal actions against the officers who are involved in lodging of arbitrary, mala fide and fictitious cases.

36. It may be noted that this application was earlier heard by a Division Bench consisting of their lordships Mr Justice Moyeenul Islam Chowdhury and Mr Justice Md Ashraful Kamal. Since initial order dated 9-10-2018 over this matter was a split one, this matter was referred to the Hon'ble Chief Justice of Bangladesh for necessary order for disposal of this application. Accordingly, this matter has been sent to this court by the Hon'ble Chief Justice of Bangladesh for disposal of the application.

37. The statements made in the writ petition by the petitioners are as follows:

1. That the petitioners are law abiding citizen of Bangladesh. All the petitioners are legal practitioners and are practicing law regularly before both the Divisions of the Supreme Court of Bangladesh. They are members of Bangladesh Supreme Court Bar Association. The Petitioner No. 1 is a senior Advocate and former president of Supreme Court Bar Association for 4 consecutive terms and was also elected as vice-chairman of Bangladesh Bar council for 2 consecutive terms. He is the vice-chairman of Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP). The Petitioner No. 2 is an advocate and is the vice-chairman of BNP. He was Cabinet Minister for Youth and Sports and he was also served as the State Minister for Ministry of Education and Ministry of Law Justice and Parliamentary Affairs. The Petitioner No. 3 is an Advocate and former president of Dhaka Bar Association. He is the law secretary of BNP. All the Petitioners have been falsely entangled in various criminal cases, which are currently pending.

2. That the petitioners are conscious of their duty as politicians and citizens in consonance with Article 21 of the Constitution to ensure the observance of the Constitution and the laws of Bangladesh and to ensure the prevention of illegal and unconstitutional encroachments upon the civil rights of the indefinite number of people and citizens of Bangladesh. The petitioners are interested in the welfare of the Republic and also aware of the fundamental rights enshrined in the Part III of the Constitution in general and in Articles 27, 33, 35, 36, 37, 38 and 39 of the Constitution in particular whereby all citizens are entitled to equal protection of law and which prohibit taking any action detrimental to the life, liberty, body, reputation or property of any person except in accordance with law. As democratic politicians and practicing lawyers of the Supreme Court of Bangladesh, the petitioners, having sufficient interest and being aggrieved by the impugned actions, have filed this writ petition under Article 102 of the Constitution.

3. That the writ petition is filed by the petitioners in their capacity as concerned, affected and aggrieved persons to protect the national interest of Bangladesh being it democratic character having the best rule of law and independence of judiciary and to ensure the interest of indefinite number of people of Bangladesh and to uphold the Rule of Law by way of public interest litigation. The petitioners being committed to the welfare of the Republic and to ensure that the Rule of law is upheld and to protect the public interest and as a public good spirited and concerned persons have brought the actions as pro bono publico in respect of matters set out herein. The petitioners are aware that all powers in the Republic belong to the people, and their exercise on behalf of the people shall be effected under, and by the authority of this Constitution and that the Constitution is the solemn expression of the will of the people, and the Supreme Law of the Republic, and if any law and/or actions are inconsistent with this Constitution, that law and/or actions, to the extent of the inconsistency, shall be void.

4. That this writ petition is also maintainable in view of the latest guidelines given in the case of National Board of Revenue vs Abu Saeed Khan reported in 18 BLC (AD) 116 inasmuch as it has been brought before this Court as a public interest litigation challenging the blatant abuse and misuse of power violating the direction of law in general and direction of the Appellate Division of the Supreme Court of Bangladesh in particular given in the case of Bangladesh vs BLAST reported in 69 DLR (AD) 63.

5. That the Respondents No. l is Bangladesh represented by the Secretary, Ministry of Home Affairs; Respondent No.2 is Inspector-General of Police; Respondent No.3 is Commissioner, Dhaka Metropolitan Police; Respondent No.4 is Deputy Commissioner of Police, Ramna Zone, Dhaka Metropolitan Police; Respondent No.5 is Deputy Commissioner of Police, Detective Branch, North Zone, Office of Detective Branch; Respondent No.6 is Additional Deputy Police Commissioner, Ramna Zone, Dhaka Metropolitan Police; Respondent No.7 is the Officer-in-Charge, Ramna Police Station, Dhaka; Respondent No.8 is Officer-in-Charge, Paltan Police Station, Dhaka; and Respondent No.9 is the Officer-in-Charge, Shahbagh Police Station.

6. That the petitioners impugn in this Writ Petition the arbitrary and mala fide actions of the respondents executing through police officers under their control and supervision upon filing of fictitious criminal cases against the petitioners and other indefinite number of people who belong to different political groups other than the government, which is evident from different newspaper reportings including the Daily Star, Prothom Alo, Nayadiganta and Manab Zamin published on several dates in September 2018. The petitioners further pray for an order of direction upon the respondents to take appropriate legal actions against the officers who are involved in lodging of arbitrary, mala fide and fictitious cases.

7. That it transpires from the record maintained by BNP that in last 20 days (between 1-9-2018 and 20-9-20 I 8) as many as 3,736 cases have been filed against 3, 13, 130 known and unknown number of persons who belong to BNP and its alliances all over Bangladesh. Such cases are no doubt based on fictitious and concocted stories which have been filed by the respondents under their supervision having malicious intention to harass, detain and control the opposition activists ahead of the ensuing parliamentary election scheduled to be held on any date between October 2018 and 9th January 2019. The reports supporting the aforesaid statements of the petitioners, were published in the Daily Prothom Alo dated 5-9-2018 and 12-9-2018, and the Daily Naya Diganta dated 19-9-2018, amongst others. The said newspapers reporting and a report dated 20-9-2018 obtained from the office of BNP are annexed and marked as Annexure-A series to the application.

8. That it is stated that several newspaper reports also suggest that the police out of their blue designs have filed some cases against the leaders, activists, and supporters of BNP and its alliances, dead persons, persons having severe health conditions, persons admitted into intensive care unit of various hospitals and clinics, persons who had gone for performing Hajj and so on. For instance, (i) in the Daily Prothom Alo, a news report has been published with a caption "পুলিশের মামলায় আসামি মৃত ব্যক্তি ও প্রবাসীরা"; (ii) in Jagonews24.com, a news report has been published with a caption “মামলায় প্রধান আসামি মৃত ব্যক্তি”  (iii) in Daily Ittefaq, a news report has been published with a caption "খুলনায় পুলিশের মামলায় আসামি কৃত ব্যক্তি"; iv) in Daily Nayadiganta, a news report has been published with a caption "মৃত ব্যক্তি নাশকতা মামলার আসামি: রেহাই পাচ্ছেন না বিদেশে অবস্থানকারীরাও"; (v) in Daily Poriborton, a news report has been published with a caption "বিএনপির মৃত নেতার নামে ২ মামলা" (vi) In Daily Subarno Bhumi, a news report has been published with a caption “ঝিনাইদহে মৃত ব্যক্তিকে আসামি করলো পুলিশ”; (vii) in Daily Prothom Alo on 9-9-2018, a news report has been published with a caption "মৃত ব্যক্তিকেও ককটেল ছুড়তে দেখেছে পুলিশ"; (viii)in Daily Mana Zamin dated 10-9-2018, a news report has been published with a caption“মৃত ব্যক্তিকে আসামি করে পুলিশের মামলায় তোলপাড়; (ix) In Daily Jugantor dated 15-9-2018 and 19-9-2018, news reports have been published with captions "আজগুবি মামলায় ভুতুরে আসামি" and "আশুগঙ্জে গায়েবি মামলায় মৃত ব্যক্তিও আসামি”;   (x) in Daily lnquilab dated 20-9-2018, a news report has been published with a caption "হাজতী প্রবাসী ও মৃততা সরকার উৎখাতে জড়িত" The online printed copies of such reports are annexed and marked as Annexure- B series to the application.

9. That the petitioners have been subjected to victims of such malicious actions of the respondents inasmuch as as many as 7 cases have been filed against all of them in different police stations. The petitioners have obtained anticipatory bail from the High Court Division of the Supreme Court of Bangladesh in all the 7 cases, being Paltan PS Case No. 23 dated 11-9-2018, Paltan PS Case No. 25 dated 13-9-2018, Paltan PS Case No. 26 dated 13-9-2018, Paltan PS Case No. 31 dated 15-9-2018, Paltan PS Case No. 38 dated 17-9-2018, Paltan PS Case No. 38 dated 16-9-2018 and Mirpur Model PS Case No. 56 dated 16-9-2018. It appears from the FIR of all the 7 cases that the time, manner and articulation of the story are identical and any man of ordinary prudence can understand that all the FIRs are predesigned and those are made like a prescribed form and are used upon inserting some fictitious facts as and when required. Photocopies of the FIR of all the cases and bail granting orders are annexed and marked as Annexure-C series to the application.

10. That it is stated in the Supplementary-Affidavit that the news published in the following newspapers demonstrates the ex facie arbitrariness in exercising colourable exercise of power by the respondents and such exercise of Power is not only without any lawful authority but also hit the basic structure of the Constitution in general and Article 7 of the Constitution being democratic character of the State in particular. The news published in the news papers runs as follows:

(i) On 24-9-2018, The Daily Jugantor newspaper published that “বিএনপির নেতাকরমীদের বিরুদ্ধে গায়েবী মামলা, ভাবমুর্তি রক্ষায় পুলিশ সদর দপ্তর ।” It further published that (8) গত ৫ সেপ্টেম্বর রাজধানীর চকবাজার মডেল মামলায় আসামী করা হয়েছে চকবাজার থানা বিএনপির আহ্বায়ক আব্দুল আজিজ উল্লাহকে । অথচ আব্দুল আজিজ উল্লাহ মারা গেছেন ২০১৬ সালের মে মাসে। একই মামলায় আব্দুল মান্নান ওরফে টান মিয়াকে সৌদি আরবে হজ্ব করতে যান। (b) ৩ একইভাবে কামরীঙগীরচর থানা বিএনপির সাবেক সভাপতি নুরবল ইসলামকে আসামী করা হয়। অথচ তিনি ৩১ শে আগস্ট ইন্তেকাল করেন। (c)-১১ সেপ্টেম্বর পল্টন থানায় এসআই জাহিদুল ইসলাম বাদী হয়ে একটি মামলা করেন । ২৬ নম্বর আসামী করা হয়েছে মিন্টু কুমার দাসকে অথচ তিনি ১১ বছর আগেই মারা গিয়েছেন।”

(ii) The Daily Bangladesh Protidin published a report on 3-10-2018 making a caption that “লাখো মামলার জালে বিএনপি” আসামী ২৫ লাখেরও বেশী, সেপ্টেম্বরই ৪ হাজার মামলায় সাড়ে ৩ লাখ আসামী” গায়েবী মামলার রীট শুনানীর অপেক্ষায় ।

(iii) The Daily Star published a report on 3-10-2018 disclosing that “BNP IN THE RUN-UP TO POLLS, Case-spree hints at a rough ride.”

(iv) The Daily Prothom Alo published a report on 3-10-2018 by stating that“গায়েবী মামলা, ভাংচুর হওয়া গাড়ীর নম্বর জানে না পুলিশ।”

(v) The Daily Prothom Alo published a report on 2-10-2018 by stating that

(vi) The Daily Prothom Alo published a report on 1-10-2018 by stating that “ছিলেন বিদেশে, নাশকতা করেছেন নারায়নগঞ্জে” with further statement that “নারায়নগঞ্জ জেলা বিএনপির জ্যেষ্ঠ সহ-সভাপতি মোহাম্মদ শাহ আলম ৩১ শে আগস্ট থেকে যুক্তরাজ্যে আছেন চিকিৎসার জন্য কিন্তু ২৫ সেপ্টেম্বর ফতুল্লাহ থানার মামলায় আসামী করা হয়েছে । একই ভাবে ২৯ শে আগস্ট রূপগঞ্জ থানার এসআই আল তিনি চিকিৎসার জন্য ২৬ শে আগস্ট থাইল্যান্ডে যান। ২ সেপ্টেম্বর দেশে ফিরে আসেন। একই ভাবে নাসিরউদ্দিন ২৬ জুলাই হজ্ব করতে সৌদি আরব যান ২৯ শে সেপ্টেম্বর দেশে আসেন । তিনিও ২৯ আগস্টের মামলার আসামী । ”

11 . That is stated that it is now well known to all concerned at home and abroad that the government and Bangladesh Awami League have prepared a blue design to retain their power through another farcical election and the summary of the said blue design can be presumed form their recent actions, which may be articulated in the following terms:

A. To keep the BNP Chairperson in Jail until the election is over under any circumstances;

B. To convict the BNP acting Chairperson in 21 August case to demoralize the BNP supporters and to malign and defame them internationally;

C. In addition to the above two tasks, they are also preparing to deceive the local society to show that they are ready to hold a moderately free election. But under the veil, they have asked the puppet police to make sure that the grassroots of BNP and its alliances are fragile through the bundles of cases against them and to cause delay in obtaining bail in mechanical manners;

D. In order to execute plan 3 above, the police administration has been given verbal instructions to file several cases against the leaders and workers of BNP and its alliances in every constituency and accordingly, all the active members in poling centre wise are made accused in order to prevent them from being available for election campaign and selection of poling agents;

E. As part of the assignment mentioned in plan 4 above, fictitious cases like sedition, arms, ammunition, conspiracy etc, are being filed even where no iota of incidents was found to have occurred;

F. There is also verbal instruction upon the judicial magistrates not to grant bail in these types of cases though they are fully authorized to grant bail and, as such, once someone is arrested, it takes around 3-4 months to get bail after completing higher judicial process. Thus, if any political activist is arrested now in such fictitious cases, he will not get bail at least before January 2019, that is, he will only get bail after the elections;

G. Police is receiving bribes from the activists of BNP and its allies under coercion and threat of custodial, extrajudicial killing and forced disappearances;

H. The intellectuals/civil society members have been kept under threat of Section 57 of the ICT Act, 2006 so that they cannot express their opinion;

I. To make the activists of BNP and its alliances, their family members and supporters financially crippled so that they cannot spend money during movements/election;

J. To purchase lobbyists by spending their looted money to pacify the western world; and

K. If peaceful movement/demonstration/procession is organized by BNP, Sheikh Hasina's public and private cadres will burn vehicles and kill people and will shift the liability upon BNP and its alliances.

38. Being aggrieved and dissatisfied with the impugned actions, the petitioners have approached this court with this application under Article 102 of the Constitution of the people's Republic of Bangladesh.

39. At the very outside, Mr Khandker Mahbub Hossain, the learned Advocate appearing in person before this court, submits that the arbitrary and malafide actions of the respondents by way of filing fictitious criminal cases against the petitioners and indefinite number of other people who belong to different political groups other than the government are being done in the furtherance of a blue design in order to continue in power through another farcical election without any hindrance from any quarter and, as such, the impugned actions of the respondents are liable to be declared to have been made without any lawful authority and are of no legal effect and the respondents are required to be directed to take appropriate legal actions against the officers who are involved in the said arbitrary and mala fide lodging of cases against the petitioners.

40. He next submits that the recent actions of the respondents treating the activists of BNP, its allies and critics of Government are ex-facie discriminatory with the people who belong to the government shadow and such actions of the respondents suppressing the opposition activists upon lodging cases against them, restricting their movement, freedom of speech, freedom of conscience, freedom of association, are nothing but a violation of Articles 27, 31, 33, 35, 36, 37, 38, and 39 of the Constitution and, as such, the impugned actions of respondents are liable to be declared to have been made without any lawful authority and are of no legal effect and the respondents are required to be directed to take appropriate legal actions against the officers who are involved in the said arbitrary and mala fide lodging of cases against the petitioners.

41. He then submits that the purported cases filed against the petitioners and indefinite number of people have been done upon misusing the provision of section 154 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898 having arbitrary and mala fide intention to keep them away from the election process or to do certain election engineering under the blue design of the government, which are liable to be declared to have done without any lawful authority and are of no legal effect.

42. He candidly submits that the actions of the respondents suffers from gross malice in fact and malice in law as has been settled in the case of Dr. Nurul Islam vs Bangladesh reported in 33 DLR (AD) 201, inasmuch as the impugned actions of the respondents taken against the petitioners demonstrate and wrongful act done intentionally without just cause and the facts and circumstances of the issues constitute malice in law inasmuch as the wrongful act done intentionally, without just cause or excuse in total disregard of the principle of the rule of law, fundamental rights and ratio settled in different cases by our apex court including the case of Bangladesh vs BLAST, reported in 69 DLR (AD) 63 and, as such„ the impugned actions of the respondents are liable to be declared to have been made without any lawful authority and are of no legal effect and the respondents are required to take appropriate legal actions against the officers who are involved in the said arbitrary and mala fide lodging of cases against the petitioners.

43. He lastly submits that in the given facts and circumstances, it has become a Frankenstein of the law enforcement agencies not only to abuse its power violating the fundamental rights of the citizens but also to undermine and disregard the guidelines given by the Appellate Division of the Supreme Court of Bangladesh in the case of Bangladesh vs BLAST, reported in 69 DLR (AD) 63 and if this is allowed to be continued, the basic structure of the Constitution, being the supremacy of the constitution, independence of judiciary in general and Article 111 of the Constitution in particular may be undermined and thus the democracy, rule of law, and independence of judiciary will be allowed to be violated and, as such„ the impugned actions of the respondents are liable to be declared to have been made without any lawful authority and are of no legal effect and the respondents are required to be directed to take appropriate legal actions against the officers, who are involved in the said arbitrary and mala fide lodging of cases against the petitioners.

44. On the other hand, Mr Mahbubey Alam, the learned Attorney-General, appearing on behalf of the respondents, very vigorously opposes the prayers of the petitioners and categorically submits that when Begum Khaleda Zia, the Chairperson of BNP was convicted and sentenced in Zia Orphanage Case, the petitioners and other supporters and activists of BNP made serious agitation and demonstration in the different roads of Dhaka City and as a part of it, they charged bombs and cocktails on the police as a result of which different volatile and chaotic incidents were happened during the period from 11-9-2018 to 16-9-2018 in order to free Begum Khaleda Zia from jail and during the protest, the police discharged their duties and tried to save the life and liberties of the citizen of country and to protect the government properties from the hands of unruly activists and supporters of BNP but the unruly supporters and activists of BNP and its alliances mercilessly assaulted and wounded the police personnel and thereby the police were compelled to lodge cases against the present petitioners and others with different police stations.

45. He next submits that the present petitioners are the accused of different police station cases and they are also senior leaders of BNP and, as such, it is crystal clear that they are very interested persons in this matter and in that count, this writ petition cannot be treated as public interest litigation and in that view of the matter, this writ petition is not maintainable in the eye of law.

46. He then submits that since there are specific cases against the petitioners disclosing offences against them, the falsehood and/or truthfulness of the allegations can only be looked into by the investigating officers and also by the learned trial judge at the time of framing charge and if there is any illegality or irregularity in the prosecution case or in the proceeding, that can be challenged before the competent criminal court invoking its jurisdiction under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure but the actions and/ or cases lodged against the petitioners cannot be challenged before this Court invoking its writ jurisdiction since there are efficacious alternative remedies in the Code of Criminal Procedure and considering that aspect of the case, this writ petition is not maintainable and the same should be rejected summarily.

47. He lastly submits that there is no bar to challenge the criminal proceedings under a writ jurisdiction but in that case, the petitioners have to challenge the concerned law to declare it ultra vires but in the instant case, no law has been challenged and in that view of the matter, the legal decisions referred to by the petitioners are not applicable to the present writ petition and in that view of the matter, this writ petition is not maintainable.

<u>48. I have gone through the applications filed by the petitioners under Article 102 of the Constitution and the materials annexed thereto. I have also considered the submissions made by the learned Advocates for the petitioners and the learned Attorney-General for Bangladesh. I have also considered their submissions to the best of my wit and wisdom. From the writ petition, it is noticeable that the petitioners have challenged the arbitrary and mala fide actions of the respondents committed through police officers under their control and supervision upon filing of fictitious criminal cases against the petitioners and others and they have also prayed for direction upon the respondents to take appropriate legal actions against the officers who are involved in lodging of arbitrary, mala fide and fictitious cases against the petitioners and others. From the cause title and the prayer portion of the writ petition, it is clear that the petitioners have basically challenged the criminal cases filed against the petitioners and others under writ jurisdiction. The actions of police officers and the respondents are meant for criminal cases filed against the petitioners and others. It appears from the record that the petitioners are the accused of some cases of Paltan Model Police station and Mirpur Model Police station. It is evident from the record that the facts of some cases were published in different newspapers. On going through the FIR, it appears that some specific facts and offences narrating the chaotic situation in different roads of Dhaka City have been disclosed in those FIR. It may be stated that the facts and offences disclosed in the FIR are highly contentious and disputed question of fact. The truthfulness or falsehood of the allegations can be looked into by the investigating officers and the learned judges of the Court below at the time of framing charge and after recording evidence from the respective parties. The truthfulness and/or falsehood of the allegations cannot be decided in writ jurisdiction. If there is any illegality or irregularity in the cases, that can be addressed under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure if so challenged by the aggrieved person/s. Under the aforesaid facts and circumstances, this writ petition is not maintainable in the eye of law. In the case of Samsunnahar Salam vs Mohammad Ohidur Rahman, reported in 51 DLR (AD) 232, it was held that:</u>

<u>"A writ Court cannot and should not decide any disputed question of fact which required evidence to be taken for settlement."</u>

49. In the case of TaeHung Packaging (BD) Ltd. vs Bangladesh reported in 18 BLC (AD) 2013 144, it was decided that:

"Even in presence of alternative remedy, the High Court Division can invoke the power of writ jurisdiction if the aggrieved person challenges the vires of a statute which requires interpretation of such statute."

50. It was further explicated in that decision that:

"The Court normally does not interfere with the investigation of a case where the offence has been disclosed in the FIR or complaint. The tendency of interference at the stage of investigation of a case is now on the rise which has not happened earlier even though it has repeatedly been pointed out that such assumption is not correct. The Courts should be weary of its possible consequence."

51. In the case of ACC vs Mehedi Hasan reported in 67 DLR (AD) 137, it was construed that:

"There is no scope for quashing a criminal proceeding under the writ-jurisdiction unless the vires of the law involved is challenged. The vires of the law involved in the case has not been challenged. Therefore, there is no scope for aggrandizement of jurisdiction of the High Court Division in quashing a criminal proceeding. Consequently, the High Court Division was not justified in quashing criminal cases in exercise of its power under Article 102 of the Constitution."

52. In the case of Begum Khaleda Zia vs Anti-Corruption Commission reported in 69 DLR (AD) 181, it was decided that:

"There is no scope for quashing a criminal proceeding under the writ jurisdiction unless the vires of the law involved is challenged. There is no scope for aggrandizement of jurisdiction of the High Court Division in quashing a criminal proceeding."

53. In the case of ACC vs Enayetur Rahman reported in 64 DLR (AD) 14, it was laid down that:

"This Court on repeated occasions argued that Article 102(2) of the Constitution is not meant to circumvent the statutory procedures. The High Court Division will not allow a litigant to invoke the extraordinary jurisdiction to be converted into Courts of appeal or revision. It is only where statutory remedies are entirely ill suited to meet the demands of extraordinary situations that is to say where vires of a statute is in question or where the determination is mala fide or where any action is taken by the executives in contravention of principles of natural justice or where the fundamental right of a citizen has been affected by an act or where the statute is intra vires but the action taken is without jurisdiction and the vindication of public justice require that recourse may be had to Article 102(2) of the Constitution."

54. In the case of ACC vs Shahidul Islam reported in 68 DLR (AD) 242, it was held that: "Challenging the proceedings of special cases, writ petition are not maintainable inasmuch as Code of Criminal Procedure provides efficacious remedy to get redress if one feels himself aggrieved due to initiation of such criminal proceedings."

55. In the case of Begum Khaleda Zia vs ACC, reported in 70 DLR (AD) 50, it was decided that:

"Where a person has an equally efficacious remedy, the High Court Division would not interfere with criminal proceeding in exercising extraordinary jurisdiction. Such powers are to be exercised in rare and exceptional cases."

56. It was further formulated in the aforesaid case that:

"Existence of alternative remedy is not an absolute bar to entertain writ petition by the High Court Division but to declare a criminal proceeding illegal, it is to be established that the Court acted without jurisdiction or the vires of the law is in question."

<u>57. It is evident from the FIR that the petitioners are the senior leaders of BNP and at the same time, they are made accused in different cases. So I have no hesitation to say that the petitioners are very interested persons in this writ petition and they have not come before this Court with clean hands. In view of the above, this writ petition cannot be considered as public interest litigation. 58. In this regard, the decision taken in the case of Dattaraj Nathuji Thaware vs State of Maharashtra, (2005) 1 SCC 590, 592-93 may be given as reference wherein it was spelt out that:</u>

<u>"A person acting bona fide and having sufficient interest in the proceeding of public interest litigation will alone have a locus standi and can approach the Court to wipe out violation of fundamental rights and genuine infraction of statutory provisions but not for personal gain or private profit or political motive or any oblique consideration."</u>

59. It was further decided in that case that:

"A writ petitioner who comes to the Court for relief in public interest must come not only with clean hands like any other writ petitioner but also with a clear heart, clean mind and clean objective."

<u>60. It is stated in the application that some cases have been filed against the dead person and the persons who were in abroad at the time of incidents and the very facts have been published in different newspapers. Basing on the aforesaid news, the petitioners have approached this Court challenging the actions of cases taken against them. It has been decided in a series of case laws that the disputed question of facts can be decided in writ jurisdiction. It is now well settled that newspaper reports cannot be admitted into evidence unless the correspondent of such a report comes to the witness box to vouchsafe in support of the report on oath. The aforesaid view finds support in the decision in the case of Osena Begum alias Babuler Ma vs State, reported in 55 DLR 299.</u>

61. I have also gone through the legal decisions referred to by the petitioners. The facts of those cases are quite different and distinguishable from the facts and circumstances of the present case and do not match with the facts of the present case. Accordingly, those decisions are not applicable to the matter at hand. The petitioners could not produce a single case law which is apparently applicable to the facts and circumstances of the present case at hand.

62. Having considered all the facts and circumstances of the case, the submissions of the respective parties, the propositions of law and the discussions made above, I do not find any merit in this application and accordingly, I am at one with the views and opinion of Mr Justice Md Ashraful Kamal.

63. In consequence thereof, this application under Article 102 filed by the petitioners is summarily rejected.

Let a copy of this judgment and order be communicated to the concerned respondents at once.

End.

full_judgment:
Fatema Najib J: This appeal is directed against the judgment and decree dated 24-11-2014 passed by learned Joint District Judge, First Court, Narayangonj in Title Suit No. 18 of 2011 dismissing the suit.

2. The appellants as plaintiffs instituted Title Suit No. 18 of 2011 against the respondents as defendants for declaration of title in respect of suit land and further declaration that the compromise decree passed by learned Joint District Judge, First Court, Narayangonj in Title Suit No. 331 of 2009 is illegal, collusive, void, and not binding upon the plaintiffs.

3. During pendency of appeal the appellant No. 9 died on 14-8-2016 and his legal heirs has been duly substituted by order of this court dated 14-12-2016.

4. The case of the plaintiffs, in short, is that the suit land of CS plot No. 1827 measuring 50 decimals along with other lands was originally belonged to Nizamuddin and accordingly CS Khatian No. 142 was recorded in his name. Nizamuddin transferred the suit land by registered Mortgage Deed being No. 5146 on 29-8-1925 to one Wahed Ali. An amicable partition was made among the brothers of Wahed Ali in respect of suit land along with other undisputed lands and through an amicable partition Durjon, brother of Wahed Ali got the suit land. Durjan died leaving behind two sons namely, Jinnat Ali and Habibullah who later on sold the suit land to one Alim Mia son of Jonab Ali by registered Kabala No. 1836 dated 18-1-1956 and delivered possession to him, accordingly RS khatian No. 322 was prepared in the name of Mid alias Alimuddin. Alim Mia transferred the entire suit land by registered hebanama being No. 2582 on 14-6-1987 in favour of his wife Rabeya Khatoon, three sons—Sirajul, Samsul Hoq, Md Ramjan Hossain and four daughters—Hasenur Begum, Fatema Khatoon, Halima Khatoon and Shaheena Begum. In this way Rabeya and Ramjan got 15 decimals and 10 decimals of the suit land respectively. In the same way Hasenur, Fatema Khatoon, Halima Khatoon got together 11.15 decimals and Shaheena Begum got 13.75 decimals of land in the suit land. Subsequently Rabeya, Ramjan, Hasenur, Fatema Khatoon, Halima Khatoon mutated their names by declaration Deed No. 1148 dated 25-5-1993 and paid rents to the Government. Halima Khatoon sold her portion i.e 3 decimals of the suit land to one Abdul Ali by registered kabala being No. 3908 on 7-9-1995. Mst Shaheena Begum extinguished her share from the suit land by selling her portion to plaintiff No. 1, 2 and 3 through three registered Kabala Nos. 2669, 2670, 2671 all dated 18-7-1999 in equal share. Abdul Ali, who purchased the suit land from Halima sold his entire portion to plaintiff Nos. 1-3 by registered kabala No. 1031 on 1-4-2001. In this way the plaintiff No. 1-2 got 6 decimal each and plaintiff No. 3 got 51/4 decimals of land. Fatema Khatoon daughter of Alimuddin sold her entire share of suit land to Mafizul Islam, plaintiff No. 4 by saf-kabala on 12-9-1999. Ramjan (defendant No. 15) who got from his father Alimuddin by way of heba sold 3 decimals to plaintiff No.5 on 26-5-1999. Most. Rabeya, who got 15 decimals of land from her husband sold to the plaintiff Nos. 6-9 through three Kabalas on 23-6-1999. Hasenur Begum, who also got by heba sold it to one Habibullah and thereafter Habibullah sold it to the plaintiff No. 10 through Kabala No. 6568 on 9-12-2007. Ramjan (defendant No.15) and Halima Khatoon sold their remaining portion of land to the plaintiff No.11. Thus the plaintiffs have been possessing the entire suit land by mutating, paying rents, planting crops and taking loan from bank by mortgaging the suit land. The defendants were trying to demolish the boundary, then the plaintiffs filed the petition case No. 639 dated 1-12-2010. Thereafter the defendants were trying to disposes the plaintiffs and on 1-8-2010 the defendants disclosed that they got title over the suit land on the basis of the decree passed in Title Suit No. 331 of 2009, wherein the defendant Nos. 1-12 of the present suit as plaintiffs filed said Title Suit No. 331 of 2009 impleading the present defendant Nos. 4-7 and 13-15 as defendants.

5. The defendant Nos. 1-6 and 8-11 con-tested the suit by filing a joint written statement. They denied material averments made in the plaint. The case of the defendants are that the suit land was originally belonged to Nizamuddin who died leaving behind two sons namely, Jonab Ali and Kamfu Mia. Janab Ali died leaving behind four sons namely, Alim Ali, Ayet Ali, Ameer Ali and Jamir All and two daughters namely, Topi Bibi, Aleshi Bibi. SA Khatian 321 was prepared in the name of Kamfu Mia and the aforesaid heirs of Jonab Ali. While in possession of 50% share i.e 25 decimals of suit land, Kamfu Mia died leaving behind wife Aimon Bibi and only son Hossain Mia. After death of Aimon bibi, Hossain ali got the share of Kamfu Mia and possessed the southern 25 decimals of the suit land. Hossain Ali died leaving behind six sons defendant Nos. 1-6 and one daughter defendant No. 11. Elachi bibi, daughter of Jonab Ali died leaving behind 4 brothers-Ameer Ali, Alim Ali, Ayet Ali, Jamir Ali and one sister Tohi Bibi. Ameer Ali died leaving behind 2 sons namely, Anwar Hossain, Amjad Hossain and one daughter Sahnaj i.e defendant Nos: 8-10. Thus defendant Nos. 1-6 and 8-10 along with defendant No. 11 have been possessing 31decimals of land together with another piece of land by planting crops. The defendant Nos. 1-6 and 8-10 executed power of attorney infavour of defendant No. 11 and 12 on 8-10-09 to look after the land and to deal with the suits. The defendants 1-6, 8-10 and 11 went to Tohsil Office to mutate their names and knew about wrong recording of RS Khatian in plaintiffs names. Thereafter the aforesaid defendants filed a Miscellaneous Case No. 420 of 2010 in which their names has been mutated and accordingly they paid tax, rent etc. The further case of the defendants is that Nizamuddin took loan 200 from one Wahed Ali subject to payment of 2% interest per month and accordingly a registered deed was executed between them on 29-8-1925. Subsequently, Nizamuddin paid the entire loan money to Wahid Ali and SA record was correctly prepared in the name of the heirs of Nizamuddin. Thus all the successive transfers were made on the basis of the said deed dated 29-8-1925 are illegal, inoperative and not binding upon the defendants.

6. The Trial Court had framed the issues in the following manner:—

১।অত্র মোকদ্দমা বর্তমান আকারে ও প্রকারে সচল কিনা?

বাদীপক্ষের প্রাইমাফেসি টাইটেল আছে কিনা?

৩।বাদীপক্ষের অপূরণীয় ক্ষতির সম্ভাবনা আছে কিনা?

৪।সুবিধা অসুবিধা ভারসাম্য বাদীপক্ষের অনুকূলে আছে কিনা।

৫।বাদীপক্ষ প্রার্থনা মোতাবেক ডিক্রী পাইতে পারে কিনা?

7. In the suit, the plaintiffs examined 6(six) PWs including the plaintiff No. 1 as PW 1. The defendants in support of their case examined 2 DWs including defendant No. 11 as DW 1. Documents filed by the plaintiffs were marked as Exhibits 1-9 and the documents filed by the defendants were marked as Exhibits-ka-um (series). The learned Joint District Judge, after considering the oral and documentary evidence dismissed the suit.

8. Being aggrieved by the aforesaid judgment and decree, the plaintiffs preferred this appeal.

9. Ms Nahid Yesmin, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the plaintiffs-appellants primarily submits that the court below erroneously held that Deed No. 5146 dated 28-8-1925 (Exhibit-8(4) executed by Nizamuddin is not a mortgage deed but “জোত জমি বিক্রয় সুদি রেহানী” which effects or purports to effect the sale and said transaction cannot be treated as Mortgage as per section 58 of the Transfer of Property Act. She further submits that the learned Joint District Judge below failed to consider the oral and documentary evidence by which the plaintiffs were successfully proved their title and possession over the suit land. She finally argued further that the learned court below has committed gross illegality in not considering the stipulation made in the Deed in question that Nizamuddin sold the suit land, not mortgage the same to Wahid Ali.

10. Today 31-10-2018 this appeal was fixed for delivery of judgment. Learned Advocate for the plaintiffs-Appellants with permission of the court further argued on some issues. She departed from her earlier argument that the deed in question dated 25-8-1925 is not a Deed of sale, but Mortgage by conditional sale. She argued that though there was no condition of sale embodied in the said deed but intention to sale exists there which deals with mortgage by conditional sale. She also argued that one Alim Mia, legal heirs of Nizamuddin sold the suit land to the legal heirs of Wahed Ali which clearly proved that by the said Deed the heirs of Wahid Ali became owner of the suit land. In support of her submissions, she referred decisions reported in AIR Nagpur 264 and 44 DLR (AD) 83.

11. Mr Md Delowar Hossain, the learned senior Advocate appearing for defendants respondents submits that the deed in question is a mortgage deed which purports to create a simple mortgage as the conditions mentioned in section 58(b) of the Transfer of Property Act. He submits further that no stipulation has been contained in the aforesaid deed that the mortgagor Nizamuddin delivered possession of the suit property to mortgagee, Wahid Ali. It was further stipulated that mortgagor took loan Taka 200 from the mortgagee subject to payment of 2% interest per month and the same loan will be returned to the mortgagee within Chaitra 1332 BS. It was also stipulated that in case of failure to pay the loan money, the mortgagee shall have right to get the property with intervention of the court. He next submits that the plaintiffs have miserably failed to produce any oral and documentary evidence to prove their title and possession of the suit land. He also submits that since the plaintiffs failed to prove by oral or documentary that the mortgagor Nizamuddin failed to pay loan with interest and the mortgagee got the suit land in auction through court, rather it was evident that SA Khatian was prepared in the name of legal heirs of Nizamuddin which clearly proved the title and possession of Nizamuddin predecessors of the defendants in the suit land. He further submits that the schedule of the present suit and the schedule of the earlier Title Suit No. 331 of 2009 are same and all the defendants were made parties either as plaintiffs or defendants in both the suits. The suit land on which the plaintiff claimed their title but their predecessors Wahed Ali did not acquire any title and possession. He finally submits that the court below has not committed error of law and facts and rightly found that the deed in question neither a Sale Deed nor a Deed of Mortgage by conditional sale.

12. We have heard the submissions and counter submissions of the learned Advocate of the contesting parties. Perused the oral and documentary evidence, relevant provisions of law and also citations referred by the parties.

13. From plain reading of the pleadings, documents produced and oral evidence adduced before court, it is admitted that the suit land measuring 50 decimals of land was originally belonged to Nizamuddin predecessors of the defendants, who executed a registered mortgage deed dated 29-8-1925 in favour of one Wahed Ali, Predecessors of the plaintiffs in respect of suit land by taking Taka 200 as loan subject to payment of interest @ 2% pin till realization of money. There was a clear stipulation for payment of interest on repayment of loan amount and in case of failure to repayment within specified time, 30th Chaitra, the mortgagee shall have a right to cause the mortgaged property to be sold with intervention of the court.

14. It is contented by the plaintiffs that Nizamuddin could not pay the money taken as loan from Wahed Ali and thus Wahed Ali became the owner of the suit land. Thereafter, an amicable partition was made among the brothers of Wahed Ali in respect of suit land along with other lands. Durjon, the brother of Wahed Ali got the suit land by dint of amicable partition, subsequently the legal heirs of Durjon transferred the entire suit land to different persons on different dates. Ultimately, the plaintiffs got the entire suit land by successive transfers.

15. On the other hand, the defendants contended that Nizamuddin paid entire loan money taken from Wahed Ali. After the death of Nizamuddin, his two sons Kamfu Mia and Jonab Ali inherited the suit land and thereafter the defendants as their legal heirs got the suit land.

16. The core issue in this appeal is that whether the Deed No. 5146 dated 29-8-1925 (Exhibit-8/4) the basic document upon which the plaintiffs based their title is a Simple Mortgage or Mortgage by conditional sale.

17. To determine this question, we like to quote the relevant portion of the Mortgage Deed which reads as under:

“এইক্ষণ আমার টাকার প্রয়োজন বশত আপনার নিকট হইতে নগদ মং ২০০ টাকা কর্জ্জ গ্রহণ করিয়া অঙ্গীকার করিতেছি যে উক্ত টাকার সুদ শতকরা মাসিক ২ টাকা হিসাবে দিব ৫ ফর্দে বর্তমান সনের মাহে চৈত্র ময় সুদ আসল টাকা পরিশোধ করিব অন্যথায় টাকা আদায়ের শেষ তারিখ পর্যন্ত | উপরোক্ত হারে সুদ দিব। উক্ত সুদসহ সম্যক টাকা  আদায়ের সাফ করিতে আমার স্বত্ব দখলীর নিন | তফসীলের লিখিত অসহাই জমার রায়তি জোত স্বত্বের নাল জমি অত্র রেহানে আবদ্ধ রাখিলাম। উক্ত টাকা  আদায় না হওয়া পর্যন্ত এ সম্পত্তি অন্যত্র রেহান দান বিক্রয় মালিকানা ইস্তফা ইত্যাদি রেহানী স্বত্বের হানি জনক কোন কার্যা করি নাই । অথবা করিতে পারিব না।

করিলে আদালত অগ্রাহ্য হইবে । আর আপনার টাকা  আদায় না করিলে যথা সময়ে আদালতে নালিশ নিলাম লইতে পারিবেন।”

It appears from the recital of the document that:

i) the existence of debt,

ii) the period of repayment open ended i.e. long period,

iii) possession was not handed over,

iv) a stipulation for interest on repayment,

v) default of payment will be realized by selling the mortgaged property through auction by court of law.

<u>18. In order to appreciate the submissions advanced by the learned Advocates, Now we can look into the definition of Mortgage which is dealt in section 58 of The Transfer Property Act.</u>

<u>Section 58. "Mortgage", "mortgagor", "mortgagee", "mortgagemoney" and "mortgagedeed" defined. (a) A mortgage is the transfer of an interest in specific immovable property for the purpose of securing the payment of money advanced or to be advanced by way of loan, an existing or future debt, or the performance of an engagement which may give rise to a pecuniary liability.</u>

<u>19. The transferor is called a mortgagor, the transferee a mortgagee; the principal money and interest of which payment is secured for the time being are called the mortgage-money, and the instrument (if any) by which the transfer is effected is called a mortgage-deed.</u>

<u>20. There are 6 kinds of mortgage. Those are, Simple Mortgage, Mortgage by conditional sale, Usufructuary mortgage, English mortgage, Mortgage by deposit of title deeds and Anomalous mortgage.</u>

<u>21. As regards the nature of the deed in question raised by the parties, we like to refer only those mortgage which are necessary for proper adjudication of the present case.</u>

<u>Simple mortgage-58—(b) Where, without delivering possession of the mortgaged property, the mortgagor binds himself personally to pay the mortgage-money, and agrees, expressly or impliedly, that, in the event of his failing to pay according to his contract, the mortgagee shall have a right to cause the mortgaged property to be sold and the proceeds of sale to be applied, so far as may be necessary, in payment of the mortgage-money, the transaction is called a simple mortgage and the mortgagee a simple mortgagee."</u>

22. From the definition of Simple mortgage the following elements are found:

1. Without delivery of possession.

2. The existence of debt.

3. The period of repayment.

4. of mortgaged money, mortgaged property to be sold.

5. No actual transfer of interest or confer express power of sale.

Mortgage by conditional sale—(c) Where the mortgagor ostensibly sells the mortgaged property—

On condition that on default of payment of the mortgage-money on a certain date the sale shall become absolute, or

On condition that on such payment being made the sale shall become void, or On condition that on such payment being made the buyer shall transfer the property to the seller.

The transaction is called a mortgage by conditional sale and the mortgagee a mortgagee by conditional sale:

Provided that no such transaction shall be deemed to be a mortgage, unless the condition is embodied in the document which effects or purports to effect the sale;

The learned Advocate for the plaintiffs-appellants by referring section 58(c) of Transfer of Property Act, vehemently argued that the Mortgage Deed in question (Exhibit-8/4) is in fact Mortgage by conditional sale.

23. We have perused the Mortgage Deed (Exhibit-8/4). It is clear from its recital of the deed that in case of default by the Mortgagor to pay mortgaged money, the mortgagee will have to go to court of law with a prayer for sale. That means in the eventuality the mortgaged property to be sold in auction, for payment of the mortgaged money.

24. Further recital of the deed regarding nonpayment is so clear that it cannot be interpreted in any way. Moreover, Mortgaged property was not delivered to the Mortgagor. We have carefully examined the substance of the Mortgaged Deed and find that it was a Simple mortgage and not a Mortgage by conditional sale as agitated by the learned counsel for the plaintiffs-appellants. Thus the present mortgage is not hit by the provision of section 58(c) of the Transfer of Property Act which deals with the definition of a mortgage by conditional Sale; there must be a condition that in default of payment of the mortgage money on a certain date the sale shall become absolute. But such condition is not in the embodied in the Mortgage Deed (Exhibit-8(4). It is an inviolable rule that in considering the question whether a transaction is a sale or a mortgage the court should look at the substance of deed not the form. The trial court rightly found that the Deed (Exhibit-8(4) is a simple Mortgage Deed.

25. The plaintiffs could not produce any documents which testify that the matter was interfered by any court of law or there have been auction sale by which the predecessor of the plaintiffs became the owner of the suit land.

26. The plaintiffs claimed that by successive transfers they became owner of the suit land. Since we have already observed that the predecessor of the plaintiffs, Wahed Ali did not become owner of the suit land in the first place, the subsequent transfers based on the transfers by dint of deed dated 19-8-1925 needs no discussion. It is hereby mentioned that the learned Advocate argued that Alim Mia grandson of Nizamuddin purchased the entire portion of suit land from Jinnat Ali, Habibulla, son of Durjon Ali, brother of Wahed Ali. Learned Advocate for the appellants tried to submit that since Wahed Ali became the owner of the suit land and his brother Durjon who also got it by amicable partition and then his heirs sold it to Alim Mia, son of Jonab Ali. But upon examining the photocopy of the deed No. 836 dated 18-1-1956 (Exhibit-9), it looks like a mortgage deed, not a sale deed. Md Osman Gani copyist, Sadar record room, District Registered office, Narayangonj as PW 5 deposed before court. He carried the volume wherein the description of the said deed was mentioned. He compared the description of the certified copy of the said deed with the volume and found similar. But the deed filed is not certified copy, it is a photocopy of the original. In his cross-examinations he has stated that he has no knowledge about the transaction and also did not know who are transferor and transferee. The said deed was not proved in accordance of law. So, we did not find merit in the argument made by the learned Advocate of the plaintiffs.

27. In the present suit the plaintiffs filed SA khatian (Exhibit-1/1) to prove their possession in the suit land. It appears that the said khatian was prepared in the name of Kamfu, and the heirs of Jonab Ali, who are sons of Nizamuddin which clearly proved the possession of the predecessor of the defendants and not the plaintiffs. It further proved that the original owner Nizamuddin never lost his title by executing the mortgage deed in favour of Wahed Ali.

28. Apart from the Exhibit-1/1, the plaintiffs to prove their possession examined one Md Abbas Ali, uncle of the plaintiff No. 2 as PW 2, who in his cross examination could not say the boundary of the suit land. Mr Sirazul Islam PW 3 and Md Delwar Hossain PW 4 in their cross-examination could not say the number of the plaintiffs, the plaintiffs quantam of land purchased by them. So, from the scrutiny the oral evidences it proved that no witnesses could say the quantum of the lands purchased by each plaintiffs and also the boundary of lands which do not prove the possession of the plaintiffs over the suit land. We have perused the Mutation Khatian, DCR, dhakilas land development tax (Exhibit-4 series) has been filed by the plaintiffs. Dhakhila, DCR, land development tax has been filed on the basis of Mutation Khatian Nos. 4632 (Exhibit-415), 16139 (Exhibit-4/7), 4690 (Exhibit-4/11). Those mutation Khatian were prepared on the basis of RS Khatian No. 322 (Exhibit-1/2). But the defendants have filed a Title Suit No. 331 of 2009 challenging that RS Khatian No. 322 was wrong. The said suit was decreed by the judgment and decree dated 1-8-2010 (Exhibit-5). On the basis of the said decree a Miscellaneous Case No. 420 of 10 Exhibit-uma(1) was initiated. In that Miscellaneous Case, Revenue Officer cancelled the Mutation Khatian prepared in the name of the plaintiffs and directed to mutate the names of the defendants in place of the plaintiffs. Against this order no step has been taken, by the plaintiff. Thus the defendants were successfully proved their possession in the suit land by filing Exhibit-uma(1).

29. The plaintiffs-appellants also prayed for declaration that the judgment and decree dated 1-8-2010 passed by learned Joint District Judge First Court in Title Suit No. 33J of 2009 is illegal collusive, void and not binding upon the plaintiffs. Perused the said judgment (Exhibit-5). It appears that the suit lands of previous suit and the suit land of the present suit are similar. All the defendants were made parties to previous suit either as plaintiffs or defendants. But the present plaintiffs were not made parties of in the previous suit.

30. We have already held that Wahed All did not acquire any title on the basis of the alleged mortgage deed and, as such, his legal heirs has no transferable interest to execute the deeds in favour of different people on different dates in respect of the suit land. We have also found that the plaintiffs have failed to prove the deeds in accordance of law and their possession in the suit land on the basis thereof. Thus the learned Sub-ordinate Judge did not commit any error or illegality in dismissing the suit. The learned Sub-ordinate Judge, of course, did not consider the prayer made by the plaintiffs as regards declaration that the decree passed in Title Suit No. 331 of 2009 is collusive, void and not binding upon the plaintiffs. Since we have found that the plaintiffs have failed to prove their title and possession over the suit land as such the plaintiffs have no locus-standi to challenge the decree obtained by the defendants in Title Suit No. 331 of 2009.

31. The learned Advocate for the Appellants has cited two decisions reported in 44 DLR (AD) 84 and AIR (Nagpur) 264. We have carefully gone through the decisions but facts and circumstances of those cited decisions have no manner and application in the facts and circumstance of the present case and it will not help any way to the appellants.

32. In the result, the appeal is dismissed without any order as to cost. The judgment and decree dated 24-11-2014 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, First Court Narayangonj in Title Suit No. 18 of 2011 is affirmed. The connected rule being Civil Rule No. 45(F) 2015 is discharged and the order of status-quo granted at the time of admission of the appeal is hereby vacated.

Send down the lower court records along with a copy of this judgment at once.

End.
