case_source: (From the judgment and order dated 07.01.2010, passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 1034 of 1998)
full_judgment:
Mirza Hussain Haider J. This Civil Appeal, by leave, is directed against the judgment and order dated 07.01.2010, passed by a Single Bench of the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 1034 of 1998, discharging the Rule and thereby affirming the judgment and decree dated 1.7.1997 passed by the learned District Judge, Gopalgonj, in Title Appeal No. 92 of 1996 reversing those dated 24.8.1996 passed by the learned Subordinate Judge(now Joint District Judge), 2nd Court, Gopalganj in Title Suit No. 67 of 1995 dismissing the suit.

2. Facts necessary for disposal of this Civil Appeal, in brief, are:

<u>3. That the present respondents No. 1-7, as plaintiffs instituted Title 'Suit No.114 of 1993 in the Court of Assistant Judge, Muksudpur, Gopalganj (subsequently on transfer renumbered as Title Suit No. 67 of 1995 of the 1st Court of Sub-ordinate Judge, Gopalgonj) against the present appellants and respondent Nos. 8-57 for partition claiming saham to the extent of 1.581/2 acres out of 25.34 acres from schedule No.1 and 7.65 acres out of 11.79 acres from schedule Nos. 2-5 and also for declaration that the order dated 03.03.1983, passed by the Revenue Officer, Muksudpur as approved by the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue) on 20.4.83 in Miscellaneous Case No. XIII 124/82 on the basis of an application filed by Pulin Behari, the predecessor-in-interest of defendant Nos. 1 and 2 was fraudulent, collusive, null and void, inoperative in law, ultra-vires, illegal, without jurisdiction and not binding upon the plaintiffs. It is stated in the plaint, inter alia, that originally the land of schedule No.1 property belonged to Abhoy Charan Haider and Debendra Nath Haider with 16 gondas each and Pulin Behari Haider, Shaibalini Haider and Sarju Bala Haider having 10 gandas, 2 Kara and 2 Kranti each. Similarly land of schedule Nos. 2-5 properties belonged to Abhoy Charan Haider and Debendra Nath Haider in 4 (four) annas share each and Pulin Behari, Shaibalini and Sarojini @ Sarju Bala Haider had 2 annas, 13 gands, 1 kara and 1 kranti share each. Accordingly the R.S record was correctly prepared in their names. Surja Bala died leaving behind only daughter Kanak Prova who, entered into a contract to transfer 3.56 acres of land to Samiruddin, the predecessor of the plaintiffs, upon receipt of TK. 1,000/= out of total consideration money of TK.1500/- on 21.10.1952 and subsequently on receipt of the balance consideration filed by defendant Nos. 1 and 2 the Revenue Officer of Muksudpur submitted a report to the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue), Faridpur, on 30.03.83 and on the basis of the said report the names of the defendant Nos. 1 and 2 were mutated vide order dated 19.4.1983 in respect of the suit land. Subsequently, Samiruddin filed Review Case No. XII-G.M. 67/83-84 before the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue), Gopalganj, which was rejected on 15.2.87. Under such circumstances Samiruddin died leaving behind plaintiff Nos. 1, 2 and defendant No. 8 as his three sons and defendant Nos. 3-7 as his five daughters and a widow (plaintiff No. 8, since deceased); that plaintiff No. 2 and defendant No. 8(two sons of Samiruddin) filed a revisional application before the Additional Divisional Commissioner, Dhaka, and obtained an order of stay of all previous orders passed in connection with Case No. XII-GM. 67/83-84; however, the said revisional application was unfortunately rejected on 14.10.91 as none appeared on behalf of the plaintiffs when the same was taken up for hearing. The plaintiffs knew nothing about the rejection of the revisional application and subsequently on 4.9.1993 they having come to know about the same obtained the certified copy of the order dated 14.10.1991 and requested the defendants on 20th Bhadra, 1400 B.S for partition of the suit land on which they do not have any absolute right, title and possession and rather the plaintiffs have right, title and possession in ejmali with the defendants but being refused the plaintiffs instituted the suit.</u>

4. Defendant Nos. 1-2, 23 and 28 contested the suit by filing three separate written statements.

<u>5. The defendant Nos.1 and 2 in their writ-ten statement contended inter alia that Sarju Bala was the owner of 10 gondas 2 kara and 2 kranti out of 24.34 acres of land in R.S Khatian No. 30 and 2 annas 13 gondas 1 kara and 1 kranti of land in R.S. Khatian Nos. 44, 33, 462, 41 and 113. She died leaving behind her only daughter, Konok Prova, who sold 10.00 acres of land including the suit khatians to Abhoy Charan, Debendra and Pulin Bihari Halder at a consideration of TK. 1,000/00; that though Konok Probha executed kabala on 25.11.53, yet she could not register the same for want of time and as such Abhoy Charan and others applied to the District Register for registering the kabala and accordingly the kabala was registered on 28.8.54. Thus Abhoy Charan and others have been possessing the said transferred land as the rightful owners. Although Samiruddin had full knowledge of the said kabala, he firstly created a bainapatra on 21.10.52 and then created the registered kabala on 04.2.1954 which was never executed and registered by Konok Prova. On the other hand Debendra Nath Halder after his purchase from Konok Prova entered into an agreement on 22.2.1955 to transfer 3.01 acres of land to Gadadhar Roy but when he delayed to execute and register the kabala, Gadadhar filed Title Suit No. 282 of 1958 in the Second Court of the then Munsif, Gopalganj for specific performance of contract and obtained decree on 29.9.58 and got kabala through Court on 24.9.1959 and got possession of the said 3.01 acres of land; that Pulin Behari, the other transferee of Konok Prova, entered into an agreement with Nishi kanta Roy on 20.1.56 to sell 2.98 acres of land at a consideration of taka 4,00/00 and on receipt of a sum of taka 200/00 handed over possession of the same to him on the same day. Subsequently Nishi Kanta filed Title Suit No. 309 of 1958 in the Second Court of the then Munsif, Gopalganj, for specific performance of contact and obtained decree on 9.2.59 and eventually got kabala through Court on 28.9.59 being kabala No. 4802. Thereafter, Gadadhar Roy by two registered kabalas No. 3828 and 3866 both dated 01.07.1974 transferred his 3.01 acres of land to Pulin Behari Haider and Nishi Kanto Roy also transferred his 2.98 acres of land also to Pulin Behari Haider by 2 (two) kabalas both dated 01.07.1974 being kabala Nos. 3829 and 3867. Thus Pulin Behari became the owner of 5.99 acres of land by purchase and after his death his 2(two) sons, defendant Nos.1 and 2, have been possessing the said land upon getting their names mutated and paying rents to the government. Thereafter when Samiruddin relying on the aforementioned forged and created deeds started creating disturbance in respect of possession of the said land, Abhoy Charan and others filed Title Suit No. 4 of 1955 in the Second Court of Subordinate Judge, Faridpur, for permanent injunction which was dismissed on contest with observation that 'without the prayer for declaration of title and confirmation of possession the plaintiffs were not entitled to get any decree in the suit'. However, the said defendant Nos. 1 and 2 claimed that Samiruddin never purchased the lands of Debendra and others in auction pursuant to Execution Case No.12 of 1956. That the plaintiffs' Title Suit No. 114 of 1993 was false and fraudulent nor he got possession of the alleged auction purchased land or got his name mutated in S.A record. The S.A. record was collusive and fraudulent. The names of defendant Nos. 1 and 2 were rightly mutated. Moreover the suit was barred by limitation and as such the suit being filed on false claim the same is liable to be dismissed with costs.</u>

6. Defendant No. 23 in his written statement contended, inter alia, that he purchased 2.56 acres of land from Debendra Nath Haider by Kabala No. 1664 dated 15.03.1956 and got possession of the same and then he sold some portion of the said purchased land to Pulin Behari Haider, Sheikh Abdul, Sheikh Mofazzel and Sheikh Motaleb by Kabala No.1665 dated 15.03.1956. Subsequently, Dhonaullah (father of this defendant No.23) purchased some lands from Pulin Behari Haider, (the father of defendant Nos. 1 and 2) who died while was in possession of the said land leaving behind a widow, 6 (six) sons including defendant No. 23 and 6 (six) daughters. Defendant No. 23 along with his brothers and sisters are in possession of the said purchased land. Thus the plaintiffs' suit being not maintainable the same is liable to be dismissed.

7. Though Defendant No. 25 filed written statement but eventually he did not contest the suit at the hearing.

8. Defendant No.28 in his written statement contended that Debendra Nath Haider, sold .52 acre of land out of 1.64 acres from plot No. 1184 of R.S Khatian No.41 to Abdul Hamid Sheikh, R. Sheikh Abdul, Dhonaullah and Mofazzal Sheikh by kabala No. 2766 dated 27.8.55. Pulin Behari Haider sold .90 acre of land to Sheikh Abdul, Sheikh Mofazzel, Sheikh Abdul Motaleb by kabala No. 1656 dated 15.3.56. That Abdul Sheikh died leaving behind five sons and three daughters as his heirs,(i.e. defendant Nos.27-38). The plaintiffs filed the suit on some false statements so they are not entitled to get my relief in the suit.

9. The trial Court, on examination of the materials on record and on hearing all the parties dismissed the suit on contest by judgment and decree dated 24.08.1996 whereupon the plaintiffs preferred Title Appeal No. 92 of 1996 before the learned District Judge, Gopalganj, who allowed the appeal in part and thereby decreed the suit declaring that the plaintiffs have got title and possession in respect of 3.29 acres of land on the basis of their purchase vide kabala dated 04.02.1954(Exhibit-2) and accordingly, allotted saham to the plaintiffs for the said quantum of land (3.29 acres of land) by his judgment and decree dated 1.7.1997. Against the said judgment and decree of reversal, the defendant’s No. 1 and 2 moved the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 1034 of 1998 and obtained Rule. The High Court Division, on hearing the Rule, dis-charged the same by the impugned judgment and order dated 07.01.2010, observing that in Title Suit No. 4 of 1955 filed by the present defendants for permanent injunction against Samiruddin, (the predecessor of the plaintiffs), Court found Samiruddin's purchase of 3.29 acres of land from Konok Prova by kabala dated 4.2.1954 was valid and the said finding having been affirmed by the appellate Court as well as by the High Court Division the same is still subsisting. Moreover the SA record also stands in the name of Samiruddin and after his death in the names of the plaintiffs'.

10. Being aggrieved by the aforesaid judgment and order of the High Court Division the defendants preferred Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 174 of 2011 before this Division and obtained leave which gave rise to this appeal.

11. From the leave granting order it appears that leave has been granted to determine the point as follows: "Because out of 3.29 acres of land covered by the disputed kabala deed No. 1436 dated 04.02.1954 only 1.99 acres of land of RS Khatian Nos. 33, 44 and 30 are included in the schedule of the plaint of Title Suit No. 67 of 1995, the plaintiff-respondents were/are not entitled to get preliminary decree for more than 1.99 acres of land but without examining the contents of the kabala an area of 3.29 acres has been given in the preliminary decree."

12. Mr. Quamrul Haque Siddique, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the defendant-appellants submits that though the sale deed dated 04.02.1954 contained 3.29 acres of land on six different khatians but all those six khatians have not been brought in the hotch-pot of the schedule of the plaint as a result the plain-tiffs are not entitled to get saham for the entire 3.29 acres of land sold through the said Kabala. He submits that out of the six khatians incorporated in the said deed, Khatian Nos. 19, 42 and 428 containing 1.30 acres of land have not been included in the hotch-pot of the suit, rather only Khatian Nos. 33, 44 and 30 containing total 1.99 acres of land have been incorporated in the schedule of the plaint and saham has been sought for only to that extent. Since all the khatians described in the Kabala, which covers 3.29 acres of land have not been brought within the botch-pot of the plaint and as such the plaintiffs are not entitled to get saham to the extent of entire 3.29 acres of land described in the said kabala. Thus the reasons given by the High Court Division as well as by the Court of appeal below giving saham to the extent of 3.29 acres of land, which is the entire subject matter of the kabala, in favour of the plaintiff-respondents is erroneous. Hence this appeal should be allowed.

13. It appears that the plaintiff respondent No.1 filed caveat but did not file any concise statement in this appeal. Thus under the Appellate Division Rules the arguments advanced by the learned Advocate-On-Record on behalf of the plaintiff respondent No.1 cannot be taken into consideration.

<u>14. From the record, it appears that other than defendants No. 1 and 2 none challenged the saham given in favour of the plaintiff-respondents to the extent of 3.29 acres of land. It also appears that the ownership of Konok Prova is admitted by both the parties and the present defendants namely, Abhoy Charan, Debendra Nath and Pulin Behari, earlier instituted Title Suit No. 4 of 1955 for permanent injunction against Samiruddin which was dismissed with cost by the Court below holding that Samiruddin's, (predecessor of the plaintiffs), purchase of 3.29 acres of land from Konok Prova by Kabala dated 4.2.1954 was valid and genuine. The said finding having not been challenged has not been set aside by any of the higher Courts. When a competent Court found the kabala of the predecessor of the plain-tiffs is valid and the said finding is still in force now it is difficult to hold that the predecessor of the plaintiffs is not entitled to get saham to the extent of 3.29 acres of land which he purchased from Konok Prova by registered deed dated 4.2.1954. This status of the plaintiffs has been con-currently found by the court of appeal below as well as by the High Court Division.</u>

15. Even then the trial Court dismissed the suit on the ground that the deed of the predecessor of the plaintiffs was registered subsequent to deed of the predecessor of the defendants although the plaintiffs produced the baina patra dated 21.10.1952 pursuant to which the deed was registered on 4.2.1954 was an earlier document. The whole case of the plaintiffs is that Konok Prova never executed any deed in favour of the predecessor of the defendants. The Court of appeal below, as the last Court of fact, on consideration of the entire facts and circumstances found the deed of the plaintiffs dated 4.2.1954 to be valid and held that the plaintiffs proved their title in respect of 3.29 acres of land transferred by Konok Prova. This finding of the court of appeal below has been affirmed by the High Court Division. While considering this aspect the Court of appeal below also considered the judgment and order passed in Title Suit No. 4 of 1955 filed by the defendants, wherein the present defendants failed to prove their claim of prima facie title and possession over 3.29 acres of land of the suit land. For that reason, the Court of appeal below decreed the present suit giving saham to the extent of 3.29 acres of land, (which is the subject matter of the deed of the plain-tiffs dated 4.2.1954) to the plaintiffs. The High Court Division also affirmed the said finding of the Court of appeal below. The defendants, now, before this Division, has come up with a new plea that all the six khatians contained in the deed of the plaintiffs dated 4.2.1954 has not been incorporated in the hotch-pot of the suit. Thus they are 'entitled to get saham to the extent of land which they have incorporated in the schedule of the plaint only i.e. only to the extent of 1.99 acres and the land remaining in three other khatians (khatian Nos. 19, 42 and 42 of the deed) covering 1.30 acres of land having not been incorporated in the hotch-pot of the suit they are not entitled to get saham to that extent. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case it is prayed that if the plaintiffs at all get any saham they will at best be entitled to 1.99 acres of land not the entire property purchased by their predecessor vide the said deed. To determine this question we need to examine the plaint, as well as the deed.

16. The trial Court framed a particular issue being issue No. 4 which reads as follows :

“অত্র মোকদ্দমা হচপট দোষে অচল কি?”

<u>17. While discussing the said issue the trial Court specifically found that though the defendants claim that the suit should be dismissed because of the fact that the entire property has not been incorporated within the hotch-pot of the case but on perusal of the five schedules described in the plaint it found that all the plots have not been brought within the hotch pot of the suit and thus held that the suit and thus held that “বাদীগণ খরিদ সমস্ত জমি বাবদ বন্টনের প্রতিকার প্রার্থনা না করিয়া আংশিক ভুমি দাবী হইতে বাদ দিলে উহার দ্বারা সমস্ত হচপট ভূক্ত করা হয়নাই বুঝায় না। প্রশ্ন হইতেছে, যে খতিয়ানের জমি বাদীগণ দাবী করিতেছেন ঐ খতিয়ানের সাকুল্য ভূমি হচপট ভূক্ত করা হইয়াছে কিনা? এই প্রসঙ্গে বিবাদী পরে বিজ্ঞ কৌশুলীগণ কিছুই বলেন নাই। তাহারা শুধুমাত্র বাদীগণ সমস্ত দাবী করেন নাই এই বক্তব্যের উপরই তাহাদের যুক্তি সীমাবদ্ধ রাখিয়াছেন। ১/২ নং বিবাদীগণ নালিশী খতিয়ান সমূহের আর, এস পর্চা দাখিল করিয়াছেন যাহা প্রদর্শনী ঙ১-ঙ১(৪) হিসাবে চিহ্নিত হইয়াছে। উক্ত খতিয়ান সমূহ পর্যালোচনায় খতিয়ানের সাকুল্য জমি হচপট ভুক্ত করা হইয়াছে মর্মে সিদ্ধান্তে আসা যায়।</u>

<u>���তএব, মোকদ্দমাটি হচপট দোষে অচল নহে।”</u>

18. This being the specific finding of the trial Court and affirmed by the appellate Court and the defendants without challenging this finding before any Court of law, now has come forward with the plea that though the Court of appeal below as well as the High Court Division gave 3.29 acres of land as saham to the plaintiffs which was purchased by the predecessor of the plaintiffs vide deed dated 4.2.1954 but the entire property described in the schedule of the said deed has not been brought within the hotch-pot of the suit.

19. On examination of the schedule annexed to the plaint as well as those incorporated in the deed of sale executed by Konok Prova on 4.2.1954 it appears that schedule Nos.1 to 5 to the plaint relates to Khatian Nos. 30, 33, 41, 44 and 461 respectively. On comparing the same with the khatians described in the schedule of the deed by which the plaintiffs claim their title, it appears that schedule No.2 of the said deed covers .98 acre of land in khatian No. 33, schedule No.3 of the deed covers .23 acre of land of Khatian No. 44, schedule No.4 of the deed covers .78 acre of land within Khatian No. 30, schedule-5 of the deed covers .39 acre of land of Khatian No. 42 and schedule-6 covers .03 acre of land of Khatian No. 428 which appears to have been transferred to the predecessor of the plaintiffs.

20. So it appears that by schedule-1 to the plaint (which-attracts Khatian No. 30), the plaintiffs sought saham in respect of 1.58;1 acre of land whereas they got only .78 acre of land by the said deed in question. By Khatian No. 33 described in schedule 2 to the plaint, the plaintiffs claim for 5.59 acres of land whereas the deed shows in respect of Khatian No. 33 the predecessor of the plaintiffs purchased from Konok Prova only .98 acres of land. In schedule-4 to the plaint, the plaintiff claims 1.28 acres of land within khatian No. 44 but the kabala shows that the predecessor of the plaintiffs purchased only .23 acre of land in the said khatian by the said deed.

21. So it is clear that although the plain-tiffs prayed for saham to the extent of 9.241-t acres of land described in five schedules of the plaint but actually the plaintiffs appear to have purchased 3.29 acres of land from the aforesaid schedules of the deed in six khatians. Interestingly the plaintiffs did not bring three out of six khatians of the deed in the hotch-pot of the suit and as such the plaintiffs did not pray for saham to the extent of 1.30 acres of land as described in Khatians No. 19, 42 and 428. Under such circumstances Mr. Siddique submits that the plaintiffs can at best get saham to the extent of 1.99 acres of land only from Khatian Nos. 33, 44 and 30 as brought in the hotch pot of the suit which their predecessor purchased from Konok Prova not beyond that. If this contention of Mr. Siddique is accepted then conclusion may be drawn to the effect that the deed dated 4.2.1954 though has been proved to be true and valid but the plain-tiffs are not entitled to get saham to the extent of the whole of the property transferred by the said deed i.e. 3.29 acres of land as they have not incorporated 1.99 acres of land from three khatians, as mentioned above, of the said deed in the hotch pot of the suit.

<u>22. It is required to be mentioned here that the plaintiffs claimed 9.24 acres of land in five schedules of the plaint out of which, 3.29 acres of land has been purchased by their predecessor from Konok Prova by deed dated 4.2.1954 and the rest of the 5.95 acres of land is the land which their predecessor purchased through auction in Execution Case No. 12 of 1956 for realization of the cost awarded in Title Suit No. 4 of 1953. Though the plaintiffs also claimed saham for the said auction purchased land but the Court of appeal below as well as the High Court Division did not grant any saham in respect of that auction purchased land and the plaintiffs did not take any step against such finding. As such we shall have to confine ourselves within the subject matter of kabala dated 4.2.1954 which the Court of appeal below found to be genuine and valid and affirmed by the High Court Division.</u>

<u>23. From the discussions made herein-above it appears that the plaintiffs' title to the extent of 3.29 acres of land has been proved before the court of appeal below who granted saham to the said extent and allowed the appeal in part which has been affirmed by the High Court Division. But admittedly in the schedule of the plaint the plaintiffs did not incorporate all the khatians described in the schedule of the said deed. Unless the saham is sought for in respect of any particular property, even if the Court holds that the plaintiffs have title, it cannot grant saham to the extent which the plaintiffs did not bring within the hotch pot. Therefore, we are of the view that the plaintiffs' saham to the extent of 1.99 acres of land in Khatian Nos. 33, 44 and 30 has been properly given in their favour. But since 1.30 acres of land from Khatian Nos. 19, 42 and 428, though has been transferred in favour of the predecessor of the plaintiffs by deed dated 4.2.1954, and they have title therein but they having not incorporated the same in the hotch pot of the suit and thereby ask for saham for the same the same cannot be granted in this particular partition suit. As the cause of action of a suit for partition is admittedly a recurring cause of action whenever a party or a co sharer of a case jote feels that he requires partition and the defendant refuses to give partition he can file a suit for partition claiming saham to that extent. Thus the plaintiffs may take appropriate steps as and when requires in respect of the rest of their saham which were not incorporated in the schedule of the plaint.</u>

24. With these observations this civil appeal is disposed of granting saham of 1.99 acres of land in Khatian Nos. 33, 44 and 30 in favour of the plaintiffs.

25. There will be no order as to cost.

End.

full_judgment:
Mirza Hussain Haider J. These two appeals, by leave, are directed against the judgment and order dated 16.5.2007, passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision Nos. 2431 and 2432 of 1994 making the Rule issued in Civil Revision No.2431 of 1994 absolute in part and Rule issued in Civil Revision No.2432 of 1994 absolute.

2. Relevant facts leading to filing of these two Civil Appeals, in brief, are:

<u>3. That the present appellants (in both the appeals) and one Saleha Khatun instituted Title Suit No.31 of 1991 in the 2nd Court of Assistant Judge, Barisal, (originally Title Suit No. 224 of 1985 in the 1st Court of the then Munsif, Barisal) seeking declaration that the auction sale of the suit land as mentioned in schedule 'Ka' to the plaint in Certificate Case No. 472(KT)/1983-84 is fraudulent, collusive, illegal and not binding upon them. On the other hand, the present respondent Nos. 1 and 2 also instituted Title Suit No. 35 of 1991 in the 2nd Court of Assistant Judge, Barisal, (originally Title Suit No. 241 of 1985 in the First Court of the then Munsif, Barisal) against the present appellants and proforma respondent Nos.3-14 (in both the appeals) as defendants, seeking declaration of their title in the suit land and for further declaration that the decree dated 10.8.1959 passed in Title Suit No.220 of 1959 of the 2nd Court of Munsif, Barisal is fraudulent, illegal and not binding upon them.</u>

4. It is stated in the plaint of Title Suit No. 31 of 1991 that the suit land originally belonged to Amorendra Nath and others who settled the same with one Abdus Sobahan and Abdul Hamid Howlader; that the said Abdus Sobahan died leaving behind his only son, the plaintiff No.1 and Abdul Hamid Howlader died leaving behind plaintiff Nos.2 to 5 as heirs. It is alleged that when the suit land was wrongly recorded in SA Khatian they instituted Title Suit No. 220 of 1959 and obtained a compromise decree on 10.8.1959, on the basis of which the plaintiffs got the suit land recorded in their names and since then they have been possessing the same. It is further alleged that the defendants fraudulently created an auction sale proceeding in respect of the suit land in Certificate Case No. 472 (KT)/83-84 but did not acquire any title or possession in the same. Hence, the suit.

5. On the other hand, the plaintiffs of Title Suit No. 35 of 1991 (the present respondent Nos. 1 & 2) in their plaint stated that the suit land belonged to Amorendra Nath and others and the same was put in auction in Certificate Case No. 472(KT)/83-84 and defendant Nos.13 to 16 purchased the same; that the sale was confirmed and the auction purchasers were given possession of the same. The plaintiffs (present respondent Nos.1 and 2) purchased the suit land from the auction purchasers by registered kabala dated 11.4.1985 and have been in possession of the same since then. It is further alleged that the defendants (plaintiffs of Title Suit No.31 of 1991) instituted false Title Suit No. 220 of 1959 and obtained a forged and collusive compromise decree on 10.8.1959 by practicing fraud upon the court. Hence, Title suit No. 224 of 1985 (original Title suit No.31 of 1991) should be dismissed and Title suit No. 241 of 1985 (original Title suit No. 35 of 1991) should be decreed.

6. The defendants of both the suits contested the above suits by filing their respective written statements denying the claims of each other and relied upon the statements made in their respective plaints.

7. The learned Assistant Judge, after hearing both the suits analogously, dismissed both the suits by judgment and decree dated 19.02.1992. Then the plaintiffs of Title Suit No. 35 of 1991 (present respondent Nos. 1 and 2) preferred Title Appeal No. 53 of 1992 and the plaintiffs of Title Suit No.31 of 1981 (present appellants) preferred Title Appeal No.135 of 1992. The learned Subordinate Judge (Now Joint District Judge) after hearing both the appeals analogously, allowed Title Appeal No. 135 of 1992 and thereby decreed Title Suit No. 31 of 1991 and dismissed Title Appeal No. 53 of 1992 and thereby affirmed the dismissal of Title Suit No. 35 of 1991 by judgment and decree dated 27.4.1994. As against that, the plaintiffs of Title Suit No. 35 of 1991 (present respondents) moved the High Court Division and obtained two Rules in Civil Revision Nos. 2431 and 2432 of 1994.

8. The High Court Division after hearing both the parties, made the Rule issued in Civil Revision No. 2432 of 1994 absolute and thereby dismissed Title, Suit No. 31 of 1991 filed by the present appellants and made the Rule issued in Civil Revision 2431 of 1994 absolute in part and thereby decreed Title Suit No. 35 of 1991 (filed by the present respondent Nos. 1 and 2) in part declaring only to the extent that the judgment and decree dated 10.08.1959 passed in Title suit No. 220 of 1959 is illegal, void and not binding upon the present respondents, by the impugned judgment and order dated 16.5.2007.

9. Being aggrieved by the aforesaid judgment and order dated 16.5.2007, passed in Civil Revision Nos. 2431 of 1994 and 2432 of 1994, the present appellants moved this Court in Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal Nos.1618 of 2007 and 1619 of 2007 and obtained leave giving rise to the instant two appeals.

10. Mr. Mahbubey Alam, the learned senior Advocate, appearing on behalf of the appellants of both the appeals submits that the respondents filed title suit No.35 of 1985 praying for declaration of title to the land mentioned it schedule 'ka' to the plaint on the basis of auction purchase and also praying for a declaration that the decree passed in Title Suit No. 220 of 1959 as illegal and void and the trial court after having found the alleged auction purchase fraudulent and void dismissed the suit and the said judgment and decree of the trial court was affirmed by the appellate court. But the High Court Division affirmed the judgment of two lower courts regarding acquisition of title by that alleged auction purchase but committed error in passing part decree so far it relates to the validity of Title Suit No. 220 of 1959 without considering the fact that since the plaintiffs of Title Suit No. 35 of 1991 failed to establish their title to the suit property they have no locus standi to challenge the decree obtained by the plaintiffs in Title Suit No. 220 of 1959. He further submits that the plaintiffs of Title Suit No.31 of 1991(i.e. the present appellants) filed the suit in respect of 1.40 acres of land of Plot No. 21 and .85 acre of land of Plot No.3 on the basis of the decree passed in Title Suit No. 220 of 1959, the plaintiffs of Title Suit No. 35 of 1991(i.e. the respondent Nos. 1 and 2) herein, filed their suit in respect of 1.40 acres of land of Plot No. 21 only, but the High Court Division committed error in passing a part decree in favour of the plaintiffs of Title Suit No. 35 of 1991 in respect of entire suit land of Title Suit No.31 of 1991.So the judgment and order of the High Court Division is liable to be set aside.

11. Mr. Abdul Quiyum, the learned Senior Advocate appearing on behalf of the respondents submits that the lower appellate court did not reverse the finding of the trial court as regards fraud in respect of the disputed decree of Title Suit No. 220 of 1959 but reversed the judgment of the trial court relying upon the Bank of Calcutta Ltd. vs. Debendra Nath Singh and others reported in 19 DLR 400, which is not applicable in this case. He also submits that the plaintiffs of Title Suit No. 31 of 1991 (the present appellants) have no locus standi to challenge the auction of the defendants as the so called settlement in 1358 BS, which is the basis of their title, is not proved by them. He further submits that the courts below misconstrued the evidence of PW-1 who proved mutation by the defendant respondents after the auction purchase within the knowledge of the plaintiffs, so the auction was not fraudulent and as a result the appellants are not entitled to get decree as prayed for.

<u>12. On consideration of the submissions advanced on behalf of both the parties and on perusal of the impugned judgment and order and the materials on record it appears that, admittedly, the suit land belonged to Amarendra Nath and others. The plaintiffs of Title Suit No.31 of 20,09, (hereinafter mentioned as appellants claimed that Abdus Subhan Mia, (the plaintiff appellant No. l) and Abdul Hamid Hawlader (predecessor of Plaintiff appellant Nos. 2 to 6) took settlement of the suit land from Amarendra Nath and others; but they did not disclose the date or year of such settlement in their plaint. PW-1, Abdus Sobhan Miah, in his deposition stated that they took settlement from Baidhyanath in the year 1358 BS; but no other PW corroborated PW-1 in this respect nor has the settlement been proved by producing either Patta or Kabuliyat or any other written document. Under the Bengal Tenancy Act, though settlement may be granted orally without any written instrument but in case, if any question arose as to genuineness of such settlement then burden always lies upon the person claiming as such to prove the same settlement by proper oral evidence. But in the present case the appellants have failed to prove such settlement by any proper evidence either oral or documentary. Thus when the settlement, the basis of appellants title, is not proved by proper evidence, they cannot claim title through auction purchase.</u>

13. The learned advocate for the appellants claimed that the suit land was not recorded in the names of the settlement holders in the SA Khatian and as a result they filed Title suit No. 220 of 1959 and obtained a compromise decree and by that decree the appellants made the record corrected and thereby included their names in the record and relying upon such submission the appellate court decreed Title Suit No. 31 of 1991 only on the basis of the said compromise decree [Exhibit-2(ka)] passed on 10.8.1959. But on examination of the plaint of Title Suit No. 220 of 1959, the solenama (Exhibit-2) and the Sole decree [Exhibit-2(Ka)] it transpires that there were two plaintiffs and seven defendants in the said suit but none other than Amarendranath (one defendant) and the sole plaintiff No.1, Abdul Hamed, signed the said solenama and the plaintiff No.1 alone put his signature at the bottom of the same. Interestingly neither the other six defendants nor the plaintiff No. 2, Abdul Subhan Miah, signed the said solenama. Moreover, the solenama was not proved by either party of the suit and there is no explanation as to why others did not sign that solenama. On the other hand PW-2, Subudh Chandra Majhi, in his cross examination admitted that “বাবুদের সহিত পত্তনের সময় কথা হইয়াছে যে, মোকদ্দমা করিলেই সোলে করিয়া দিবে। ঐ সময় অন্য বাবুরা বাড়িতেই ছিল।

<u>14. Moreover, it also appears that Title Suit No. 220 of 1959 was filed in 1959 and the same claimed to have been decreed on compromise on 10.8.1959 but the Vokalatnama of the said suit appears to have been accepted on 5.5.1985 which is illusive and rather creates doubt. It also appears that no notice was served upon the original owners of the suit land and the defendants of that suit did not appear in the court before signing the Solenama. That's why the trial court found the Vokalatnama of the said suit to be forged one. Again, on perusal of the sole decree [Exhibit-2(ka)] it appears that the suit was disposed of on compromise on 10.08.1959 bit the said decree appears to have been signed by the learned Judge on 19.08.1958. Thus, it is not clear how the decree was prepared and signed one year before passing of the same. These abundant discrepancies in the decree of Title Suit No.220 of 1959 clearly prove that the solenama was not only a fraudulent one but also collusive one and as a result such illegal decree cannot confer any title upon the appellants.</u>

<u>15. It appears that the trial court upon considering all these aspects rightly assessed the evidence and considered the materials on record and dismissed the suit but the lower appellate court without properly considering the evidence on record, simply relied upon the aforesaid compromise decree and allowed the appeal and decreed the suit which the High Court Division on consideration of materials on record found the orders of the court of appeal below not sustainable in the eye of law and as a result set aside the judgment and decree of the lower appellate court and affirmed those of the trial court.</u>

<u>16. On the other hand the plaintiffs of Title Suit No.35 of 1991 (hereinafter mentioned as present respondents) claimed that the suit land was put in auction in Certificate Case Nos. 472(KT)/1983-84 and 387(KT)/1976- 77which was purchased by defendant Nos. 1-3 and 5 who took possession of the same through court on 12.10.1984 and since then they have been possessing the same. Subsequently, on 11.04.1985 they transferred .85 acre of land out of the said auction purchased land to this respondent who was given possession of the same. But the courts below found that they failed to prove the sale certificate in support of such auction sale/purchase, also failed to prove delivery of possession and service of notice under sections 7 and 46 of the Public Demand Recovery Act. Though the plaintiffs of Title suit No. 220 of 1959 claimed that they purchased the same from the persons who purchased such land in auction they failed to prove that auction by producing proper evidence. DW-1, Abdur Rashid Khan, deposed that he got possession of the suit land in 1985 but DW-2, Sultan Howladar, admitted in his cross examination that ‘One Gobinda Babu possessed the suit land till 1991' Interestingly DW-4, Razni Kanta Baliar, in his cross examination stated that the plaintiffs (the present respondents) have been possessing the suit land for 20/21 years. On the other hand PW-5, Wazed Ali, in his cross examination stated that the plaintiffs (present respondents) have been possessing the suit land for about 14/15 years. From the aforesaid evidence and discussion it is abundantly clear that the plaintiffs of Title Suit No. 35 of 1991 have totally failed to prove their possession in the suit land.</u>

17. The learned Advocate for the appellants, on the face of the respondents' Title Suit No. 35 of 1991 for declaration of their title to the suit land on the basis of auction purchase in the year 1985 and also for a declaration that the decree passed in Title Suit No. 220 of 1959 is illegal and void submitted that since they failed to prove the auction purchase they cannot get a decree for declaration that the decree passed in Title Suit No. 220 of 1959 is illegal and void. It is true that the respondents filed their Title Suit No. 35 of 1991 for two declarations, one for declaration of title to the land described in schedule-I to the plaint and another for two declarations, one for declaration of title to the land described in schedule-I to the plaint and another for declaration that the decree passed in title suit No. 220 of 1959 is fraudulent, collusive and not binding upon them. These two prayers are separate and independent and they filed that suit by paying separate court fees for these two separate prayers. Though they filed to prove their title to the land described in schedule-I to the plaint they have successfully proved that the decree passed in Title Suit No. 220 of 1959 is fraudulent, illegal and collusive.

So, they can get part decree to the extent of their second prayer. Hence, the High Court Division Committed no wrong in decreeing the suit in part to extent of declaring the decree passed in the Title Suit No. 220 of 1959 to be fraudulent, void, illegal and not binding upon them.

18. The appellants further claimed that they filed their Title Suit No. 31 of 1991 in respect of 2.25 acres of land in plot Nos. 21 and 3 but the respondent Nos. 1 and 2 filed Title Suit No. 35 of 1991 in respect of 1.40 acres of land only in plot No. 21 along with a prayer for declaring the decree of Title Suit No. 220 of 1959 fraudulent and void etc. So, the decree passed by the High Court Division is not maintainable in the eye of law. It is required to mention here that though the respondents’ first prayer was in respect of 1.40 acres of land their second prayer for declaration was in respect of the whole suit land i.e. 2.25 acres of land including 1.40 acre of land described in schedule-1 which was the subject matter of Title Suit No. 220 of 1959. So, the claim of the learned Advocate for the appellants finds no legal ground in this respect.

19. So, the trial court and the lower appellate court after examining the evidence and materials on record rightly dis-missed both the suits to the extent to which the plaintiffs failed to prove and the High Court Division also rightly affirmed the judgment and order of those two lower courts. But, the High Court Division in its revisional jurisdiction rightly observed that the evidence on record clearly proved that the decree passed in Title Suit No. 220 of 1959 was fraudulent and collusive and as a result the plaintiffs of Title Suit No.35 of 1991 can get part decree to that extent in that suit.

20. Thus the findings and decision arrived at by the High Court Division being based on proper appreciation of fact and law do not call for interference by this Division.

21. Accordingly, these two civil appeals are dismissed without any order as to costs.

End.

caseno: Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No.4154 of 2017
lawyer:
Mr. Khair Ezaz Maswood, Advocate instructed by Mr. Md. Abdul Hye Bhuiyan, Advocate-on-Record ------ For the Petitioners 
Mr. M Amirul Islam, Senior Advocate instructed by Mr. Md. Bodrul Islam, Advocate-on-Record   ------ For Respondent No.1 
None represented ---- For Respondent Nos.2-15
parties:
Md. Salim Sarder being dead his legal heirs: Most Monira Sultana and another. ------- Petitioners
-Vs-
Md. Abul Kashem and others ----- Respondents
case_source: (From the judgment and order dated the 16th day of May, 2017 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No.255 of 2009)
full_judgment:
Abu Bakar Siddiquee J. This civil petition for leave to appeal is directed against the judgment and order dated the 161h day of May, 2017 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No.255 of 2009 making the Rule absolute.

<u>2. The facts, relevant for disposal of this petition, are that the present petitioners as plaintiffs filed Other Class Suit No.98 of 1996 in the Court of Subordinate Judge, Court No.2, Rajshahi for declaration that the plaintiffs had title over the suit property as described in schedule-A to the plaint by way of adverse possession. By subsequent amendment of the plaint, another prayer was inserted to the effect that a decree may be passed that the deed of exchange bearing No. 718 dated 03.01.1975 executed and registered in Exchange Case No.134/Sadar/ 1972-1973 in favour of the defendant as described in schedule-B to the plaint is false, baseless, forged, ante-dated and not binding upon the plaintiffs.</u>

3. The case as has been described in the plaint, in short, is that the suit lands appertaining to S.A Khatian No.142 originally belonged to one, Kanai Lal Ghosh and Moniram Ghosh in equal share and the S.A. record was accordingly prepared and published in their names. While enjoying title and possession over the said property, they exchanged the same with those of the Indian property belonged to one Layebuddin Sarkar and accordingly, a deed of exchange was registered in between the parties on 27.01.1964. While Layebuddin Sarkar was enjoying title and possession over the properties, he sold out the same to one Habibur Rahman, predecessor of the plaintiffs at a consideration of taka 10,000.00 and executed a deed of sale on 03.04.1967, but due to time constrained, the same could not be registered on that very date, but it was agreed that the said deed would be presented for registration on the following day, but it could not be registered on the following day as Layebuddin Sarkar had to go to India and eventually, for his not coming back, the said deed remained unregistered.

4. Though the said deed was not registered, the recipient of it, Habibur Rahman, got possession of the suit properties on 04.04.1967 and continued to possess the same. However, during enjoyment of title and possession over the suit properties, Habibur Rahman died on 29.09.1979 leaving behind 4(four) sons and 5(five) daughters, the plaintiffs as his legal heirs who have been possessing the suit property to the hostile of the title of the defendants for more than 12 years since 04.04.1967 and as such, the plaintiffs have acquired title by way of adverse possession. It has further been stated that the defendants have got no right, title and possession over the suit properties. They by virtue of some false and concocted documents denied the title of the plaintiffs in the suit properties on 17.11.1986 and hence the suit.

5. Soon after filing of the said suit, the plaintiffs also filed an application for amendment of the plaint claiming that the deed of exchange as has been executed in favour of the defendants by the Deputy Commissioner, Rajshahi dated 03.01.1975 was illegal, vague and the trial Court allowed the said application and the said claim was inserted in the plaint as of schedule-B.

6. Defendant No.1 contested the said suit by filing a written statement denying all the material allegations made in the plaint contending, inter alia, that, one Kanai Lal Ghosh executed a deed of exchange with the present defendant of his Indian property and accordingly, a power of attorney was executed and to revalidate the said deed of exchange, the defendant presented the said deed of exchange before the Deputy Commissioner, Rajshahi and thus, Exchange Case No.134/Sadar/1972- 1973 was started and after investigation, the deed of exchange was found to be genuine basing on which the Deputy Commission validated 6.20 acres land including the suit land by registered deed of exchange dated 03.01.1975. It has further been stated in the written statement that, in the event of enlisting the suit properties as vested and non-resident property in R.S record in the name of the Government, this defendant filed an application for releasing the same from the list and the Government released the said property on 20.10.1983. Upon releasing the said property, the defendant then mutated his name and accordingly paid rent to the Government. It has further been stated that, during enjoyment of title and possession over the said property, defendant No.1 transferred 8.14 decimals land to defendant No.2 on 25.11.1986 as well as some portion of land to defendant No.3 on 18.12.1986 and the said recipients have also been in possession over the same. In aforesaid manner, the defendants acquired title and possession over the suit land by adverse possession and the suit so filed by the plaintiffs has no basis which is liable to be dismissed.

7. Defendant Nos.2-3 contested the said suit by filing a joint written statement denying all the material allegations made in the plaint contending that they purchased the suit properties from defendant No.1 dated 25.11.1986 as well as 18.12.1986 and since then, they have been enjoying title and possession over the suit property. After purchase, these two defendants also mutated their names and paid rent, so they prayed for dismissing the suit.

8. In view of the said pleadings of the parties, the learned Subordinate Judge framed as many as 6(six) issues. In order to prove the case, the plaintiffs examined as many as 9(nine) witnesses while defendant No.1 examined 3(nine) wit-nesses. Apart from those, both the parties produced several documents which were also marked as exhibits.

9. The learned Subordinate Judge, after conclusion of the trial, by his judgment and decree dated 06.07.1998 dismissed the suit on contest against defendant No.1 and ex-parte against the rest.

10. Challenging the said judgment and decree passed by the learned Subordinate Judge, the plaintiffs then preferred Title Appeal No.165 of 1998 before the District Judge, Rajshahi. The said appeal was subsequently heard by the learned Judge, Jananirapatta Bingnokari Oporadh Daman Tribunal and Special Judge No.2, Rajshahi.

11. The learned Special Judge after hearing the parties to the appeal and considering the materials and evidence on record allowed the appeal and thereby set aside the judgment and decree passed by the learned Subordinate Judge, and eventually decreed the suit.

12. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the said judgment and decree passed by the Appellate Court below, defendant Nos.1-3 as petitioners preferred the revisional application before the High Court Division and the Judge of the Single Bench of the High Court Division having heard the Rule made the same absolute; hence the plaintiff-petitioners have filed this civil petition for leave to appeal.

13. Mr. Khair Ezaz Maswood, learned Advocate, appearing for the petitioners, submits that their predecessor, Layebuddin Sarker, got the suit proper-ties by way of deed of exchange dated 27.01.1964 executed in Murshidabad, India with the properties of Kanai Lal Ghosh and Moniram Ghosh located in Bangladesh and by virtue of the said deed of exchange, Layebuddin Sarkar transferred the same to the predecessor of the plaintiffs, Habibur Rahman on 03.04.1967 and since then, the plaintiffs have been enjoying title and possession over the suit land uninterruptedly within the every knowledge of the defendants and thereby the plaintiffs acquired title by adverse possession and the said deed dated 03.04.1967 has correctly been marked as exhibit No. 1. He further submits that the very deed dated 03.04.1967 has subsequently been acted upon by virtue of the deed dated 12.11.1990 through which the plaintiffs transferred an area of 10 decimals land to a school who was made co-plaintiff No.8 to the suit and the Headmaster of the school deposed as PW8 to prove the transfer of the suit land in their favour which has alternatively proves that the plaintiffs by virtue of the said deed acquired indefeasible title over the suit properties. He further submits that though defendant No.1 claimed to have acquired the suit properties by way of deed of exchange dated 18.01.1965 executed and registered in Murshidabad, India marked as exhibit No.2, but the same was out and out a sale deed and not a deed of exchange and the plaintiffs by collecting the said deed as well as other documents related to the said deed has been able to prove that defendant No.1 never executed any deed of exchange in India which alternatively proves that the plaintiffs have got title and possession in the suit properties. He further submits that in order to prove the execution of their deed dated 03.04.1967 as genuine, the plaintiffs adduced PW2 who is the attested witness of the said deed and the said PW2 has very perfectly proved the execution of the said deed without any deviation in his cross-examination by defendant No.1. He further submits that since the defendant's alleged deed of exchange dated 18.01.1965 has been proved to be false, the subsequent deed of exchange dated 03.01.1975 executed and registered by the Deputy Commissioner in favour of defendant No.1 has also been proved to be vague and collusive. He lastly submits that the deed dated 03.04.1967, date has been mentioned on the upper side of the stamp paper on which the said deed was written and also pointed out that since the stamp paper had been purchased in the name of the predecessor of the plaintiffs, so there has been no ambiguity with regard to the execution of the said deed as the said deed was also marked as exhibit even without any objection on the part of the defendants.

14. Mr. M. Amirul Islam, learned Counsel, who entered caveat on behalf of respondent No.1, has supported the impugned judgment and order. He further submits that though the plaintiffs claimed title over the suit property by way of adverse possession, but they have utterly failed to prove so by any convincing evidence while the defendants have produced rent receipt which was marked as exhibit-'Ghat series which aptly proves that the defendants have possession in the suit properties. He further submits that in order to validate a deed of exchange by any persons who are not the national of this country has to show and prove power of attorney supposed to be given by the person who belonged to the land in this country and by virtue of which, the Government used to validate such deed of exchange and in compliance so, the deed of exchange executed in favour of defendant No.1 was validated by the Government on 03.01.1975 which was marked as exhibit. But on the contrary, though the plaintiff claimed to have a deed of exchange from Kanai Lal Ghosh and Moniram Ghosh by their predecessor, Habibur Rahman, but not a scrap of paper of such sort has ever produced by the plaintiff which clearly implies that the plaintiffs have utterly failed to show the basis of acquiring title in the suit land. He further submits that in order to establish title by way of adverse possession, the claim has to be made against the real owner in assertion of their hostile title and denying the title of the real owner. But in the instant case, the plaintiff though claimed title against the defendants, they did not admit defendant No.1 as the real owner in the suit land and without admitting said defendant No.1 as the real owner in the suit property, the suit could not be maintained. He further submits that the title in favour of the defendants has rightly been accrued and acted upon in view of subsequent transfer of near about 17 decimals land to defendant Nos.2-3 which clearly proves that having been acquired right, title and possession over the suit proper-ties, the defendants transferred the suit properties on acquiring title by virtue of the deed of exchange dated 03.01.1975. He further submits that though the plain-tiffs based their title over the suit proper-ties by virtue of sale deed dated 03.04.1967, there has been no mention of any date in the alleged deed, neither in the schedule nor in the body of the said deed. In that regard, he candidly submits that since there has been no date basing on the said, no title can be passed in favour of the plaintiffs and that there being no merit in the leave petition, the same is liable to be dismissed.

15. From the record, it appears that the petitioners as plaintiffs claimed to have purchased the suit land from Layebuddin Sarkar alias Liabuddin Sarkar, father of defendant No.1 by executing an exchange deed in lieu of his Indian property and have been possessing the same un-interruptedly. They further claimed that on the day of registration, Liabuddin Sarkar had to go to India and eventually, it was not possible on his part to go to the Sub-Registrar Office for registration and consequently, the said deed remained unregistered.

16. On the other hand, the respondents as defendants counter-claimed inter-alia that original owner, Kanai Lal Ghosh and Moniram Ghosh executed a deed of exchange which was duly validated by the Deputy Commissioner, Rajshahi through Exchange Case No.134/Sadar/ 1972-1973. It has been further alleged that the defendant-respondents duly released the suit property from the list of vested and non-resident property and got the same mutated in their names and also have been possessing the same on payment of rent to the Government. It has further been claimed that during the period of such enjoyment, defendant No.1 transferred 8.14 acres lands to defendant No.2 on 25.11.1986 as well as some portion of land to defendant No.3 on 18.12.1986 who used to possess the aforesaid property and as such, they prayed for dismissal of the suit.

17. Having considered the entire facts and circumstances, it appears that the present respondents, Abul Kashem and others, have been able to prove their claim by sufficient evidence that they have got their predecessor's exchanges deed duly validated by the Deputy Commissioner, Rajshahi, on the basis of which they have been able to release the suit properties from list of vested and non-resident property and also have been able to mutate their names in the suit khatian.

18. On the other hand, the petitioners' claim is based on an unregistered sale deed which does not confer any title to the recipient of such deed as per provision of sections 17 and 49 of the Registration Act. The petitioners' further claim is that they have been inducted into possession in 1967 and being in such possession, they have acquired statutory title by way of adverse possession and as such, the petitioners are entitled to get a decree for such statutory right. The defendant-respondents have vehemently opposed such statement of uninterrupted 'possession on adducing three DWs including defendant No.1, Abul Kashem. At this stage, it is impossible to taste the veracity of those wit-nesses, but it can be safely concluded that title follows possession. Over and above, it reveals from the record that La.yebuddin, alleged vendor of the plaintiff had to go to India frequently even on the date of registration of deed. Thus, the uninterrupted possession as alleged by the plaintiff is not at all believable. Apart from that, the act of hostility in support of their adverse possession is absent in this case which is very much essential with a view to acquire such statutory title. It is a bonafide proposition that in order to obtain a statutory title by way of adverse possession, the possession is to be not only openly but also hostily, notoriously runs against the true owner beyond statutory period of limitation and also that apparent show of exclusive possession is not sufficient of defeat the title of the real owner. The evidence from the plaintiffs (petitioners) side is totally lacking for establishing the fact that from a particular point of time, they started to possess the suit land asserting their title by adverse possession denying that title of the real owner to their knowledge as well as to the knowledge of the others as has been held by their lordships in the case of Shaik Farik-Vs-Abdul Wadud Sikder reported in 58 DLR (AD) 2006 page 248.

19. It reveals from exhibit-Thha' filed by the defendant that on 19.12.1987, one Selim Sarder, Abu Sarder, Anower Sarder and Shamsur Sarder who are none but the sons of plaintiff No.1 filed this petition before the Deputy Commissioner, Rajshahi for allotting the suit land in their favour stating that they have been possessing the suit land for some years (কয়েক বছর). If that very assertion is taken to be true, then the very assertion of the plaintiff that they have been enjoying title and possession for more than 30 years proves to be totally untrue. Thus, it appears that no adverse possession by way of statutory title has been accrued in favour of the plaintiff.

<u>20. On perusal of the judgment of the High Court Division, it appears that the learned Single Judge came to the conclusion that the judgment of the Appellate Court was not a proper judgment of reversal. In coming to this conclusion, the said Court noticed that the trial Court had considered the material evidence in detail in coming to its finding of title and possession in favour of the plaintiffs, but the Appellate Court without discussing the evidence had abruptly reversed the findings of fact arrived at by the trial Court on holding that the petitioners have acquired statutory title on the basis of their possession which is not sufficient to detect the title of real owner. We find no error of law in the view taken by the High Court Division.</u>

<u>21. On perusal of the impugned judgment, we find that there was no ambiguity, non-consideration and misreading of fact in the same which calls for no interference.</u>

<u>22. Therefore, we find no merit in this petition and accordingly, the same is dismissed.</u>

End.

Mr. Kamal-ul-Alam, Senior Advocate instructed by Mr. Zainul Abedin, Advocate-on-Record.   For the Appellants 
Mr. Abdul Wadud Bhuiyan Senior Advocate with Mr. Subrata Saha, Advocate instructed by Mr. Abdul Hye Bhuiyan, Advocate-on-Record. For the Respondent No.1 (a), (b) & (c)

case_source: (From the judgment and decree dated 20.03.2012 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 2359 of 2006)
full_judgment:
Zinat Ara J. This Civil Appeal No. 220 of 2016 is directed against the judgment and decree dated 20.03.2012 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 2359 of 2006 making the rule absolute and thereby setting aside the judgment and decree dated 26.04.2006 of the 2nd Court of Additional District Judge, Brahmanharia in Title Appeal No. 118 of 1997 and restoring the judgment and decree dated 30.10.1997 of the Court of Senior Assistant Judge, Brahmanbaria in Title Suit No. 10 of 1994.

<u>Background of the case</u>

<u>2. Plaintiff Gangacharan Debnath and others filed Title Suit No. 10 of 1994 before the Court of Senior Assistant Judge, Brahmanbaria (the trial Court) for declaration of their title to the property measuring an area of 15 decimals of homestead property of C.S Plot No. 1069, S.A Plot No. 1350 under Mouza, Police Station and District-Brahmanbaria (previously Tripura District) as described in the 2nu schedule of the plaint (hereinafter referred to as the suit property) and 23 decimals of pond of C.S Plot No. 1068, S.A Plot No. 1349 under Mouza, Police Station and District-Brahmanbaria (previously Tripura District) as described in the 3rd schedule of the plaint(hereinafter referred to as the suit pond) stating, inter alia, that the suit property and suit pond along with some other lands as described in the 1st schedule of the plaint originally belonged to Kunja Mohan Debnath (Kunja), Piyare Mohan Debnath (Piyare), Raj Mohan Nath (Raj) and Sarupa Sundari Nath (Sarupa). Their names were duly recorded in C.S khatian Nos. 632, 633 and 634 of C.S. Plot Nos. 1064, 1069, 1060, 1068 and 1063 for 83 decimals of land. Kunja died leaving behind wife Muktakeshi Nath (Muktakeshi) and daughter Suchitra Debi (Suchitra), Muktakeshi filed Title Suit No. 241 of 1933 against the father of the defendant Nos. 1-3 i,e. Banamali Debnath (Banamali), son of Piyare, Raj and others for partition of the 1st schedule property along with other properties. Mahananda Debnath (Mahananda), father of the plaintiff Nos. 2 and 3 were added as defendant No. 4 in the said suit. The said suit being Title Suit No. 241 of 1933 was decreed on compromise. According to Solenama and final decree the plaintiff of partition suit Muktakeshi got 15 decimals of homestead land from C.S. Plot No. 1069, 05 decimals from C.S Plot No. 1064, 01 decimal from C.S. Plot No. 1062 and 10 /9 decimals i.e. 4/9 share from C.S. Plot No. 1068 out of 23 decimals. Banamali, father of the defendant Nos. 1-3 got 13 decimals of lands in some other plots and Chapala got 05 decimals. Muktakeshi by registered deed date 07.05.1942 sold the suit property and 5 ¾ decimals of the pond out of the suit pond in favour of Sanatan Debnath (Sanatan) and delivered possession to Sanatan. Suchitra got 05 decimals of land of C.S. Plot No. 1064 after the death of her mother. Banamali, father of the defendant Nos. 1-3 fraudulently created a deed of purchase from Suchitra, Thereafter, Banamali filed a pre-emption case against Sanatan in the 2nd Court of Munsif, Brahmanbaria in the year 1945. But that suit was dismissed on contest. Thereafter, Banamali filed another suit being Title Suit No. 20 of 1947 and the said suit was also dismissed on contest. Sanatan had been in exclusive possession of the suit property and 5 ¾ decimals share in the suit pond for more than 12(twelve) years. Thereafter, in 1952, he sold the suit property and his share to the suit pond in favour of Gangacharan Debnath (Gangacharan) plaintiff No. 1 and Mahananda, father of the plaintiff Nos. 2 and 3 verbally on receipt of part consideration money. But Gangacharan and Mahananada could not pay the entire price for which the document of sale could not be registered. As they were relatives, Gangacharan and Mahananda did not deem it necessary for registration of a sale deed in their favour from Sanatan. The plaintiffs have been in possession of the suit property by erecting homestead thereon and enjoying their share of the suit pond with other co-sharers. Banamali once set fire to the house of the plaintiffs for which all the documents of the plaintiffs were burnt into ashes. The plaintiffs filed a criminal case and Banamali was convicted in the said case. Presently, the plaintiffs and defendant Nos. 1-3 and others have been in possession of the suit pond jointly as owners thereof. The defendants with false statements filed Miscellaneous Case No. 19 of 1993-1994 against mutation of the suit property in the names of the plaintiffs. Upon hearing, mutation of the suit property in the names of the plaintiffs was cancelled. However, the Assistant Commissioner (Land), Brahmanbaria observed that the 2nd schedule i.e. the suit property and the suit pond are in possession of the plaintiffs. The defendant Nos. 13 were never owners or possessors of the 2nd schedule property i.e. the suit property. Recently, after cancellation of the names of the plaintiffs in the mutation case, the defendants are claiming that they are the owners of the suit property. In the above backdrop, the plaintiffs filed the suit for declaration of their title to the above properties by adverse possession.</u>

3. Defendant Nos. 1-3 contested the suit by filing a written statement denying the averments made in the plaint of the suit contending, inter alia, that the suit property was duly recorded in the names of C.S. recorded owners and thereafter by amicable partition among the C.S. recorded owners Kunja and Sarupa got 58 decimals of land out of C.S. Plot Nos. 1069, 1068, 1064, 1060, 1063 and 1052 in their shares along with a share in the suit pond.

4. C.S. recorded tenant Mohan Nath while owner of C.S. Plot Nos. 1068 and 1064 measuring an area of 14 ½ decimals of land, died leaving behind 2(two) sons, namely, Puma Chand Debnath (Puma) and Banamali. The said sons became 8 annas owner each of the said property. While Kunja and Sarupa were in ejmali possession of 58 decimals of property, Sarupa died leaving behind Kunja as her sole heir. Kunja while owner of 29 decimals of land out of 58 decimals of land, gifted 29 decimals of land out of the said land to his wife Muktakeshi and grandsons Puma and Radhika. Radhika gifted his share to his wife Chapala. Chapala transferred the said land to Kali Mohan. Kunja while owner of the rest 29 decimals of land out of 58 decimals of land, died leaving behind wife Muktakeshi and daughter Suchitra as his heirs. Muktakeshi while owner of 29 decimals of land with Suchitra by inheritence and 9 2/3 decimals of land by way of gift from her husband, died leaving behind Suchitra as her sole heir. Suchitra became the owner of 38 2/3  decimals of land out of the said property and she due to legal necessity sold the said land to Banamali by a registered deed dated 24.02.1944 and delivered possession to him. Subsequently, the said deed was corrected as a plot number was wrongly recorded in the previous deed. But the said corrected deed was subsequently lost. Piyare while owner of 14 V2 decimals of land died leaving behind his son Puma and Banamali. They became the owners of the said land and also became the owner of 9 2/3 decimals of land from Kunja. Puma died unmarried leaving Banmali as his sole heir and Banamali became owner of total 62 2/3 decimals of land by way of inheritance and purchase and he had been in uninterrupted possession of the said land including the suit property and suit pond peacefully by exercising his own right for more than 12(twelve) years and his name was correctly recorded in the S.A. khatian. Mahananda, father of the plaintiff Nos. 2 and 3 and their mother Indumoyee became shelterless after death of their father and they being relatives of Banamali, he permitted them to live in 08 decimals of land on the suit property and he was in possession of the rest 07 decimals of land out of it. Defendant Nos. 1-3 are now in possession of rest 07 decimals of land and also owner of 08 decimals of land. The plaintiffs were ejectable licensee of the defendants since the lifetime of their father but they collusively mutated their names relating to the suit property. Therefore, the defendants filed the miscellaneous case and the names of the plaintiffs were cancelled from the record-of-rights. Muktakeshi never filed any suit for partition against Banamali and Mahananda was not defendant No. 4 in the suit. Muktakeshi did not get 15 decimals of land of C.S. Plot No.1069 (suit property) and 109 decimals of land of C.S. Plot No. 1068 (suit pond). Muktakeshi neither sold the suit property to Sanatan by any registered deed nor he was in possession of the suit property at any time. The statements made in the plaint are all false and defendant Nos.1-3 are in possession of the suit property. The suit is liable to be dismissed.

Issues

5. The following issues were framed by the trial Court for deciding the suit:

“বিচার্য বিষয় সমূহঃ

১। বর্তমান আকারে ও প্রকারে অত্র মোকদ্দমা রক্ষণীয় কি না?

২। উপর্যুক্ত তায়দাদ ও কোর্ট ফি যুক্তি অত্র মোকদ্দমা দায়ের হইয়াছে কি না?

৩। নালিশী সম্পত্তিতে বাদীপক্ষের বিরুদ্ধে স্বত্ত্ব (Adverse possession) অর্জিত হইয়াছে কি না?

৪। বাদীপক্ষ তাহাদের প্রার্থীত মতে নালিশী দ্বিতীয় তপছিলের ভূমিতে ৪০ বৎসরের একক দখল এবং তৃতীয় তপছিলের পুকুরে এজমালিতে দখল আছে কি না?

৫। বাদী পক্ষ প্রার্থীত ডিক্রী পাইতে পারেন কি না?

Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 303 of 2013
