II. Because both the trial Court and the High Court Division in arriving at their findings as to possession of the plaintiffs relied upon exhibit-6 series which are tax receipts issued from

office of Brahmanbaria Pourashava and exhibit-7 which is a rent receipt but while relying on those documents both the Courts failed to notice that no plot number has been mentioned in the said Pourashava tax receipts and those are only for the years 1991 to 1995 and rent is only for the year 1399 B.S. corresponding to 1992 A.D. and, as such, came to an erroneous findings that the plaintiffs proved their title by adverse possession and therefore, the impugned judgment and order is liable to be set aside."

10. This appeal is the outcome of the aforesaid civil petition.

Arguments of the appellant’s side

11. Mr. Kamal-ul-Alam, the learned Senior Advocate appearing for the appellants, has taken us through the various judgments and decrees passed by the trial Court, the Appellate Court, the High Court Division, the connected materials on record and put forward the following arguments before us:

1. The plaintiffs filed the suit for declaration of their title to the suit property and suit pond by way of adverse possession for more than 30/35 years. But the owners of the plots against whom the plaintiffs claim title to those properties by adverse possession were not made parties to the suit and therefore, the suit was not at all maintainable.

2. P.W.1 Gangacharan in his cross-examination admits that defendant Nos. 1-3 are in possession in 07 decimals of land out of the suit property and, as such, the impugned judgment and order passed by the High Court Division is without application of judicial mind and thus, the same is liable to be set aside.

3. Both the trial Court and the High Court Division though mainly decided the suit and revision considering Pourashava tax receipts issued from office of Brahmanbaria Pourashava (exhibit-6 series) and the rent receipt (exhibit-7), but both the Courts failed to notice that plot numbers were not mentioned in the said Pourashava tax receipts and those are only for the years 1991 to 1995 and the rent receipt is only for the year 1399 B.S. and the mutation in the names of the plaintiffs in the record-of-rights has been cancelled. The trial Court and the High Court Division without considering the value of those documents and the evidence on record erroneously decided that the plaintiffs proved their title to the suit property and the suit pond by way of adverse possession.

4. The decision of the Appellate Court relating to ownership and possession of defendant Nos. 1-3 relating to 07 decimals of land was correct as plaintiff No. 1 himself admitted it in his cross-examination. But the trial Court and the High Court Division without properly considering the evidence on record unlawfully decided that the plaintiffs are the owners of the entire suit property (2na schedule).

5. It is admitted in the plaint that both the plaintiffs and the defendants are in joint possession of the suit pond.

Therefore, the suit for declaration of title on the basis of the adverse possession in the suit pond where admittedly other co-sharers are in joint possession is not at all maintainable. Thus, the judgment and order passed by the High Court Division is liable to be set aside and those of the Appellate Court is liable to be restored.

12. Mr. Alam, in support of his submissions has relied on the decisions of the following cases: (i) Pushpa Rani Saha Podder Vs. Rash Mohan Saha being dead his heirs:- Kartick Chowdhury Saha and others reported in 10 MLR (AD) 345; (ii) Md. Sheikh Farid and others Vs. Abdul Wadud Sikder and others reported in 12 MLR (AD) 201; (iii) Md. Ali Bepary and others Vs, Garupranjan Chakraborty and others reported in 14 BLC (AD) 97; (iv) Md. Abdul Rahman Vs. Abdul Jabbar and others reported in 13 DLR (HCD) 576; (v) Mt. Jahan Ara Begum Vs. A.L.Md. Shamsul Hoque reported in 27 DLR (AD) 129; and (vi) Probir Kumar Rakshit Vs. Abdas Sabur and others reported in 14 BLC (AD) 28.

Arguments of the respondents side

13. In reply, Mr. Abdul Wadud Bhuiyan, the learned Senior Advocate appearing with Mr. Subrata Saha, the learned Advocate for the plaintiff-respondents, takes us through the judgment and decree of various Courts and the evidence on record and contends as under:

a) The plaintiffs by examining as many as 7(seven) witnesses proved their adverse possession in the suit property and the suit pond since the period of their predecessors in interest for more than 30/35 years.

b) The defendants failed to prove that they are in possession of the suit property for more than 12 (twelve) years. Rather, the defendants' witnesses admit that the plaintiffs are in possession of the suit property (homestead).

c) The report relating to cancellation of plaintiffs' mutation also shows that the plaintiffs were/are in possession of the suit property. However, mutation in their names was cancelled as notices were not duly served upon all the co-sharers at the time of mutation of their names in the record-of-rights.

d) The owners through whom the plaintiffs claim the suit property and suit pond were/are not opposing their title to or possession in the suit property or the suit pond. Rather, defendant Nos. 1-3 were/are only claiming their ownership, title to and possession in the suit property and the suit pond. Therefore, the original owners were not necessary parties to the suit and the suit was maintainable and the appeal is thus liable to be dismissed.

14. However, Mr. Abdul Wadud Bhuiyan could not give any satisfactory reply as to how a suit for declaration of title to the suit pond by way of adverse possession would be maintainable, as admittedly all the co-sharers including defendant Nos. 1-3 and the plaintiffs are in joint possession of the suit pond.

15. Mr. Bhuiyan, in support of his arguments relating to acquisition of plaintiffs' title to the suit property by way of adverse possession, has relied on the decisions in the cases of-(1) Abdus Sattar Vs. Abdul Rahman @ Abdur Rahman and others reported in 44 DLR (AD) 100; and (2) Mir Laik Ali Vs. Standard Vacuum Oil Company (ES.50) and Abdur Razzak reported in 16 DLR (SC) 287.

Examination of Records

16. We have examined the judgments and decrees of various Courts and the evidence on record.

<u>Deliberation of the Court</u>

<u>17. It is an admitted proposition that C.S. recorded owners of the suit property and the suit pond along with other properties were Kunja, Raj, Piyare and Sarupa. The plaintiffs claimed their title to the suit property by adverse possession for the last 30/35 years.</u>

<u>18. In support of their case, the plaintiffs filed Municipality tax receipts and a rent receipt (exhibit-6 series and exhibit-7 respectively). However, those receipts are not relating to payment of Municipal tax to the Municipality or rent to the Government continuously for the last 30-35 years. Municipal tax receipts are for a few years and the rent receipt is, only for one year and those receipts do not contain the plot numbers. So, it cannot be presumed that those were/are for the suit property or the suit pond. However, the plaintiffs' case is that Muktakeshi sold the suit property by the deed dated 07.05.1942 to Sanatan and the other side denied it. The plaintiffs' further case is that Gangacharan and Mahananda purchased the suit property and the share of the suit pond from Sanatan who had purchased the same from Muktakeshi. Anyway, the deed of purchase of Gangacharan and Mahananda could not be registered and the actual owners did not claim the suit property or the suit pond from Gangacharan and Mahananda or heirs of Mahananda. The plaintiffs claim the suit property and the suit pond by way of adverse possession through Gangacharan and Mahananda against defendant Nos. 1-3, who claimed ownership of the suit property and the suit pond. Therefore, it cannot be said that the suit is not maintain-able as only the persons claiming owner-ship have been made parties to the suit.</u>

19. The trial Court decreed the suit by way of adverse possession in favour of the plaintiffs holing that the plaintiffs have been in possession of the suit property peacefully and uninterruptedly for the last 30/35 years. The trial Court also declared the plaintiffs' title to 53/4 decimals out of the suit pond in ejmali.

20. The Appellate Court, on the other hand, allowed the appeal in part and declared the plaintiffs' title to 08 decimals of land (part of suit property) of C.S. Plot No. 1069 only by way of adverse possession in consideration of the evidence on record.

21. The High Court Division set aside the judgment of the Appellate Court and restored those of the trial Court.

22. Since the decision of the Appellate Court and the High Court Division are different, we have to decide the merit of this appeal on the evidence laid down by the parties relating to possession.

23. The plaintiffs in support of their possession have examined 7(seven) witnesses.

24. P.W.1 Gangacharan Debnath described the details of the plaint case. P.W.1 stated that they are in possession of the suit property since 1952 from the time of purchase thereof by Gangacharan and Mahananda and that they got delivery of possession of the suit property in the year 1952 from Sanatan. However, he could not remember the exact date. He also stated that although a deed was executed between Sanatan and Gangacharan as well as Mahananda it was not registered. It appears that he supported his case during the cross-examination stating as under:

“মুক্তকেশী কর্তৃক ০৭-০৫-৪২ ইং তারিখের সনাতন বরাবরে দলিলটি আদালতে দাখিল করি নাই। মুক্তকেশী যখন সনাতনের নিকট বিক্রয় করে তখন আমি উপস্থিত ছিলাম এবং ১৯৪৪ সনে উক্ত খরিদ বিক্রি হয় এবং তখন নিত্যানন্দ পাল (মনত), স্বীয় লক্ষী কান্ত দেবনাথ, উপেন্দ্র দেবনাথ (মৃত), এরা তখন উপস্থিত ছিল। উক্ত ব্যক্তিদের কেহ জীবিত নাই এবং উক্ত লেন-দেনের ব্যক্তিগন জীবিত নাই। বিক্রির পরে পুকুরে মুক্তকেশীর তিন আনা অংশ ছিল। মুক্তকেশী নাঃ পুকুরের অংশ ইন্দমোহন ও গোপিনাথ সাহা বরাবর ২ পয়সার অংশ, পরেশ

দেবনাথ বরাবর এক পয়সা, নারায়ন খান বরাবর ১ পয়সা, সুরেন্দ্র নাথ বরাবর ২ পয়সা, অমর পাল বরাবর ২ পয়সা, লক্ষীকান্ত দেবনাথ বরাবর এক আনা অংশ বিক্রি করিয়াছে। আমি উক্ত বিক্রয় দলিলে সাক্ষী ছিলাম না। মুক্তকেশী আমার সহিত পরামর্শ করিয়া উক্ত বিক্রয় করে নাই এবং আমি তাহাতে উপস্থিত ছিলাম না। সত্য নহে যে মুক্তকেশী কোন জায়গা সনাতন বরাবর বিক্রয় করে নাই। মাইঝ পাড়া গ্রামে সনাতন নামে কোন লোক ছিল না ইহা সত্য নহে। বনমালী দেবনাথ (১-৩ নং বিবাদীর পিতা) নামে দলিলের সময় উপস্থিতে ছিলাম না। বনমালী নামে দলিল আমার কাছে আছে। বনমালী সুচিত্রা দেবনাথ হইতে খরিদ করিয়াছে। সূচিত্রা ও বনমালীর মধ্যে বেচাকেনা, কথাবার্তার সময় ছিলাম না। সনাতনের ওয়ারিশ কে আছে বলিতে পারি না । সনাতন আমার বরাবর আনরেজিষ্ট্রি দলিল দিয়েছিল এবং উক্ত দলিলটি পুড়িয়া গিয়াছে। উক্ত দলিল পুড়িবার বিষয়ে আমার উকিল সাহেবকে বলিয়াছি। সত্য নয় যে, বনমালি মৃত্যুবরণ করিলে ১-৩ নং বিবাদী তাহার ওয়ারিশ হিসাবে নাঃ ভূমিতে মালিক দখলকার আছে। সত্য নহে যে, বনমালির মৃত্যুর পর বনমালির পুত্র উত্তরকারী বিবাদীগণের নিকট হইতে অনুমতি লইয়া আমরা দখলকার আছি ১০৬৯ দাগে ৮ শতকে। সত্য নয় যে, বেআইনীভাবে খারিজা খতিয়ান করিলে তাহা বাতিল হইয়াছে। সত্য নয় যে, নাঃ জমি হইতে চলিয়া যাইতে উত্তরকারী বিবাদীগণ তলব তাগাদা করিয়াছে। সত্য নয় যে, আমরা নাঃ জমি হইতে চলিয়া যাইতে আইনতঃ বাধ্য। ১০৬৯ দাগে ৭ শতক ভূমি উত্তরকারী বিবাদি দখলকার আছে। সত্য নহে যে, উত্তরকারী বিবাদি গণ বক্রি ভূমিতে সবজি করিয়া ও পুকুরে মাছ চাষ করিয়া দখলকার আছে।

১০৬৮ দাগের পুকুরে আমাদের দখল নাই ইহা সত্য নহে। ১০৬৮ দাগের পুকুর বাবদ দখলের কাগজ দাখিল করি নাই।”

25. It appears that the Appellate Court decided that plaintiff No. 1 Gangacharan himself admitted possession of contested defendant Nos. 1, 2 and 3 by deposing “১০৬৯ দাগে ৭ শতক ভূমি উত্তরকারী বিবাদী দখলকার আছে” But from his statement as a whole, quoted hereinbefore, it appears that in the next sentence, he denied “সত্য নহে যে, উত্তরকারী বিবাদীগণ বক্রি ভূমিতে সবজী করিয়া ও পুকুরে মাছ চাষ করিয়া দখলকার আছে”.

26. Moreover, from the deposition of P.W.1 as a whole, it is evident that in fact, P.W.1 denied that the possession of defendant Nos. 1-3 in 07 decimals of land or in any part of the suit property. But due to a "।" (দাঁড়ি) between the words, the Appellate Court decided that plaintiff No. 1 (P.W.1) admitted the possession of the defendant Nos. 1-3, which is not the correct picture. Moreover, P.W.2 Manmohan Majumder stated that he constructed his house in 1973 near the suit property. Since then he has seen the plaintiffs in possession of the suit property. This witness is an old man of 80 years. P.W.3 Poresh Chandra Debnath aged 45 years stated that he has been seeing the plaintiffs in possession of the suit property since his childhood. P.W.5 Kazi Abdul Bari stated that in 1969 he started living near the suit property. Since then be has seen the plaintiffs in possession of the suit property. P.W.4 Baikontha Debnath, P.W. 6 Radha Charan Debnath and P.W.7 Surendra Chandra Paul all in a voice sup-ported possession of the plaintiffs in the suit property for the last 30-35 years. Some from the years 1969, 1971 and 1973, when they started living near the suit property i.e. more than 20 years back. It also appears that P.W.4 Baikontha Debnath deposed that the plaintiffs' house is at the north side of the suit pond and the defendant Nos. 1-3's house is at the south side of the suit pond. D.W.1 Binod Biheri Debnath in his cross-examination also admitted that “নালিশী পুকুরের লাগ দক্ষিণে আমাদের বসত ঘর। নালিশী পুকুরের লাগ উত্তরে বাদীদের বসত বাড়ী”।

27. Now let us examine how far the contesting defendants have been able to prove their case of possession in the suit property.

28. D.W.1 in his examination-in-chief supports the defendants' case. During cross-examination, he initially denied that Muktakeshi filed a suit against his father Banamali and Raj being Partition Suit No. 241 of 1939 but then stated that suit was collusive and that he has no knowledge about the suit. He claims that the plain-tiffs' father was in permissive possession of 08 decimals of land from the suit property but could not say if there was any agreement between Mahananda Debnath, plaintiff Nos. 2 and 3's father and the defendant Nos. 1-3's father. He admitted that the defendants never issued any notice for their eviction at any time. He also admits neither their father nor they ever paid Municipal/Pourashava taxes of the suit property. He also admits that the deed through which his father allegedly claimed the suit property from Suchitra was destroyed in 1971. He also admits that presently a homestead is situated in the suit property. He further admits that their house is situated towards the contiguous south of the suit pond and the house of the plaintiffs is towards the north side of the suit pond. He further admits that there is a road after the suit pond and then the suit property. He further admitted property. He further admitted “নালিশা পুকুরের লাগ দক্ষিণে আমাদের বসত ঘর। নালিশী পুকরের লাগ উত্তরে বাদীদের নালিশী বাড়ী। পুকুরটি ১৬০-১৬৫ হাত লম্বা হইবে । নালিশী পুকুরের সংলগ্ন উত্তরে পৌরসভার রাস্তা তৎপর নালিশী বাড়ী। নালিশী বাড়ীর উত্তর/দক্ষিণ্/পূর্ব/ পশ্চিম ভিটিতে ঘর আছে। বাড়ীতে পাকা ল্যাট্রিন ও টিউব-ওয়েল আছে। নালিশী ভূমি একটি Compact এবং চারিদিকে ওয়াল এবং তাহাতে বাহির হইবার জন্য বেড়ার গেট আছে ।”Thus, from the statement of D.W.1, it is clear that the suit property is a house with boundary walls. Therefore, it is hardly believable that those defendants are in possession in part of the suit property by cultivating vegetables.

29. D.W.2 Abdul Kadir claims that his Uncle Bashu Miah used to cultivate the suit property by taking 'Barga' and that the plaintiffs are in possession of half of the suit property and the rest are in the possession of the defendants. During cross-examination, he could not say the name of the father of the plaintiffs. He also admits that the suit house is surrounded with Bera (বেড়া) in three side and there are four houses in four side of the suit property. Thus, it appears that he could not prove possession of the defendants in any part of the suit property.

30. D.W.3 Dhan Miah though mentioned that he was a 'Bargader' in the suit property under Banamali relating to half of the suit property, but during cross-examination, he admits that “নালিশী বাড়ীর ৪ ভিটিতে ৪টি ঘর আছে” So it appears from his statement, there are four houses in four side of the suit property, which is also the case of the plaintiffs.

31. D.W.4 Md. Mostaque Ahmed stated that the deed of purchase of Banamali and Suchitra as shown in the certified copy tallied with the volume. The deed of correction also tallied with the volume. So, it appears that he is an official witness only.

32. It appears from the evidence on record as discussed that the plaintiffs though could not produce the document of purchase of the suit property from Mulctakeshi by Sanatan or purchase of the suit property by Gangacharan and Mahananda from Sanatan, but they could prove their exclusive uninterrupted possession in the suit property by erecting four houses and living there for more than 30/35 years. On the other hand, the defendants' witnesses could not prove their possession. Rather, one of the defendants, D.W.1 admits that the suit property is a compact property with boundaries in four side of the land.

33. In consideration of the evidence on record, we are of the view that both the trial Court as well as the High Court Division properly decided that the plaintiffs are in possession of the suit property uninterruptedly for more than 30-35 years.

We find no misreading or non-consideration of the evidence on record by the trial Court or the High Court Division. Therefore, the declaration of the plaintiffs' title to the suit property (C.S. Plot No. 1069, 2nd schedule property) appears to be lawful. It appears that the Appellate Court considering only a part of the statement made by P. W.1 during the cross-examination decided that the plaintiffs admitted possession of the defendants relating to 07 decimals of land without considering the whole statement of the P. W.1 erroneously.

34. However, so far the suit pond is concerned, it appears that in the plaint of suit, the plaintiffs claimed adverse possession in the suit pond relating to some shares. It also appears that the defendant Nos. 1-3 also enjoy the suit pond as co-sharers along with other co-sharers jointly. From the deposition of witnesses it is also found that the plaintiffs, the defendants and other co-sharers enjoy the suit pond jointly. Therefore, the decision of the trial Court as well as the High Court Division declaring 53/4 decimals share of the suit pond to the plaintiffs by adverse possession is not tenable. The plaintiffs, the defendants and others are in ejmali (joint) possession of the suit pond. Ejmali possession of co-sharers in the suit pond means all of them are in joint possession of every inch of the suit pond. Thus, declaration of the plaintiffs' title to certain share of the suit pond by adverse possession by the trial Court and the High Court Division appears to be ,erroneous and liable to be interfered with.

35. We have considered the decisions as referred to by the learned Senior Advocates for the contending parties. We find that the decisions as referred to by Mr. Kamal-ul-Alam are not applicable in the instant case as the facts and circumstances of the present case is distinguishable with the facts and circumstances of the referred cases. Similarly, the decisions as referred to by Mr. Abdul Wadud Bhuiyan are not also applicable in this case as the facts of the referred cases are quite distinguishable from the instant case.

36. In view of the discussions made hereinbefore, we find part merit in the appeal.

37. Accordingly, the appeal is allowed in part without any order as to costs.

<u>38. The judgment and decree passed by the trial Court and the High, Court Division, so far as it relates to 3rd schedule property (suit pond) is hereby set aside and those of the Appellate Court i§ restored i.e. the suit relating to the 3rd schedule property is dismissed. The judgment and decree in favour of the plaintiffs relating to the suit property (2nd schedule) is hereby affirmed.</u>

End.

lawyer:

case_source: (From the judgment and order dated 10.12.2007, passed by the High Court Division in First Miscellaneous Appeal Nos. 86 of 2006 and 145 of 2007 along with Civil Rule Nos. 803(FM) of 2005 and 795(FM) of 2005.
full_judgment:
Mirza Hussain Haider J. Civil Appeal No. 375 of 2009 by leave and Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 216 of 2008 are directed against the judgment and order dated 10.12.2007, passed by the High Court Division in First Miscellaneous Appeal Nos. 86 of 2006 and 145 of 2007 respectively, allowing both the appeals and disposing of the connected Civil Rule Nos. 803(FM) of 2005 and 795(FM) of 2005 and thereby setting aside the judgment and order dated 21.5.2005 passed by the Fourth Artharin Adalat, Dhaka, in Miscellaneous Case Nos. 36 of 2003 and 35 of 2003 respectively filed under Order XXI Rule 58 read with section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure.

2. Since the facts and circumstances of both the cases are similar and the facts of Civil Appeal No. 375 of 2009 will govern Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 216 of 2008, as such the fact of Civil Appeal No. 375 of 2009 is narrated in short below:

3. That the present respondent No.2 (National Bank Limited) as plaintiff instituted Title Suit No. 32 of 1989 in the then Court of Subordinate Judge and First Commercial Court, Dhaka, against M/S. Cosmopolitan Trading Corporation and Abul Hossain (present respondent No. 3 and predecessor of present proforma respondent Nos. 4 to 13 of Civil Appeal No. 375 of 2009 respectively, who are also present respondent No. 23 and predecessor of present proforma respondent Nos. 24 to 33 of Civil Petition No. 216 of 2008 (respectively) as defendants for realization of loan, with interest, amounting to TK.38,91,338.00 stating inter alia that the present respondent No.3 M/s. Cosmopolitan Trading Corporation, for the purpose of its business, took loan of TK. 25,00,000/- from the plaintiff bank and Abul Hossain, the predecessor of the present respondent Nos. 4 to 13, signed the guarantee form as guarantor upon mortgaging the property as described in the schedule to the plaint alleging that Abul Hossain, the full brother of Dr. Abdul Mannan being appointed as the attorney of Dr. Abdul Mannan by registered Power of Attorney dated 23.10.1983 mortgaged 2.375 acres of land of SA Plot No. 2029 and 1.20 acres of land of SA Plot No. 91 to the plaintiff bank against the loan obtained by M/S. Cosmopolitan Trading Corporation belonging to Abdul Kader Patwari father-in-law of the said Abul Hossain. The said M/S. Cosmopolitan Trading Corporation having failed to repay the loan the bank instituted the said suit. The said suit was subsequently transferred to the Fourth Artharin Adalat, Dhaka and renumbered as Title Suit No. 177 of 1998 and was ultimately decreed ex parte by judgment and decree dated 8.4.2001. Thereaft6r, the plaintiff bank put the said decree into execution vide Title Execution Case No. 37 of 2002 in the First Additional Artharin Adalat, Dhaka. The said execution case was subsequently transferred to the Fourth Artharin Adalat, Dhaka and renumbered as Execution Case No. 1242 of 2003. Since Md. Abul Hossain, the constituted attorney of Dr. Abdul Mannan, the owner of the property under mortgage, died and Dr. Abdul Mannan himself also died earlier, the present appellant, Mohammad Zahangir Alam, was added in the execution case as judgment debtor being heir of late Dr. Abdul Mannan.

4. The present respondent No.1 (Concord Condominium Limited) having come to know about inclusion of its purchased property in the schedule of the Money Execution Case No. 37 of 2002, filed an application under Order XXI Rule 58 read with section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure as third party, which was registered as Miscellaneous Case No. 36 of 2003. It is stated in the said application that Dr. Abdul Mannan, the owner, by purchase, of 2.375 acres of land appertaining to CS and SA Plot No. 2029 of Mouza-Uttar Kaundia, P.S. Savar, Dhaka, who subsequently, out of the aforesaid 2.3750 acres of land, transferred 1.00 acre of land to Abdul Baten and Md. Abul Kashem by registered Deed No. 3166 dated 4.4.1994 and on the same day also he transferred 1.00 acre of land to Haji Md. Ahsan Ullah and Asia Begum by registered Deed No. 3167 dated 4.4.1994 and thereafter he transferred 0.3750 acre of land to Md. Ohidul Islam by registered Deed No. 3976 dated 27.4.1994 and as such he exhausted his entire share in the said plot. All the aforesaid transfer deeds were executed and registered by one Fazlul Hoque, the constituted attorney of Dr. Abdul Mannan. That all the aforesaid purchasers, in their turn, transferred the entire 2.375 acres of land to the present respondent No.1 (Concord Condomonium Limited) by three registered Deeds bearing Nos. 7789, 11111 and 15076 dated 7.7.1996, 9.9.1996 and 24.11.1996 respectively and since then the same has been in possession and enjoyment of the present respondent No.1 who got its name mutated and is paying rents in accordance with law.

5. On the other hand, the present respondent Nos. 1 to 21 of Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 216 of 2008 having come to know about the said ex parte decree and inclusion of their purchased property in the schedule of the Money Execution Case No. 37 of 2002 also filed Miscellaneous Case No. 35 of 2003 under Order XXI Rule 58 of the Code of Civil Procedure stating that Dr. Abdul Mannan, owner by purchase, of 1.1315 acres of land appertaining to SA Plot No. 91 of Mouza-Ranchandrapur, PS.  Mohammadpur, District-Dhaka, transferred .8750 acre of land out of the said 1.1315 acres of land, to Md. Abdul Baten and Md. Shahjahan Miah by four deeds of transfer all dated 7.12.1989(deed Nos. 4010-4013) who in their turn by different registered deeds transferred the same to different persons including the present respondent Nos. 1 to 21 of Civil Petition for. Leave to Appeal No. 216 of 2008, and accordingly they are in possession of the same.

6. On hearing the parties of both the Miscellaneous cases and on perusal of the materials on record, the Fourth Artharin Adalat, Dhaka, by judgment and order dated 21.5.2005, dismissed both the cases on contest holding that the property in question being not attached the miscellaneous cases under Order XXI Rule 58 read with section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure are mere abuse of the process of the Court; the petitioners failed to prove execution of their title deeds by Md. Fazlul Hoque, the alleged attorney of Dr. Abdul Mannan and on the other hand the execution of the mortgage deed by Abul Hossain, the constituted attorney of Dr. Abdul Mannan, being earlier to the purchase deeds of all the petitioners of both the cases and all such deeds being executed at a point of time when the entire property was under mortgage to the respondent bank and the same being not released from mortgage and that the power of attorney to Abul Hossain having been proved to be genuine and the petitioners having not specifically described their property in the schedule, both the miscellaneous cases are not maintainable.

7. Being aggrieved by the aforesaid judgment and order dated 21.5.2005 the present respondent No.1 of Civil Appeal No. 375 of 2009, preferred First Miscellaneous Appeal No. 86 of 2006 before the High Court Division and obtained order of stay of operation of the said judgment and order of the 4th Artharin Adalat, in Civil Rule No. 803(FM) of 2005. Similarly respondent Nos. 1 to 21 of Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 216 of 2008 also preferred First Miscellaneous Appeal No. 145 of 2007 and obtained stay of the operation of the said judgment and order of the 4th Artharin, in Civil Rule No. 795(FM) of 2005.

8. During the pendency of the aforesaid two miscellaneous appeals and the connected civil rules before the High Court Division, the appellants of both the aforesaid two miscellaneous appeals (present respondent Nos. 1 of the Civil Appeal and respondent Nos. 1 to 21 of the civil petition) jointly filed application on 22.12.2005 to the respondent bank expressing their willingness to pay off the decretal amount, if the mortgaged property is released in their favour, on the basis of which, negotiations started between the parties and ultimately the respondent bank, by letter dated 3.9.2009, informed the appellants of both the aforesaid miscellaneous appeals that since they agreed to withdraw the appeals and assumed the liabilities of the decreetal amount of TK.50,00,000/- it had no objection if they pay off the said amount subject to the decision of the Court. After receiving the said letter the appellants of both the miscellaneous appeals filed two applications before the appellate Court for disposal of both the said miscellaneous appeals with direction upon the respondent bank to release the mortgaged property on accepting TK.50,00,000/= and as per direction of the Court the appellants filed applications stating that they had purchased 14 Pay Orders of different banks in favour of the respondent bank for a sum of TK.50,00,000/= and accordingly they are ready to hand over the same to Mr. ASM Abdur Razzaque the learned Advocate for the respondent bank and thereby sought necessary directions.

9. Mr. ASM Abdur Razzaque, the learned Advocate appearing for the respondent bank before the High Court Division, admitted that the parties have reached to an agreement outside Court and the bank has no objection to release the mortgaged property in favour of the appellants of the two miscellaneous appeals since they have agreed to pay TK.50,00000/= in full satisfaction of the decreetal amount.

<u>10. Considering the aforesaid facts and circumstances, the High Court Division, by the impugned judgment and order dated 10.12.2007, allowed both the first miscellaneous appeals and disposed of the connected rules upon setting aside the judgment and order dated 21.5.2005 passed by the Fourth Artharin Adalat, Dhaka, in the Miscellaneous Case Nos. 35 and 36 of 2003 and directed the respondent bank to release the mortgaged property and handover the connected title 'deeds, submitted at the time of creating mortgage, which are lying with the respondent bank, in favour of the appellants of both the first miscellaneous appeals.</u>

11. Now the present appellant being the heir of late Dr. Abdul Mannan filed two Civil Petitions for Leave to Appeal Nos. 215 and 216 both of 2008 against the impugned judgment and order dated 10.12.2007 passed by the. High Court Division and obtained leave in Civil Petition No. 215 of 2008 which gave rise to Civil Appeal No. 375 of 2009. But Civil Petition No. 216 of 2008 being not moved earlier leave was yet to be granted. Hence, the same is being heard now along with the appeal.

12. Since, the subject matter and the question of law involved in the civil appeal and the civil petition are same, they are taken up together for hearing and disposal.

13. Mr. Habibul Islam Bhuiyan, the learned Senior Advocate appearing on behalf of the appellant and the petitioner in both the cases submits that as per provision of section 41(1) of the Artharin Adalat Ain, 2003 the miscellaneous appeals filed by the present respondents before the High Court Division are not maintainable since the value of the same is TK.38,91,338.00, which is below TK. 50,00,000/= and as such, the impugned judgment and order is not sustainable in law. He next submits that both the aforesaid miscellaneous appeals were filed without depositing the statutory deposit of 50% of the decreetal amount as required under section 41(1) of the Ain and as such on this score also the same are not maintainable. Lastly, he submits that no order of the Artharin Adalat is entertainable by any Court which is not authorized or empowered under section 20 of the Ain and as such he prayed that the impugned order is liable to be set aside and the appeal is liable to be allowed and the civil petition is also to be disposed of in the light of the appeal.

14. On the other hand, Mr. ASM. Abdur Razzaque, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the respondent bank in both the cases submits that the High Court Division did not commit any illegality n passing the judgment and order as the same are passed on admission/consent of both the parties on the basis of compromise and as such, the same are liable to be affirmed by this Division.

15. To resolve the dispute raised in this appeal and in the civil petition, it is required to see the chronology of events in these two cases. It appears from the record that admittedly the property in question was mortgaged to the National Bank Ltd., the present respondent No.2 of the civil appeal against the loan sanctioned in favour of the present respondent No.3 of the appeal, by Abul Hossain, the constituted attorney of Dr. Abdul Mannan, who was the owner of the property in question, pursuant to the Power of Attorney dated 23.10.1983. But, the present respondent No.3 having failed to repay the loan the respondent bank instituted Title Suit no.177 of 1998 against the present respondent No.3, M/S Cosmopolitan Trading Corporation and Abul Hossen, predecessor of respondent Nos. 4 to 13 for realization of unpaid loan. The said suit was decreed ex parte on 8.4.2001. The plaintiff bank then put the said decree into execution vide Execution C.4se No. 37 of 2002 which on transfer was renumbered as Execution Case No. 1242 of 2003. The present respondent No.1 (Concord Condominium Ltd.) of the civil appeal and respondent No. 1 to 21 of civil petition, having come to know about such decree and about inclusion of their purchased properties in the schedule to the decree filed two Miscellaneous cases being Nos. 35 of 2003 and 36 of 2003, as third party, under Order XXI Rule 58 read with section 151 of the Code narrating their story of purchasing the scheduled property from Dr. Abdul Mannan through his constituted attorney Md. Fazlul Hoque on different dates in 1994 and 1996 which upon hearing all the parties were dismissed on con-test on the ground as stated before. Against the same, the aforementioned First Miscellaneous Appeal No. 86 of 2006 and First Miscellaneous Appeal No. 145 of 2007 were preferred before the High Court Division by the said third party petitioners which were heard and allowed by a Division Bench of the High Court Division by the impugned judgment and order dated 10.12.2007 on the basis of settlement/compromise between the said third party petitioners and the bank. Against the said compromise/consented judgment and order the present appellant of civil appeal and the petitioner of the civil petition, (son of late Dr. Abdul Mannan, the original owner of the scheduled property) who was respondent No.14 in the miscellaneous appeals preferred these two civil appeals and the civil petition.

<u>16. On perusal of the impugned judgment it appears that the High Court Division observed that on the basis of settlement/ compromise between the appellants of the two miscellaneous appeals and the respondent bank and the appellants of both the miscellaneous appeals having paid TK.50,00,000/= by fourteen cheques in full satisfaction of the decretal amount to the respondent bank and the decree holder respondent bank,(who put the decree, into execution), having admitted that the parties have reached to an agreement out of Court and it has no objection to release the mortgaged property in favour of the said appellants pursuant to letter dated 03.09.2006' and as such the High Court Division allowed both the miscellaneous appeals. It also held that 'in view of the liquidation of the entire debts by the said appellant-purchasers as per demand of the respondent bank, we find no legal bar on the part of the respondent bank in releasing the mortgaged property in favour of the third party appellants'.</u>

17. After the loan amount and the demand of the respondent bank has been met by the third party-purchasers, Mohammad Zahangir Alam, son of judgment debtor late Dr. Abdul Mannan, who has been added as judgment debtor in the execution case in place of his late father filed this appeal and the civil petition before this Division challenging the aforesaid consented judgment and order passed by the High Court Division and thereby raising the question as noted in the submission of the learned advocate for the appellant/ petitioner.

<u>18. It is true that against the judgment and decree of the Artharin Adalat none, including the aggrieved party took any step. If an appeal against the decree was to be filed it ought to have been filed before the District Judge if the decretal amount is less than TK.50,00,000/= and if it is higher than TK.50,00,000 then before the High Court Division, of course upon depositing 50% of the decretal amount in either of the cases, as provided in section 41 of the Artharin Adalat Ain. In the present cases it appears that both the aforesaid first miscellaneous appeals were filed by the present respondents as third party-purchaser who purchased the properties in question from the original owner Dr. Abdul Mannan and in the said two miscellaneous appeals the present appellant and his mother (heirs of late Dr. Abdul Mannan) were made respondents Nos. 14 and 13 respectively. It further appears that the said two miscellaneous appeals were preferred against the judgment and order dated 21.5.2005 passed in Miscellaneous Case Nos. 36 and 35 both of 2003, filed under Order XXI Rule 58 read with section 151 of the Code, not, against the original judgment and decree dated 8.4.2001 of the Artha Rin Adalat. The aforesaid respondent Nos. 13 and 14 (of whom respondent No. 14 is the present appellant) being the widow and the son of late Dr. Abdul Mannan respectively, who exhausted his entire share by transfer to some persons from whom the present respondents of both the cases ultimately purchased the same and also by appointing Abul Hossain (predecessor of present respondents No. 4 to 13 of the civil appeal and respondent Nos. 24 to 33 in the civil petition) as his attorney to deal with the said property, accordingly and pursuant to such power dated 23.10.1983, the said attorney, Abul Hossain, mortgaged the same to the respondent bank against the loan sanctioned to respondent No.3. But the present appellant and his mother being parties in the said proceeding and having not challenged the same at any stage now has come before this Division to challenge the impugned order by which a consented judgment and order has been passed.</u>

19. When the parties to an action has expressly and by implication waived or has foregone the right and has come to a consensus to resolve the dispute by any lawful agreement or compromise or even by conduct, they/he cannot challenge such action/order on the ground of acquiescence, waiver and estoppel as well as such order having been passed where he was a party and never raised any objection rather on consent of both the parties, he cannot now raise any objection of pecuniary jurisdiction specially when he kept silent throughout the proceeding and specially when the order has been passed on coin-promise between all other parties and now by preferring this appeal he cannot for the first time raise this issue. In a case reported in 1993 MLR 247=PLD 1984 Quetta 92 it has been held 'where the appeal lay to the District Judge but was filed in the High Court and no objection was raised by the respondent in respect of the procedure and raised only when the decision went against him that irregular mode adopted by the High Court in entertaining the appeal had not resulted in prejudicing the merit of the case. Therefore, the decision of the High Court did not merit reversal.' Though the general principle is 'if the Court has no jurisdiction, no amount of waiver or consent can confer jurisdiction on the Court' but, a distinction must be made between "patent" and "latent" want of jurisdiction, in one, submission to the jurisdiction cannot cure the defect, while in the other, no objection to want of juris-diction can be taken at a later stage if the objection is not taken at the earliest (Altaf Hossain Vs. Chief Settlement Commissioner 18 DLR(SC)164). Again in the case of Sharafat Vs. Dr. Islamuddin (1998 BLD 92) it has been held that 'when a case has been decided on merit, it should not be reversed unless it has resulted in failure of justice'. In the case of Kiran Singh Vs. Chaman (A 1954 SC 340 1 SCR 117) it has been observed that a case tried on merits Should not be liable to be reversed purely on technical grounds, unless it has resulted in failure of justice, and the policy of the legislature has been to treat objections to jurisdiction, both territorial and pecuniary, as technical". Under the Indian jurisdiction, in a series of decisions, it has been held 'when a case is disposed of on merit, no interference by the Appellate or Revisional Court on technical ground of territorial and pecuniary jurisdiction is called for unless prejudiced (AIR 1983 Mad 9). In AIR 1984 Punj 345 it has been held 'lack of pecuniary jurisdiction is no inherent lack of jurisdiction.' Apart from the aforementioned series of decisions on the question of lack of jurisdiction it appears that the predecessor of the present appellant having transferred his entire share in the property in question by registered instruments, his heir, the appellant, cannot now challenge the same before this Division after 25 years of keeping the property under mortgage to the bank against a loan or by transfer without proving his title and possession over the suit land.

20. From the facts and circumstances and the law discussed above, it is clear that the present appellant was a party in the execution proceeding as well as in the appeal who did not raise any objection anywhere before any Court in respect of his right or claim. Even when the purchasers from his father settled the dispute, by compromise with the decree holder bank and the appeals were disposed of in terms of the said compromise to the satisfaction of the decree holder bank, the present appellant did not raise objection.

<u>21. In respect of submission of Mr. Bhuiyan on non-depositing 50% of the decreetal dues as provided under section 41(2) of the Ain it is to be mentioned that section 41 provides preferring appeal against decree or order passed by the Artharin Adalat and in such case the aggrieved party may prefer appeal upon depositing 50% of the decreetal dues if he acknowledges such claim. But in case the aggrieved party does not acknowledge such claim he is to deposit such amount as security in the Adalat which passed the decree otherwise the appeal under section 41(5) will not be in effect accepted. Such pre-condition has also been incorporated in section 19 of the Ain which has provided remedy against exparte decree. But under this section the amount to be deposited is 10% of the decreetal dues. Both these two provisions are in respect of remedy against decree passed in the suit which are not at all applicable in the cases in hand since the decree, either contested or exparte have been challenged. Rather the third party purchasers have filed the miscellaneous cases under Order XXI Rule 58 of the Civil Procedure Code since there was no such provision in the Ain earlier, and there is no such provision of depositing money. Section 6 of the Ain provides applicability of the provisions of the Code which not inconsistent with the AM. In the Artharin Ain of 2003, which came into force from 1st of May 2003, in section 32 has provided remedy against execution wherein under subsection 2 the provision of depositing 25% equal to decreetal amount has been inserted. So prior to that there was no necessity of depositing any amount for challenging the execution proceeding. From the aforesaid provisions of the Ain reading with the pre-amble of the same it appears that the Arthain Adalat Ain 2003 or the earlier Ain of 1999 has been enacted for the purpose of realization/recovery of loans by the financial institutions. The intention of the legislature is very clear. When it appeared that the borrowers of such loans are in the habit of not repaying back the same the legislature enacted such law to compel such defaulting borrowers who has developed a loan defaulting culture, to pay off the loan or to face the consequence of losing their property mortgaged against such loan. And as such the lending bank has been given right to recover the loan along with interests accrued thereon by selling off the property of the defaulting borrower in auction in the execution case filed after the decree.</u>

<u>22. The present cases have arisen out of such execution proceeding which have been filed by the third party purchasers who claimed to have purchased the same from the original owner without notice after the scheduled properties have been mortgaged to the plaintiff-respondent bank. The purpose of enacting laws is to protect the interests of all concerned and as such the present respondents, when came to know that their purchased proper-ties have been included in the schedule of the execution case they filed the miscellaneous cases to protect their purchased property. On the other hand, the financial institutions are also to protect their interests by recovering the unpaid loans by all means. Thus when the third party purchasers came forward to pay off the decreetal dues as per demand of the lending bank and they paid off the same in the two miscellaneous appeals before the High Court Division to the satisfaction of the decree holder bank and none else having come forward to pay off the unpaid loan there is no illegality in passing the impugned judgment and order as the whole purpose of enacting the Ain has been fulfilled which has not resulted in failure of justice.</u>

<u>23. Thus the impugned judgment having been decided on merit and the same having not resulted in failure of justice it is not liable to be reversed. So it is clear that the submissions as advanced by the learned advocate for the appellant in the appeal as well as the petitioner in the civil petition on all points are of no substance.</u>

24. Apart from the aforesaid conduct of the appellant it appears that the appellant did not come with clean hands because he had adequate opportunity to agitate the points raised herein, before the High Court Division and in not doing so and rather after the loan amount as well as the decretal dues having been paid off by the parties to the litigation, who claimed to have purchased the same from his father, to the satisfaction of the decree holder bank this appeal filed by one of the heirs of the original owner, who has exhausted his entire Share much earlier, before this Division is not at all sustainable in law.

<u>25. Thus we find no merit in the submissions of the learned advocate for the appellant as well as for the leave petitioner and as such, this appeal and the leave petition are liable to be dismissed.</u>

<u>26. In the result, this civil appeal is dismissed. Since Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 216 of 2008 has been filed against the same judgment and order of the High Court Division by the same appellant, on the self same grounds, this civil petition is also disposed of in the light of the judgment' passed in the civil appeal. However, there will be no order as to costs.</u>

End.

case_source: (From the judgment and order dated 11.03.2012 passed by the High Court Division in First Appeal No.157 of 2001 and order dated 31.07.1997 passed by the Appellate Division in C.P.No.595 of 1997.)
full_judgment:
Hasan Foez Siddique J. The delay in filing of the C.R.P.No.334 of 2019 is condoned.

2. Civil Appeal No.191 of 2015 and C.R.P.No.334 of 2019 have been heard analogously and they are being disposed of by this common judgment.

3. Sheikh Liakat Ali and two others tiled Writ Petition No.333 of 1993 in the High Court Division challenging the orders passed in L.A. Case No.27 of 1969-70 and taking over possession of the land and the structure of holding No.14/1, Topkhana Road, Dhaka stating that they are the owners of the "Usree" house and the land measuring an area of .4925 acre of khas mohal plot No. 188, ward No.3, Sheet No.20, Dhaka (hereinafter referred to as "disputed property"). The disputed property originally belonged to the Collectorate of Dhaka who settled the same to Satyendra Nath Roy (S.N.Roy), Professor of the University of Dhaka on 08.12.1937 for a period of 23 years 3 months by a registered deed of lease. Satyendra Nath Roy constructed two storied building thereon and named the same as "Usree". He gifted the disputed property to his wife Sreemoti Sujata Roy by registered deed dated 18.05.1940. The Government requisitioned the said building on 23.09.1947 and paid rent to Sujata Roy. Sujata Roy transferred the said property to Munshi Ashraf Ali, predecessor-in-interest of the writ petitioner-respondents by a registered sale deed dated 26.03.1951. Said Ashraf Ali got the order of lease extended by registered deed of lease dated 07.08.1961. Ashraf Ali submitted several representations to the Government to get the said property released from the order of requisition. Thus, the Government de-requisitioned the said "Usree" house on 09.07.1971. He let out the said house to Bangladesh National Awami Party (NAP). After creation of BAKSAL in January 1975, NAP was merged with BAKSAL. NAP left the disputed house in May 1975. Ashraf Ali went to ascertain the position of the disputed property and found that the police locked up the house and posted police force for its security. On inquiry, he came to know that the Deputy Commissioner, Dhaka had taken over possession of the said house. Ashraf Ali went to the office of the Deputy Commissioner and he was informed that the disputed property had been acquired by the Government in L.A. Case No.27 of 1969-70 for construction of the building of Press Club. No notice for acquisition was ever served upon Ashraf Ali. He submitted several representations to the Government to get the said property released from acquisition. Ashraf All died on 18.03.1976 and his wife died on 05.04.1992. Thereafter, his heirs the petitioners made similar representations that notice of acquisition was served upon the owner of the disputed property and that the building of the Press Club was constructed elsewhere so they are entitled to get the disputed property released. Meanwhile, the possession of the disputed property was taken over by the Government Accommodation Directorate, Ministry of Works and the Ministry of Works let out the same to the National Security Intelligence Department (NSI) on 27.08.1976. In such circumstances, the writ petitioner-respondents filed the instant writ petition and obtained Rule.

4. The High Court Division, by its judgment and order dated 17th June, 1996, made the said Rule absolute holding that (i) no gazette notification as to the decision of acquisition under section 5(7) of the (Emergency) Requisition of Property Act, 1948 was published; (ii) allotment of the disputed property to the National Security Intelligence was illegal and unauthorised and (iii) the possession of the Government was also illegal.

5. Against the said judgment and order, the Government tiled Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No.597 of 1997 in this Division which was dismissed as being time barred. Then the government has tiled this Civil Review Petition along with the prayer for condonation of delay.

6. The appellants of Civil Appeal No.191 of 2015, who are the respondents of the Civil Review Petition No.334 of 2019, have-preferred that appeal upon getting leave against the judgment and decree dated 11.03.2012 passed by the High Court Division in First Appeal No.157 of 2001 affirming those dated 18.06.2000 passed by the then learned Subordinate Judge, First Court, Dhaka in Title Suit No.232 of 1997. The Government filed the said suit for declaration of its title and recovery of khas possession stating, inter alia, that the Government represented by the Collector, Dhaka, being owner of the disputed property, leased out the same to Professor Satyendra Nath Roy by a registered lease deed dated 08.12.1937 which became effective on and from 01.01.1938. It was alleged that violating the terms of the said lease deed, Professor Roy transferred the disputed property to his wife Sujata Roy by a registered deed of gift dated 18.05.1940. Subsequently, Sujata Roy sold the same to Munshi Ashraf Ali, father of the defendants 1-3, by a registered kabala dated 26.03.1951. Thereafter, Munshi Ashraf Ali got the period of lease extended by another registered lease deed dated 07.08.1961 with effect from 01.04.1961 to 31.03.1991. During continuance of the period of lease, the Government took over possession of the disputed property on 17.69.1971 in L.A. Case No.27 of 1969-70 for the purpose of construction of the building of National Press Club. Subsequently when the Press Club was given alternative land, the disputed property was handed over to the Government Accommodation Directorate. In the meantime, period of lease of Munshi Ashraf Ali had expired on 31.03.1991 but his heirs did not apply for further renewal of the periodical lease and the lessor-Government automatically became owner of the disputed property on 31.03.1991. However, the heirs of Ashraf Ali started claiming the right, title to and possession in the same from 07.03.1993. They filed Writ Petition No.333 of 1993 challenging the act of taking over possession by the Government in L.A. Case No.27 of 1969-70, which gave rise to the cause or action for filing the suit by the Government for declaration of title to and recovery of khan possession in the suit property with further declaration that the defendants 1-3 have no right, title to and interest in the disputed property.

7. The defendant Nos.1-3 contested the suit by filing written statement and additional written statement contending, inter alia, that the suit is barred by the provision of res-judicata and the same was not maintainable. The Government leased out disputed property to Professor Satyendra Nath Roy by a registered lease deed dated 31.11.1937 for a period of 23 years and 5 months. The said lessee constructed a two storied building thereon and named the same as "Uusree" house. He gifted the said property to his wile Sujata Roy by a registered deed dated 18.05.1940. Sujata Roy sold the disputed property to Munshi Ashraf Ali by a registered kabala dated 26.03. 1951. The Government renewed the original lease by a registered lease deed dated 07.08.1961 extending the period of lease for another 30 years with effect from 01.04.1961 to 31.03.1991. On the prayer of the Munshi Ashraf Ali, the Government de-requisitioned the suit property on 09.07.1971. After independence of Bangladesh. lessee Munshi Ashraf Ali let out the disputed property to Bangladesh National Awami Party (NAP). After formation of BAKSAL in the year 1975, the tenant (NAP) vacated the house in the month May, 1976 without giving any intimation to the landlord Munshi Ashraf Ali. Though the Government started L.A. Case No.27 of 1969-70 to acquire the disputed property for construction of the building of National Press Club which was not ultimately constructed. Meanwhile, the Director, Government Accommodation Directorate, claiming ownership of the disputed property, allotted the same for accommodation of the Office of N.S.I. When the defendants tried to get the disputed property released, the Deputy Commissioner, Dhaka recommended for release of the same as it was not required for the Press Club vide his letter dated 07.03.1985. But the N.S.I. denied to vacate the suit property. Thus, the defendants filed Writ Petition No.333 of 1993 and obtained Rule which was made absolute. The High Court Division declared the alleged acquisition illegal and void with a direction to the concerned authority to hand over possession of the disputed property to the defendants within 60 days and also to pay compensation for unauthorised occupation of the house. The leave petition against the said judgment dated 17.06.1996 was dismissed by the Appellate Division. The Government was compelled to hand over physical possession of the disputed property to these defendants. According to them their lease hold right had not been extinguished after 31.03.1991 since the same became permanent lease.

8. The trial Court decreed the suit Appeal preferred by the defendants was dismissed by the High Court Division. Then they preferred this appeal. At this stage, the Government has filed an application for withdrawal of the aforesaid suit.

9. Mr. Mahbubey Alam, learned Attorney General appearing for the petitioner in Civil Review Petition No.334 of 2019, submits that the disputed property was acquired by the Government after due service of notice upon its lessee, that is, Munshi Ashraf Ali, predecessor-in-interest of the respondents of this review petition and the appellants of the Civil Appeal. He further submits that though the decision of acquisition was not notified in the official gazette, notices were duly served upon Munshi Ashraf Ali. After assessment of compensation, notice was issued upon him requesting to accept compensation but he did not turn up. Possession of the said property was duly taken over by the Government and same was handed over to the National Security Intelligence since Press Club, for which, the disputed property was acquired, was established elsewhere. He submits that though the disputed property was acquired for the Press Club, there is no legal bar for utilization of the same for another purpose. He submits that since notice of acquisition was duly served upon Munshi Ashraf Ali and the Government took over possession of the same and compensation was duly assessed and Munshi Ashraf Ali was duly notified to receive the compensation money, the right, title, interest and possession of the disputed land has been vested in the Government, the High Court Division erred in law in holding that the acquisition was illegal and the Government is unlawful possessor of the disputed land, this Division also committed error of law apparent on the face of the record in dismissing the civil petition.

10. Mr. Alam appeared for the respondent in Civil Appeal No.191 of 2015 submits that since the right, title, interest and possession of the disputed land has been vested in the Government free from all encumbrances in L.A. Case No.27 of 1969-70, Title Suit filed by the Government was misconceived one and the same is redundant as such he prayed for withdrawal of the said suit at this stage.

11. Mr. Qumrul Haque Siddique, learned Counsel for the respondent in Civil Review Petition submits that the disputed property was proposed to be acquired for Press Club but Press Club building was constructed in another place and that no agreement was effected as per provision of section 7D of the (Emergency) Requisition of Property Act, 1948 and no compensation was paid. Even the same was not finally assessed so the right, title and interest of the disputed property had not been vested in the Government free from all encumbrances as such the review petition is liable to be dismissed and First Appeal is liable to be allowed. He submits that the instant review petition is hopelessly barred by limitation so also the same is liable to be dismissed.

12. The disputed property is measuring an area of .4927 acre = 1(one) bigha 9 (nine) kathas 13 chattacks of Khas Mahal plot No.188, Sheet No.20 Ward No. 3, Municipal Holing no.14/1, Topkhana Road, Touzi No.15725. It was recorded in C.S. plot No.53 to the extent of .06 acre and C.S. plot No. 55 to the extent of .42 acre under C.S. khatian No.6947/6947(A) and R.S. plot No. 544 under R.S. khatian No.2089. The boundary of the said land is:

13. North- Mathor passage, South-road, East-Koruna Babu and West plot No.187.

14. Admittedly, the disputed property originally belonged to the Government. Case of the writ petitioner-respondents is that the Government settled the same to Professor Sattyandra Nath Roy on 30.11.1937 for a period of 23 years 3 months with effect from 01.01.1938 by registered deed of lease. S.N. Roy gifted his leasehold right to his wife Sujata Roy by registered deed of gift dated 18.05.1940. Sujata Roy sold the said property to Munshi Ashraf Ali, the predecessor-in-interest of the writ petitioner respondents. Ashraf Ali got his lease renewed on 07.08.1961 for a period of 30 years with effect from 01.04.1961. It is not disputed that the Government requisitioned the said property on 03.09.1947, that is, before the aforesaid transfer of Sujata Roy to Munshi Ashraf Ali. The further case of writ petitioners is that though the Government derequisitioned the disputed property on 17.09.1971 it did not handover the possession of the same to Munshi Ashraf Ali. He came to know that disputed property has been again requisitioned and, then, acquired in L.A. Case No.27 of 1969-70. Ashraf Ali made several representations to the Government to get the disputed property released from acquisition but the Government did not pay any heed. Rather, the Directorate of Government Accommodation, Ministry of Works illegally allotted the same to the National Security Intelligence Department (NSI).

15. It appears from the judgment of the High Court Division that the case record of L.A. Case No.27 of 1969-70 was called for by the High Court Division at the time of hearing of the writ petition and the High Court Division perused the same. The High Court Division held that the L.A. case was started on 07.07.1971 for acquisition but no notice in that regard was served upon the writ petitioner respondents. At the time of hearing of this review petition, learned Attorney General produced the case record of L.A. Case No.27/1969-70 for our perusal. We have also perused the record of the said L.A. case thoroughly. On perusal of the same, it appears that some papers from the said L.A. case are missing from the record. From the note sheet of L.A. Case it appears that on 07.07.1971, it was stated that "USREE" house was requisitioned immediately after partition on 23.09.1947 for the residential accommodation of the Government officials. Since then the disputed property was under the administrative control of the Estate Office, Dhaka. Subsequently, the Government decided to acquire the disputed property for the accommodation of Press Club. Accordingly, proposal for acquisition was made on 09.07.1971. For the said purpose of acquisition, it became necessary to derequisition of the disputed property. It further appears from the order dated 10.07.1971 of the L.A. Case No.27 of 69-70 that notice for derequisition was prepared for releasing the disputed property. The orders dated 07.07.1971 and 10.07.1971 in L.A. Case No.27 of 196970 were as follows:

"07.07.1971

The premises No. 14/3 Topkhana Road, Dacca known as USREE was requisitioned immediately after partition on 23.09.1947 for Residential accommodation. Since then the premises was under the administrative control of Estate office Dacca. Subsequently Govt. decided to acquire the land and building for the accommodation of the Press Club. Accordingly a proposal for requisition and acquisition of the holding was sought for on 09.07.1971 while it is necessary to derequisition the holding first & then to issue requisition notice with a view to acquire on urgent next basis. Kgo will please put up derequisition notice."

10.07.1971

De-requisition notice prepared under section 10(2) for release and restoration of a requisition property by kgo. Signed by me. Issue derequisition notices for release the property from requisition with effect from 02.06.1971. Kgo will please put up Reqn. notices."

16. Accordingly, the Land Acquisition Officer issued notice releasing the disputed property from requisition with effect from 02.06.1971. Contents of the said notice run as follows:

"FORM F.

Notice under rule 10(2) for releases and Restoration of Requisitioned property

To Mr. Asraf Ali S/O Hajee Munshi Belayet Ali of 68 Purana Paltan, Dacca-2.

Whereas by order, dated the 23.09.1947 the property described in the schedule below was/were requisitioned under section 3 of the East Bengal (Emergency) Requisition of property Act, 1948 (East Bengal Act, XIII of 1948); as amended upto date.

And whereas it has been decided to release the said property/properties from such requisition;

And whereas it has been held that you are entitled to get possession of he said property/properties;

Now, therefore, in exercise of the power conferred by subsection (1) of section 8, which power has been delegated to me by the provincial Government, I hereby order that possession of the said property/properties be restored to you. w/e from

02.06.1971

Possession of the said property/properties will accordingly be restored to you at a.m./p.m on the  when you are called upon to attend personally or by an agent on the spot to take delivery of possession of the property/properties.

SCHEDULE

Municipal holding No.14/1 Topkhana Road, Dacca known as Usree House with all amenities thereon.

(a two storied pacca building along with vacant land)"

17. In paragraph 8 of the writ petition the writ petitioner-respondents admitted the fact of derequisition and produced the notice of the same as annexure "E" to the writ petition which was issued pursuant to the orders dated 07.07.1971 and 10.07.1971 passed in LA Case No.27 of 1969-70.

18. Thereafter, the Land Acquisition Officer on 19.07.1971 passed the following order:

"3 19-7-71 Whereas in my opinion it is expedient and necessary in the public interest to requisition and acquisition this immoveable property described in the schedule below for requisition & acquisition of the land for accommodation of the E.P. Press Club.

Now therefore in exercise of the power conferred by section 3 read with section 9 of the East Bengal (Emergency)

Requisition of the Property Act, 1948 as amended up to date,.

I hereby requisition the said property and thereby make the following order:

The owner occupies the said property shall place the said property at my disposal and under my control with effect from 22.07.71 and deliver possession thereof on the said date to me.

Schedule C.S. plot No.53 and 55 of mouza Shahar Dacca, JL No.343 sheet No.20 Ward No.3, P.S. Ramna, District Dacca are more or less .48 acre with all trees and structures thereon. Kgo will please take further action in the matter. Nazir will please serve the notices & return the S.R.

Sd/- M.A. Khan A/L.A.O."

19. It further appears from the record of L.A. case that notice was issued on 19.07.1971 to Ashraf Ali of No.68, Purana Paltan, P.S. Ramna, Dhaka and same was served on 20.07.1971. Date of service return was on 21.07.1971. In view of the provision of section 114(e) of the Evidence Act, 1872 official acts are presumed to have been rightly and regularly done. The maxim, "omnia prae-sumuntur rite esse acta" applied to official acts. Where any official act is shown to have been done in a manner substantially regular, it is presumed that formal requisites for its validity were complied with. It is curious that the writ petitioner-respondents though admitted the service of notices issued pursuant to the orders dated 07.07.1971 and 10.07.1971 but denied the notices issued pursuant to the subsequent orders dated 19.07.1971, 20.07.1971, 22.07.1971 and 26.07.1971. The High Court Division in its judgment failed to take notice of writ petitioners' double standard in respect of procedural validity of the same L.A. Case. Moreover, notices of the requisition and acquisition of the disputed property were served upon Ashraf Ali or not is a disputed question of fact which is difficult to ascertain in writ jurisdiction.

20. From order No.4, dated 20.07.1971, it appears that the same was passed with the following words:

"Provisional award amounting to taka 216085/15 prepared by Kgo. signed by

Issued payment notice to receive advance payment after verification of title."

21. Order No.5 dated 22.07.1971 was as under:

"Ashraf Ali, owner of the house, did not turn-up to receive advance payment after verification of title. Possession of the land & building delivered to the Sub-Divisional Engineer, Ramna (BLDS) Division today the 22nd July, 71 after making joint inventory. Kgo will please pre-pare notice u/s 5(a) & 5(3) and put up early."

22. Order dated 26.07.1971 was as under:

"6 26-7-71 Whereas 1 consider that the acquisition of the property described in the schedule below which were requisitioned by an order dated 22.07.71 under section 3 of the East Bengal (Emergency) Requisition of Property Act, 1948 (Act XIII of 1948) is expedient for the purpose of East Pakistan Press Club. Notices are hereby given under sub-Section 1(a) & 3 read with Sub-Section 2 of section 5 of the said Act that the said properties are proposed to be acquired.

23. All persons interested in the properties are hereby called upon to appear before the A/L.A.O. or by an agent on the 19.08.71 at the office of the L.A.O. Dacca at 10 A.M. to state the nature of such interest in the properties objection if any to the acquisition of the property and particulars of their claims to compensation for their respective interest.

24. A plan of land proposed to be acquired may be inspected in the office of the Deputy Commissioner L.A. Section, Dacca.

Schedule

C.S. Plot no. 53 and 55 of Mouza Shahar Dacca, J.L. No.343 Sheet No.20 Ward No.3 P.S. Ramna, Dist. Dacca . Area more or less .48 acre signed the notices u/s 5(1 a) & 5(3). Nazir will please serve the notices & put up S.R."

25. It further appears from the case record of L.A. case that actual physical possession of the disputed property was taken over by the S.D.E, Ramna Building Sub-Division on 22.07.1971. Accordingly, Certificate of possession of the disputed land made over to Requiring Body was issued. The contents of which run as follows:

"L.A. Case No.27/69-70.

Certificate of Possession of Land made over to Requiring Body.

Certificate that I have this day the 22-7-1971 received possession from Mr. Md. Matiur Rahman, Add. Land Acquisition Officer, Dacca, for an area of more or less .48 acre of land in Mouza Shahar Dacca, Sheet No.20, Ward No.3, P.S. Ramna, Dist. Dacca, JL No.343, as per schedule/ below which has been requisitioned under section 3 of E.B. (Emergency) Requisition of Property Act, XIII of 1948.

SCHEDULE

Part of C.S. plot No. 06/53 and 42/55 of Mouza Shahar Dacca, JL No.343 sheet No.20 Ward No.3, P.S. Ramna, Dist. Dacaa. Area more or less .48 acres.

Joint inventory attached herewith.

Possession handed over by me.  Sd. M. Rahman, 22/7/71 Ad/L.A.O.

Possession taken over S/- A.S. Chowdhury, 22/7/71 SDE, Ramna Building Sub Division."

26. From the mote sheet of the L.A. case it appears that after the order dated 26.07.1971, rest portions of the note sheet of the L.A Case are missing. However, it further appears from the record that there is a letter issued from the Deputy Commissioner, Dhaka, Land Acquisition Department to the Section Officer, Ministry of Works and Urban Department, Public Works Division, Dhaka that notice under section 5(1 a) and 5(3) of the (Emergency) Requisition Act, 1948 was duly served upon the interested parties fixing the date 19.08.1971 for filing objection, if any, and actual possession of the land, building was delivered to the Sub-Divisional Engineer. Ramna (Bids) Division. The contents of the said letter dated 11.07.1974 run as follow:

"OFFICE OF THE DEPTUY COMMISSIONER, DACCA. LAND ACQUISITION DEPT.

Memo No.1549 L.A. Section 11A dated 11.7.74.

To The Section Officer,

Ministry of Public Works and Urban Development. Public Works Division, Dacca.

Sub: Acquisition of land and building named "USREE" at 14/3, Topkhana Road Dacca for accommodation of Press Club. LA. Case No.27/69-70.

Ref: No.VI/IL-26/72/465 dated 29.04.74.

It appears from the case record that the premises No.14/3, Topkhana Road, Dacca known as "Usree" was requisitioned immediately after partition in the year 1947 for residential accommodation. Since then the premises was under the administrative control of the Estate Officer Dacca. Subsequently Govt. decided to acquire the land and buildings for accommodation of the Press Club. Accordingly the above premises was de-requisitioned by an order dated 10.07.1971 and requisitioned the land and building of the premises No.14/1 Topkhana Road afresh by an order dated 19.7.71 with a view to permanent acquisition for accommodation of the Press Club. The owner of the premises was offered advance payment but he did not receive the same. Physical possession of the land and building was delivered by Sub Divisional Engineer, Ramna (Bids), Division Dacca on 22.7.71 after making joint inventory. It is not known to this office how National Awami Party occupied the requisitioned property.

Notice u/s 5(la) and 5(3) for acquisition of the land was duly served upon the interested parties fixing 19.08.1971 for filing objections if any against the acquisition of the property but no objection against the acquisition of the property was received. Notice of acquisition has not yet been to the Govt. for publication in the official Gazette.

Sd/ M.A. Samad 20.7.1974."

27. Mr. Qumrul Haque Siddique, in his submission contended that no agreement was effected between the requiring body and the Government and in fact there is no material on record that the requiring body had paid the compensation. But it appears from the letter issued dated 26.11.1970 by the Executive Engineer to the Deputy Commissioner, Dhaka that a sum of taka 2,18,246/- was placed from the contingency item for payment of compensation. The contents of the letter written by the Executive Engineer to the Deputy Commissioner, Dacca dated 26.11.1970 run as follows:

"To The D.C. Dacca,

Sub: Acquisition of the house "USREE" at 14/3, Topkhana Road, Dacca for accommodation of E.P. Press Club (L.A. Case No.27/69-70).

In enclosing herewith a copy of memo No. 2684(3)-B dt. 2.11.70 for, the A.C.E.(B) together with a copy of its encloser on the above subject the u/s has the honour to place a sum of Rs.2,18,246/- (Rupees two lacs eighteen thousand two hundred forty six) only as L.A. cost out of the authorised expenditure of Rs.500000/- (Ruppes five lacs) only as provided in the contingency item for 1970-71 under Grant 45. Necessary Payment to the owners and kindly be made after observing all the formalities at an early date.

The higher authorities are pressing very hard for the same.

This may kindly be treated extremely urgent.

Sd/- Illegible, 26/11 E.E."

ঢাকা।

এমতাবস্থায় উহার দখল হস্তান্তর করা সম্ভবপর  হইতেছে না।
