২৫. উপরি-উক্ত আলোচনা হতে এ সিদ্ধান্তে উপনীত হওয়া যায় যে, অর্থ খণ আদাঙ্গত আইনের ১৯ ধারা এবং ৪২ ধারা তথা জারী পর্যায় নিলাম রদের জন্য দাখিলী বিবিধ মামলাসমূহের চূড়ান্ত আদেশের বিরুদ্ধে বিবিধ আপীল রক্ষণীয় এবং অর্থ খণ মোকদ্দমা হতে উদ্ভূত জারী মোকদ্দমার সকল অস্তবতীকালীন আদেশের বিরদ্ধে আপীল বা রিভিশন গ্রহণযোগ্য নয় । তবে উক্ত ক্ষেত্রে রীট রক্ষণীয়।

২৬. উপরি-উক্ত আলোচনা হতে প্রতীয়মান হয় যে, অর্থ ঋণ আদালত আইন, ২০০৩ এর ৪১ এবং 8৪ ধারার বিধানাবলী একটি অন্যটির সহিত সাংঘর্ষিক নয় বরং দুইটি বিধানের যথার্থ কার্যকারিতা রয়েছে।

২৭. স্বীকৃত মতে, অর্থ জারী আদালতের ৬৪ নং আ���েশ বা অন্যকোনো আদেশ চ্যালেঞ্জ করে বাদী ব্যাংক কোনো রীট মামলা দায়ের করেননি । বাদী ব্যাংক ইচ্ছা করলে উক্ত আদেশের বিরুদ্ধে রীট মামলা দায়ের করতে পারতেন। কিন্তু উক্ত আদেশের বিরুদ্ধে রীট না করে মিস আপীল নং ০১/২০১৩ (অর্থ) দায়ের করেন। জেলা জজ, বগুড়া এর উক্ত আপীল গ্রহণের কোনো আইনগত ক্ষমতা না থাকা সত্বেও তিনি উক্ত আপীল গ্রহণ করে নিষ্পত্তির জন্য অতিরিক্ত জেলা জজ, ২য় আদালত বগুড়ায় পাঠিয়েছেন। অতিরিক্ত জেলা জজ, ২য় আদালতের উচিৎ ছিল উক্ত মামলাটি maintainable নয় মর্মে সিদ্ধান্ত প্রদানপূর্বক আপীলটি খারিজ করা। এখতিয়ার না থাকা সত্বেও বিজ্ঞ অতিরিক্ত জেলা জজ মামলার গুণাগুণ বিবেচনা করে সিদ্ধান্ত প্রদান করেছেন। যা দৃশ্যত বেআইনী ।

২৮. ইহা আইনের প্রতিষ্ঠিত নীতি যে, এখতিয়ার বিহীন আদালতের যে কোনো রায় বা আদেশ হচ্ছে আইনত অকার্যকর । যে আদালতের এখতিয়ার নাই সে আদালতের রায় যতই যুক্তিযুক্ত হোক না কেন, তা সর্বদাই ব্যর্থ। এখতিয়ার বিহীন আদালতের রায় প্রসঙ্গে আমাদের আপীল বিভাগের Md. Rupali Bank vs Tafazal Hossain, 44 DLR (40) 260 মামলার রায়টি প্রণিধানযোগ্য। উক্ত রায়ের Author Judge ছিলেন তৎকালীন প্রধান বিচারপতি, বিচারপতি জনাব সাহাবৃদ্দীন আহমদ। উক্ত রায়টি আদালতের এখতিয়ার বিষয়ক একটি landmark judgment। উক্ত রায়ের প্রাসঙ্গিক অংশটি নিম্নরূপ-

‘jurisdiction of a Court goes to the very root of a matter brought before it, and if the Court got no jurisdiction everything shall fall through...”

২৯. নথি পর্যালোচনায় দেখা যায় যে, দায়িক ইন্টার্ণ ব্যাংক বাংলাদেশ লিমিটেড এর বগুড়া শাখা থেকে ব্যবসায়ের উদ্দেশ্যে ২০(বিশ) লক্ষ টাকা ঝণ গ্রহণ করেন। খণ প্রদানে ব্যর্থতায় বাদী ব্যাংক অর্থ খণ আদালতে মামল! দায়ের করেন । উক্ত মামলা দায়ের করার আগে বাদী ব্যাংকে ১০(দশ) লক্ষ টাকা জমা দেন। অর্থ খণ মোকাদমায় ডিত্রী হয় ২২,৩৪,৩২৪.০২ টাকা ডিক্রী হয়। অতঃপর দায়িক মামলা চলাকালীন এবং মামলার রায়ের পরে বিভিন্ন তারিখে সর্বমোট ২৮,৬৭,৫৯৯.৩৭ টাকা ব্যাংকে জমা প্রদান করেন অর্থাৎ দায়িক ঝণগ্রহীতা সর্বমোট (১০,০০,০০০ + ২৮,৬৭,৫৯৯.৩৭) =৩৮,৬৭,৫৯৯.৩৭ টাকা প্রদান করেছেন। অর্থ ঝণ আদালতের বিজ্ঞ বিচারক আদালতে ব্যাংককে দায়িকের দাখিলী দলিলাদি উপস্থাপন করার জন্য নির্দেশ প্রদান করলেও সংশ্লিষ্ট আইনজীবী আদালত কে জনান যে ব্যাংক সংশ্লিষ্ট দলিলাদি আদালতে দাখিল করবে না। যা ধৃষ্টতাপূর্ণ এবং অপ্রত্যাশিত । ব্যাংক কর্মকর্তাদের মনে রাখতে হবে “They are bound by law, subordinate to law and answerable to law who are they may be.” আদালতের উক্ত আদেশ দ্বারা ডিক্রী জারী মামলাটি চূড়ান্তভাবে নিষ্পত্তি হয়নি। বরং ইহা একটি অস্তবর্তীকালীন আদেশ । উক্ত জারী মামলাটি চূড়ান্ত নিষ্পত্তিকালে বাদী ব্যাংকের কোনো দাবী থাকলে তা উপস্থাপন করতে পারতো । এখানে উল্লেখযোগ্য যে, বাদী ব্যাংক wrong forum এ আপীল করার ফলে এ ব্লীট মামলার উত্তব ঘটে ।

৩০. উপরি-উক্ত আলোচনা ও উত্ত মামলার ঘটনা, অবস্থা ও প্রেক্ষাপট পর্যালোচনা করলে আদালতের কাছে প্রতীয়মান হয় যে, অর্থ জারী মামলায় প্রদত্ত আদেশটি অন্তবর্তীকালীন আদেশ। উক্ত আদেশের বিরুদ্ধে আপীল মামলাটি ৪১ ধারা অনুযায়ী গ্রহণযোগ্য নয় এবং তর্কিত মিস আপীল মামলার রায় ও আদেশ আইনগত রক্ষণীয় নয়। সঙ্গত কারণে বলা যায় যে, উক্ত রুলের সারবস্তা রয়েছে । ফলে রুলটি চূড়ান্তকরণ যোগ্য ।

৩১. অতএব, আদেশ হয় যে, উক্ত রুলটি চূড়ান্ত তথা absolute করা হলো।

৩২. বিজ অতিরিক্ত জেলা জজ, ২য় আদালত, বগুড়া কর্তৃক মিস আপীল নং ০১/২০১৩ (অর্থ) এর বিগত ৫-৭-২০১৫ খ্রি. তারিখের রায় ও আদেশ এতদ্বারা রদ ও রহিত করা হলো এবং অর্থ ঋণ আদালত, বগুড়া অর্থ জারী মোকদ্দমা নং ১৭০/২০০৮ এর ১৫-১-২০১৩ খ্রি. তারিখের ৫৭ নং আদেশ, ২২-১-২০১৩ খ্রি. তারিখের ৮ নং আদেশ এবং ১১-৩-২০১৩ খ্রি. তারিখের ৬৪ নং আদেশ পুনর্বহাল করা হলো । এ মামলায় কোনো খরচের আদেশ প্রদান করা হয়নি । পক্ষগণ নিজ নিজ মামলার খরচ বহন করবেন।

অত্র রায়ের কপি জরুরী ভিত্তিতে নিম্ন-আদালতে প্রেরণ করা হউক । উক্ত রায়ের কপি প্রাপ্তির ৩০(ত্রিশ) দিনের মধ্যে প্রতিবাদী ব্যাংক সংশ্লিষ্ট দলিলাদি অর্থ খণ আদালত বগুড়ায় দাখিল করবেন। ব্যর্থতায়, অর্থ খণ আদালত ব্যাংকের সংশ্লিষ্ট কর্মকর্তার বিরুদ্ধে অর্থ ঝণ আদালত আইনের ৫২ ধারা মোতাবেক আইন অনুযায়ী কার্যক্রম গ্রহণ করবেন।

End.

lawyer:
Syed Haider Ali with Begum Shaheen Akhter Advocates—For the Petitioners. 
Abdul Bari with Khandaker Aminul Haque, Advocates—For the Opposite Parties.
parties:
Syurja Kumar Bepari and others -------- Petitioners 
vs 
Basudev others Biswas and ------ Opposite Parties
full_judgment:
In this revision Rule was issued calling upon the opposite party Nos. 1, 2 and 49 to show cause as to why the impugned judgment and decree dated 30-3-2008 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, 3rd Court, Faridpur in Title Appeal No. 207 of 2006 disallowing the appeal and thereby affirming the judgment and decree dated 15-8-2006 passed by the learned Senior Assistant Judge, Alfadanga, Faridpur, in Title Suit No. 133 of 2004 dismissing the suit should not be set aside and/or pass such other or further order or orders as to this Court may seem fit and proper. 

2. The petitioner No. 1 and the predecessor of the petitioner Nos. 2-6 of the instant Civil Revisional application, as plaintiffs, filed original Title Suit No. 103 of 1985 for a decree of partition of the suit land in respect of RS Khatian No. 1063 and declaration of title about 4 annas share of the schedule land. Subsequently, the plaintiff-petitioners have amended their plaint with a further declaration that they have reversionary right in the suit land and the two sale deeds described in schedule `Kha' to the plaint are illegal, concocted, void, without consideration and not binding upon the plaintiffs. 

3. The case of the plaintiff-appellant-petitioners, in short, are that the property described in schedule 'Ka' to the plaint belonged to Ram Joy Bepari, Madhab Bepari, Tara Chand Bepari and Guru Charan Bepari who were full brothers and all of them died before CS operation. Ram Joy died leaving behind his only son named Pitambar Bepari in 4 annas share, Madhab Bepari died leaving behind his only son named, Avoy Charan Bepari in 4 annas share, Tara Chand Bepari died leaving behind his two sons named Sadhu Bepari and Gostha Bepari in 4 annas share. Guru Charan Bepari died issueless leaving behind his only widow named Muktakeshi Bewa in 4 annas share as recorded their names in the CS Khewbat (Khatian) No. 15/1 of Mouza-Char Sultanpur. Thereafter, Avoy Charan Bepari died before RS operation leaving behind his only son named Sonatan Bepari, as such, his name was recorded in RS khatian operation in 4 annas, Sadhu Bepari died before RS operation leaving behind his only widow named Madhu Bala Dasya, her name was recorded in RS khatian in 4 annas, Pitambar Bepari died before RS operation leaving behind Jangli, Sarat Chandra, Prannath, Ghonesh Chandra, Nepal Chandra and Raghu Nath Bepari as his heirs, their names were recorded in RS khatian as per their shares. Muktakeshi died before Sonatan Bepari and Gostha Bepari and then Gostha Bepari died leaving behind his only widow Promoda Sundari and then Promoda Sundari also died on 27th Agrahayan, 1391 BS and before that, said Madhu Bala died leaving behind only Sonatan Bepari as her husband's brother's son as legal heir and lastly, Sonatan Bepari died leaving behind his two sons the original plaintiffs of this suit and in the way aforesaid the plaintiffs have been owning and possessing total 8 annas share in the suit land. 

4. The property in question were sold in auction for arrear rents and one Manik Sarder purchased the land in auction. Said Manik Sardar Settled the same to Gostha Bepari who executed and registered a kabuliyat on 11-1-1945 in favour of Manik Sarder in respect of the suit land and then Gostha Bepari erected dwelling houses on a part of the suit land and possessing rest of the same by cultivating various crops: One Ganga Charan Biswas filed Title Suit No. 43 of 1995 in the Sadar Munsif Court, Faridpur against Gostha Bepari and others for declaration of title and recovery of Khas possession. During pendency of that suit Gostha Bepari died leaving behind his only widow named Promoda Sundari who was substituted as his only legal heir. Promoda Sundari also contested the suit and it was ultimately dismissed. She acquired 1.92 acres of land as her life-estate. Promada Sundari lived with the help of the plaintiffs and with the income of the suit land and there was no legal necessity to sell the property and also she had no right to transfer the same. On her death, the plaintiffs have acquired the same as their reversionary right. The plaintiffs applied fire to the mouth of deceased Promoda Sundari (corpse) at the time of cremation and after 11 days they have performed her "Sraddha" ceremony. 

5. Husband of Promoda Sundari was very rich man and he had vest property and enough cash money those were acquired by Promoda Sundari and for this reason she never sold any property in her life-time. So, the two deeds described in schedule `Kha' schedule are forged and fabricated. Moreover, the suit land is agricultural land, so Promoda Sundari had no right to transfer the same. The defendant Nos. 1, 2 and 49 interfered with the peaceful possession of the plaintiffs and refused to partition the property in dispute, hence, the present suit for declaration and partition. 

6. The defendant Nos. 1, 2 and 49 contested the suit by filing written statements denying all the material allegations made in the plaint contending inter alia, that the claim of the plaintiffs are false, baseless; the plaintiffs are not in possession of the suit land; the plaintiffs are not reversioners and therefore, they are not entitled to file the present suit in that capacity; the defendants are bonafide purchasers for value without notice. Promoda Sundari sold the suit land in the year 1981 and 1984 for her legal necessity and to forfeit the loan of her husband, to offer food to the manes and also other obsequies of her deceased husband. The plaintiffs are not entitled to get relief as prayed for and the suit is liable to be dismissed. 

7. The trial court framed as many as nine issues for determination of the dispute. In course of hearing, the plaintiffs examined four witnesses as PWs and the defendants examined four witnesses as DWs. Both the parties submitted documents in support of their respective claim which were duly marked as exhibits. The trial court upon hearing dismissed the suit by its judgment and decree dated 15-8-2006. 

8. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the judgment and decree of the trial court, the plaintiffs preferred Title Appeal No. 207 of 2006 before the District Judge, Faridpur, Eventually, the said appeal was transferred to the court of Joint District Judge, 3rd Court, Faridpur for hearing and disposal who upon hearing by the impugned judgment and decree dated 30-3-2008 disallowed the appeal and thereby affirmed the judgment and decree of the trial court. At this juncture, the petitioners moved this Court by filing this revisional application under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure and obtained the present Rule. 

9. Mr Syed Haider Ali with Ms Begum Shaheen Akhter, learned Advocates appearing for the petitioners submit that the suit of the plaintiffs were twice decreed by the trial court on remand from appellate court, but for the third time the trial court dismissed the suit on remand by the judgment and decree dated 15-8-2006 on the ground that the petitioners, as plaintiffs, could not establish their claim of revisionary right as well as considered the sale deed executed and registered by Promoda Sundari were for her legal necessity. He further submits that a widow acquired life interest in the property left by her husband, accordingly, Promoda Sundari got the property as her life interest and she could have transferred the property for legal necessity during her life time but in the instant suit the contesting defendants who purchased the property miserably failed to prove that the property was sold by Promoda Sundari to them for any legal necessity. It is further submitted that transfer by a widow for legal necessity has to be proved by the purchasers themselves, but in the instant case except the averments made in the recital of the deed, the contesting defendants could not prove that Promada Sundari transferred the property for any legal necessity and the necessity whatever stated in the recital of the deed has not been proved by an) evidence in accordance with law. 

10. He further submits that in the earlier two judgments passed by the trial court rightly held that the petitioners are reversioners of the owner of the property Gostha Bepari and rightly held that the alienation of the property by Promoda Sundari was not for any legal necessity and the defendants in suit utterly failed to prove that the property was sold to them for any legal necessity. But for the third time the trial court wrongly held that the plaintiffs could not prove that they are reversioners of original owner by any evidence and the property was sold by Promoda Sundari for legal necessity. The appellate court though disallowed the appeal on the ground that the alienation of the property was for legal necessity of Promoda Sundari, but rightly held and found that the petitioners could able to prove that they are reversioners of original owner, Gostha Bepari. 

11. Mr Haider Ali finally submits that in a suit for claim of reversionary right in the property, onus lies upon the plaintiffs only to that extent, whether they are descendents and revisioners of the owner of the property in the absence of any legal heirs and alienation of property for any legal necessity of a widow heavily lies upon the purchaser who purchased the property. In the instant suit the petitioners successfully proved that they are reversioners of Gostha Bepari and no other obligations imposed by law upon them to prove that the property was alienated by Promoda Sundari for her legal necessity, but the defendants as purchasers by no evidence could prove that the property was sold by Promoda Sundari for her legal necessity. As such, both the courts below in dismissing the suit as well as disallowing the appeal committed serious error of law occasioning failure of justice. In support of his such submissions he has referred to the cases of Mahendra Kumar Roy vs Akbar Molla reported in 29 DLR 6, Shib Nath Sarker vs Shashi Bala Sarker reported in 1993 BLD (HCD) 415, and Nowsha Mia vs Mohammad Idris Ali reported in 10 DLR 641. 

12. Mr Abdul Bari with Mr Khandaker Aminul Hague, learned Advocates appearing for the opposite party Nos. 1, 2 and 49 submit that the genealogy given by the plaintiffs in their original plaint was replaced by subsequent amendment of plaint for several times starting from 1997-2004 and by bringing amendment of plaint introducing new facts basically destroyed the basic averments and statements of the plaintiffs made in the original plaint, as such, the trial court rightly observed and held that the plaintiffs on different times by bringing the facts inconsistent with each other could not establish their claim of reversionary right in the property and failed to prove that they are revisioners of original owner, Gostha Bepari. He further submits that the property in question admittedly, left by Gostha Bepari and acquired .by Promoda Sundari as her life interest and during her life time she transferred the property for legal necessity as stated in the recital of the deed and stated by the witnesses adduced on behalf of the defendants. It is also argued that the plaintiffs could not substantiate their claim that they took care of Promoda Sundari and maintained her expenses till her death or they incurred any costs for funeral of Gostha Bepari or his subsequent religious ceremony on their part, as such, Promoda Sundari for her maintenance and after the death of Gostha Bepari, for performing his various religious formalities transferred the property to the defendants. But the appellate court while disallowing the appeal though rightly held that the property was alienated by Promoda Sundari for her legal necessity but wrongly held that the plaintiffs could able to prove that they are reversioners of Gostha Bepari. In support of his submissions he has referred to a catena of cases Mst. Rahima Khatun vs Sree Monoranjon Saha reported in 13 MLR (HCD) 334, Matilal Sarcar vs Brajabashi Biswas reported in 12 DLR 142, Upendra Nath Mukherjee vs Gurupada Haider reported in AIR 1930 (Calcutta) 508, Golaka Chandra Nayak vs Gobinda Nayak reported in AIR 1996 (Orissa) 189, Mst. Sheo Kuer vs Nathuni Prasad Singh reported in AIR 1976 (Supreme Court) 709, Banga Chandra Dhur Biswas vs Jagat Kishore Acharja Chowdhury and others reported in XXI CWN 225 and Smt. Pramila Debbarma vs Smt. Gitasree Debbarma (Chakraborty) reported in AIR 1997 (Gauhati) 78. 

13. Heard the learned Advocates for the parties, have gone through the revisional application, plaint and written statements, evidences both oral and documentary, judgments passed by the trial court on remand and the impugned judgment and decree of both the courts below. 

14. From perusal of record, it appears that the suit was decreed by the trial court at the first instance by the judgment and decree dated 9-11-1992. The defendants preferred Title Appeal No. 324 of 1992 before the District Judge and the said appeal was heard and disposed of by the then Subordinate Judge (now Joint District Judge), 2nd Court, Faridpur who by the judgment and decree dated 7-4-1997 allowed the appeal and sent back the suit on remand to the trial court observing that the genealogy given by the plaintiffs in their plaint is not sufficient, giving an opportunity to cure the defect in that regard. After receipt of the record by the trial court, the plaintiffs amended their plaint on 12-11-1997 by introducing some facts and again amended the plaint on 28-6-1998 incorporating some facts and adding an additional prayer in suit. Thereafter, the trial court framed eight issues for retrial of the same and again decreed the suit by the judgment and decree dated 29-7-1998 on the findings that the plaintiffs are reversioners and Promoda Sundari transferred the property to the defendants without any legal necessity and also held that the suit property being agriculture land Promoda Sundari acquired no title. 

15. Against the judgment and decree of the trial court, the defendants further preferred Title Appeal No. 239 of 1998. The said appeal was heard by Additional District Judge, 1st Court, Faridpur, who allowed the appeal by judgment and decree dated 20-10-2003 and again sent back the suit on remand to the trial court with some observations made in the judgment. The appellate court again observed that fact of reversioner has not been properly substantiated by evidence and the trial court failed to observe that the property was sold by Promoda Sundari for legal necessity has to be gathered from attending circumstances. After arrival of the record, the case was transferred to the court of Assistant Judge, Alfadanga for disposal where it was renumbered as Title Suit No. 133 of 2014. Before the trial court the plaintiffs again amended their plaint by filing applications on 17-4-2004, 24-8-2005 and 11-5-2005 giving genealogy afresh with certain corrections. The learned Assistant Judge recorded evidence of the parties on recall and by the judgment and decree dated 15-8-2006 dismissed the suit on the findings and observations that the plaintiffs could not able to prove that Ram Joy and three others were full brothers as no PWs have witnessed them and nothing has come from the plaintiffs side to establish that they were full brothers and sons of a single person and secondly, held that the property was alienated by Promoda Sundari for her legal necessity and also held that admittedly, the plaintiffs have no title and possession in the property. 

16. Against the judgment and decree of the trial court, present petitioners preferred Title Appeal No. 207 of 2006 before the District Judge, Faridpur which was also disallowed on 30-3-2008. 

17. From perusal of plaint in suit filed on 25-3-1985 though in its paragraph 1, the plaintiffs stated that Pitambor Bepari, Madhob Bepari, Tara Chand Bepari and Guru Charan Bepari are full brothers but did not state who was their father and claimed that the petitioners are heirs of Avoy Charan Bepari. By subsequent amendment on 17-4-2004, the plaintiffs deleted the words "Pitambar Bepari, Madhab Bepari, Tara Chand Bepari and Guru Charan Bepari" "পরষ্পর সহোদর ভ্রাতা ছিলেন" and replaced the same with words "রাম জয় বেপারী, মাধব বেপারী তারা চাঁদ বেপারী এবং গুরু চরন বেপারী পরষ্পর সহোদর ভ্রাতা ছিলেন", But herein also the plaintiffs did not state name of their father and the said amendment brought in the plaint distorting the genealogy after about 17 years of filing of the suit. 

18. Earlier on 12-11-1997 by amendment of plaint the plaintiffs introduced the facts that: 
“অতঃপর এতদুদ্দেশ্যে Rs জরীপের কার্য শুরু হইলে পিতান্বর বেপারীর আক্তবিত্তে তাহার একমাত্র জীবিত পুত্র জংগ্রী বেপারী এবং মৃত পুত্র অর্থাৎ কৈলাশ চন্দ্রের পুত্রগণ শরৎ চন্দ্র, প্রাণনাথ এবং সতীশ চন্দ্রের নামের উপরোক্ত আর, এস, ১০৬৩ নং খতিয়ানে লিপি হইয়া প্রকাশিত হয় বটে। তবে উপরোক্ত আর, এস, রেকর্ডীয় প্রজাগণ বিভিন্ন সময় অত্র মোকদ্দমার অপরাপর ববাদীগণের নিকট তাহাদের অংশের সমূদয় সম্পত্তি বিভিন্ন সময়ে হস্তাস্তর করায় নালিশী খতিয়ানের জমা জমিতে উপরোক্ত জংমী বেপারী গং দিগের নালিশী খতিয়ানে কোন স্বত্তাংশ থাকে না। ইহা৷ ছাড়া উপরোক্ত জংগ্নী বেপারী, প্রাণনাথ বেপারী ও সতীশ চন্দ্র বেপারী এই বিবাদীগণের পিতার জীবমানে পরলোক গমন করায় উহাদিগকে অত্র মোকদ্দমায় বিবাদী শ্রেণীভুক্ত করা হয় নাই।” but failed to state who are the purchasers and why they have not been made parties.

19. The trial court in its judgment discussed the evidences led by plaintiffs in support of their claim of revisioners and the genealogy incorporated in the plaint in the year 2004. PW 3 is the vital witness who in his cross stated that Ram Joy Bepari. Madhab Bepari, Tara Chand Bepari and Guru Charan Bepari "আপন ভাই ছিল কিন্তু ইক্ত চার ব্যক্তির পিতার নাম কি ছিল তা বাদীপক্ষ আরজিতে বর্ণনা করেন নাই।" And he also stated that he heard about four brothers, but could not say who after whom died and he is also a close relative of plaintiffs and he could not say when Promoda Sundari died and all the PWs could not prove the fact that the plaintiffs are revisioners of Gostha Bepari. 

20. From perusal of Exhibit-1, CS Khatian No. 15/1, it appears that in the title Column of khatian, name of Petambor Bepari son of late Ram Joy Bepari, Avoy Charan Bepari son of late Madhab Bepari, Sadhu Bepari and Gostha Bepari son of late Tarachand Bepari, Muktakeshi Bewa wife of late Guru Charan Bepari have been recorded. From the said recording, it cannot be construed that Ram Joy Bepari, Madhab Bepari, Tarachand Bepari and Guru Charan Bepari were full brothers in the absence of any other evidences like their father's name or any other documents before CS record. Both the parties unequivocally admitted that the property in question was acquired by Gostha Bepari from the owner Manikial Bepari in the year 1945. Though the said facts were stated in the original plaint but subsequently, by way of amendment, the plaintiffs brought the fact on record that Gostha Bepari died leaving widow Promoda Sundari, SA khatian solely recorded in the name of Promoda Sundari for 1.92 acres. BS draft khatian recorded in the name of Ashananda Roy son of Pari Mohan Roy, the defendant No. 2 in suit measuring 1.20 acres who purchased the same from Promoda Sundari. Thereafter, Promoda Sundari again by a registered deed dated 25-6-1984 transferred 23 sataks of land to Sree Basudev Biswas and Sree Joydeb Biswas opposite party Nos. 1 and 49. 

21. I have gone through the evidences of PWs PW 1 claims that the deed if there be any produced by the defendants are forged and false and in cross he stated that Deed No. 440 dated 26-5-1984 executed by Promoda Sundari for 23 sataks is valid and deed dated 22-8-1981 is invalid deed and by the said deed the defendant No. 2 did not acquire any title in the property and they purchased the property from Promoda Sundari without her legal necessity. He stated that his father died 30 years ago when the plaintiffs were minors and their father did not take any care of Promoda Sundari. They used to live in the house of their maternal uncle, 2-3 miles away from the suit property and they could not produce any document showing payment of rents for the property after or before the death of Promoda Sundari. He stated that he filed the suit for recovery of possession of 1.92 acres, but the defendant Nos. 1, 2 and 49 purchased by two sale deeds only 1.53 sataks. Nowhere in the plaint or evidences the plaintiffs could state about the remaining land and he admitted that in original plaint they stated that Pitambar is one of the brother of Guru Charan, Avoy Charan and Ram Joy but subsequently, they claimed that Pitambar is son of Ram Joy and nephew of other three brothers. He also stated that Pitambar died leaving 3 sons Koilash, Jangli and another whose name is not known to him and he does not know Koilash died leaving whom and also stated that he did not see any of the heirs of Pitambar and does not know when they died. 

22. PW 2 Charubala Biswas in her exami-nation-in-chief stated that she used to live in the house left by Promoda Sundari under the plaintiffs, but in her cross she stated that the plaintiffs are living in Charmohon Mia's house and used to maintain the suit property from coming there from and also stated that the defendant No. 1 Bashudev lives in the house of the Promoda Sundari and the defendant No. 2 also in possession of the suit property and funeral of Gostha Bepari was performed by his wife Promoda Sundari and the expenses for the same was borne by her. PW 3 could not say when Promoda Sundari died and he is a barber who cut hairs of the plaintiffs after the death of Promoda Sundari. PW 4 is an old aged man Who in his examination in chief stated that he heard that Ram Joy, Madhab, Tara Chand and Guru Charan were full brothers but he did not see them. In his cross examination he unequivocally admitted that the defendant Nos. 1, 2 and 49 are in possession of the suit property. The plaintiffs used to live in Char Mohan, and the suit property is in Char Sultanpur which is 2-3 miles away from Char Mohan. He also stated that one son of Kailash used to live in India. He told that he does not know when Promoda Sundari died but in chief he claims that the funeral of Promoda Sundari was performed by the plaintiffs which contradicts each other. 

23. From the evidences and prayers made in the plaint by the plaintiff, it is clearly established that the plaintiffs are not in possession of the suit property. But 1.53 acres of land under the possession of defendant Nos. 1, 2 and 49 and in evidence, it has come out that out of the remaining land 14 sataks of land covered by plot No. 1866 is in the possession of Surandra Nath Mondal son of Akkhoy Kumar Mondal who has not been made party in the suit. It is not the case of the plaintiffs that they are in possession of the land other than the purchased land of defendant Nos. 1, 2 and 49 and could not justify why suit for recovery of possession has been filed against the defendant Nos. 1, .2 and 49 who purchased only 1.53 sataks of land out of 1.92 sataks. The trial court highlighted all those anomalies in the plaint, subsequent amendments, evidences both oral and documentary and found that the genealogy given by the plaintiffs in their original plaint as well as by subsequent amendment after 17 years contradicts each other and no clear picture has been given about acquisition of title in the property as reversioner of Gostha Bepari and the trial court also found that in the absence of clear genealogy of acquisition of property by the plaintiffs as reversioners the plaintiffs claim cannot sustain in law. 

24. In the recital of Deed No. 6163 dated 22-8-1981, it has been stated that “আমার স্বামী শ্রাদ্ধাদি ও তাহার পরলৌকিক কর্ম উদ্ধারের নিমিত্ত গয়াতে পিন্ডদান ও তীর্থ পযটন এবং নিজের ভরণ পোষনের জন্য নগদ টাকার প্রয়োজন বশতঃ”, and in the Deed No. 440 dated 26-5-1984 "আমার সাংসারিক নানা কারণ বশতঃ আমার স্বত্ব দখলিয় নিম্ন তপসিলের জমির বিক্রয় করার", but the plaintiffs to forestall the said contention in the deed could not bring any evidence that their father took care of Promoda Sundari and borne all the expenses for her livelihood or after death of their father they maintained Promoda Sundari's all the expenses including her funeral and post funeral ceremonies. It is also found that the plaintiffs were minors at the time of death of their father and they used to live in the house of their maternal uncle wherein they grown up which is 2-3 miles away from the suit property. No evidences led by the plaintiffs in regard to the fact that they constantly took care of Promoda Sundari and incurred expenses for her maintenance and all other expenses for her funeral and religious functions. It is not understandable, how a widow whose husband died in the year 1955 having no son and daughter can maintain herself without any support from any relative. In the instant case the sale deed of the year 1981 and 1984 have not been challenged by the plaintiffs at the first instance, but the prayer was made in the year 1998. 

25. Admittedly, the vendor is dead. The plaintiffs claim that they are reversioners and they took care of Promoda Sundari. In the absence of strong evidence in that regard the recital in the sale deed to the effect that in order to maintain herself and to pay the debts of her husband and for salvation of her husband's departed soul, to give Pindo and for her maintenance the property was being sold appears to be consistent with the circumstances, as there is no evidence of any independent source of income so far as the widow is concerned. In such circumstances relying upon the recital in the sale deed which raised some inferences relating to existence of necessity as held by the trial court as well as by the appellate court are found to be justified. 

26. The said recital of the deed have not been reverted in any manner by the plaintiff-appellant-petitioners by any evidence either oral or documentary that Promoda Sundari before alienation of the property earlier transferred any other property or she has other source of income or she took help from any relative other than the plaintiffs or the plaintiffs used to maintain her till her death. It is true that the fact of legal necessity has to be proved by the purchaser. The power of a Hindu female to alienate property are wider in respect of acts which conduced to the spiritual benefit of her deceased husband. The widow is entitled to sell the property even the whole of it if the income of the property is not sufficient to cover the expenses for such acts. In the present case the recital of the deed indicates legal necessity in different way; such as, spiritual benefits of her deceased husband, payment of debts and maintenance of the widow. In the absence of any other reliable evidences it can be easily inferred that the property was alienated by the widow of Gostha Bepari for legal necessity. The defendants, as purchaser of the property had obligations to prove legal necessity but in the instant case the plaintiffs in one hand could not establish and prove by any evidence that Promoda Sundari had no legal necessity to transfer the property in question and on the other hands the recital of the deed discloses some legal necessity which has to be construed liberally. The recital is clear evidence of the representation and if the circumstances are such as to justify a reasonable belief that an enquiry would have confirmed its truth, then when proof of actual enquiry has become impossible, the recital coupled with such circumstances would be sufficient evidence to support the deed. To hold otherwise would result in deciding that a title becomes weaker as it grows older, so that a transaction perfectly honest and legitimate when it took place would ultimately incapable of justification merely owning to the passage of time. Both the courts below concurrently observed and held that the widow of Gostha Bepari, Promoda Sundari had no other alternative for her livelihood. Being a widow it was necessary for her survival to alienate the property left by her husband. 

27. In view of the above, this Court thinks that both the courts below rightly dismissed the suit and disallowed the appeal on two counts firstly; the claim of reversioner has not been adequately proved as there is a grey area in the genealogy given by the plaintiffs in their plaint at the first instance and subsequently, though amended the plaint but could not substantiate by any evidence linking one with another and secondly, both the courts below concurrently found that the property was transferred by Promoda Sundari for legal necessity, therefore, this court is of the opinion that it cannot interfere with the concurrent findings of the facts sitting in revision. 

28. Taking into consideration the above, this Court finds no merit in the Rule. 

29. In the result, the Rule is discharged, however, without any order as to costs. 

Communicate a copy of this judgment to the court concerned and send down the lower court records at once. 

End.

full_judgment:
This Rule has been issued calling upon the opposite party No. 1, to show cause as to why the impugned judgment and decree dated 18-5-2014 (decree signed on 22-5-2014), passed by the Additional District Judge, Madaripur, in Title Appeal No.76 of 2012, allowing the appeal and reversing the judgment and decree dated 29-7-2012 (decree signed on 2-8-2012), passed by the Joint District Judge, 2nd Court, Madaripur, in Title Suit No.77 of 2011, should not be set-aside and/or pass such other order or orders passed as to this Court may seem fit and proper. The application for rejecting the revisional application filed by the opposite party-applicant is taken up for disposal alongwith this Rule. 

2. Facts, relevant for disposal of the Rule, in brief, are that, admittedly one Abdul Kader Khalifa, the father of the plaintiff-appellant was the owner of 92.50 acres of land in the concerned Mouza that includes the suit property as well. The case of the plaintiff is that, Abdul Kader Khalifa died leaving the plaintiff and the defendant Nos. 3-8 and their mother Zobeda Begum as his heirs. After the death of Zobeda Begum, the plaintiff and the defendant Nos. 3-8 were her heirs and accordingly the plaintiff has been owning and possessing the concerned Jama. The plaintiff admits that, the defendant No. 2 Md Younus Takukder was a co-sharer by purchase in the concerned Jama. However, the further case of the plaintiff is that, the plaintiff was enjoying the suit property along with other co-sharers, the defendant No. 2 (co-sharer by purchase) and defendant Nos. 3-8, brothers and sister, i.e. the co-sharer by inheritance. The further case of the plaintiff is that, the defendant No. 2, Md Younus Talukder, sold 12 decimals of land, secretly, by a registered deed No.4760 dated 13-12-2009. It has also been stated that, when Motiur Rahman. Howlader, brother of defendant No. 1 (purchaser) was filling earth in the suit property on 25-1-2011 and having seen this, the plaintiff asked Motiur Rahman Howlader as to why he was filling earth and then he came to know about the fact of sale of the suit property, on 25-1-2011 and at once, he, (plaintiff) shouted then and there that he has right to pre-emption in the suit property. Having heard this shout, local people, namely-Badsha Khalifa, Mozammel Khalifa, Motaleb Mollah, Mozazzel Matbor came forward, approached to the suit property, and then the plaintiff again demanded, keeping them as witnesses, that, he has right to pre-emption of the suit property and accordingly, he has filed this suit claiming that, he had already performed the formalities of Talab-e-Muasibat and Talab-e-Eshad. 

3. The defendant No. 1 Feroz Shai appeared in the suit and contested by filing written objection. His plain case is that, the plaintiff's father Abdul Kader Khalifa sold 24 decimals of land by deed No. 1227 dated 3-4-1994 to Md Younus Talukder (defendant No. 2) and one Abdul Jalil. The buyer Md Younus Talukder, thereafter, got separate mutation and separate Jama in his own name, in respect of 12 decimals of land, Md Younus Talukder by a registered sale deed No. 4760 dated 13-12-2009 sold his 12 decimals of land to the defendant No. 1. Besides, the plaintiff's had 30 decimals of land adjacent to the suit property and long before he had developed the said land (total 42 decimals) by filling earth and had constructed huts and installed Tube-well and has peacefully possessed the same with the knowledge of all. Further case of the defendant is that, the plaintiff has admitted in Title Suit No. 42 of 2011 that, they had no right in the suit property and that, in a proceeding, drawn under section 144 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, the Court of Magistrate found that, the defendant No. 1 (purchaser) had been peacefully possessing the suit property. His further case is that, the plaintiff's father Abdul Kader Khalifa having sold the suit property to defendant No. 2, Md Younus Talukder, by a registered deed 1227 dated 3-4-1994, and Younus Talukder having opened a mutation khatian and getting separate Jama in his name, the plaintiff had ceased to be a co-sharer in the 12 decimals of suit Plot since the date of deed No. 1227 dated 3-4-1994. Hence, the defendant has purchased 12 decimals of suit property by a registered deed and the plaintiff is not a co-sharer. Moreover, the defendant also asserts that, the case of the plaintiff is barred by limitation. 

4. In order to prove the case, the plaintiff had produced and proved some documents, marked as Exhibit 1 and 2 series, 3 and 4 and the defendant has produced and proved some documentary evidence, marked as Exhibit "Ka" and "Kha", as well as both sides had given oral evidence to support their respective cases. 

5. The trial court, after hearing the parties and having assessed the evidence on record, dismissed the suit by it's judgment and decree dated 29-7-2012 (decree signed on 2-8-2012). 

6. Against the said judgment and decree of the trial court, the plaintiff preferred Title Appeal No.76 of 2012 (as appellant) before the District Judge, Madaripur, which was heard by the Additional District Judge, Madaripur, who has allowed the appeal, vide judgment and decree dated 18-5-2014 (decree signed on 22-5-2014) and thereby reversed the judgment and decree of the trial court. 

7. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the judgment and decree of the appellate court, the defendant-respondent-petitioner has filed this application under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure and obtained the present Rule. 

8. Learned Advocate Mr AKM Rabiul Hassan and Mr MM Shafiullah appeared for the defendant-respondent-petitioner. Mr Rabiul Hassan, having placed the revisional application, first of all submits that, admittedly the suit property belonged to Abdul Kader Khalifa, father of the plaintiff alongwith other non-suit properties of the concerned Mouza. This Abdul Kader Khalifa, by a registered deed No. 1227 dated 03-4-1994, had sold total 24 decimals of land to Md Younus Talukder and to one Abdul Jalil and they got separate mutation and separate Jama in their respective names recording 12 decimals of land, proportionately, pursuant to deed No. 1227 dated 3-4-1994, but the plaintiff did not challenge the said deed. Thereafter, he proceeds on that, the brother and sisters of the plaintiffs are claiming to be co-sharers (defendant Nos. 3-8) of the concerned Jama. The learned Advocate then continues that, the plaintiff had ceased to be co-sharers in the 12 decimals of suit land since their father Abdul Kader Khalifa had transferred this 12 decimals of land to Md Younus Talukder (defendant No. 2) by a registered deed No. 1227 dated 3-4-1994 and Md Younus Talukder, thereafter, got a separate mutation khatian and also got the Jama in respect of that 12 decimals of land purchased by him. Therefore, the plaintiff has ceased to be a co-sharer, since the date of transfer i.e. from 3-4-1994 and they had no locus-standi to file this suit. He next submits that, the trial court has rightly found that, the suit is hopelessly barred by limitation under article 10 of schedule 1 of the Limitation Act. In support of his contention, the learned Advocate has referred to Exhibit "Kha", which is the certified copy of the plaint, filed by the plaintiff Habibur Rahman Khalifa against the said Motiur Rahman Howlader and others, seeking permanent injunction in respect of the same property, including the suit Plot No. 403, under khatian No. 228 of Mouza Mozafforpur. In the judgment, passed in the previous Title Suit No.42 of 2011, the court has recorded that, the plaintiff's father has sold 24 decimals of land from Plot No. 403 to Md Younus Talukder and Abdul Jalil by a registered deed No. 1227 dated 3-4-1994 and thereafter Md Younus Talukder has sold his 12 decimals of land to the defendant No. 1 Feroz Shai, by a registered deed No. 4760 dated 13-12-2009. As such, the learned Advocate points out that, the same plaintiff was aware about the sale deed No. 4760 dated 13-12-2009, since the Title Suit was filed by him, on 24-2-2011, i.e. long before filing of the present suit for pre-emption on 5-4-2011. But, the plaintiff has deliberately suppressed the fact of filing the previous Title Suit No. 42 of 2011 (seeking permanent injunction). The learned Advocate next submits that, the finding of the trial court that, the suit is barred by limitation under article 10 schedule 1 of the Limitation Act is absolutely lawful and that, these plaintiffs have resorted to fraud in filing the instant suit by suppressing the fact of their acquiring knowledge of the sale to the defendant No. 1, long before 25-1-2011 (the alleged date of Talab-E-Muasibat). The plaintiff is not a credible one, while his witnesses, i.e. PWs 1 and 3 are his uncle and his cultivator respectively, who are apparently partisan witnesses and that, the plaintiff could not prove his case of Talab-E-Muasibat and Talab-E-Eshad. Rather, the trial court has rightly passed the judgment and decree relying upon the deposition of P.W. Nos. 1-3 and having assessed the entire evidence on record in its proper perspective. On the contrary, the appellate court has failed to notice the fact proved by the Exhibit "Ka" and "Kha" and the deed No. 4760 dated 13-12-2009, whereby the defendant No. 1 (Pre-emptee) has derived title of 12 decimals of land from Md Younus Talukder, who is not the predecessor of the plaintiff and admittedly, the plaintiff is not heir of Md Younus Talukder. The defendant-appellant-petitioner purchased the suit property from Md Younus Talukder, which is the subject of separate .lama, he also points out. Moreover, the appellate court remained totally silent about the Exhibit "Kha", (Judgment of the previous suit for permanent injunction filed by the same plaintiff) and in which he failed to get the decree of permanent injunction in respect of the self-same suit property, which has been deliberately suppressed from the knowledge of the court by the plaintiff (pre-emptor),at the time of filing of the instant pre-emption case, and the appellate court has thus failed to perform its duty to assess the material evidence independently dispassionately. Moreso, the appellate court has totally overlooked the findings of the trial court about the contradictions found in the deposition of the witnesses of the plaintiff as recorded in the trial court's judgment, and that, the plaintiff could not mention the time of filling of the earth on 25-1-2011, while the PW 2 and 3 contradicts each other about the time at which the plaintiff allegedly shouted declaring his right of pre-emption and about the numbers of Truck etc. The learned Advocate submits that, the appellate court, without giving any cogent reason, has reversed the findings of the trial court. Therefore, the finding of the appellate court is totally perverse and clearly amounts to misreading and non-reading of the evidence, while it has made out a 3rd case that, the transaction is benami transaction and for all these reasons, the learned Advocate submits that, the judgment of the appellant court is shockingly perverse and there are misreading and non-reading of the evidence in passing its judgment, hence, the same are liable to be reversed. He argues that, the plaintiff has also failed to prove the case of Talab-E-Muasibat and Talab-E-Eshad as has been rightly pointed out by the trial court, which is very essential prerequisite for claiming the right of pre-emption under the Muhammadan Law. The learned Advocate, in support of his contention, has referred to a decision, reported in 21 DLR page 211 between Md Lokman Mondal vs Amir Ali Mondal and others. Moreover, the plaintiff did not say that he needs a prior demand i.e. Talab-E-Muasibat and Talab-E-Eshad and on this ground alone, the findings of the appellate court may kindly be reversed. 

9. Learned Senior Advocate Mr Abdul Quiyum and learned Advocate Mr Md Mahbubur Rahman appeared on behalf of the opposite party No. 1. The main contention of the learned Advocates is that, the appeal filed by the defendant No. 1 i.e. the present petitioner was incompetent because his brother Motiur Rahman Howlader, although appeared before the trial court and had filed the written objection on behalf of the defendant No. 1, Feroz Shai, but, this Motiur Rahman Howlader did not have any power of attorney as required under the provisions of rule 2(a) of Order 3 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908. Mr Quiyum has argued at length on this point and submits that, the defendant No. 1 has not been represented in this case by a competent person. Therefore, the trial court ought not to have accepted his appearance and the appellate court ought to have arrived at the finding that, the appeal was not competent, since it was not filed by Feroz Shai. The further contention of the learned Advocate is that, the appellate court, as the last court of fact, has rightly assessed the evidence on record and found that, the plaintiff has rightly proved the Talab-E-Muasibat and Talab-E-Eshad as required under the Muhammadan Law and the appellate court has also found that, the suit was not barred by limitation and on these specific findings, the appellate court has reversed the findings of the trial court and has allowed the appeal. He next submits that, the appellate court has committed no error of law in passing the impugned judgment and decree, nor that has resulted in any error in the decision occasioning failure of justice. Therefore, this Rule has no merit and the same may kindly be discharged. 

10. The learned Advocate for the petitioner, in reply to the submissions of the learned Advocate for the opposite party, further submits that, as per description of parties given in the cause title to the plaint of Title Suit No.77 of 2011, Motiur Rahman Howlader is the brother and executants of Feroz Shai. He also submits that, the summon and notices were accordingly served upon Motiur Rahman Howlader, at the instance of the plaintiff, not upon Feroz Shai. He also points out that, this submission of the opposite party, rather cuts the very root of the plaintiff's case for the admitted position that, no summon or notice has been served upon the defendant No. 1 and the plaint was not properly presented or filed before the trial court and, as such, the entire proceedings is void ab-initio and is not maintainable. 

11. I have heard the learned Advocates for both the parties, who have made their elaborate submissions, as noted hereinabove. 

12. From the examination of the plaint, I find that, the plaintiff has described the defendant as "ফিরোজ সাই, পিতা-মৃত অহেদ আলী হাওলাদার ওরফে অহেদ আলী সাই, সাং-মালেরকান্দি, পোঃ- সিকদারহাট, থানা+উপজেলা- শিবচর, জেলা-মাদারীপুর। পক্ষে-কার্য্যকারক মতিউর রহমান হাওলাদার, পিতা-মৃত অহেদ আলী হাওলাদার, সাং-মালেরকান্দি, পোঃ-সিকদারহাট, থানা-শিবচর, জেলা-মাদারীপুর। ক্রেতা-বিবাদী।” 

13. Therefore, apparently, the plaintiff has described and admitted Motiur Rahman Howlader as "কার্য্যকারক" (i.e. executants or agent) of the defendant No. 1 and the summons as well as the notices of appeal were served upon him, at the instance of the plaintiff. None of the courts below have found any difficulties, because Motiur Rahman Howlader is an admitted "কার্য্যকারক" as described by the plaintiffs. Based on this description, admitted position and narration of the plaintiff, both the courts below have proceeded to dispose of the matter before them, moreso, without any objection, that should have been raised (if there was any lawful scope) at the earliest opportunity. 

14. In my considered opinion, the provisions of rule 2(a) of Order 3 of the Code of Civil Procedure does not apply in this kind of case where the plaintiffs themselves have described the defendant-appellant-Motiur Rahman Howlader as the "কার্য্যকারক" (i.e. executant or agent) of the defendant No. 1-appellant. Moreover, the plaintiff cannot take advantage of his own conduct and is estoppels to deny his own description and admission of Motiur Rahman Howlader as the `Karjokarok' of his brother, defendant No. 1 (who was then staying at abroad). 

15. Besides, even if, it were found that, the courts below had committed an error of law in admitting Motiur Rahman Howlader as the executant of the plaintiff, then also I find that, such alleged error (though actually not) has not resulted in any erroneous decision, nor that had occasioned in the failure of justice in any manner. 

16. Next, 1 find that, the issue as to whether this plaintiff had any locus-standi to file the instant Title Suit No.77 of 2011, claiming pre-emption under the Muhammadan Law, has not been discussed by either of the courts below. It is to be recorded here that, the suit property, alongwith some other non-suit properties, belonged to the plaintiff's father Abdul Kader Khalifa, who, by a registered deed No. 1227 dated 03-4-1994, sold 24 decimals of land (that includes the 12 decimals of suit land) to Md Younus Talukder (i.e. the seller-defendant No. 2) and to Abdul Jalil Talukder, in equal shares. Thereafter, Md Younus Talukder, the defendant No. 2, has got his name mutated and his Jama was separated in respect of 12 decimals of land (the suit land), that falls into a separate Jama. As such, the 12 decimals of the suit property has ceased to be the part and parcel of the common Jama of Plot No. 403 of Mouza Mozafforpur and, admittedly, Md Younus Talukder was neither father, nor the predecessor of the plaintiff. So, the plaintiff has ceased to be a co-sharer in the suit property, sold by his father to Md Younus Talukder by registered deed 1227 dated 3-4-1994 and the suit property has, thereafter, become a property under separate Jama and khatian. As such, the plaintiffs had no locus-standi to file the Title Suit No.77 of 2011, seeking pre-emption in respect of the suit plot. 

17. Next, having turned my attention to the issue as to whether the suit is barred by limitation. I find that, the plaintiff knew about the transfer of the suit property to Md Younus Talukder, vide deed No.4760, 13-12-2009, as evident from the previous Title Suit No. 42 of 2011, filed by the plaintiff seeking permanent injunction in respect of the suit property and that suit was filed on 28-2-2011. The plaintiffs failed to get a decree of permanent injunction in that suit and then filed the instant suit, as the second chance. 

18. 1 find that, the conduct of the plaintiff, all along, is not fair. He is guilty of fraudulent suppressions of the fact of filing the previous suit for permanent injunction (Exhibit Kha), in respect of the self-same property. 

19. The plaintiff then, inspite of his having knowledge of his father's sale to Md Younus Talukder on 13-2-2009, has filed this instant frivolous, vexatious and ill-advised suit, and interestingly, tried to expose himself as an scholar about the formalities required to be performed for filing a pre-emption case under the provisions of Muhammadan Law, a practice which has almost lost into oblivion, since the pre-emption cases are now being filed, either under section 96 of the SAT Act, 1950 or under section 24 of the NAT Act, 1949. 

20. In view of the forgoing facts and circumstances, I am of the considered opinion that, the findings arrived at by the appellate court are based on misreading and non-reading of evidence as well as on misinterpretation of the oral evidence. The appellate court did not notice the lacuna and the contradictions in the deposition of PWs 1, 2 and 3, which has been rightly pointed out and duly recorded by the trial court in its judgment. Moreover, the appellate court, as the last court of fact, has neither considered the Exhibit "Kha" nor it has framed or decided the basic issue regarding the locus-standi of the plaintiffs in filing the instant suit. Hence, the findings of the appellate court should be reversed and the impugned judgment and decree should be set-aside, and those of the trial court should be upheld. 

21. This Rule has merit. 
Order 
In the result, the Rule is made absolute. 
The findings of the appellate court is hereby reversed and the judgment and decree dated 18-5-2014 (decree signed on 22-5-2014), passed by the Additional District Judge, Madaripur, in Title Appeal No.76 of 2012, is hereby set-aside and the judgment and decree dated 29-7-2012 (decree signed on 02-8-2012), passed by the Joint District Judge, 2nd Court, Madaripur, in Title Suit No.77 of 2011, is hereby affirmed. 
Consequently, the application for rejecting the revisional application filed by the opposite party-applicant is also rejected. 
The order of stay granted earlier by this Court shall stand vacated. 
This is a fit case for awarding penal cost of Taka 1,00,000. However, taking a lenient view, cost is not imposed. 
Copies of this judgment be sent to the courts concerned alongwith the LCR at once. 

End.

Md Khurshid Alam Sarker, J: This is an application under section 228 read with section 229 of the Companies Act, 1994 (briefly, the Companies Act) at the instance of Bangladesh Steel Re-Rolling. Mills Limited, being the transferee-company, and BSRM Steel Mills Limited, being the transferor-company, seeking approval of a scheme of amalgamation of the above two companies, whereby the entire undertaking of the transferor-company, as going concerns together with all assets and liabilities, are proposed to be transferred to and vested in the transferee-company.

2. The petitioner No. 1 Bangladesh Steel Re-Rolling Mills Limited (transferee-company) was incorporated as a private company under the Companies Act, 1913 (since repealed and substituted by the Companies Act, 1994) in the year 1960 in Chattogram with the objects, inter alia, to carry on the business of steel rolling and re-rolling mills for manufacturing MS products such as MS rods, rounds, flats, squares, wire rods, MS angles, tees, channels and other sections, bolts & nuts, wires etc and, thereafter, having been converted into a public limited company on 03 November, 2009, it started trading of the shares of the company in Dhaka Stock Exchange (DSE) and Chittagong Stock' Exchange (CSE) from 27 April, 2015. It is stated that the transferee-company is one of the oldest and largest producers of structural steel in Bangladesh, which has an authorized share capital of Taka 500,00,00.000 only divided into 50,00,00,000 ordinary shares of Taka I0 each and the issued, subscribed and paid-up capital is Taka 236,06,82,360 divided into 23,60,68,236 shares of Taka 10 each. 5. It is stated that the transferor-company is a subsidiary of the transferee-company and clause II1(m) of the object clause in Memorandum of Association (MoA) of the transferee company permits amalgamation with the transferor company; likewise, clause 111(23) of the object clause in MoA of the transferor company permits this .amalgamation. It is stated that the process of steel making justifies amalgamation of a final product manufacturer (the transferee company) with a backward-linkage/raw material manufacturer (the transferor company), because in the steel production process, recycled materials as well as traditional raw materials, such as iron, rods, coal, and limestone are melted and heated to produce high quality molten steel billets (MS Billets) and these billets are treated in the next step by adding or removing certain elements and/or manipulating the temperature and production environment. The MS Billets are used as raw materials for the manufacture of structural products, such as rods, angle and bars through a process called re-rolling. As the transferor-company is engaged in production of MS Billets and the transferee-company is engaged in the process of re-rolling to make the final product for sale to consumers, the amalgamation would pave the way for general consumers, dealers and suppliers of steel products to obtain a 'one-stop solution' from a single entity to meet up their need of steel products. In an expectation of increasing profitability, by creating a combined entity, the Board of Directors of the transferee company resolved in the board meeting dated 16th September, 2016 that the companies be amalgamated, and the Board of Directors of the transferor company resolved in the board meeting dated 16th September, 2016 that the companies be amalgamated. Hence, this application.

6. By filing an affidavit-in-opposition and a supplementary thereto, the respondent No. 2-Bangladesh Securities and Exchange Commission (BSEC) states, amongst other, that the proposed scheme of amalgamation should not be sanctioned due to the reasons that general shareholders will be losers as (i) the transferor company has huge liability compared to low net asset, (ii) the Net Asset Value (NAV) was considered at revaluation price rather than historical cost and (iii) the retained earnings of the transferor company was negative until 30-6-2018, in other words, the transferor company has huge liabilities. It is stated that the asset of the transferor company has been revalued by ACNABIN Chartered Accountants Firm and the petitioner-companies with malafide intention have managed the report in question as prepared by ACNABIN CA firm using tactics and without following international accounting standards to hide actual financial position of the companies, because it is evident from the audited financial statements of BSRM Steel Mills Limited as on 30-6-2019 that the transferor company incurred accumulated loss of Taka 7.25 crore as on 30-6-2018 whereas the earning based valuation of share price has been determined 34.96 per share considering 2 (two) years only which asserts ill motive of the petitioners and further, while the plant of the transferor company normally manufactures 8,62,500 Metric Ton products, in 2019 the volume of its production capacity has been shown 9,13,241 Metric Ton which is 106% of its total capacity i.e. the value of share of the transferor company has been shown to be augmented dramatically. It is stated that acceptance of that report of ACNABIN is disputed to BSEC on identical issue; on 28-1-2020, the BSEC raised objection against this firm and advised Institute of Chartered Accountants of Bangladesh (ICAB) to take legal action against them and the same information has been reported in the Financial Express on 30-1-2020 and 22-8-2020, in the New Age on 29-1-2020 and 23-8-2020 and in the Business Standard on 30-1-2020 and 23-8-2020). It is stated that the fate of the general investors shall be like that of the Keya Cosmetics Ltd which was amalgamated with private company in the manner as proposed here in this case.

7. Mr Tanjub-ul Alam, the learned Advocates appearing for the petitioners, at the very outset having presented an overview of the case, seeks this Court's permission to make detailed submission by his junior Mr lmran Anwar. Mr lmran Anwar then, takes this Court through the various clauses of the scheme of amalgamation in an endeavour to place the modus operandi of the proposed amalgamation, and contends that through the scheme of amalgamation of the transferor-company with the transferee-company, the entire undertaking of the transferor-company as a going concern, together with all its assets and liabilities relating thereto. have been proposed to be transferred to and vested in the transferee-company; that the assets, licenses, permits and other benefits and privileges held by or conferred upon the transferor-company will be vested in the transferee-company without any further act, instrument or deed, pursuant to clause 7 of the scheme; that all liabilities of the transferor-company shall likewise be vested in the transferee-company without any further act, instrument or deed, pursuant to clause 8 of the scheme.

8. Regarding valuation of these two companies, Mr Anwar contends that the transferor-company is a non-listed company and, as such, there is no published market price for the shares; that in undertaking this task, the valuer considered historical information to determine Net Asset Value (NAV) method of valuation and Earning Based Valuation (EBV) method of valuation; that historical financial information was collected from the audited financial statements of the companies and market information was collected from official website of Dhaka Stock Exchange and published report/ reviews of Dhaka Stock Exchange Limited; that applying the usual methodology, the NAV per share was deduced at Taka 34.57 based on the audited financial statements as of 30 June, 2019 in respect of the transferor-company; that in determining the Earning Per Share in respect of the transferor-company, the net profit after tax was considered for the years 2017-18 and 2018-19, being the data of last two years since the company maintained operation at desired capacity; that from the calculation done by the ACNABIN, the EBV per share stands at Taka 34.96 in respect of the transferor-company; that taking an average, the value per share has been calculated as Taka 34.76 for the transferor-company. On the other hand, he continues to submit, the transferee-company is a listed entity, its shares' market price of each day is available from DSE; that as appears in the report, the transferee-company has a NAV per share at Taka 97.46 in consideration of the audited financial statements as of 30 June, 2019; that under the EBV method, the audited financial statements of the transferee-company since 2014-15 up until 2018-19 was considered, i.e. for a period of five years, and the average P/E ratio for 6 months starting from 31-01-2019 until 30-06-2019 as available from the Dhaka Stock Exchange was taken into consideration; that applying this methodology, EBV per share for the transferee-company stood at Taka 41.44; that on average of the prices calculated under NAV and EBV method, the value for each share in the transferee-company stood at Taka 69.45 and, accordingly, for the purpose of merger, the share exchange ratio was set at 1:0.5005.

9. In an effort to detail the share exchange ratio and distribution of shares among the shareholders of the transferor company, Mr Imran Anwar submits that the method to be applied for reorganization of capital of these two companies is that the transferee-company shall issue and allot the ordinary shares of Taka 10 in the ratio of 0.5005 (zero point five zero zero five) ordinary shares in the transferee-company for every 1 (one) ordinary share of the face value of Taka 10 held in the transferor-company to the ordinary shareholders of the transferor company whose names are recorded in the register of members on a date to be fixed by the Board of Directors of the transferee-company, which would be the "Record Date"; that these newly issued shares of the transferee-company shall be issued, allotted and credited as fully paid up in favour of the shareholders of the transferor-company; that the transferee-company would issue 10,86,43,936 ordinary shares of Taka 10 each to the shareholders of the transferor-company as consideration towards the settlement of this transaction as per the scheme. In an endeavour to rebut the allegation of inflation in the value of the transferor company's assets by revaluation, Mr Anwar places before this Court the various provisions of the International Standard on Auditing (ISA) and International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS), and submits that all companies are permitted to revalue their assets within an interval of three to five years and since the last valuation was done in 2011 for Bangladesh Steel Re-rolling Mills Limited and in 2012 for BSRM Steel Mills Limited, there is no bar on revaluation in 2019 as per international accounting standards. Then, he claims that if revaluation were not done, more shares were required to be issued from the transferee entity to the shareholders of the transferor company inasmuch as in the proposed exchange ratio of 1:0.5005, the transferee company is required to issue 108,643,936 shares, whereas without revaluation the share exchange ratio stands at 1:0.513688 and the transferee company is required to issue 111,506,614 under the old valuation, resulting into 2,862,679 additional shares to be issued by the transferee company.

10. With regard to the issue of having Negative Retained Earnings of the transferor company, Mr Imran Anwar submits that negative retained earnings are not bar to amalgamation under any law, because a company may have negative retained earnings for a variety of reasons and the companies usually have negative retained earnings in initial years of operation, as is the case for transferor company up to 30-6-2018 because during early years of operation the company needs to make investment more than its income, and generation of income gradually increases over the period. By taking me through Paragraphs 39-42 of the International Accounting Standard (IAS)-16, Mr Anwar submits that revaluation of asset does not increase retained earnings, rather revaluation is recorded under a separate head, namely, revaluation reserve. He contends that the retained earnings has already became positive for the transferor company as the transferor company started to make profits since 2018 and, currently, it has a solid positive retained earnings after two consecutive years of profit and, as of today, remains as a financially healthy company. On the other hand, Mr Anwar adds, the retained earnings of transferee company as of 30 June 2019 is over 795 crore BDT as of 30th June 2019. He contends that while the transferor company has liability of 3,199 crore BDT as of 30 June 2019, it has more asset of 4,563 crore BDT as of 30 June 2019 and, in case of transferee company for the year ending on 30 June 2019, the total asset of transferee is Taka 5,255 crores and total liability is Taka 2954 crores. In the consolidated financial statement for the year ended 30 June, 2019, upon consolidation, the total asset is Taka 91,067,184,337 and the total liabilities is Taka 60,558,665,062 and, therefore, the transferor company is a profitable concern and the amalgamation is going to happen between two financially solvent and sound companies.

11. Regarding compliance of the relevant laws, Rules and this Court's Directions/Orders, Mr Anwar contends that following the meeting of the Board of Directors of the transferee company, which is a listed entity, it duly declared Price Sensitive Information ("PSI") through the Dhaka and Chittagong Stock Exchanges and published the PSI on 17-9-2019 in two newspapers as per the applicable rules framed by the Bangladesh Securities and Exchange Commission, namely, Dhaka Stock Exchange (Listing) Regulations, 2015 and সিকিউরিটিজ ও এক্সচেন্জ কমিশন (সুবিধাভোগী ব্যবসা নিষিদ্ধকরণ), বিধিমালা, ১৯৯৫; that upon preliminary Court Order on 14-10-2019, the respective companies published another PSI through Dhaka and Chittagong Stock Exchanges and published the PSI on 22-10-2019 in two newspapers as per the applicable rules framed by the Bangladesh Securities and. Exchange Commission, namely, Dhaka Stock Exchange (Listing) Regulations, 2015 and সিকিউরিটিজ ও এক্সচেন্জ কমিশন (সুবিধাভোগী ব্যবসা নিষিদ্ধকরণ), বিধিমালা, ১৯৯৫। He contends that the petitioners also have fully complied with the Order dated 14-10-2019 of this Court, such as, the transferee company called an EGM by issuing notice dated 23-10-2019, the said notice was communicated to the shareholders of the transferee company by exhausting various mechanisms to ensure maximum participation; that the shareholders of the transferee company in the EGM dated 18-12-2019 unanimously approved the scheme of amalgamation; that out of the total shareholders, 504 shareholders were present in the meeting and none of the shareholders raises any objection regarding the amalgamation and since the shareholders present unanimously voted for a special resolution, the scheme of amalgamation was duly approved; that in similar way, upon duly issuance of notice to the shareholders of the transferor company, its EGM was held on 18-12-2019 that the shareholders attending the EGM unanimously passed a special resolution to approve the scheme of amalgamation. Mr Anwar further contends that according to the Order of this Court, all the creditors of the transferee company were notified for the creditors meeting on 21-11-2019 through registered-post notice dated 29-10-2019; that the resolution was passed unanimously by all the creditors who represent 90% in terms of value of liabilities of the transferee company and, in the same manner, all the creditors of the transferor company were notified for the creditors' meeting on 21-11-2019 through registered post notice dated 29-10-2019; that the resolution was passed unanimously by all the creditors present, who in aggregate represent 90% in terms of value of liabilities of the transferee, and none of the creditors of either company raised any objection against the amalgamation till today.

12. With regard to allegation against the ACNABIN, Mr lmran Anwar contends that there is an allegation against a partner of ACNABIN named Mr Rokunuzzaman, FCA in relation to their work for Aman Feed Limited, which has nothing to do with the present case, because the partner involved in this case is Mr Mominul Karim FCA. He contends that the allegation raised by the BSEC on this score is contrary to established legal maxim of "presumption of innocence until proven guilty" and, more importantly, ACNABIN is listed as a recognized accounting firm both by the BSEC and Bangladesh Bank, and just because there is allegation against one of their partners does not invalidate their work or their credibility, particularly when a different partner, as in this present case, carries out the work. Mr lmran Anwar, the learned Advocate for the petitioners, argues that there have been numerous communications between the petitioner companies and the BSEC regarding this merger and, in none of these occasions, the BSEC raised any issue of objection relating to the amalgamation, nor did it issue any letter of objection to the transferee company or the transferor company. He contends that ACNABIN being not disqualified from carrying out the audit work or valuation work by any Court in Bangladesh or by any regulatory authority and, in the absence of such disqualification, ACNABIN's report should not be questioned inasmuch as that would render all work of ACNABIN invalid, questionable and dubious since the point of time when the allegation was raised; that the petitioners engaged ACNABIN because it is a widely reputed chartered accountant firm who has considerable experience in carrying out audit and valuation work; that the valuation was carried out much earlier compared to the point in time when the allegation against ACNABIN was raised and the allegation relating to Aman Feed has no connection with regard to the valuation in the present case so as to render their entire work unreliable. Mr Imran Anwar submits that there is no illegality in the valuation process, as not a single one that the respondent BSEC has been able to point out, nor has there been any violation or non-compliance of legal provision in carrying out the valuation exercise and so there is no justification to appoint an audit firm adding costs and complexity to the process of amalgamation. He submits that there is no requirement under law for appointment of valuation expert in the given scenario where a valuation has already been conducted by an independent audit firm having enlistment with the BSEC and the Bangladesh Bank. He claims that this petition is completely a bona fide one.

13. He then prays that since all the requirements of section 228(2) of the Companies Act have been clearly satisfied, this Court should allow this petition.

14. Per contra Mr AM Masum, the learned Advocate for the BSEC, submits that the proposed scheme of amalgamation is inaccurate and unfair inasmuch as the assets of the transferor company have been revalued from around Taka 323 crore to Taka 978 crore which is 3 times of actual value, whereas, the assets of the transferee company have not been revalued and consequently it impacts upon the calculation of NAV, EPS, EBV, PIE etc and thereby the price of the share of transferor company has been shown to be increased which is totally incongruous with accounting policy and practice. By taking me through the provisions of Rules 3(3)(a) and 14(d) of the Bangladesh Securities and Exchange Commission (Public Issue) Rules, 2015, the learned Advocate for the BSEC strenuously submits that the petitioner-companies have prepared the scheme of amalgamation in violation of the aforesaid laws. He submits that ERRS-13 (Fair Value Measurement) prescribes three widely used valuation techniques which are (i) market approach, (ii) the cost approach and (iii) the income approach, and single valuation technique may be applied in case of quoted price in active market, otherwise multiple valuation techniques shall be apt and evaluated considering the reasonableness of the range of values indicated by those result, but ACNABIN has prepared the audit report without following the said principles of accounting.

15. In a bid to place before this Court his concerns about the interest and right of the general shareholders, Mr Masum, the learned Advocate for the BSEC, submits that as per the scheme of amalgamation, the net asset value of the transferee company is Taka 2,300 crore against its debt worth of Taka 1,527 crore and hence, the debt is 33.61 percent lower than net asset but after merger, this debt would be about 15.11 percent more than its net asset value which consequently will be shifted upon shoulder of its general investor. He submits that in the report prepared by ACNABIN Chartered Accountants Firm, 5 years weighted average earning per share has been considered for the transferee company's share valuation and its EPS is shown as 6.7438 whereas EPS has been shown as 2.6800 for the transferor company by taking into only 2 years weighted average earning per share and, furthermore, only the transferee company's market price earnings ratio (P/E-6.10) has been considered for the transferee company's share valuation whereas summation of 4 peers has been considered in case of the transferor company which inflated share price and exchange ratio of the transferor company abnormally and in case of transfer of shares and repatriation of sale proceeds of shares in favor of non-listed company, fair value of the shares shall be determined by weighted average calculation of all the 3 (three) valuation approaches i.e. NAV, market value and discounted cash flow approach, but only one method of valuation and exchange ratio has been used by ACNABIN Chartered Accountants Firm in proposed amalgamation which is not justified.

16. He submits that from the audited financial statements of both the companies as on 30-6-2019, it is apparent that the transferor company is high geared company having total bank liabilities of Taka 2,788 crore whereas the transferee company is a lower risky company having total bank liabilities of Taka 1,527.75 crore and therefore after amalgamation, unquoted shares of the transferor company shall be liquidated in a publically listed company by exchanging quoted shares of publicly listed company; and since 59.06% share belongs to general investors, burden of this colossal amount of aforesaid loan will go upon the public shareholders and, as such, the merger of these companies should not be allowed. 20. After hearing the learned Advocates, perusing the petition and affidavits-in-opposition together with their annexures and reading the relevant statutory laws plus case-laws, it appears to this. Court that the issues to be adjudicated upon by this Court are; (i) whether the petitioner companies' instant application satisfies the legal requirements under section 228 of the Companies Act, (ii) whether the petitioner companies violated any laws of the land in preparation of the scheme of amalgamation, (iii) whether the petitioner companies' audit reports were prepared in consonance with the provisions/Guidelines of the International Accounting Standard (IAS), (iv) whether the interests of the general shareholders i.e. the public interest would be jeopardized in any manner because of the proposed amalgamation, (v) whether this Court is competent to interfere with the audit report prepared by the petitioner-companies CA Firm for the purpose of amalgamation and (vi) if this Court decides to okay the proposed scheme of the amalgamation, then, what provisions should be made by this Court under section 229 of the Companies Act.

21. For an effective adjudication of the issue No. 1, namely, whether the petitioner-companies' instant application satisfies the legal requirements under sections 228 & 229 of the Companies Act, it would be useful to be acquainted with the provisions of sections 228 and 229 of the Companies Act, which are reproduced below:

Section 228: Power to compromise with creditors and members:—

(1) Where a compromise or arrangement is proposed between a company and its creditors or any class of them, or between the company and its members or any class of them, the Court may, on the application in summary way of the company or of any creditor or member of the company or, in the case of a company being wound up, of the liquidator, order a meeting of the creditors or class of creditors, or the members of the company or class of members, as the case may be, to be called held and conducted in such manner as the Court directs.

(2) If a majority in number representing three-fourths in value of creditors, or of members as the case may be, present either in person or by proxy at the meeting, agree to any compromise or arrangement, the compromise or arrangement shall if sanctioned by the Court be binding on all the creditors or the class of creditors, on all the members or class of members, as the case may be, and also on the company, in the case of a company in the course of being wound up, on the liquidator and contributories of the company.
