case_source: (From the judgment and order dated 17-12-2009 passed by the High Court Division in Writ Petition No.6053 of 2008)
full_judgment:
Obaidul Hassan, J: This civil appeal has arisen out of a petition for leave to appeal under Article 103 of the Constitution of the People's Republic of Bangladesh filed by the appellants against the judgment and order dated 17-12-2009 passed by the High Court Division in Writ Petition No.6053 of 2008 making the Rule absolute.

2. Facts necessary for the disposal of the appeal are that the respondent No. 1 as the writ petitioner filed Writ Petition No.6053 of 2008 before the High Court Division against the appellants seeking for a direction upon them to release his 11 decimals of land appertaining to SA Plots No.71 and 30 decimals of land appertaining to SA Plot No. 66 both under SA Khatian No.112, No.88 Bagchar Mouza, under Police Station-Kotwali, District-Jessore from the list of vested property.

3. The writ-petitioner, herein respondent, stated inter alia that he is permanent citizen of Bangladesh and owner of 11 decimals of land appertaining to SA Plots No.71 and 30 decimals of land appertaining to SA Plot No.66 both under SA Khatian No.112, No.88 Bagchar Mouza, under Police Station-Kotwali, District-Jessore. The land belonged to one Sujayet Ali Kha, but it was wrongly recorded in the name of one Noni Gopal Das in SA Khatian No.112 under the same mouza. Challenging the wrong recording Sujayet Ali Kha instituted Title Suit No.587 of 1970 seeking declaration of his title in the said land impleading Noni Gopal Shah and the Assistant Custodian of Enemy Property, Jessore, the then Sub-Divisional Officer, Jessore as defendants. The said suit was decreed in favour of Sujayet Ali Kha by the judgment and decree dated 15-3-1971 passed by the learned Munsif, 3rd Court, Jessore. While Sujayet Ali Kha had been in possession of the said property died leaving behind his wife Anwara Khatun along with his three sons namely, Mohammad Ali, Swakat Ali and Jahangir and one daughter Fatima Khatun as his heirs. The successors of said Sujayet Ali Kha by executing five kabalas dated 16-8-1998, 11-6-1998 and 7-6-1998 sold the said land to Nawab Ali, Momtaz Khanam, Zillur Rahman, Abul Kashem, Shahabuddin, Laila Afroz, Nazir Ahmed and Akram Hossain, who subsequently sold the same by executing four kabalas dated 16-7-2005, 28-2-2006, 6-3-2006 and 28-4-2006 to the writ petitioners-respondents and handed over possession to him and since then he has been enjoying and possessing the land in question. The said land also had been mutated in his name and he has been paying the rent and taxes regularly. The aforesaid vendors of the respondents before selling the said land to the respondents filed an application before the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue), Jessore being VP Miscellaneous Case No.98-Kot of 1997 with a prayer to release the said land from the list of vested property. The application was rejected on 11-7-1999 by the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue), Jessore and he also referred the same to the learned advocate for the vested property to take necessary steps for getting the decree passed in Title Suit No.587 of 1970 set-aside. The learned advocate gave opinion that the steps to be taken as asked for would be fruitless. Even then the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue), Jessore by his order dated 29-3-2000 directed the local government pleader to file suit for setting aside the aforesaid judgment and decree. During 7(seven) years from the date of purchase of the land in question by the writ-petitioners, no step was taken on behalf of the government to get the said decree set-aside. As such, the respondent again on 16-4-2007 filed an application before the Additional Divisional Commissioner, Khulna to release the suit property from the list of vested property. On receipt of his such application, no action was taken by the Additional Divisional Commissioner. There-after, the respondent filed an application to the Member, Land Appeal Board on 24-5-2007, but he did not pass any order. The respondent also filed another application before the Chairman, Land Appeal Board on 15-8-2007 with similar prayer, but received no response. Thereafter, the respondents served a notice demanding justice through his learned advocate requesting the writ-respondents, herein appellants, to release property in question from the list of vested property, but did not get any response. In such circumstances, finding no other alternative the writ petitioners-respondents invoked the original jurisdiction of the High Court Division under Article 102 of the Constitution of the People's Republic of Bangladesh by filing writ petition and obtained Rule; that in a supplementary affidavit sworn on 26-4-2009 it was further stated that the writ petitioner-respondent also submitted an application dated 15-2-2009 before the Deputy Commissioner, Jessore praying for the release of the said property from the list of the vested property, but without any success.

4. Writ-respondent No.5, petitioner No.4 Additional Deputy Commissioner, Jessore contested the Rule by submitting affidavit-in-opposition stating, inter alia, that the writ-petitioner has the alternative forum to move the Tribunal constituted under অর্পিত সম্পত্তি প্রত্যার্পণ আিইন, ২০০১ and, as such, the writ petition was not maintainable.

5. A Division Bench of the High Court Division by its judgment and order dated 17-2-2009 made the Rule absolute and directed the respondents to release the property of the writ-petitioners from the list of vested property within one month from the date of receipt of the copy of the judgment.

6. In the above scenario, the appellants preferred Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 671 of 2010 challenging the judgment/decision dated 17-12-2009 passed by the High Court Division in Writ Petition No.6053 of 2008 making the Rule absolute. Upon hearing the learned Advocates for the contending parties, this Division, granted leave to appeal.

7. Mr Biswajit Deb Nath, learned Deputy Attorney General, appearing for the appellants has taken us through the judgment and order dated 17-12-2009 passed by the High Court Division in Writ Petition No.6053 of 2008, relevant provisions of the অর্পিত সম্পত্তি প্রত্যার্পণ আিইন, ২০০১, the materials on record and submits that the High Court Division failed to appreciate that the respondents have not acquired any right over the disputed property for releasing the same from the list of vested property. The ex-parte decree dated 15-3-1971 passed by the Court of Munsif, 3rd Court, Jessore in Title Suit No.587 of 1970 is not binding upon the appellants to release the disputed property from the list of vested property, which was enlisted in 1968. He also submits that the respondents having alternative forum to move the Tribunal constituted under the অর্পিত সম্পত্তি প্রত্যার্পণ আিইন, ২০০১ for return of the land, the writ not being maintainable the High Court Division erred in law in entertaining the same and making the Rule absolute. He again submits that serious disputed question of title relating to immovable property having been involved, the writ petition not being maintainable the High Court Division erred in law in making the Rule absolute sitting in a writ jurisdiction under Article 102 of the Constitution of the People's Republic of Bangladesh.

8. Mr Bivash Chandra Biswas, learned advocate-on-record appearing on behalf of the respondent No.1, submits that the decree passed in Title Suit No.587 of 1970 is still in existence and as the government was party in that suit in that case the applicant without setting aside the judgment and decree passed in Title Suit No.587 of 1970 cannot claim that the property is vested property. He also submits that the plaintiff has been possessing the property in question and the same has been mutated in his name in the government seresta. The writ-petitioner-respondent No.1 paid rent to the government and in that view of the matter it can be said that the government has accepted the tenancy right of the writ-petitioner by taking rent from him. He again submits that the government (writ-respondent) could not prove that the SA recorded tenant left the then East Pakistan to India and since a competent Civil Court has passed the decree of declaration of title in favour of Sujayet Ali Kha, then the appellant herein cannot claim that the suit land is vested property, and, as such, the appeal is liable to be dismissed.

9. We have considered the submissions of the learned advocates appearing on behalf of the parties concerned, perused the impugned judgment and order passed by the High Court Division and other connected papers on record. From the evidence on record it appears that the Appellate Division granted civil petition for leave to appeal to consider only two matters, which have been quoted hereunder: "I. Whether the High Court Division failed to consider that the respondents had not acquired any right over the disputed property for releasing the same from the list of vested property. II. Whether the High Court Division failed to appreciate that the ex-parte decree dated 15-3-1971 passed by the Court of Munsiff, 3rd Court, Jessore in Title Suit No.587 of 1970 is not binding upon the petitioners to release the disputed property from the list of vested property which was enlisted in 1968."

10. Now question arises regarding the rights of the respondents over the disputed property. The respondent claimed that he is a permanent citizen of Bangladesh and owner of 11 decimals of land appertaining to SA Plots No.71 and 30 decimals of land appertaining to SA Plot No.66 both under SA Khatian No.112, No.88 Bagchar Mouza, under Police Station-Kotwali, District-Jessore. The vendors of the writ-petitioner-respondent purchased the land in question from the heirs of Sujayet Ali Kha. So, according to the deposition of the respondents, the recorded owner of the disputed land was Sujayet Ali Kha, who got corrected record-of-rights in his name by virtue of judgment and decree dated 15-3-1971 passed in Title Suit No.587 of 1970.

11. Seeing the said order dated 15-3-1971 claimed by the writ petitioners-respondents to have been passed by the learned 3rd Munsif, Jessore we became suspicious and accordingly, the Registrar, Supreme Court of Bangladesh (Appellate Division) was asked to take detail information regarding the passing of aforesaid order in Title Suit No.587 of 1970. The Registrar by sending letter to the learned District Judge, Jashore asked him to let this Court know through him (Registrar) about Title Suit No.587 of 1970 and to submit a report. Accordingly, on reply the learned District Judge, Jashore sent a report to the Registrar and a copy of the same was placed before us from the office.

12. From the materials on record i.e. the report forwarded by Mr Md Ikhtiarul Islam Mallick, Senior District Judge, Jashore, it appears that no judgment or decree was passed in the month of March after 1st March, 1971. It was stated in the report that— “…অত্র রেকর্ড রুমে রক্ষিত হাইকোর্ট ফরম নং (আর)৩২(তেরিজ) দৃষ্টে দেখা যায়, যশোর ৩য় মুন্সেফী আদালতে ১৯৭১ সালের মার্চ মাসের ১ তারিখে ৩(তিন) টি দেওয়ানী মোকদ্দমা নিষ্পত্তি অস্তে মহাফেজ খানায় সংরক্ষণের জন্য রক্ষিত হইয়াছে ।

প্রকাশ থাকে যে, ১৯৭১ সালের মার্চ মাসের ১ তারিখের পরে এ মাসে আর কোন মোকদ্দমা সংশ্লিষ্ট আদালত হইতে অত্র মহাফেজা খানায় সংরক্ষণের জন্য প্রেরণ করা হয় নাই। যাহা তেরিজ দৃষ্টে প্রতীয়মান হয়। উক্ত তিনটি মোকদ্দমার বিচারক ছিলেন জনাব সুলতান আহমেদ ৷ আরো প্রকাশ থাকে যে, অত্র জজশীপের পুরাতন রেকর্ডরমে রক্ষিত সমস্ত রেকর্ড ও রেজিস্ট্রী ও অন্যান্য কাগজপত্র সমূহ নতুন বিল্ডিং হওয়ার পর পুরাতন রেকর্ড রুম হইতে নতুন বিল্ডিং এর রেকর্ড রুমে স্থানান্তর করা হইয়াছে। উক্ত তেরিজ রেজিষ্রারের সার্টিফাইভ কপি ও ফটোকপি অব্রসহিত সংযুক্ত করা হলো ।” From the record it is clear that the respondents by practicing fraud obtained the judgment and order in their favour from the High Court Division. According to Section 72 of the Evidence Act, 1872, the register of the record room of the Court is a public document and a certified copy of the register of the record room of the Judge Court, Jashore has also been produced by the appellants, which is admissible by the Court. Thus, from the certified copy of the register of the record room it appears that on the 1st March, 1971 three orders were passed in three title suits, those are Title Suits No.203 of 1970, 508 of 1970 and 143 of 1969.

13. Thereafter, no judgment was passed in the month of March. Since as per record of the িconcerned Court no judgment was passed on 15-3-1971, the respondents could not produce any certified copy of the judgment and decree dated 15-3-1971 passed in Title Suit No.587 of 1970. So, it is crystal clear that the respondents practiced fraud upon the Court.

14. Fraud vitiates everything. As the respondents practiced fraud and no judgment and decree was passed on 15-3-1971, so the said Sujayet Ali Kha did not have any right title over the disputed property as well as the respondents had not acquired any right over the disputed property. So, the question of releasing the property from the list of vested property in favour of the respondents does not arise at all as they have no right over the disputed land/ property.

15. Besides, as there is no existence of Title Suit No.587 of 1970, so the judgment and decree passed in Title Suit No.587 of 1970 dated 15-3-1971 is also non-existent in the eye of law. The question of binding effect of the judgment and decree of Title Suit No.587 of 1970 dated 15-3-1971 upon the appellants is completely fictitious. The appellants are not under any legal obligations to release the property from the list of vested property in favour of the respondents.

16. On consideration of the matters discussed above, we are of the view that the respondents obtained judgment and decree practicing fraud upon the High Court Division. If fraud is practiced upon Court for obtaining any order, then the order of the Court is liable to be set-aside. It was held in the case of Government of Bangladesh vs Mashiur Rahman, 50 DLR (AD) 205 that— "It is a cardinal principle of administration of justice that no result of any judicial proceeding should be allowed to receive judicial approval from any court of law whenever it is obtained by practicing fraud upon the court; reason being fraud demolishes the very foundation of sanctity of such judicial proceeding. It is also well established principle of law that fraud vitiates all judicial proceeding. Thus contravention of the provision of law, cannot be a valid ground for allowing an order obtained by fraud to stand. When the trial court itself on consideration of the materials on record was satisfied that a fraud had been committed in obtaining the ex-parte decree it was the duty of the trial court to set-aside the ex-parte decree."

17. In the case of Abdul Jalil vs Islami Bank Bangladesh Ltd., 64 DLR (AD) 107 the Appellate Division observed that— "It is true that fraud vitiates every-thing; even a judgment and decree affirmed by the apex Court of the country can be declared illegal and void by the trial Court if it is proved that the judgment and decree was obtained by practicing fraud upon Court. But mere allegation of fraud is not enough to entertain a suit for declaring a judgment and decree affirmed by the apex Court of country illegal. Unless strong prima facie case of fraud is made out and sufficient acceptable evidence and materials are produced before Court to substantiate the allegation of fraud a suit for declaring a judgment and decree affirmed by the apex Court of the country should not be-entertained." In this present case, it has been proved that the respondents obtained judgment and decree practicing fraud upon the High Court Division. The High Court Division made a serious error of law making the Rule absolute based on fictitious judgment and decree passed in Title Suit No.587 of 1970 dated 15-3-1971, which has no existence at all. So, we are constraint to interfere with the judgment and order passed by the High Court Division in Writ Petition No.6053 of 2008 on 17-12-2009. Accordingly, the judgment and order passed in Writ Petition No.6053 of 2008 on 17-12-2009 is set-aside.

Thus, the appeal is allowed without any order as to costs.

End.

Md Nurul Amin, Senior Advocate, instructed by Zainul Abed in, Advocate-on-Record—For the Petitioners. 
Biswajit Debnath, Advocate, instructed by Md Ali Azam, Advocate-on-Record—For the Respondent.

Joad Ali Mondal being dead his legal heirs: 1(a) ) Most. Azirun Nessa and others ---- Petitioners
vs
Arun Chandra Biswas -------- Respondent
case_source: (Prom the judgment and order dated 3-8-2017 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No.5276 of 1998)
full_judgment:
Md Nuruzzaman, J: This Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal is directed against the judgment and order dated 3-8-201.7 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No.5276 of 1998 making the Rule absolute and thereby reversing the judgment and decree dated 21-9-1998 passed by the Sub-Ordinate Judge (now Joint District Judge), Jhenaidah in Title Appeal No.41 of 1991 reversing the judgment and decree dated 17-2-1991 passed by the Assistant Judge, Shailkupa, Jhenaidah in Title Suit No.257 of 1985 dismissing the suit.

2. The relevant facts for disposal of- this Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal in short, are that the petitioner Nos.1-4 and others as plaintiffs, instituted the Title Suit No.257 of 1985 in the Court of learned Munsif, Shailkupa, Jhenaidah against the respondent for declaration that the decree of Title Suit No.400 of 1983 of the said Court was collusive, fraudulent and not binding upon them stating, inter alia, that the defendant obtained a collusive decree on 15-2-1984 in Title Suit No.400 of 1983 by suppressing process of the Court though all the defendants of the aforesaid suit were alive and, as such, the decree of the aforesaid Title Suit No.400 of 1983 was collusive and not binding upon them.

3. The defendant contested the suit by filing written statement denying the material allegations made in the plaint contending, inter alia, that the disputed land was recorded in the name of Surendra Nath and others. Debrani, mother of the defendant is the daughter of Upendra Nath, brother of Surendra Nath who inherited the property of her father. Surendra Nath and others gave settlement of their land on 15th Baishak 1358 BS to Amullay Kumar Biswas, the father of the defendant. Debrani transferred her share to the defendant by two deeds of gift. There was a dwelling house in the portion of Debrani where the defendant's father shifted. After the death of his father, the defendant has been possessing the disputed land. In the Hal record the disputed land was not recorded in the name of defendants as a result he filed the Title Suit No.772 of 1983 in the Court of Jhenaidah which was transferred to Shailkupa and renumbered as Title Suit No.400 of 1983. Summons were duly served upon all the defendants. The plaintiff No.6 of the instant case was not alive at the time of filling the suit and the plaintiff No.1 did not file the suit. The plaintiffs have no right, title and interest in the disputed land.

4. The trial Court, after hearing the parties, and considering the facts and circumstances of the case and materials evidence on record dismissed the suit by its judgment and decree dated 17-2-1991.

5. Feeling aggrieved, by the impugned judgment and decree dated 17-2-1991 passed by the trial Court, the plaintiff-appellants prefer-red Title Appeal No.41 of 1991 before the learned District Judge, Jhenaidah and on transferred the appeal was heard by the learned Sub-ordinate Judge (now Joint District Judge), Jhenaidah who allowed the appeal by the judgment and decree dated 21-9-1998.

6. Feeling aggrieved, by the judgment and decree dated 21-9-1998 passed by the Sub-ordinate Judge (now Joint District Judge), Jhenaidah, the defendant as petitioner preferred Civil Revision No.5276 of 1998 before the High Court Division and obtained the Rule.

7. In due course, a Single Bench of the High Court Division upon hearing the parties was pleased to make the Rule absolute by the impugned judgment and order dated 3-8-2017.

8. Feeling aggrieved, by the impugned judgment and order dated 3-8-2017 passed by the High Court Division the plaintiffs as petitioners filed the instant civil Petition for leave to appeal.

9. Mr Md Nurul Amin, the learned Senior Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioners submits that the trial Court as well the appellate Court found that on examination of the return of the summons of the Title Suit No.400 of 1983 it is evident that the process server affixed a copy of the summons at the outside of the door of the house of the defendants and in whose presence the copy was affixed was not mentioned in the report. But the High Court Division overlooked the mandatory provision of law and made the Rule absolute which is erred in law and, as such, the impugned judgment and order passed by the High Court Division is liable to be set-aside. He further submits that it is an obligation of the process server to mention in his report the name and address of the person by whom the house in question was identified and in whose presence the copy of summons was affixed. When the service reports were devoid of this essential information, it is unacceptable. In the instant case the process server could not mention the name and address of the person in whose presence the summons were affixed which was proved by the trial Court as well as the appellate Court. The High Court Division without following the mandatory provision of law under Order 5 Rule 17 of the Code of Civil Procedure made the Rule absolute and, as such, the impugned judgment and order passed by the High Court Division is liable to be set-aside. He also submits that in a case for challenging the ex-parte decree for non service of summons, the important issue is that whether the summons was served upon the defendant. But the trial Court as well as the High Court Division erred in law made the Rule absolute by passing the actual issue and, as such, the impugned judgment and order passed by the High Court Division is liable to be set-aside. He next submits that the mandatory provision of law that an ex-parte decree will be set-aside if it is found that there was no service of summons on the defendant. The trial Court as well as the appellate Court held that the summons was not served upon the defendant. In such a situation it is the duty of the High Court Division to set-aside the ex-parte decree and discharge the Rule, but the High Court Division erred in law by making the Rule absolute and, as such, the impugned judgment and order passed by the High Court Division is liable to be interfered by this Division for ends of justice. He finally submits that in an ex-parte decree, the Court has to observe the minimum legal requirements in passing the ex-parte judgment and decree. In the instant case the learned Munsif Judge observed that "the case is taken up for ex-parte disposal, PW 1 Arun Chandra Biswas is examined on SA case is proved, CF paid is correct. Hence, it is ordered that the suit be decreed on ex-parte against the defendants without cost. Plaintiffs' title over the suit Land be declared. And it is also declared that the RoR is erroneous and not binding upon the plaintiffs". in the ex-parte judgment, the trial Court is not uttered a single word in respect of possession and also about the documents. This does not at all satisfy the legal requirements, nor is it possible from reading the judgment that the trial Court at all applied judicial mind and, as such, the High Court Division erred in law by making the Rule absolute. Hence, the impugned judgment and order passed by the High Court Division is liable to be set-aside.

10. Mr Biswajit Debnath, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the respondent made submissions in support of the impugned judgment and order of the High Court Division. He submits that the Court of a meal below reversed the judgment of the trial Court without discussing the evidence on record both oral and documentary occasioning failure of justice and, as such, the High Court Division rightly made the Rule absolute. Hence, the instant petition may kindly be dismissed. He further submits that non service of process of the Court upon the defendants in Title Suit No.400 of 1983 was not proved by the plaintiffs by necessary and legal witnesses and, as such, the High Court Division rightly made the Rule absolute. He also submits that the trial Court after due consideration and discussion of evidence arrived at a correct decision that the plaintiffs had no right, title, interest in the suit land of Title Suit No. 400 of 1983 and therefore, they cannot challenge the decree of the said suit and on the other hand the Sub-ordinate Judge (now Joint District Judge), Jhenaidah being final Court of fact reversed the judgment of the trial Court without sifting and discussing the evidence on record and, as such, the High Court Division rightly made the Rule absolute. He finally submits that the appellate Court below misconceived the judgment of the trial Court in holding that the trial Court committed error in dismissing the suit since he found that the process of the Court were not served upon the defendants but in fact the trial Court held that though there was some irregularities in serving the summons but since the defendants had no right, title, interest and possession in the disputed land, the decree should not be set-aside. In support of his contention the learned Advocate has referred a decision as reported in 39 DLR 339 and, as such, the High Court Division rightly made the Rule absolute.

11. We have considered the submissions of the learned Advocates for the respective parties. Perused the impugned judgment of the High Court Division and other materials on record.

12. By this civil petition the plaintiffs-appellants challenges the judgment of the Single Judge of the High Court Division making the Rule absolute reversing the judgment and decree of the Court of appeal below, the suit was for simple declaration that judgment and decree passed in Title Suit No.400 of 1983 is collusive, fraudulent and not binding upon them. The trial Court dismissed the suit on the finding that—

“যাহা হোক উপরের আলোচনা থেকে এই সিদ্ধান্ত উপনীত হওয়া গেল যে, তর্কিত দেং-৪০০/৮৩ নং মোকদ্দমার সমন জারীর ক্ষেত্রে কিছু অনিয়ম দৃষ্ট হলো নালিশী জমিতে বাদীপক্ষের কোন স্বত্ব দখল না থাকায় তর্কিত ডিক্রী রদ রহিত যোগ্য লয়। কাজেই বিচার্য্য বিষয় দুটি বাদী পক্ষের প্রতিকূলে নিষ্পত্তি করা হলো । ৫/৬ নং বিচার্ধ্য বিষয়ঃ উপরোক্ত আলোচনা ও সিদ্ধান্তের আলোকে বলা যায় যে, বাদীপক্ষ তাদের প্রার্থিত প্রতিকার বা অন্য কোন প্রতিকার পেতে হকদার নন। কোর্ট ফি সঠিক । অতএব আদেশ হয় যে, অত্র মোকদ্দমাটি বিবাদীর বিরুদ্ধে দোতরফা সূত্রে খরচাসহ ডিসমিস হয়।”

13. On appeal, the Court of appeal below on consideration of evidence reversed the judgment holding that the trial Court failed to decide the real controversy of the suit which is whether service of summons of the earlier title suit was suppressed or not and, as such, the decree is collusive, fraudulent and not binding upon the plaintiffs-appellants, rather, raised the question of title, thus, committed error. The learned Single Judge without making any decision regarding the judgment of the Court of appeal below made the Rule absolute. Hence, this Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal.

14. Before adverting to the contentions raised from the respective sides it will be useful to notice the relevant provisions of law i.e. Rule 17 of Order V of the Code of Civil Procedure (briefly the Code) which contemplated the provisions servicing of summon affixing when the defendants are absent or refuses to sign the acknowledgement. The Rule 17 under Order V of the Code is hereby quoted below: "17. Where the defendant or his agent or such other person as aforesaid refuses to sign the acknowledgement, or where the serving officer, after using all due and reasonable diligence, cannot find the defendant, and there is no agent empowered to accept service of the summons on his behalf, nor any other person on whom service can be made, the serving officer shall affix a copy of the summons on the outer door or some other conspicuous part of the house in which the defendant ordinarily resides or carries on business or personally works for gain, and shall then return the original to the Court from which it was issued, with a report endorsed thereon or annexed thereto stating that he has so affixed the copy, the circumstances under which he did so, and the name and address of the person (if any) by whom the house was identified and in whose presence the copy was affixed."

15. The plaintiffs filed the suit not for declaration of title but declaration that ex-parte decree was collusive, fraudulent and not binding upon them. The trial Court took the view that the plaintiffs failed to establish their title, hence, suit was dismissed. The same view took the learned Single Judge of the High Court Division but Court of appeal below took the different view asserting that the real dispute in the suit is whether summons of the suit was served according to taw and ex-parte judgment is collusive and fraudulent.

16. We now turn to the vital contentions whether in a suit for declaration to set-aside the ex-parte decree Court can consider the servicing of summons or title of the plaintiffs as opined by the High Court Division.

17. It is the cardinal maxim of the law that in a judgment the Court must decide the real controversy between the parties framing issues. The learned Assistant Judge framed the following issues those are reproduced herein below. ১। মোকদ্দমাটি বর্তমান আকারে প্রকারে চলতে পারে কিনা? ২। মোকদ্দমাটি তামাদি বারিত কিনা? ৩। দেং ৪০০/৮৩ নং মোকদ্দমায় প্রদত্ত ডিক্রী রদ রহিত যোগ্য কিনা? ৪। নালিশী জমিতে বাদীপক্ষে স্বত্ব দখল আছে কিনা? ৫। বাদী প্রার্থীত প্রতিকার পেতে পারেন কিনা? ৬। বাদী আর কি প্রতিকার পেতে পারেন?

18. It appears from the judgment that the learned Assistant Judge discussed the issue Nos.3 and 4 analogously and did not opine about the issue No.3 independently. The issue No.3 is the essential issuein the suit, issue No.4 is not the proper issue in the suit. The learned Single Judge of the High Court Division failed to appreciate the above failure of the Judge of the trial Court, not only so, rather, concurred with the findings and discussion of the trial Court on the issues, although the Court of appeal below clearly found that the discussion of the trial Court was erroneous, thus the Court of appeal below after proper appreciation of the materials on issues, thus, appeal was allowed. The learned Single Judge of the High Court Division without rebutting finding of the Court of appeal below reversed the judgment which is not only improper, rather, erroneous, thus committed serious error in law, occasioning failure of justice.

19. In a suit for cancellation of ex-parte decree essential element is whether there was fraudulent suppression of summons. Now, the question is who will prove the service of summons in the present suit. It is found from the averment of the suit and the testimony of PW No.1, who has categorically denied the service of summons of the suit upon him and told that summons were suppressed by the plaintiffs of the earlier suit with the connivance of the process server of the Court. Upon such allegation of the PW 1 in his testimonies which are prima facie proving the case in his favour, then it is incumbent upon the defendant to prove the service of summons of the earlier suit by adducing proper witness. Because burden of proof has been shifted upon the defendant to prove that summons were duly served upon the defendant of earlier suit as per provisions of section 103 of the Evidence Act which is quoted herein below for the benefit of the discussions; "103. Burden of proof as to particular fact—The burden of proof as to any particular fact lies on that person who wishes the Court to believe in its existence, unless it is provided by any law that the proof of that fact shall lie on any particular person."

20. The learned Assistant Judge himself opined in the judgment that there are same anomalies on serving the summons. In view of such opinion the ex-parte judgment cannot be sustained in law. The proper service of summons is a pre-requisite of sustainability of an ex-parte decree. It has held by this Division in the case of Abdur Rashed vs Abdul Barik reported in 35 DLR (AD) 162— "An ex-parte decree will be set-aside if it is found that there was no service of summons on the defendant."

21. In a suit for setting aside the ex-parte decree, in a case of service by hanging because of alleged refusal by the plaintiff appellant to receive notices, where the names and addresses of the mukabila witnesses were not noted in the service reports by the process server, it is the settled principles of law from the long line of catena, obviously process server most examine by the Court, but in the instant case the process server was not adduced to examine by the Court, even then, the trial Court found from record that there are some anomalies in the serving of the summons, such facts would lead to disbelieve the service which is devoid of the essential information as requires by law. But the learned Single Judge of the High Court Division failed to appreciate the above legal proposition. Thus, committed serious error of law point occasioning failure of justice. It is the cardinal principles of law that in a suit for setting aside the ex-parte decree determination of title is not the essential ingredient as decided by the learned Single Judge in the instant revisional case, thus acted beyond the revisional jurisdiction in making the Rule absolute setting aside well founded judgment of the Court of appeal below. Thus, committed error of law occasioning failure of justice. However, we are of the opinion that, if we grant leave to appeal then the litigation will prolong for the uncertain period, hence, we are inclined to dispose of the petition for early disposal of the suit.

22. In view of the above discussion, we find merit in this petition. Accordingly, this petition is disposed of. The judgment of the High Court Division is hereby set-aside. The trial Court is hereby directed to conclude the trial as early as possible preferably within 1(one) year from the date of receipt of this judgment positively.

End.

case_source: (From the judgment and order dated the 24th day of November, 2009 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No.3505 of 2007)
full_judgment:
Abu Bakar Siddiquee, J: This civil appeal, by leave, is directed against the judgment and order dated the 24th day of November, 2009 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No.3505 of 2007 discharging the Rule and affirming the judgment and decree dated 17-7-2007 passed by the Joint District Judge, Brahmanbaria in Other Appeal No.53 of 2006 allowing the appeal and reversing those dated 10-5-2006 in Other Suit No.71 of 2005 of trial Court. 2. The facts relevant to dispose of the appeal, in short, are that respondent No. 1-9 as the plaintiffs instituted Other SuitNo.71 of 2005 in the Court of Senior Assistant Judge, Brahmanbaria for declaration of title and for recovery of khas possession. The case of the plaintiffs was that CS Khatian No.114 in respect of the disputed land was prepared in the name of their predecessor-in-interest. CS recorded 'Ka' group tenants, Zalfur Uddin, Patchu, father of Kala Miah and Kalfur Uddin, father of Lai Mahmud, were full brothers. Zalfur Uddin died issueless leaving two full brothers: Patchu and Kalfur Uddin as his heirs and accordingly, they inherited the share of Zalfur Uddin in the suit plots. Subsequently, Patchu died leaving behind his son, Kala Miah and Kalfur Uddin died leaving behind his son, Lai Mahmud. The CS recorded tenants. Bashu .Miah died leaving behind plaintiff No.9 as his heir and Seraj Ali died leaving behind his three sons: plaintiff Nos.6 and 7 and Sultan Meah, father of plaintiff No.8. Kala Miah died leaving behind his two sons and two daughters: plaintiff Nos.4, 5, 10 and 11. Lal Mahmud died leaving behind his son named Abdul Khaleque. Thereafter, Abdul Khaleque died leaving behind his three sons and three daughters: plaintiff Nos. 1-3 and 12-14. Thus, the plaintiffs became the owners of the suit land and some other lands. The suit land was correctly recorded in the names of the plaintiffs and in the name of their predecessor-in-interest during the SA operation. The plaintiffs had been possessing the suit land for a long time through their bargader, defendant No. l. Since the plaintiffs had to stay outside the area in connection with their business, defendant No.1 was entrusted to get the suit land recorded in their names during Bangladesh Survey. The plaintiffs recently came to know that defendant No.1 had been planning to construct houses on the suit land by filling it up with earth. Thereafter, the plaintiffs made a search of their khatian in the survey office and found that defendant No.1 had got DP Khatian No. 1107 in respect of the suit land along with some other lands recorded in his name. The plaintiffs asked defendant No.1 on 28-1-2005 to quit the possession of the suit land, but defendant No.1 refused to do so and instead, he claimed his title over the same. Thus, a cloud was created on the title of the plaintiffs in the suit land hence, they filed the suit for the relief as aforementioned.

3. Defendant No.1 contested the suit by filing written statement contending, inter alia, that he was never a bargader in the suit land under the plaintiffs. He took settlement of some portion of the suit land from one Abdul Malek Haji and that he had been possessing the same. One Jogendra Mohan Chowdhury being the owner had been possessing 121/2 decimals land in Suit Plot Nos.434, 435 and 436 by way of purchase from the CS recorded tenants and sold the same to Kashem Ali and Sadir Meah by a registered kabala being No.7791 dated 6-10-1984. Besides Abdul Khaleque, the plaintiffs' father sold 2½ decimals land from Plot No.434 by registered deed No.37094 dated 3-4-1961. Sadir Meah sold 6¼ decimals land from the suit plots to Tuku Meah, Abu Bakar, Bazlu Meah and delivered possession thereof to them. SA Khatian No.112 was prepared in the names of Tuku Meah and other sons of Kala Meah. Tuku Meah, Abu Bakar, Nurul Huq and Bazlu Meah by a registered exchange deed bearing No.6973 dated 28-10-1958 exchanged 6¼ decimals land of the suit plots with Kashem Ali and delivered possession and thus, they became disinterested in the suit plots. Kashem Ali became owner of the entire suit land and he being in possession thereof sold the same to Zaher Meah by a registered deed being No.224 executed on 9-1-1977 and registered on 18-1-1977 and delivered possession of the transferred land to him. Zaher Meah exchanged the suit land with defendant No.1 by a registered exchange deed dated 13-6-1988. In this way, defendant No.1 became the owner of the suit land and had been possessing the same by growing crops thereon and by paying rents regularly to the Government. The plaintiffs having no right, title and possession in the suit land were not entitled to get any relief in the suit and the same was liable to be dismissed.

4. The suit was dismissed by the learned Senior Assistant Judge by his judgment and decree dated 10-5-2006.

5. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the judgment and decree of the learned Senior Assistant Judge, the plaintiffs filed Title Appeal No.53 of 2006 before the District Judge, Brahmanbaria. The learned Joint District Judge, 1st Court, Brahmanbaria after hearing the appeal allowed the same by his judgment and decree dated 17-7-2007 and set-aside the judgment and decree of the trial Court and decreed the suit.

6. Against the judgment and decree of the Appellate Court, the defendants field above-mentioned civil revision before the High Court Division. A Division Bench heard the same and by the impugned judgment and order discharged the Rule and thereby affirmed the judgment and decree passed by the Appellate Court below.

7. Against the said judgment and order of the High Court Division, the defendant filed Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 1623 of 2012 and leave was granted to consider the following submissions of the learned Advocate for the appellants: "I. Because the High Court Division failed to notice that the Appellate Court being the last Court of facts having not determined the issue of Borga cultivation by the defendants with reference to the evidence on record committed error of law in decreeing the suit. II. Because the High Court Division fell in error in not holding that the finding of the trial Court on question of Borga cultivation and possession having not been reversed by the Appellate .Court considering the relevant evidence, the decree of the Appellate Court is not sustainable in law. III. Because the High Court Division proceeded upon the wrong assumption as to the original owner inasmuch as the documentary evidence of title of the predecessors of the defendant as well as the defendants are available on record to prove the title and the possession of the defendants."

8. Mr Abdul Quayum, learned Counsel, appearing on behalf of the appellants, submits that the Appellate Court below being the last Court of fact failed to appreciate that the appellant is the purchaser of the land from the true owner of the suit land and they are not the Borgadar under the present respondent whereas the trial Court rightly held the aforesaid fact and dismissed the suit. He further adds that the positive findings of the trial Court were not adverted by the Appellate Court below who wrongly held that the appellants are liable to be evicted from the suit land although DP Khatian has been prepared in the name of the defendant-appellants on the basis of their title and possession for more than 12 years and, as such, the defendants acquired statutory right by way of adverse possession. He further adds that the revisional Court also failed to appreciate the aforesaid fact of right, title and possession of the defendant- appellants and wrongly supported the Appellate Court below which are the product of mere non-consideration, misreading and non-appreciation of the evidence on record.

9. On the other hand, Dr. Kazi Aktar Hamid, learned Advocate, appearing on behalf of the plaintiff-respondents, submits that the plaintiffs have been able to prove their genealogy through which they have acquired right, title and interest in the suit land by way of inheritance and the contesting defendant is their Borgardar who had no right, title and interest in the suit land.

10. He further adds that the trial Court failed to appreciate the evidentiary value of CS and SA Khatian which created an unrebuttable presumption in favour of the plaintiff and also that Jogendra Mohan Chowdhury had no saleable interest in the suit land and the defendants have failed to prove the very basis of preparation of the DP Khatian. He further adds that the DP Khatian and the rent receipt conferred no title.

11. We have heard the learned Advocates for both the parties and perused the materials on the record.

12. It is admitted by the parties that CS Khatian No.114 in respect of the disputed land was prepared in the name of plaintiffs predecessor-in-interest. CS recorded "Ka" group tenants Zalfur Uddin, Patchu, father of Kala Miah and Kalfur Uddin, father of Lai Mahmud were full brothers and that Zalfur Uddin died issueless leaving two full brothers, Patchu and Kalfur Uddin as his heirs and accordingly, they inherited the share of Zalfur Uddin in the suit plots. It is not denied that subsequently, Patchu died leaving behind his son, Kala Miah and that Kalfur Uddin died leaving behind his son, Lai Mahmud. It is also undisputed that the other CS recorded tenants, Bashu Miah died leaving behind plaintiff No.9 and Seraj Ali died leaving behind of plaintiff Nos.6 and 7 and Sultan, father of plaintiff No.8 and Kala Miah died leaving behind his two sons and two daughters, plaintiff Nos.4, 5, 10 and 11 and that Lai Mahmud died leaving behind his son, Abdul Khaleque. It is also not denied that Abdul Khaleque died leaving behind his three sons and three daughters: plaintiff Nos. 1-3 and 12-14 and in this way, the plaintiffs claimed to have acquired the suit land and some other lands. It appears that the suit land was recorded in the names of the plaintiffs and in the name of their predecessor-in-interest during the SA operation. The plaintiffs also claimed that they had been possessing the suit land for a long time through their bragader, defendant No. l. It is also contended that since the plaintiffs had to stay outside the area in connection with their business, defendant No. 1 was entrusted to get the suit land recorded in their names during Bangladesh Survey and that the plaintiffs recently came to know that defendant No. l had been planning to construct house on the suit land by filling it up with earth.

13. The plaintiffs (respondents) have come with an allegation that they made a search of their khatian in the survey office and found that defendant No. 1 got his name recorded in DP Khatian No.l 107 in respect of the suit land along with some other lands. The plaintiffs asked defendant No.1 on 28-1-2005 to vacate the possession of the suit land, but defendant No.1 on the event of refusal to do so and instead of vacating, he claimed his title over the same.

14. On the other hand, the present appellants (defendants) filed RoR Khatian No.1 12 (Exhibit-Gha') from which it is seen that the name of Bazlu Mia, Nurubaksha, Tuku Mia and Abu Bakar son of Kala Gazi are the recorded tenants who are the successive heirs of CS tenant Bashu. The present, plaintiffs filed an exchange deed being No.6973 dated 28-10-1956 (Exhibit-Gail) from which it revealed that the aforesaid successive heirs of Bashu (who appears to be RS tenant) exchanged the suit property with one Kashem Ali and the suit property has fallen in the share of the second party, Kashem Ali through this exchange deed. The appellants (defendants) has filed another kabala dated 9-1-1977 executed by Kashem Ali (Exhibit-Ga) from which it appears that the suit property has been sold by Kashem Ali in favour of Zaher Mia (DW 3). Thereafter, the present appellants (defendants) filed another deed of exchange dated 13-6-1988 (Exhibit-Kha) from which it is seen that aforementioned Zaher Mia exchanged the suit property with Shahidul Haque who is the present defendant. On perusal of those registered deeds, it appears that the successive heirs of Bashu transferred their share in favour of the present defendants. It is admitted by the respondents (plaintiffs) that they have been possessing the suit land through their borgadar, defendant No. 1 which has been denied by defendant No. 1. But the said defendant claimed that he has been possessing the suit land for more than 17/18 years and thereby he has acquired a statutory right by way of adverse possession.

15. Plaintiff Nos.2, 3, 12 and 13 filed an application on 18-4-1985 and disowned their interest in the property. In support thereof, DW 2, namely, Nazma Begum (plaintiff No. 12) disowned her signature in the plaint and also admitted that the land belongs to defendant No.1 who is in possession over the suit land and in this circumstance, the suit became incompetent and no step has been taken against such statement. DW 2 is the full sister of plaintiff Nos. 1-3 and plaintiff Nos. 13-14. She is also distant relation of defendant No. l. Aforesaid Nazma Bagum while deposing as DW 2 clearly stated that other plaintiffs impleaded them as plaintiffs in this case in a fraudulent manner and she identified her signature on the petition dated 18-4-2005 and also deposed that she disowned her interest in the property in favour of the defendant who has been possessing the land in dispute for more than 17/18 years. Apart from this witness, the executant of deed of exchange dated 19-6-1988, Zaher Mia has been examined as DW 3 in this case who deposed that he exchanged the suit land with defendant No.1 and he (defendant No.1) has been possessing the same for about 16 years. DW 4, Hazi Abdul Malak, is a man of 69 years of age who deposed that me suit land belongs to Shaid Mia (defendant No.1) who has been possessing the suit land for more than 16/17 years. DW 5, Khurshed Alam, also corroborated the aforesaid DWs. On perusal of those evidence on record, we find that nothing cogent could be elicited to disbelieve those DWs. The trial Court discussed those evidence elaborately, but the Appellate Court without adverting the aforesaid evidence reversed the judgment of the learned Judge of the trial Court which is nothing, but a product of misreading and non-consideration of the evidence on record. The revisional Court also failed to appreciate the decision taken by the trial Court.

16. The trial Court observed that the respondents (plaintiffs) failed to proof their date of dispossession by adducing corrobo-rative evidence since PW 2, Nuruzzaman and PW3, Abul Kasham never uttered any fact of such dispossession. Thus, we have no other alternative but to hold that there is no corroborative evidence as to the fact of alleged dispossession. Rather they deposed that defendant No.1 has been possessing the suit land as borgadar of the plaintiff which goes to show the possession of the defendant. The Appellate Court has lost sight to the effect that the tact of possession and dispossession remained not proved. Whereas the plaintiff has sought for recovery of khan possession the learned Judge of the High Court Division also failed to appreciate such aspect and thereby committed illegality.

17. Defendant No.1 while deposing as DW 1 stated that certain portion of the suit land belonged to one Jogendra Mohan Chowdhury who granted settlement of such land to one Haji Khaleque and he transferred the said land to One Kashem Ali in the benami of Tawkin Mia and Shadek Mia who exchanged the same in favour of Zaher Ali and he subsequently exchanged such land with him (defendant No. 1). Aforesaid Zaher Mia while deposing as DW3 slated that he transferred the land in favour defendant No.1, but he could not say as to which land he has transferred. The learned Judge of the trial Court held that the defendant filed a RoR porcha. But there is no record which Jogendra Mohan Chowdhury was CS recorded tenant. The RoR is not a document of title. The Appellate Court observed that the name of Jogendra Mohan Chowdhury does not appear as the recorded tenant either in CS Khatian No.114 or kabala dated 6-10-1984. If Jogendra Mohan Chowdhury's title and possession in the suit land remained unproved, the purchaser (defendant) has acquired no title and possession. This observation made by the Appellate Court below has been approved by the revisional Court. We also find that Jogandra Mohan Chowdhury was not CS record tenant. The appellant (defendant) thus acquired no right and title in respect of such portion of land. Excepting such portion of land which defendant No.1 claimed to have been acquired from Jogendra Mohan, the appellant acquired other portion of the suit land as has been discussed by us earlier. In that case, we are of the view that the present appellant and respondent appears to be co-sharers in the suit jams and in that case, the respondent may be allowed to remain in joint possession with defendant No. 1.

18. However, the civil appeal may be allowed in part.

19. The judgment and decree passed by the learned Judge of the High Court Division as well as the Joint District Judge in Other Class Appeal No.53 of 2006 is hereby partly set-aside and thereby the judgment and decree passed by the learned Senior Assistant Judge in Title Suit No.71 of 2005 is hereby partly upheld in light of the observation made by this Court.

Thus, the civil appeal is allowed in part without any order as to cost.

End.
