5. The petitioners in the above mentioned writ petitions have taken various grounds on merit assailing the impugned orders, judgments and decrees concerned. Some of them even referred to various evidences which have been considered, or allegedly not considered, by the concerned Tribunals.

 

6. In the course of hearing, learned advocates appearing for the parties have referred to a judgment (not yet released) delivered by a Division Bench of this Court comprising his Lordships Mr Justice Moyeenul Islam Chowdhury and Mr Justice Md Ashraful Kamal in Suo Motu Rule No. 3 of 2015. According to them, the said Suo Motu Rule, as issued by the said bench seeking a mandamus on the government to establish Land Survey Appellate Tribunals, has been made absolute vide judgment and order dated 25-7-2019 with a direction upon the government to establish such Appellate Tribunals within a period of 90(ninety) days from receipt of the copy of the said judgment.

 

7. Learned advocates in the instant writ petitions have argued, at length, various issues regarding the evidences on record and tried to make reference to different evidences from the lower Court records of the cases concerned, as have already been sent to this Court. However, this Court is of the view that disposing of such issues by this Court under writ jurisdiction will encompass re-examination and re-assessment of evidences, as adduced by the parties before the Tribunals, which is not permitted under writ jurisdiction.

 

8. As against this aspect, we have examined the relevant provisions of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950, in particular Chapter-XVIIA of the same as inserted vide section 2 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy (Amendment) Act, 2004 (Act No. 09 of 2004). For the purpose of the revision of the record-of-rights in respect of the Lands in Bangladesh, as provided by section 144 of the said Act, the government has in the meantime promulgated Tenancy Rules, 1955 specifying the stages of works to be conducted by the concerned Revenue officials and Land Field Officers. In such exercise of different functions at different stages, when a draft record of right is published under Rule 29 of the said Tenancy Rules by the concerned Revenue Officer, the aggrieved person has the right to file objection against the same under Rule 30 of the said Rules. After disposal of such objection upon hearing the parties, the aggrieved person will have the right to prefer appeal under Rule 31 of the said Rules to the Revenue Officer appointed with the additional designation of Settlement Officer or additional designation of Assistant Settlement Officer. Once such appeals are disposed of, the final record-of-rights in respect of the concerned land are prepared, if such orders of the Appellate Authority are not interfered with in the meantime on some limited grounds including fraud under Rules 42 and 42A of the said Rules. The matter does not end there, even after final publication of record-of-rights, the aggrieved party has been given an opportunity to challenge any entry in the said final record-of-rights by filing a suit before the Land Survey Tribunals concerned as established by the government in exercise of its power under section 145A of the said Act specifying the territorial limits and jurisdiction of such Tribunals. Such Tribunals have been empowered by the said provision only to entertain suits challenging the entry in the finally published record-of-rights as stated above. Such Tribunals have also been empowered by the said provision to declare the concerned record-of-rights to be incorrect and further to direct the concerned office to correct such record-of-rights in accordance with its decision and may also pass such other orders as may be necessary.

 

9. Obviously, because of such scheme as provided by the parliament through the aforesaid insertion of the Chapter XVIIA in the said Act and the Rules made there-under, thousands of citizens and persons approached such Tribunals with numerous suits challenging the entries in the finally published record-of-rights. Consequently, such Tribunals comprising of Joint District Judges have been flooded with various number of cases. Since the Tribunals have been given the powers to dispose of such cases in accordance with the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, so far as the same is not inconsistent with the provisions of the said Act, in respect of certain matters mentioned tinder section 145B of the said Act, thereby making the Tribunal a quasi-civil court having limited powers of the Civil Court, the same have disposed of, or are in the process of disposing of, the said numerous number of suits. In such process, the litigants before the Tribunals have every reason to become aggrieved either against any order passed by the Tribunals in interlocutory matters or against judgment and decrees passed by them after conclusion of hearing. In such circumstances, it appears, the said huge number of litigant persons found themselves in a very helpless position to challenge or assail such orders, judgments and decrees passed by the said Tribunals in view of the admitted position that the government has not yet established any Land Survey Appellate Tribunal for giving redresses to the said aggrieved litigants in appeals to be filed by them against the said orders, judgment and decrees.

 

10. It may be mentioned here that in accordance with the provisions under sub-section (4) of section 145B of the said Act, judgments, decrees or orders passed by the said Land Survey Tribunals are appealable and, as such, it was necessary and incumbent on the part of the government to establish such required number of Land Survey Appellate Tribunals in exercise of its power under section 145B immediately after the establishment of the Land Survey Tribunals concerned. Given that even the orders passed by the Land Tribunal Tribunals are appealable orders, the government was not in a position to wait for any further time to establish such Appellate Tribunals in view of the probability that even on the very day of filing of a suit before the Tribunal, a litigant may become aggrieved by any order passed by the Tribunal.

 

11. In the Course of hearing, Md Dider Alam (Kollol), learned advocate in Writ petition No. 5434 of 2017, has drawn this Court's attention to a gazette notification published by the government on 5-11-2012. The said gazette is quoted below:— "এস আর ও নং ৩৭১-আইন/২০১২।—State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 (Act No. XXVII of 1951) এর section 145B এর sub-section (1) এবং (2) এ প্রদত্ত ক্ষমতাবলে সরকার এতদ্বারা ল্যান্ড সার্ভে আপীল ট্রাইব্যুনাল, ঢাকা প্রতিষ্ঠা করিল এবং ইহার স্থানীয় অধিক্ষেত্র হইবে সমগ্র বাংলাদেশ”।

 

12. It appears from the above quoted gazette that by this gazette, the government has established. Land Survey Appellate Tribunal, Dhaka giving it entire territorial jurisdiction of Bangladesh. There is nothing in that gazette as to who would be the judges of the said Appellate Tribunal or as to where the said Tribunal shall have its seat. Learned Deputy Attorney-General, present in Court, also has not given us any information as regards any other further steps as taken by the government pursuant the said gazette.

 

13. Nevertheless, even after publication of the said gazette, this Court issued the said Suo Motu Rule on 3-3-2015, being Suo Muto Rule No. 3 of 2015, and, according to the information given by the learned advocate concerned, the said Rule has been made absolute on 25-7-2019 with the direction upon the government to establish as many Land Survey Appellate Tribunals as may be required to hear appeals arising out of judgments, decrees or orders of the Land Survey Tribunals in Bangladesh. There is nothing on record as well as in the submissions of the learned Deputy Attorney-General that the government has taken any steps as of today for establishing such Appellate Tribunals which may function properly. Therefore, huge number of litigants, who are aggrieved by different orders, judgments and decrees passed by the Land Survey Tribunals, are now moving from one bench to another bench of the High Court Division with writ petitions to get redress. However, as stated above, in order to give such redress, we are required to reassess or reexamine the evidences adduced by the parties before the Tribunals concerned, which is not possible under writ jurisdiction. Though the statute, in particular section 145B of the said Act, provides that the government 'may' establish Land Survey Appellate Tribunals to hear the appeals arising out of the judgment and decree or order of the Land Survey Tribunals, with the establishment of Land Survey Tribunals in the meantime, this Court is of the view that, this 'may' as used in the said provision must be read as 'shall'. Otherwise, the entire purpose of the provisions under Chapter XVIIA of the said Act will become useless.

 

14. In view of above, we have no option but to express our frustration because of the failure of the government in establishing required number of Land Survey Appellate Tribunals and appointing judges therein. This being so, we find partial merit in the Rules, in so far as seeking direction on the government for establishment of such Tribunals is concerned, and, accordingly, said part of the Rules should be made absolute.

 

15. In the result, the Rules are made absolute in part. The respondent-government, in particular the concerned Ministries, are directed to establish as many number of Appellate Tribunals, appoint judges in those Tribunals and determine the seats of such Tribunals through such appointment by publishing gazette under section 145B of the said Act within a period of 90(ninety) days from receipt of the copy of this judgment. At the same time, since we are not in a position to determine the merit of the cases before us, which may only be determined by the Appellate Tribunals to be established by the government, the parties will be at liberty to address those issues before the Appellate Tribunals to be constituted by the government by preferring appeals before it. Thus, till the establishment of such Land Survey Appellate Tribunals and filing of such appeals by the litigants concerned, the parties should maintain status-quo in respect of the position and possession of the lands in question. Accordingly, operation of the impugned judgments, decrees and orders shall remain stayed till such filing of appeals. Parties are directed to maintain status-quo in respect of the position and possession of the land in question till filing of such Appeals by them before the Land Survey Appellate Tribunals to be established by the government. In preferring such appeals, delay occurred in the meantime shall be condoned.

 

16. Let the Lower Courts' Records, which have already been sent and tagged with the concerned writ petitions, be sent down to the concerned Tribunals.

 

Communicate this.

 

End.

full_judgment:
AKM Abdul Hakim J : This Rule was issued calling upon the opposite party No. 1 to show case as to why the Order dated 4-11-2019 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, Second Court, Dhaka in Title Suit No. 514 of 2019 rejecting the application filed by the defendant-petitioners on 26-8-2019 under Order III, rule 1 read with section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure for direction upon the plaintiff to appear in person in court for cross-examination by the defendants on that points as specified in the application and the another Order passed on the same date (4-11-2019) rejecting the application filed by the defendant-petitioners under Order VII, rule 11 read with section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure should not be set-aside and or to pass such other further order/orders as this court may seem fit and proper. 

2. The present Title Suit No. 56 of 2013 was filed by the opposite party No. 1 as plaintiff on 27-5-2013 in the First Court of Joint District Judge, Narsingdi impleading the petitioner Nos. 1 and 2 and opposite party No. 2 as defendant Nos. 1, 2 and 3 for declaration of title in respect of suit schedule `Ka' and further declaration that Saf Kabala Deed described in schedule 'Kha' and Bainapatra Deed described in schedule 'Ca' are void, illegal, fraudulent, collusive and not binding upon the plaintiff. 

3. The plaintiff's case, in short, are that mother of the plaintiff, Amena Khanam acquired the suit land through 2 registered kabalas being Nos. 5975 dated 13-7-1961 area 0.3125 acre and 8501 dated 24-9-1987 area 04.50; that thereafter she made an oral gift infavour of her son, the plaintiff on 2-12-2011 measuring an area of 07.625 decimal land in presence of plaintiff's full brothers Khan Gaffar Mohammad, KGM Zahid Hossain and Khan Gaffar Mohammad, Ashraf Mahmud and delivered possession thereof to him before executing unregistered Bonton Nama dated 04-12-2001; that subsequently, in order to avoid any further complications amongst her other sons and daughters, the plaintiff's mother declared heba by a registered a deed being No. 27610 on 14-12-2012 in respect of 04.50 decimal of land out of total area of 0.24 acre from CS and SA plot No. 22, RS plot No. 90 and 03.125 acre land out total 0.36 acre of land of RS plot No. 90/176 i.e. in total 07.625 acre of land from the said two plots and delivered possession, since then the plaintiff has been possessing the said area of land by virtue the said gift. In the plaint it is further stated that his full brother, defendant No. 3 Mahbubur Rahman Khan did not get any land from the suit land which was described in schedule 'Ka' to the plaint in the 'ghoroa aposh bontonnama' dated 4-12-2001; that on 17-12-2012 the plaintiff through his younger brother, Zahid Hossain came to learn that defendant No. 3 appointed defendant No. 2 as his attorney on 12-12-2012 in respect of the 'ka' schedule land, then the plaintiff through his said brother made a search by vender in the Sub-Registrar's Office, Narsingdi and after obtaining the certified copy on 19-12-2012 confirmed that defendant No. 3 appointed defendant No. 2 as his constituted attorney by a registered power of attorney No. 27492 dated 12-12-2012 and the said power of attorney was executed and registered on commission; that thereafter, the plaintiff through his younger brother Zahid Hossain came to know on 18-12-2012 that defendant No. 1 entered into registered Bainanama with defendant No. 3 dated 12-12-2012, then the plaintiff through his younger brother obtained certified copy on 10-1-2013 and confirmed about the registered bainapotro No. 27493 dated 12-12-2012 executed by defendant No. 3 in favour of defendant No. 1; that thereafter through his said brother, the plaintiff came to know on 12-1-2013 that defendant. No. 2 as constituted Attorney of Defendant No. 3 executed and registered Saf-kabala in favour of defendant No. 1; that plaintiff through his younger brother obtained the certified copy of the kabala on 16-1-2013 and confirmed that defendant No. 2 executed and registered a Saf-kabala Deed No 28315 on 23-12-2013; that it apparent from the bainapotro dated 12-12-2012 and Saf-Kabala deed dated 23-12-2012 that defendant Nos. 1, 2 and 3 in collusion with each other fraudulently created the power of attorney and bainapotro on 12-12-2012 and saf-kabala dated 23-12-2012; that defendant No. 3 revoked the power of attorney No. 27492 dated 12-12-2012 executed in favour of Defendant No. 2 by a Deed of Revocation being deed No. 29015 dated 31-12-2012; that Defendant No. 1 on the basis of Family Settlement Deed dated 4-12-2011, a Deed of partition was executed on 21-1-2013 and registered by Deed No. 1508 dated 22-1-2013 between the plaintiff and his brothers Md Mozibur Rahman Khan, Md Mahbubur Rahman Khan (defendant No. 3), Md Badrul Hossain Khan, KGM Ashraf Mahud, KKM Mohammad, Zahid and 4(four) sisters, namely, Rahima Khanam, Fahmida Khanam, Mahfuza Khanam. As per said partition deed plaintiff got 0.11 acre of land including 0.5 acre land of said schedule 'ka'; that elder brother, Mojibur Rahman Khan got 0.6 acre, younger brother Md Zahid Hossain got 0.03 acre in suit plot, in total 0.20 acre, 0.0288 acre was remained as ejmali for Graveyard and road. Defendant No. 3 did not get any property from suit plot; that defendant No. 1 by dint of kabala dated 23-12-2012 did not get possession of suit 'ka' scheduled land and the plaintiff is in possession thereof; that when defendant No. 1 in collaboration with his uncle Dr. Rafiqul Islam Khan and other terrorists of the locality attempted to take forcible possession of the 'ka' schedule land, plaintiff through his Assistant Bench officer, Md Asaduzzaman lodged a GD entry being number 453 dated 8-2-2013 with the Narsingdi Model Police Station and then on the direction of the Officer-in-charge of the Police Station, Sub-Inspector Moqsed Mollah issued a notice on 08-2-2013 asking both the parties to maintain status quo. The plaintiff further, asserted that defendant No. 3 did not get any share in the suit property by virtue of the 'ghoroa bontonnama' dated 4-12-2011 which was acknowledged in the registered bontonnama dated 21-1-2013. Since defendant No. 3 had no right, title, interest and possession in the 'ka' schedule and after 4-12-2011 executing the power of attorney appointing defendant No. 2 on 12-12-2012 authorising her to sell the 'ka' schedule land and the bainapotro in favour of defendant No. 1 and subsequently to execute and register the kabala dated 23-12-2012 was without jurisdiction; that since the activities of defendant No. 3 as stated herein before, created a cloud to the plaintiff's title in the 'ka' scheduled land, he was constrained to file the suit for declaration of title in 'ka' schedule and further declaration that the deeds as described in schedule 'kha' and 'ga' as illegal, void, fraudulent, collusive and not binding upon the plaintiff. 

4. The defendant Nos. 1 and 2, petitioners herein contested the suit by filing written statement denying the material allegations of the plaint and contended, inter-alia, that specially the 'ghoroa bontonnama' amongst the plaintiff and his six brothers on 4-12-2011 (wrongly written as 6-12-2011) in the written statement amongst others. The defendant further alleged that in order to file the suit the plaintiff in collusion with each other created bontonnama in an antedated stamp paper Taka 150 leaving aside the other co-sharers; that the plaintiff's brother Md Mahbubur Rahman Khan (defendant No. 3) being the rightful owner of the suit 'ka' schedule land executed a registered bainapotro on 12-12-2012 on commission and on the same date also executed a registered power of attorney in favour of defendant No. 2 being deed No. 27492 in which plaintiff's full brother Md Badrul Hasan Khan has figured as a witness; that subsequently, the defendant No. 2 executed a registered Sub-kabala deed being number 28315 dated 24-12-2012 and delivered possession of suit land to him. In order to make the defendant No. l's deed ineffective, registered bontonnama Deed No. 1508 dated 22-1-2013 was created and the same was nothing but a collusive deed created with malafide motive; that Defendant No. 3 being the full brother of the plaintiff on his ill-advice cancelled the power of attorney on 30-12-2012 executed in favour of defendant No. 2 knowing fully well about the execution and registration of the kabala; that the plaintiff's mother, Amena Khanam had no legal authority to transfer 07.625 acres of land in favour of the plaintiff on 14-12-2012 from CS plot No. 22, RS plot No. 90 and 90/176, as she was owner of only 0.037 acres of land in CS plot No. 22, so the plaintiff did not acquire any title to the suit land by virtue of the said heba made in his favour; that the plaintiff has got no possession in the suit land and it is defendant No. 1, who is in possession thereof; that Md Mahbubur Rahman Khan is the full brother of the plaintiff and he acquired title over the suit land by inheritance as well as by purchase from one Badrunnesa by kabala dated 11-3-1989 and from heirs of Abdul Kadir Khan by two kabala's dated 16-10-1991 and 26.4-1989, so he had every right to transfer the suit land in favour of the defendant No. 1 and, as such, the suit is liable to be dismissed. 

5. That when the Title Suit No. 56 of 2013 was pending in the First Court of Joint District Judge, Narsingdi, due to unavoidable circum-stances the defendants was constrained to file a Transfer Miscellaneous Case No. 21 of 2015 before the Hon'ble High Court and accordingly the suit was transferred to the Court of District Judge, Dhaka by the judgment and order dated 30-11-2015. Thereafter the learned District Judge, Dhaka transferred the suit to the Fourth Court of Joint District judge, Dhaka and same was registered as Title Suit No. 36 of 2016 but at one stage of the said proceeding the presiding Judge of the said Court felt embarrassed to hear the suit, then the District Judge, Dhaka transferred the suit to the Court of Joint District Judge, Fifth Court, Dhaka, while the suit was registered as Title Suit No. 273 of 2017 and in the said court after conclusion of the trial i.e. examination and cross-examination of the witnesses and hearing argument suit was fixed on 28-4-2019 for delivery of the judgment. At this stage, the plaintiff filed an application before the Court of District Judge, Dhaka on 28-4-2019 under section 24 of the Code of Civil Procedure for withdrawing the suit from the Fifth Court of Joint District Judge, Dhaka and to transfer the same to any other competent Court, Dhaka. In the meantime the Joint District Judge, Fifth Court, Dhaka also felt embarrassed to hear the suit and the learned District Judge, Dhaka again transferred the suit to the Fourth Court of Joint District Judge, 'Dhaka by an administrative order and the said suit was again registered as Title Suit No. 305 of 2019; that again the defendants filed Transfer Miscellaneous Case No. 354 of 2019 before Court of District judge, Dhaka and upon hearing both the parties the learned District Judge, Dhaka transferred the same to the Second Court of Joint District Judge, Dhaka and the suit was renumbered as Title Suit No. 514 of 2019. 

6. That after transfer of the suit in the Second Court of Joint District Judge, the defendants-petitioners herein firstly filed an application under Order III, rule 1 read with section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure on 26-8-2019 praying for passing an order directing the plaintiff to appear before this court personally for cross-examining the plaintiff on the subject matter made in the application upon which the plaintiff based his claim in the suit, namely, registered Heba Declaration Deed dated 14-12-2012 (Exhibit-9) and other issues involved in the suit. It was further stated that previously engaged learned Advocate of the defendants could not realise importance of submitting an application to cross-examine the plaintiff in-person in this respect, otherwise, the defendants will be seriously prejudiced. 

7. That thereafter the defendants also filed another application on 28-10-2019 under Order VII, rule 11 read with section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure for rejection of the plaint or the suit is not maintainable and prayed for dismissal of the suit. In the application in paragraph No. 3 it is stated that in the meantime the plaintiff's full brother, Md Mujibur Rahman, defendant No. 3 who lives in USA, came to Bangladesh and he transferred 0.6 (six) acres of land in favour of defendant No. 1 by registered Heba-bil-Eawaj dated 9-10-2019 being deed No. 14652 and delivered possession thereof to him on the very date (9-10-2019), defendant No. 1 also transferred the 0.5(five) acres of land purchased by him from defendant No. 3 by the kabala dated 23-12-2012 being deed No. 28315 to Md Mujibur Rahman Khan by another registered Heba-bil-Eawaj being No. 14653 and delivered possession to Md Mujibur Rahman Khan. On the next day i.e. on 10-10-2019, the plaintiff's full brother transferred the land to the plaintiff which he got from defendant No. 1 by a Heba-bil-Eawaj deed being number 14839 and delivered possession of the transferred land to him. It may be noted that the suit land measuring 0.5(five) acres land and the land transferred in favour of Md Mujibur Rahman Khan (plaintiff's full brother) is the same land; that since by virtue of the transfer, by the heba declaration made by the plaintiff's full brother of the suit land, which he got through deed of Heba-bil-Eawaj made by defendant No. 1, the plaihtiff became the owner of the suit land as described in 'ka' schedule land, the prayer made for 'ka' schedule of land became infructuous and consequently, prayer made in schedule 'kha' also became infructuous and in fact no cause of action is subsisting to proceed with the suit. Accordingly, prayed for dismissal of the suit as not maintainable. 

8 The learned Joint District Judge fixed both the application for hearing on 4-11-2019 and after contested hearing both the applications were rejected by the impugned order dated 4-11-2019. 

9. That being aggrieved by the aforesaid impugned orders dated 4-11-2019, the defendant Nos. 1 and 2 moved this court by filing revisional application under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure and subsequently the defendants-petitioners filed supplementary-affidavit on 25-11-2019 by annexing plaint of the Title Suit No. 56 of 2013, as (Annexure-E), application under Order III, rule 1 read with section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure dated 26-8-2019 (Annexure-F) and registered Heba-bil-Eawaj Deed being number 14839 dated 15-10-2019 executed by defendant No. 3, Md Mujibur Rahman Khan to the plaintiff (Annexure-G). 

10. In this Revision, Rule was issued and proceedings of Title Suit No. 514 of 2019 now pending in the Second Court of Joint District Judge, Dhaka was stayed for a period of 2(two) months by order dated 25-11-2019. Against the said interim order dated 25-11-2019 passed in this Revision, the plaintiff-opposite-party filed Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 3727 of 2019. Upon hearing the parties, their Lordships of the Appellate Division of the opinion that ends of justice would be best served, if the Rule itself is disposed on merit by the High Court Division. Accordingly, the Appellate Division by order dated 26-1-2020 directed to heard and disposal of the Rule by the Division Bench of the High Court Division presided over by AKM Abdul Hakim, J, within 4(four) weeks from the date of receipt a copy of the order. 

11. The plaintiff-opposite party No. 1 contested the said rule by filing counter-affidavit dated 17-2-2020 denying the materials allegations made in the revisional application and contending, inter alia, that the plaintiff opposite party No. 1 was in London at the relevant date 9-10-2019 and 10-10-2019; that there was an order of temporary injunction dated 20-5-2013 passed by the trial court restraining the defendant-petitioners from disturbing the peaceful possession of the plaintiff's in respect of suit 'ka' schedule land, which is still inforce. Thus the suit 'ka' schedule land transferred by petitioner defendant No. 1 to Md Mujibur Rahman Khan on 9-10-2019 vide Deed No. 14653, which the defendant No. 1 purchased from defendant No. 3 on 23-12-2012 vide deed No. 28315 is only a paper transaction; that on the other hand, the deed of Heba-bil-Eawaj being Deed No. 14839 dated 10-10-2019 is also a paper transaction; that the plaintiff-opposite party No. 1 is totally ignorant about the so called Heba-bil-Eawaj Deed dated 10-10-2019; that the so-called purchase by the defendant-petitioner No. It through sale deed No. 28315 dated 23-12-2012 is otherwise a void deed because of forgery and therefore, he being a title less person, cannot transfer anything which he do not have. 

12. Mr JK Paul, the learned Advocate for the petitioners submits that the learned Joint District Judge committed error of law in rejecting the application filed under Order III, rule 1 read with section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure totally fail to conceive the facts and circumstances of the case and the question on which defendants wanted to cross-examine the plaintiff in person has pointed out in the application. He further submits that there is no bar either in the Code of Civil Procedure or in the Evidence Act to give direction to the plaintiff for his personal appearance for cross-examination in the material points involved in suit when plaintiff did not examine himself in support of his case. He finally submits that learned Joint District Judge rejected the application filed under Order VII, rule 11 read with section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure wrongly invoking the Doctrine of Lispendence as envised in section 52 of the Transfer of Property Act, as the plaintiff did not deny the fact since his full brother having acquired the suit property has already transferred the same to the plaintiff by executing registered declaration of heba. Therefore, no cause of action is subsisting to proceed with the suit by the plaintiff. 

13. On the other hand, Mr Mohammad Bakir Uddin Bhuiyan, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the plaintiff-opposite party No. 1 submits that the defendant categorically stated in paragraph No. 3 of the application under Order VII; rule 11 read with section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure dated 28-10-2019 (Annexure-A) that defendant No. 1 transferred the suit `Ica' schedule land which he purchased by 'kha' schedule deed being number 28315 dated 23-12-2012 in favour of Md Mujibur Rahman Khan by registered Heba-bil-Eawaj Deed No. 14653 dated 9-10-2019. This statement of the defendants clearly shows that the defendant No. 1 and 2 have no subsisting interest in the suit 'ka' schedule as such learned Joint District Judge did not commit any error of law in passing the impugned judgment and order dated 4-11-2019 and same has not occasioned failure of justice. He has further submitted that the learned Joint District Judge rightly rejected the application dated 26-8-2019 under Order III, rule 1 read with section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure (Annexure F) there is no scope to recall the plaintiff at this belated stage of suit since evidence was closed long before and the suit is now fixed for argument. Moreover, the plaintiff conducted the present suit through his constituted, who deposed in the suit as PW 1 without any objection by the defendants. Thus the learned Joint District Judge correctly found that the defendants filed this application at this belated stage just to delay and disposal of the suit. He has also submitted that at the time of disposing Civil Miscellaneous Case No. 21 of 2015, the Hon'ble High Court Division by order dated 30-12-2015 directed the trial court to dispose of the suit within 4(four) months but the defendant adopted dilatory tactics to prolong the delivery of judgment and, as such, the trial court could not pass the judgment of the suit till today. 

14. He has finally submitted that the learned Joint District Judge rightly found that the suit property was transferred during pendency of the suit, same is hit by doctrine of Lis pendens. Plaintiff had no knowledge about the transfer, which is a colourful transactions and not within the knowledge of the plaintiff. Thus there is no legal impediment to get relief by the plaintiff in the suit, since the cause of action of the suit is still subsisting. 

15. We have heard the learned Advocate of both the parties and perused the revisional application, supplementary-affidavit filed by the petitioners and Counter Affidavit filed by the opposite party. 

16. It appears that the Title Suit No. 56 of 2013 was filed by the plaintiff-opposite party No. 1 through his constituted attorney on 27-5-2013 in the First Court of Joint District Judge, Narsingdi for the following reliefs: 
“(ক) নালিশী ‘a’ SAM atts সম্পতিতে বাদী ১ যোল আনা মালিক মর্মে বিবাদীগণের বিরুদ্ধে এক ঘোষণামূলক ডিক্রী দিতে; 
(খ) নালিশা “খ' তপসিল বর্ণিত সাব কবলা দলিল নং ২৮৩১৫ তাং ২৩-১২-২০১২ইং ‘গ’ তপসিল বর্ণিত বায়নাপত্র দলিল নং ২৭৪৯৩ তাং ১২-৯২-২০১২ইং অবৈধ, বেআইনী, তঞ্চকতাপূর্ণ, যোগসাজসী এবং বাদীর উপর বাধ্যকর নহে মর্মে বিবাদীগণের বিরুদ্ধে এক ঘোষণীমূলক ডিক্রী দিতে;
(গ) মোকদ্দমার সম্যক খরচের ডিক্রী দিতে;
(ঘ) বাদী বিজ্ঞ আদালতের ন্যায় বিচারের স্বার্থে আর যে সকল প্রতিকার পাইতে পারে তার সম্যক ডিক্রী দিতে মর্জি হয়।”

17. Then on the prayer of the defendants-petitioners it was withdrawn from the Court of Joint District Judge, Narsingdi by order of a Division Bench of the Hon'ble High Court Division in Civil Miscellaneous Case No. 21 of 2015 dated 30-11-2015 and sent the same to the learned Court of District Judge, Dhaka with a direction to dispose of the suit with 4(four) months. Subsequently, the learned 'District Judge, Dhaka transferred the aforesaid suit to the Court of Joint District Judge, Fourth Court, Dhaka and the same was renumbered as Title Suit No. 36 of 2016 and then it was again transferred to the Court of Joint District Judge, Fifth Court, Dhaka and renumbered as Title Suit No. 273 of 2017 and in this court trial was concluded, argument was made by the parties and then date was fixed for delivery of judgment on 28-4-2019. At this stage, the suit was again transferred from the Court of Joint District Judge, Fifth Court, Dhaka to Joint District Judge, Fourth Court, Dhaka and renumbered as Title Suit No. 305 of 2019, then again it was transferred to the Court of Joint District Judge, Second Court, Dhaka and renumbered as Title Suit No. 514 of 2019 and the learned Joint District Judge, Second Court, Dhaka fixed the suit for hearing argument. 

18. That it appears that after transfer, when the suit was fixed for argument in the Second Court of Joint District Judge, Dhaka, the defendants-petitioners filed a misconceived application on 28-6-2019, under Order III, rule 1 read with section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure (Annexure-F) for personal appearance of the plaintiff before the court for cross-examining him on the points stated in the said application. Admittedly, the plaintiff of the instant suit is a sitting Judge of the High Court Division of the Supreme Court of Bangladesh, who filed the instant suit by his constituted attorney, Zahid Hossain on 27-5-2013. 

19. It further appears from record PW 1 was examined on 27-5-2015, 28-6-2015, 07-7-2015 and 28-7-2015 and his cross-examination was over on 25-5-2016. Thereafter by 19-4-2017 PW 2-5 deposed in the suit, whereupon the examination of d.w.1 started on 05-6-2017 and thereafter deposition of DW 2-4 were completed on 12-2-2019. The learned Advocate of both the parties concluded their arguments on 23-3-2019. Then the suit was fixed for pronouncement of judgment on 28-4-2019. 

20. It also appears that the plaintiff filed the suit through his Constituted Attorney, KGM Zahid Hossain on 27-5-2013 and his attorney was examined as PW1. For conducting the suit the registered Power of Attorney No. 33 dated 17-2-2013 was filed and marked as (Exhibit No. 1). After filing of the suit and even after closing of the evidence of PW1, the defendants did not feel necessity for personal appearance of the plaintiff. Now, the defendant at this belated stage, when the suit was fixed for Argument filed two applications just to delay and drag the suit and to harass the plaintiff. It is for the plaintiff to decide how he will prove his case, whether by adducing evidence by himself or through his constituted Attorney, there is no legal bar in this respect. 

21. It is important to note that on behalf of the plaintiff his constituted attorney was examined PW 1 and he was duly cross-examined by the defendants long before. Since the plaintiff did not depose in the suit, the defendant had no right to cross-examine him. Actually a person was cross-examined on the basis of evidence made in examination-in-chief. So, present application filed by defendants for prayer for personal appearance of the plaintiff to cross-examine him by the defendant is an attempt to harass and humiliate the plaintiff and not sanctioned by law. 

22. In this connection we may look into the Order XVIII, rule 17 of the Code of Civil Procedure is in the following terms: 
"Rule 17: Court may recall and examine witness: The Court may at any stage of a suit recall any witness who has been examined and may (subject to the law of evidence for the time being in force) put such questions to him as the court thinks fit." 

23. This is an enabling power and very wide power has been conferred for adjudication of the dispute and this power is only available for giving justice inasmuch the enabling power conferred upon the Court to put such question "to him as the court thinks fit". This discretionary power is to be used for ends of justice and a litigant cannot claim exercise of such discretionary power when the rules of evidence do not permit such course. The Rule itself says that this power may be exercised subject to the law of evidence for the time being in force. In the foregoing paragraph the material dates have been noticed and it is clear that this is an attempt for an obvious purpose inasmuch as after about 2 years such a petition was filed. Discretionary power of the Court cannot be exercised for helping the litigant who is not vigilant and certainly such power cannot be exercised for giving undue advantage to a party. 

24. The power of the court to act under Order XVIII, rule 17 are very wide. Thus, it the Court while considering the judgment finds that there is any ambiguity on the face of the record Court can in proper case, recalls witness, ' who had given evidence, for that purpose. But the power under the rule is discretionary and ought to be exercised with the greatest care and only in the most peculiar circumstances. 

25. In view of the facts and circumstances of this case, it can not be held that by making the impugned order by the learned Joint District Judge rejecting an application under Order III, rule 1 read with section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure there has been a failure of justice, as such no interference is called for. 

26. It is worthy to note after conclusion of trial, the learned Joint District Judge, Fifth Court, Dhaka fixed the suit for judgment long before on 28-4-2019. So, the learned Joint District Judge, Second Court can easily dispose of the suit on consideration and appreciation of the evidence and materials on record. Moreover, in the facts and circumstances of the present case, it is apparent the defendants unnecessarily filed this misconceived application at this belated stage in the suit for personal appearance of the plaintiff just to harass, humiliate the plaintiff and adopted dilatory tactics to prolong the disposal of the suit. The said application are not dealt with in this Rule. That the plaintiff has every right to file his case though his constituted Attorney and there is no legal bar to file the suit through his attorney and to prove his case either by himself or through his constituted Attorney. 

27. It further transpires that the defendants filed another application before the learned Joint District Judge, Second Court on 28-10-2019 under Order VII, rule 11 read with section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure for rejecting the plaint. In that application the defendant-petitioners in paragraph No. 3 stated that in the meantime the plaintiff's full brother, Md Mojibur Rahman Khan, who lives in America came to Bangladesh and on the basis of registered Bantan-Nama deed executed among his brother and sisters he transferred to the extent of 6(six) decimals of land from his share by a registered Heba-bil-Eawaj Deed No. 14652 dated 9-10-2019 to defendant No. 1 Md Rubel Khan and delivered possession in favour of him. On the other hand, on the same day, the defendant No. 1 transferred suit 5(five) decimals of land which he purchased by a registered Saf Kabala Deed No. 28315 dated 23-12-2012 in favour of Md Mojibur Khan by a registered Heba-bil-Eawaj Deed No. 14653 dated 9-10-2019 and delivered possession to him. The aforesaid fact was described by the petitioners in paragraph No. 12 of the instant Civil Revision No. 3351 of 2019. The defendants further stated that. Md Mojibur Rahman Khan by another registered Heba-bil-Eawaj Deed No. 14839 dated 10-10-2019 transferred the said land to the plaintiff. Hence the prayer of the plaintiff in respect of "Ka" and "Kha" schedule became infractuous and thus the suit cannot be continued and, as such, prayed for rejecting the plaint as the suit has no cause of action. 

28. In the facts and circumstance of the case, it appears that the suit was filed in the year 2013 and the defendant filed the application under Order VII, rule 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure on 28-10-2019. Generally however, ends of justice is require that power should be exercised at the earliest opportunity not at this belated stage when the suit was once fixed for delivery of judgment on 28-4-2019 and now fixed for argument. 

29. In this connection we may profitably refer the decision in the case of Knzi Md Shahjahan vs Md Khalitur Rahman Mndbar reported in 54 DLR (AD) 125 wherein their Lordships held: 
"There is no hard and fast Rule when an application for rejection of plaint is to be filed but ends of justice demands that it must be filed at the earliest opportunity." 

30. There is no legal scope to reject the plaint unless the plaint itself does not disclose a cause of action or the suit is barred by any law. The court, in considering the question of cause of action, shall apply its mind to the averment made in the plaint and not any other matter and in doing so shall presume every allegation made in the plaint as true. 

31. Further examining good number of decisions of our apex Court in respect of Order VII Rule 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure, we may refer some decisions reported in 1982 BLD 160, 49 DLR (AD) 236 and 53 DLR (AD) 62 wherein principles laid down as under: 
(i) "The well settled principle of laws relating to Order VII, rule 11 are the plaint can be rejected only on reference to plaint itself as whether it is barred in any of the four clauses of Order VII, rule 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure. 
(ii) Plaint cannot be rejected on defense material as well as on mixed question of law and fact.
(iii) Where evidence is required and where there is material, plaint cannot be rejected. 
(iv) Plaint can be rejected if it does not disclose a cause of action and barred by any law. 
(v) There is no hard and fast Rule when an application for rejection of plaint is to be filed but ends of justice demands that it must be filed at the earliest opportunity. 
(vi) Plaint cannot be rejected before filing of the written statement". 

32. Having regard to the facts and circumstance of the case and the decisions cited above, we are of the view that the learned Joint District Judge did not commit any error of law in rejecting the application filed by the defendant-petitioners under Order VII, rule 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure and same has not occasioned failure of justice. 

33. Thus the impugned orders dated 4-11-2019 passed by the learned Joint District Judge is affirmed. Order of stay granted at time of issuance of the rule stands vacated. 

34. Accordingly, we find no merit in this Rule. 

35. In the result, the rule is discharged without any order as to costs. 36. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case and since the suit is pending for last 7(seven) years, the trial court is directed to dispose of the suit within a period of 3(three) months from the date of receipt of this judgment and order. The learned Joint District Judge, Second Court, Dhaka is further directed not to give any adjournment to either parties since the suit was once fixed for delivery of judgment on 28-4-2019. Earlier on 30-12-2015 this Court in disposing Civil Miscellaneous Case No. 21 of 2015 directed the trial court to dispose of the suit within 4(four) months. 

Send down the Lower Court Records at once and a copy of the judgment be sent to the concerned court expeditiously. 

End.

full_judgment:
In this revision Rule was issued granting leave to revision at the instance of the petitioner calling upon the opposite party No. 1 to show cause as to why the impugned judgment and order dated 20-2-2018 passed by the learned District Judge, Barguna, in Civil Revision No. 32 of 2017 allowing the revision and reversing the judgment and order dated 1-6-2017 passed by  the learned Senior Assistant Judge, Patharghata, Barguna in Title Suit No. 31 of 2017 allowing the application for staying all further proceedings of Title Execution Suit No. 04 of 2016 should not be set-aside and/or pass such other or further order or orders as to this Court may seem fit and proper. 2. Facts relevant for disposal of the Rule, in short, are that the petitioner along with 19 others, as plaintiff, instituted Title Suit No. 31 of 2017 in the Court of Assistant Judge, Patharghata, Barguna, against the opposite party No. 1 along with others for a declaration in the following manner: “ক) আরজির নিম্ন (খ) তপসিল বর্ণিত ভূমি সম্পর্কে (ক) তপসিল বর্ণিত বিরোধীয় রায় ও ডিক্রি ভাক্ত, যোগাযোগী, ফেরবী, অকার্যকরী, অকর্মন্য, শঠতামি, তঞ্চকলা মূলক মর্মে রদ ও রহিতের ডিক্রি দিবার ।”

3. In the plaint the plaintiffs amongst other stated that opposite party No. 1, as plaintiff, instituted Title Suit No. 32 of 2011 against the petitioner and others, as defendant, for a decree of partition and in the said suit no summons were duly served upon the defendants. Consequently, they could not contest the suit by filing written statement and leading evidences. Resultantly, the suit was decreed ex-parte on 2-3-2015 in preliminary form and thereafter an Advocate Commissioner was appointed for effecting partition physically who without visiting the suit property and letting know the fact to the defendants submitted a report before the trial court. 

4. The trial court in the absence of any objection against the report accepted the same and made the preliminary decree final on 24-2-2016. Thereafter, the decree holder opposite party No. 1 put the decree in execution by filing Title Execution Case No. 04 of 2016 on 09-6-2016. The petitioner filed Miscellaneous Case No. 05 of 2017 on 16-5-2017 under Order 9 Rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure praying for setting aside the ex-parte decree. In the said case the plaintiff opposite party appeared and filed written objection, before filing of the said miscellaneous case the present petitioner along with others, instituted Title Suit No. 31 of 2017 on 23-3-2017, challenging the preliminary decree signed on 08-3-2016 passed in Partition Suit No. 32 of 2011. 

5. By this time, execution case was proceeding in accordance with law and for effecting delivery of possession, the court deployed police force with District Nazir and appointed Advocate Commissioner and issued writ of delivery of possession by order No. 13 dated 13-3-2017. Pursuant to writ of delivery of possession Advocate Commissioner and Nazir of the court submitted their report on 27-3-2017 along with bill, praying for withdrawing the same. In the meantime, plaintiff of Title Suit No. 31 of 2017 filed an application on 23-3-2017 praying for stay further proceeding of the Execution Case No. 04 of 2017. 

6. The trial court heard the application and upon hearing by its order dated 1-6-2017 allowed the application and stayed proceedings in Title Execution Suit No. 04 of 2016 and also by the said order rejected the report submitted by the Advocate Commissioner. 

7. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the judgment and order of the trial court, passed in Title Suit No. 31 of 2017, the opposite party No. 1 preferred Civil Revision No. 32 of 2017 before the District Judge, Barguna who upon hearing by the impugned judgment and order dated 28-2-2018 allowed the revision and set-aside the order of the trial court, directing Advocate Commissioner to submit report afresh by investigating physically. At this juncture, the petitioner moved this Court by filing this revisional application under section 115(4) of the Code of Civil Procedure seeking leave to revision and obtained the present Rule and order of stay. 

8. Mr Md Sagir Hossain, learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner submits that in the event of filing a suit by the judgment debtor against whom decree was passed, challenging the decree, the court ought to have stayed the proceeding of execution case till disposal of the suit. Accordingly, the trial court rightly allowed the application and stayed further proceeding of the execution case by order dated 1-6-2017, but the revisional court while allowing the revision and setting aside the order of the trial court did not even given a single finding why the execution proceeding should not be stayed but the revisional court only decided the matter in respect of rejection of Advocate Commissioner's report, thus, the judgment and order of the revisional court below suffers from legal insufficiency, as such, the same is liable to be set-aside. In support of his submissions he has referred to the cases of Zagir Hussain vs Aminul Hague and others reported in 1999 BLD (HCD) 366 = 51 DLR 425 and Narsidas Nathubhai Vohra vs Manharsingh Agarsing Thakor reported in AIR 1931 Bombay 247. 

9. Mr Hasan Tareq, learned Advocate appearing for the opposite party No.1 submits that after passing preliminary decree the suit property was physically partitioned by an Advocate Commissioner who submitted an exhaustive report, wherein the petitioner himself put his hand as one of the witnesses. Therefore, it was very much within their knowledge that a decree has been passed by the court giving saham to the plaintiff in Partition Suit No. 32 of 2011. 

10. He further submits that the petitioner along with others filed Title Suit No. 31 of 2017 challenging the decree passed in Title Suit No. 32 of 2011 and after filing of the suit they also filed a Miscellaneous Case No. 05 of 2017 under Order 9 Rule 13 of the Code on 16-5-2017. When the opposite party No. 1 filed written objection in the case they did not proceed with the same, consequently, the case was dismissed for default on 24-4-2018. 

11. The petitioner knowing fully well about the decree allowed to proceed the Execution Case No. 04 of 2016 upto delivery of possession. When delivery of possession was made and report has been submitted before the executing court to that effect, the plaintiffs in Title Suit No. 31 of 2017 filed an application praying for stay further proceedings of the Execution Case No. 04 of 2016 wherein no further action was required to be taken. After delivery of possession only thing left with the court to accept the report and to pass an order disposing the execution case with full satisfaction, as such, there is nothing to be stayed by the court below. Hence the revisional court rightly set-aside the order of the trial court. 

12. Heard the learned Advocates of both the parties, have gone through the revisional application, plaint in Title Suit No. 31 of 2017, order sheet in Execution Case No. 04 of 2016, application for stay, impugned judgment and order of both the courts below. 

13. From annexue-Al it appears that Partition Suit No. 32 of 2011 was decreed ex-parte on 2-3-2015 and decree was drawn on 8-3-2015. Thereafter, for effecting partition physically, an Advocate Commissioner was appointed who submitted a report with a sketch map effecting partition of the suit property. Then, the preliminary decree was made final on 24-2-2016 by accepting and making the report of the commissioner part of the decree. Thereafter, the decree was put in execution by filing Title Execution Case No. 04 of 2016. The petitioner along with others instituted Title Suit No. 31 of 2017 as well as filed Miscellaneous Case No. 05 of 2017 under Order 9, rule 13 of the Code praying for setting aside the ex-parte decree. Subsequently, the petitioners allowed to dismiss the case for default on 24-4-2018. The petitioner, as plaintiff, in Title Suit No. 31 of 2017 filed an application before the trial court on 23-3-2017 praying for stay further proceedings of Execution Case No 04 of 2016. The opposite party No. 1, as defendant, contested the application and the trial court upon hearing allowed the application and stayed further proceeding of the execution case. But the trial court while staying the proceeding in Execution Case No. 04 of 2016, unfortunately and wrongly rejected the commission report submitted by the Advocate Commissioner in Execution Case No. 04 of 2016, which it cannot do legally. Because in Title Suit No. 31 of 2017 no report was filed by the Advocate Commissioner but it was submitted in Execution Case No. 04 of 2016 and the court can accept or reject the same by passing an order in the execution proceeding, not in any other suit or case. 

14. The defendant opposite party No. 1 challenged the order of the trial court by filing Civil Revision No. 32 of 2017 before the District Judge, who by the impugned judgment and order dated 28-2-2018 allowed the revision and set-aside the order dated 1-6-2017 passed by the trial court in Title Suit No. 31 of 2017 and directed further investigation of the property and to file a fresh report. 

15. From perusal of impugned order passed by the revisional court, it appears that unfortunately the revisional court failed to appreciate the fact that the commissioner report was submitted by the Advocate Commissioner in Title Execution Case No. 04 of 2016 not in Title Suit No. 31 of 2017 and the trial court has had no scope or reason to accept or reject the commission report in Title Suit No. 31 of 2017. The revisional court also validated the order of the trial court and directed for further investigation and to submit a fresh report which the revisional court also cannot do. The order of the trial court connects two things, one is; rejection of commission report and another is order of stay staying proceeding in Execution Case No. 04 of 2016. But the revisional court only considered Advocate Commissioner report without applying judicial mind and did not even a single word or finding given in respect of stay further proceeding of the Execution Case No. 04 of 2016. The impugned order as a whole seems to be unjust and impracticable. 

16. As apprised by Mr Hasan Tareq, learned Advocate for the opposite party, the report submitted by the Advocate Commissioner is relating to delivery of possession and for withdrawal of commission fee and the said report in no way touches the merit of the preliminary decree or measurement and distribution of property by filed book or sketch-map and there was nothing contrary to the decree of the trial court. As such, there was no earthly reason to reject that report which only said that they effected physical possession with police force and District Nazir. However, this matter is not at all concerned in this revision, as no revision preferred by the decree holder against the rejection of Advocate Commissioner's report. 

17. Now the question before this court, whether in the event of challenging a decree by filing an independent suit by the judgment debtor, execution proceeding can be stayed till disposal of the suit. To appreciate the matter, I have gone through the relevant provisions contain in Order 21, rule 29 of the Code of Civil Procedure. Said provision of law provides that an application for stay of execution case is maintainable in the subsequent suit filed by the judgment debtor challenging the decree passed in earlier suit and arising out of the decree between the decree holder and the judgment debtor. In the instant case it appears that the Title Suit No. 31 of 2017 has been filed challenging the decree passed in Title Suit No. 32 of 2011 in preliminary form. But not against the final decree and in the suit, the plaintiff filed application praying for stay further proceeding of Execution Case No. 04 of 2016, wherein record shows that possession of the property already delivered but in the order sheet of Execution Case No. 04 of 2016, this Court finds nothing to the effect that in execution of the decree possession of the property has been delivered to the decree holder as yet. 

18. Both the parties could not apprise the court actual fact and position of the execution case, but from last order dated 8-6-2017 passed in Execution Case No. 04 of 2016, it appears that the proceedings of the case has been stayed by the court in Title Suit No. 31 of 2017. 

19. In this situation, I find that admittedly, a suit is pending before the court challenging the decree under execution and the execution proceedings has not yet been ended with full satisfaction, meaning thereby, it is still pending. For ensuring justice and to prevent various proceedings, I think that the proper course is to stay further proceeding of the execution case till disposal of the suit. It is to be mentioned that the plaintiff did not file the suit challenging the final decree which is under execution and the plaintiff could not confirm whether possession of the property already delivered to the decree holder in Title Suit No. 32 of 2011. In the event of delivery of possession to the decree holder the present Title Suit No. 31 of 2017 filed by the plaintiff would be incompetent for want of consequential relief in the form of recovery of possession. 

20. Since this matter is relating to an order of stay only, this Court refrained itself from making any observations regarding maintainability of the suit. 

21. Learned Advocate for the opposite party No. 1 submits that in the event of staying proceeding of execution case the possession delivered through court to the opposite party would be threatened by the plaintiff in suit. Considering such submissions, this court thinks that purpose of the parties will be served and justice will be met if the parties are directed to maintain status quo in respect of the suit property. 

22. Taking into consideration the above, I find merit in the Rule. 

23. In the result, the Rule is made absolute, however without any order as to costs. 

24. The impugned judgment and order dated 28-2-2018 passed in Civil Revision No. 42 of 2018 is hereby set-aside and the order dated 1-6-2017 passed by the trial court is hereby restored only to the extent of stay. 

25. Both the parties are directed to maintain status quo in respect of possession of the suit property till disposal of Title Suit No. 31 of 2017. 

26. The trial court is hereby directed to dispose of the Title Suit No. 31 of 2017 within 06 (six) months from the date of receipt of this judgment and order positively. 

27. The order of stay granted at the time of issuance of the Rule is hereby vacated. 

Communicate a copy of this judgment to the court concerned. 

End.
