full_judgment:
এম ইনায়েতুর রহিম, J: বর্তমান স্ব-প্রণোদিত রুলটি বিগত ২-১-২০২০ইং তারিখ নিন্মোক্ত শর্তে ইস্যু করা হয়:
Let a suo-motu Rule Nisi be issued calling upon the 1. Government of Bangladesh, represented by the Secretary (স্বাস্থ্য সেবা বিভাগ), Ministry of Health and family welfare, 2. Director-General, Directorate of Health, Mohakhali Dhaka, 3. Dr. Moarraf Hossen, outgoing Director of National Institute of Cancer Research and Hospital (NICRH), now on LPR, Mohakhali, Dhaka, 4. Director, National Institute of Cancer Research and Hospital (NICRH), Mohakhali, Dhaka, 5. Editor, The Daily Star, 64-65, Kazi Nazrul Islam Avenue, Dhaka and 6. Mr. Mohammad Al-Masum Molla, Correspondent, the Daily Star, 64-65, Kazi Nazrul Islam Avenue, Dhaka to show cause as to why the negligence of Respondent Nos.1-3 in management of National Institute of Cancer Research and Hospital (NICRH), Mohakhali, Dhaka as well as failure to install, protect and preserve the lifesaving devices equipments/machineries device described in the report in question should not be declared to have been done without lawful authority and is of no legal effect and/or pass such other or further order or orders as to this Court may seem fit and proper".

২. সুপ্রীম কোর্টের বিজ্ঞ আইনজীবী জনাব মনোজ কুমার মন্ডল ২-১-২০২০ইং তারিখে দৈনিক ইংরেজি সংবাদপত্র “দি ডেইলি স্টার”-এ প্রকাশিত "ICU on Sickbed’ প্রতিবেদনটি আদালতে উপস্থাপন করেন । উক্ত প্রতিবেদনে উল্লেখ করা হয় যে, জাতীয় ক্যান্সার রিসার্স ইনস্টিটিউট এবং হাসপাতাল (NICRH) কর্তৃপক্ষ ১২ বছর পূর্বে ক্রয়কৃত ৮টি উচ্চক্ষমতা সম্পন্ন জীবন রক্ষাকারী ভেন্টিলেটর অদ্যাবধি স্থাপন করেনি । ফলে গুরুতর অসুস্থ রোগীদের আইসিইউ সেবা প্রদান করা সম্ভব হচ্ছে না এবং রোগীদের আইসিইউর প্রয়োজন হলে বিভিন্ন হাসপাতালে পাঠিয়ে দেয়া হয় । উক্ত ভেন্টিলেটরগুলি প্রতিটি ৭০ লক্ষ টাকা মূল্যে ক্রয় করা হয়। তিন বছর পূর্বে কেন্দ্রীয়ভাবে অক্সিজেন সরবরাহ ব্যবস্থা স্থাপন করা হলেও ঐ ভেন্টিলেটরগুলি স্থাপন করা হয়নি। বর্তমানে উক্ত ভেন্টিলেটরগুলি অকোজো অবস্থায় পড়ে আছে।

৩. উপরোক্ত প্রতিবেদনের সূত্রে জনস্বার্থে অত্র রুলটি ইস্যু করা হয়।

8. রুলটি ইস্যুকালীন সময়ে প্রতিপক্ষ নং-১, সচিব স্বাস্থ্য সেবা বিভাগ) স্বাস্থ্য ও পরিবার কল্যাণ মন্ত্রনালয় এবং প্রতিপক্ষ নং- ২, মহা-পরিচালক, স্বাস্থ্য অধিদপ্তরকে-কে পত্রিকায় প্রকাশিত তর্কিত সংবাদটি বিষয়ে অনুসন্ধান পূর্বক একটি প্রতিবেদন প্রদানের নির্দেশ দেয়া হয় এবং প্রতিপক্ষ নং-৩ এর অবসরোত্তর আর্থিক সুবিধাদি স্থগিত রাখার নির্দেশ দেয়া হয়।

৫. আদালতের নির্দেশ প্রতিপালনে স্বাস্থ্য ও পরিবার কল্যাণ মন্ত্রণালয় (স্বাস্থ্য সেবা বিভাগ) প্রতিবেদনে বর্ণিত অভিযোগের বিষয়ে তদন্ত পূর্বক অত্র আদালতে একটি প্রতিবেদন প্রেরণ করে। ঐ প্রতিবেদনে ভেন্টিলেটর স্থাপনা না করে আইসিইউ চালু না হওয়ার জন্য নিম্নলিখিত কর্মকর্তাগণকে দায়ী করা হয়:-

১। ডাঃ এএমএম শরিফুল আলম, 
২। ডাঃ মোল্লা ওবায়দুল্লাহ (৩৭৪২৭), 
৩। ডাঃ মোঃ মোসাররফ হোসেন (৩৭৫০৯) এবং 
৪। ডাঃ মানস কুমার বসু (৩৯০১৩) ।

৬. দায়ী এ সকল ডাক্তারদের মধ্যে ডাঃ শরিফুল আলম গত ৮-২-২০০৯ইং তারিখে, ডাঃ মোল্লা ওবায়দুল্লাহ ১-১-২০১৩ইং তারিখে এবং ডাঃ এবং ডাঃ মোঃ মোসাররফ হোসেন ২৯-১২-২০১৯ইং তারিখে পিআরএল-এ গমন করেছেন। প্রতিবেদনে আরো উল্লেখ করা হয় যে, উপরোক্ত তিনজন কর্মকর্তা বর্তমানে সরকারী চাকুরিতে না থাকায় তাদের বিরুদ্ধে কোন ব্যবস্থা গ্রহণ করা যায়নি । তবে আইসিইউ এর দায়িত্ব পালনকারী কর্মকর্তা ডাঃ মানস কুমার বসু-র বিরুদ্ধে অসদাচরন এর দায়ে বিভাগীয় শাস্তিমূলক ব্যবস্থা গ্রহণের পদক্ষেপ নেয়া হয়েছে। প্রতিবেদনে আরো উল্লেখ করা হয় যে, তদন্তে দায়ী ক্যান্সার ইনস্টিটিউটের প্রাক্তন পরিচালক ডাঃ মোয়াররফ হোসেন তার দায়িত্ব পালন কালে (২০১৪-২০১৯)আইসিইউ সংস্থাপন সংক্রান্তে ন্যাশনাল ইলেকট্রো মেডিকেল ইকুইপমেন্ট মেইনটেন্যান্স ওয়ার্কশপ অ্যান্ড ট্রেনিং সেন্টার (নিমিউ এন্ড টিসি)এর চিফ টেকনিক্যাল ম্যানেজারদের সঙ্গে বেশ কয়েকবার পত্র যোগাযোগ করেন । কিন্তু নিমিউ এন্ড টিসি হতে জানানো হয়েছে যে, ২০১৪-২০১৯ পর্যন্ত নিমিউ এন্ড টিসি এর চীফ টেকনিক্যাল ম্যানেজার হিসেবে কর্মরত ছিলেন - ১। জনাব মোঃ আবদুল কাইয়ুম যুগ্ম সচিব, বর্তমানে অবসরপ্রাপ্ত, ৫-৬-২০১৩ হতে ১৪-৫-২০১৫), ২। জনাব মোঃ রেজানুর রহমান (যুগ্ম সচিব, ২৬-৭-২০১৫ তারিখ হতে ১৪-৫-২০১৮) এবং ৩। জনাব মোহাঃ আমিনুর রহমান (উপ-সচিব), ২০-১-২০১৯ হতে অদ্যাবধি এ প্রতিষ্ঠানের দায়িত্বে আছেন। জনাব আমিনুর রহমান জানিয়েছেন যে, ক্যান্সার ইন্সটিটিউট হতে ২০১৪ সালে প্রেরিত পত্র (স্মারক নং ৩৪৩৮ তারিখ ২৫-১১-২০১৪) এবং ২০১৫ সালে প্রেরিত পত্রটি (স্মারক নং ৬১৭০ তারিখ ২৪-৭-২০১৫) অর্থাৎ প্রাক্তন চিফ টেকনিক্যাল ম্যানেজার জনাব মোঃ আবদুল কাইয়ুম ও  জনাব মোঃ রেজানুর রহমান দায়িত্ব পালনকালে প্রেরিত উক্ত পত্র দুটির হদিস নিমিউ এন্ড টিসিতে পাওয়া যায়নি । বর্তমানে কর্মরত চিফ টেকনিক্যাল ম্যানেজারের (জনাব আমিনুর রহমান) সময়কালে ক্যান্সার ইঙ্গটিটিউট হতে প্রেরিত পত্রের (স্মারক নং ৬১৭০ তারিখ ২৯-৯-২০১৯) প্রেক্ষিতে তিনি আইসিইউ ভেন্টিলেটর সংক্রান্ত চেকলিস্ট প্রেরণের জন্য অনুরোধ জানান এবং ক্যান্সার ইন্সটিটিউট হতে পাওয়া গিয়েছে । ইতোঃমধ্যে মন্ত্রণীলয়ের টিম কর্তৃক তদন্ত কার্যক্রম শুরু হওয়ায় মেরামতের উদ্যোগ গ্রহণ করা যায়নি ।

৭. প্রতিপক্ষ নং-৩, রুলটি খারিজের জন্য একটি দরখাস্ত দাখিল করেন। এই প্রতিপক্ষের বক্তব্য, পত্রিকায় প্রকাশিত প্রতিবেদনটি সত্য নয় এবং প্রকৃত অবস্থার বিপরীত । মেশিনগুলি ক্রয়ের সময়ে তিনি দায়িতে ছিলেন না। প্রতিষ্ঠানটির পরিচালক ও অধ্যাপক রেডিওথেরাপী হিসেবে তিনি ১৮-১০-২০১৪ইং তারিখে যোগদান করে হাসপাতালের প্রভূত উন্নয়ন সাধন করেছেন। ভেন্টিলেটরগুলির ২২-৬-২০০৬ইং তারিখে ক্রয় করা হয় । তিনি দুটি পৃথক পত্রের মাধ্যমে ২৫-১১-২০১৪ এবং ২৮-৭-২০১৫ইং তারিখে নিম���উ-এর নিকট মেশিনগুলি মেরামত সেলে সার্ভিসিং করার অনুরোধ জানিয়ে ব্যবস্থা গ্রহণের অনুরোধ জানান । সর্বশেষ ২৯-৯-২০১৯ইং তারিখে পুনরায় নিমিউ-কে অনুরোধ জানিয়ে পত্র প্রদান করেন। তিনি তার দায়িত্ব ও কর্তব্য পালনে কোন অবহেলা করেননি।

৮. প্রতিপক্ষ নং-৫, সম্পাদক, দি ডেইলী ইস্টার, একটি হলফনামা দাখিল ক্রমে প্রকাশিত সংবাদটির সত্যতা নিশ্চিত করেছেন।

৯. প্রতিপক্ষ নং-২ এর দাখিলকৃত প্রতিবেদন হতে এটা সুস্পষ্ট যে, আইসিইউ ভেস্টিলেটর সমূহ ১২ বছর পূর্বে ক্রয় করা হলেও হাসপাতালের দায়িত্বপ্রাপ্ত কর্মকর্তাগণের চরম অবহেলা ও দায়িত্বহীনতার কারণে তা স্থাপন করা সম্ভব হয় নাই। উচ্চ মূল্যের এই ভেন্টিলেটরগুলি সংস্থাপন না হওয়ার কারণে ব্যবহার অনুপোযোগী ও অকেজো হয়ে পড়েছে। এটা আদালতের কাছে বিস্ময়কর মনে হয়েছে যে, জনাব ডাঃ মোয়াররফ হোসেন আইসিইউ সংস্থাপন সংক্রান্তে নিমিউ এন্ড টিসি এর চীফ টেকনিক্যাল ম্যানেজারগণের বরাবরে প্রেরিত ২৫-১১-২০১৪ইং এবং ২৪-৭-২০১৫ইং তারিখে পত্র দুটির প্রাপ্তি সম্পর্কে সংশ্লিষ্ট কর্তৃপক্ষ অস্বীকার করেছে। এছাড়া স্বাস্থ্য মন্ত্রণালয় কর্তৃক প্রেরিত প্রতিবেদনে এ সংক্রান্তে দায়ী ব্যক্তিদের চিহ্নিত করা হয়নি ।

১০. দেশের একমাত্র ক্যান্সার রিসার্স ইন্সটিটিউট এবং হাসপাতালে চরম অব্যবস্থাপনা, দায়িত্বশীল ব্যক্তিদের কর্তব্য অবহেলা শুধু দুঃখজনকই নয়, তা নিন্দনীয় ও উদ্বেগের বিষয়। প্রতিপক্ষ নং-২ এর প্রতিবেদনে উল্লেখিত চারজন ব্যক্তি-কে দায়ী করা হয়েছে। তবে প্রতিবেদনে উল্লেখ করা হয়েছে ডাঃ মোঃ মোয়াররফ হোসেন তার দায়িত্ব পালনকালে আইসিইউ সংস্থাপন সংক্রান্তে নিমিউ এন্ড টিসি এর চীফ টেকনিক্যাল ম্যানেজারদের সঙ্গে বেশ কয়েকবার পত্রযোগাযোগ করেছেন। কিন্তু ঐ কর্তৃপক্ষ পত্রসমূহ প্রাপ্তি অস্বীকার করেছে। এমতাবস্থায়, উপরোক্ত বিষয়টি নিয়ে অধিকতর তদন্ত হওয়া প্রয়োজন । এলপিআর-এ যাওয়ার কারনে দায়ী ব্যক্তিগণের বিরুদ্ধে বিভাগীয় ব্যবস্থা নেয়া সম্ভব হয়নি বলে প্রতিবেদনে উল্লেখ করা হয়েছে।

১১. সামগ্রিক অবস্থা বিবেচনায় আদালত জনস্বার্থে নিম্নোক্ত আদেশ ও পর্যবেক্ষণসমূহ প্রদান করছে:-

১। দায়ী ডাঃ এএমএম শরিফুল আলম এবং ডাঃ মোল্লা ওবায়দুল্লাহ ৩৭৪২৭) এর বিরুদ্ধে পিআরএল জনিত কারনে যেহেতু বিভাগীয় ব্যবস্থা নেয়া সম্ভব নয়, সেহেতু তাদের প্রত্যেকের নিকট হতে দায়িত্ব পালনে অবহেলার কারনে প্রতিকী (token) ক্ষতিপূরণ বাবদ ৫(পীচ) লক্ষ টাকা ক্ষতিপূরণ আদায়ের সচিব, স্বাস্থ্য ও পরিবার কল্যাণ মন্ত্রণালয় স্বাস্থ্য সেবা বিভাগ) কে নির্দেশ দেয়া হলো।আদায়কৃত ক্ষতিপূরণের অর্থ সংশ্লিষ্ট হাসপাতালের উন্নয়ন তহবিলে/সরকারি কোষাগারে জমা করতে হবে।

২। রুল ইস্যুর সময়ে প্রদত্ত ডাঃ মোঃ মোয়াররফ হোলেন-এর অবসরকালীন আর্থিক সুবিধাদি স্থগিত রাখার যে অন্তবর্তী আদেশ প্রদান করা হয়েছিল তা প্রত্যাহার করা হলো ।

ডাঃ মোয়াররফ হোসেন দাবী করেছেন তিনি ২৫-১১-২০১৪ এবং ২৮-৭-২০১৫ইং তারিখে দুটি পত্রের মাধ্যমে নিমিউ-কে তর্কিত ভেন্টিলেটরগুলি সচল করার অনুরোধ জানিয়েছিলেন । তবে প্রতিপক্ষ নং-২ এর তদন্ত প্রতিবেদন অনুযায়ী নিমিউ কর্তৃপক্ষ উক্ত পত্র দুটি প্রাপ্ত হয়নি৷ সে কারনে প্রতিপক্ষ নং-১, সচিব, (স্বাস্থ্য সেবা বিভাগ) স্বাস্থ্য ও পরিবার কল্যাণ মন্ত্রণালয়-কে ডাঃ মোঃ মোয়াররফ হোসেন প্রকৃতপক্ষেই তর্কিত ভেন্টিলেটরগুলি সচল করার জন্য কোন পত্র নিমিউ এন্ড টিসি এর চীফ টেকনিক্যাল ম্যানেজারদের দিয়েছেন কিনা সে বিষয়টি সম্পর্কে অধিকতর তদন্তের জন্য স্বাস্থ্য মন্ত্রণালয় (স্বাস্থ্য সেবা বিভাগ), স্বাস্থ্য অধিদপ্তর এবং ক্যান্সার রিসার্স ইনস্টিটিউট-এর উচ্চ পদস্থ তিন জন কর্মকর্তার সমন্বয়ে একটি তদন্ত কমিটি অত্র আদেশ প্রাপ্তির ৭ (সাত) কার্য দিবসের মধ্যে গঠন করে পরবর্তী ১৫ কার্য দিবসের মধ্যে তদন্ত সম্পন্ন করার নির্দেশ দেওয়া হলো । উক্ত তদন্তে যদি ডাঃ মোয়াররফ-এর দাবী সঠিক প্রমাণিত না হয়, সেক্ষেত্রে তার কাছ থেকেও ৫(পাঁচ) লক্ষ টাকা ক্ষতিপূরণ আদায় করতে হবে । আর যদি প্রমাণিত হয় যে তিনি পত্র দিয়েছিলেন কিন্তু নিমিউ এন্ড টিসি-র দায়িত্ব প্রাপ্ত কর্মকর্তা বিষয়টি গোপন করছে, সেক্ষেত্রে সংশ্লিষ্ট সময়ে নিমিউ-এর দায়িত্বপ্রাপ্ত জনাব মোঃ আব্দুল কাইয়ুম (যুগ্ম সচিব, বর্তমানে অবসরপ্রাপ্ত) এবং মোঃ রেজানুর রহমান (যুগ্ম সচিব) প্রত্যেকের নিকট হতে ৫(পাঁচ) লক্ষ টাকা ক্ষতিপূরণ আদায় করতে হবে।

৩l ডাঃ মানস কুমার বসুর বিরুদ্ধে বিভাগীয় ব্যবস্থা গ্রহণের পাশাপাশি ৫ (পাঁচ) লক্ষ টাকা ক্ষতিপূরণ আদায় করতে হবে।
সংশ্লিষ্ট ব্যক্তিগণ ক্ষতিপূরণ প্রদানে ব্যর্থ হলে পিডিআর আইনের বিধান মতে ঐ টাকা আদায় করতে হবে।

৪। অত্র আদালত, রাষ্ট্রীয় অর্থ যথাযথভাবে ব্যয়, স্বচ্ছতা ও জবাবদিহিতা নিশ্চিতের জন্য দেশের সকল পর্যায়ের সরকারী হাসপাতালে চিকিৎসা সামগ্রী ও যন্ত্রপাতি ক্রয় ও রক্ষণাবেক্ষণ নিম্নবর্ণিত নিয়ম-নীতির অনুসরণ করা আবশ্যক মনে করে --

i. চিকিৎসার জন্য যেকোন যন্ত্রপাতি, চিকিৎসা সামগ্রী বা ঔষধ ক্রয়ের পূর্বে অবশ্যই বিশেষজ্ঞ কমিটি দ্বারা সংশ্লিষ্ট প্রতিষ্ঠানের চাহিদা নিরূপন করা; চিকিৎসা সামগ্রী বা যন্ত্রপাতি ক্রয়ের ক্ষেত্রেও বিশেষজ্ঞ কমিটির দ্বারা চাহিদা নিরূপন করে সরকারী ক্রয় বিধিমালা অনুসরণ করে সর্বোচ্চ মান সম্পন্ন চিকিৎসা সামগ্রী/যন্ত্রপাতি ক্রয় করা;

ii, চাহিদা চূড়ান্ত হওয়ার পরে সংশ্লিষ্ট প্রতিষ্ঠানে উক্ত চাহিদা সম্পন্ন যন্ত্রপাতি স্থাপনের জন্য প্রয়োজনীয় অবকাঠামো/ইমারত নির্মাণ প্রয়োজন কিনা তা নিরূপন এবং অবকাঠামো প্রস্তুত হওয়া সাপেক্ষে যন্ত্রপাতি ক্রয় করা;

iii, সংশ্লিষ্ট যন্ত্রপাতি পরিচালনা ও রক্ষনাবেক্ষণের জন্য পর্যাপ্ত সংখ্যক উপযুক্ত কর্মকর্তা/কর্মচারী নিয়োগ প্রদান এবং তাদের প্রশিক্ষণ প্রদান করা। এক্ষেত্রে উল্লেখ করা প্রয়োজন মূল্যবান যন্ত্রপাতি ব্যবহারে কর্মকর্তা/ কর্মচারীদের নিয়োগ রাজস্ব খাতে হওয়া বাঞ্চনীয়, আউট সোর্সিং-এ নয়। কেননা আউট সোর্সিং এ নিয়োগকৃত কর্মকর্তা/কর্মচারীদের কোন জবাবদিহিতা থাকে না;

iv. যন্ত্রপাতি/চিকিৎসা সামগ্রী ক্রয়ের ক্ষেত্রে অবাস্তব ও অতিমূল্য নির্ধারণ করে প্রাক্কলন তৈরী করা হয়; সেক্ষেত্রে প্রাক্কলন তৈরীতে সঠিক ও বাস্তব সম্মত মূল্য নির্ধারণ নিশ্চিত করা;

v. ঠিকাদারের কাছ থেকে যন্ত্রপাতি গ্রহণ বা বুঝে নেয়ার পূর্বে সরবরাহকৃত পণ্যের মান ও গুণ নিশ্চিত করা;

vi. জরুরীভিত্তিতে কোন যন্ত্র ক্রয় ও চালু করার ক্ষেত্রেও একই ভাবে নং i-ii শর্ত পূরণ করা;

vii. প্রতিটি হাসপাতালে সার্বক্ষণিক তদারকির জন্য উচ্চক্ষমতা সম্পন্ন কমিটি করা, যাদের দায়িত্ব হবে যন্ত্রপাতি ও চিকিৎসা সামগ্রির যথাযথ মান নিরীক্ষা করা এবং যন্ত্রপাতিগুলো সার্বক্ষণিকভাবে কার্যকর ও সচল রাখা;

viii. এক্ষেত্রে কোন যন্ত্রপাতি মেরামত কিংবা ওভার হোলিংয়ের প্রয়োজন হলে অবশ্যই উক্ত যন্ত্রপাতি চালু ও রক্ষণাবেক্ষণের দায়িত্ব নিয়োজিত সংশ্লিষ্ট কর্মকর্তা/কর্মচারী অবিলম্বে তার উর্ধতন কর্তৃপক্ষকে নিয়মিতভাবে জানাবেন এবং নির্ধারিত সময়ের মধ্যে উর্ধ্বতন কর্তৃপক্ষ প্রয়োজনীয় পদক্ষেপ গ্রহণ না করলে তদারকির জন্য গঠিত উচ্চ ক্ষমতা সম্পন্ন কমিটিকে বিষয়টি উর্ধ্বতন কর্মকর্তার মাধ্যমে অবহিত করার ব্যবস্থা নিশ্চিত করা;

ix. এ বিষয়ে যথাসময়ে প্রয়োজনীয় পদক্ষেপ গ্রহণ না করা হলে সংশ্লিষ্ট কর্তৃপক্ষ বিষয়টি তদন্ত করে দায় নির্ধারণ করবেন এবং কোন আর্থিক ক্ষতি যার ক��রণে ক্ষতি হবে তার কাছ থেকে ক্ষতিপূরণ আদায়ের ব্যবস্থা করা;

x. এছাড়া প্রতিটি স্থাপিত যন্ত্রের কক্ষের বাহিরে উক্ত যন্ত্রের কর্মদক্ষতা ও মেয়াদকাল লিখিতভাবে উল্লেখ করে দেয়ালে টাঙ্গিয়ে রাখার ব্যবস্থা করা, যাতে যন্ত্রটির মেয়াদকাল এবং বর্তমান অবস্থা দৃশ্যমান থাকে;

xi. উপজেলা, জেলা ও কেন্দ্রীয় পর্যায়ে কমিটি গঠন করা যেতে পারে যন্ত্রপাতিগুলির বিষয়ে সংশ্লিষ্ট কর্তৃপক্ষের নজর থাকে।

৫। দুর্নীতি দমন কমিশন কর্তৃক স্বাস্থ্য খাতে দুনীতি ও অনিয়ম প্রতিরোধে সুপারিশমালা, যা কমিশন কর্তৃক ইতোঃমধ্যে স্বাস্থ্য ও পরিবার কল্যাণ মন্ত্রণালয় পেশ করা হয়েছে, সে বিষয়ে অবিলম্বে প্রয়োজনীয় ব্যবস্থা ও পদক্ষেপ গ্রহণ জরুরী আবশ্যকীয় একটি বিষয়। আদালতের প্রত্যাশা ১। সচিব, স্বাস্থ্য সেবা বিভাগ, স্বাস্থ্য ও পরিবার কল্যাণ মন্ত্রণালয় ও ২। মহা-পরিচালক, স্বাস্থ্য অধিদপ্তর উপরোক্ত বিষয়ে অবিলম্বে যথাযথ পদক্ষেপ গ্রহণ করবেন।

১২. উপরোক্ত পর্যবেক্ষণ ও নির্দেশনা সহ উক্ত রুলটি নিষ্পত্তি করা হলো । তবে খরচের বিষয়ে কোন আদেশ প্রদান করা হলো না।

অবগতি এবং প্রয়োজনীয় ব্যবস্থা গ্রহণের জন্য আদেশের কপি প্রেরণ করা হোক- ১। সচিব, স্বাস্থ্য সেবা বিভাগ, স্বাস্থ্য ও পরিবার কল্যাণ মন্ত্রণালয়, ২। মহা-পরিচালক, স্বাস্থ্য অধিদপ্তর এবং ৩। পরিচালক, ন্যাশনাল ইনস্টিটিউট অব ক্যান্সার রিসার্স এবং হাসপাতাল, মহাখালী, ঢাকা।

 End.

caseno: Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 3980 of 2016
lawyer:
Mr. Md. Ali Reza, Advocate instructed by Syed Mahbubar Rahman, Advocate-on-Record …… For the Petitioner

Mr. Quamrul Hoque Siddique, Senior Advocate instructed by Mr. Mohammad Abdul Hai, Advocate-on-Record ……. For Respondent No. 1

For Respondent Nos.2-6 …….. None represented
parties:
Ganoshasthya Kendra Ashulia ----- Petitioner

-Vs-

AKM Jahangir Khan and others ------- Respondents
case_source: (From the judgment and decree dated the 25th day of July, 2016 passed by the High Court Division in F.M.A.No.217 of 2015)
full_judgment:
Abu Bakar Siddiquee J. This civil petition for leave to appeal is directed against the judgment and decree dated the 25th day of July, 2016 passed by the High Court Division in F.M.A.No.217 of 2015 allowing the appeal.

2. The facts, relevant for disposal of this petition, are that the petitioner as plaintiff filed the Title Suit No.994 of 2012 in the Court of 2nd Joint District Judge, Dhaka alleging, inter alia, that the suit property along with some other non-suited property belongs to Dilbar Pramanik, Out of 21.95 acres land, only 17.21 acres land was purchased by Khetra Mohan Paul and Taherun Nessa on 22.09.1932 by an auction sale through Court. Taherun Nessa exhausted her share of the suit property by selling it to others. The plaintiff purchased the suit land from different person in between 1974-1991 and that it got right, title, interest and possession on the suit land. The defendants having no right, title and interest in the suit property claim title therein which compelled them to institute the suit.

3. The plaintiff filed an application for injunction under Order XXXIX, rules 1 and 2 read with section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure for restraining defendant No.1 from disturbing or dispossessing him from his peaceful possession of the suit property.

4. The respondents as defendants contested the aforesaid application by filing written objection contending, inter alia, that the suit property along with other properties were sold in Rent Execution Case No.269 of 1.932. Taherun Nessa and Khetra Mohan and others partitioned their land among themselves and 7.97 acres land of Plot No.522 fell in saham of Khetra Mohan and the land of Plot No.520 along with the land of other plots fell in the saham of Taherun Nessa Bebi and accordingly, S.A. Khatian No.49 was correctly prepared in their names. 2.92 acres land of C.S. Plot No.522 was acquired by the Government for the construction of Dhaka Aricha Road through L.A. Case No.39/51-52 and that while rest 5.05 acres land of C.S. Plot No.522 remained in possession of Khetra Mohan Paul and others, they transferred the said land to Chan Miah through Registered Sub-kabala Deed dated 20.04.1962 and delivered possession to them. Thereafter, Chan Miah transferred 3.29 acres land to Korpula Bibi by Registered Deed No.329 dated 10.01.1963. While Taherun Nessa and Chan Miah had been in possession of their land of C.S. Plot No.520, they transferred 7.73 acres land to Abdur Rob and others vide Registered Deed No.431 dated 16.01.1993. Korpula Bibi transferred 2.31 acres land to Alhaj Sekender Khan through Registered Sub-kabala Deed Nos.3498, 3499, 3500 and 3502. Korpula Bibi on 25.05.1963 further transferred 0.98 acre land to Mrs. Momtaz Akter Kashem through Deed No.3501. Chan Miah transferred her rest 1.76 acres land to Alhaj Sekander Khan on 24.04.1963 through two Registered Deed Nos.4777 and 4778 and delivered possession of the same to the purchaser. Thereafter, Momataz Akter Kashem transferred 0.98 acre land through a sab-kabala Deed being No.4256 to defendant No.1, A.K.M. Jahangir Khan. The land of CS and SA Plot No.522 was recorded in the name of defendant No.1 and his father, Sekander Khan measuring 0.98 and 4.07 acres respectively and that in R.S.Khatian No.221, the said record of rights was correctly prepared in his name. Thereafter, Alhaj Sakender Khan died leaving behind his wife-Mrs. Tahera Khatun, one son, AKM Jahangir Khan. (the defendant) and four daughters who got their names mutated and they had been in possession of the same one payment of the rents to the Government. Taharun Nessa, wife of Sakender Khan, gifted her property in favour of her four daughters and thereafter passed away leaving son and daughters. Momtaz Begum, daughter of Sakender Khan thereafter expired leaving behind her husband, two daughters and three sisters. Out of 4.07 acres land of late Sekander Khan, defendant No.1, AKM Jahangir Khan, got 1.19 acres land and he also purchased 0.98 acre land from Momtaz Akther through sub-kabala Deed No.4256 dated 11.07.1963 and thus, he acquired 2.17 acres land. Defendant No.1 filed Title Suit No.5733 of 2008 in the Court of Joint District Judge, 6th Court, Dhaka against the co-sharers for partition of their ejmali land and on 25.05.2009, the said suit was decreed on compromise. As per the said decree, 2.17 acres land fell in the saham of defendant No.1 who mutated his name and had been in possession of the said land and had been paying rents regularly to the Government. During B.S. Survey, 2.17 acres land was recorded in the name of defendant No.1 in Plot No.4707 in Khatian No.968 in the field porcha, defendant No.1 constructed a boundary wall on four sides of his 2.17 acres land and constructed three pucca houses therein and he has been in possession of the same by appointing caretaker. Defendant Nos.1-6 previously instituted Title Suit No.325 of 1981 and in the said suit, the plaintiff was impleaded as defendant No.13 and the said suit was decreed in favour of the present defendants. The plaintiffs along with some other miscreants on 03.11.2011 demolished the defendants boundary wall and also constructed semi-pucca houses constructed thereon. The application for injunction is based on a false story and the same is liable to be rejected.

5. The learned Joint District Judge after hearing the parties by the judgment and order dated 27.01.2013 granted injunction restraining defendant No.1 from disturbing the peaceful possession of the plaintiff in the suit property. 6. Being aggrieved by the judgment and decree of the trial Court, the defendant preferred First Miscellaneous Appeal (FMA) No.217 of 2015 before the High Court Division, and the High Court Division after hearing the appeal allowed the same reversing the judgment and order dated 27.01.2013 of the learned Joint District Judge, 2nd Court, Dhaka in Title Suit No.994 of 2012; hence, this petition for leave to appeal.

7. Mr. Md. Ali Reza, learned Advocate, appearing for the petitioner, submits that the High Court Division failed to conceive the points raised in the arguments of the learned Advocate for the plaintiff-respondent appellant in Miscellaneous Appeal No.217 of 2015 and failed to discuss the same in the judgment. He further submits that the High Court Division committed an error of law in considering the facts and legal aspect of the appeal and arbitrarily allowed the appeal setting aside the judgment and order dated 27.01.2013 of the trial Court. He also submits that the High Court Division failed to consider that order No.4 dated 22.04.2010 of Title Execution Case No.5 of 2006 is still valid since the decree-holder, namely, the appellant did not challenge the same in any higher Court and as such, the judgment and order is liable to be set aside. He again submits that the plaintiff filed Title Suit No. 994 of 2012 for declaration about the suit property and the plaintiff stated in his plaint that the defendants had been never in possession of the suit property within the same boundary, the plaintiff would prove the same by producing evidence and that the High Court Division ought to have considered the matter and as such, the judgment and order is liable to be set aside. He further submits that the High Court Division failed to consider that the decree in Title Suit No.325 of 1982 for permanent injunction and the respondent stated in his written objection and written statement that the plaintiff violated the decree and as such, they filed Execution Case No.05 of 2006 and on this aspect, the decree cannot sustain in law and as such, the judgment and order is liable to be set aside.

8. Mr. Quarnrul Hoque Siddique, learned Counsel, appearing for respondent No.1, AKM Jahangir Khan, in his submissions, supported the impugned judgment and order of the High Court Division. He contends that this respondent and others as plaintiff previously instituted Title Suit No.325 of 1981 against the present petitioner and others for permanent injunction and the suit was decreed in favour of the present respondents on being satisfied that they are in possession of the suit property and in the present suit, i.e. Suit No.994 of 2012 the learned Joint District Judge illegally granted injunction restraining the present respondent not to disturb the present petitioner in the suit property which is against the principle of law. He also submits that the present petitioner has got no possession in the suit property and by misrepresenting the facts of the case have obtained the injunction which is not sustainable in law.

9. We have heard the learned Advocates for both the parties, perused the materials on record.

10. It is admitted that Title Suit No.325 of 1981 and Title Suit No.5733 of 2008 were disposed of in between the parties. The learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the defendant-appellant vehemently argued the aforesaid fact of institution of more than one suit earlier operates res judicata and as such, the present Title Suit No.994 of 2012 is not maintainable in its present form. He further submits that no interim injunction can be granted when the suit is found prima facie barred res judicata. It is true that previously when in previous litigations, it is found that the defendant-appellant is the true owner in possession of the property, it is difficult to make an order of equitable relief like injunction.

11. The present defendant-respondent and his other co-sharers (present defendant Nos. 1-6) as plaintiffs instituted Title Suit No.325 of 1981 before the then Sub-ordinate Judge, 2" Court, Dhaka impleading the present plaintiff (as defendant No.13) and others for permanent injunction in respect of 5.05 acres land of C.S Khatian No.32 and C.S and S.A Plot No.522 corresponding to R.S. Khatian No.221 and R.S Plot No.1127. The suit was contested by defendant Nos.7 and 13 (present plaintiff) and the learned Sub-ordinate Judge by his judgment and decree dated 01.03.2001 decreed the suit restraining the present plaintiff from dispossessing or disturbing the plaintiffs of that suit from their peaceful possession of the suit property. The present plaintiff did not move the higher Court against the said judgment and decree with a view to challenge the said decree. Thereafter, defendant No.13 of the aforementioned suit, as plain-tiff, instituted present Title Suit No.994of 2012 impleading the present defendants (plaintiff of the previous suit as defendant Nos.1-6) and prayed for declaration of his title in the suit property and for further declaration that 5.05 acres land of R.S Plot No.1127 of R.S. khatian No. 221 published in the name of Alhaj Sekander Khan is wrong and that the name of the predecessor of the present plaintiff wrongly has been omitted and that the title deeds of the plain-tiff in respect of Kha scheduled land are false, forged and collusive and not binding upon the plaintiff only. In the present suit, the plaintiff-petitioner claims title over 2.56 acres land out of 5.05 acres land of C.S and S.A. Plot No.522 corresponding to R.S. Khatian No.221 and R.S. Plot No.1127. The learned Advocate for the defendant-respondent raised objection to the claim of the plaintiff-petitioner and submitted that the present defendant-respondent claims title over 1.17 acres land out of 5.05 acres land and the rest land of the CS Plot No.522 is in possession of the present plaintiff. In reply to the said submission, the learned Advocate for the defendant-respondent has submitted that it would be evident from the written objection of the plaintiff-respondent filed against the application for injunction that defendant No.1 had filed Title Suit No.5733 of 2008 in the 6th Court of the learned Joint District Judge, Dhaka against his co-sharers for partition and obtained a compromise decree on 25.05.2009 and as per solenama, this 2.17 acres land out of 5.05 acres land has fallen in the saham of this defendant-respondent and the rest land has fallen in the saham of other co-sharers.

12. From the description of the plaint of the present suit, it appears that the present plaintiff-petitioner has claimed his title over 2.56 acres land out of 5.05 acres land which was the subject matter of the previous Title Suit No.325 of 1981 instituted by the present defendant-respondent and other co-sharers for permanent injunction and obtained decree for permanent injunction against the present plaintiff-respondent on 01.03.2001. Thereafter, this defendant brought an allegation that on 15.02.2006 at 7 P.M., the present plaintiff-petitioner forcibly entered into the suit land and took away house container from the decreetal land through a crane and was trying to dis-possess them from the decreetal land.

13. Jurisdiction of the Court to interfere with an order of interlocutory or temporary injunction is purely equitable and, therefore, the Court being approached, will, apart from other considerations, also to look into the conduct of the party invoking the jurisdiction of the Court, and may refuse to interfere unless his conduct was free from blame. Since the relief is wholly equitable in nature, the party invoking the jurisdiction of the Courts to show that he him-self was not at fault and that he himself was not responsible for bringing about the state of things complained of and that he was not unfair or inequitable in his dealings with the party against whom he was seeking relief. These considerations will arise not only in respect of the person who seeks an order of injunction, but also in respect of the party approaching the Court for vacating the ad-interim or temporary injunction order.

14. The learned Joint District Judge allowed the injunction petition relying on the contents of order dated 22.04.2010 and held that from order dated 22.04.2010 passed in Title Execution Case No.05 of 2006 shows that the suit land is in possession of the present plaintiff-petitioner. On careful examining the order dated 22.04.2010, it appears that the defendant-respondent never admitted that the plaintiff-petitioner on 15.02.2006 dispossessed him from the suit land and that defendant is not in possession of the suit property. The plaintiff-petitioner was restrained by a decree for permanent injunction in Title Suit No.325 of 1981 not to evict the defendant-respondent or to disturb his peaceful possession in the suit land. In such circumstances, the trial Court was not justified in granting injunction holding that the defendant-respondent is not in possession of the suit property. But the learned Judges of the High Court Division is very much justified on reversing the judgment and order passed by the learned Joint District Judge. Thus, there is no scope to interfere with the impugned judgment.

15. Considering the entire facts and circumstances of the case, the jurisdiction of granting injunction being an equitable relief, no injunction should be granted at the instance of the plaintiff-petitioner against the defendant-respondent since he has not come with clean hand. We also hold the view that the learned Judge of the High Court Division refused to extend his hand in granting such judicial discretion and as such, there is nothing to interfere into the matter.

16. We find no merit in this leave petition. Accordingly, the civil petition for leave to appeal is dismissed without any order as to costs.

End.

case_source: (From the judgment and decree dated 25.01.2018 passed by the High Court Division in First Appeal No.37 of 2017)
full_judgment:
Abu Bakar Siddiquee J. This civil petition for leave to appeal is directed against the judgment and decree dated 25.01.2018 passed by the High Court Division in First Appeal No.37 of 2017 allowing the appeal.

2. The facts, relevant for disposal of this petition, are that the present respondents as plaintiffs instituted. Title Suit No.94 of 2016 in the Court of Joint District Judge, Barguna for setting aside the ex-parte decree dated 25.09.2012 passed by the First Court of Joint District Judge, Barguna in Title Suit No.10 of 2009. In the suit, the plaintiffs, on 10.01.2017, filed an application for staying further proceedings of Execution Case No.04 of 2016 arising out of Title Suit No.10 of 2009. The learned Judge of the trial Court rejected such application for stay and also dis-missed the suit summarily at this initial stage stating that the suit is not maintain-able. Against such order of dismissal, the plaintiff who was defendant in partition suit being No.10 of 2009 moved before the High Court Division and obtained Rule which was made absolute subsequently. The plaintiff in original suit being No.10 of 2009 as petitioner filed the present petition for leave to appeal. The case of the plaintiffs, in short, is that the suit lands originally belonged to Chhaferuddin, Hochanuddin and others. Their names were correctly recorded in CS Khatian mentioning their respective shares. The said recorded tenants and Hochanuddin while enjoying and possessing the suit land, Hochanuddin died leaving behind two wives, namely, Chhahera Bibi and Kadbhanu Bibi. Kadbhanu Bibi gave birth to one son, namely, Amzat Ali and three daughters, namely, Bibishan, Kulsum and Orful. Other wife, Chhahera Bibi gave birth to two sons, namely, Afchher Ali and Hazrat Ali and 4(four) daughters, namely, Gedi Bibi, Duli Bibi, Barojan, Alekjan. One of the wives, namely, Chhahera Bibi got married to a recorded tenant, Chhaferuddin. The daughter of Hochanuddin named Bibishan died leaving behind 4(four) daughters, namely, Hamida, Rokeya, Rahila and Habibunnessa along with mother named Kadbhanu, one brother Amzad Ali and two sisters, namely, Kulsum and Orful. Kulsum died leaving behind her full sister, Orful Bibi and step brother Hazrat Ali and Orful Bibi died leaving behind only son, Abdur Rahim and only daughter, Chherjan Bibi. Amzad Ali died leaving behind his mother, Kadbhanu, two full sisters, namely, Kulsum and Orful Bibi.

3. Afchher Ali, the son of Hochanuddin, died leaving behind his mother, Chhahera Bibi, full brother, Hazrat Ali and 4(four) full sisters, namely, Gedi Bibi, Duli Bibi, Barojan and Alekjan, Dull Bibi died leaving behind her mother, Chhahera Bibi, one daughter, Kadbhanu (according to plaint), two full brothers, namely, Afchher Ali, Hazrat Ali, three full sisters, namely, Gedi Bibi, Barojan and Alekjan as her legal heirs to inherit her properties. Gedi Bibi died leaving behind her mother, Chhahera Bibi, one daughter, Jamina Khatun, two full brothers, namely, Afchher Ali and Hazrat Ali and two sisters, namely, Barojan and Alekjan. Barojan died leaving behind her heirs. Hazrat Ali inherited the share of Jamina Khatun, daughter of Gedi Bibi. Alekjan (wrongly written "Samettban") Bibi, while enjoying and possessing her share, transferred her entire share in favour of Mohammad. Ali and Azahar Ali, they turned it to Hazrat Ali.

4. Said Hazrat Ali died leaving behind his two sons, namely, Chan Miah (plaintiff No.1), Sona Miah (defendant No.9) and two daughters: plaintiff Nos.2 and 3.

5. One of the purchasers named Ismail died leaving behind wife- Mairam Bibi, one son-Tajem Ali and one daughter-Urfur Bibi as his legal heirs and subsequently, Mairam Bibi died leaving behind her son, Tajem Ali and daughter-Urfur Bibi. Tajem Ali died leaving behind his wife-Chan Baru, and only son-Anowar Hossain. Urfur Bibi died leaving behind her husband, Hazrat Ali and only son, Chan Mia. Chan Baru died leaving behind her second husband named Akon Ali, one son, Anowar Hossain and three daughters, namely, Anowara, Pearu and Golbhanu. Johura Bibi died leaving behind her three sons, namely, Meher Ali, Siddique and Sahar Ali and only daughter, Moyful. Said Meher Ali died leaving behind his wife, two full brothers and only full sister. Said brother, Siddique died leaving behind his wife, Surjoban, full brother, Sahar Ali (wrongly written "Goher") and full sister, Moyful and Moyful transferred her entire share in favour of Kashem and others. Said Sahar Ali died leaving behind his wife, Aysnan Bibi and only son Safej, and two daughter, namely, Azitonnessa and Jobetonnessa.

6. The CS recorded tenant, Chhaferuddin died leaving behind his two wives named Aishan @ Ayna Bibi and Chhahera Bibi, two sons named Kashem and Hashem and one daughter, Fulshan. Said Fulshan, daughter of Chhaferuddin, died leaving behind her mother, Ayna Bibi, two full brothers, Hashem Ali and Kashem Ali. Ayna Bibi died leaving behind her two sons, namely, Kashem Ali and Hashem Ali. Said Hashem Ali died leaving behind his wife, Senai Bibi and only son, Sanu Miah. Kashem Ali died leaving behind his only daughter named Golbhanu.

7. The CS recorded tenant, Yasinuddin while enjoying and possessing his share died leaving behind his mother, Chherbhanu, two full brothers, namely, Dalu and Lalu as his legal heirs. Said Chherbhanu died leaving behind her two sons, namely, Dalu and Lalu. Lalu died leaving behind his four sons, namely, Abdul, Ganjar, Chhattar, Rakmon and two daughters, namely, Bibishan and Sufia. Said recorded tenant, Yasinuddin died leaving behind his heirs, Abdul Jabbar and others and they have instituted Title Suit No.187 of 1977 before the then Munsif (now the Assistant Judge), Barguna and the said suit was dismissed on contest and an appeal bearing No.65 of 1987 was being preferred which had been allowed and the defendants preferred Civil Revision No.2759 of 1996 before the High Court Division and obtained Rule which was discharged on 29.10.2007.

8. Defendant Nos.2, 12, 33-38, 40-42, 69 and 72 contested the suit by filing written statement contending, inter alia, that this suit cannot run in the present form and is barred by limitation and defect of parties. It is also barred by res-judicata. The plaintiff falsely and fraudulently filed the instant snit. 5.76 acres land is in possession of defendant Nos.2/14-35 and others, Defendant No. 37 claimed that he is in possession of .74 acre land. Defendant No.72 contended that he is in possession of .60 acre land and defendant Nos.12, 33/69-71/78 claimed saham of (.60+2.16) =2.66 acres land. Defendant Nos.36/38/40-42 contended that they are in possession of 2.88 acres land. Therefore, the suit is liable to be dismissed with costs.

9. The partition suit being No.10 of 2009 was decreed ex-parte on 25.09.2012 passed by the trial Court. The present respondents as plaintiff filed the present regular suit for setting aside the ex-parte decree dated 25.09.2012 on the ground of non service of summons in which the present respondent filed an application for staying further proceeding of Title Execution Case No.04 of 2016 arising out Title Suit No.10 of 2009. The learned Judge of the trial Court has rejected not only the application for stay but also dis-missed the suit as being non-maintainable.

10. Being aggrieved by the judgment and decree of the trial Court, the plaintiffs preferred First Appeal No.37 of 2017 before the High Court Division, the High Court Division after hearing the appeal allowed the same setting aside the judgment and decree dated 10.01.2017 and thereby restored the original suit being No.94 of 2016.

11. Against the judgment and order of the High Court Division, the defendants filed Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No.1028 of 2018 before this Division seeking leave.

12. Mr. A. J. Mohammad Ali, learned Counsel, appearing on behalf of the petitioners, submits present respondents as plaintiffs instituted Title Suit No.94 of 2016 for setting aside an ex-parte decree on the ground that summonses were not duly served upon them in the original suit and the plaintiffs (present respondents) filed an application for staying the execution proceeding Title Execution being No.04 of 2015 arising out from Titles Suit No. 10 of 2009 and only point for determination for the trial Court to ascertain as to whether the said application for staying would be sustainable. He further submits that the present petitioners as plaintiffs instituted Title Suit No.10 of 2009 in the Court of Joint District Judge, 1st Court, Barguna for partition of the suit lands impleading present respondents and others as defendants. Wherein several sets of the defendants contested the said partition suit including the full brother of present respondent named Sona Miah after receiving the summonses of the Court, but the present respondents (plaintiffs in Title Suit No.94 of 2016) did not contest the said suit though the summonses were duly served upon them and it is evident from the decree of Title Suit No.10 of 2009 that the addresses of all defendants are the same and they are residing in the same mess and the preliminary decree of the said suit made final, but respondent Nos.1-3 instituted subsequent Title Suit No.94 of 2016 long delay and on the mere plea that the summonses were not duly served upon them by suppressing the material facts and as such, the trial Court rightly dismissed the suit, but the High Court Division passed an order of restoration of original suit after setting aside the order of trial Court. The learned Counsel further submits that admittedly the judgment and decree dated 25.09.2012 has been challenged by one defendant named Abdur Rahman in Title Appeal No.69 of 2012 impleading the present defendants as respondent Nos.9-20 in the said title appeal by mentioning their addresses and their summonses have been duly served in the said title appeal, but they are reluctant to proceed with the said appeal and at a stage, the said appeal is dismissed affirming those of the trial Court and accordingly, the preliminary judgment and decree of the trial Court is made final and the defendants of the original partition suit tried to create an obstacle to enjoy the fruit of the said judgment and decree passed in favour of the plaintiffs by filing the vexatious suit and the trial Court rightly dismissed the same, but the High Court Division as the appellate Court without going through materials on record very illegally restored the original suit being No.10 of 2009 after setting aside the well-founded judgment and decree. He finally submits that Title Suit No.94 of 2016 is not maintainable without challenging the final decree passed in Decree Execution Case No.04 of 2016 arising out of judgment and decree dated 25.09.2012 passed in Title Suit No.10 of 2009; the High Court Division ought to have considered the said moot question in deciding First Appeal No.37 of 2017, but most illegally set aside the judgment and decree of the trial Court by the judgment and decree dated 25.01.2018.

13. Mr. Parietal Chandra Guha, learned Advocate, appearing on behalf of the respondents, in his submissions, supported the impugned judgment and order of the High Court Division.

14. We have heard the learned Advocates of both the parties and perused the materials on record.

15. Title Suit No.10 of 2009 was a partition suit instituted by the present petitioners as plaintiffs against the present respondents, Chan Miah and others and that summonses and notices were alleged to have been duly served upon all the defendants of that suit and thereafter, the suit has been decreed against defendant Nos.12/33/61-- -71/78/72/36/38/80-42/37 on contest and ex-parte against the rests. The defendant (in Title Suit No.94 of 2016) i.e. present petitioners have come with an allegation that the allegation regarding non-service of summons does not hold any water whereas present respondents, Chart Mia and others filed Title Suit No.94 of 2016 claiming that due to non-service of summons decree passed in Title Suit No.10 of 2009 is illegal, inoperative and liable to be set aside.

16. Mr. A.J. Mohammad Ali, learned Senior Advocate, appearing on behalf of the present petitioners argued that although on the ground of non-service of summons, defendant Nos.1 to 3 of Title Suit No.10 of 2009 instituted Title Suit No.94 of 2016 against the present petitioners, but they were duly served with summonses and notices. He further adds that the brother of plaintiff No.1, Chan Mia appeared and contested Title Suit No.10 of 2009 whereas the three plaintiff-respondent demanded that they were not ever served with summonses and notices. He further adds that Title Suit No.94 of 2016 was filed beyond the statutory period of limitation and as such, that suit is hopelessly barred by limitation. He also argued that Title Suit No.94 of 2016 is not maintainable without challenging the final decree passed in Decree Execution Case No.04 of 2016 arising out of judgment and decree dated 25.09.2012 passed in Title Suit No.10 of 2009 and as an appellate Court, the High Court Division ought to have considered the said moot question in deciding First Appeal No.37 of 2017, but most illegally setting aside the judgment and decree of the trial Court by the judgment and decree dated 25.01.2018 and as such, the judgment and order of the High Court Division is liable to be set aside.

17. According to the procedure, an ex-parte decree can be impeached in three distinct ways:-

l. By filing a miscellaneous case under Order IX Rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure.

2. By filing an appeal before the appellate Court.

3. By filing a regular suit in the trial Court.

18. There plaintiff-respondents have chosen the third category intending to assail the impugned ex-parte decree, that is, the plaintiff-respondent filed a regular suit on the ground of non-service summons and notices upon them. The learned trial Court has opined in the initial stage that the present suit is not maintainable. It has been further opined that the plaintiff-respondent earlier preferred an appeal bearing No.69 of 2012 which has been dismissed subsequently and that whenever an execution proceeding has been started, the plaintiff-respondents have initiated this malafide suit for setting aside the ex-parte decree on the flimsy ground of non-service of summons. It has been revealed that the ground of dismissal should be determined after taking or recording evidence. The learned Judge of the Division Bench of the High Court Division held the view that in any way, the suit cannot be dismissed on such ground of maintainability at initial stage. It has been further held that the learned Judge of the Court below dismissed the suit at his own initiative, but the reason assigned will not come within the ambit of Order-VII, rule 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure (briefly as the Code). So the impugned judgment and order is illegal and caused a serious miscarriage of justice.

19. For the convenience of understanding the provisions of Order VII, rule 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure can be reviewed which reads as under:

"Rule ll-The plaint shall be rejected on the following issues:

(a) Where it does not disclose a cause of action.

(b) Where the relief claimed is under-valued, and the plaintiff, on being required by the Court to correct the valuation within a time to be fixed by the court fails to do so;

(c) Where the relief claimed is properly valued, but the plaint is written upon paper insufficiently stamped and the plaintiff, on being required by the Court to supply the requisite stamp-paper within a time to be fixed by the Court, fails to do so.

(d) Where the suit appears from the statement in the plaint to be barred by any law"

20. On perusal of the materials on record, it transpires that the plaintiffs (defendant in Title Suit No.10 of 2009) instituted Title Suit No.94 of 2016 for setting aside the ex-parte decree on the ground that summonses were not served upon them in that suit. The only point assigned in the impugned judgment and order is whether the execution case of the former suit should be stayed or not? But the learned Judge of the trial Court in course of deciding the fate of stay petition has dismissed the suit summarily. The learned Judge of the trial Court finds in the following verbatim:-

“বিজ্ঞ কৌশুলীর বক্তব্য শুনিলাম। নথি সমূহ পর্যালোচনায় দেখা যায় মূল দেং ১০/২০০৯ তে এই বাদীপক্ষ বিবাদী শ্রেণীভুক্ত ছিল। তারা ছিল ১/৩/৪নং মূল বিবাদী মূল নথি দৃষ্টে দেখা যায়। ১৬/০৭/২০০৯ইং তারিখে তাদের উপর যথারীতি সমন/নোটিশ জারী হলে তারা প্রতিদ্বন্বিতা করে। নথি দৃষ্টে আরো দেখা যায় যে, নোটিশ জারী হওয়ায় ত বৎসর পরে বাদী প্রতিদ্বন্দিতা বিবাদীপক্ষ প্রতিদন্বিতা করিয়াছে। ফলে দোতরফা সূত্রে ডিক্রী হয় বিগত ইং ২৫/০৯২০১২ তারিখে নিষ্পত্তি আপীল ৬৯/২০১২ দায়ের হইলে ২৩/১০/২০১৪ তারিখে মুল দেং ১০/২০০৯ মোকদ্দমার রায় ডিক্রী জারী মোকদ্দরার কার্যক্রম সম্পন্ন হয় এবং উহা পূর্ন সন্তষ্টিতে নিষ্পত্তি হয়। এমতাবস্থায় অদ্যকার দাখিলী দরখাস্তখানা সরাসরি নামঞ্জুর করা হইল। উপরোক্ত পর্যালোচনার আলোকে মোকদ্দমাটি গ্রহনযোগ্যতা নাই মর্মে প্রতীয়মান হওয়ায় তা খারিজ যোগ্য। কোর্ট ফি সঠিক । অতএব, আদেশ হয় যে, অন্র দেওয়ানী মোকদমাটি গ্রহণযোগ্যতা শুনানী অন্তে সরাসরি খারিজ করা হইল ।”

21. Now the question that falls for determination as to how far the trial Court is justified in dismissing the suit summarily in course of deciding an application for staying the further proceeding of Title Execution No.04 of 2015.

22. In this respect, the learned Judge of the High Court Division has observed in the following verbatim:-

"Now coming to clause (d) of rule 11 of the order 7 it appears that clause (d) of the rule authorizes the rejection of a plaint when the suit appears from the statements in the plaint to be barred by any law. This clause applies when it appear from the statements in the plaint that the suit is barred but it has no application where there is no clear or specific admission in the plaint suggesting that the suit is barred. This clause is attracted only when on the admitted facts as appearing from the plaint itself the suit is prima facie barred. As for instance when from the statements made in the plaint it appears that the cause of action arose beyond the period of limitation fixed under the statute and no indication is given that limitation has been saved, the plaint may be rejected. In a proper case, when it appears to be barred by limitation, the plaint may be allowed to be amended without rejection. It is not mandatory for the Court to reject the pliant. It may ask the plaintiff to amend it so as to make suit maintainable. Where the plaintiff failed to comply with such an order, the Court may reject the plaint. Reference may be made to the cases reported in 18 CWN 1340 AIR 1928 Oudh 495 and AIR 1953 Ca1.222. "

23. The learned Judge of the Division Bench of the High Court Division further observed that the learned trial Court below without considering the materials on record as well as prevailing law of the land dismissed the suit and thereby committed an error of law and as such, the order of the trial Court is liable to be interfered with. The Division Bench of the High Court Division further held that the dismissal order in its entirety is not well founded in the facts and circumstances of the case and as such, the preponderant judicial views emerging out of the authorities led us to hold that the judgment and decree of the trial Court suffers from legal infirmities which calls for interference by this Court.

24. We have gone through the finding and decisions of the learned Judge of the Division Bench of the High Court Division. Since the dismissal order passed by the trial Court does not come under the mischief under Order VII, rule 2 of the Code of Civil Procedure, we have no option but to agree with the finding and decision of the learned Judge of the High Court Division. We also hold the view that the learned Judges of the High Court Division have made threadbare discussion about the facts and circumstances of the case and so also relevant law and left no stone unturned in deciding the appeal and there is no legal infirmity or misreading or non-consideration of evidence on record.

25. The question of limitation is also a mixed question of fact and law and as such, it is not wise to dispose of this issue on the score of rejection of plaint at an initial stage of the suit.

26. Having considered those facts and circumstances, materials on record, we find no illegality and infirmity in the impugned judgment.

27. Therefore, we find no reason to interfere with the decision and findings of the High Court Division.

28. Accordingly, this civil petition is dis-missed without any order as to costs.

End.

case_source: (From the judgment and order dated the 3rd day of August, 2008 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No.2728 of 2006)
full_judgment:
Muhammad Imman Ali, J.: This civil appeal, by leave, is directed against the judgment and order dated 03.08.2008 passed by a Single Bench of the High Court Division in Civil Revision No.2728 of 2006 discharging the Rule. 

2. The facts of the case, in short, are that the appellant herein and others as plain-tiffs filed Other Class Suit No.131 of 1997 before the Senior Assistant Judge, 1st Court, Chattogram for partition. They contended, inter alia, that the land described in the schedule to the plaint has been finally published in R.S. Khatian No.291 with the name of Anu Mia being an owner of the properties, who sold 44 decimal land to Ashu Mia, the predecessor of the plaintiffs by registered deed No.724 dated 31.01.1954. The plaintiffs obtained total 58% decimal land and have been owning and possessing the suit land. The defendants have no right, title and interest in the suit land of the plaintiffs. On 19.09.1997 when the defendants denied to partition the said land from the jote, the cause of action arose and hence, the plain-tiffs filed the suit. 

3. Defendant Nos. l-4 contested the suit by filing a written statement denying all material averments made in the plaint. They contended, inter alia, that the plaintiffs have no right, title and interest over the suit land. Moreover, the deed in question, which was registered on 04.02.1954 did not create any title in favour of the plaintiffs in the suit land because there is no similarly between the land in question in schedule No.1 to the plaint and the land described in the schedule to the deed. The defendants and their predecessor never sold the suit land to the plaintiffs' predecessor and the defendants have been in possession of the suit land, hence the plaintiffs' suit should be dismissed. 

4. Upon hearing the parties and considering the evidence and materials on record the learned Senior Assistant Judge, Patiya, Chattogram, by the judgment and decree dated 06.10.2005 decreed the suit. Being aggrieved the defendants preferred Other Class Appeal No.565 of 2005 in the Court of learned District Judge, Chattogram. On transfer, the appeal was heard by the learned Additional District Judge, Bankruptcy Court, Chattogram, who by the judgment and decree dated 18.06.2006 allowed the appeal and set aside the judgment and decree passed by the trial Court. Then the plaintiffs preferred Civil Revision No.2728 of 2006 before the High Court Division and obtained Rule, which upon hearing the parties was discharged. Being aggrieved plaintiff No.1 filed Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No.2044 of 2008 and leave was granted to consider the following grounds of the learned Advocate for the petitioner: 
"I. That the petitioner did not seek partition of the tank which is in Khatian No.202 in Plot Nos.124, 125, 131 and on receiving the written statement, made it clear by an amendment of the plaint that the tank has not been incorporated in the schedule of the plaint as it has been peacefully possessed by the co-sharers jointly and the appellate Court by misreading of those arrived at a finding that all the co-sharers have not been impleaded in the suit and observed “বিবাদী পক্ষে কথিত ২০২ নং খতিয়ানে ১২৪/১২৫/১৩১ দাগে ভূমি জলে পড়ে দিঘী। এখানে ২০০ জনের উপরে শরীক আছে। দিঘীর পরিমান ১০—কানি। আছু মিঞার অন্দরে ভূমি পরিমাণ ৩—গন্ডা বাকী সম জোতের উক্ত শরীকগণকে পক্ষ করেননি বলে অত্র আদালতে বিবেচনায় মূল মোকদ্দমা পক্ষভাবে দোষে দুষ্ট হবে।”and the High Court Division committed an error of law in not considering the fact that the finding of the appellate Court is perverse, which affected the merit of the case. II. That the appellate Court further observed in its finding that 
“বাদীপক্ষের স্বীকারোক্তি মতেই নালিশী ১৩২ দাগের ১৮ শতক ১১৫ দাগে ৪১ শতক ভূমি পুকুর শ্রেণী ভূমি। উক্ত পুকুর ভরাট না করে ভাগ বন্টন করা সম্ভব নহে—পুকুর শেনী ভূমি ভাগ বন্টনযোগ্য হওয়ায় মূল মোকদ্দমা ডিসমিস যোগ্য বটে। আমার এইরুপ সিদ্ধান্ত বসন্ত কুমার বনাম মতিলাল ১৫ সি.ডব্লিউ.এন ৫৫৫ এবং নিত্য গোপাল বনাম প্রানকৃষ্ণ সি.ডব্লিউ.এন ৪৩৯ মোকদ্দমা দ্বায়ের নজিরের উপর নির্ভরশীল” and the High Court Division committed an error of law not to interfere with the judgment and decree of the appellate Court as the finding is not based on the material evidence on record." 

5. This appeal was heard using virtual means under the provisions of the আদালত কর্তৃক তথ্য-প্রযুক্তি ব্যবহার আইন, ২০২০।

6. Mr. Abdus Sobhan, learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the appellant made submissions in line with the grounds upon which leave was granted. In addition the learned Advocate submitted that the evidence on record itself speaks that one Anu Mia originally owned and possessed the property in schedule No.1 and the R.S. record of rights khatian No.291 was finally published, (Exhibit 2 Series) and the property of schedule No.2 also belonged to Anu Mia and others whose names appear in the R.S. record of rights finally published (Exhibit-2 Series) and who sold 44 decimals land to the predecessors of the plaintiff by deed No.724 registered on 04.02.1954 (Exhibit-3) and the plaintiffs produced B.S. Khatian No. 254 (C.C) and Asu Mia Majhi, predecessor of the plain-tiffs also purchased 141/3 decimals land by Exhibit-3 from Plot Nos.106/115/112 shown in schedule No.2 and in such a way the plaintiffs owned and are possessing 44 + 14 1/3 = 581/3 decimals land in both the schedules and sought partition and the High Court Division by misreading of those erroneously affirmed the finding of the appellate Court. He submitted that the predecessor of the plaintiffs and subsequently the plaintiffs themselves are in possession of the said quantum of land by virtue of the said sale deed (Exhibit-3) and the record of rights (Exhibit-2 series) on payment of usual taxes to the government, and in such circumstances the finding of possession of the, Court of first appeal was made through inadvertence and the High Court Division committed an error of law to give emphasis of the finding of possession of the Court on first appeal without considering the relevant aspects of possession. 

7. Mr. Abdus Salam Mamun, learned Advocate appearing for respondent No.1(a)-1(j) made submissions in support of the impugned judgment and order of the High Court Division. He further submitted that the petitioner is entitled to 22 decimals land in 1/3rd share of 66 decimals land in the schedule No.1 to the sale Deed No.724 dated 04.02.1954, Ext3 and not 44 decimals land as claimed by the plaintiffs in the schedule No.1 to the plaint based on the schedule No.1 to the said sale deed and decree by the trial Court for 44 decimals in schedule No.1 to the plaint is erroneous. He also submitted that in schedule No.1 to the sale deed. No.724 dated 04.02.1954, Ext-3, on the basis of which the appellant has made his claim has specifically provided that “উক্ত বশত ভিটায় আপনার সাবেক দখালি ঘর দখল মতে থাকিবেন” and the appellant is not entitled to make extension of the dwelling house and possession in the homestead making contrary claim in the partition suit. He submitted that the quantum of the land to which the petitioner is entitled in schedule No.1 to the sale deed No.724 dated 04.02.19 54, Ext-3 has to be determined first in a properly framed title suit. The learned Advocate submitted that the judgment and decree of the trial Court is based on surmises and conjectures and the appellate Court has committed no error of law in allowing the appeal and dismissing the suit and the revisional Court has committed no error of law in upholding the judgment and decree of the appellate Court. 

8. We have considered the submissions of the learned Advocates for the parties concerned, perused the impugned judgment and order of the High Court Division and other connected papers on record.

9. There was a claim and counter claim with regard to the fraction/share of land mentioned iii the schedule of deed No.724 registered on 04.2.1954. On direction from this Court the original volume containing the deed in question was transmit-ted to this Court by the (office of the District Registrar, Chattogram. On perusal of the volume and the deed in question, it transpires that the deed was created by Anu Miah Majhi, in favour of Asu Mia Majhi on 31.01.1954 and registered on 04.2.1954. The quantum of land sold is in total 58 1/3 decimals. Out of that lad, the disputed quantum of 44 decimals of R.S. Khatian No.291 is under the scanner. 

10. The first schedule of the deed reads as follows: 
“তপশীল (১) মৌংগৈড়লা থানা-পটিয়া মহল ২৪৫৯ নং তাং-রঘুরাম মতওলী মং মনিরুজ্জমা সওদাগর অধিনে আমার কায়মি রায়তি স্বত্ত্বীয় খাস দখল RS ২৯১/খং ১৩১/১৩২/১৩৩/ দাং পিছনের পুনি ও ১০১/দাং বশত বাড়ী ১/৩ অংশে মোং ৪০ শঃ ও ডেহরী ঘরের পশ্চিম ১০১/- দাং আং ১/২ অংশে কুড়িয়া তালা ভিটা মোং ৪শঃ মোট 8৪ শতক মং ২/১ আনা জমা সেস সহ উক্ত বশত ভিটায় আপনার সাবেক দখলি ঘর দখল মতে থাকিবেন।
 
11. The defendants claim that in the second schedule to the deed registered on 04.02.1954 the total land is 46 decimals of which the plaintiffs claim 1/3 that is 14 1/3 decimals. In the same way the predecessor of the defendants sold only 1/3 of the total land of khatian No. 291 that is 22 decimals out of total 66 decimals. Hence, the plaintiffs claim to title over remaining 44 decimals is false. 

12. We find from the deposition of P.W.1 that he claims that his predecessor purchased 13 decimals land from plot No.101 and 31 decimals land from plot Nos.131/132/133 which is correctly reflected in the 1st schedule of deed No.724. And the second schedule is in respect of 14 1/3 decimals land. But the record of rights wrongly shows a lesser quantum of land in the name of his father. The plaintiffs thus claimed saham for 58 1/3 decimals land. 

13. In his deposition defendant No.1 deposing as D.W.1 stated that in R.S. khatian No. 291 from plot Nos. 131, 132,133 and 101 his father sold only 1/3, i.e. 22 decimals by deed No. 724, and the plaintiffs have no claim to the remaining 44 decimals land. The trial Court accepted that the plaintiffs claim to title over 5873 decimals land is supported by the kabala Ext.3. On the other hand, the appellate Court observed that the schedule in the sale deed is self-contradictory because the plaintiffs' predecessor purchased only 'hot' the land detailed in the schedule 1 of the deed and, therefore, they could claim only 22 decimals land out of 66 decimals. It was also observed that in the B.S. khatian it is stated that the land sold is 1/3. The appellate Court also found defect of party and hotchpot. 

14. The High Court Division did not decide the issues regarding defect of party and hotchpot. But relied upon decisions of this Division to the effect that the findings of the appellate Court as the last court of fact are binding on the revisional, Court. However, the High Court Division did not consider the cited decisions of this Division where it has been held that a suit for partition will not be defeated for reason of defect of party and hotchpot. On the point of the quantum of land for which saham was claimed, the High Court Division followed the appellate Court's reasoning and held that the plaintiffs could not get saharn for 44 decimals in respect of '/3 Share of the plaintiffs' predecessor. 

15. We have scrutinised deed No.724. We may point out that the certified copy on record is same as the volume transmitted by the Registrar, Chattogram. We find that both the appellate Court and the High Court Division misread Schedule-1 of the deed. The reference to 1/3 share does not refer to the total quantum of land mentioned in that schedule but only to 1/3 of plot No.101 homestead. The reference to 40 decimals is the sun total of land of plot Nos. 131/132/133 plus 1/3 of the homestead of plot No. 101. In addition there is a further 4 decimals land of plot No. 101 to the west of the Dehari Ghar being 1/2 portion of "Kuria tala bhita". So, the land sold in the first schedule is neither 1/3 of 66 decimals nor 2/3 of 66 decimals as surmised by the High Court Division. 

16. In view of the above discussion, we find that the decisions of the appellate Court and the High Court Division are based on misreading of the schedule to the concerned deed of sale. 

17. The issues relating to defect of party and hotchpot are covered by the decisions of this Division as cited before the High Court Division. We need not revisit those here. 

18. Accordingly, we find merit in the appeal which is allowed, without however, any order as to costs. The impugned judgment and order is set aside. The judgment and decree of the trial Court is restored. 

End.

caseno: First Miscellaneous Appeal No. 57 of 2002 with (Civil Rule No. 156 (FM) of 2002).
lawyer:
Mohammad Ali Khan, Advocate------For the Appellants. 
Arun Kumar Battachira, Advocate------For the Respondents.
parties:
Ershad Ali (Md) and another ------ Appellants
Vs.
Rampada Das & others ------ Respondents
full_judgment:
Md Abdur Rashid J: Purchaser (pre-emptee) presented the appeal against an order dated 11-12-2001 passed by the Subordinate Judge. Court No.2 at Jessore in Miscellaneous Case No.1 of 2000, which allowed pre-emption.

2. Respondent No. 1 on 2-9-97 made an application under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 being Miscellaneous Case No. 25 of 1997 for pre-emption of transfer of the case land measuring about 2.89 acres of land appertaining to SA Khatian Nos. 589 and 596 fully described in the schedule to the application. The case was then renumbered as aforesaid Miscellaneous Case No. 1 of 2000.

3. In the application, it is stated that SA Khatian Nos. 589 and 596 of mouje Helanchi under Thana Monirampur were recorded in the names of Eshan Chandra Das, Hazari Das, Rajbihari Das, Satish Chardra Das, Panchamoni Dasi and Sudhir Das in their specified shares. While jointly possessing his shares, Satish Chandra Das died leaving three sons, namely, the pre-emptor and respondent Nos. 2 and 3 (opposite party Nos. 4 and 5 in the application).

4. Besides, Panchamoni Dasi exhausted her interest in the holdings by transfer to the pre-emptor said respondent Nos.2 and 3 and Purnima Rani and Subola Rani Dasi and delivery of possession thereof.

5. Other co-sharer Hazari Das died leaving three sons namely, Durgapada, Kalipada Das and respondent No. 4 (Opposite party No.6 in the application). Kalipada Das already transferred his interest to the pre-emptor and Durga Das to said respondent No.4, Eshan Chandra Das died leaving his wife Hazu Rani Dasi as his only legal representative, Rajbihari Das also exhausted his interest in the' holdings by transfers to the pre-emptor and others. As per wish of Eshan Chandra Das on the death of Hazu Bala the pre-emptor and respondent Nos.2 and 3 inherited her share. Thus, the pre-emptor became co-sharer in the holdings both by inheritance as well as purchase.

6. Sudhir Kumar Das, opposite party No.3 in the application, by a registered deed being No.4715 dated 2-6-97 transferred the case land to the appellants at a consideration of Taka 3,00,000 without service of any notice upon the co-sharers and behind their back. On 13-8-97 obtaining certified copy of the impugned sale deed she became sure about the transfer and deposited in Court the consideration money along with statutory compensation for pre-emption of the case land.

7. Appellants opposed the application by filing a written objection. They admitted that said SA Khatian No. 589 and 596 were finally published recording the names of said Ehsan Chandra Das, Hazari Das, Rajbihari, Satish Chandra Das and Panchamoni Dasi and Sudhir Das to the extent of their respective shares.

8. Their further case is that Hazari, Rajbihari and Satish Das got the interest of Panchamani Dasi, After death of Satish Das his interest devolved upon Rampada Das (pre-emptor). Shyamapada and Joyanta, and after death of Hazari Lal Das his interest devolved upon his three sons, namely, Durgapada, Shibpada and Kalipada. After death of Eshan Das his share devolved upon his wife Hazubala. Hazubala transferred 1.8425 acres of land to Sudhir Kumar Das by a deed dated 30-6-80. Sudhir Kumar Das got his name mutated in Miscellaneous Case No. 45/IX-I/79- 80 and No.317/ IX-I/82-83 and possessed accordingly. As Sudhir Das possessed his entire land inherited and purchased under khatian No. 1102 and the pre-emptor was not a co-sharer in such khatian the pre-emptor was not entitled to pre-empt the impugned transfer.

9. They claimed that as the pre-emptor already disposed of all his land Including his share in the homestead and ceased to have any interest in the holdings; the application for pre-emption was therefore not maintainable.

10. Joyanta, brother of the pre-emptor along with the pre-emptor, mediated the sale by said opposite party No.3, Sudhir Kumar Das to the appellants. Price of the land was settled at Taka 5,00,000 and value of shallow machine, trees, etc. at Taka 1,50,000 and on 1-6-97 they paid Taka 6,50,000. As the pre-emptor assured them not to pre-empt the transfer, the price of the land was written in the deed at Taka 3,00,000 only.

11. On the pleadings following issues were settled: (a) Was the case maintainable in the manner and form as framed? (b) Was the case barred by limitation? (c) Was the case bad for defect of parties? (d) Was the case hit by principles of waiver and acquiescence? (e) Was the pre-emptor entitled to pre-empt the transfer dated 2-6-97 ? (f) What relief the pre-emptor was entitled to?

12. In support of his case, the pre-emptor examined three witnesses including himself. The appellant also examined three witnesses including himself. The appellants also examined three witnesses including appellant No.1, Copy of impugned sale deed dated 2-6-97 was marked as Exhibit-1 while the documents of the appellants were marked as Exhibit 'Ka' to 'Cha'.

13. Upon the evidence oral and documentary on record learned Subordinate Judge found that the. pre-emptor was a co-sharer in the holding while the appellants strangers; the application for pre-emption was not barred by limitation and not bad for defect of parties; the appellants failed to prove their case that the right of pre-emption was barred by principles of waiver and acquiescence and the order dated 16-10-79 passed in Miscellaneous Case No. 45/IX-I/79-80 opening new Khatian No. 1102 was not valid for want of service of notice upon Satish Chandra Das (father of the pre-emptor) and order dated 17-2-83 passed in 317/IX-I/82-83 did not, in fact, open any khatian, and would not be binding upon the pre-emptor.

14. Upon such findings, learned Subordinate Judge allowed the application for pre-emption by impugned judgment and order.

15. Mr Mohammad Ali Khan, learned Advocate for the appellants, challenged the order on various grounds.

16. Firstly, he submitted that in view of said orders passed in Miscellaneous Case No. 45/IX- I/79-80 and 317/IX-I/82-83 opening new khatians in the name of Sudhir Kumar Das in respect of his entire land and payment of rents on the basis of such khatian the pre-emptor was not entitled to pre-empt the impugned transfer since he was not a co-sharer in any of such holdings.

17. In support he cited case of Md Jabed All and others vs Rakhal Chandra Mandal and others 33 DLR (AD) 309; Abdur Rouf vs Ahmuda Khatun. 33 DLR (AD) 323; Md Rais Ali vs Imam Hossain and others. 33 DIR 318; Chandra Kumar vs Abdul Motaleb 19 DLR (SC) 36 and Md Khairullah Bhuiyan vs Haji Nurul Alam, 35 DLR (AD) 338.

18. In the written objection, it is stated that Sudhir Kumar Das possessed his shares by separa- tion and amalgamation in Miscellaneous Case No. 45/IX-I/79-80 and under new Khatian No. 1102. Then, after purchase of 1.8425 acres of land from Hazubala he got his name again separated and amalgamated in Miscellaneous Case being No. 317/IX-I/82-83. Consequently, the pre-emptor who was not a co-sharer in such separated and amalgamated holdings was not entitled to pre-empt.

19. Appellant No.1 as OPW-1 deposed in support of such case. He said that appellant No.2 was his younger brother. Hazubala transferred 1.8425 acres to Sudhir Kumar Das. Sudhir Das got that land mutated in his name in Miscellaneous Case No. 317/IX-I/82-83. Sudhir Das also got his name mutated in Miscellaneous Case No.45/IX-I/79-S0. The pre-emptor was not a co-sharer in such mutated holdings. He did not see as to whether those mutated Khatians were mentioned in the impugned sale deed. He however denied that Sudhir Das did not file Miscellaneous Case No. 45/IX.-1/79-80 and obtained an antedated order therein.

20. Orders passed in Miscellaneous Case No. 45/IX-1/79-80 and No. 317/IX-I/82-S3 were adduced as Exhibit 'Ka' and 'Ka-1'. Four rent receipts were also adduced as Exhibit 'Gha' to 'Gha-3'. Of them, Exhibit 'Gha-2' and 'Gha-3' show payment of rents under impugned khatian No.1102. None of the rent receipts was proved by any witness. Even OPW-1 Ershad Ali in his deposition did not claim that Sudhir Das or anybody else ever paid rents under such Khatians No.1102 or 1134.

21. By ex parte order dated 16-10-79, Exhibit- 'Ka' the Circle Officer (Rev) at Manirampur allowed separation and amalgamation of said SA Khatian Nos. 589 and 596 and opened new Khatian No. 1102 in respect of 2.46 acres of land in the name of Sudhir Kumar Das. By another ex parte order dated 17-2-83 Exhibit-'Ka-1' the Circle Officer (Rev) purportedly again allowed separation and amalgamation of 1.8425 acre of land in the name of said Sudhir Kumar Das. But, in the orders space meant for writing Khatian No. and amount of rent is found vacant. No other evidence is found on record to prove that said Khatian No. 1134 was at all opened by said Circle Officer.

22. OPW 2 brought the record of said miscellaneous cases. After perusal of the record of mutation proceedings the learned Subordinate Judge found that return of the notice does not show that Satish Chandra Das, father of the pre-emptor, received the notice and/or anybody else received the notice on his behalf. We have also examined the undated return of the notice of Miscellaneous Case No. 45/IX-1/79-80 by one Md Mojam Ali, peon Exhibit-'Uma (Uma)' and find that the notice was not at all served upon Satish Chandra Das, father of the pre-emptor. We could not find any notice of other mutation case in the record. Sudhir Kumar Das has not been examined. Nor any explanation was furnished for his non-examination.

23. OPW 3 Santosh Kumar Das proved the agreement which is marked as Exhibit 'Gha' and 'Cha(1)' for sale of shallow machine, trees, etc.

<u>24. It is now well settled by good authorities including those cited above that the pre-emptor must not only have a subsisting interest in the holding when he makes the application for pre-emption. but must continue to hold such interest until disposal of such proceeding for pre-emption. And a co-sharer means a person whose interest subsists throughout the course of the proceedings for pre-emption and not a person who had such interest in the holding at the time of making the application but lost it before disposal of the case. A fresh interest acquired at a later stage cannot be tacked on the interest held at the commencement of the proceeding but lost during the proceeding; Cf: Chandra Kumar vs Abdul Motaleb, 19 DLR (SC) 36 and Mofizuddin Patwari vs Abdul Hakim and others, 33 DLR (AD) 305.</u>

<u>25. Secondly, if the record of rights is changed by way of mutation in accordance with the procedure laid down in law by a valid order before the commencement of the -proceeding for pre-emption the pre-emptor must be held to cease to have any interest in the holding. When such mutation was ordered after service of notice upon the pre-emptor such order would be binding upon him. But if mutation brought about without any service of notice upon the pre-emptor, such sub-division of the holding would not be binding upon the pre-emptor. In Md Jabed Ali and others vs Rakhal Chandra Mandai and others 33 DLR (AD) 309, the Appellate Division held that-</u>

" ...when ,an order is passed, by competent Revenue Officer under section 117 (of the State, Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950) and the order is in conformity with the statutory requirements and the order has been given effect by the co-sharer tenants of the holding the holding stands separated under the law"

26. So, in order to bind and/or disentitle the pre-emptor to pre-empt, the order separating and/ or subdividing the existing holding must be shown to have been passed by a competent authority after compliance with the law namely, after due service of notice upon all co-sharer tenants of the holding and such separation must be given effect to or acted upon by such tenants.

27. It is also needless to say, in deciding an application for pre-emption limited jurisdiction of the Court is now well recognised to examine as to whether or not subdivision of the existing holding in question is valid.

28. In the case ,before us we find there was an order passed by the revenue authority for opening a new khatian being No. 1102 in respect of 2.46 acres of land ata jama of Taka 4.30. As found already, the order was passed without any service of notice upon Satish Chandra Das, father of the pre-emptor. Moreover, no evidence could be adduced that such order and/or subdivision of the holdings was acted upon by the co-sharer tenants of the holdings. Payment of rents on the basis of such mutation Khatian by the co-sharer tenants over a period of seventeen year; could not be proved.

<u>29. Last but not the least, vendor Sudhir Kumar Das transferred the land of Khatian Nos. 589 and 596 and the appellants purchased the same land of said holdings. Mere reading of the deed clearly evidences the intention of the appellants to purchase land of impugned khatians not new Khatian No. 1102. Now, sections 91 and 92 of the Evidence Act would not permit them to introduce any other intention of the parties to disentitle pre-emption.</u>

30. Mr Mohammad All Khan submitted that in case of pre-emption unless necessity for pre- emption could be proved the pre-emptor would not be entitled to pre-emption. In support, he relied upon aforesaid Ahmed Hossain and others vs Basharat Hossain and others 32 DLR (AD) 54.

31. In the application for pre-emption, the pre- emptor averred that he was a co-sharer by inheritance and purchase in the holdings. Transferred .land was a part of their ancestral homestead. He was living with his family therein. They needed the land for maintenance of privacy and dignity. In evidence, the pre-emptor as PW 1 testified in support of such averments. Such case of pre-emptor on necessity was never dented by the appellants. Intention of the pre-emptor therefore, cannot be termed as luxury, Moreover, the purchaser appellants belonged to separate community from that of the pre-emptor. If they are allowed to enter into the homestead very object and purpose of the law for pre-emption would be frustrated.

32. Lastly, he submitted that the pre-emptor already disposed of all his land acquired by inheritance and purchase. He also drew our attention to the documents filed in Court. Learned Subordinate Judge considered the question and found that the appellants hopelessly failed to prove that the pre-emptor disposed of all his interest in the suit holdings by way of transfer and thereby, ceased to have any right to pre-empt.

33. Mr Mohammad Ali Khan also submitted that the pre-emptor himself filed documents by which he purchased 1.745 acres of land. The appellants also filed copy of documents by which the pre-emptor already disposed of all his shares by transfer. No attempt was however taken by them to prove any of the documents, none of documents was tendered and marked Exhibit. Accordingly, trial Court had to exclude them from consideration, After examination of tile record, we also could not find any substance in such submissions that the pre-emptor ceased to have the right to pre-empt.

34. Attempt of the appellants to disentitle the pre-emptor from pre-empting the transfer on the principles of waiver and/or acquiescence is so ridiculous that the trial Court rightly rejected such plea.

35. No other issue was taken on behalf of the appellants.

36. In above view of the matter, we find the impugned judgment and order of the trial Court do not suffer from any illegality or infirmity, Appeal accordingly, fails.

37. In the result, the appeal is dismissed with cost. Impugned judgment and order allowing pre-emption are hereby affirmed. In view of order of dismissal of the appeal, connected Civil Rule No. 156 (FM) of 2002 is also discharged with cost, Order of stay granted at the time of issue of the Rule is hereby recalled and vacated.

Send down the records at once.

End.

lawyer:
Manzill Murshid with Sanjoy Mandal, Advocates ------ For the Petitioners. 
AKM Zahirul Huq, DAG with Samira Tarannum Rabeya, AAG ------ For the Respondents.
parties:
Human Rights and Peace for Bangladesh (HRPB) and others ------ Petitioners
Vs.
Bangladesh, represented by the Secretary, 
Ministry of Planning and others ------ Respondents.
full_judgment:
Md. Rezaul Hasan J: On this application, filed under Article 102 of the Constitution of the People's Republic of Bangladesh, a Rule Nisi has been issued, calling upon the respondents to show cause as to why directions should not be given upon the respondents to protect the river Kornofuli at Chittagong, from encroachment and earth filling and why the respondents should not be directed to remove all permanent and temporary structures made within the river Kornofuli if they are found to have been constructed in breach of the law and/or pass such other or further order or orders as to this Court may seem fit and proper.

2. Facts stated in the writ petition, in brief, are that the petitioners are seeking direction upon the respondents to stop encroachment, earth filling, construction of temporary and permanent structures and buildings on the Banks of River Kornofuli, at Chittagong, that were being made or done violating the provisions of the Bangladesh Environment Conservation Act 1995 (amended in 2000 and 2002), and মহানগরী, বিভাগীয় শহর ও জেলা শহরের পৌর এলাকাসহ দেশের সকল পৌর এলাকার খেলার মাঠ উন্মুক্ত স্থান, উদ্যান এবং প্রাকৃতিক জলাধার সংরক্ষণ আইন, 2000.
