full_judgment:
Earlier Rule was obtained by defendant Nos. 1 to 3 on behalf of the Dhaka City Corporation, in short, the DCC, upon making a revision application under section 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure against the judgment and decree dated 24-5-05 passed by Additional District Judge and Bankruptcy Court at Dhaka in Title Appeal No. 393 of 2004, which reversed the judgment and decree dated 6-11-04 of the trial Court and decreed the suit as prayed for.

2. Later Rule was obtained by defendant No, 4 upon similar revision application against same judgment and decree of reversal. Defendant No.4 appears to be a multipurpose co-operative society of motor parts owners.

3. Opposite party No.1 as plaintiff on 27-11-02 instituted a suit being Title Suit No. 308 of 2002 against the petitioners and another for a decree of declaration that RS record of rights as prepared and finally published in the name of erstwhile DIT now added defendant No.5, RAJUK, in respect of the suit land measuring about 0.3480 acres of RS plot No. 9541 fully described in the schedule 'Kha' a part of schedule 'Ka' measuring about 0.6281 acre was wrong, illegal, ineffective and not binding upon the plaintiff and that the application of defendant No. 4 dated 13-10-02 submitted before defendant No.2 for lease of the suit land was illegal, ineffective and also not binding upon the plaintiff. The plaintiff also prayed for perpetual injunction for restraining defendant Nos. 1 and 2 permanently from leasing out the suit land or any part thereof in favour of defendant No. 4 or any other third party and/or also for restraining them from interfering in any way with the title and possession of the plaintiff in the suit land. The suit was then renumbered as aforesaid Title Suit No. 124 of 2003. By an order dated 2-4-03 RAJUK was added as defendant No.5.

4. Plaint case, in short, is that the land measuring about 0.6864 acre of plot No. 118 appertaining to CS khatian No. 13369 was originally owned and possessed by Indro Mohan and Rajkumar and Mukta Sundari in equal shares. Indro Mohan and Mukta Sundari died without any issue and leaving Rajkumar as their only heir and legal representative. Rajkumar was survived by two sons, namely, Radhagobinda and Pratap Chandra. By successive devolution, Radhagobinda and others became owners in possession of said land. They on 2-1-54 transferred said land to the plaintiff by way of a registered 'Patta' being No. 7441 and a registered sale deed being No. 7442 and delivered possession. Record of rights was accordingly prepared in the names of said recorded tenants and the plaintiff in SA khatian No. 2190 in plot No. 6163. Said land was also recorded as holding No. 47 Lal Chan Mokim Lane in the office of defendant No. 4, the DCC.

5. Then, on the requisition of the erstwhile DIT for making a road over the Dholaikhal in LA Case No. 37/1961-62 land measuring 0.3018 acre out of said 0.6864 acre was requisitioned.

6. The plaintiff originally received as compensation Taka 9,856 for said acquisition. Ultimately, 0.0583 acre out of the requisitioned land was used for the road. Land measuring about 0.2435 acre remained unused. The plaintiff amalgamated said unused land with his land into 0.6281 acre and filled with earth and constructed 62 semi-pucca shops. Said shops were comprised of a supermarket under the name and style "Shamsur Rahman Boro Market". The plaintiff kept two shops in his possession and let out others.

7. Then RAJUK decided to release the unused land and on the application of the plaintiff, the Ministry of Land by its memo dated 24-3-86 released 0.1482 acre of land in favour of the plaintiff and asked the DC, Dhaka to complete the process of release. When by an order dated 8-4-86 the plaintiff was asked to return Taka 5229.90 proportionate price of the released land out of the compensation received, the plaintiff on 8-4-86 deposited said amount by treasury 'Chalan'. Then, pursuant to the final order of release dated 19-4-86, the government handed over formal possession of said released land to the plaintiff. Meanwhile, in the revision survey, the plaintiff found that said land measuring about 0.3480 acre schedule 'Kha' part of the suit land was wrongly recorded in the name of erstwhile DIT and such record of rights had got no basis.

8. It is further stated that when some of the tenants defaulted in the payment of rents, the plaintiff had to institute suits for their eviction. Defaulting tenants then approached the DCC and claimed in collusion with the DCC depositing rents in the Sixth Court of Assistant Judge at Dhaka. Then, the DCC at the instigation of defaulted tenants on 27-6-02 most illegally asked the plaintiff to show cause as to why he should not be evicted from the suit land. The representation submitted on behalf of the plaintiff was not still disposed of by the DCC.

9. The tenants of the plaintiff then formed them into a society as defendant No.4 and made an application on 13-10-02 to the DCC for allotment. A server on behalf of the DCC came to the suit land on 6-11-02 for measurement. Then, the plaintiff came to know about the wrong record of rights in respect of 0.3480 acres of land in the name of erstwhile DIT. Hence, the suit.

10. Defendant Nos. 1 to 3 in one set and defendant No. 4 alone contested by filing two separate written statements.

11. Case of the defendant Nos. 1 to 3, in brief, is that land of schedule 'Kha' measuring about 0.3480 acre was acquired in the aforesaid LA Case for building of Dholaikhal Road. Then by a memo dated 5-6-82 the DIT transferred Dholaikhal and the adjacent land to the DCC. Being thus owner in possession, the DCC started development of the road, footpath, drain, etc, which was still pending. Said land was recorded in the name of the DCC. Such record of rights shows possession of the DCC.

12. It was further stated that the plaintiff got recorded 0.3292 acre in his name in the DP Khatian No. 5392 behind the back of the DCC. Against said record of rights, an appeal was filed and decided wrongly against the DCC. Then, an application was made for review which was fixed for hearing on 25-6-03. Against the review order, the petitioner moved this Division and got a stay in Writ Petition No. 4522 of 2003. By transfer from the DIT the DCC became owner of the suit land. The plaintiff has got no right or title in the suit land and the suit was therefore not maintainable.

13. Defendant No. 4 contended that after requisition of the land of CS plot No. 118 by the DIT in the aforesaid case of 0.6281 acres remained unused. The members of defendant No.4, 'Samity' raised on their own cost 62 shops on said unused land and started business of old iron. When the plaintiff claimed to be owner of the suit land, defendant No. 4 and its members entered into monthly lease agreement with him due to ignorance and started paying rents thinking the plaintiff was the real owner of the land. On 25-4-02, the DCC demanded ownership of the suit shops. When the matter was brought to the notice of the plaintiff, he could not do anything. Then, people of DCC on 8-2-02 came to the land and disclosed that they would be evicted unless they started paying rents to the DCC. When it was informed to the plaintiff, he could not take any step. On 27-6-02 the DCC issued notice upon the members of defendant No. 4 for eviction. Being thus compelled, they took shelter of the Court and started depositing rents in the Court. Having learnt that the DCC was the owner of the suit land, they on 13-10-02 applied for allotment. The plaintiff is not entitled to any relief as the DCC was the owner of the suit land.

14. On the party pleadings, the trial Court settled five issues including,

(1) whether there was any cause of action for the suit?;

(2) Whether the suit is barred by limitation?; and

(3) Whether the plaintiff has got right, title, possession or interest in the suit land?

15. In support of his case, the plaintiff examined three witnesses including himself while defendants examined two witnesses for their each set. Papers and documents adduced by the plaintiff were marked Exhibits 1 to 14 and those of the defendants were marked as Exhibit 'Ka to Ka(4)".

16. On the evidence oral and documentary on the record, the trial Court was of the view that seeking declaration in respect of the wrong record of rights without praying for declaration of title in the suit land was not sufficient and upon such view, it dismissed the suit as not maintainable.

17. On appeal therefrom at the instance of the plaintiff, the appellate Court on the other hand on the evidence both oral and documentary on record found 0.2435 acre of land was finally released and the plaintiff returned the money as was required for such release of the unused land. It found possession of the plaintiff in the suit land which was admitted by defendant No. 4. It also found RS Khatian was wrongly recorded in the name of defendant No.5.

18. Upon such views, the appellate Court allowed the appeal, set aside the judgment and decree of the trial Court and decreed the suit as prayed for by impugned judgment and decree.

19. Dr Rafiqur Rahman, learned Senior Advocate appearing in the earlier Rule for and on behalf of the DCC, submitted that in view of transfer of the suit land to the DCC vide Exhibit 'Ka(2)', the DCC since possessed the suit land and the trial Court was also of the view that development work on behalf of the DCC was going on in the suit land. In such view of the matter, the appellate Court was wrong in reversing the judgment and decree of the trial Court and dismissing the suit.

20. He submitted that in the absence of a relief sought for declaration of title in the suit land as was found by the trial Court, the plaintiff was not entitled to a mere decree for declaration that RS record of rights as prepared and published was wrong.

21. Mr Khondaker Mahbubuddin Ahammad, learned Senior Advocate appearing on behalf of defendant No.4 in the later Rule, somehow adopted the submissions of Mr Rafiqur Rahman and submitted that the suit as framed was barred by limitation after acquisition and the Court of appeal below therefore fell in serious error in decreeing such time barred suit.

22. He also submitted that in view of the findings of the trial Court that development works at the instance of the DCC were going on over the suit land, the suit for perpetual injunction was not maintainable.

23. He also submitted that the trial Court was justified in dismissing the suit for want of declaration of title.

24. Lastly, he submitted that after requisition and acquisition, the plaintiff lost all right or interest in the suit land and the appellate Court committed serious error without notice of such legal consequence, which resulted in failure of justice. In support, he cited Bangladesh vs Samodra Narayan Mohajan and another 2006 BLD (AD) 145 =.11 BLC (AD) 226.

25. Mr Md Khalilur Rahman appearing for the plaintiff-opposite party in both the Rules however, submitted that the acquisition case was not yet completed and the acquisition process was not yet final After release of the schedule 'Kha' land, the plaintiff possessed the entire suit land through tenants and two shops through his sons.

26. He submitted that the Court of appeal below rightly decreed the suit in the facts and circumstances of the case and the evidence on record and such decree does not call for any interference.

27. He submitted that when the plaintiff was admittedly owner in possession of the entire suit land and after release of schedule 'Kha' land, the plaintiff was not required to seek declaration of title and the suit instituted for declaration that the RS record of rights as prepared and published Was wrong was maintainable in law. In support, he cited Sarashijaksha Chatterjee and others vs Karpor Kamini Devi and others. AIR 1937 Calcutta 745.

28. Lastly, he submitted that if the Court found that the plaintiff was entitled to a relief on the case made out and proved but was not prayed for, the Court under Order VII, rule 7 of the Code of Civil Procedure can always grant such relief. In support, he cited S Sibtain Fazli vs Messrs Star Film Distributors 14 DLR 307; Kayemat Ali Sakidar and others vs Jainuddin Talukder, 14 DLR 657 and Commander (Retd) AA Chowdhury vs AKM Imam Hossain and others, 49 DLR 23.

29. I have perused the record.

30. Only issue facing me is, as to whether the Court of appeal below was justified in the facts and circumstances of the case and the evidence on record in reversing the judgment and decree of the trial Court and in decreeing the suit in its entirety as prayed for.

31. The facts which do not admit of any controversy are, that the plaintiff was owner in possession of entire 0.6864 acre of land. In LA Case No. 37/1961-62 land measuring about 0.3018 acre out of said 0.6864 acre was required for construction of Dholaikhal Road at the requisition of the then DIT. Out of the requisitioned land 0.0583 acre only was used and 0.2435 acre of land remained unused.

32. It is the case of the plaintiff that land measuring about 0.1482 acre out of said unused land was first released by the acquiring body, that is the government, vide memo dated 24-3-86. Then, the government released 0.953 acre. On being asked to deposit Taka 5229.00 as proportionate price of the released land measuring 0.2435 acre to the plaint, the plaintiff deposited on 8-4-86 by a treasury 'Chalan' said amount out of total compensation of Taka 9856.00 received by him.

33. Amalgamated released land with his other land now measured about 0.6281 acre fully described in schedule 'Ka' and comprised of holding No. 47 Lal Chan Mokim Lane under the DCC. Plaintiff made 62 shops and let them out to different tenants excepting two shops, which his sons were carrying 011 business in.

34. Further case of the plaintiff was that the land of schedule 'Kha' measuring 0.3480 was recorded wrongly in the name of DIT in the revision survey in RS khatian No.6, which had no basis. In support of such case, he adduced evidence both oral and documentary.

35. Trial Court found that 0.3018 acre out of the land of the plaintiff was acquired in aforesaid acquisition proceeding. Out of said acquired land, 0.0583 acre was used. In view of Exhibits 8, 8(ka), 10 and 14 land measuring about 0.1482 acre seemed to have been released and formal possession was delivered to the plaintiff. But though rest 0.953 acre was claimed to have been released but in support of such release no separate order was submitted. By Exhibit 14, the plaintiff deposited the money price of released land as was asked to.

36. It was also the view of the trial Court that RS khatian might have been prepared in 1969/70 to 1972/73 and the plaintiff got release of the land in 1986. So, there was no occasion for recording the land in the name of the plaintiff. Such record of rights cast a doubt over the title of plaintiff and the declaration sought for in respect of the wrong record of rights was not sufficient in the absence of a declaration of title.

37. With regard to possession, the trial Court found that defendant No.4 paid rents to the plaintiff as landlord, which they did not deny. Plaintiff adduced exhibits 4 to 6 series to evidence lease agreements with the tenants, payment of rents and taxes. Existence of shops in the suit land was also admitted. Shop owners never paid rent to the DCC as landlord. There was no proof that the DCC built the shops and/or the tenants were under the DCC.

38. The trial Court further found that the acquisition was not yet final. The suit was therefore, not barred by limitation.

39. The trial Court dismissed the suit as not maintainable on the view that after acquisition, there were development works and the record of rights was prepared in the name of DCC. I find no justification for such observation. The finding of the trial Court that there were development works on the suit land has got no basis since it is admitted that the suit land is now occupied by shops and there cannot be thought of and development works by the DCC in the shops,

40. The Court of appeal below however, on consideration of Exhibits 7, 8/Ka, 9 and 10 found in clear terms that out of required 0.3018 acre, 0.0583 acre was used by the requiring body in building footpath and road and the government de-requisitioned in two installments 0.2435 acre and received back proportionate price of said released land.

41. The fact that the plaintiff amalgamated derequisitioned land with his other land and built a market there and let out the shops to the tenants was proved and admitted, Consequently, the plaintiff had got title and possession in the entire suit land and preparation and publication of RS record of rights in the name of RAJUK was wrong, illegal, ineffective and not binding upon the plaintiff.

42. It also found that no notice under sub-section 7 of section 5 of the Emergency (Requisition) of Property Act, 1948 was published by the government. Upon such view, it reversed the finding of the trial Court that the suit without declaration of title was not maintainable.

43. Neither the acquiring body, the government nor the requiring body the erstwhile DIT now RAJUK appear in and contest the suit. Section 8 of the Emergency (Requisition) of Property Act, 1948, empowers the Deputy Commissioner only to release unused land. Claim of the DCC that it got possession of said unused land of 0.2435 acre from the DIT vide memo dated 3-6-82 and thereby became owner of said land is nothing but a hoax and was correctly rejected by the Court of appeal below. The trial Court could not go that far to accept the case of the DCC.

44. Members of defendant No.4, who having admitted to be tenants of the plaintiff and paid rents to him, would not be allowed to change their standing and/or disowning their landlord before surrender of possession of their respective premises. On such view of the legal position of the tenants, submissions of Mr Khondakar Mahbubuddin have got no substance.

45. On the aforesaid findings, there is little difficulty to hold that the plaintiff became owner in possession of 0.3480 acre as described in schedule 'Kha'. Said land was finally recorded and published in the name of the erstwhile DIT. Such record has got no basis. Decree passed by the Court of appeal below declaring such record of rights prepared in respect of said 0.3480 acre in plot No. 9541 in the name of the DIT wrong, illegal and not binding upon the plaintiff is well justified in the facts and circumstances of the case and the evidence on record.

46. The trial Court however tried to find that when the record of rights was prepared the plaintiff did not get back possession of said unused land of 0.2480 acre. Such record of rights cast a cloud over the title of the plaintiff Upon such view, it finally found that the suit was not maintainable without declaration of title.

<u>47. Such view of the trial Court was reversed rightly by the appellate Court. Because, the decision of the trial Court is based on no authority. Earlier, wrong record of rights could be corrected by a mere application under section 143A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950. In such proceeding, the aggrieved party was never required to establish title to get an order for correction of the record of rights. Reason is not far away to find. Record of rights does neither create nor destroy title. It is mere a record of physical possession at the time when it is prepared.</u>

48. A suit for declaration that the record of rights is wrong and for direction for correction of such record of rights falls under section 42 of the Specific Relief Act, 1877. I find support from an old judgment of MC Ghosh, J in 1937 AIR Cal 745,

"Now in this case the plaintiffs asked for a declaration that the Record of Rights was wrong and they prayed that the said record might be corrected. The suit was therefore maintainable and the learned Judge was wrong to hold that it did not come under section 42."

49. The Court of appeal below decreed the suit that the record of rights as prepared in Khatian No. 06 in respect of 0.3480 acre of schedule 'Kha' in the name of DIT (RAJUK) was illegal, ineffective and not binding upon the plaintiff as prayed for. I find such declaration was not sufficient, effective and complete relief. Because, the record of rights would not be corrected even after such declaration and continue to remain as before, with at best a copy of the decree attached with the relevant page.

50. It occasioned no doubt, for the omission in the prayer for correction of the record of rights in the name of the plaintiff. What can be done if the art of pleadings does not improve even over a century in this part of the civil law world But a litigant cannot be denied the relief which he is entitled to in law.

<u>51. Order VII, rule 7 of the Code of Civil Procedure in such case empowers the Court to give relief to the plaintiff as he is found entitled to but omit to pray. Otherwise, the plaintiff would be driven back to seek another declaration and/or correction of the record of rights in another suit which would not only cost the plaintiff but also consume valuable time of the Court.</u>

52. The question was settled long before by Mr Ali, J in 14 DLR 657. Let me quote him:

"There is no doubt that the plaintiff in his plaint might ask for an alternative relief, that is, he might ask that he might be given a declaration of his under raiyati right in the disputed lands under the defendants 1 and 2. But his omission can hardly be a sufficient justification for driving the parties to a separate suit for determination of the question determined in the present suit."

53. In 14 DLR 307 a Division Bench also took the view:

"It is always open to a Court to give a plaintiff such general or other relief as it deems just to the same extent as it had been asked for provided that occasions no prejudice to the other side beyond that can be compensated for in costs.

54. Relying upon 14 DLR 307 a Division Bench in 49 DLR 23 took the view:

"The Code permits the grant of such general or other relief as the plaintiff is entitled to get upon the evidence even if the plaint does not contain a prayer for the relief"

55. On the other hand, the decree of the appellate Court declaring the application of defendant No.4 dated 13-10-02 submitted before defendant No.2 for lease illegal, ineffective and not binding upon the plaintiff appears to be misconceived. Right of access to any authority, constitutional or statutory, is basic to a citizen of any jurisdiction. Such right to approach any such authority either by writing or otherwise cannot be denied. Only when an action is taken or omission occurred upon .such application or prayer that injures anyone the person feels aggrieved may have a cause of action against such action or omission. Such declaration therefore must be denied.

56. For foregoing reasons, ultimate decision of the appellate Court below does not suffer from any illegality or irregularity, which occasioned no failure of justice.

57. In the result, the Rule is discharged with cost. The cost is assessed at Taka five thousand.

58. The suit is accordingly decreed declaring the record of rights as prepared and finally published vide Exhibit 11/Ka in respect of land measuring about 3480 described in schedule 'Kha' to the plaint in the name of the then DIT and now RAJUK in RS Khatian No. 6 is wrong, illegal, ineffective and not binding upon the plaintiff. It is directed that the relevant record of rights must be corrected in the name of the plaintiff.

59. The defendants are accordingly, restrained by a decree of permanent injunction from disturbing and/or interfering with peaceful possession of the plaintiff in the suit land, in any way, as prayed for.

Send down the records, at once.

End.

Ekramul Haque, DAG, instructed by Md. Zahirul Islam, Advocate-on-Record ------ For the Appellants. 
Sufia Khatun. Advocate-on-Record ------ For the Respondent

Secretary, Ministry of Communication and others ------ Appellants

Md. lqbal Hossain ------ Respondent
case_source: (From the judgment and order dated 16-3-2005 passed by the High Court Division in Writ Petition No. 2396 of 2000)
full_judgment:
Nazmun Ara Sultana J : I have gone through the draft copy of the judgment prepared by learned brother Hasan Foez Siddique, J. While I do not differ with the decision of the learned brother Hasan Foez Siddique, J to the effect that the writ-petition filed by the writ-petitioner, who is in the service of the republic, challenging the impugned order cancelling the charge of his designation as Assistant Foreman under the Work-Charged Establishment of Roads and Highways Department is not maintainable as the Administrative Tribunal has exclusive jurisdiction to adjudicate this issue I respectfully disagree with his other decision holding the impugned orders lawful.

2. The writ-petitioner Md. Iqbal Hossain started working in the Road and Highways Department as a Heavy Vehicle Driver under Work-Charged Establishment on 28-4-1985 and continued to so work until 11-3-1997 when his status was changed to that of an Assistant Foreman by a letter vide memo No.367/l (5) E dated 10-3-1997 issued by the respondent No.3, Chief Engineer, Roads and Highways Department. The writ-petitioner accordingly took up his responsibilities as Assistant Foreman under respondent No.3 and worked as such for about 3 years. But on 18-1-2000 the respondent No.2, the Senior Assistant Secretary, Ministry of Communication, Road and Highways Division by a memo dated 18-1-2000 (annexure-D to the writ petition) addressed to the respondent No.3 sought cancellation of the order dated 10-3-1997 changing the status of the writ-petitioner as Assistant Foreman and as per this annexure-D the respondent No.3 vide the impugned memo dated 12-4-2000 (annexure-E) cancelled his earlier order dated 10-3-1997 changing the designation of the writ-petitioner as Assistant Foreman.

3. The High Court Division, by the impugned judgment and order declared this impugned memos dated 18-1-2000 and 12-4-2000 (the annexures-D and E to the writ petition) without lawful authority and to be of no legal effect holding to the effect that since the petitioner was in the service under Work-Charged Establishment and by the order dated 10-3-1997 his designation was changed as an Assistant Foreman in the same Work-Charged Establishment and since there being no law or rules regulating recruitment and other service conditions of the Work-Charged employees, the Chief Engineer of the Roads and Highways Department had authority to change the designation of the writ-petitioner from Heavy Vehicle Driver to Assistant Foreman under the Work-Charged Establishment and holding to the effect also that the cancellation of the order changing the status of the writ-petitioner after a long period of about 3 years of his taking responsibility of that post without giving him any opportunity of being heard has violated the minimum requirement of natural justice. In the proposed judgment Hasan Foez Siddique, J. however, found this impugned order lawful making observations to the effect that the service rules does not provide any provision for promotion of the Driver working under work-charged establishment as Assistant Foreman.

4. The writ-petitioner admittedly had been working under the Work-Charged Establishment of Roads and Highways Department as a Heavy Vehicle Driver for a pretty long time. He was appointed in the said post under Work-Charged Establishment on 28-4-1985 by the respondent No.5, the Superintendent Engineer, Roads and Highways Department who, undisputedly, had authority to appoint the writ-petitioner in the said post under the Work-Charged Establishment. Subsequently by the order dated 10-3-1997 the Chief Engineer, Roads and Highways Department changed his designation from Heavy Vehicle Driver to Assistant Foreman in the same pay scale under the same work-charged establishment. 1 like to quote the said order dated 10-3-1997 made by the Chief Engineer, Roads and Highways Department, the writ-respondent No.3, here. “অত্র অধিদপ্তরাধীন সংগ্রহ ও সংরক্ষণ (সাঃ) উপ-বিভাগ, তেজগাঁও, ঢাকার অফিসে কর্মরত ও ওয়ার্কচাজর্ড ভারী গাড়ী চালক, জনাব মোঃ ইকবাল হোসেন এর আবেদনের প্রেক্ষিতে পরবর্তী নির্দেশ না দেওয়া পযন্ত এই কার্যালয়ে ওয়ার্কচাজর্ড সংস্থাপনে সম স্কেলে (টাঃ ১৩৭৫-২৮৭৫) সহকারী ফোরম্যান পদে পদবী পরিবর্তন করিয়া বহাল করা হইল।

এই আদেশ অবিলম্বে কার্যকর হইবে।”

5. Evidently, the above quoted order not a promotion, rather it may be termed as a new appointment as Assistant Foreman under Work-Charged Establishment. The contesting respondent did not claim that the Chief Engineer, Roads and Highways Department had no authority to appoint any person in the post of Assistant Foreman under Work-Charged Establishment. It is also not denied that till now no law or rule has been enacted regulating the recruitment and other service conditions of the employees under Work-Charged Establishment. The Chief Engineer of Roads and Highways Department, being the highest authority of the department, for necessity, can appoint in any post under Work-Charged Establishment for the efficient running of the department. The order dated 10-3-1997 quoted above shows that the Chief Engineer, employed the writ-petitioner as Assistant Foreman under the Work-Charged Establishment. This order cannot be said a promotion order, since in this order it has been clearly stated that this is only change of designation in the same pay-scale.

6. Since the order dated 10-3-1997 is not a promotion order at all the contention of the contesting respondents that this order has not been in accordance with the Roads and Highways Department (Gazetted and Non-Gazetted Employees) Recruitment Rules 1984-is not acceptable. In the order dated 18-1-2000 under the signature of Senior Assistant Secretary to cancel the order of change of designation of the writ-petitioner as Assistant Foreman (the annexure-D) also it has been stated thus:

“------ নিয়োগবিধি অনুযায়ী সহকারী ফোরম্যান পদে পদোন্নতির জন্য যে বিধান রহিয়াছে, তাহা আলোচ্য ক্ষেত্রে অনুসরণ করা হয় নাই। উপরন্ত, অধিদপ্তরের ৩য় ও ৪র্থ শ্রেণীর কর্মচারীদের নিয়োগ, পদোন্নতি ও সিলেকশন গ্রেড/টাইম স্কেল প্রদানের জন্য একটি বিভাগীয় পদোন্নতির কমিটি রহিয়াছে আলোচ্য ক্ষেত্রে উক্ত কমিটির কোন মতামতও গৃহীত হয় নাই। ইহা ছাড়া ওয়ার্কচাজর্ড কর্মচারীদের পদোন্নতি/পদবী পরিবর্তনের কোন বিধান নাই। -----”

7. Evidently the change of the designation of the writ-petitioner as Assistant Foreman under Work-Charged Establishment was sought to be cancelled on the main ground that it was not made in accordance with rules with the consent of departmental promotion committee. But admittedly the writ-petitioner was working under Work-Charged Establishment and the change of his designation or, in other words, his fresh appointment as Assistant Foreman also was under Work-Charged Establishment. The service rules mentioned in this letter dated 18-1-2000 quoted above was not applicable at all for the Work-Charged employees. There is no Rules providing for promotion of any Work-Charged Employee.

8. However, the order dated 10-3-1997 changing the designation of the writ-petitioner as Assistant Foreman was not promotion at all, rather it can be treated as the fresh appointment of the writ-petitioner as Assistant Foreman under the Work-Charged Establishment and this order was passed by the Chief Engineer of the Department and it is not stated that the Chief Engineer, Roads and Highways Department had no authority to make any appointment in any post under Work-Charged Establishment when necessity arises.

9. The High Court Division noticed also that other Work-Charged employees of the Roads and Highways Department were appointed in the higher post and they have also been working in the said post without any objection from any quarter. The High Court Division pointed out also that the writ-petitioner had been working in the post of Assistant Foreman for a long period of about 3 years and thereafter, suddenly, the order of his appointment in the post of Assistant Foreman was cancelled by the impugned order-annexure-E without giving him any opportunity of being heard and this has violated the principle of natural justice.

10. However, in my opinion, the High Court Division rightly found both the impugned orders-the annexure-D and E without lawful authority and of no legal effect.

11. Hasan Foez Siddique J: This appeal is directed against the judgment and order dated 16-3-2005 passed fey the High Court Division in Writ Petition No.2396 of 2000 making the Rule absolute.

12. The relevant facts for the disposal of this appeal, in short, are that the writ petitioner-respondent joined as Heavy Vehicle Driver on work-charged basis in the Roads and Highways Department (RHD) on 28-4-1985. On 11-3-1997, his official designation was changed to that of an Assistant Foreman by a letter issued by the writ respondent No.3, Chief Engineer, RHD vide memo No.367/1(5)E dated 10-3-1997. The writ petitioner accordingly took up his responsibilities as Assistant Foreman under the writ respondent No.9. The writ respondent No.2, Senior Assistant Secretary, Ministry of Communication by letter dated 18-1-2000 (Annexure-D) addressed to the writ respondent No.3 requesting him to cancel the order dated 10-3-1997 since the same was not issued following the law. Accordingly, writ respondent No.3 cancelled order dated 10-3-1997 by a letter communicated under memo No.3 মি-4/74 (খন্ড) 508/1(15) B dated 12-4-2000. The writ petitioner, being aggrieved by the letter dated 12-4-2000, filed writ petition and obtained Rule. The writ respondent No.2 contented in his affidavit-in-opposition that the change of designation of the writ petitioner was effected under the order dated 10-3-1997 (Annexure-B) under a bonafide mistake on the part of the writ respondent No.3 which was rectified by the order dated 18-1-2000. It was further contended that in the absence of specific provision to that effect the writ petitioner was not entitled to be appointed as Assistant Foreman, that is, the order dated 10-3-1997 was ex-facie void and illegal.

13. The High Court Division hearing the parties made the Rule absolute. Against the judgment and order of the High Court Division the appellant preferred this appeal after getting leave.

14. Mr. Ekramul Haque, learned Deputy Attorney' General appearing on behalf of the appellant, submits that the instant writ petition was not maintainable in view of the provision of Article 117 of the Constitution read with section 4 of the Administrative Tribunal Act. He submits that the Roads and Highways Department (Gazetted and Non-Gazetted Employees) Recruitment Rules, 1984 (the Rules) having set out the post of "Assistant Foreman" being a post to be filled up by promotion from the post of Mechanics and Electricians and the Rules specially provides that appointment to such posts by promotion shall be made on the recommendation of the Departmental Promotion Committee, the High Court Division erred in law in holding that -a general discretionary authority has been given both to the Chief Engineer and the Superintendent Engineer to take decisions with regard to the employment of work charged employees in the interest of administrative efficiency and convenience" and therefore misdirected itself in declaring the impugned orders unlawful.

15. Admittedly, the writ petitioner joined as Heavy Vehicle Driver under RHD on 28-4-1985. On 10-3-1997, a letter was communicated to the writ petitioner under memo No. 367/1(5) C dated 10-3-1997 under the signature of the Chief Engineer, RHD. The contents of the said letters were as follows:

‘অত্র অধিদপ্তরাধীন সংগ্রহ ও সংরক্ষন (সাঃ উপ-বিভাগ, তেজগাঁও, ঢাকার অফিসে কর্মরত ওয়ার্কচার্জড ভারী গাড়ী চালক জনাব মোঃ ইকবাল হোসেন এর আবেদনের প্রেক্ষিতে পরবর্তী নির্দেশ না দেওয়া পর্যন্ত এই কার্যালয়ে ওয়ার্কচার্জড সংস্থাপনে সম স্কেলে (টাঃ ১৩৭৫-২৮৭৫) সহকারী ফোরম্যান পদে পদবী পরিবর্তন করিয়া বহাল করা হইল।

এই আদেশ অবিলম্বে কার্য্যকর হইবে।’

16. Serial No.73 of the schedule of the Roads and Highways Department (Gazetted and Non-Gazetted Employees) Recruitment Rules, 1984 provided specific provision for appointment of Assistant Foreman which is as follows:

'73. Assistant Foreman by promotion from Mechanics/Electrician 5 year’s service in the feeder post'.

17. That is, the law provides that in order to get promotion as Assistant Foreman 5 years service experience in the feeder post is necessary and the said post should be filled up by way of promotion from Mechanics/Electrician. In such circumstances, a letter was issued from the Ministry of Communication Roads and Railway Division communicated under memo No. আরএইচই/২এম-২৩-২৩/৯৫ (অংশ-২)-১০ dated 18-1-2000 under the signature of a Senior Assistant Secretary to cancel order of promotion of writ petitioner. Contents of the said letter were as follows:

‘উপরোক্ত বিষয়ে জানানো যাইতেছে যে, সড়ক ও জনপথ অধিদপ্তরের যান্ত্রিক উইংয়ের অধীনে ড্রাইভার পদে কর্মরত জনাব মোঃ ইকবাল হোসেনকে অধিদপ্তরের স্মারক নং ৩৬৭/১(৫) ইং তারিখেঃ ৬-৩-১৯৯৭ খ্রিঃ মোতাবেক ওয়ার্কচার্জড সংস্থাপনে সমস্কেলে পদবী পরিবর্তন করতঃ সহকারী ফোরম্যান পদে নিয়োগ প্রদান করা হয় মর্মে মন্ত্রণালয়ের গোচরীভূত হইয়াছে। কিন্তু নিয়োগবিধি অনুযায়ী সহকারী ফোরম্যান পদে পদোন্নতির জন্য যে বিধান রহিয়াছে, তাহা আলোচ্য ক্ষেত্রে অনুসরণ করা হয় নাই। উপরন্ত, অধিদপ্তরের ৩য় ও ৪র্থ শ্রেণীর কর্মচারীদের নিয়োগ, পদোন্নতি ও সিলেকশন গ্রেড/টাইম স্কেল প্রদানের জন্য একটি বিভাগীয় পদোন্নতি কমিটি রহিয়াছে আলোচ্য ক্ষেত্রে উক্ত কমিটির কোন মতামত গৃহীত হয় নাই। ইহা ছাড়া ওয়ার্কচার্জড কর্মচারীদের পদোন্নতি/পদবী পরিবর্তনের কোন বিধান নাই। কারন, ওয়ার্কচার্জড কর্মচারীদের নিয়মিতকরণের ক্ষেত্রে কোন পদে নূন্যতম ১০ বৎসর চাকরি করিতে হয়, এই বিধি অনুসরণ করা না হইলে নিয়মিতকরণ করা বিধি সম্মত হয় না।

এমতাবস্থায়, অধিদপ্তরের ৬-৩-১৯৯৭ খ্রিঃ তারিখের স্মারক নং ৩৬৭/১(৫)ই মূলে জারীকৃত অফিস আদেশ এতদ্বারা বাতিল করতঃ বিধি মোতাবেক প্রয়োজনীয় ব্যবস্থা গ্রহণের জন্য নির্দেশক্রমে অনুরোধ করা হইল।

18. In view of the letter issued from the Ministry, the Chief Engineer, RHD issued a letter communicated under memo No. 51-4/74(i)/508 dated 12-4-2000. Contents of which were as follows:

‘অত্র দপ্তরের স্মারক নং ৩৬৭ ইং তারিখ ১০-৩-১৯৯৭ ইং মাধ্যমে অত্র অধিদপ্তরাধীন সংগ্রহ ও সংরক্ষন (যান্ত্রিক) উপ-বিভাগ, তেজগাঁও ,  ঢাকার দপ্তরে কর্মরত ওয়ার্কচার্জড ভারী গাড়ী চালক জনাব মোঃ ইকবাল হোসনকে ওয়ার্কচাজর্ড সংস্থাপনে সম স্কেলে সহকারী ফোরম্যান পদে পদবী পরিবর্তন করা হইয়াছিল। যোগাযোগ মন্ত্রণালয়ের স্মারক নং আরএইচ/২এম-২৩/৯৫(অংশ-২)-১০ তারিখ ১৮-১-২০০০ ইং এর নির্দেশ অনুসারে অত্র দপ্তরের স্মারক নং ৩৬৭-ই তারিখ ১০-৩-১৯৯৭ ইং মাধ্যমে জারীকৃত অফিস আদেশটি এতদ্বারা বাতিল করা হইল। এই আদেশ অবিলম্বে কার্য্যকর হইবে।’

19. Since the Service Rules do not provide any provision of promotion as Assistant Foreman from the driver who has been working as work charged employee, rather the Rules provide that the post of Assistant Foreman should be filled up by way of promotion from Mechanics/Electrician having 5 years service experience in the feeder post, the High Court Division has committed error of law in making the Rule absolute declaring the letter dated. 18-172000 and 12-4-2000 (quoted above) unlawful.

20. The learned Deputy Attorney-General raised an important question of law that the instant writ petition was not maintainable since the writ petitioner is a public servant and the dispute is in relation to the terms and conditions of his service. According to him, this writ petition was barred under the provision of section 4 of the Administrative Tribunal Act read with Article 117 of the Constitution. In the case of Mujibur Rahman (Md.) vs Government of Bangladesh reported in 44 DLR (AD) 111, this Division has observed:

"Within its jurisdiction the Tribunal can strike down an order for violation of principles of natural justice as well as for infringement of fundamental rights, guaranteed by the Constitution, or of any other law, in respect of matters relating to or arising of sub-clause (a), but such tribunals cannot, like the Indian Administrative Tribunals in exercise of a more comprehensive jurisdiction under Article 323A (see SP Sampath Kumar vs Union of India. AIR 1937 SC 386 (para 16) and JB Chopra vs Union of India AIR 1987 SC 357 (para 2) strike down any law or rule on the ground of its constitutionality. A person in the service of the Republic who intends to invoke fundamental right for challenging the vires of a law will seek his remedy under Article 102(1), but in all other cases he will be required to seek remedy under Article 117(2)."

21. Similar view has been expressed by this Division in the case of Government of Bangladesh vs Mohammad Faruque reported in 51 DLR (AD) 112, In the cited case, this Division has observed that if there is a violation of any instruction having the force of law touching upon his terms and conditions of service, the Constitution requires him to take recourse to the specific remedy provided in Article 117 of the Constitution. Violation of terms and conditions of service may indeed be a violation of law, but if a specific remedy is provided in the Constitution for remedy then that specific remedy shall be availed of by the aggrieved person. In the case of Khalilur Rahman vs Md. Kamrul Ahsan reported in 2010 (XVIII) BLT (AD) 486 = 10 BLC (AD) 193 this Division again observed that Article 117(2) the Constitution provides that the matters falling within the jurisdiction of the Administrative Tribunal constituted under Article 117(1) of the; Constitution will not be entertainable by any other Court. As has already been mentioned that in the case of Mujibur Rahman it has clearly been stated in the background of what circumstance in spite, of the bar of Article 117(2) of the Constitution a writ petition can be filed under Article 102 of the Constitution and can be entertained by the High Court Division even the contention raised and adjudication sought relates to term and condition of service of a person in the service of the Republic. Therein it has been held that except on the limited ground i.e. when the vires of the law is challenged or a relief by way of striking down of a particular law on the ground of constitutionality sought writ petition by the High Court Division can be entertained or in other words a person in the service of the Republic can file a writ petition on limited grounds as regards the matters, even though the same relates to the condition of service. So law is now settled that except on the limited scope a writ petition involving question of determination of the matters relating to term and condition of service of a person in the service of the Republic is not entertainable by the High Court Division under Article 102 of the Constitution. The object of providing Article 117(2) is obviously to relieve the congestion in courts and provide for speedy disposal of service matters clogging the courts for year by establishing alternative forums with exclusive jurisdiction. Administrative Tribunal has the jurisdiction, power and authority to adjudicate upon the disputes relating to service matter including the power to deal with the questions involving fundamental rights.

<u>22. In the instant case, the writ petitioner in his petition did not challenge the vires of any law so he could not seek his remedy under Article 102(1) of the Constitution. The proper forum to ventilate the grievance of the writ petitioner was the Administrative Tribunal. In such view of the matter, the instant writ petition was not maintainable.</u>

23. Considering the aforesaid facts and circumstances, we find substance in the submissions made by the learned Deputy Attorney-General.

24. Accordingly, the appeal is allowed. The judgment and order dated 16-3-2005 passed by the High Court Division in Writ Petition No.2396 of 2000 is hereby set aside.

The appeal is allowed by majority decision.

End.

case_source: (From the Judgment and Order dated August 13, 1996 passed by the High Court Division in First Appeal No. 208 of 1995).
full_judgment:
Md Ruhul Amin J: This appeal by the defendant No. 1, by leave, is against the judgment and decree dated August 13, 1996 passed by a Division Bench of the High Court Division in First Appeal No. 208 of 1995 allowing the appeal and thereupon decreeing the suit upon reversing the judgment and decree dated March 19, 1995 of the 1st Court of Subordinate Judge (now Joint District Judge), Gazipur, in Title Suit No. 44 of 1993 dismissing the suit which was filed seeking declaration of title in the land in suit and for a further declaration that names of Ananda Mohan Mondal, Gobinda Chandra Mondal, Fatik Chandra Mondal and Ganesh Chandra Mondal, sons of Durga Charan Mondal as well as name of Ganesh Chandra Mondal, son of late Joy Gopal Mondal have been wrongly recorded in the finally published SA record of rights as well as in the RS record along with the names of plaintiffs vendor Krishna Mondal and others and the land in suit has been wrongly recorded in the RS record in the name of the Custodian of Vested Property.

2. The plaintiff-respondent Nos. 1 and 2 filed the aforesaid suit stating, infer alia, that the land of CS Khatian No. 122 comprising 34.64 acres of land belonged in equal share to Raj Chandra Mondal and Lechu Mondal, sons of late Kanai Mondal. Raj Chandra Mondal died leaving wife Rajrani Mondal and son Rai Charan Mondal. Rajrani Mondal sold her interest to Keru Mondal and Khetra Mondal and delivered possession to them. Keru Mondal died leaving 2 sons, Fatik Mondal and Natu Mondal and they inherited the property left by their father. Khetra Mondal died leaving 2 daughters by name Kazali Dasi and Bilashi Dasi. Kazali Dasi recorded the land she got in the name of her minor son Dowri Mondal in the RS record and Bilashi Dasi recorded her share of the property in the name of her minor son Sree Mohon in the RS record. On the death of Rajrani Mondal her son Rai Charan Mondal inherited her remaining interest. Rai Charan Mondal died leaving wife Maha Dasi who sold her inherited share measuring 2.82-1/2 acres of land to Narendra Sarker, son of Umesh Sarker. Lechu Mondal died leaving sons-Krishna Mondal and Joy Gopal Mondal. Krishna Mondal sold 1.98 acres of land out of his share to Abdur Rahman and Torap Ali Dewan and delivered possession to them. Torap Ali Dewan sold 0.33 acre of land to Mofazzal and his wife and they exchanged the same with the plaintiffs. Joy Gopal Mondal died leaving 2 sons, Kartik Mondal and Gonesh Mondal. Gonesh Mondal exchanged his share with his brother Kartik Mondal and thereby Kartik Mondal became 16 annas owner of the property left by Joy Gopal Mondal in Sarabo Mouza within Savar and Gonesh Mondal in exchange got in his share property in Kanakbari Mouza. Property of the successive heirs of Raj Chandra Mondal and Lechu Mondal and the property of the purchasers from the heirs of said two original owners was recorded in the SA record. It is the further case of the plaintiff-respondents that in 1950 Ananda Mohan Mondal, Gobinda Chandra Mondal, Gouranga Mondal and Fatik Chandra Mondal, sons of Durga Charan Mondal, the relations of the successive heirs of Raj Chandra Mondal and Lechu Mondal, fell in distress and took shelter in the house of Krishna Mondal and others and started living in a small portion of the land of CS Khatian No. 122 and, as such, their names were recorded in SA Khatian No. 185 along with the names of the successive heirs of the original owners. The said relations of Raj Chandra Mondal and Lechu Mondal later on left the house of Krishna Mondal and others. Rajrani Mondal transferred 2.82½ acres of land to Sachi Ram and Sachi Ram sold the said land to the plaintiffs and delivered possession. Krishna Mondal and others transferred 31.04 acres of land out of the land of suit khatian to the plaintiffs. As the plaintiffs purchased land of CS Khatian No. 122 from Kartik Mondal and as there was amicable partition amongst Kartik Mondal and Gonesh Mondal, sons of Joy Gopal Mondal and thereupon Kartik Mondal got land of Mouza Sarabo in his share and Gonesh Mondal got the land or Mouza Ganakbari so to avoid future complication Gonesh Mondal's son Haripada Mondal executed “নাদাবি পত্র” in respect of the land of Mouza Sarabo. The total quantity of land in CS and RS is 34.64 acres of land and out of that plaintiffs are claiming 32.63 acres of land although their kabalas reflect 35.12½  It is the specific case of the plaintiffs that they are in possession of the land in suit and the land recorded in SA Khatian No. 185 was correctly recorded in RS (DP) Khatian No. 170 in the name of the plaintiffs vendor Krishna Chandra Mondal and others but later on in the finally published RS Khatian No. 42 wrongly names of Ananda Mondal, Gobinda Mondal, Fatik Mondal, sons of Durga Charan Mondal, and Genesh Chandra Mondal son of Joy Gopal Mondal were recorded and their address has been shown in India and in the middle of 1992 plaintiffs came to know about the wrong preparation of finally published RS record and as because of the wrong entry in the record of rights serious injury to their right actually arising they are constrained to file the suit.

3. The suit was contested by the defendant No.1, herein the appellant and the defendant No.2, Deputy Custodian of Vested Property as well as by the defendant No.5 (Respondent No.6 herein) by filing separate sets of written statements. The case of the contesting defendant Nos. 1 and 2 was that plaintiffs had no causes of action for the suit and the suit has been filed to grab the land of the government raising claim on the basis of false and forged papers. The specific cases of the said defendants was that land of SA Khatian No. 185 has been listed as enemy property, as the real owners left for India and staying there and, as such, their property was listed as enemy property, that RS Khatian No. 42 has been prepared in the light of the SA Khatian No. 185 and the same has been prepared correctly, that the land in suit is being managed by the Government, that the plaintiffs have no possession in the land in suit.

4. The trial Court dismissed the suit on the finding that the plaintiffs have neither title to nor possession in the suit land in suit and the suit was barred by limitation.

5. On appeal the High Court Division reversed the finding of the trial Court as to limitation holding that against the wrong entry in the SA and RS Khatian suit was not needed be filed within 6 years from the date of knowledge thereof and also from the date of final publication of the said Khatians but from the date of invasion made on the basis of wrong record of rights. The High Court  Division further held that the date of cause of action in the suit is not the essence of the suit and, as such, filing of written statement denying the title and possession of the plaintiff in the land in suit can even be a cause of action of the suit and thus the suit cannot be held to be barred by limitation. The High Court Division was of the view that treating a portion of the land as recorded in SA Khatian later on in RS Khatian as vested property was not legal. The High Court Division further held that from the side of the defendant Nos. 1 and 2 no material whatsoever was placed as to how Ananda Mohan Mondal and others became co-sharers in the land as recorded in SA and RS Khatians and thereupon held that Ananda Mohan Mondal and others have got no interest in the land in the suit and, as such, the land in suit cannot be treated as vested property.

6. Leave has been granted to consider the submissions that the judgment of the High Court Division was not a proper judgment of  reversal and the High Court Division was wrong in holding that there was no presumption of correctness of RS Khatian under the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act and the observations in that behalf on the basis of which only the suit was decreed, were not at all correct and justified, that there having no consideration of the plaintiffs' case and the finding made by the trial Court against the plaintiffs, the decree passed in their favour is not legal and sustainable in law.

<u>7. The law is now settled that against the wrong record of rights the person whose interest is affected by such wrong recording need not file suit questioning legality of the record of rights so prepared and finally published within 6 years from said date or from the date of knowledge of such wrong record of rights, but he is required to tile the suit seeking declaration of title within six years from the date the person in whose name record has been wrongly prepared and finally published raises claim denying his claim on the basis of wrong record. But if the entry in the record of rights is made the cause of action one has to file  the suit within 6 (six) years from the date of final publication of the record of rights and not from the date of the certificate of the final publication. In view of the said position of law the learned Counsel for the appellant has not taken any exception to the finding of the High Court Division that the suit was not barred by limitation.</u>

8. The land in suit as recorded in CS Khatian belonged to Raj Chandra Mondal and Lechu Mondal. Raj Chandra Mondal died leaving wife Rajrani Mondal and a son by name Rai Charan Mondal and Rai Charan Mondal died leaving wife Maha Dasi. Lechu Mondal died leaving 2 sons Krishna Mondal and Joy Gopal Mondal. Joy Gopal Mondal died leaving sons Kartik Mondal and Gonesh Mondal. The aforesaid genealogical tree of the CS record tenants was not challenged or proved as not correct by the contesting defendant Nos. 1 and 2. The fact of transfer by the successive heirs of Raj Chandra Mondal and Lechu Mondal deposed by PW 1, plaintiff No.1, was not challenged by the defendant Nos. 1 and 2, nor proved the statement made by PW 1 as incorrect. The fact of amicable partition between Kartik Mondal and Gonesh Mondal, sons of Joy Gopal Mondal and thereupon Kartik Mondal got the property in Sarabo Mouza has not been disproved by the contesting defendant Nos. 1 and 2, rather plaintiffs have proved the said fact by the “নাদাবি” deed (Exhibit 6) executed by the son of Gonesh Mondal. It may be mentioned part of the property out of 32.63 acres of land of Sarabo Mouza in Savar PS has been treated as vested property claiming to be the property of Ananda Mohan Mondal, Gobinda Chandra Mondal and Fatik Chandra Mondal, sons of Durga Charan Mondal and Gonesh Chandra Mondal, son of Joy Gopal Mondal. It has already been mentioned that by amicable partition between Kartik Mondal and Gonesh Mondal, sons of Joy Gopal Mondal, the property in Sarabo Mouza was obtained by Kartik Mondal and in exchange thereof Gonesh Mondal got the property of Kanakbari Mouza. It is the definite case of the plaintiffs that Ananda Mohan Mondal, Gobinda Chandra Mondal, Gouranga Mondal and Fatik Chandra Mondal, sons of Durga Charan Mondal having had fallen in distress in the year 1950 took shelter in the homestead of Krishna Mondal and others and later on they left the homestead of Krishna Mondal and others. It is also the case of the plaintiffs that sons of Durga Charan Mondal had no interest in the land owned by Raj Chandra Mondal and Lechu Mondal and later on inherited by their successive heirs. From the contesting defendants' (defendant Nos. 1 and 2) side no material has been placed on the record to show that sons of Durga Charan Mondal had acquired interest in any manner in the land recorded' in CS Khatian No. 122, later on in the SA Khatian No. 185 and RS Khatian No. 42.

9. Part ofthe property in suit has been treated as vested property on the basis of the SA Khatian No. 185 and the finally published RS Khatian No. 42. It is the case of the plaintiffs that SA Khatian No. 185 and RS record was wrongly prepared in the name of sons of Durga Charan Mondal and that also the name of Gonesh Chandra Mondal was wrongly entered in the RS Khatian No. 42 since by amicable partition Kartik Mondal, son of Joy Gopal Mondal got the property of Sarabo Mouza and in exchange thereof Gonesh Chandra Mondal, son of Joy Gopal Mondal got the property of Ganakbari Mouza. The plaintiff in support of the fact of amicable partition has put into evidence Exhibit 6, deed of 'nadabi' executed by Haripada Mondal, son of Gonesh Chandra Mondal.

10. The trial Court dismissed the suit on the finding that plaintiffs have no title and possession in the land in suit. The contesting defendant Nos. 1 and 2 claimed that they are possessing the land through their men. It may be mentioned defendant Nos. 1 and 2 have not examined any witness in support of their claim of managing the land in suit or the property that has been treated as vested property by examining any witness. The lone witness (DE 1) of the appellant, the Assistant tahshilder of Kashimpur Union Land Office, although has stated that the land in suit is being looked after and enjoyed by the Government and it is not correct to say that plaintiffs are in possession of the land in suit and they have their establishments and structures in the land in suit, but there is no corroboration of the aforesaid statements, nor any material has been brought on record to establish that the land in suit or the land treated as vested property is being looked after and managed by the defendant Nos. 1 and 2. The plaintiffs in proof of their case that they are in possession of the land in suit by raising structures and they have their establishments in the land in suit have examined PWs 2-4 to corroborate PW 1. These witnesses have stated that the plaintiffs are in possession of the land in suit and they have their structures as well as their establishments therein and they have planted trees in the land in suit. The evidence from the side of the defendant Nos. 1 and 2 as against the evidence of the plaintiffs to disprove claim of possession of the plaintiffs is of no worth. In the background of the evidence of the plaintiffs as discussed above we are of the view trial Court was in serious error in holding that plaintiffs have no possession in the land in suit. The plaintiffs by oral and documentary evidence have established that they have acquired title to the land in suit from the undisputed successive heirs of the CS recorded tenants as well as from the transferees of the heirs of the CS recorded tenants.

11. The appellant has based its claim as regard the property in suit or part of the property in suit as of being the vested property on the RS Khatian and the census list of the vested property. It may be mentioned census list as it appears has been prepared either on the basis of SA or RS Khatian. In the RS Khatian along with the names of the heirs of the CS recorded tenants and their transferees names of the sons of Durga Charan Mondal have also been recorded and in the RS Khatian address of Durga Charan Mondal's sons and Joy Gopal Mondal's son Gonesh Chandra Mondal has been shown as India and consequent thereupon,. there is an entry in the RS Khatian to the effect "পক্ষে" Custodian land and building".

<u>12. The learned Counsel for the appellant has submitted that as in the RS Khatian No. 42 prepared under section 144 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 (the Act) names of sons of Durga Charan Mondal as well as Joy Gopal Mondal's son Ganesh Chandra Mondal appear and consequent thereupon as there is presumption of correctness of the entries in the said RS Khatian under section 144A of the Act, as such, treating the property of the said persons as vested property was quite legal. The presumption as regards the entries in the RS Khatian so attached under section 144A of the Act is rebuttable by leading evidence from the side of the person questioning correctness of the entry made therein. It is in the evidence of PW 1 that Durga Charan Mondal's sons having had fallen in distress some time in 1950 came to the house of Raj Chandra Mondal and Durga Charan Mandai's sons had no title in the land of Raj Chandra Mondal and Lechu Mondal and they stayed for some time but later on left the house of Raj Chandra Mondal. It is also in the evidence of PW 1 that names of Durga Charan Mondal's sons were wrongly recorded in the SA and RS Khatian. As against the aforesaid contention of PW 1 the evidence of DW 1 is that Ananda Mohan Mondal and others sons of Durga Charan Mondal were the SA recorded tenants and that they left for India at the time of war of 1965 and thereupon their land has been listed as vested property. This witness in cross-examination has stated that he cannot say on what basis names of sons of Durga Charan Mondal have been recorded in SA Khatian and that he cannot say Durga Charan Mondal's sons and Joy Gopal Mondal's son Gonesh Chandra Mondal at what point of time went to India. Since from the materials on record it is seen that there was no. basis for recording names of Durga Charan Mondal's sons and also name of Gonesh Chandra Mondal in the SA Khatian and also for making entries in the RS Khatian as regards address of Durga Charan Mondal's sons and. Joy Gopal Mondal's son Gonesh Chandra Mondal shown as India has no basis, so the said entries in the RS Khatian were incorrect. Moreover, the Exhibit 6, Nadabi deed executed by Gonesh Chandra Mondal's son of Haripada Mondal reflects the fact of amicable partition of the property of Joy, Gopal Mondal between his, sons Kartik Mondal and Gonesh Chandra Mondal and thereupon Kartik Mondal got the property of Sarabo Mouza wherein the land in suit situates. It is seenfrom the materials on the, record that the entry in the RS Khatian as regards name of Gonesh Chandra Mondal, son of Joy Gopal Mondal reflecting interest in the land of Sarabo Mouza, wherein the land situates, is not correct. Since the presumption of correctness that has been attached to the RS Khatian by  the provision of section 144A of the Act has been rebutted and consequent thereupon recording of names of Durga Charan Mondal's sons and Joy Gopal Mondal's son Gonesh Chandra Mondal was not correct, rather there was no basis for entering their names in the RS Khatian No. 42 and, as such, defendants (defendant Nos. 1 and 2) case of vested property on the basis of wrong entry of the names of persons having no title and interest in the land so listed in the RS Khatian in question has no leg to stand, rather the property in suit has been listed in the census list as vested property without ascertaining the correct position or without ascertaining particulars of the persons who have, in fact, right, title and interest in the land in suit. It appears the vested property authority has prepared the census list merely on the basis of wrongly prepared RS Khatian No. 42, and without ascertaining the real state of the matter is the property in suit in reality belongs to whom.</u>

13. The learned Counsel for the appellant has submitted that in the background of the gazette notification dated December 3, 1965 property that assumed character of enemy property, later on vested property, vested in the Government, as such, transfers made in 1970 by successive heirs of CS recorded tenants and the purchasers therefrom were not legal and valid and the Exhibit 6, Nadabi deed, executed by Gonesh Chandra Mondal's son Haripada Mondal ought notto have been taken into consideration for the purpose of arriving at a decision that Gonesh Chandra Mondal, son of Joy Gopal Mondal ceased to be the owner of the land of Sarabo Mouza because of amicable partition between the brothers, namely Kartick Mondal and Gonesh Chandra Mondal, sons of Joy Gopal Mondal. We have already observed that part of the land recorded in RS Khatian has been listed as vested property on the basis of entry in the said Khatian. Since incorrectness of the entries in the said RS Khatian No. 42 in so far names of Durga Charan Mondal's sons and the name of Gonesh Chandra Mondal, son of Joy Gopal Mondal have been established by the respondent Nos. 1 and 2, as such, treating the property in suit as vested property on the basis of said wrong entries was illegal. As to treating the property of Gonesh Chandra Mondal son of Joy Gopal Mondal in Sarabo Mouza as vested property is, also not correct, as firstly it is in the evidence of DW 1 that he cannot say when Gonesh Chandra Mondal left for India and second by the Exhibit 6 it has been established by the respondent Nos. 1 and 2 that Gonesh Chandra Mondal ceased to have any interest in the land of Sarabo Mouza because of amicable partition with his brother Kartik Mondal. So there being no reliable evidence that the property legally vested in the Government as enemy property, later on vested property, as such, because of the notification of December 3, 1965 it cannot be said property in suit has vested in the Government as enemy property, later on vested property.

14. It is seen from the judgment of the High Court Division that the said Division: was of the view that RS record was prepared in terms of the provisions as are in Chapter IV of Part IV of the Act and thereupon expressed the view that presumption of correctness as to the entries in the SA and RS record finally published under section 19(3) in Chapter IV has no presumption of correctness. As against the said finding of the High Court Division the learned Counsel for the appellant has submitted that R'S record has been prepared as per provision of section 144 of Chapter XVII of part V of the Act and to the entries in the RS record so prepared under the said section of the Act presumption of correctness has been attached under section 144A of the Act. We have already held that presumption so attached under section 144A of the Act to the Khatians prepared under section 144 of the Act is rebuttable and the respondent Nos. 1 and 2 has rebutted the correctness of the entry made therein as regard the name of Durga Charan Mondal's sons and name or Gonesh Chandra Mondal son of Joy Gopal Mondal and, as such, the finding of the High Court Division that presumption of correctness as regard the entries in the RS Khatian is not available, is not correct, as submitted by the learned Counsel for the appellant, though of merit but for that the decision arrived at by the High Court Division that the property in suit is not vested property has not been materially affected since it has been established by the respondent Nos. 1 and 2 that recording of the names of Durga Charan Mondal's sons as well as Gonesh Chandra Mondal, son of Joy Gopal Mondal in the SA and RS record of rights was not correct.

15. In view of our discussions made hereinabove we find no merit in this appeal.

16. Accordingly the appeal is dismissed.

There is no order as to costs.

End.
