full_judgment:
Soumendra Sarker, J: The Rule was issued calling upon the opposite party No. 1 to show cause as to why the impugned judgment and order dated 18-11-2013 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, 5th Court, Dhaka, in Title Suit No. 201 of 2013 rejecting the application filed by the defendants No. 1-3 under Order VII, rule 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure should not be set aside and/or such other or further order or orders passed as to this Court may seem fit and proper.

2. The facts leading to the issuance of the Rule in a nutshell can be stated thus that the present opposite party No. 1 as plaintiff instituted the original Title Suit being No. 201 of 2013 in the Court of learned Joint District Judge, 5th Court, Dhaka for declaration of title and recovery of khash possession in the suit property contending inter alia that the disputed property had been owned and possessed by the plaintiff in his exclusive 16 annas share. In the disputed land there exist 4 (four) shops of the plaintiff in which the tenants are one Md Shafiullah in shop No. 1 and in shop No. 2 the other tenant was one Monjur Mia and the shops No. 3 and 4 respectively were possessed by the plaintiffs tenants Manju Mia and Rafique Mia. The defendants No. 1-3 claiming the property as of their own from their predecessor-in-interest Dr Sirajul Islam. The remaining defendants No. 4-8 are also claiming title in the disputed property on the basis of their papers. The further case of the plaintiff is such that the defendants to the suit denying the plaintiffs title dispossessed the plaintiff from the suit property including his shops on 3-12-2009. The defendant's claim in the disputed property on the basis of waqf is baseless, at which the title of the plaintiff has been clouded. To dispel that cloud the plaintiff instituted the original suit for declaration of the title-and recovery of khash possession.

3. The contrary case of the defendants No. 1-3 in short is thus that the plaintiff to the suit having no manner of right, title, interest and possession in the disputed property on the basis of false allegation filed the original suit and the defendants had been owning and possessing the disputed properties including the shops therein in their own interest and knowledge of all from the very beginning. The further case of the defendants is such that the plaintiffs suit is barred by the principle of res-judicata as for the same suit-premises earlier a Title Suit being No. 158 of 2010 have been filed against the same parties and the earlier suit have been dismissed on contest vide judgment and decree dated 31-7-2012.

4. During pendency of this suit the defendant-petitioners filed an application under Order VII, rule 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure before the trial court for rejection of the plaint on the ground that in respect of the self-same suit properties earlier the plaintiff in the 3rd court of Assistant Judge, Dhaka filed a Title Suit being No. 158 of 2010 and in that suit the plaintiff have failed to establish his case and also failed to prove his right, title and possession in the disputed premises. As a result of which the learned Assistant Judge, 3rd Court, Dhaka by his judgment and dismissal decree dated 31-7-2012 dismissed the suit on contest and, as such, the present suit is not tenable in the eye of law which is barred by the principle of res-judicata.

5. Against the aforesaid application for rejection of the plaint the plaintiff-opposite party filed a written objection on the ground that the application for rejection of the plaint is liable to be rejected inasmuch as there is no scope to entertain the said application under VII, rule 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure. The plaintiff-opposite parties in their written objection specifically contended that the principle of res-judicata is not applicable in the instant case and the defendants out of ill-motive only to harass the plaintiff have preferred such application for rejection of plaint.

6. The learned trial court viz, the learned Joint District Judge, 5th Court, Dhaka by the impugned judgment and order dated 18-11-2013 hearing the parties to the suit rejected the application under Order VII, rule 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure.

7. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the impugned judgment and order the defendant-petitioners have preferred this revisional application under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure and obtained the Rule with an interim order of stay.

8. MGH Ruhullah the learned Advocate appeared on behalf of the petitioners while NAM Abdur Razzaque the learned Advocate appeared on behalf of the plaintiff- opposite-party No. 1.

9. The learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioners submits that in passing the impugned judgment and order dated 18-11-2013 the learned trial court committed an error of law resulting in an error in the decision in not considering that the plaintiff to the suit prior to the present suit for declaration of title filed a Title Suit being No. 158 of 2010 and in that suit the plaintiff prayed for eviction of the defendants from the suit land on the ground that the plaintiff is the owner of the suit land but the learned Senior Assistant Judge, 3rd Court, Dhaka dismissed the suit on contest on 31-7-2012 and thus the present suit is barred by the principle of res-judicata as provided in section 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure. The learned Advocate further submits that the learned Joint District Judge, 5th Court, Dhaka having failed to appreciate the actual proposition of law arrived at an erroneous view that the provision of law as incorporated in Order VII, rule 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure is not applicable in the instant suit and it is a mailer of evidence by virtue of which the matter agitated from the side of the defendants can be adjudicated and finally settled. The learned Advocate lastly submits that the learned trial court erred in law as well as in facts resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice and, as such, the impugned judgment and order is not sustainable.

10. As against the aforesaid submissions of the learned counsel of the petitioners the learned counsel appearing on behalf of the plaintiff-opposite party opposing the Rule controverted the arguments advanced from the side of the learned Advocate of the petitioners and submits that the trial Judge, viz. the learned Joint District Judge, 5th Court, Dhaka during passing the impugned judgment and order committed no illegality or irregularity. The learned Advocate further submits that in the instant suit at the present moment there is no scope to entertain such application under Order VII, rule 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure and it is apparent from the face of the papers that the earlier suit which was filed by the plaintiff in the third court of learned Assistant Judge, Dhaka being Title Suit No. 158 of 2010 was not between the same parties and the matter-in-issues are quite different and the points for determination on which that suit was disposed of are different with that of the present suit. The learned Advocate also submits that the earlier suit was not a suit for declaration of title and recovery of khash possession. Hence; the provision laid down in section 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure is very much inconsistent for its application in the instant suit as the principle of Res judicata itself provides that, "No Court shall try any suit or issue in which the matter directly and substantially in issue has been directly and substantially in issue in a former suit between the same parties or between parties under whom they or any of them claim, litigating under the same title, in a court competent to try subsequent suit or the suit in which such issue has been subsequently raised and has been heard and finally decided "by such court."

11. Therefore, the former suit being Title Suit No. 158 of 2010 was quite different and the matter for adjudication therein is not identical with the present suit being Title Suit No.201 of 2013. The learned Advocate lastly submits that the learned trial Judge rightly held that at this stage; there is no scope for rejection of the plaint as the matter of res-judicata and the point of limitation is a mixed question of facts and law.

12. We have considered the submissions of the learned Advocates and have perused the impugned judgment and order passed by the learned trial Court i.e. the learned Joint District Judge, 5th Court, Dhaka in Title Suit No.201 of 2013 including the judgment and dismissal decree passed in the earlier suit being No.158 of 2010 along with the connected papers as well as the application filed under Order VII rule 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure.

13. Having gone through the connected papers it transpires that the former suit i.e. the Title Suit No.158 of 2010 was instituted by the present plaintiff-opposite party No. 1 for eviction of tenant from the suit premises and the subsequent suit which is Title Suit No.201 of 2013 is a suit for declaration of title and recovery of khash possession. It further transpires from the connected papers that the learned trial Judge in the former suit framed four issues for decisions and those were as follows:

“ক) অত্র মোকদ্দমাটি বর্তমান আকারে ও প্রকারে চলতে পারে কিনা?

(খ) অত্র মোকদ্দমার নালিশী সম্পত্তির সংশ্লিষ্টতায় বাদী বিবাদীদের মধ্যে মালিক ভাড়াটিয়া সম্পর্ক বিদ্যমান ছিল বা আছে কিনা?

(গ) বাদী মালিক মর্মে অত্র মোকদ্দমা আনয়ন করার Locus Standi আছে কি না এবং বিবাদীগণ খেলাপী ভাড়াটিয়া গণ্যে উচ্ছেদযোগ্য কি না?

(ঘ) অত্র মোকদ্দমা প্রার্থিত মতে বাদী প্রতিকার পেতে পারে কিনা?

14. On the aforesaid four issues for determination the learned trial Court decided the fate of that suit and dismissed the suit for want of necessary proof.

15. We have come across from the instant Title Suit being No. 201 of 2013 that this suit is a suit for declaration of title and recovery of khash possession. In the said suit the proposed issues from the side of the plaintiff were as follows:

১। অত্র মোকদ্দমা বর্তমানে আকারে ও প্রকারে চলিতে পারে কি না?

২। অত্র মোকদ্দমা পক্ষদোষে দুষ্ট কিনা?

৩। অত্র মোকদ্দমা তামাদি আইনে বারিত কি না?

৪। অত্র মোকদ্দমা রেস জুডিকেটা দ্বারা বারিত কি না?

৫। নালিশী সম্পত্তি ওয়াকফকৃত সম্পত্তি কি না?

৬। বাদী স্বত্ব সাব্যস্থক্রমে খাস দখল পাইতে পারে কি না?

16. Obviously, in view of the nature of the present suit the issues which have been proposed from the side of the plaintiff deserve consideration of the trial Judge inasmuch as the matter of controversy between the parties to the suit is encircled within the right, title, interest and the matter of possession and dispossession of the concerned parties. Besides this; the provision laid down in section 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure provides as many as five conditions, which are necessary to constitute res-judicata. These are: (1) 'The matter directly and substantially in issue" in the former suit must be the same in the subsequent suit, (ii) The former suit must have been between the same parties or between parties under whom they or any of them claim, (iii) The parties in the subsequent suit must have litigated under the same title in the former suit, (iv) The Court which decided the former suit must have been competent to try the subsequent suit, (v) The matter directly and substantially in issue in the subsequent suit must have been heard and finally decided in the former suit.

<u>17. On meticulous consideration of the application for rejection of the plaint in connection with the former suit and the present Suit being No.201 of 2013 it is apparent from the face of the papers that the matter in issues are not at all identical with the former suit and it is not directly or substantially in issues which has been heard and decided finally by a competent court of law. Apart from this; it transpires that the parties to the suits are not same. Beside this; it is a decided matter that the question of res-judicata as well as the question of limitation is a mixed question of facts and laws which is required to be adjudicated and decided during trial of the original suit. The learned trial Judge with regard to this; relying upon the decision of our Apex Court reported in 20 BLD (AD) 82 = 52 DLR (AD) 49 rightly held that there is no scope at the present stage to entertain such application under Order VII, rule 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure.</u>

18. Having regard to the facts, circumstances and proposition of law we have every reason to inclined such a view that the learned Joint District Judge, 5th Court. Dhaka committed no illegality in disallowing the application for rejection of the plaint, rather; he was quite justified in holding the view that this provision of law is not applicable in the instant suit. Hence, we find no substance in the Rule.

19. In the result, the Rule is discharged. The impugned judgment and order dated 18-11-2013 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, 5th Court, Dhaka, in Title Suit No. 201 of 2013 rejecting the application filed by the defendants No. 1-3 under Order VII, rule 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure stands good.

20. Let the order of stay granted earlier by this Court at the time of issuance of the Rule be vacated.

21. However; there will be no order as to costs.

Communicate the judgment and order immediately.

End.

full_judgment:
AK Badrul Huq J: This civil proceeding by way of First Appeal before this Court depicts a lamentable episode and an apt parading how blood of one organ of Government could be sucked by another unit of the said Government.

2. In challenge of a Judgment dated August 16, 1998 followed by a decree dismissing plaintiff's suit for a declaration of title and also for a decree of permanent injunction plaintiffs as appellants approached this Court in this First Appeal.

3. Plaintiffs are appellants and defendants are respondents to the appeal.

4. Appellants as plaintiffs on 4-3-1989 instituted a suit being Title Suit No. 87 of 1989 in first Court of Subordinate Judge. Dhaka for a declaration that property described in schedule-A to plaint is acquired land of Government and legally leased out to plaintiff and plaintiff's title therein is unaffected by defendants documents and also, for decree of permanent injunction restraining defendants from disturbing possession of plaintiff on schedule 'A' property, Schedule 'A' land shall be described hereinafter as suit property.

5. Lifeblood of plaint case is hereunder:

a.	Suit property along with other properties was recorded in CS Khatian No. 910 in Mouza Shahar Dhaka in the name of Raghunath Das. Suit property was requisitioned and acquired for Dhaka Improvement Trust (for short DIT) now Rajdhani Unnayan Kartripakhya (briefly RAJUK) under Land Acquisition Case No. 3 of 1963-64. DlT having exercised right and ownership granted lease in respect of 35 Bighas 2 Kathas and 2 Chattaks of property to plaintiff Bangladesh Bank. Plaintiff Bangladesh Bank got ka lease from Government for public purpose and for economic development and, also, for building and constructing staff and officer’s quarters. Plaintiff Bank got allotment and physical possession upon management. Possession of the property was delivered on 21-12-1979. Standard Leave Agreement was executed and registered on 6-4-1981. Plaintiff Bank exercised owner-ship and took possession on leased out suit property. Plaintiff Bank constructed staff and officer’s quarters. Suit property was wrongly and fraudulently recorded in State Acquisition Khatian in SA Plot Nos. 8705 and 8707 in the name of one Golam Hossain Rezwani.

b. Property standing in the name of Golam Hossain Rezwani mainly comprised of a glass factory and building and it was treated as an abandoned property and it was taken over by Ministry of Industries as an abandoned industry. Ministry of Industries, thereafter, transferred the property by a deed of transfer in favour of defendant No. 1 Saiyed Shahidul Huq as proprietor of Eastern Trading Corporation. In the deed of transfer CS Plot No. 254 corresponding to SA Plot Nos. 8705 and 8707 had been wrongly inserted. Defendant No. 1 Saiyed Shahidul Huq having been unable to possess the property fraudulently sold out to defendant No.2 and other defendants preparing Block Map.

c. Defendant No. 2 and other defendants, thereafter, transferred their purchased property in favour of defendant Nos. 6-12.

d. Defendants instituted a suit being Title Suit No. 39 of 1984 through defendant No.2 Md Zulfiquer Ali Talukder for declaration of title and decree of permanent injunction.

e. Defendants after creating various fraudulent documents against the title of plaintiff Bank. Defendants and their associates threatened plaintiff Bank to make forcible entrance on suit property and illegally dispossessed plaintiff Bank and that dispossession gave rise to cause of action on part of plaintiff Bank to lay the suit before Court.

The suit was, thereafter, renumbered as Title Suit No. 64 of 1993 on transfer to the Court of Sub-ordinate Judge and Fourth Artha Rin Adalat, Dhaka.

6. Respondent Nos. 6-13 of the appeal had been added as defendant Nos. 6-13 in the suit, respondent No.2 and 3 as defendant Nos. 2 and 3 and respondent No. 13 as added defendant No. 13 put up resistance in the suit and traversed allegations mounted against them on presentation of three separate written statements.

7. Essence of statements embodied in three sets of written statements are:

a. Suit is not maintainable without a prayer for declaration of title on suit property and, also, recovery of Khas possession thereon.

b. Plaintiff got no cause of action to lay suit.

c. Suit is barred by limitation.

d. Suit property originally belonged to Golam Hossain Rezwani and others and Golam Hossain Rezwani and others left former East Pakistan during Liberation War of Bangladesh of the year 1971 and .their whereabouts were not known and property was enlisted as Abandoned Property under President's Order No. 16 of 1972. Chief Martial Law Administrator on behalf of the Government of Bangladesh through Section Officer Ministry of Industries sold the suit property along with other properties to defendant No.1 Saiyed Shahidul Huq, proprietor of Mis Eastern Trading Corporation for valuable consideration of Taka 22,00,000 and possession had been handed over to defendant No. 1 Saiyed Shahidul Huq who got his name mutated in the concerned Tahsil Office, and paid rent and got rent receipts.

e. Defendant No. 1 Saiyed Shahidul Huq for the purpose of sale made some small plots of land and transferred the property in favour of defendant No. 2 and defendant No. 2 thereafter, sold some properties in favour of other defendants.

f. Suit land was neither requisitioned nor acquisition in Land Acquisition Case No.3 of 1963-64 and plaintiff did not acquireany title on suit properties, plaintiff Bank, also, got no possession on suit property.

8. Over pleadings of parties, following five (5) issues had been framed:

(i) Suit as framed is maintainable?

(ii) Is there any cause of action in filing the suit?

(iii) Is the suit barred by limitation?

(iv) Has the plaintiff got any title, interest and possession on the suit property?

(v) Is the plaintiff entitled to a decree as prayed for?

9. Evidence, both oral and documentary, had been led in support of the respective contentions of the parties. Two (2) witnesses got examined in support of plaintiff case and four (4)witnesses stood on the witness box to buttress the case of the defendants. Some of the documents filed from the side of defendants-respondents had not been proved in accordance with law.

10. Syed Ahmed, Deputy Director of plaintiff Bangladesh Bank stood on witness box as PW 1 in support of plaint case.

11. AKM Motiur Rahman, Deputy Director, Engineering Department, plaintiff Bank gave evidence as PW 2.

12. Haji Md Rafiqul Islam as Holder of Power of Attorney for and on behalf of defendant Nos. 6 to 11 gave evidence as DW 1.

13. Md Anwarul Haque added defendant No. 12 for himself and on behalf of defendant No.2 gave evidence as DW 2.

14. Haji Abdur Razzak and Haji Md Alauddin stood on witness box as DWs and 4 respectively. They are witnesses on factum of possession.

15. Learned Subordinate Judge did not decide Issue No.1 in the strict term of the issue framed. Learned Subordinate Judge his directed his approach on the legal character of General Manager of plaintiff Bank to lay the suit and held that General Manager got no legal character to file the suit on behalf of Bangladesh Bank.

16. Learned Subordinate Judge decided Issue No. 11 in the negative and found that the plaintiff did not state in plaint on which date defendant forcibly entered into the suit property and dispossessed plaintiff and it could not be ascertained on which date the cause of action arose.

17. Learned Subordinate Judge also, decided Issue No. III in the negative and held that plaintiff had been aware of preparation of SA Record of Right in respect of suit property and being aware of wrong record did not present suit within proper time and suit stood barred by limitation.

18. Learned Subordinate Judge, also, decided Issue No. IV against the plaintiff and held that plaintiff failed to prove title and possession on suit property.

19. Learned Subordinate Judge, also, held that plaintiff failed to produce relevant papers and documents in support of right of DIT to acquire any  property without prior permission of Government of Bangladesh and, also, right to lease out property in favour of any institution.

20. Learned Subordinate Judge with the above decisions dismissed the suit.

21. Plaintiff having been resentful of the above adjudication sought setting aside those through medium of this first appeal before this Court.

22. Contentions pressed into service from the side of plaintiff-appellant are catalogued hereunder:

i. Government as acquiring body did acquire the suit property along with other properties of requiring body Dhaka Improvement Trust and acquisition was complete on publication of Gazette Notification, Exhibit-2, Plaintiff Bank acquired title on suit property by way of lease deed, Exhibit-3 and, thereafter by way of demarcation and layout plan, Exhibit-4 and Exhibit-4(Ka) respectively and suit property could not be treated as abandoned property and also leased out by Ministry of Industries to one Saiyed Shahidul Huq defendant No. 1 and the lease matter and subsequent deeds of transfer by defendant No. 1 to other defendants are absolutely void, illegal and without jurisdiction and learned Judge failed to take into account the legal implications of Gazette Notification, lease deed and deeds of title and possession of plaintiff Bank and committed a substantial error of law in the decisions.

ii. Enlistment of suit property as abandoned property and sale deed by Ministry of Industries in favour of defendant No.1. and subsequent transfer of suit property by defendant No. 1 in favour of other defendants could not in any way affect title of plaintiff and learned judge did not take into account this legal aspect and, thus, fell into a serious error of law in not awarding decree in favour of plaintiff-appellant.

iii. Suit was not at all barred by limitation and suit was well within time and decision of learned judge on point of limitation is ex facie, contrary to materials on record and decision on limitation cannot be sustained in law.

iv. Plaintiff Bank got delivery of possession upon layout plan and demarcation and admittedly in possession of a substantial portion of the acquired and leased out property and plaintiff Bank paid advalorem court fee and the suit was not even barred by limitation, plaintiff bank was entitled to relief of recovery of possession of portion of property if found to be out of possession and learned Judge committed a patent illegality in his decision in dismissing the suit.

v. Property on which Golam Hossain Rezwani stood was outside acquired property and State Acquisition Record of Right had been wrongly prepared and wrong record cannot in any way affect legality and validity of acquisition of property and acquisition proceeding was not challenged from side of defendants on institution of suit and learned Judge erred in holding that plaintiff Bank's title under acquisition by Government was not affected by documents allegedly created by defendants.

vi. Bangladesh Bank is the plaintiff and Bank has been stated to be represented by General Manager and misdescription, if any, could not make plaintiff out of court and the substance and not the form of suit was required to be gone into by learned Judge and amendment sought by plaintiff in this respect was refused by learned Judge and dismissal of suit on question of legal character of plaintiff Bank is absolutely illegal and decision cannot be sustained in law.

23. Contentions advanced from side of plaintiff appellant had been adopted by defendant-Fifth- respondent, Chairman former DIT now RAJUK.

i. Golam Hossain Rezwani having been the rightful owner of suit property same had been correctly recorded in his name and Golam Hossain Rezwani during war of liberation of Bangladesh left for Pakistan and the property had been enlisted as abandoned property and Ministry of Industries took over the management of glass factory and then transferred the suit factory in favour of defendant No. 1 Saiyed Shahidul Huq who took over possession of suit property and being owner in possession of suit property by way of sale deeds transferred property in favour of other defendants and some of the transferee defendants transferred their purchased property to other defendants and defendants acquired good title and possession over suit property.

ii.	In a suit for permanent injunction exclusive possession of party seeking permanent injunction is required to be proved and plaintiff-appellant failed to prove exclusive possession over suit property and, on the other hand, defendant-respondents through evidences, oral and documentary, proved possession of defendants over suit property. Defendants got their names mutated in record of right and paid rents and receipts are evidences of possession of defendants.

iii.	Suit was barred by limitation and learned Judge was well justified in dismissing suit on point of limitation.

iv. Bangladesh Bank did not come forward to be plaintiff and General Manager, Bangladesh Bank could not be plaintiff for Bangladesh Bank.

25. In the wake of rival contentions advanced from the Bar, points that survive for determination are:

1. (a)Whether suit property is acquired property of Government and legally leased out to plaintiff Bank. and

(b) Whether title, interest and possession of plaintiff-appellant's Bank on suit property have been affected by subsequent treatment of suit property as abandoned property and also, by deeds of transfer by Ministry of Industries in favour of defendant No. 1 and subsequent deeds of conveyances by defendant No. 1 to other defendants.

2. Whether suit stood barred by limitation.

3. Whether suit can be thrown away on point that General Manger, Bangladesh Bank filed the suit.

4.(a) Whether the decisions rendered by Trial Judge in dismissing plaintiff Bank's suit can be sustained and those are susceptible to be overturned and

(b) Whether plaintiff Bank can be graced with reliefs prayed for.

26. Points formulated now may be approached and resolved.

27. Point No.1 plaintiff bank traced its title on the strength of an allotment and the execution and registration of a lease deed from former DIT now RAJUK who is said to have acquired property in dispute in a Requisition and Acquisition proceeding.

28. Plaintiff Bank put forward claim that DIT in Land Acquisition Case No.3 of 1963-64 acquired 14, 2118 acres equivalent to 43 big has of property from full of CS Plot Nos. 253, 254, 255, 256, 258, 259, 260 and part of CS plot No. 235 under sheet No. 76 and full of CS plot Nos. 10, 11, 12, 13 and 14 under sheet No. 78 of Mouza Shahar Dhaka, Police Station Sutrapur, District Dhaka. Requisition proceeding was on 28-5-1963, property was acquired on 18-11-1965. Acquisition was concluded and reached to its finality on Notification in Gazette on 25-11-1965 (Exhibit-2) DIT allotted 35 bighas 2 kahtas and 2 chataks of property in favour of plaintiff Bank on 21-12-1979 Standard Lease Agreement by  DIT in favour of plaintiff Bank was on 15-4-1981 (Exhibit-3), plaintiff Bank took over possession of leased out property on 21-12-1979 (Exhibit-4). plaintiff Bank's property faced dispute in respect of CS Plot No. 254 converting an area of .61 acres and this 0.61 acres of property is the suit property. CS Plot No. 254 corresponds to SA Plot Nos. 8705 and 8707 and SA Record of the two (2) plots had been prepared in the name of Golam Hossain Rezwani and the said record of right has been challenged as wrong by plaintiff Bank. Plaintiff Bank asserted that treating suit property as abandoned property is absolutely illegal and without jurisdiction and transfer of the property by Ministry of Industry in favour of defendant No. 1 and transfer by defendant No. 1 by way of deeds of transfer in favour of other defendants are also illegal and void and defendants did not acquire any title on suit property and title of plaintiff Bank on suit property had not been at all affected by said deeds of transfer.

29. Defendants-respondents rested their claim on the basis of a deed of sale by Ministry of Industries in favour of defendant No. 1 Saiyed Shahidul Huq and Ministry said its right to transfer by way of sale deeds on the strength that the property was an abandoned property as abandoned by recorded owner Golam Hossain Rezwani. Defendant No.1 being the owner by a good number of deeds transferred property to other defendants and transferee defendants, thereafter, again sold their purchased property to another group of defendants.

30. Exhibit-1 is Cadastral Survey Record of Right containing CS Plot No. 254 (in full) measuring an area of .61 acres, Exhibit-2 is Gazate Notification dated 25-11-1965 and Gazette Notification was published in exercise of power conferred by sub-section (b) of section 93A of Town Improvement Act XIII of 1953 (Act of 1953). In schedule noted in Gazette Notification CS plot No. 254 (in full) are being more or less 14.2118 acres along with other plots had been listed. Exhibit-3 is Standard Lease Agreement dated 6-4-1981 for residential property between Dhaka Improvement Trust on the one part who is called the Lessor and Manager Bangladesh Bank, Dhaka referred to as Lessee or the other part. In schedule of Lease Agreement, area of property leased out is 35 bighas, 2 kathas and 2 chhataks which is equivalent 11-2/3 acres CS plot No. 254 (in full) is suit plot. Suit plot No. 254 (in full ) along with other plots (full or part) had been noted in the schedule. Exhibit-4 is final survey performed by Dhaka Improvement Trust in respect of leased out 35 bighas, 2 kathas and 2 chhataks. Final survey had been performed on 21-12-1979. Exhibit 4(Ka) is map showing CS Plot No. 254 and other leased out plots.

31. Town Improvement Act, 1953 had undergone massive amendments by way of Town Improvement (Amendment) Act, 1987 which came into force on 30th April, 1987.

32. Relevant provisions of section 93A (1) and 93A(3) and 93A (4)(b) of The Act of 1953 before amendment by Town Improvement (Amendment) Act 1987 are meditated and now conveniently pressed in aid in resolving the controversy.

33. Section 93A(1) enjoined that if in the opinion of Provincial Government it was expedient or necessary so to do, for construction, betterment of roads, waterways or any other communications and the developments of areas for residential, commercial, industrial purpose or for establishment of parks, playing fields and open space for relief of congestion in any area to which this Act extends Provincial Government might, by order in writing, requisition any property for the Board and could make such further order as might appear to Government necessary or expedient in connection with such requisition.

34. Section 93A(3) postulated that when order of requisition had been served under sub-section (2) in respect of a property provincial Government might direct District Magistrate to take and deliver possession of property within 2 weeks to the Board and Board might use or deal with property as might appear to it to be expedient.

35. Section 93A(4)(h) enshrined that provincial Government would publish in Official Gazette a notice to the effect that provincial Government had decided to acquire requisitioned property for Board and on and from beginning of the day on which the notice was published, requisitioned property would vest absolutely to Board free from all encumbrance and period of such requisition of such property would come to an end.

36. From above it has become crystallised that with the publication in Official Gazette in respect of an acquired property by way of requisition and acquisition proceeding, requisitioned and acquired property would vest absolutely to Board free from all encumbrances.

37. Exhibit-Kha is the list of properties taken over by Ministry of Industries and in serial No. 556 there is nothing manifesting that MS Dhaka Glass Works and Cork Industries had been taken as an abandoned property. Date of taking over is noted on 19-4-1972. Exhibit - Uma is deed of sale dated 8-7-1982 between MS Eastern Trading Corporation, represented by its sole proprietor Mr Saiyed Shahidul Huq (defendant No.1) of First Part and Chief Martial Law Administrator, Government of the People's Republic of Bangladesh, represented by MK Zaman, Section Officer, Ministry of Industries and Commerce of Second Part, Exhibit-Gha is certificate of taking over and making over physical possession of Dhaka Glass Works by defendant No. 1 Saiyed Shahidul Huq figuring himself as Administrator, Dhaka Glass Works. The date is 25-3-1980. Exhibits Cha-1 and Cha-2 are two Rent Receipts of the year 1984 showing payment of rent in respect of State Acquisition Khatian No. 4836. Exhibit Jhaha is certified copy of irrevocable General Power of Attorney by defendant No. 1 Saiyed Shahidul Huq in favour of Md Motiur Rahman Rentu empowering the latter to execute and register any document including deed of transfer. Exhibits-Cheha-1, Ja,Tha-1, Tha-3, Tha-4, Tha-5, Tha-6, Tha-10, Tha-11, Tha-12, Da-2 and Da-3 are deeds of defendants who are transferees and subsequent transferees from defendant No. 1.

<u>38. Admittedly, alleged taking over of suit property as abandoned property either by Ministry of Works or by Ministry of Industries was much later than Gazette Notification published by Government giving finality to requisition and acquisition proceeding when suit property absolutely vested with Government free from all encumbrances as mandated by section 93A(4)(h) of the Town Improvement Act of 1953. The property which vested with the Government i.e. Dhaka Improvement Trust, free from all encumbrances cannot at all vest subsequently with any other organ of the Government either Ministry of Works or Ministry of Industries under the garb of abandoned property.</u>

39. Dhaka Improvement Trust, an important organ of Government, entered into a lease agreement with plaintiff Bangladesh Bank, another important limb of Government and date of Lease Agreement is 6-4-1981. Sale deed in favour of defendant No.1 by Ministry of Industries is dated 8-7-1982 which is, also, much later than Lease Agreement between Dhaka Improvement Trust and plaintiff Bangladesh Bank. Plaintiff Bangladesh Bank, thus, acquired title and interest in suit property before alleged acquisition of any right and interest by defendant No. 1 and by deeds of conveyances, mutations and payment of rents and other acts performed by defendants, which were much later acts, cannot affect at all the right, title and interest and possession of plaintiff Bangladesh Bank in any way and right, title and interest and possession of plaintiff Bank remained and remain unaffected.

40. Exhibit-Ka is certified copy of State Acquisition Khatian No. 4836 standing in name of Golam Hossain Rezwani, No documents had been produced from side of defendant-respondents to show basis of preparation of State Acquisition Record of Right in name of Golam Hossain Rezwani. Mere State Acquisition Record of Right in name of Golam Hossain Rezwani is no evidence of title. It had earlier been stated that defendants respondents, also, failed to produce any documentary evidence manifesting that suit property was declared as an abandoned property under President's Order No. 16 of 1972.

41. Exhibit-5 is photocopy of certified copy of Judgment recorded in Title Suit No. 39 of 1984 of Sixth Court of Assistant Judge, Dhaka in Title Suit. Defendant No.2 Md Zulfiqar Ali Talukder had been plaintiff and Bangladesh Bank had been defendant No. 1 and former DIT now RAJUK had been defendant No.2 and the suit was for decree of permanent injunction in respect of plaintiff's purchased property from defendant No. 1 Saiyed Shahidul Huq. Suit was dismissed by judgment dated 23-11-1989 and judgment was followed by a decree. Learned Assistant Judge in recording dismissal of suit positively found that plaintiff of suit failed to prove possession in suit property.

42. Exhibit-5(ka) is certified copy of Title Appeal No. 39 of 1990 of First Court of Additional District Judge, Dhaka and appeal was carried by plaintiff of suit Md Zulfiquar Ali Talukder having felt aggrieved of judgment and decree passed in Title Suit No. 39 of 1984. Learned Additional District Judge, First Court, Dhaka by Judgment dated 31-8-1995 dismissed appeal and maintained judgment and decree passed by learned Assistant Judge. In dismissing appeal learned Additional District Judge recorded following decisions, amongst others:

(a) Plaintiff (Md Zulfiqar Ali Talukder) could not produce any title showing that Golam Hossain Rezwani was owner of suit property and plaintiff only filed certified copy of State Acquisition Khatian in name of Golam Hossain Rezwani which is no evidence of title.

(b) Plaintiff failed to produce any Gazette Notification showing that suit property was declared as an abandoned property under President's Order No. 16 of 1972.

(c) Plaintiff failed to prove that suit property belonged to Golam Hossain Rezwani and it was declared as abandoned property and

(d) CS plot No. 254 i.e. suit plot was acquired by Government in November, 1965. Deed of Lease dated 15A-1981 shows that entire CS Plot No. 254 and other plots were leased out in favour of Bangladesh Bank. Delivery of possession Certificate, Plan approved by DIT, Mouza Map of Sutrapur etc. show that defendant (Bangladesh Bank) became owner of suit property in 1981 by taking lease from DIT i.e. prior to alleged purchase of plaintiff's vendor.

<u>43. In view of discussion made above conclusion that can safely be reached is that ,suit property is acquired property of Government and it was legally leased out to plaintiff Bank whose right, title, interest and possession on suit property had not been at all affected by defendants-respondent's sale deeds, mutations and payment of rents.</u>

44. Point No.2: Plaintiff Bank sought reliefs in the following terms:

(a) a decree be passed declaring that the land described in schedule-A to the plaint is acquired land of the Government and legally leased out: to the plaintiff and plaintiff’s title therein is not affected by defendant’s documents.

(b) Defendants be restrained permanently from disturbing the possession of the plaintiff in the suit land.

45. DIT leased out suit property along with other properties under acquisition in favour of plaintiff Bank by way of Lease document dated 15-4-1981. Plaintiff claimed to have entered into possession of suit property and defendant No.1 claimed title and possession on suit property on the strength of a deed of sale from Ministry of Industries on 8-9-1982 and the other defendant's title rested on sale deed dated 8-9-1982. Plaintiff Bank's suit had been laid on 22-4-1985 and claim put forward from side of defendants was definitely not before 8-9-1982 and surely after 8-9-1982. Suit had been, therefore, presented well within time and could not be at all said to have been barred by limitation.

<u>46. This takes us to finding reached by trial judge on limitation. Learned Judge found that plaintiff had been aware of preparation of wrong record in respect of suit property and being aware of the, wrong record did not lay suit within stipulated time and there was no cause of action of suit and suit stood barred by limitation. Finding reached by learned Judge on limitation is absolutely wrong. Knowledge of wrong record of right can be starting point of limitation and a litigant public even if aware of wrong record of a record of right can wait and wait till his right is invaded by other side and his suit will be well within time if he institutes Suit within six years from date when his right on suit property is denied and invaded by other party. This view of ours is fortified with three authorities. Raj Kiran Chandra Roy Bahadur and others vs Tarak Nath Gongopadhyay and others, 40 CW No. 566, Abdul Hafez and another vs Lal Miah and others, 1988 BLD 497 and Banghadar Mitra and others vs Natabar Sardar, being dead & others, 1 BCR 393. In the case in hand the plaintiff Bank laid the suit within the period of limitation and it cannot be said as of Trial Judge that suit stood barred by limitation. Point No; 2 stands answered in negative.</u>

47. Point No.3: Examination of Lease Agreement, Exhibit-S indicates that the Lease Agreement had been between DIT on the one part and BM Ahmed, Manager Bangladesh Bank of the other part and all transactions in respect of Lease Agreement had been performed by General Manager on behalf of Bangladesh Bank. In the suit in hand General Manager of Bangladesh Bank laid the suit. Bangladesh Bank is an organ of the Government Order. XXIX, rule 1 enjoins that in any suit by or against Government, the plaint or written statement shall be signed by such person as the Government may by general or special order appoint in this behalf and shall be verified by the person whom the Government may so appoint and who is acquainted with the fact of the case. General Manager having signed the Lease Agreement for Bangladesh Bank, he laid suit in Court. Plaintiff’s suit cannot be thrown away on ground that General Manager filed suit. Bangladesh Bank is represented by General Manager, defect is merely a technical one and not at all substantial and technicality must be to cause of justice. Point No. 3 also, stands answered in firm negative.

48. Point No. 4(a) : One of reasons found favour with Trial Judge in dismissing plaintiff's suit was that plaintiff failed to produce any paper evidencing that DIT without obtaining permission from Government of Bangladesh could acquire any property and also, could enter into Lease Agreement with any institution. The said reason canvassed by learned Trial Judge was absolutely misconceived inasmuch as DIT did not acquire any property and it is former East Pakistan Government who acquired suit property along with other properties Government was Requiring Body and DIT was Requiring Body. Acquiring Authority Government on asking of Requiring Body DIT acquired property for Requiring Body DIT and DIT thereafter being owner of suit property leased out property in favour of plaintiff Bangladesh Bank. Exhibit-2, Gazette Notification is best evidence demonstrating that suit property along with other properties stood acquired by Government for DIT.

49. Other ground taken by learned Trial Judge in dismissing suit was that no date had been stated in plaint indicating defendant's forcible entrance into suit property and, as such, it could not be gathered on which date cause of action of suit arose.

<u>50. Expression "cause of action means entire bundle of facts a plaintiff has to prove in order to be eligible for grant of relief. It can, also be said that cause of action pre-supposed the existence of a right in plaintiff which right has either been infringed or is threatened to be infringed. Cause of action cannot be construed in an isolated way and whole averments made in plaint are to be seen and taken together to see whether any cause of action has been disclosed or not. It is the plaint as a whole which is to be construed and not terminology or, for that matter, a few stray references.</u>

51. True it is that no specific date had been stated in plaint when defendant and associates threatened to enter into suit property forcibly and illegally dispossessed plaintiff from suit property. In paragraph No. 11 of plaint it had been simply stated that cause of action of suit arose while defendants and associates threatened to forcibly enter into suit land and illegally dispossessed plaintiff from suit property.

52. Specific date of threatened dispossession had not been noted down in plaint but that cannot be characterised to be a fundamental defect and infirmity in plaint. It cannot be at all suggested that plaint did not consist of material facts giving rise to a cause of action on the part of plaintiff to lay suit in Court. Decision of learned Trial Judge on question of non-disclosure of cause of action cannot be sustained in law.

53. Regard being had to above discussion we are of this considered view that decisions reached by learned Judge in dismissing suit cannot be sustained in law and thus stand overturned.

54. Point No. 4(b): Point No. 4(b) is surviving point in appeal. In disposing Point No.1 it has been posited that plaintiff Bank acquired title on suit property and title and interest of plaintiff Bank on .suit property cannot be at all affected by deed of sale in favour of defendant No. 1 and other deeds of sale in favour of other defendants from defendant No.1 Plaintiff through documentary evidence, Exhibit- 4(Ka) proved act of taking possession on suit property along with other properties. Defendant No.1 did not come forward to .support case that suit property was treated as abandoned property and subsequent deed of transfer in his favour by Ministry of Industries and his transfer by way of deeds of conveyances to other defendants were legal. Defendant No.2, also, did not stand on witness box though he filed written statement. DW 2 as defendant No. 12 for himself and for defendant No. 2 gave evidence. DW 2 got no right or authority to give testimony in favour of defendant No. 2 unless he was authorised with a Power of Attorney. From the above the irresistible decision that can be safely rendered is that plaintiff Bank can be graced with decree declaring that property described in schedule "A" to plaint i.e. suit property, is acquired property of Government and legally leased out to plaintiff Bank and plaintiff Bank's title is unaffected by defendant's documents.

55. It comes out from testimonies of DW 2 who is added defendant No. 12 that he got a kutcha house on suit property and defendant Nos. 6-9 got four(4) kutch a houses and defendant No. 10 got shop. It also, came out from mouth of DW 3 and DW 4 that in suit property there were three (3) shops and six (6) kutcha houses. Possession, if any, of defendant on a portion of suit property by way of construction of shops and kutch a houses, that possession is not lawful and possession is absolutely illegal and unauthorised. Defendant could not acquire any right, title and interest on suit property on basis of deeds of conveyance. which were much later than the title deed of plaintiff Bank.

56. In a suit for Permanent Injunction, factum of possession in fundamental and plaintiff can be graced with a decree of permanent injunction in respect of the suit property if he can prove exclusive possession over suit property. It has earlier stated that possession by way of construction of shops and kutcha houses, three and six in number respectively, no matter whether possession of defendants were lawful or not but it became evident that plaintiff got no possession in some portion of suit property. It is no where in plaint that plaintiff had been threatened with dispossession on a particular portion of suit property arid no evidence, as came forth from the mouth of PW 1 and PW 2 on which portion of suit property plaintiff was threatened with dispossession. It cannot be , thus, said that plaintiff Bank succeeded in proving its exclusive possession on suit property to be graced with a decree of Permanent Injunction restraining defendants respondents from entering into suit property. Plaintiff, thus, cannot be granted a decree of Permanent Injunction.

57. This takes us to petition presented by defendant Nos. 6-12 respondent sunder Order XLI, rule 27 of the Code of Civil Procedure for admitting certified copies of two sale deeds executed ot1:5-3-1984 and 30-9-1986 as additional evidence and making those as Exhibits for canvassing ground that due to inadvertence and bonafide mistake said deeds had not been filed in trial Court. Hearing of First Appeal commenced on 27-4-2003 and hearing occupied a good number of days i.e. 28-4-2003, 12-5-2003, 17-5-2003, 18-5-2003, 21-5-2003, 26-5- 2003, 27-5-2003, 17-6-2003 and 18-6-2003. Hearing came to an end on 18-6-2003. Defendant respondents slept and slept for all the days of hearing and woke up only on 18-6-2003 and on that date affidavit was sworn. It was too late in the day for the defendant-respondents in filing the petition .There had been serious laches and unpardonable delay on the part of defendant-respondents in presenting petition. Moreover, grounds urged are not satisfactory. The petition has not been also prepared happily and carelessness has' been demonstrated. No. grounds exist in allowing the petition. Petition is rejected.

58. In view of disclosure made above conclusion that cart be reached is that appeal stands allowed in part. Suit is decreed in terms that property described in schedule A to the plaint is acquired property of the Government and that been legally leased out to plaintiff Bank and plaintiff Bank's title on suit property remains unaffected by defendant's documents. Plaintiff Bank's relief in respect of decree of permanent injunction stands dismissed.

59. Regard being had to the fact and circumstances of the case we direct that parties shall bear their respective costs of litigation.

Lower Court's Record be sent down as early as possible.

End.

AJ Mohammad Ali, Senior Advocate instructed by Md. Taufique Hossain, Advocate-on-Record ------ For Respondent Nos. 5-6. 
None Represented ------ For Respondent Nos. 1-4.

case_source: (From the judgment and order dated the 12th day of December, 2007 passed by the High Court Division in Writ Petition No. 1302 of 1998)
full_judgment:
Md. Abdul Wahhab Miah J.: This appeal, by leave, is from the judgment and order dated the 12th day of December, 2007 passed by a Division Bench of the High Court Division in Writ Petition No.1302 of 1998 discharging the Rule Nisi.

2. Facts necessary to dispose this appeal are that the appellants herein as the petitioners (hereinafter referred to as the writ-petitioners) filed the above mentioned writ petition before the High Court Division challenging Memo No. Parti: 21/97/576 dated 28-5-1997 issued by writ-respondent No.2, the Director General, Directorate of Land Record and Survey, Government of the People's Republic of Bangladesh, Tejgaon, Dhaka with a direction upon writ-respondent No.3, the Settlement Officer, Dhaka to correct the order dated 25-4-1996 passed by writ-respondent No.4, the Assistant Settlement Officer, Dhaka Southern Office of the Land Record and Survey, Tejgaon, Dhaka.

<u>3. In the writ petition, it was stated, inter alia, that respondent No.5, the Capital Co-operative Housing Society Limited, as the petitioner filed Writ Petition No.1080 of 1989 before the High Court Division impleading the Director, the Settlement Office and the Assistant Settlement Officer, all of Land Records and Survey, Tejgaon, Dhaka, appellant No.1 herein (hereinafter referred to as writ-petitioner No.1) and 18 others challenging the order dated 5-2-1989 passed in Appeal Case Nos. 34046 of 1984 to 34054 of 1984 heard analogously by way of review by the Assistant Settlement Officer to have been passed without lawful authority and was no legal effect and to declare the striking out the name of the writ-petitioner (the Capital Co-operative Housing Society) from the RS Khatian No.1600(DP) as illegal and without any basis and lawful authority and also to declare the inclusion of the names of respondent Nos. 3-21 (in Writ Petition No.1080 of 1989) in the RS Khatian as fraudulent and without any basis. Subsequently, by filing a supplementary affidavit a prayer was added as to why the order dated 18-1-1989 passed by writ-respondent No.1 (a), the Settlement Officer be not declared to have been passed with-out lawful authority and was of no legal effect.</u>

4. The case of the writ-respondent No.5 (in the instant writ petition) in Writ Petition No.1080 of 1989 was that the land recorded in CS Khatian Nos. 138 and 330 bearing Plot Nos.881, 890, 893, 894 with a total area of 9.46 acres land and plot Nos.878, 879 with an area of 2.86 acres land respectively within Mouza-Uttar Khan, formerly within Police Station-Keraniganj, now Police Station-Gulshan, Dhaka originally belonged to Sharafatullah who died leaving behind 4(four) sons named Abdur Rahman, Pokai, Nazimuddin, Faizuddin and one daughter named Jewar Bibi. Bhawal Raj Estate, superior landlord of the case land, got a rent decree against the said tenants for arrear of rents in respect of CS Khatian No.330 and put the decree into execution and auction purchased the lands of this khatian and got delivery of possession thereof on 20-2-1930 and the said landlord also got another decree in a title suit against the said tenants and filed an execution case for the realization of the decretal costs, attached and put the lands of CS Khatian No. 138 in Court sale, auction purchased the same and got delivery of possession thereof on 20-6-1940. Subsequently, the said landlord settled the lands of those two CS Khatians with one Rahmat Banu on 3-3-1943 and she also got her name recorded in the SA Khatian and as she was threatened to be dispossessed from the case lands, she filed Title Suit No.80 of 1965 in the 1st Court of Munsif, Dhaka for permanent injunction against the successors-in-interest of said Sharafatullah and the purchasers, but as eventually, she was dispossessed from the case land, she filed another suit being Title Suit No.9 of 1970 in the 5th Court of Subordinate Judge, Dhaka for declaration of title and for recovery of possession which was decreed in her favour and she got delivery of possession of the case land and later on, the said writ-petitioner purchased the entire lands from Rahmat Banu by a registered sale deed bearing No.10884 dated 24-3-1978 and got delivery of possession thereof.

5. Respondent Nos.1-2 and respondent Nos.3-21 of Writ Petition No.1080 of 1989 contested the writ petition (Writ Petition No. 1080 of 1989) by filing two separate affidavits-in-opposition (detailed of the facts stated in their affidavit-in-opposition are not stated as those are not necessary for disposal of the instant appeal).

6. The Rule Nisi issued in Writ Petition No. 1080 of 1989 was discharged on 2-3-1993.

7. On 2-4-1995, one Suruj Mea and his 28 co-sharers, on 19-4-1995, one Motiur Rahman and his two co-sharers, on 21-4-1995, one Majir uddin and another co-sharer and on 23-4-1995, Manwara Begum separately submitted four applications before respondent No.2 who directed respondent No.3 for taking legal steps upon examining those applications and in compliance with the said direction, Syed Ahammad Gazi, Assistant Settlement Officer was assigned to enquire into the matter and he submitted an enquiry report on 8-5-1995. Considering the said enquiry report, comment of the Assistant Settlement Officer and recommendation of the charge officer, it was found that there were some mistakes and irregularities in the matter of apportioning land in the draft records of rights prepared earlier, the Settlement Officer, respondent No.3 vide his order dated 17-9-1995 started Miscellaneous Case No.3439 of 1995 under rule 82A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Rules, 1955, in short, the Rules, 1955 in order to remove the mistakes and irregularities and to prepare correct record of right and directed Joynal Abedin Bhuiyan, Assistant Settlement Officer to submit his opinion to the Settlement Officer for approval, after hearing the matter upon giving notices on the parties.

8. Writ-petitioner No.2, purchased-"in-possession" from the successive heirs-in-interest of said Sharafatullah and their vendee was added as opposite party in Miscellaneous Case No.3439 of 1995 vide the order dated 8-10-1995. After receipt of the notices, all the parties concerned recorded in the said RS Khatian No. 1600(DP) and also respondent No.5 appeared in the said miscellaneous case and contested the same. After perusing the said four applications, order dated 5-2-1989 passed in the said nine appeals, the judgment passed in Writ Petition No.1080 of 1989 and hearing the parties, Joynal Abedin Bhuiyan, the Assistant Settlement Officer, vide his order dated 2-1-1996 passed in Miscellaneous Case No.439 of 1995 proposed to prepare the RS Khatian in the names of the successive heirs-in-interest of said Sharafatullah and the petitioners along with other purchasers in possession from them after deleting the names of said Rahmat Banu and Capital Co-operative Housing Society Ltd (writ-respondent No.5 in the instant writ petition) from draft RS Khatian No.1600 and on 4-1-1996 submitted his said proposal before respondent No.3 for approval. Respondent No.3 after consulting the records vide his order dated 5-4-1996 accepted/approved the said proposal of Joynal Abedin Bhuiyan and ordered preparation of the record of right in conformity with the approved proposal and directed him to carry out the said order. Joynal Abedin Bhuiyan, vide his order dated 25-4-1996 carried out the earlier order dated 5-4-1996 passed by respondent No.3 and prepared the final RS Khatian No. 1600 of Mouza-Uttarkhan, Police Station-Gulshan Dhaka in the name of the petitioners and other successive heirs-in-interest and the purchasers-in-possession from them under rule 32 of the Rules, 1955. Thereafter the said RS Khatian No. 1600 was published finally under Rule 33 of the Rules, 1955 and a certificate stating the fact of such final publication was made by the revenue officer under rule 34(1) thereof. And then in the official Gazette Notification dated 26-9-1996, a declaration under rule 34(2) of the Tenancy Rules, 1955 was made by the Government to the effect that the records of right of Mouza-Uttar Khan, Police Station-Gulshan, Dhaka was finally published under section 144(7) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950. Following the said Gazette Notification dated 26-9-1996, respondent No.1 vide Memo No. Bhu:Ma/Sha-3/ Bhu:U :Ka/20/94/234(123) dated 6-10-1996 directed all concerned persons including respondent No.2 to take necessary steps so that fixation of LD Taxes and other functioning in this regard were done on the basis of the said finally published RS Khatians and thereby RS Khatian No.1600 was acted upon. Respondent No.5 having failed in Writ Petition No.1080 of 1989, tried to mislead and influence various authorities including the offices of respondent Nos. 1 and 2 with an intention to get extra procedural, extra statutorily and extra-judicial benefits and privileges and in course of his said improper attempts, respondent No. 2 vide his office Memo No. Prati:/21/97/576 dated 28-5-1997 passed order directing correction of the record of rights stating that an illegal order dated 25-4-1996 was passed for preparation of record of rights, when the matter was finally settled in appeal and preparation of record of rights was in the last stage of printing. The impugned Memo dated 28-5-1997 was issued without giving the writ-petitioners any chance to be heard, though the same was entirely prejudicial for them. Writ-petitioner No.2 and one Mosammat Mallika Begum being unofficially informed of the impugned order dated 28-5-1997 on 16-6-1997 submitted a memorandum to the State Minister for Land to cancel the same and the State Minister forwarded the said memorandum to writ-respondent No.2 with a direction to consult the matter with writ-petitioner No.2 who though met writ-respondent No.2, went in vain. There-after, writ-petitioner No.2 and said Mosammat Mallika Begum on 5-10-1997 submitted another memorandum to the State Minister of Land with the same prayer which was forwarded to writ-respondent No.1 vide Memo Bhu:Ma/Sha-2 (Prakalapo/17/97-503 dated 21-10-1997 with a direction for enquiry by the Director (Record), Land Record and Survey Directorate, but the said Memorandum has still been kept in abeyance. On 26-4-1998 the concerned officers visited the case land for further preparation of the record of rights thereof and they verbally informed the writ-petitioners that they were officially bound by the impugned order dated 28-5-1997 to prepare the said record of rights in accordance with the same.

9. The writ-petitioners on 9-5-1998 through their lawyer sent a notice demanding justice by express telegram to the writ-respondents with a request to cancel, rescind and withdraw the impugned order dated 28-5-1997 and with a further request to communicate their decision in this regard by 10-30 am of May 10, 1998, but the writ-respondents did not respond to the said notice.

10. In the above circumstances, the writ-petitioners, having no other equally efficacious remedy provided by law, filed the writ petition and obtained the Rule Nisi.

11. Writ-respondent No.5 in whose favour the impugned order was passed though appeared in the writ petition did not file any affidavit-in-opposition.

12. Respondent Nos.6-11 got themselves added in the writ petition by filing separate petitions. Added respondent No.6, Syed Golam Mostafa filed an affidavit-in-opposition to contest the Rule contending, inter alia, that the case land belonged to Bhawal Courts of Wards. One Sharafatullah took settlement of that land from Bhawal Estate; Bhawal Estate instituted Rent Suit No.2525 of 1927 for arrears of rent; that suit was decreed; thereafter the Bhawal Courts of Wards purchased the suit land in auction in Rent Execution Case No.373 of 1928 on 20-2-1930; Bhawal Court of Wards got possession of the land through Court on 20-2-1930; Bhawal Court of Wards thereafter settled the land with Rahmat Banu on 22-3-1943; legal heirs of Sharafatullah filed Title Suit No.652 of 1930 challenging the aforesaid auction; that the said suit was dismissed on contest on 10-9-1930; that the legal heirs of Sharafatullah filed Title Appeal No.1011 of 1930 on 17-3-1931 which was also dismissed; thereafter the plaintiff of Title Suit No.652 of 1930 filed Second Appeal No.2927 of 1931 before the High Court Division which was also dismissed; thus auction purchase was confirmed by all the three Courts; that one Zewar Bibi, daughter of Sharafatullah filed Title Suit No.113 of 1946 for declaration of title; that the suit was dismissed on 6-1-1948; Zewar Bibi filed another suit being Title Suit No.31 of 1950 renumbered as Title Suit No.72 of 1951; that suit was dismissed on 19-4-1952; that on 22-12-1964 Zewar Bibi filed title appeal (number is not available from the record) against the aforesaid judgment which was also dismissed; accordingly, the land was recorded in the name of Rahmat Banu who took settlement from the landlord auction purchaser; the heirs of Sharafatullah took barga of the case land from Rahmat Banu; since the Bargadars stopped giving barga paddy to Rahmat Banu, she filed Title Suit No.9 of 1970 against Asia Khatun and others (legal heirs of Sharafatullah); that suit was decreed on 22-8-1972; that Rahmat Banu got possession in Title Execution Case No.6 of 1973. The Bargadars filed First Appeal No.6 of 1976 before the High Court Division; that appeal was dismissed on 30-4-1975 for non prosecution, thus title of Rahmat Banu was again reaffirmed; that on 23-3-1978 Rahmat Banu by a registered sale deed sold the case land to Capital Co-operative Society, i.e. respondent No.5; that respondent No.5 being a developer developed the case lands, divided the same into 155 plots and distributed those to 155 members who constructed pucca and semi pucca residential houses and have been residing in those houses; that in pursuance of the aforesaid registered sale deeds, the respondents and the other allottees got their names duly mutated and paid rents to the Government upto 1996, but because of the dispute as mentioned in earlier paragraphs the Government was not taking any ground rent from the allottees.

13. Writ-petitioner No. 1 (appellant No.1) filed a supplementary affidavit stating, inter alia, that the original owner of the land of CS Khatian No.330 of Mouza 195, Uttar Khan under present Police Station-Uttar Khan was one Bholanath Singh and from whom Sharafatullah, son of late Robiullah became the owner and possessor under sthitiban rayoti title in respect of Plot Nos. 878, 879, 881, 890, 89. 994 measuring in total 12.32 acres land and the name of Sharafatullah was correctly recorded in CS Khatian Nos.138 and 330. After the death of CS recorded tenant, Sharafatullah, the name of one Rahmat Banu appeared in SA Khatian Nos. 239 and 434 in respect of the aforesaid 12.32 acres land appertaining to those six plots and, as such, the heirs of Sharafatullah at the time of last RS operation filed 9(nine) objection cases under rule 30 of the Rules, 1955 and those objection cases were allowed in part. Respondent No.5 (Capital Co-operative Housing Society Ltd) being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the order passed in the aforesaid 9(nine) objection cases filed 9 (nine) appeals under Rule 31 of the Rules, 1955 bearing numbers: 34046-34054 of 1984 and on consideration of the papers and documents those appeals were finally dismissed on contest by the Assistant Settlement Officer, Dhaka Zone, Dhaka by his order dated 5-2-1989 with a direction to record the names of the objector appellants only in RS Khatian No.1600. As it appeared from annexure-' Ka', respondent No.5 settled the properties of SA Khatian Nos.239 and 434 covering 6 plots of original CS Khatian Nos.138 and 330 measuring 12.32 acres land by way of perpetual lease to 162 persons and after they lost in the settlement appeals under rule 31 being Nos.3446-3454 of 1948, filed Writ Petition No. 1080 of 1989 and obtained a Rule Nisi; the Rule Nisi issued in the aforesaid writ petition was discharged on 2-3-1993; Another Division Bench by its judgment and order dated 14-11-1991 in Writ Petition Nos.207 and 208 of 1989 dealing with more or less the same principle of law involved in Writ Petition No.1080 of 1989, amongst others, declared that the Director General of Land Records could not exceed his power by entertaining and disposing of a second review petition against the order passed by the Settlement Officer in appellate jurisdiction in respect of correction of record of rights. Respondent No.5 did not challenge the judgment and order dated 2-3-1993 passed in Writ Petition No.1080 of 1989 before this Division and thus accepted the result of their above mentioned writ petition, but got a series of suits filed through their lessees before the 1st Court of Subordinate Judge, Dhaka impleading the writ-petitioners as defendant Nos.27 and 34 respectively and respondent No.5 as pro-forma defendant No.55. Writ-petitioner No.2 was contesting those suits by filing written statements and to the knowledge of the petitioners, respondent No.5 was giving active support and assistance to the plaintiffs of those ongoing title suits in which they challenged the Gazette being No. ভুঃ মঃ/শাঃ-২(গঃ বিঃ)-৭৪-৯৫-৩৯২ dated 24-9-1996 in respect of RS Khatian No. 1600 more or less attracting the subject matter of the writ petition.

14. Appellant No.1 (writ-petitioner No.1) filed affidavit-in-reply against the affidavit-in-opposition filed by added respondent No.11 denying the statements, allegations and submissions made therein.

15. Respondent No.5 filed supplementary affidavit on 12-11-2005 making some statements and submissions which were strongly denied by writ-petitioner No.1 through her affidavit-in-reply on 19-11-2005.

16. A Division Bench hearing the parties by the impugned judgment and order discharged the Rule. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the judgment and order of the High Court Division, the writ-petitioners filed Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No.899 of 2008 before this Division and leave was granted to consider the following submissions:

"Mr. Rokonuddin Mahmud, learned Counsel, appearing for the petitioners submit-ted that after preparation and final publication and gazette notification of khatian on completion of all legal requirements as provided in State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 and the State Acquisition Rules, 1955 there was no scope for the respondent No.2 to reopen the issue on any pretext and in these circumstances, the High Court Division seriously erred in law in holding that the impugned memo is merely a communication from one office to another to perform certain official acts and committed gross injustice in discharging the Rule on the ground of maintainability alone without going to the merit of the case; that after publication of the official gazette notification under section 144(7) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 read with Rule 34(2) of the State Acquisition Rules, 1955, the record of right is to be presumed to be correct under Rule 35 of the said State Acquisition Rules which can only be declared incorrect by the competent memo issued by the respondent No.2 is without jurisdiction and is liable to be declared to have been made without lawful authority and is of no legal effect; that all the necessary parties were made parties in the writ petition and, as such, the case law referred to by the High Court Division are not applicable in the present case. The learned Counsel further submitted that having regard to the provision of rule 42 of the State Acquisition Rules, 1955 which vested the Revenue Officer appointed with additional designation of 'Settlement Officer' with the power to direct cancellation of any portion of the proceedings referred to in rules 28 to 30 in respect of any district or part of a district or local area at any time before publication of the final record of rights, the High Court Division was wrong in failing to hold that the impugned order passed by the respondent No.2 after publication of the gazette notification dated 24-9-1999 under section 144(7) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, which is final, directing the Settlement Officer to correct the record of right in favour of respondent No.5 upon finding that the direction dated 24-4-1996 to publish the record of rights in the name of the petitioner and others, ultra vires, the provision of the said rule 42 and is without lawful authority, arbitrary and malafide."

17. Mr. Shikder Moqbul Hoque, learned Advocate, appearing for the appellants, has canvassed the submissions on which leave was granted.

18. Mr. AJ Mohammad Ali learned Counsel, for respondent Nos.5 and 6, on the other hand, has supported the impugned judgment and order.

19. From the impugned judgment and order, it appears that the High Court Division discharged the Rule Nisi on the findings, inter alia, that: (i) The interest of the writ-petitioners (there were two writ-petitioners) in the case land was not stated in the writ petition; it was not clear what quantum of land belonged to each of them "singularly and/or jointly" and how they would be aggrieved if the survey records were amended pursuant to the impugned Memo; (ii) the impugned memo did not contain any quantum of land or mention any specific plot number or khatian number except referring to the land "as that recorded in the name of Capital Co-operative Housing Society Limited in Mouza-Uttar Khan"; (iii) the occupants and the owners of the land in question had not been made parties, if the Rule Nisi was made absolute as prayed for by the appellants, then all the persons in possession of the concerned land and the persons who claimed title thereof would be adversely affected. They also had a right to be heard before any order could be passed affecting their interest in the land, no one except certain officials connected with the Land Record and Survey and Capital Co-operative Housing Society Limited represented by its Chairman were made respondents; (iv) the appellants impugned memo No.Prati:21/97/576 dated 28-5-1997 issued under the signature of writ-respondent No.2, Director General, Directorate of Land Record and Survey, Tejgaon, Dhaka addressed to the Settlement Officer. Dhaka regarding correction of records in Mouza-Uttar Khan in the name of Capital Co-operative Housing Society Limited stating that the land survey records prepared as per rules in the name of Capital Co-operative Housing Society Limited was at the last stage for publication; that after hearing the appeal through an illegal order dated 25-4-1996 under rule 42 of the Rules, 1955, an order was passed for recording the said land in the name of some other persons; the Director General, Land Records and Survey, after enquiry found the said order illegal and gave direction for correction of the survey records as per the rules; (v) the impugned Memo was merely a communication from one office to another to perform certain official acts and that was not acted upon.

20. The High Court Division concluded that the writ petition was not maintainable and it, restrained itself "from going into its merits."

21. Though many facts are involved in the appeal, the same can be disposed of in a very short compass, namely, whether the High Court Division was correct in discharging the Rule Nisi on the ground of maintainability of the writ petition. The High Court Division in holding that the writ petition was not maintainable gave clear finding that the Memo challenged in the writ petition was not communicated to the writ-petitioners and, in fact, the same was not at all acted upon.

<u>22. The impugned memo was annexed to the writ petition as annexure-'F'. A perusal of the same shows that the same was not communicated to the writ-petitioners and it was a correspondence made by the Director-General of the Land Records and Land Survey, the Government of Bangladesh, Tejgaon to one of its Settlement Officer. In the writ petition, the writ-petitioners also made statements that—"As the writ-petitioners were not served upon any copy of the said memo dated 28-5-1997 they collected an attested copy thereof from the office of the respondent No. 1 and the same is annexed hereto and marked as annexure-'F'." From the above statements, it is clear that the impugned memo was not communicated to the writ-petitioners. Internal correspondence unless communicated to the person concerned cannot be the basis of cause of action for moving the High Court Division under its power of judicial review and we hold that since the copy of the impugned memo was not communicated to the writ-petitioners, no cause of action arose to seek any remedy challenging the said Memo.</u>

<u>23. It further appears that, in fact, no action was taken pursuant to the Memo impugned in the writ petition. Therefore, the writ-petitioners had no cause of action to invoke the writ jurisdiction of the High Court Division under article 102 of the Constitution. In the context, we state the law that though the provisions of Code of Civil Procedure are not as such applicable in the case of a writ petition, the principle of the provisions of the Code of Civil Procedure can be borrowed in deciding a writ petition like the provisions of Order VII, rule 11, clause (a) thereof. In the absence of the cause of action, the writ petition was not maintainable in law and therefore, the High Court Division did not commit any error of law in discharging the Rule Nisi on the view that the writ petition was not maintainable. In the context, the High Court Division rightly relied upon the case of Kamaluddin vs Bangladesh, 56 (AD) 212. However, we are of the view that if any action is taken affecting the right of the petitioners in the lands in question pursuant to the memo impugned in the writ petition, they shall have every right to challenge the said action by resorting to appropriate forum including the writ jurisdiction of the High Court Division.</u>

With the above observations, this appeal is dismissed.

End.
