During all this period the plaintiff-bank could not produce the concerned bank statement or any other document to prove payment to the beneficiary constituting completion of negotiation although this is the very allegation raised on behalf of the defendant-bank both in its written statement as well as in the deposition adduced on their behalf.

50. It is a well established principle that the plaintiff has to prove its own case on preponderance of evidence but from the discussions made above it would be too apparent that the plaintiff-bank although fully aware of the requirement of payment to effect negotiation, did not take any step to prove so, as such, they should also be prepared for the inevitable legal consequence for such lapse on their part.

51. The learned Counsel for the plaintiff- respondent lastly, contends that the learned Judge in the trial Court found the negotiation to be proved.

52. It appears, that the learned Judge at the first instance, accepted the documents marked Exhibits 2, 4, 5, 6 and 9 as proof of negotiation and claiming reimbursement. We have also gone through those documents. The telexes Exhibit 2 and Exhibit 4 were from HBL, Dubai to HBL, NY. the telex Exhibit 3 was from HBL, NY to AMEX NY, the telex Exhibit 5 was from HBL, NY to HBL, Dubai, the telex Exhibit 6 was from HBL, Dubai to NBL, Khulna, the telex Exhibit 9 was from AMEX, NY to HBL, NY. These telexes were exchanged in connection with the reimbursement claim of the plaintiff-bank but had nothing to do with negotiation. As a matter of fact, although the learned Judge framed certain questions in this regard but completely overlooked these all important questions in its proper perspective as to what constitutes a negotiation. Whether the ingredients or incidents of negotiation were established in this case and whether the plaintiff bank at all comes within the description of negotiable bank.

53. Since, the plaintiff-respondent failed to prove payment to the beneficiary, their claim of negotiation of the draft and the documents failed and they are not entitled to the decree as prayed for. Their suit is liable to be dismissed.

54. Under the circumstances, the decree in the Money Suit No. 108 of 1990, in the Court of Subordinate Judge, Second Commercial Court, Dhaka, is set aside and the suit is dismissed.

55. The First Appeal No. 204 of 1993 arises out of the Title Suit No. 56 of 1987. The suit was decreed on contest against the defendant No. 1 (NBL, Khulna), Defendant No.4 (Aquamarine Ltd), defendant No.5 (Navegadora Panocenica SA) and defendant No.6 (Shuwa Kaiun Kaisha Ltd.) It was declared that the defendant No. 5 is not entitled to  get their claimed amount from the plaintiff in respect of the letter of credit, and that the defendant No. 1 would not pay any amount in respect of LC No. 7-9-86 dated 3-3-1986, in favour of the defendant No. 5 or their banker or representative. The defendant No. 1 was further directed to repay the plaintiff the rest of the money paid by him earlier to the defendant No. 1 after deduction of interest from the date of opening of the LC till the plaintiff instructed the defendant No. 1 to stop payment on the LC. Only the defendant No. 1 (NBL Khulna) filed the appeal.

56. In this appeal Dr M Zahir, the learned Advocate on behalf of the appellant, frankly submits that the NBL, Khulna, held up the margin money of Taka 35,00 lakh only because of their apprehension that in case the claims of the HBL, Dubai is allowed, which, according to them, they were not entitled to, they will have to pay them the said entire claimed amount which includes the aforesaid margin money, as such, they resisted the claims of the plaintiff. But the learned Advocate candidly concedes that if the claims of the HBL, Dubai, is not allowed, then of course, the NBL, Khulna, has no right to the said margin money.

57. We have already held in FA No. 202 of 1993 that the HBL, Dubai, is not entitled to the decree in the Money Suit No.108 of 1990, based on the LC No. 7-9-1986 dated 3-3-1986, as such, the NBL, Khulna, the said LC issuing bank, can no longer hold Taka 35,00 lakh received from the plaintiff in Title Suit No. 56 of 1987, at the time of opening of the aforesaid letter of credit as margin money. This will, apart from everything else, be unjust enrichment on the part of the defendant No. 1. This is also conceded to by Dr M Zahir. Under such circumstances, the appeal is liable to be dismissed.

58. In the result, the FA No. 202 of 1993 is allowed while the FA No. 204 of 1993 is dismissed.

59. In the circumstances, there shall be no order of costs in any of the appeals.

Send down the lower Court records forthwith.

End.

caseno: First Miscellaneous Appeal No.135 of 2001 with Civil Rule No.384 (FM)/2001
lawyer:
Nazibur Rahman, Advocate ----- For the Appellant. 
Shafique Ahmed, Advocate ----- For the Respondents.
parties:
Shah Alam (Md) ----- Appellant
Vs 
Md Shahidur Rahman and others  ----- Respondents
full_judgment:
Sheikh Rezowan Ali, J: This First Miscellaneous Appeal is directed against the judgment and order dated 28-2-2001 passed by the learned Subordinate Judge, 1st Court, Rangpur in Miscellaneous Case No. 25 of 1995 (a proceeding under section 24 of the Non-Agricultural Tenancy Act) disallowing the pre-emption.

2. Facts relevant for the purpose of disposal of this appellant, in short, are that 0.0913 acre of land appertaining to plot No. 4376 of CS Khatian No. 883 and 0.1087 acre of land appertaining to plot No of CS khatian No.881 (both the khatians now corresponding to RS khatian No. 757), containing 0.20 acre of land of mouja Radhaballav, police station and district Rangpur (as described in the schedule Ka of the pre-emption petition) belonged to one Hafez Mohammad Hossain Sowdagar who died leaving opposite party Nos. 2-10 as his heirs and heiresses. Subsequently, opposite party Nos. 5 and 6 transferred 0.0833 acre of land to the pre- emptor petitioner Shah Alam by a registered kabala dated 16-4-1992 whereby he became a co-sharer to the pre-emption petition Ka schedule land. Later, opposite party Nos. 2 and 3 transferred the case land, 0.0467 in area, as described in the schedule Kha of the pre-emption petition to the pre-emptee opposite party No.1 by a kabala dated 23-11-1994 beyond the knowledge of the pre-emptor petitioner and without service of notice upon him. Under the circumstances he sought pre-emption of the case land under section 24 of the Non-Agricultural Tenancy Act.

3. Pre-emptee opposite party No.1 contested the case by filing a written objection contending, inter alia, that the pre-emptor petitioner was not a co-sharer in the case land inasmuch as pursuant to his purchase of 0.0833 acre of land from opposite party Nos. 5 and 6 in the year 1992 he got his name mutated in respect of the said land vide Mutation Case No.1354/1992-1993 and thereby ceased to be a co-sharer in respect of the case land. He had thus no locus standi to pre-empt the case land.

4. During the course of trial pre-emptor petitioner examined 3 witnesses while the contesting pre-emptee opposite party No.1 examined 4 witnesses.

5. It deserves mention here that earlier by a judgment and order dated 26-2-1997 learned Subordinate Judge, 1st Court, Rangpur disallowed pre-emption in the instant Miscellaneous Case No. 25 of 1995. Being aggrieved the pre-emptor petitioner preferred First Miscellaneous Appeal No.121 of 1997 which was heard by this Court. It was categorically contended by the petitioner therein that he. did not ever submit any petition seeking mutation of the land purchased by him from the opposite party Nos. 5 and 6 in 1992 and that all the papers that came before the court below in that connection were fabricated. It then appeared to this Court that the proceeding record of the said mutation case was not produced before the court below for considering its legality, regularity or otherwise. In order to dispel doubt about it this Court sent the case on remand to the court below asking it to cause production of the mutation case record before it and determine the said allegation raised by the petitioner appellant. The learned court below was also instructed to dispose of the case within 3 months from the date of receipt of judgment and order of this Court. Learned Judge, it appears, made a persistent endeavour to cause production of the said case record before him but it did not come. Concerned Assistant Commissioner (Land) reported that the said mutation proceeding record was not available on search and might have gone missing at the time of shifting of his earlier office from Sadar Upazilla premises to its new premises. However, the learned Judge by placing full reliance upon the Mutation Register (Exhibit- Gha), 2 Rent Collection Registers (exhibit Uma, Uma-(1), Duplicate Carbon Receipt Book (exhibit Cha) showing realisation of mutation fees, etc and Rent Receipt Book (exhibit Chha) found that such mutation did, indeed, take place and that the petitioner thereby ceased to be a co-sharer in the case land. He had, therefore, no locus standi to claim pre-emption under section 24 of the Non- Agricultural Tenancy Act. Accordingly, the learned Judge disallowed the pre-emption petition.

6. Being aggrieved by the impugned judgment and order of the court below dated 28-2-2001 the pre-emptor petitioner has preferred the instant appeal.

<u>7. Mr. Nazibur Rahman, learned Advocate for the petitioner-appellant, has repeated the selfsame argument as he did earlier by pointing out before this Court that the proceeding record of the mutation case having not been produced before the court below it could be presumed that no genuine mutation did, indeed, take place and that all those registers and receipt books produced in support of such mutation were wholly unreliable and the learned Judge should not have relied upon those documents and disallowed the pre-emption petition. Further, according to him, original co-sharership in the land does not extinguish without a partition being made in pursuance of a final decree passed in a regularly constituted suit for partition and, therefore, the petitioner appellant did not cease to be a co-sharer in the case land in absence of such partition and lose his right of pre-emption. To illustrate his submission he has cited a decision in the case of Md Shafiuddin Chowdhury vs Md Abdul Karim and others reported in 52 DLR (AD) 41.</u>

<u>8. Mr Shafique Ahmed, learned Advocate for the pre-emptee respondent, on the other hand, has submitted that mutation related receipt books and register produced in the court below were genuine documents and were sufficiently indicative of a mutation having taken place in the name of the petitioner-appellant thereby extinguishing his former co-shareship and divesting him of his right of pre-emption of the case land. It was, therefore, hardly of any substance, he submits, if the mutation case record did not come up before the court because of its having gone missing at the time of shifting of the office of the Assistant Commissioner (Land) as reported by the concerned Assistant Commissioner duly endorsed by the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue), Rangpur. According to him, learned Judge thus correctly held that his co-sharership in the case land having extinguished earlier he had no locus standi to claim pre-emption of the said land. In order to substantiate his submission that splitting up of jama extinguishes original co-sharership he has cited a decision in the case of Sunil Krishna Banik and others vs Kailas Chandra Saha and others reported in BCR 1984 (AD) 243 = 36 DLR (AD) 220.</u>

9. We have perused the materials on record and have also given our anxious consideration to the submissions made by the learned Advocates for both the sides.

10. By now it is well-settled that for the purpose of pre-emption under section 24(1) of the Non-Agricultural Tenancy Act co-sharership in the land' is material. A co-sharer in the land becomes entitled to pre-empt under section 24(1) of the Act if any portion of such land is transferred to a stranger. A pertinent question, however, involved in the instant appeal, is whether the petitioner-appellant, who became a co-sharer in the case land by purchase of a portion thereof earlier, ceased to be a co-sharer therein by getting his portion separated through a mutation proceeding opening a separate jama in his name and whether his co-sharership in the land could not be treated to have ceased without partition of his portion by a final decree passed in a regularly constituted suit for partition.

<u>11. The decision in the case of Sunil Krishna Banik and others vs Kailash Chandra Saha and others reported in BCR 1984 (AD) 243, which related to a proceeding under section 24 of the Non-Agricultural Tenancy Act, reveals that in the trial Court the pre-emptees raised a plea of disability of the pre-emptor to pre-empt the case land on the ground of his having lost his co-sharership in the holding by separation of his jama through a mutation proceeding. In support of such separation the pre-emptees produced two rent receipts, two municipal tax receipts and another document (not specified) which were received by the trial Court as exhibits A, A (1), B, B (1) and C respectively but the learned Judge declined to consider them in his judgment because of their belated production and eventually allowed pre-emption. Being aggrieved the pre-emptees preferred an appeal before the High Court Division and during the pendency of the appeal filed an application under Order XLI, rule 27 of the Code of Civil Procedure by annexing certified copies of application for separation of old jama which initiated two mutation proceedings, orders passed in the said mutation proceedings separating the old holding and two newly opened khatians as annexures A, A (1), B, B(1) and C, C(1) respectively and prayed for receiving the said documents as additional evidence regarding separation of the said jama. But the appellate High Court Division refused to receive them, as such, and dismissed the appeal. On appeal, their Lordships of the Appellate Division observed" the evidence offered by the appellants to prove that the respondent was no longer a co-sharer was already produced before the trial Court, but this was done only at a late stage of the trial. The evidence was not considered by the trial Court for this reason. It was not produced for the first time before the appellate Court. On the other hand, the exhibits referred to in their application for additional evidence could, if considered according to the appellants, have shown that the respondents had ceased to be co-sharers, particularly when the necessary issue to determine this point was already framed by the trial Court. "With the aforesaid observation their Lordships allowed the appeal and sent the case on remand to the High Court Division for disposal in accordance with law. The aforesaid observation by their Lordships left a clear indication that a co-sharer loses his co-sharership in the tenancy or holding by separating his jama through a mutation proceeding and cannot apply for pre-emption.</u>

<u>12. In the aforesaid decision reported in BCR 1984 (AD) 243 reference was also made to another decision in the case of Md Mafizuddin Patwari vs Abdul Hakim Miazi reported in 33 DLR (AD) 305 wherein it was held that an original co-sharer who ceased to be a co-sharer of the jama cannot apply for pre-emption. It was further held that a co-sharer seeking pre-emption must have a subsisting interest in the holding at the time when he files an application for pre-emption and must continue to hold such interest until the case is finally disposed. It will not be out of place to mention here that separation of jama or sub-division of a holding or tenancy distributing rent whether in the case of agricultural land under State Acquisition and Tenancy Act or in the case of non-agricultural land under Non-Agricultural Tenancy Act, takes place under section 117(1)(c) of State Acquisition and Tenancy Act and the original co-sharers on such separation cease to be co-sharers as such and cannot apply for pre-emption on the ground of co-sharership. The principle is equally applicable in both the cases of agricultural and non-agricultural land.</u>

<u>13. Mr Nazibur Rahman, learned Advocate for the appellant, has, however, drawn our attention, as stated earlier, to a decision in the case of Shafiuddin Chowdhury vs Md. Abdul Karim reported in 52 DLR (AD) 41 wherein it has been enunciated by their Lordships in the concluding paragraph passing of the final decree in a partition suit finally determines the rights of the co-sharers in the land. Hence, the application for the pre-emptor respondents on the basis of co-sharership is not maintainable." Supporting the above view learned Advocate for the appellant has tried to impress upon us that a co-sharer does not cease to be a co-sharer in the land forfeiting his right of pre-emption until his portion has been partitioned by a decree passed in a regularly constituted partition suit and that separation of jam a has nothing to do with termination of his co-sharership debarring him of his right of pre-emption. But a contrary view has been expressed in a decision in the case of SM Basiruddin vs Zahurul Islam Chowdhury and another reported in 35 DLR (AD) 230 wherein it has been held by their Lordships of the Appellate Division, "Partition of the land amongst co-sharers on the basis of Civil Court decree does not bring about the division of the tenancy having the same jama." Consequently, we find, co-sharership in the land does not terminate on partition and right of pre-emption is not lost unless the jama has been split up in accordance with law. Placing reliance upon the said decision reported in 35 DLR (AD) 230 a Division Bench of this court in its decision in the case of SM Nasirul Haque vs Omar Faruque Chowdhury and others, reported in 7 MLR 46 = 54 DLR 181, reiterated, "A final decree passed in a partition suit or amicable partition though separates and divides the land for the purpose of possession but does not ipso facto terminate co-ownership in such land till subdivision of the holding and distribution of rents takes place only in accordance with law." In our natural anxiety to be cautious in dispensing justice we have meticulously found that the decision reported in 35 DLR (AD) 230 was not brought to the notice of their Lordships when they were pronouncing the decision in the case of Shafiuddin Chowdhury vs Md. Abdul Karim reported in 52 DLR (AD) 41 propagating forfeiture of right of pre-emption on account of a final decree being passed in a suit for partition extinguishing co-sharership in the land. It does not also appear to us that their Lordships expressed any disapproval of separation of jama as a recognised form of extinction of co-sharership in the land debarring right of pre-emption. So, in our view, separation of jama also terminates co- sharership.</u>

14. Now let us consider if, on the basis of the materials and evidence on record, learned court below correctly held that the petitioner-appellant separated his jama in respect of the land which he purchased from the opposite party Nos. 5 and 6 in the year 1992 and lost his right of pre-emption of the case land. Exhibit Gha, Mutation Register, clearly shows that mutation was approved in his name in respect of 0.0833 acre of land appertaining to the pre-emption petition schedule Ka land under the signature of Assistant Commissioner (Land) on 28-6-1993 vide Mutation Case No. 1354/92-93 DCR book of the year 1992/1993 (Exhibit Cha) shows that mutation fees and other fees amounting to Taka 28.50 were realised from him in connection with mutation case No.1354/92/-93 wherein a separate Khatian being No. 8399 with a jama of Taka 55.76 was opened anew in his name on 13-6-1993. Exhibit Chha, Rent Receipt Book, shows that land development tax ranging from 1396 BS to 1401 BS amounting to Taka 1163.50 paisa was realised from him on 23-1-1995 in respect of the said mutated Khatian being No.8399. Rent Collection Registers (Exhibit Uma, Uma (1) also carried particulars of such collection. By placing reliance on the said documents the learned Judge found that the petitioner-appellant, indeed, got his name mutated in 1993 in respect of the land which he purchased out of the case jote in the year of 1992 and already ceased to be a co-sharer in the case land when it was sold to the pre-emptee respondent No.1 in 1994. The aforesaid entries found place in those registers and receipt books in the usual course of business carried out by the public functionaries in the regular discharge of their duties. They have, therefore, presumptive value unless rebutted. The petitioner- appellant could not furnish any cogent evidence rebutting the same. Learned Judge rightly found that the petitioner-appellant had the opportunity to challenge the mutation proceeding to be a collusive and fictitious one by citing any of the co-sharers as a witness to prove that no notice was issued upon any of them in respect of mutation case No.1354/92-93 wherein his name was shown to have been mutated in respect of the land he purchased out of the case jote in 1992. But he refrained, which was quite meaningful. The learned Judge who closely scrutinised those registers and receipt books expressed with a profound belief that he found them to be genuine documents. There was thus overwhelming evidence on record showing a mutation case being No 13454/1992-1993 to have been legally started and completed at his instance opening a new Khatian bearing No. 8399 with a jama Taka 55.76 in his name on 13-6-1993 in respect of the land he purchased in 1992. It was not, therefore, much worthy of consideration if the mutation proceeding case record did not come before the court below on account of the circumstances, mention of which we have made earlier. The learned Judge thus rightly held that the petitioner having ceased to be a co-sharer in the case land he had no locus standi to claim pre-emption under section 24 of the Non-Agricultural Tenancy Act.

15. We do not find any illegality to have been committed by the learned Judge in disallowing the pre-emption petition. It does not call for any interference by this court in its revisional jurisdiction.

16. In the result, the appeal is dismissed with costs. The impugned judgment and order dated 28- 2-2001 passed by the learned Subordinate Judge, 1st Court, Rangpur in Miscellaneous Case No. 25 of 1995 (a proceedings under section 24 of the Non-Agricultural Tenancy Act) disallowing pre-emption is hereby upheld.

Connected Rule No. 384 (FM) 2002 is discharged accordingly. Communicate the order to the court below at once. Send down the lower court records along with a copy of this judgment expeditiously.

End.

lawyer:
Humayun Kabir; Advocate ----- For the Petitioner.
ASM Nazmul Hoque, DAG with Md Jahangir Alam, AAG Md Abdur Rahman Howlader, AAG ----- For the Respondents.
parties:
Nurun Nabir Sarker (Md) ----- Petitioner
Vs.
Secretary, Ministry of Education and others -----Respondents
full_judgment:
Md Rezaul Hasan J: In this petition, 'filed under Article 102 of the Constitution, a Rule has been issued calling upon the respondents to show cause as to why respondents No.3 to.5 shall not be directed to dispose of the application filed by the petitioner on 22-3-20 15 before them (Annexure-C to the application), praying for taking necessary action against the order of suspension of the petitioner from his service as the Headmaster. UzanTeura TUM High School, Sundargonj, Gaibandha under rule 38(3) of the মাধ্যমিক ও উচ্চ মাধ্যমিক শিক্ষা বোর্ড, দিনাজপুর (মাধ্যমিক ও উচ্চ মাধ্যমিক স্তরের বেসরকারী শিক্ষাপ্রতিষ্ঠানের গভর্নিংবডি ও ম্যানেজিং কমিটি) প্রবিধানমালা, ২০০৯ and/or pass such other or further order or orders as to this Court may seem fit and proper.

2. Fact relevant for the disposal of this Rule, in brief, are that the petitioner applied for the post of Headmaster, in response to the advertisement published by the concerned authority and that a duly constituted selection committee selected the petitioner to be appointed for the said post and consequently the petitioner has joined the said School, on 11-4-1999, pursuant to the appointment letter dated 7-4-1999 issued by the Chairman of the Managing Committee UzanTeura TUM High School, Sundargonj, Gaibandha, and since then he has been discharging his duties honestly, sincerely and to the full satisfaction of the authority concerned; that the name of the petitioner was enlisted in the monthly pay order (MPO) from May, 1995, being Index No. 258346, and since then he has been receiving government portion of his monthly salary and other financial benefit regularly. without any interruption, till to date; that without complying the mandatory provisions of the Recognised Non-Government School Teachers (Board of Intermediate and Secondary Education, Rajshahi)Terms And Conditions of Service Regulations, 1979" and with a malafide intention, the Managing Committee of the said school took a decision on 12-10-2014 to suspend the petitioner from his service; that the Governing Body of the said School has failed to conclude the proceedings against the petitioner in compliance with the provisions of the Regulation- 11,12,13 and 14 of the said Regulation, 1979; that on 22-3- 2015 the petitioner filed an application before the Chairman, the Secretary and the Inspector of Schools, Board of Intermediate and Secondary Education, Dinajpur, (respondent No.3, 4 & 5) requesting them to take necessary action against the order of suspension of the petitioner from his service as the Headmaster, UzanTeura TUM High School, Sundargonj, Gaibandha under Regulation-38 (3) of the মাধ্যমিক ও উচ্চ মাধ্যমিক শিক্ষা বোর্ড, দিনাজপুর (মাধ্যমিক ও উচ্চ মাধ্যমিক স্তরের বেসরকারী শিক্ষা প্রতিষ্ঠানের গভর্নিংবডি ও ম্যানেজিংকমিটি) প্রবিধানমালা, ২০০৯ but the respondents remained silent without considering the prayer of the petitioner and without giving any reply; that though the said application has duly been received by the office of the Chairman, the Secretary and the Inspector of Schools, Board of Intermediate and Secondary Education, Dinajpur (respondent Nos. 3, 4 & 5), but they did not take any steps in respect the matter till to date that it is humbly submitted that the inordinate delay of the respondents to dispose of the application filed by the petitioner on 22-3-2015 is illegal, malafide and arbitrarily and, as such the inordinate delay of the respondents to dispose of the application filed by the petitioner on 22-3-2015 is required to be declared to have been done without any lawful authority and is of no legal effect; that it is the statutory duty of the respondents to dispose of the application filed by the petitioner within a reasonable time and, as such the respondents are required to be directed to dispose of the application filed by the petitioner without making any delay; that the action of the respondents in not disposing the application filed by the petitioner on 1-10-2013 (ANNEXURE-C) is malafide, arbitrarily and amounts to refusal to exercise their jurisdiction and hence, the respondents are required to be directed to dispose of the application filed by the petitioner without making any delay; that being aggrieved by the action of the respondents in not disposing the application filed by the petitioner on 22-3-2015 praying for taking necessary action against the order of suspension of the petitioner from his service as the Headmaster, Uzan Teura TUM High School, Sundargonj, Gaibandha under Regulation-38 (3) of the মাধ্যমিক ও উচ্চ মাধ্যমিক শিক্ষা বোর্ড, দিনাজপুর (মাধ্যমিক ও উচ্চ মাধ্যমিক স্তরের বেসরকারী শিক্ষা প্রতিষ্ঠানের গভর্নিংবডি ও ম্যানেজিং কমিটি) প্রবিধানমালা, ২০০৯ (ANNEXURE)-C) and finding no other equally efficacious alternative remedy available in law your humble petitioner begs to file this petition under Article 1 02(2)(a)(i) & (ii) of the Constitution on the following amongst others. Hence this petition.

3. The learned advocate, appearing for the petitioner, Mr. Humayun Kabir having placed the petition along with the documents annexed there-With, and first up all submits that the petitioner is the Headmaster of Uzan Teura TUM High School Sundargonj, Gaibandha. The learned advocate further submits that the petitioner was appointed in said post after compliance of all formalities and procedure as required by the concerned Rules and Regulations. He next submits that the name of the petitioner has been enlisted in the Monthly Pay Order (MPO) for May, 1995, being index No. 258346, and since then he has been receiving the govern portion of his monthly salary and other financial benefits regularly, without any interruption, till today. But, without compliance with the provisions of "The Recognised Non-Government School Teachers (Board of Intermediate and Secondary Education, Rajshahi Terms and Conditions of Service Regulations, 1979" the petitioner was suspended by the Managing Committee on 12-10-2014. with a malafide intention. But they have not initiated any departmental proceeding against the petitioner by way of issuing any show cause notice or charge sheet, although the petitioner has been kept under suspension till today without apprising him as to what was his fault and without bringing any allegation against him, by issuing show cause notice, as required by. Regulations 11 and 12 of the above mentioned Regulation. Thereafter the petitioner filed an application on 22-3-2015 to the Chairman of the Board of Intermediate and Secondary Education (respondent No.3,4 and 5) seeking appropriate remedy in the background of the hardship and sufferings he has been put to by the aforesaid illegal order of suspension, but they remained silent. He further submits that, it is statutory duty of the respondent Nos. 3,4 and 5 i.e the Chairman, the Secretary and the inspector of the Schools, Board of Intermediate and Secondary Education. Dinajpur, to disposed of the said representation date 22-3-2015 within a reasonable time by giving direction upon the Managing Committee and that the board has power under Regulation No. 38(3) of the aforesaid Regulation of 2009. He further submits that, in the manner aforesaid, the fundamental right to be treated and accordance with law, as guaranteed to the petitioner by Article 31 read with Article 44 of the Constitution, has been denied to him. Accordingly he has prayed for-appropriate direction. In support of his contention, the learned advocate has referred to the decisions reported in 2012 (XX) BLT (AD) 239: Bangladesh Live Stock Research Institute vs Dr Md Jahangir A lam Khan; 60 DLR 40: Zulfiker Mahmud vs National University and has also placed an unreported judgment dated 9-3- 2014 passed in Writ Petition No. 1897 of 2014:

Md Jashimuddin vs Government of the PRE. He has prayed making the Rule absolute in the facts and circumstances of this case.

4. The Learned Deputy Attorney-General Mr ASM Nazmul Hoque a appearing along with the learned Assistant Attorney-General Mr Md Jahangir Alam, has found in the difficult to show as to why the board is to not be directed to the disposed of the petitioner's representation date 22-3- 2015 (Annexure-C) within reasonable time to be fixed by this court.

5. .Heard the learned advocates for both sides, perused the writ petition including the materials on record and also consulted the law cited before us.

6. We find from that the materials on record that the petitioner has been appointed as Headmaster of the concerned School after compliance with all the procedure as laid down in the concerned Rules and Regulations. His name has been listed in the MPO from May, 1995. We also find that the petitioner has been suspended on 12- 10-2014 (Annexure-B), but no time has been mentioned in the said letter as to the period of suspension. On the other hand we do not find any materials on record that the governing body has initialed any disciplinary proceeding against the petitioner, though it has kept the petitioner under suspension for in definite period.

7. In our consider view, this order of suspension dated 12-10-2014 bearing Memo No. উ/তে/বি/০২/১৪ (Annexure-B) does not mention any period for which the petitioner has been suspended or kept under suspension. Similarly, we do not find any material on record showing that the petitioner has been suspended pending any disciplinary proceeding or that any disciplinary proceeding has been initiated following the order/letter of suspension dated 12-10-2014.

8. In our considered view, this act of Respondent No. 7 tantamount to colorable exercise of the power, violation of the petitioner's fundamental right to be treated in accordance with law. We are also of the view that in order to be a valid suspension order the same must contain the period for which the incumbent shall remain suspended and such suspension order can only be issued pending a disciplinary proceeding. But, neither of these two conditions are met or found present in the letter/order of suspension dated 12-10-2014. The respondent No.7 is not authorised by law to issue such an order or letter. Hence, this order/letter of suspension is bound to be declared to have been issued without any lawful authority and is of no legal effect. But, the petitioner has neither prayed for any relief under Article 102(1) for violation of his fundamental right, nor prayed for issuing any supplementary Rule challenging the suspension letter dated 12-10-2014.

9. We also find that the petitioner made a representation to the Board on 22-3-2015, giving the facts and particulars in the detail and pointing out that the Managing Committee did not follow the provisions Regulations No. 13(a), 14(a) and 14(b) of the above mentioned Service Regulations, 1979 as well as they have violated the provisions of the Regulations No. 33(5), 33(6), 35(1) and 35(4) of Governing Body and Managing Committee Regulations, 2009.

10. Sub-regulation (3) of regulations 38 reads as follows:-

৩৮। গভর্নিংবডি বা ক্ষেত্রমত, ম্যানেজিংকমিটি বাতিলকরন ইত্যাদি:- (১)........................................................

(২).....................................................................................................................................................

(৩০) বোর্ড স্বপ্রণোদিত হইয়া বা সরকারের নির্দেশে গভনিংবর্ডি বা ক্ষেত্রমত, ম্যানেজিং কমিটির যে কোন কার্য বিষয়ের অনুমোদন করিতে কিংবা কোন অভিযোগের বিষয়ে তদন্ত করিতে পারিবেন এবং সংশ্লিষ্ট রেকর্ডপত্র তলব করিতে পারিবে।

<u>11. As such, in our considered view, the board has authority to examine any order or decision passed by the Governing Body or Managing Committee of the educational institution placed under it's supervision and control and to pass appropriate order, though this cannot be treated as an efficacious alternative remedy.</u>

<u>12. We are also of the considered view that in order to prevent malafide exercise of power, to ensure equitable and fair treatment to all employees, including the petitioner, this court should declare law as contemplated under Article III of the Constitution, to put an end to this unjust situation and shall fix a period as to how long a person can be kept suspended pending inquiry, when such suspension is not imposed as penal measures. According, we declare that in the absence of any law providing, otherwise, no person shall be kept under suspension beyond 60 (sixty) days from the date of his/her suspension. If the suspension continues for further period, exceeding 60(sixty) days, then the person suspended shall be entitled to receive full pay, instead of subsistence allowance, till the suspension order/letter ends up in a final order.</u>

13. Next, we also record that, for the conducts noted above, the Chairman and other members of the Managing Committee as well as the concerned official of the board should have been compensated, for their inaction that in fact amounts to gross neglect of duty.

<u>14. We are also of the view that government officials are conferred powers not to victimize innocent person or teacher. They are bound to dis- charge their duties as fairly and as provided in law. Their findings should be based on materials on the record. They should take into consideration all material facts in taking any decision or step. Their bonafide and neutrality must be visible at the first sight. They are not permitted to secure unlawful gain to their selves or to any other person. Nor they are permitted to act unreasonably, disproportionately, discriminatorily, arbitrarily, whimsically or to resort to colorable exercise of their power. They will lose indemnity if they don't act bonafide.</u>

15. We find merit in this Rule.

Order

16. Accordingly this Rule is made absolute.

17. In consequence, the Chairman, Board of Intermediate and Secondary Education. Dinajpur is hereby directed to dispose of this application within 10(ten) working days from the date of receiving copy of this judgment and order to ensure that the Governing body/Managing Committee follows the procedure laid 'down in aforesaid Regulation, 1979. He should also keep in mind the guidelines provided herein above the Chairman is directed to file an affidavit of compliance within 15 days thereafter to this court, through the .learned Registrar of the High Court Division.

18. Since the petitioner or any other person cannot be kept suspended for indefinite period, therefore, as consequential order and to secure ends of justice the respondent No. 7 and the respondents No.1, 2 and 6 are hereby directed to ensure the full payment or the balance amount of the full payment of the petitioner's salary, due after expiry of 60 (sixty) days from 12-10-2014, within 30 (thirty) days of receiving copy of this judgment and order.

19. The respondent No.7, Chairmen of the Managing Committee, is hereby directed to pay of Taka 10,000 (then thousand only) as cost to the petitioner within 15 (fifteen) days from the date of receiving copy of this judgment and order and to file an affidavit of compliance within 15 (fifteen) days thereafter, through the learned Registrar of the High Court Division.

20. Let a copy of the judgment and order be sent to the respondent No.3 and 7 at the expenses of the petitioner and two other copies be sent to the secretaries Ministry of Education and to the Secretary Ministry of Primary and Mass Education, Bangladesh Secretariat, to issue directives or circular upon all Chairman and the Director Generals, as the case may be, in the light of the law declared in paragraph 12 herein above. They should ensure compliance as required under the provisions of Article 112 of the Constitution of the People's Republic of Bangladesh and submit an affidavit of compliance through the learned Registrar of the High Court Division, within 30 (thirty) working days of receiving copies of this judgment and order.

End.

lawyer:
Moynul Hossain with Jahedul Islam, Advocates ------For the Petitioner. 
Md. Khurshid Alam Khan, Advocate ------ For the Respondent No. 1.
parties:
Abdus Salam (Md.) ------ Petitioner
Vs.
Anti-Corruption Commission, represented by its 
Chairman and others ------ Respondents
full_judgment:
M Enayetur Rahim, J: By filing this application under Article 102 of the Constitution of the People's Republic of Bangladesh the petitioner has challenged the Notice as contained in Memo No. 44565 dated 6-11-2016 (Annexure-A) issued by the Respondent No. 2 purportedly under section 26 of the Anti-Corruption Commission Act, 2004 (hereinafter referred to as Act of 2004).

2. In the application it is contended that the petitioner, an Ex-Chairman of Ekushey Television Ltd. while is in detention in central jail, Dhaka in connection with some criminal cases, on 16-10-2016 a notice under section 26(1) of the Act of 2004 bearing memo No. 44565 along with a form under rule 17(2) of the Anti-Corruption Commission Rules, 2007 was issued under the signature of Respondent No. 2 directing him to submit statement of all moveable and immovable properties in his name and in benami, liabilities, source of income and detailed statement within 7 (seven) days of receipt of the said notice, since the Respondent No. 1, Anti-Corruption Commission on the basis of receipt of information and enquiry reached firm belief that the petitioner had amassed huge amount of wealth and property in his name and in benami and owning the same, which is beyond his known source of income. The jail authority served the notice upon the petitioner on 5-2-2016.

3. Being aggrieved by the said notice the petitioner has filed this application.

4. Mr. Moynul Hossain, the learned Advocate, appearing with Mr. Jahedul Islam, the learned Advocate, for the writ petitioner submits that the impugned notice is without lawful authority and is of no legal effect as the same being served upon a detenue who has no way to access his papers so as to give accurate reply to the same failing which he faces threat of three years imprisonment is a nullity and not a notice contemplated under section 26 of the Act of 2004.

5. In this connection Mr. Hossain referred to the case of Anti-Corruption Commission vs Dr. Mohiuddin Khan Alamgir, reported in 62 DLR (AD) 290.

6. He further submits that along with the notice the Anti-Corruption Commission ought to have furnished the report of the inquiry on the basis of which the notice was issued and the petitioner has a right to get the said report of inquiry to give proper reply of the impugned notice.

7. We have also heard Mr. Khurshid Alam Khan, the learned Advocate for the Respondent No. 1.

8. Heard the learned Advocate for the parties, perused the impugned notice and other materials annexured to the application.

9. In the case of Moudud Ahmed vs. State (heard along with four other Appeals), reported in 68 DLR (AD) 118 Appellate Division has reviewed some of the observations made in the case of Anti-Corruption Commission vs. Mohiuddin Khan Alamgir, reported in 62 DLR (AD) 290.

10. In the above case Appellate Division has observed to the effect:

"In the case reported in 62 DLR (AD) 290 the learned Advocate for the ACC failed to make proper submissions in respect of the issues involved in the case. Because of the learned Advocate's failure to make correct sub-missions in assisting the court properly at the time of hearing of the leave petition this Division made some passing observations by the way in paragraph Nos. 44 and 45, in the absence of argument, without reference to the relevant provisions of law, which have no relevance or bearing in the disposal of the case and those observations have not arisen in such a manner as to require a decision in the disposal of the matter. Even some of the observations in paragraph Nos. 44 and 45 do not reflect the correct principle of law in view of the discussions made and decisions cited herein above and all these observations made in paragraph Nos. 44 and 45 are obiter dictum and some of the observations do not depict the correct principle of law and cannot be justified by the relevant provisions of law"

And

"In the instant case there is no difficulty in reviewing the decision of this Division in the case reported in 62 DLR (AD) 290 and passing necessary order with regard to the aforesaid observations made in paragraph Nos. 44 and 45 of the judgment and order of this Division passed in the Criminal Petition for leave Appeal No. 398 of 2009."

<u>11. In the above case the Appellate Division has held that if the notice is served upon a detenue by the Commission is valid one and on the plea of detention there is no scope to say that the Commission has no authority (to serve a notice upon a detenue.</u>

12. In the impugned notice it has been categorically mentioned that;

“যেহেতু প্রাপ্ত তথ্যের ভিত্তিতে অনুসন্ধান করিয়া দুর্নীতি দমন কমিশনের স্থির বিশ্বাস জন্মিয়াছে যে, আপনি জনাব আব্দুস সালাম, সাবেক চেয়ারম্যান, একুশে টেলিভিশন লিঃ, পিতা-মৃত এম এ করিম, বর্তমান ঠিকানা হাউজ নং-৩৩৬, রোড নং-২৩, নিউ ডিওএইচএস, মহাখালী, ঢাকা-১২১২। জ্ঞাত আয়ের বর্হির্ভূত স্বনামে/বেনামে বিপুল পরিমাণ সম্পদ/সম্পত্তির মালিক হইয়াছেন।”

<u>13. In view of the above assertions made by the Commission there is no scope to say that the Commission being a statutory body issued the notice without applying its judicial mind and mechanically having no materials before it. Further, ‘স্থির বিশ্বাস’ in other word satisfaction of the Commission cannot be challenged and decided invoking Article 102 of the Constitution.</u>

14. In case of Moudud Ahmed vs. State, Appellate Division also observed to the effect:

"Therefore, there is no difficulty to say that before issuance of any notice under section 26 of the ACC Act upon a person the Commission must have knowledge that the said person has acquired property beyond known source of income. In other words, the fact of acquiring property beyond some one's known source of income was within the knowledge of the Commission long before the issuance of the order/notice under section 26 of the Act."

15. In the case of ACC vs. Sheikh Hasina, reported in 60 DLR (AD) 172 (paragraph-32) the Appellate Division held as under:

"Moreover, the Commission was not required to disclose any specific material or investigation report for issuing an order asking for statement of assets and the satisfaction is that of the Commission and none else as has been held in the case of Mustafizur Rahman vs DG Anti-Corruption Commission, reported in 49 DLR, 599. So, the objective satisfaction is not contemplated by the Act."

<u>16. In the case of Mustafizur Rahman and 3 others vs. DG, Anti-Corruption, 49 DLR 599 it has been held by a Division Bench of the High Division that the Bureau of Anti-Corruption is not required to disclose specific material or investigation report to the petitioner in the notice requiring submission of statement of income and assets (paragraph 31).</u>

17. Having considered as above we do not find any merit in the application. And the same is misconceived one.

Accordingly, the application is rejected summarily.

End.

lawyer:
জনাব সৈয়দ মোঃ হায়দার আলী সঙ্গে জনাব মোঃ আঃ লতিফ মিয়া এ্যাডভোকেটবৃন্দ--------দরখাস্তকারীপক্ষে
জনাব মোঃ জাফর ইমাম, এ, এ, জি সঙ্গে বেগম নসরাত জাহান, এ, এ, পি-------১নং প্রতিবাদীপক্ষে
parties:
Moktar Hossain ------ Petitioner
vs
Bangladesh and others ------ Respondents
full_judgment:
বিচারপতি এ,বি,এম, খায়রুল হক : দরখাস্তকারী তাহার মুক্তিযোদ্ধা ভাতা বন্ধ করিবার বিরুদ্ধে ক্ষুদ্ধ হইয়া বাংলাদেশ সংবিধানের ১০২ অনুচ্ছেদ অনুসারে অত্র দরখাস্ত দাখিল করিয়াছেন।

২। দরখাস্তে দরখাস্তকারী নিবেদন করেন যে, ১৯৭১ ইং সনে মুক্তিযুদ্ধে অংশ গ্রহণ করিবার জন্য তিনি ভারতে গমন করেন এং তথায় রামপুরহাট প্রশিক্ষণ কেন্দ্রে সশস্ত্র প্রশিক্ষণ গ্রহণ করতঃ বাংলাদেশের মুক্তিযুদ্ধে অংশগ্রহণ করেন এবং হানাদার বাহিনীর বিরুদ্ধে যুদ্ধ করেন। স্বাধীনতার পর মাদারীপুর মিলিশিয়া ক্যাম্পে ১৫-১-১৯৭২ ইং তারিখে তিনি অস্ত্র ফেরত প্রদান করিয়া সনদ পত্র গ্রহণ করেন (এ্যানেক্সার-এ)। যথাসময়ে, বাংলাদেশের দেশ রক্ষা বিভাগ, বাংলাদেশের সশস্ত্র বাহিনীর অধিনায়ক জেনারেল মোঃ আতাউল মোঃ আতাউল গণি ওসমানীর স্বাক্ষরিত স্বাধীনতা সংগ্রামের একটি সনদপত্র দরখাস্তকারীকে প্রদান করা হয় (এ্যানেক্সার-এ-১)। দরখাস্তকারী আরও উল্লেখ করেন যে, দরখাস্তকারীর নাম এবং অন্যান্য বিবরণ ৮নং সেকটর বইয়ের ৮৪ পাতায় লিপিবদ্ধ রহিয়াছে এবং সেই বাবদে দরখাস্তকারীকে ২৩-৫-২০০৫ ইং তারিখে একটি প্রত্যয়নপত্র প্রদান করা হয় (এ্যানেক্সার-বি)।

৩। গণপ্রজাতন্ত্রী বাংলাদেশ সরকার অসহায় মুক্তিযোদ্ধাদের জন্য ভাতা প্রদানের ব্যবস্থা করেন এবং সেই লক্ষ্যে মুক্তিযোদ্ধাগণের একটি তালিকা প্রস্তুত করা হয়। মুক্তি বার্তা পত্রিকার ৪৬ পাতায় ০১১০০১০৫৮৮ নং ক্রমিকে মুক্তিযোদ্ধা হিসেবে দরখাস্তকারীর নাম প্রকাশিত হয়। সরকারি সিদ্ধান্ত অনুসারে অসহায় মুক্তিযোদ্ধাগণের তালিকা প্রস্তুতের পর অন্যান্য দুস্থ মুক্তিযোদ্ধাদের সহিত দরখাস্তকারীকে মাসিক টাঃ ৩০০ হিসেবে অসহায় মুক্তিযোদ্ধার ভাতা ১-৭-২০০০ইং তারিখ হইতে প্রদান করা হইতে থাকে। দরখাস্তকারী সরকার কর্তৃক সরবরাহকৃত অসহায় মুক্তিযোদ্ধাদের ভাতা পরিশোধ বহিতে স্বাক্ষর করতঃ অসাহায় মুক্তিযোদ্ধা ভাতা গ্রহণ করিতে আরম্ভ করেন (এ্যানেক্সার-সি) কিন্তু পরবর্তীতে ৩০-৭-২০০২ ইং তরিখ হইতে তাহার উক্ত ভাতা প্রদান বন্ধ করিয়া দেওয়া হয়। তৎপর দরখাস্তকারী প্রতিরক্ষা মন্ত্রণালয়, মুক্তিযোদ্ধা মন্ত্রণালয়, জেলা প্রশাসক, মাদারীপুর ও সভাপতি, মুক্তিযোদ্ধা যাচাই বাছাই কমিটি, বরাবরে বিভিন্ন সময়ে আবেদন করতঃ দুস্থ মুক্তিযোদ্ধা হিসেবে তাহার পাওনা পরিশোধ করিবার জন্য বারংবার নিবেদন করা সত্ত্বেও কোন ফলোদয় না হওয়ায় দরখাস্তকারী তাহার বিজ্ঞ এ্যাডভোকেট মহোদয়ের মাধ্যমে প্রতিবাদীগণের বরাবরে একটি Notice Demanding Justice জারী করতঃ দুস্থ মুক্তিযোদ্ধা হিসেবে তাহার ভাতা প্রদানের আবেদন করেন কিন্তু কোন ফলোদয় না হওয়ায় বাংলাদেশ সংবিধানের ১০২ অনুচ্ছেদ অনুসারে অত্র দরখাস্তটি দাখিল করিলে সুপ্রীম  কোর্টের হাইকোর্ট বিভাগ নিম্নলিখিত রুল জারী করেন :

"Let a Rule Nisi issue calling upon the Respondents to show cause as to why the respondents should not be directed to give the Helpless Muktijuddah Bhata by the State to the petitioner as per the amount received by him as shown in Annexure "C" with effect from July 2002 with enhanced rate and as to why the action of stopping the said State Bhata of the petitioner should not be declared to have been made without lawful authority and is of no legal effect and/or such other or further order or orders passed as to this Court may seem fit and proper.

The Rule is made returnable within 4(four) weeks."

৪। দরখাস্তকারীর পক্ষে সৈয়দ মোঃ হায়দার আলী, এ্যাডভোকেট, মোকদ্দমায় বক্তব্য উপস্থাপন করেন এবং জনাব মোঃ আঃ লতিফ মিয়া, এ্যাডভোকেট তাহাকে সহযোগিতা করেন।

৫। অপরপ্েক্ষ জনাব মোঃ জাফর ইমাম, সহকারী এ্যাটর্ণী জেনারেল এবং বেগম নুসরাত জাহান, সহকারী এ্যাটর্নী জেনারেল, কোন এফিডেভিট ইন অপজিশান দাখিল ব্যতিরেকে প্রতিবাদীগণের পক্ষে বক্তব্য উপস্থাপন করেন।

৬। দরখাস্তকারী পক্ষে বিজ্ঞ এ্যাডভোকেট সৈয়দ মোঃ হায়দার আলী নিবেদন করেন যে, স্বীকৃত মতেই দরখাস্তকারী একজন বীর মুক্তিযোদ্ধা। তিনি বাংলাদেশের স্বাধীনতা সংগ্রামের সক্রিয় অংশ গ্রহণ করিয়াছিলেন এবং হানাদার বাহিনলি বিরুদ্ধে সশস্ত্র সংগ্রাম করিয়াছিলেন। এ সম্পর্কে বিজ্ঞ এ্যাডভোকেট মহোদয় দরখাস্তের সহিত সংযুক্ত মিলিশিয়া ক্যাম্প, মাদারীপুর এবং ম্যাজিষ্ট্রেট মহোদয় কর্তৃক প্রদত্ত লিভসার্টিফিকেট তাং ১৫-১-১৯৭২ ইং (এ্যানেক্সার এ), বাংলাদেশের সশস্ত্র বাহিনীর তদানিন্তন অধিনায়ক জেনারেল মোঃ আতউল গণি ওসমানি স্বাক্ষরিত এবং গণপ্রজান্ত্রী বাংলাদেশের দেশ রক্ষা বিভাগ কর্তৃক প্রদত্ত স্বাধীনতা সংগ্রামের সনদপত্র (এ্যানেক্সা-এ-১) এবং বাংলাদেশ মুক্তিযুদ্ধ কল্যাণ ট্রাষ্ট কর্তৃক প্রদত্ত সনদপত্র তাং ২৩-৫-২০০৫ ইং (এ্যানেক্সার-বি) এর প্রতি দৃষ্টি আকর্ষণ পূর্বক জোরালভাবে নিবেদন করেন যে, দরখাস্তকারী স্বীকৃতমতেই একজন বীরমুক্তিযোদ্ধা ও স্বাধীনতা সংগ্রামে তাহার অংশ গ্রহণ বাংলাদেশের তদানিন্তন মুক্তিযুদ্ধের অধিনায়ক কর্তৃক স্বীকৃত ও প্রশংসিত। এই মুক্তিযোদ্ধা দরখাস্তকারী কালক্রমে হত দরিদ্র দশায় উপনীত হইলে তাহার আবেদনক্রমে সরকারের সংশ্লিষ্ট কর্তৃপক্ষ কর্তৃক যথারীতি যাচাই করতঃ অসহায় মুক্তিযোদ্ধা হিসেবে তাহাকে তালিকাভূক্ত করা হয় এবং ১-৭-২০০০ ইং তারিখ হইতে তাহাকে মাসিক ৩০০ টাকা হারে অসহায় মুক্তিযোদ্ধা ভাতা প্রদান করা হইতে থাকে কিন্তু পরবর্তীতে ৩০-৭-২০০২ ইং তারিখ হইতে কোন কারণ প্রদর্শন ব্যতিরেকেই তাহাকে আত্মপক্ষ সমর্থনের কোন প্রকার সুযোগ প্রদান না করিয়া সহসাই তাহাকে প্রদত্ত মাসিক ৩০০ টাকা অসহায় মুক্তিযোদ্ধা ভাতা প্রদান বন্ধ করিয়া দেওয়া হয় যাহা আইন ও ন্যায় বিচারের সম্পূর্ণ পরিপন্থী।

৭। ইহাছাড়া তিনি অসহায় মুক্তিযোদ্ধাগণের ভাতার পরিমাণের প্রসঙ্গ উত্থাপন করেন। তিনি নিবেদন করেন যে, ঢাকা শহরে একটি মোটর গাড়ী ১ (এক) ঘন্টা পার্ক করিয়া রাখিতে কমপক্ষে ১০ টাকা ফি প্রদান করিতে হয়। দুস্থ মুক্তিযোদ্ধাগণকে মাসিক ৩০০ টাকা হারে ভাতা প্রদানের অর্থ দৈনিক মাত্র ১০ টাকা যাহা চরম অবমাননাকর কিন্তু তাহাও সরকারে বিনা কারণে বন্ধ করিয়াছেন বলিয়া তিনি নিবেদন করেন।

৮। এমতাবস্থায় বিজ্ঞ এ্যাডভোকেট মহোদয় দরখাস্তকারীকে বকেয়াসহগ অসহায় মুক্তিযোদ্ধা ভাতা প্রদানের নির্দেশ প্রার্থনা করেন।

৯। অপরপক্ষে জনাব মোঃ জাফর ইমাম, বিজ্ঞ সহকারী এ্যাটর্নী জেনারেল দরখাস্তকারী যে একজন মুক্তিযোদ্ধা তাহা অস্বীকার করেন নাই বা তাহাকে যে ১-৭-২০০০ ইং তারিখ হইতে অসহায় মুক্তিযোদ্ধা ভাতা প্রদান করা হইয়াছিল তাহাও তিনি অস্বীকার করেন নাই। ৩০-৭-২০০২ ইং তারিখ হইতে কেন দরখাস্তকারীকে পূর্বে প্রদত্ত ভাতা প্রদান বন্ধ করা হইয়াছে তাহারও কো ব্যাখ্যা তিনি প্রদান করিতে পারেন নাই।

১০। আমরা উভয়পক্ষের বিজ্ঞ এ্যাডভোকেট মহোদয়গেণর বক্তব্য শ্রবণ করিলাম, দরখাস্ত ও তৎসংযুক্তকাগজাদি পর্যালোচনা করিলাম। ইহা স্বীকৃত যে, দরখাস্তকারী একজন বীর মুক্তিযোদ্ধা। তিনি ১৯৭১ ইং সনে দেশ ত্যাগ করিয়া ভারতে গমন করেন এবং তথায় সশস্ত্র প্রশিক্ষণ গ্রহণ করেন। তৎপর তিনি বাংলাদেশের স্বাধীনতার জন্য সশস্ত্র মুক্তিযুদ্ধে অংশগ্রহণ করেন। ইহাও স্বীকৃত যে, সংশ্লিষ্ট কর্তৃপক্ষ সরকারী সিদ্ধান্ত অনুসারে দুস্থ এবং অসহায় মুক্তিযোদ্ধা হিসেবে যথারীতি যাচাই বাছাই করতঃ সংশ্লিষ্ট ভাতা পরিশোধ বহি মারফৎ (এ্যানেক্সার-সি) তাহাকে ৩০-৭-২০০২ ইং তারিখ পর্যন্ত অসহায় মুক্তিযোদ্ধা ভাতা প্রদান করেন। তৎপর এক অজ্ঞাত কারণে আকস্মাৎ তাহার উক্ত ভাতা বন্ধ করিয়া দেওয়া হয়। ভাতা প্রদান বন্ধ করিবার কোন কারণ প্রতিবাদীপক্ষ সেই সময়েও প্রদান করেন নাই বা অত্র রুল প্রাপ্ত হইবার পরেও তাহাদের পক্ষ হইতে কোনরূপ ব্যাখ্যা প্রদান হয় নাই।

১১। মুক্তিযোদ্ধাগণ বাংলাদেশের জাতীয় বীর। তাহারা ১৯৭১ ইং সনে তাহাদের গৃহকোণ পরিত্যাগ করতঃ নিজেদের জীবনের প্রতি ভ্রুক্ষেপ না করিয়া সম্পূর্ণ অনিশ্চয়তা মধ্যে নিজেদের বাবা-মা, ভাই-বোন, আত্মীয়-স্বজন এবং নিরাপদ আশ্রয়স্থল ত্যাগ করিয়া বাংলাদেশের স্বাধীনতা সংগ্রামে ঝাঁপাইয়া পড়েন। তাহারা তখন জানিতেন না বা যে দেশ আদৌ স্বাধীন হইবে কিনা বা আদৌ তাহারা জীবিত অবস্থায় দেশ মাতৃকায় ফিরিয়া আসিতে পারিবেন কিনা। তাহাদের সম্মুখে তখন এক ভয়াবহ কালান্তক যুদ্ধ অপেক্ষা করিতেছিল। বাংলাদেশের শিক্ষিত, অর্ধশিক্ষিত সকল মুক্তিযোদ্ধাগণ সেই মুক্তিযুদ্ধে জীবন পণ করিয়া সম্পূর্ণ অনিশ্চয়তার মধ্যে ঝাঁপাইয়া পড়েন। তাহাদের সেই নিস্বার্থ ও চরম ত্যাগের ফলশ্রুতিতে বাঙালী জাতি ‘বাংলাদেশ’ নামে একটি স্বাধীন ভূ-খন্ড, একটি জাতীয় সঙ্গীত প্রাপ্ত হইয়া বিশ্ব সভ্যতার ইতিহাসে এই সর্ব প্রথম একটি জাতি হিসেবে বিশ্বের দরবারে আত্মপ্রকাশ করে। মুক্তিযোদ্ধাগণের চরম ও পরম ত্যাগের বিনিময়ে এই অমূল্য স্বাধীনতা অর্জিত হয়। এই স্বাধীনতা ভূ-খন্ড মুক্তিযোদ্ধাদেরই অবিস্মরণীয় দান। এই দানের জন্য বাঙালী জাতি চিরদিন মুক্তিযোদ্ধাগণকে কৃতজ্ঞচিত্তে স্মরণ করিবে। বাঙালী জাতি কখনও ভূলিতে পারে না যে জাতি হিসেবে ইহার যাহাকিছু অর্জন তাহার পিছনে রহিয়াছে মুক্তিযোদ্ধাদের সেই নিঃস্বার্থ অম্লান আত্মদান যাহা কোন প্রতিদান বা কোন মূল্যেই বাঙালী জাতি মুক্তিযোদ্ধাদের সেই ঋণ পরিশোধ করিতে কখনই সক্ষম হইবে না। মুক্তিযোদ্ধাগণের সেই সম্মানই প্রাপ্য যাহাতে ভবিষ্যৎ প্রজন্ম যেন গর্বের সহিত বলিতে পারে যে তাহার পূর্ব পুরুষ একজন মুক্তিযোদ্ধা ছিলেন। সেই পরিচয়ই হইবে তাহার সর্বশ্রেষ্ঠ পরিচয়।

১২। এই প্রেক্ষাপটে সংশ্লিষ্ট কর্তৃপক্ষ এবং অন্যান্য সকলের স্মরণ রাখা অবশ্য কর্তব্য যে, মুক্তিযোদ্ধাগণকে কোন ভাতা প্রদান করিয়া তাহাদেরকে কোন কৃপা হইতেছে না বরঞ্চ সংশ্লিষ্ট সকলের অন্তরে ইহা ক্ষোদিত হওয়া আবশ্যক যে সরকারের পক্ষ হইতে মুক্তিযোদ্ধাগণকে যে ভাতা বা সম্মানী প্রদান করা হউক না কেন তাহা মুক্তিযোদ্ধাগণেরই দান। মুক্তিযোদ্ধাগণ ভাতা বা সম্মানী গ্রহণ করতঃ ঋণী হন নাই, বরঞ্চ বাঙালী জাতিকেই ঋণে আবদ্ধ করিয়াছেন। এই প্রেক্ষাপটে মুক্তিযোদ্ধাদের দাবী বিবেচনার অপেক্ষা রাখে। সংশ্লিষ্ট সকলেরই স্মরণ রাখিতে হইবে যে, দরখাস্তকারী একজন মুক্তিযোদ্ধা এবং তাহার যে কোন আইনানুগ প্রার্থনা সর্বদাই অগ্রগণ্য। কারণ তাহাদের ত্যাগের ফলশ্রুতিতেই আজিকার এই বাংলাদেশ এবং বাংলাদেশের সকল প্রতিষ্ঠান। দরখাস্তকারী স্বীকৃত মতেই একজন মুক্তিযোদ্ধা এবং মুক্তিযোদ্ধা মানেই একজন জাতীয় বীর।

১৩। যেহেতু দরখাস্তকারী স্বীকৃতমতেই একজন বীরমু্ক্তিযোদ্ধা এবং সরকারী সিদ্ধান্ত অনুসারে এবং সংশ্লিষ্ট কর্তৃপক্ষ যথারীতি যাচাই বাছাই অন্তে তাহাকে অসহায় মুক্তিযোদ্ধাভাতা প্রদান করিয়াছিলেন সেহেতু আমরা সরকারের ও সংশ্লিষ্ট সরকারি কর্তৃপক্ষের উক্ত প্রশংসনীয় সিদ্ধান্ত ও ভাতা প্রদান কার্যক্রম আইনানুগভাবে সঠিক ছিল বলিয়াই গ্রহণ করিব। উল্লেখ্য যে উক্ত অসহায় মুক্তিযোদ্ধা ভাতা প্রদান বন্ধ করিবার সময় প্রতিবাদীগণ কোন কারণ প্রদর্শন করেন নাই বা কেন তাহার ভাতা বন্ধ করা হইবে না তাহার কারণ দরখাস্তকারীকে দর্শানোর কোন সুযোগ প্রদান করেন নাই। ইহা ন্যায় বিচারের পরিপন্থী। আরও উল্লেখ্য যে অত্র রুল জারী হইবার পরেও প্রতিবাদীগণ দরখাস্তকারীর ভাতা প্রদান বন্ধ করিবার কোন কারণ দর্শান নাই।

<u>১৪। যেহেতু যথাযথ যাচাই বাছাই অন্তে সরকারি সিদ্ধান্ত অনুসারে দরখাস্তকারীকে অসহায় মুক্তিযোদ্ধা ভাতা প্রদান করা হইয়াছিল সেহেতু অন্য কো প্রতিকূল সাক্ষ্যের অনুপস্থিতিতে দরখাস্তকারীকে অসহায় মুক্তিযোদ্ধাভাতা প্রদানের জন্য সরকারি পূর্বোক্ত সিদ্ধান্ত সঠিক বলিয়াই গণ্য করা হইবে।</u>

<u>১৫। যেহেতু প্রতিবাদীপক্ষ ভাতা বন্ধ করিবার কোন কারণই প্রদর্শন করিতে পারেন নাই সেহেতু দরখাস্তকারীর ভাতা বন্ধ করণ বে-আইনী ঘোষণা করা হইল।</u>

১৬। এখন প্রশ্ন উঠিতেছে যে, একজন দুঃস্থ মুক্তিযোদ্ধাকে কি হাে অসহায় মুক্তিযোদ্ধা ভাতা প্রদান করা হইবে। সংশ্লিষ্ট সকলকেই স্মরণ রাখিতে হইবে যে তাহারা মুক্তিযোদ্ধাগণকে এইরূপ ভাতা প্রদানের মাধ্যমে কো ভিক্ষা প্রদান করিতেছেন না, তাহারা একজন জাতীয় বীরকে সম্মান প্রদর্শন করিতেছেন। যুদ্ধ ক্ষেত্রে চরম ত্যাগের মুখোমুখি হইয়া তাহারা সেই দুর্লভ সম্মান যথার্থ ভাবেই নিজ অধিকারে অজর্ন করিয়াছেন। একজন মুক্তিযোদ্ধার মাসিক সম্মানীভাতা টাকা ৩০০ অর্থাৎ দৈনিক টাকা ১০ হারে ভাতা প্রদানকে ভাতা না বলিয়া ভিক্ষা বলাই মুক্তিযুদ্ধ। একজন মুক্তিযোদ্ধাকে এইরূপ পরিমাণ ভাতা প্রদান বাঙালী জাতির গৌরবকে বহন করে না বরঞ্চ আমরা জাতি হিসেবে মানসিকভাবে দেউলিয়াত্ব বরণ করিয়াছি তাহাই প্রমাণ করে। এই আদালত মুক্তিযোদ্ধাগণের প্রতি প্রতিবাদীগণের এইরূপ ব্যবহারে অসন্তোষ প্রকাশ করিতেছে।

১৭। এই আদালত আশা প্রকাশ করে যে সরকার দরখাস্তকারী এবং তাহার ন্যায় অসহায় মুক্তিযোদ্ধাগণকে কমপক্ষে সরকার কর্তৃক নির্ধারিত নিম্নতম বেতনের/মজুরীর সমপরিমাণ টাকা দুস্থ ও অসহায় মুক্তিযোদ্ধাগণকে মাসিক ভাতা হিসেবে প্রদান করিবে।

১৮। এখানে আরও উল্লেখ করা প্রয়োজন যে মুক্তিযোদ্ধাদের প্রতি জাতি হিসেবে আমাদের যে অনীহা ও অবহেলা তাহা মুক্তিযুদ্ধ ও মুক্তিযোদ্ধাদের আত্মত্যাগের ইতিহাস সম্বন্ধে আমাদের অজ্ঞতা ও নির্লিপ্ততাই দায়ী। কিন্তু জাতি হিসেবে আমাদের গর্ব এই মুক্তিযুদ্ধ সম্বন্ধে নূতন প্রজন্মকে অবহিত করা জাতীয় স্বার্থে প্রয়োজন। এই কারণে মুক্তিযুদ্ধ এবং মুক্তিযোদ্ধাদের সঠিক ইতিহাস বাংলা মাধ্যম, ইংরেজী মাধ্যম ও সকল ধরণের মাদ্রাসায় মাধ্যমিক বা সমপর্যায়ভুক্ত সকল শিক্ষা প্রতিষ্ঠানে ১ম শ্রেণী হইতে ১০ শ্রেণী বা সমপর্যায়ভূক্ত সকল শ্রেণীতে এবং মাধ্যমিক বা সমপর্যায়ভূক্ত সকল পরীক্ষায় আবশ্যিক পাঠ্য হিসেবে অন্তর্ভূক্ত করিবার জন্য সরকারের সংশ্লিষ্ট শিক্ষা মন্ত্রণালয়কে আহ্বান জানান হইল যাহাতে মুক্তিযুদ্ধের চেতনার আদর্শ, আলোকে ও দর্পণে বাঙালী জাতি যেন আরারও নিজেকে চিনিতে পারে ও মূল্যায়ন করিতে পারে এবং বিশ্বে একটি আলোকিত জাত হিসেবে প্রতিষ্ঠিত হইতে পারে।

১৯। এই আদালত আশা করে যে সংশ্লিষ্ট মন্ত্রণালয় এ ব্যাপারে যথা প্রয়োজনীয় ব্যবস্থা ও পদক্ষেপ অনতিবিলম্বে জাতীয় স্বার্থে গ্রহণ করিবে।

২০। এমতাবস্থায় অসহায় মুক্তিযোদ্ধা ভাতা এই রায়ের কপি প্রাপ্তির এক মাসের মধ্যে দরখাস্তকারীকে প্রদান করিতে প্রতিবাদীগণকে নির্দেশ প্রদান করা হইল।

২১। উপরোক���ত মন্তব্য ও নির্দেশনা সহকারে অত্র রুলটি খরচা ব্যতিরেকে এ্যাবসলিউট করা হইল।

অত্র রায়ের কপি  সচিব, শিক্ষা মন্ত্রণালয় ও সচিব, আইন মন্ত্রণালয়ে পাঠানো হউক।

End.
