Respondent Contemner No. (2) Masud Milad, reporter of the Daily Prothom Alo. Respondent Contemner No. (3) Matiur Rahman, Editor of the Daily Prothom Alo and Respondent Contemner No. (4) Mahfuz Anam, Publisher of the Daily Prothom Alo are sentenced to pay fine of Taka 1000 (Taka one thousand) each in default to suffer simple imprisonment for one month. The Contemner-respondent No. (5) Shamaresh Baidya, reporter of the Daily Bhorer Kagoj who not only scandalised the judge of the Court in unsavory language but also caused a photo of the judge in question to be published is sentenced to suffer simple imprisonment for 2 months and to pay a fine of Taka 1000 (Taka one thousand) in default to suffer simple imprisonment for one month more. Contemner-Respondent Nos. (6) Abed Khan, Editor of the Daily Bhorer Kagoj and Contemner-Respondent No.(7) Saber Hossain Chowdhury, Publisher of the Daily Bhorer Kagoj are also sentenced to pay a fine of Taka 1000 (Taka one thousand) each in default to suffer simple imprisonment for one month.

<u>72. We have taken a lenient view about the sentence in recognition of the past services of the respondents to the nation.</u>

<u>73. Before parting with the judgment we want to observe that the Press and the Bar may formulate some joint guidelines in line with the guidelines as per appendix to the judgment of justice Brennan in the case of Nebraska Press Association vs Stuart reported in 427 US 539 in reporting Court matters. We further like to observe that no communication 'with the Judges of this Court either over telephone or otherwise is permissible except through the Registrar of the Court. The press should not publish news creating unnecessary sensations about Court matters. We further observe that step should be taken to codify the laws of contempt as has been done in India and Pakistan. The High Court Division should either frame its own Contempt Rules or adopt the rules framed by the Appellate Division without further delay.</u>

74. We want to put on record our deep appreciation for the able assistance rendered by the learned Advocates of both the sides including their learned juniors.

The application filed by the petitioner for directing the contemner-respondents to disclose their sources of information is disposed of as no finding is necessary in this case.

End.

Abdul Quayum with HS Deb Brahman, Advocates -----For the Petitioner.
